What do the stories of the Qur'an teach us? Are these merely stories, or are there real, sound, relatable lessons to be drawn from them? Who is Iblis, or Shaytan — and what is this creature's problem with us? If he is the cause of every trouble, why does Allah not simply destroy Shaytan and be done with it? Why must I pray? Does Allah need my prayers? I thought Allah needs nothing, yet the way the prayer is spoken of, and the way its importance is described, almost makes it feel as though Allah needs our prayers. You know, the Greeks believed in their myths that their gods needed human prayer to sustain their powers. That is why their gods created destruction and fear in the world, so that human beings would pray, and in this way their gods held on to their power. Does our Allah work the same way? Do we have an unjust Allah? Does it give Him some kind of pleasure to burn us in the Fire? Why could His message not be entirely about love? Why must He speak of hellfire, torment, and pain?

Let us ask all of these very difficult questions, and in the end, if we find our answers — answers that satisfy the demands of our hearts as well as of our intellects — then let us choose this religion for ourselves. Because when we choose it this time, it will be so different. This time we will do it with conviction and understanding, not merely because we are supposed to. This time it will be a living Islam, built on the foundation and the spirit of faith, and it will not feel like some dead weight upon our shoulders.

A great many young people feel exactly this way about Islam. Everyone leads a very busy life, with responsibilities of family and work — even the youngsters and the teenagers. The amount of work some of you must do for school or college is astonishing.

And as an aside, I wish to say how deeply impressed I am by the way you young ones make time for these sessions. Most of you have not missed a single one, and not only these — from the days of those earlier Chahal Sabaq sessions as well. And when you do miss one, you ask me to hold a makeup session with you. MashaAllah! The same is true of the rest of the members. But I wished especially to take a moment to acknowledge and applaud the young ones in this group. Believe me, I know what setting aside one hour on a weekend means to everyone. Yet in spite of all your busy schedules, you make time for these sessions. For some of you it is mid-afternoon right now, and for others late at night, and still you make this enormous effort to learn. Jazakum Allah Khair. Only the other day, someone was telling me that children these days have no interest in religion, that they do not wish to learn about Islam, that they are not serious about their faith. And my immediate response to that was:

Well, you have not met my children. The children in my session. I am so proud of all of you. In any case, what was I saying?

So today it makes no difference whether we are adults or teenagers. Life is extremely busy for every one of us. We can scarcely find time for anything, not even for ourselves. Now, on top of all of this, what happens is that the weight of our Islamic responsibilities gets added to all the responsibilities we already carry. And so, naturally, we feel burdened by it. That is why prayer, fasting, and all these other obligations feel like such a burden, such an inconvenience in our daily lives. Some people choose to carry on with this burden whether they like it or not, while others simply decide to set the weight down and forget about the obligations altogether. But the real question is this: why do these obligations feel like a burden? And I think it is because Islam has become a dead weight to us, a body without a soul, that we have to carry upon our shoulders until the day we die.

But now imagine for a moment what would happen if our Islam had a soul, an energy of its own. What if the body of Islam were alive with the soul of Eman, the spirit of faith? Would we still feel a burden, or such a reluctance, in carrying out these compulsory obligations of Islam? I do not think so. Islam should not be something we have to follow; it should be something that drives us. It should energize us; it should strengthen us when we feel weak; it should motivate us when we feel low; it should give us courage in the face of trials and hardships. It should not be the other way around. We should not be carrying the dead weight of Islam upon our shoulders. We should not be praying our prayers merely to get them out of the way or to keep a score. We should not be fasting out of fear of burning in the fire of hell. We should not love our parents simply because we are told to, or because we are threatened with the consequences. These obligations, this obedience to Allah and His Prophet, all of this should come from within. The fire of faith, the fire of Eman, needs to be kindled inside us; and once it grows strong, it will rise to the surface of its own accord. It will translate into action of its own accord. It is not merely that fulfilling our obligations will no longer feel difficult; it will actually become impossible not to fulfill them. And this is what we find in the seerah of the Prophet and his sahaba. They were not carrying the weight of Islam; the spirit of Islam was carrying them. They were not being controlled from the outside; they were being driven from within.

But this is a very real challenge of our times. And I know this because I have been through it. Even after studying so much taveel, mabda maad, haqaiq, and daqaiq, I still found it hard to practice basic Islam from one day to the next. Why? Because everything I had learned was merely information stacked up in my brain. There was no connection with the heart, because only when information connects with the heart does it become knowledge. As long as it is simply sitting in the brain, it is only information. It is like books sitting on a shelf. They may be full of information,

but they are of no use to me until I read them, are they not? It was only when I connected with the essence of Islam, when the Islam of my intellect entered my heart, that things began to change for me. You see, once the foundation of Emaan, of faith, is established, once the groundwork is laid, it is so easy to build the structure of Islam upon it. But if there is no foundation, and you keep trying to force a building up on top of nothing, how long do you suppose it will stand?

That is why, in these sessions, I want us to work on this foundation of Islam. And if you can relate to what I am saying, even in the smallest way, then InshaAllah you will find these sessions of use.

Now the question is how we solve this problem, this problem of reviving the spirit of Islam in our hearts. I think it can be divided into three parts.

First and foremost, it is a spiritual problem, and most people will agree with that: it is a problem of the heart. The second is that it is an intellectual problem, and this is the part many people do not attend to. Faith is not a spiritual matter alone; it is also an intellectual one. It is something of which we must be convinced intellectually as well. Blind belief simply does not suffice in this day and age. And then, finally, on account of the flaw in both of those things, the heart and the intellect, it is also a moral problem. That is to say, when a person truly benefits from the fruits of Eman, what issues from them is this very high standard of morality and ethics; they become a person of noble character. So when Allah (AWJ) speaks of the people of Eman, He says:

قد افلح المؤمنون

Indeed the believers have succeeded. And of the Mo'min, He mentions these very lofty ethical qualities in the Quran.

These, then, are the three problems bound up with the revival of faith in our hearts. So I think of it as Heart + Intellect = FAITH.

Of these, the one most people struggle with, at least from what I have seen, is the intellectual component. As Muslims we are meant to have faith, and faith is born of the union of the heart and the intellect, and this faith then matures over time into an excellent moral and ethical character. Do you understand?

Think of the heart as the king. It is the one that makes all our final decisions for us. Whatever the heart commands comes to pass. And think of the intellect as the king's advisor, the wazir. Do not picture the film Aladdin, now, with Jaffar and an evil parrot perched on his shoulder. That would be a poor image indeed.

So the heart is the king and the intellect is the advisor. Both are very strong and powerful authorities that govern all our decisions, but the heart is the ultimate king.

Now let me give you an example. A volunteer, please. I am watching an action film, and right in the middle of it, it is time for namaaz. Now, this is a conversation that takes place between my heart and my intellect. The heart says: come now, it is time for namaaz; you ought to leave your film and pray. But what does my intellect say? Why? Why should I pray? Why is prayer more interesting, or even more important, than this film right now? The heart says: no, no, no, we are meant to pray because we are good Muslims. The intellect says: yes, but why?

At this point the heart has three choices.

First, the heart can say to the intellect: Be silent! Do not ask foolish questions! Simply do as I tell you, because you must — is that not so? And since the heart is the king, it can make the body comply. But the intellect says: Very well, do so; yet I will keep telling you that you are making the wrong decision, and that you ought to be watching the film instead of praying. So I stand up for namaaz. But now, as I am praying, the intellect keeps on: Oh, you are missing such a wonderful film! I say, "Sami Allahu liman hamida." The intellect says: Yes, but what do you suppose Ironman is doing right now? "Rabbana laka-l-hamd." I cannot believe you are missing all this marvelous action for the sake of this cardiovascular exercise — is that not so? Yes, my intellect does address my heart as "dude." So now tell me: am I going to enjoy this namaaz? No. So that is one option.

Second option: the heart says, Very well, watch the film; but I will constantly remind you that you ought to be praying instead of watching it. There is a wonderful action scene you are trying to enjoy, and the heart says: You know this is a sin, do you not? You know you are going to go to hell for this, do you not? Allah is going to punish you for this. I am not stopping you from watching the film; I am only telling you. It is fine — do as you wish; I am only letting you know. So now, with this option, am I going to enjoy the film? No, because the heart is filling me with guilt.

Third option: the heart says to the intellect, You know what — you are right; this film is rather more enjoyable. We can always pray after the film; or we can make it up later as qaza; or, you know what, let us simply forget the prayer. There will still be zohr tomorrow, will there not? So let us enjoy the film together. Now, will I enjoy the film? Of course; I will have a wonderful time.

So in these situations, when was I able to have a wonderful time? When the heart and the intellect were what? In perfect agreement — is that not so? But in all of these options, worship, or salaah, is losing every single time, is it not? Even when I am actually standing up for prayer and going through the motions, I am thinking only of the film.

But a fourth option is possible. That is the option in which the heart says: it is time for namaaz — and the intellect immediately says, "حی علی الصلوۃ حی علی الفلاح." Let us make haste for prayer; let us make haste for success. Not merely, let us go for namaaz — let us make haste. Hayya, in Arabic, is used for rushing toward something. It does not mean to be quick. The Arabic word for "quick" is سرع, and from it comes the word سرعۃ, which means to do something quickly. حی, on the other hand, is a superlative form. If there is a fire in the building, the word hayya will be used, because it carries a sense of urgency; it is bound up with salvation. So the azaan does not say, سرع علی الصلوۃ ؛ سرع علی الفلح — quickly go for prayer, quickly go for success. It says, "rush" — rush for prayer, rush for success. Why rush?

Because it will not last forever. In third-world countries, where people are starving to death, when relief trucks bring them food and water, they rush toward it. They do not merely move quickly toward it; they rush toward it, because the supplies will run out. Do you understand the difference? So we "rush" to prayer because the benefits we are about to receive will last for a very limited time.

So when the intellect is convinced, it does not stand against the heart; it urges the heart to rush for namaaz above anything else in the world. But when can that happen? Only when the heart and the intellect harmoniously make the same decision together. Now, in this fourth scenario, is prayer going to feel like a burden? Is it going to be something I simply want to be done with and get out of the way? Of course not.

Now, very interestingly, this same dialogue that I have just explained at the micro level takes place in our lives at the macro level. Allah has gifted human beings with two faculties: the spiritual faculty, which is the heart (the commander in chief), and the intellectual faculty, which is the mind (the chief of staff). All of us, as Muslims, are born with the love of Allah and the love of His messenger (SWS) in our hearts, so the spiritual aspect is covered. All of us, as Muslims, also want to have a high moral and ethical character, so the moral component is covered too. But the intellectual aspect is where we face problems. Without it, all we are left with is blind faith.

We all want to be good Muslims and to follow the teachings of Islam, but we also have this need to know why. That gives birth to questions. My friends, it is not bad or wrong for us to have questions. That is perfectly natural. It is a demand of the intellect. It is by design. It would be wrong not to have questions. It is actually constructive. But the conflict begins when we do not get logical answers to our questions, or, even worse, when we are asked not to question at all. That is when it really starts getting bad.

So then, in order to resolve this conflict, we start making an effort to understand Islam. But then what happens is that we come across people in our lives who, willingly or unwillingly, discourage the needs of our intellect. Do not ask questions. Do not think, just do it. You are too young to understand. You will understand it later. You just have to do this. You just cannot do that.

But when we try to ask why, the response we get is not convincing at all. Because Rasul Allah did it this way. Yes, but why did he do it this way? What is the purpose of doing it? He did it because Allah commanded him to. All right, but why did Allah command him to do it? Do not ask such questions. But I need answers to these questions so that things can make sense to me. Do not worry about the answers; you will get them later when you grow up. Well, then, if I am going to get the answers later, then I will do my namaz or roza later too.

Now, the intentions of these people are not bad. Sometimes the people we turn to do not know the answers themselves. Or sometimes they do have the answers but cannot explain them well. Or they have the answers and hold them back from us because we are not ready for them yet.

We have not matured intellectually enough to understand those answers. So there are all of these different factors at work. But in the absence of answers, the next step becomes to control by force. And the most popular method is the one that comes from the carrot-and-stick philosophy: the carrot is the reward, jannah, and the stick is the hellfire.

Yet this makes us wonder. Is this truly the best that Islam can do to convince us? Is this what Islam is all about? Is Jannat the ultimate goal, or is Allah the ultimate goal? Is Jannah the end, or is it only a means to an end?

But do you know what happens as a result of this carrot and stick, this accounting mindset? Religion becomes nothing more than balancing a checkbook. A person thinks: I drank alcohol, so I have collected a certain amount of gunaah; now tell me how much charity I must give to offset it. Or perhaps: I have given too much charity this year, I have collected too much sawaab, so it is acceptable if I sin a little, because I am still in the positive. I assure you, this is no exaggeration. I know people in our jamaat who hold this mentality and who truly, deeply believe in this logic.

Is this really what Islam, this glorious religion of Allah, amounts to? Is this what Allah wants from us? Is this all that Rasul Allah struggled for? Is this what Maulana Ali, Imam Hassan, and Imam Hussain sacrificed their lives and their families for? Merely for an account ledger?

Another mechanism of control is the one in which some of us are told that Shaitaan is putting these questions into our heads. I believe I shared this with you earlier. As a teenager, I had a few questions about Islam, so I approached someone I thought might have the answers. He heard my first question, and his response to me was this: Listen, you need to go and perform wuzu, pray two rakaat of Maghfiratuz Zunoob, recite a tasbeeh of Astaghfirullah, and seek forgiveness for your sins from Allah, because Shaitan has taken over your mind. Shaitan is placing these thoughts, these questions, into your head. That is what he said to me.

But do you know what the problem with that approach was? Even after I performed wuzu, even after I prayed the two rakaat, even after I recited the Astaghfirullah tasbeeh and asked forgiveness for my sins, I still had the exact same questions I had before. The only thing that changed for me was that I had now learned it was not safe for me to ask questions. And the more this happened, the more I was turned away from Islam, until one day I began to believe that all of this was nonsense, that Islam had no answers at all.

So crushing the intellectual needs of those who wish to learn is not the right solution. This may have worked fifty years ago, but not today. Today, children do not follow anything until they are convinced of it, and they are not acting out of rebellion or arrogance. This is the way it should be.

And to you children, I say this as well: just because one person could not give you answers, to stop striving to find answers is also not the right approach. If one person does not have the answer, find another, and then another. Make the effort on your own. Study the Quran, even if only in translation. If the whole of it does not make sense, take what does make sense.

We Muslims are not meant to be people who use only their hearts and not their intellects, as the Christians do.

The Quran describes the Christian community as people of soft hearts, and at the same time it points to what they abandoned: the dimension of the intellect. That three gods are one and that one is three no longer had to make sense. Why? Because spirituality had become so important to them that they shut the door on the intellect entirely. So even today, if you ask them—and these are very intelligent priests, with doctorates in the sciences and in religion—if you ask them about the Trinity, or how the blood of Christ saves them from all their sins, which of course makes no sense from a logical point of view, they will say, "This is the mystery of faith." In other words, when it comes to certain matters, they have shut off their minds completely.

At the opposite extreme, Allah describes the people of the Children of Israel in the Quran: their minds are very sharp, but their hearts have grown hard. ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةًۭ ۚ Their hearts become like stones, even harder than stones. When they saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), they recognized him at once—that he was the one described in our books, that all the signs we have studied in our books point to the fact that this is, in truth, the messenger of Allah. Now, it takes a very intelligent person to work that out. Yet they said, "We will not believe in him. We will not accept his religion." So where does the problem lie this time? Not in the intellect, but in the heart. For the Christian community the problem became a lack of intellect, and for the Children of Israel the problem was a lack of heart.

But we Muslims are a community of balance. We are people of sound hearts and sound intellects alike. We are not blind followers. Allah did not invite us to His religion with our eyes closed. قُلْ هَذِهِۦ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَة Say to them, my messenger: This is the path I call to with open eyes, with insight. Beautiful words! I call to Allah with my eyes open! Baseerah—baseerah in Arabic is when you have a full and complete view of something. According to the Arabic lexicon, if there is any obstacle in my sight—a pillar, a table, anything that blocks my direct or peripheral view—that is not called baseerah. Baseerah means a complete, unhindered view. Allah commands the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) to say: This is the true path of Islam. I call to it with my eyes open! With baseerah! With insight!

Do you know what that means? It means that we have a full understanding of why we are Muslims. Not merely that we are Muslims, but that we must also understand why we are Muslims. Why do we say La ilaha illa Allah? What does it mean to say Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasul Allah? What does it mean to say Mawlana Ali Wali Allah? What is this message of Allah?

So many Muslims today are Muslims only because their parents are Muslims. You ask them, why are you a Muslim? And they say, because my parents are Muslims, or because I was raised in a Muslim country, or because everyone around me is Muslim, I suppose. These are not good answers! These are not good answers to that question. قُلْ هَذِهِۦ سَبِيلِىٓ أَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۚ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۠ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِى I call to Allah with my eyes open—I and whoever follows me! Our faith is different. Our faith is different.

When others ask us why we follow Islam, our answer is not, "I do not know—I simply do it; it is only our culture." Other religions may respond in that way; other religions may give such an answer, but we may not. We always have a reason for what we do, because we are not merely people of belief—we are also people of intellect. Our belief is supported by the reasoning of the mind. We are not blind; we are people of baseerah, of inner sight! Unlike every other religion, our deen invites us to think; it invites us to ponder.

افلا تعقلون ؟ أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ؟ أَفَلَا تَتَفَكَّرُونَ؟ أَفَلَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ أَفَلَا تَسْمَعُونَ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ

Why do you not think? Why do you not ponder? Why do you not reflect? Why do you not listen? Why do you not see?

كِتَبٌ أَنزَلْنَهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَرَكٌۭ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓا۟ آيَتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَبِ

A book we have revealed to you so that people may ponder over its messages, and so that those with intellect may take heed.

So we must study our religion, and we must study this astonishing book. This book, this Quran, holds the answers to all our questions! Hazrat Abdullah and Hazrat Ibrahim (عطا اللہ بقاھم) have said on many occasions that we labor to learn taveel and haqaiq, yet the greatest book of all haqaiq sits on the shelf of every Muslim home—and that is the Quran.

And with this book as well—this is not the first time you have heard how remarkable this Quran is and how it holds every answer, is it? But what language must you know in order to understand this book? Arabic! Yet you do not know Arabic, so how are you to follow a book you do not understand? Well, the obvious answer to that is: then learn Arabic! But in practical terms, no one is going to devote five or six years of his life to learning Arabic first, merely to understand the Quran. I have studied Arabic for fourteen years and I still know hardly anything. So that, too, becomes an impossible option, does it not?

There is Islam, then Iman, and then Ehsan. Ehsan is defined as:

أَن تَعبُدَ اللہَ کَأَنَّکَ تَراَہُ ، فَأِن لَّم تَکُن تَراہُ فَاِنَّہُ یَریٰ

کُلُّ أِناَءٍ بِمَا فِیہِ یَنضَا

A container gives out what it contains.

الحکمۃ ضالۃ المومن فأِنیّٰ وَجَدَھَا فَھُوَ أَحَقُّ بِھَا

Wisdom is the lost beast of a momin..... wherever he sees it, he has a right to it......

العَبدُ عَبدٌ وَ أِن تَرَقّٰی وَ الرَّبُّ رَبٌّ وِ أِن تَنَزَّل

A slave remains a slave no matter how high he goes..... A master remains a master no matter how low he comes.

The Rasul goes up to Sidratul Muntaha..... the highest place possible..... he is still a slave...... Allah comes to the lowest heaven every night..... no matter how low he comes down, He is still master.....

وقال وهب بن منبه أوحى الله إلى نبي من أنبياء بني إسرائيل - يقال له شعياء - أن قم في بني إسرائيل فإني سأطلق لسانك بوحي . فقام فقال يا سماء اسمعي ، ويا أرض انصتي ، فإن الله يريد أن يقضي شأنا ويدبر أمرا هو منفذه ، إنه يريد أن يحول الريف إلى الفلاة ، والآجام في الغيطان ، والأنهار في الصحاري ، والنعمة في الفقراء ، والملك في الرعاة ، ويريد أن يبعث أميا من الأميين ، ليس بفظ ولا غليظ ولا سخاب في الأسواق ، لو يمر إلى جنب السراج لم يطفئه من سكينته ، ولو يمشي على القصب اليابس لم يسمع من تحت قدميه . أبعثه مبشرا ونذيرا ، لا يقول [ ص 77 ] الخنا ، أفتح به أعينا عميا ، وآذانا صما ، وقلوبا غلفا ، وأسدده لكل أمر جميل ، وأهب له كل خلق كريم ، وأجعل السكينة لباسه ، والبر شعاره ، والتقوى ضميره ، والحكمة منطقه ، والصدق والوفاء طبيعته ، والعفو والمعروف خلقه ، والحق شريعته ، والعدل سيرته ، والهدى إمامه ، والإسلام ملته ، وأحمد اسمه ، أهدي به بعد الضلالة ، وأعلم به من الجهالة ، وأرفع به بعد الخمالة ، وأعرف به بعد النكرة ، وأكثر به بعد القلة وأغني به بعد العيلة ، وأجمع به بعد الفرقة ، وأؤلف به بين أمم متفرقة ، وقلوب مختلفة ، وأهواء متشتتة ، وأستنقذ به فئاما من الناس عظيما من الهلكة ، وأجعل أمته خير أمة أخرجت للناس ، يأمرون بالمعروف ، وينهون عن المنكر ، موحدين مؤمنين مخلصين ، مصدقين بما جاءت به رسلي . رواه ابن أبي حاتم .

القَرد فِی عَینِ أُمِّہِ غِزَالْ

A monkey in the eyes of its mother is a gazelle.

body.chapter: سلام علی رسول اللہ و آلہ
body.text_en:
Based on your text, it appears that you have written an introduction for a speech or a sermon (khutbah) in Arabic, containing praises of Allah, salutations upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his family, and a supplication. It includes several Qur'anic verses and phrases drawn from hadith. I have corrected the spelling and the grammar, applied the proper diacritical marks (tashkeel), and supplied a few missing words so that the text reads more naturally and more accurately.

Corrected and Vocalized Arabic Text

Praise and Testimonies

اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ؛ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ. وَهُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ، وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ. اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ مُوجِدِ الْوُجُودِ مِنْ عَدَمٍ غَيْرِ مَوْجُودٍ، وَمُقِيمِ مَرَاتِبِ الْحُدُودِ، تَفَضُّلًا وَإِنْعَامًا عَلَى مَنْ دَنَا. اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ لِيَكُونَ لِلْعَالَمِينَ نَذِيرًا. اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ الَّذِي هَدَانَا لِهَٰذَا، وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهْتَدِيَ لَوْلَا أَنْ هَدَانَا اللّٰهُ. وَنَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللّٰهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَنَشْهَدُ أَنَّ سَيِّدَنَا مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، وَنَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مَوْلَانَا عَلِيًّا وَصِيُّهُ وَوَزِيرُهُ. وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْخَلْقِ وَنُورِ الْعَرْشِ، أَفْضَلِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَالْمُرْسَلِينَ، وَأَشْرَفِ الْمُوَحِّدِينَ، حَبِيبِنَا وَسَيِّدِنَا وَسَنَدِنَا وَشَفِيعِنَا أَبِي الْقَاسِمِ مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى أَخِيهِ وَصِيِّهِ وَوَزِيرِهِ، أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، الْأَنْزَعِ الْبَطِينِ، وَيَعْسُوبِ الدِّينِ، غَالِبٍ عَلَى كُلِّ غَالِبٍ، مَطْلُوبِ كُلِّ طَالِبٍ، مَوْلَانَا عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، وَعَلَى الْأَئِمَّةِ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِمُ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ، اَلْخُلَفَاءِ الرَّاشِدِينَ، آلِ طه وَيٰس. اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ فِي كُلِّ وَقْتٍ وَكُلِّ أَوَانٍ وَعَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ؛ عَدَدَ مَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى مَنْ صَلَّيْتَ عَلَيْهِ؛ وَأَضْعَافَ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ بِالْأَضْعَافِ الَّتِي لَا يُحْصِيهَا غَيْرُكَ.

اَللّٰهُمَّ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ. اَللّٰهُمَّ عَلِّمْنَا بِمَا يَنْفَعُنَا، وَانْفَعْنَا بِمَا عَلَّمْتَنَا. اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ لَا يَنْفَعُ، وَمِنْ قَلْبٍ لَا يَخْشَعُ، وَمِنْ عَيْنٍ لَا تَدْمَعُ، وَمِنْ نَفْسٍ لَا تَشْبَعُ، وَمِنْ دَعْوَةٍ لَا يُسْتَجَابُ لَهَا، وَمِنْ مُنْكَرَاتِ الْأَخْلَاقِ وَالْأَعْمَالِ وَالْأَهْوَاءِ.

فَأَمَّا بَعْدُ... يَقُولُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ، بَعْدَ أَنْ نَقُولَ ("أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ." رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي، وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي، وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي، يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي. رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا. رَبِّ يَسِّرْ وَلَا تُعَسِّرْ وَتَمِّمْ بِالْخَيْرِ. اَللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْنَا عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ بِلَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَاللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنَا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ، وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ. آمِينَ يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ. اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللّٰهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ.)
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, to Whom Belongs the Dominion of the Heavens and the Earth, Who Gives Life and Death
body.topic_title_ur: الحمد للہ الذی لہ ملک السموات والارض یحی و یمیت

body.chapter: سلام علی رسول اللہ و آلہ
body.text_en:
الحَمْدُ للهِ الَّذِي لَا يَبْلُغُ مِدْحَتَهُ الْقَائِلُونَ، وَلَا يُحْصِي نَعْمَاءَهُ الْعَادُّونَ، وَلَا يُؤَدِّي حَقَّهُ الْمُجْتَهِدُونَ، الَّذِي لَا يُدْرِكُهُ بُعْدُ الْهِمَمِ، وَلَا يَنَالُهُ غَوْصُ الْفِطَنِ، الَّذِي لَيْسَ لِصِفَتِهِ حَدٌّ مَحْدُودٌ، وَلَا نَعْتٌ مَوْجُودٌ، وَلَا وَقْتٌ مَعْدُودٌ، وَلَا أَجَلٌ مَمْدُودٌ، فَطَرَ الْخَلَائِقَ بِقُدْرَتِهِ، وَنَشَرَ الرِّيَاحَ بِرَحْمَتِهِ، وَوَتَّدَ بِالصُّخُورِ مَيَدَانَ أَرْضِهِ.

وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَالْمُرْسَلِينَ، خَاتَمِ النَّبِيِّينَ، سَيِّدِنَا الْمُمَجَّدِ، الْبَشِيرِ الْمُصَدَّقِ، النَّذِيرِ الْمُؤَيَّدِ، الْمُصْطَفَى الْأَمْجَدِ، مَحْمُودٍ الْأَحْمَدِ، أَبِي الْقَاسِمِ مُحَمَّدٍ. وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى وَصِيِّهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، أَشْرَفِ الْوَصِيِّينَ وَأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا الْإِمَامِ الطَّيِّبِ صَاحِبِ الدَّعْوَةِ النَّبَوِيَّةِ، وَصَوْلَةِ الْحَيْدَرِيَّةِ، وَالْعِصْمَةِ الْفَاطِمِيَّةِ، وَالشَّجَاعَةِ الْحُسَيْنِيَّةِ، وَالْعُلُومِ الْبَاقِرِيَّةِ، وَالْمَعَاقِلِ الْجَعْفَرِيَّةِ، وَالْحِكْمَةِ الْإِسْمَاعِيلِيَّةِ، وَالْجُودِ الْمُحَمَّدِيَّةِ. فَصَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَعَلَى آلِهِمْ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا كَثِيرًا.

اللَّهُمَّ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَا إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَا، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ. اللَّهُمَّ عَلِّمْنَا بِمَا يَنْفَعُنَا، وَانْفَعْنَا بِمَا عَلَّمْتَنَا. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ لَا يَنْفَعُ، وَمِنْ قَلْبٍ لَا يَخْشَعُ، وَمِنْ عَيْنٍ لَا تَدْمَعُ، وَمِنْ نَفْسٍ لَا تَشْبَعُ، وَمِنْ دَعْوَةٍ لَا يُسْتَجَابُ لَهَا، وَمِنْ مُنْكَرَاتِ الْأَخْلَاقِ وَالْأَعْمَالِ وَالْأَهْوَاءِ. فَأَمَّا بَعْدُ، يَقُولُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ، بَعْدَ أَنْ نَقُولَ أَعُوذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ، بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ. رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي، وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي، وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي، يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي.

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَضِلَّ أَوْ أُضَلَّ، أَوْ أَزِلَّ أَوْ أُزَلَّ، أَوْ أَظْلِمَ أَوْ أُظْلَمَ، أَوْ أَجْهَلَ أَوْ يُجْهَلَ عَلَيَّ.

اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْنَا عِنْدَ الْمَوْتِ بِـ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ. وَاللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنَا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ، وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ. آمِينَ يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ.
body.topic_title_en: Beyond the Reach of All Praise

body.chapter: سلام علی رسول اللہ و آلہ
body.text_en:
الحمدُ للہِ خَالقِ الوُجودِ مِنَ العَدَم ، وَ جَاعِلِ النُّورِ مِنَ الظُّلَموَ مُخرِجِ الصَّبرِ مِنَ الاَلَم ، وَ مُلکِ التَّوبَۃِ عَلی النَّدَم

All praise belongs to Allah alone, who brought existence forth out of non-existence, and made light out of darkness, and drew patience out of pain, and granted the kingdom of forgiveness in return for remorse.

فَنَشکُرُہُ عَلیَ المصَائِبِ کما نَشکُرُہُ عَلی النِّعَم

We thank Him in our calamities just as we thank Him for His blessings.

وَ نُصَلِّی عَلی رَسُولِہِ الاکرَم ، لِشَّرَفِ الاَشَم ، وَ النُّورِ الاتَموَالکِتاَبِ المُحکَم ، وَ کمالِ النَّبِیِّنَ وَ الخَاتَم

And may the blessings of Allah be upon His most noble Messenger, for his towering honor, and his perfect light, and for the decisive Book; he who is the perfection of all the prophets and their jewel.

سَیِّدِی وَلَدِ آدَم ۔ اَلَّذِی بَشَّرَ بِہِ عِیسیَ ابْنُ مَریَموَ دَعَا لِبِعثَتِہِ اِبرَاھِیمُ عَلیہِ السَّلام ، حِینَ کاَنَ یَرفَعُ قَواَعِدَ بَیتِ اللہِ المحَّرم

The best of the children of Adam, the one whose coming Jesus foretold as glad tidings, and the one for whom Ibraheem AS prayed while he was raising the walls of the sacred House of God.

فَصَلَّ اللہ علیہ و آلہ و سلم ، و علی أَتباَعِہِ خَیرِ الاُمَمالَّذِینَ بَارکَ اللہُ بِہِم کاَفَّۃَ النَّاس العَرَبَ مِنھُم وَالعَجَم

May the blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny, and upon those who followed him as the best of nations; the one whom Allah sent as a blessing for all mankind, Arab and non-Arab alike.

و صل اللہ علی أمیر المؤمنین، الانزع البطین، وَ قائد الغر المحجلینغالب علی کل غالب، مطلوب کل طالب

And may the blessings of Allah be upon the Commander of the Faithful, highest in rank and deepest in knowledge, the leader of the horses with shining foreheads; the victor over every victor, and the ultimate desire of every seeker.

الحمد للہ ، الَّذِی أَنزَلَ عَلی عَبدِہِ الکتابَ وَلَم یَجعَل لَّہُ عِوَجَا

All praise belongs to Allah, who sent down the Book upon His servant and left no crookedness in it.

والحمد للہ ، الذی لم یتخذ ولداً ولم یکن لہ شریک فی الملکو لم یکن لہ ولی من الذل و کبرہ تکبیرا

All praise belongs to Allah, who has taken no son, who has no partner in His dominion, and who has no need of a protector out of weakness. Everything glorifies Him with the greatest glorification.

والحمد للہ ، الذی نَحمَدُہُ وَ نَستَعِینُہُ وَ نَستَغفِرُہُ وَ نُئمِنُ بِہِ وَ نَتَوَکَّلُ عَلَیہ

And praise belongs to Allah, whom we praise, from whom we seek help, and to whom we turn in repentance; in whom we believe and upon whom we depend.

و نغوذُ باللہ مِن شُرُورِ أَنفُسِنَا ، وَ مِن سَیِّئاَتِ اعمَالِنَا

And we seek refuge in Him from the evils of our souls and from the ugliness of our deeds.

مَن یَھدِہِ اللہُ فَلاَ مُضِلَّ لَہ وَ مَن یُضلِل فَلا ھادِیَ لَہ

The one whom Allah guides never goes astray, and the one whom He leaves to stray never finds guidance.

و نشھدُ ان لا الہ الا اللہ وحدہ لا شریک لہ

And we bear witness that there is no god but Allah.

body.chapter: سلام علی رسول اللہ و آلہ
body.text_en: He is one without any partners. و نشھد ان محمد عبدُ اللہ و رسولہ أَرسَلَہُ اللہُ تَعاَلی بِالھُدَی وَ دِینِ الَحقِّ لِیُظھِرَہُ عَلی الدِّینِ کُلِّہ ، وَ کفَا بِاللہِ شَھِیدَا And we bear witness that Muhammad (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) is His servant and His messenger. Allah sent him with guidance and the true religion so that the path would stand clearly revealed; and Allah is enough as a witness over that. و نشھد ان مولانا علی ابن ابی طالب، وصیہ و وزیرہ And we bear witness that Maulana Ali, son of Abu Talib, is his successor and his legate. فصل اللہ علیہم و علی آلہم و سَلِّمُھُم تَسلِیماً کثیراً کثیرا May the blessings and salutations of Allah descend upon them and upon their progeny, and may these blessings go on increasing in number forever. اللّٰھم لا عِلمَ لَنا اِلَّا ما عَلَّمتَنَا۔ أِنَّک أَنتَ العَلِیمُ الحکیم O Allah, we have no knowledge except that which You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the Most Wise. اللّٰھم عَلِّمنَا بِما یَنفَعْنَا ؛ وَ یَنفَعنَا بِمَا عَلَّمتَنَا O Allah, teach us what is of benefit to us, and grant us benefit from what You have taught us. اَللّٰھُمَّ اِنِّا نَعُوْذُ بِکَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ لاَّ یَنْفَعُ ، وَمِنْ قَلْبٍ لاَّ یَخْشَعُ وِ مِن عَینٍ لا تَدمَع ، وَمِنْ نَّفْسٍ لاَّ تَشْبَعُ O Allah, we seek refuge in You from knowledge that brings no benefit, and from a heart that does not fear You, and from eyes that shed no tears (in repentance), and from a soul that is never satisfied. فأما بعد ، یقول سبحانہ و تعالی فی کتابہ الکریم ، بعد أَقولُ أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم Allah says in the noble Quran, (and I say this) after seeking refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: With the name of Allah, the intensely merciful, the constantly merciful. رب اشرحلی صدری و یسرلی أمری ۔ وحلل عقدۃ من لسانی یفقھو قولی Master, open my heart and make my task easy for me. Loosen the knots of my tongue so that I may speak clearly. اللہم ثَبِّتنا عِندَ الموتی بی لا الہ الا اللہ و اللھم جعلنا من الذین آمنو و عمل الصالحات و تواصو بالحق وتواصو بالصبر O Allah, at the hour of our death, keep us firm upon the belief that there is no god but Allah. O Allah, make us of those who believe, and do good deeds, and counsel one another to the truth, and counsel one another to patience. آمین یا رب العلمین

body.text_en:
الہ — a generic term, closest to the word God. It is a very rich word, and it carries a whole range of meanings.

An entity that is worthy of worship. A deity. An object of devotion and love. Someone you turn to in desperate times. Someone you are so passionately in love with that you cannot stop thinking about that person.

Literally it means: something you lean on. When you are exhausted and you lean on something, that thing is literally called الہ.

The word love is already embedded in the word ilah.

body.chapter: سلام علی رسول اللہ و آلہ
body.text_en:
الحمد للہِ صَانِعِ الخَلقِ عَلی أکمَلِ نِظَام وَ أَحسِنِ قَوام
All praise is for Allah, who fashioned creation upon the most perfect order and the most beautiful form.

الواَضِعِ الاَشیَاءِ فی أَشْدَرِ مُقَام و أرْفَقِ مَصاَم
Who placed all things in their rightful station and their most fitting place.

والحمد للہ عدد خلقُہُ و زِ یْنَۃُ العرشہ و مِدادُ کلماتہ ومنتھی علمُہُ و جَمِیع ما شاء و خَلَقَ وَ بَرَأَ

وھو عالم الغیب و الشھادۃ، الرحمن الرحیم، المالک القدوس العزیز الحکیم

والصلواۃ و السلام علی المُؤَیِّدِ أَبلَغِ الکَلام
And blessings and salutations be upon the one who was supported with the most eloquent speech,

مُحمدٍ المَبعُوثْ صلی اللہ علیہ و علی آلہ و سلَّم
Muhammad, who was sent forth — may the blessings of all be upon him and upon his progeny —

لِھِدایَۃِ کَافَّۃِ أَنَام اِلی سُبُلِ السَّلام و الی مَدَیٰ الَّیاَلِ وَ الأَیَّامْ
for the guidance of all mankind toward the paths of peace, and for as long as the nights and the days endure.

الذی أَرسَلَہُ اللہُ تَعاَلی بِالھُدَی وَ دِینِ الَحقِّ لِیُظھِرَہُ عَلی الدِّینِ کُلِّہ، وَ کفَا بِاللہِ شَھِیدَا
All praise belongs to Allah, who has taken no son, and who has no partner in His dominion, and who has no need of a protector out of weakness. Everything glorifies Him with the greatest of glorifications.

و نشھدُ ان لا الہ الا اللہ وحدہ لا شریک لہ
And we testify that there is no god but Allah. He is one, without any partner.

و نشھد ان محمد عبدُ اللہ و رسولہ
And we testify that Muhammad (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) is His servant and His messenger.

و نشھد ان مولانا علیاً، وصیہ و وزیرہ
And we testify that Maulana Ali, son of Abu Talib, is his successor and his legatee.

فصل اللہ علیہم و علی آلہم و سَلِّمُھُم تَسلِیماً کثیراً کثیرا
May the blessings and salutations of Allah descend upon them and upon their progeny, and may these blessings keep increasing in number forever.

اللّٰھم لا عِلمَ لَنا اِلَّا ما عَلَّمتَنَا۔ أِنَّک أَنتَ العَلِیمُ الحکیم
O Allah, we have no knowledge except that which You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the Most Wise.

اللّٰھم عَلِّمنَا بِما یَنفَعْنَا؛ وَ یَنفَعنَا بِمَا عَلَّمتَنَا
O Allah, teach us what is of benefit to us, and benefit us through what You have taught us.

اللھم آتنا نُفُوسِنَا تَقوَاھا وَ زَکَّنا فأنت خیرُ من زَکَّاھا۔
O Allah, grant piety to our souls, and purify them, for You are the best of purifiers.
O Allah, grant our souls protection and cleanse them, for You are in the best position to purify our souls.
You are our protective and protecting friend.

أنت وَلِیُّنا و مولانا و نعم المولی و نعم النصیر۔
You are our friend and our guardian, and the best of friends and the best of helpers.

ولا حول ولا قوۃ الا باللہ العلی العظیم
And there is no power and no strength except by Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent.

فأما بعد، یقول سبحانہ و تعالی فی کتابہ الکریم، بعد أَقولُ أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم
Allah says in the noble Qur'an — and I say this after seeking refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan — with the name of Allah, the intensely merciful, the constantly merciful.

رب اشرحلی صدری و یسرلی أمری۔ وحلل عقدۃ من لسانی یفقھو قولی
My Master, open my heart and make my task easy for me. Remove the knots from my tongue so that I am able to speak clearly.

body.text_en:
Why do I see religious elders, men who speak of the ideal character of Islam, behaving in ways that contradict the teachings of Islam? Should they not be the ones who lead by example? If these learned people cannot act upon these teachings, what chance do I have?

Do you remember that conversation I had in one of my sessions, where I compared the rules of Islam to the rules of a video game? Do you remember it? I showed you that Islam resembles an online multiplayer role-playing video game. We are all players in the game. We have a system for scoring points, called sawaab, and a system for losing points, called "gunaah."

In a game there are always certain potions, certain swords, certain shields — various things we collect at every level that give us great rewards. These acquisitions help us move on to the next level. In Islam we collect those points through actions such as namaaz, roza, hajj, and zakaat.

In the same way, a game contains certain poisons, certain traps, and certain poor choices that make us lose points, or even get us killed, so that we must begin all over again. In Islam these are acts such as lying, cheating, gossip, slander, and emotional and verbal abuse, which make us lose points. Then there are also the major sins, such as smoking, drinking alcohol, taking drugs, adultery, and murder, which can cause severe damage.

Every game has a final level, an ultimate purpose, an ultimate success, where you attain the final aim of that game. You get to meet the BIG BOSS and win the final prize. In Islam that BIG BOSS is Allah, and that final, eternal prize is Jannah. That is what this game is being played for.

So, to oversimplify greatly, we are playing this game of Islam. We are all players in this game, and we are playing alongside, or against, other players at the same time. Each person is playing the same game, but at various different levels.

Now, every game has a rule book, does it not? Something that sets out the rules of the game. And these rules are a list of DOs and DON'Ts, are they not? Do this, and this is the reward you receive. Do not do this, or this bad thing will happen to you.

Now let us say you have just bought the latest game from the store. When you unwrap it, you see that the rule book for this game is printed in Chinese, and you cannot read Chinese. So how do you play the game now? One way is that you simply improvise. You begin playing and work it out as you go along. But how far do you think that approach will carry you?

The second way is that you find somebody else who knows the same game. Let us say I am that person. You discover that I have actually read the rule book. I have mastered it. I know all the rules: what to do, what not to do, what things to collect, what to avoid. Very well. So now you are watching me play the game, and on the basis of how you see me playing, what do you assume? That this is how the game is meant to be played.

For the sake of our discussion, do you yourself know the rules of the game? No. But do you believe that I know the rules of the game? Yes. So now you watch me playing the game. You see what I do and you see what I avoid, and you say, ah, very well, these must be the rules of the game. You assume this quite naturally. Because you do not know the rules of the game, and you believe that I do know the rules, therefore whatever you see me doing, what do you assume?

These must be the rules of the game. Now what happens when you see me do something wrong, something I am not supposed to do? Whom do you blame? You cannot blame me, because you believe that I know the rules. And if I know the rules and still do this, then where must the fault lie? In the game itself. Do you understand?

So you end up saying: this game is stupid, it makes no sense, there is a flaw in its design.

The Qur'an is the rule book of Islam. It is the book of guidance that contains all the things to do and all the things not to do. Do we understand the Qur'an? Have we studied it as we ought to have studied it? No. So what do we do? We begin to follow the people who have read it and understood it. Correct? But when we see them do something unIslamic, whom do we generally end up blaming? Islam. We blame the game and not the player.

If someone cheats at cricket, or cheats at basketball, does that mean the game is bad? Of course not. It is the player. But what do we normally end up saying? This game is worthless. I am never going to watch cricket again. It is so depressing.

So we truly need to begin by understanding this fundamental idea: the difference between the game and the player. Islam is the game. Muslims, momins, mullas, manaseebs, they are all the players. If you see a fault in the player, the first rule is this: do not blame the game.

Now, is it possible that you are not seeing the wisdom behind a decision an elder is taking? It is possible. How can you make yourself able to see that wisdom? Learn the rules of the game yourself. So study the rule book first. Study the rules of the game before you form a judgment about others.

Now, if you have studied the book and you clearly see another person doing something wrong, even a person in a position of authority, then it is the player and not the game that is making that error. Do not confuse the actions of the player with the game. There are thousands of people acting barbarically in the name of Islam. That does not mean Islam is bad. It only means that the player is bad.

If you want to see the example of a perfect player playing the game, read the seerah of Rasul Allah. Read the seerah of Maulana Ali, Maulatina Fatima, Hassan, and Hussain (علھیم السلام). Only there will you see the perfection of this game. So if you want to study the players, those are the players you want to study, and no one else.

Now as for the question: if these people of knowledge cannot act upon these teachings, what chance do I have? Well, the first thing is that each of us has to play this game individually.

كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌۭ

Everyone is associated with his own actions.

مَّنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌۭ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ

Whoever is guided is only guided for the benefit of his soul. And whoever errs only errs against it. And none will bear the burden of another.

So do not worry about them. Do not compare yourself to anyone. You begin at the level you are comfortable with and progress from there. You do not have to begin at anyone else's level. Begin where you feel comfortable. You do not have to go to extremes. If you feel you can manage only one namaaz in a day, begin with one namaaz in a day, then move on to two, then to three. If you feel you can do only the farz, then do only the farz. Begin wherever you think you can.

That is not the problem. The problem arises when you become stagnant at the same level. As long as you are moving forward and making improvements, you will eventually reach the next level. I began with one namaaz a day, only the fajr, because I was always an early riser. And today I am wherever I am. But do something. Do not simply do nothing at all.

To return to the example of a video game: it would not make much sense to keep playing at the same level, would it? You want to move on to the next level. Yet you cannot begin at the final level either, for you would not survive there for long. So that is the first thing. Begin where you are comfortable and advance from there.

Second, do not trouble yourself over what others are doing, over whether they are good Muslims or not, over whether they are acting according to Shareeah or not. You are not responsible for them. مَّنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِى لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا ۚ The one who does good does it for his own benefit; the one who does not is responsible for his own harm. All you have to do is concern yourself with yourself, with taking yourself to the next level, with planning your own advancement in this game of Islam. This game of Islam has been given to you so that you may play it and enjoy it, not so that you may judge how others are playing it.

If you see a great player and you draw inspiration from him, Hamdulillah, by all means do so. If you like the way someone plays the game and you wish to adopt his style, go ahead. And if you must judge others, then turn that judgment to your own advantage, to your own benefit. If you see a player making the wrong move, make sure that YOU are not making the same mistake, and correct yourself if you are. Do you understand?

Look at other players only to improve your own game, to judge your own game and not theirs. If you like something they are doing, adopt their skillful moves. If you see them doing something wrong, make sure you do not make the same wrong move. That is the essence of Islam.

Two seats remain open. Everyone is welcome to ask questions. I have prepared some images that I will send over WhatsApp. We are beginning our study of the message of the Qur'an, God willing.

God puts a few questions to us in the Qur'an:

أَم خُلق من غیر شئ ؟

Do you suppose that you came into being by accident? By yourself alone, with no creator?

An ancient belief has been passed down through the ages: that everything simply came into being on its own. There is this universal matter, this organic soup, that went on boiling and boiling, and then one day the frog leapt out. The universe burst open from a single point, and everything began to take shape entirely by itself. The sun grew hotter and hotter, the moon grew cooler and cooler, the winds began to blow, mountains began to form, the earth began to turn, oceans began to flow, flowers began to bloom, and plants began to grow.

So God asks us in the Qur'an: What do you think? Did all of this happen entirely by itself?

Allama Iqbal, a renowned poet of Pakistan, says that it is plainly impossible for things to create themselves. If a piece of steel is left in one place, even for hundreds of years, no one has ever seen it turn into daggers and swords on its own. If you wish to learn how to make a particular kind of candy, you need a confectioner to teach you how it is done. Raw material must be shaped into different forms, skills must be learned, and nothing in this universe can come about by itself.

So God asks us:

أَم خُلق من غیر شئ ؟

Do you truly think that you were created just like that, by accident? Then He asks:

أَم ھُمُ الخالقون ؟

Did you create yourself? The color of your eyes, the features of your face, your height, the shade of your skin, the family into which you were born, the country in which you were born—did you choose any of this?

And then a third question:

أَم خُلِق السموات والارض

Very well, set yourself aside for a moment. What of these heavens and this earth? These lofty skies above your head that provide your means of sustenance and make life possible for you, and this vast expanse beneath your feet that you explore and walk upon—did you create all of this?

If you have indeed created all of this—if you have created yourself and everything around you—then do as you please. No one will hold you to account for anything. Do good deeds, commit sins, build mosques, build temples, eat what is lawful or drink alcohol, worship stones—do whatever you desire. You are entirely free to do as you please. Only prove that you are the creator of everything, and then do whatever you wish; no one will question you about anything.

But if you cannot prove that you created all of this, then before you learn anything else—before you become a doctor, before you become an engineer, a lawyer, a psychologist, a mathematician, a computer engineer—before everything else, the very first thing you need to know, the very first thing you need to learn, is who created all of this that you see around you, and for whom He created it. Who created us? And why did He create us? What does He want from you?

Syedna Jaffar bin Syedna Suleman, may God sanctify his soul, says in his poems that the faith in a believer's heart is not complete until he understands four things: Where did man come from, and where will he return? And why was he sent into this world, and why is he returning?

So, even though these questions are rhetorical—

These are extremely important questions that God challenges us with. Have we been created only to eat, drink, bear children, and then die? If that were so, then animals do the same, so what would set us human beings apart from the animals? Are we meant to live the lives of animals, or is there a higher purpose?

To answer this question, let us consider the one essential difference between us and the animals. Did God give us something that He did not give the animals? He did. He blessed us with an intellect, العَقْلُ.

Al-Aql, in ancient Arabic, is used for two things. First, Aql is used for a container that can hold something; and second, Aql is used for a restraint, for the rope with which a camel is tied is called an عِقَال. Let us begin with the first sense, the container that can hold something, and we will discuss the other later, God willing.

So, linguistically, Aql basically means a container, does it not? What is truly interesting is that in Arabic it signifies a very flexible container, one that expands to fit its contents. The more you put into it, the more it stretches and expands to hold it; in other words, a container that grows as its contents increase. Do you understand? A fixed container, by contrast, one that does not expand, is called حاویۃ، أِناءَ، صندوق. These are containers that can hold only a set amount, but not Al-Aql. The more you store in Al-Aql, the more it expands to hold its contents. Is that clear?

So what is Aql a container for? What does it hold? It is a container for العِلْمُ, for knowledge. The more your knowledge expands, the more your intellect expands along with it, to hold that knowledge. And this is what we see in a child as he grows older: as he keeps taking in knowledge, his intellect keeps growing. Glory be to God!

Now, what is Ilm, or knowledge? Ilm in Arabic means the true quality of something, or the true reality of something, حقیقۃ الاشیاء. And the faculty that can not only store but also measure and distinguish between the qualities of things is called Aql, or intellect. So there are two things. There is Ilm, knowledge, which is the true reality of something; and then there is the container for that knowledge, which can store it, understand it, and apply logic and reasoning to it, which is Al-Aql, the intellect.

So gold is a valuable metal, and that is a reality; a rock is worthless, and that too is a reality. The intellect can not only store these realities as knowledge but can also compare and distinguish between the two. It can understand that gold is more valuable than rocks. And as knowledge grows, the intellect too expands to hold more of it. Are there any questions?

So God gave us this priceless gift of the intellect. In fact, it was the very first thing He created. There is a beautiful and profoundly deep Hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he said:

You see, the trouble is that all these worldly comforts can give ease to our bodies, but not to our hearts. The heart was never made for this world. Yet we constantly try to satisfy its needs with worldly possessions: money, fame, luxuries, jewelry, and glitter of every kind. But the heart's need is not physical in nature. The body's need is physical; the heart's need is spiritual. And until it finds the object of its search, the heart will always remain unsatisfied.

So then, what is the heart looking for? And how can it attain the satisfaction it longs for? Allah answers these questions very plainly in the Qur'an: أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ Beware! It is only in the remembrance of Allah that hearts find peace. Allah is the ultimate goal of hearts. Until it finds Allah, the heart does not find peace. As a fish out of water yearns to return to it, our hearts crave the love of Allah. As a man thirsty for water is satisfied by nothing else, distracted by nothing except water, so it is here: even if you give him the finest juices, the most delicious drinks, he still craves that cold sip of water that can put out his thirst completely. The heart cannot find satisfaction until it finds Allah.

So Allah asks all of us: أَم خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ Were you created out of nothing? أَمْ هُمُ الْخَالِقُونَ Did you create yourselves? أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ Did you create the heavens and the earth? If not, then the first responsibility I have as His creation is to find out who my creator is. And then to find out why He has created me, and what it is that He wants from me. Why did He create this world? Why did He create me and everyone in it? Then, what is this thing called death? Why do we die, even though I do not want to die? Who ever wishes to die? Who would desire to leave this vast enterprise that a person spends his whole life building up from the ground? So then, who is taking us away? Who is removing us against our will from our thrones and placing us under the ground? What happens after death? Where do we go? What is going to happen when we arrive there? Who are these prophets? Why have they been sent? And who sent them?

These are extremely important questions that we need to ask ourselves. These are extremely important truths that we need to understand. And the best place to find these answers is in the book sent down by the creator for His creation, which is the Qur'an. This book, the Qur'an, holds the answers to all our questions: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ Do you not see that they wander aimlessly in every valley? ھاما فی کل واد. Hama is used of a camel when it becomes lost in the desert looking for water. It goes into one valley, then another, then another, searching for water, wandering aimlessly in search of water. This is how Allah describes those who wander about trying to find a connection somewhere else.

Do artists have power? More than they realize. They have the power to affect thousands upon thousands of minds.

What you are listening to is shaping your thoughts, and your thoughts are shaping your conduct and your speech. Whatever you take in is what will come out of you. کُلُّ أِناَءٍ بِمَا فیہِ یَنضَا — every vessel exudes what is inside it. If we constantly take in filth, what is going to come out of us? The same filth. That is what will happen. Whatever goes in eventually comes out.

The Qur'an gives us roads to conviction. How is a person to become absolutely certain that this is the truth, that this is a revelation from Allah? The first step is this: does a God in fact exist? Is there in fact an Ilah? How does one arrive at the absolute conviction that this is so, that it is not a theory, not a theology, but an absolute fact?

The Qur'an's argument is that if people genuinely reflect upon the creation around them, there is no way they will arrive at any other conclusion. That is the Qur'an's argument.

إِنَّ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱخْتِلَفِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ لَآيَتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَبِ

Verily, in the heavens and the earth, and the changing of night and day, there are miraculous signs for those of intellect.

What is an ayah? What does a sign mean? Consider the relation of the sign to the intellect. In other words, Allah did not even use revelation to prove His existence. Allah did not use the Qur'an to prove His existence. Interestingly enough, the proof of Allah's existence is not in the Qur'an. Allah never speaks of the proof of His existence in the Qur'an. It is not even a subject there. If an atheist asks, "Show me a surah in which Allah proves that He exists," we cannot do that. I do not have one.

What doubt does the Qur'an address? Whether or not this is revelation. ذلک الکتاب لا ریب فیہ. Nowhere in the Qur'an does Allah say ذلک الألہ لا ریب فیہ. It is not a discussion in the Qur'an, because Allah's declaration in the Qur'an is that you already have another set of ayat, another set of signs, that will bring you to that conclusion. You do not need these ayat in My book for that. Look around you. Look at all the signs I have placed all around you; those will bring you to that conclusion of their own accord.

What are those signs? The skies, the earth, the mountains, the clouds, the breeze, the rain, the plants, the animals — all of this will bring you to that conclusion if you reflect seriously and honestly. It will become very hard for you to say that this is the product of an accident. Nobody in their right mind will be able to say that all of this is part of an accident. People cannot explain simple things such as beauty. Why would beauty exist as part of an accident? Why would delicious taste exist as part of an accident? Why would that exist? How would that make any sense?

How would symmetry exist in the universe as part of an accident? Take a little snowflake — why does it have such incredibly artistic symmetry? We have super-expensive chandeliers designed with inspiration drawn from it. How could that be merely because of an accident? It ought to be chaos; it ought to be all mangled and twisted. Why is it so beautiful? SubhanAllah! Look at the symmetry in a leaf. Just examine it — how the left side mirrors the right side. How could this be an accident?

You know how you walk into the store, pick up the iPhone 6 or the Samsung Galaxy, and admire it. So sleek, so beautiful, amazing symmetry. Who is the designer? Who is the manufacturer? That leaf is Allah's design.

He is the maker of that leaf. Look at it! Appreciate it. It gives you something else. Think about the phones too. Did the iPhone come together as the result of an accident? Did the flip phones, over time, all on their own, by some cosmic accident, evolve into the iPhone 6? No. Someone designed the flip phone, and someone designed the iPhone. Now, if you cannot believe that a simple device like a phone could come together by some accident, then ask yourself this as you reflect on this vast universe: did these entire universes come into being by an accident?

Seriously, if you ever have a crisis of faith, simply step out of your home and examine the nature around you. Reflect upon it. For a Muslim there is no greater exercise in increasing faith than reflecting on nature. SubhanAllah! You can speak to Allah through a flower. You can speak to Allah through the bark of a tree. Even the breeze you feel on your face reminds you of Allah. This is the true Muslim life. You do not really have to be sitting in these Sunday sessions or in any Islamic lecture to experience faith. You only have to pay attention to the world around you. You only have to pay attention to the signs Allah creates for you everywhere.

This is so beautiful. Such amazing symmetry. The verses in the Qur'an are called ayaat. These ayaat of the Qur'an push you outside to examine the ayaat beyond the Qur'an, and the ayaat that lie outside push you back to the Qur'an to understand the one the signs are pointing to. SubhanAllah. The book drives us to look at the world, and the world drives us back to look into the book. The Qur'an, as the center of the circle, pushes us out into the universe, all the way to the circumference of the circle, and everything inside the circle pushes us back to the center. SubhanAllah. How amazing is that? We are constantly moving back and forth between the book and the universe. Our entire life is a passage from one set of signs to another set of signs, back and forth.

On the Day of Judgment Allah will say to the disbelievers: Did you not feel the wind? The soft breeze on your face? فلملکیات ذکرا۔ عذرا و نظرا Allah says the winds are My reminder. You and I think that these sessions, these gatherings, these lessons are our reminders. Allah says in the Qur'an that the wind is enough as My reminder. عذرا اور نظرا. The wind will be enough for them to say, "I am willing to change, Master. I recognize and submit to Your power." It is as though the wind were a slap on their face to make them set themselves right. They experience faith simply by experiencing the breeze on their face. Wow!

And the one who becomes conscious of these inner and outer signs, what happens to him? فزادتھم ایمانٌ He experiences an increase in faith. His faith increases. His faith grows strong. سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَتِنَا فِى ٱلأٓفَاقِ وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ شَهِيدٌ In the near future We will show them Our signs in the horizons and in their own souls. This whole imagery is drawn from desert life. أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ مِهَدًۭا Did We not make the earth a cradle? The word mihaad comes from the word mahd, which means a cradle. When a mother holds her baby in her arms, it is called a mahd, comforting it, its neck supported, its back not bent over.

She cradles the child perfectly, for the comfort of her child. Allah says: I made the whole world a mihaad for you. The most beautiful image of sleep is the image of a child, is it not? Allah says: I made the whole world as comfortable for you as a mother's cradle. What bedding could you set against it? وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًۭا And the mountains as pegs. So the mother cradles the baby, and then she walks into her tent. What holds the tent together? The pegs — the awtaad. Allah says: look at your pegs and compare them to My tents. And, by the way, what shape are tents? They are shaped like mountains. Allah says: look at your tents, and look at Mine. This is what you made; this is what I made. I pegged mountains into this earth so that you would stand in awe. This is how you construct, and this is how Allah constructs. Who do you think you are?

اول ما خلق اللہُ العقل، فقال لہ اقبل فاقبل، و قال لہ ادبر فادبر
فقال لہ اللہ تبارک و تعاليٰ: و عزتي و جلالي ما خلقت خلقاً اعظم منک ولا اَطوعُ منک
بک أُبدي و أُعيد، لک الثواب و عليک العقاب

The first thing God created was the intellect. Then He commanded it to come forward, and it came forward. He then commanded it to move back, and it moved back. Now, what does it mean to move forward and to move back? Freedom of choice!

Allah gave the intellect complete freedom of choice — to do good, or to do evil; to accept or to refuse; to obey or to disobey; to eat what is lawful or to eat what is forbidden; to submit or to resist. Allah gave the intellect complete freedom of choice. فقال لہ اقبل فاقبل، و قال لہ ادبر فادبر Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said to it: و عزتي و جلالي ما خَلَقْتَ خلقاً أعظمُ منک ولا أَطوعُ منک By my strength and my majesty! I have not created anything greater than you, ولا اَطوعُ منک nor have I created anything more obedient than you. بک أُبدي و أُعيد Through you I begin creation, and through you that creation will return to me. لک الثواب و عليک العقاب Because of your good decisions they will be rewarded, and because of your bad decisions they will be punished. Glory be to Allah!

And then the Messenger of Allah (SAS) said: اول ما خلق اللہُ العقل ۔ فقال لہ اقبل فاقبل و قال لہ ادبر فادبر فقال لہ اللہ تبارک و تعاليٰ: و عزتي و جلالي ما خلقت خلقاً اعظم منک ولا اَطوعُ منک بک أُبدي و أُعيد، لک الثواب و عليک العقاب ۔ تشعب من العقل الحلم ، و من الحلم العلم، و من العلم الرشد، و من الرشد العفاف و من العفاف الصيانة، و من الصيانة الحيائ، ومن الحياء الرَّزانة من الرَّزانة المَداَوِمَةِ عليٰ الخير ، و کراھية الشر، و من کراھية الشر طاعة الناصح فھذہ عشرة اصناف من انواع الخير، و لکل واحد من ھذہ العشرة الاصناف، عشرة انواع

تشعب من العقل الحلم — from the intellect, forbearance was created; و من الحلم العلم — and forbearance created knowledge; و من العلم الرشد — and knowledge created guidance; و من الرشد العفاف — and guidance created virtue; و من العفاف الصيانة — and virtue created safeguarding; و من الصيانة الحيائ — and safeguarding created modesty; ومن الحياء الرزانة — and modesty created dignity; و من الرزانة المداومة عليٰ الخير و کراھية الشر، — and dignity created the love of good and the loathing of evil; و من کراھية الشر طاعة الناصح — and the one who loathed evil became obedient to the counselor. فھذہ عشرة اصناف من انواع الخير، و لکل واحد من ھذہ العشرة الاصناف عشرة انواع — These are ten characteristics from among the categories of good, and for every one of these ten characteristics, there are ten further characteristics.

So through the creation of the intellect, these ten primary qualities were created: forbearance, knowledge, guidance, virtue, safeguarding, modesty, dignity, attraction toward good, and repulsion from evil; and this distinction between good and evil led the intellect to become obedient to the one giving counsel. So the final purpose, the fruit of the intellect, is obedience. Obedience to whom? To the one giving counsel, to the one providing guidance — the message and the messenger! Obedience to the Qur'an and the Messenger of Allah (SAS). So obedience is the purpose of the intellect!

Any questions?

But we know that even animals have some lower form of intellect, because even they can distinguish between good and bad. If you set stale, dried-up grass before a goat, and then at a short distance you set some fresh grass, it will ignore the dry grass and eat the fresh grass, because it can tell good from bad. If you place raw meat and cooked meat before a lion, it will eat the raw meat, even though both are meat. So animals too can distinguish.

So then what is the difference in intellect between us and them? Imam Jaffar al-Sadiq (AS) defined human intellect as a faculty that can not only distinguish between good and bad, but can also distinguish between two goods and between two evils.

When faced with two goods, it can choose the greater good, and when faced with two evils, it can choose the lesser evil. And it is on the basis of this discernment — this ability to choose between two goods and between two evils — that man has made all the progress we see in the world today. This is something only human beings can do; animals cannot. That is why the intellect is the greatest gift Allah has bestowed upon His creation, and it was given for the sake of obedience.

Lastly, aql also means a restraint. It is the rope used to tie a camel. عقل البعیر literally means the tying of the camel, and the rope used to tie it is called an عِقَال. So the intellect is also a restraint — a restraint for what? For the soul. What happens when the camel is tied to a post? Its movement becomes limited. It can now move only within the boundary permitted by the length of the rope.

So the intellect is a restraint for the soul, one that lets it establish a fixed boundary for itself and move or act only within that boundary — the boundary of what is permissible. Everything within the boundary is permitted, and everything outside it is not. The soul can hold itself within this boundary by means of the intellect.

None of what we have discussed so far has anything to do with Islam yet. This is not something particular to Muslims; it applies to all human beings in general. So what have we learned about the intellect up to now? It is a container that holds knowledge and expands as knowledge increases. It was the first thing Allah created, and He gave it complete freedom of choice. It was created for the sake of obedience. It is a scale, a meezaan, that can distinguish between two goods and two evils. And it is a restraint, a boundary of what is acceptable for the soul, which the soul can use to stop itself from wrongdoing.

Now let us look at this in action. Let us do an exercise together. Going to the movies, or standing in namaaz — both are good. Which one do you think I will choose, and why? The movie is good for two reasons: first, its reward is visible; second, it is immediately at hand — it is close, and I can enjoy it right now. Namaaz, on the other hand: first, its reward is not visible, because I will not see it until I die; second, it is not immediately at hand — I have to wait fifty or seventy years before I can reach it. So which one do I choose?

You see, the human intellect will always choose what it believes is beneficial for its soul. To the intellect, what is visible and immediately at hand is always better than what is invisible and far off. That is why it is so easy to choose this world over the hereafter, duniya over aakhira. And that is in fact what the word duniya means in classical Arabic. It comes from the word دنی, which means something that is close, and it also means something that is inferior, أدنی. This is why the life of this world is called حیاۃ الدنیا, the inferior life. We think it means the life of this world, but linguistically it actually means the inferior life. Why? Because if there is an inferior life, then by contrast there must be a superior life, حیاۃ الآخرۃ. The word آخرۃ comes from the word خیر, which means good or superior. When you add a ta marboota at the end of it, as in the word آخرۃ, it means the best of the best. SubhanAllah. You see how beautiful the Arabic language is?

So anything in duniya is low and inferior; however,

it is always visible and near at hand. And to the intellect, what is visible and near at hand is a bargain worth taking. People find beauty in the love of that which they desire — of women, and sons, mountains of gold and silver, fine branded horses and cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of this worldly, inferior life; but what Allah has with Him is the best of returns.

So what, then, can change our perspective? What can turn our perspective so that we see the Hereafter as the thing visible and near at hand? What can make us see the Hereafter as gold and this world as mere rocks? What must we do in order to change our perspective? We must study the Qur'an. It is only through the study of this book that we will see what this world in reality is, and how superior the life of the Hereafter is. Only this book can help us keep our eyes on the prize, as they say.

This is no different from your life at school. The intelligent one, the one of intellect, fixes his attention on his education and delays his desire for fun and enjoyment until after he graduates. He keeps his eyes on the prize, on that degree that will earn him a good life. The one who is set on instant gratification, on the other hand, enjoys his way through school with fun and games, with parties, with alcohol and drugs; but what happens when it is time to graduate? He has nothing, and he spends the remainder of his life flipping burgers at McDonald's.

The life and the pleasures of this world are certainly within reach; they are right in front of you. All you have to do is stretch out your arm and take hold of them. But their pleasures are brief. This world is temporary, it is inferior, it is filled with losses and pain and misery. It is "Duniya," from the word "Danaa," which means inferior. The pleasures of the afterlife, however, never end; they are permanent — only happiness, only pleasure, happiness without end, pleasures forever growing. It is "Akhirah," from the word "Khair," meaning the best of the best.

That is why Maulana Ali (AS), in his final words — after he was struck by the sword of Ibn Muljim al-Laeen — gives counsel to his beloved sons, Imam Hassan and Hussain, and explains to them, as his last words, the inferiority and imperfection of this worldly life:

أَحیَ قَلبَکَ بِالمَوعِضَۃ، وَ نَوِّرہُ بِالحِکمَۃ، وَقوِّھِی بِالزُّھَد، وَذَلِّلہُ بِالمَوت، وَقَرِّرہُ بِالفَناَء،وحَزِّنہُ وَسُولَتَ الدَّھَر،وَتَقَلُّبَ الَّیالِی وَالأَیَّام ،  وأَعرِض علیهِ أخبارالماضین وذکرهُ بما أصابَ مَن کانَ قَبلُکَ مِن الاوَّلِین ۔ و سِر فِی دِیارِهِم فانْظُر فی آثارِهِم ۔مَا فَعَلُو؟ و أَینَ حَلُّو ؟ فأِنَّک تَریٰ قَد أَنتَقِلُو مِن دارِ الغُرور وَنَزلُو فی دَارِ الغُربۃ۔  فأِنَّ سِرتَک أحدِھِم۔ ولا تبع آخرتک بالدنیا ، بل بیع دنیا بآخرتک

Even if you do not understand what I have just recited, you can still take pleasure in the perfection and the beauty of the style of his words. But what I actually wished to share with you were these words:

ولا تبع آخرتک بالدنیا ، بل بیع دنیا بآخرتک

My sons, a day will soon come when, on the one hand, there will be this inferior world, and on the other hand you will have the afterlife. And you will find yourself in a dilemma: if you try to save the life of this world, you will end up losing the afterlife; and if you try to save your afterlife, you will lose your life in this world. When that day comes, save your afterlife.

and let go of the pleasures of this inferior world. ولا تبع آخرتک بالدنیا ، بل بیع دنیا بآخرتک If you must let go of this world, then let it go, because death will eventually snatch it away from you in any case. But never let go of your afterlife. Never let go of your afterlife.

Through the anguish of drinking poison and of their own beheading, and the beheading of the members of their family at Karbala, these final words of their father are being honored.

اول ما خلق اللہُ العقل And then what did He do? He tested it, to make certain that it was functioning properly. فقال لہ اقبل فاقبل، و قال لہ ادبر فادبر

Why do you suppose we commit bad deeds? أَم خُلق من غیر شئ ؟ Were you created for no reason at all? أَم ھُمُ الخالقون ؟ Have you created yourselves? أَم خُلِق السموات والارض Have you created the heavens and the earth?

So that we may think. So that we may reflect upon His signs in the universe and examine them, so that we may recognize His existence. So that we may conclude that this magnificent universe around us could not have come into being by itself. And supposing, for a moment, that it did come into being by itself, how has it been maintained for billions of years with no one to maintain it? If all of this is happening by itself, of its own free will, then why does the night not precede the day? Why does autumn not come immediately after spring? Why does water always fall from the sky? Why does the speed of the earth's rotation never vary? Why do the planets move so consistently and so uniformly within their orbits? Why do they never step out of them?

How can all of this order exist in the universe without someone imposing that order upon it? A child's tricycle cannot ride itself; the child has to ride it. And this vast, magnificent universe is functioning so perfectly all by itself? How is such a notion comprehensible, or even conceivable? It is logically impossible.
