So there has to be a creator who created you, me, and everything around us. There has to be a maintainer, a sustainer, who is controlling and maintaining everything around us. If the planets are bound within an orbit, then logically there has to be someone who bound them within their orbits. And even if it is gravity, there has to be someone who created gravity, someone who does not permit the value of that gravity to change.

There are these accusations against Islam that it is a very difficult religion. I want to tell you today that this accusation is not true. Islam is not a difficult religion. It is a very, very difficult one. I am joking. Islam is a religion of nature. It is called Deen Al-Fitrah, which means the religion of nature. God willing, as we proceed, you will see that everything about Islam is founded upon natural phenomena. It conforms to the nature of the human being, and the nature of the human being conforms to the nature of Allah Himself. Allah says: فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًۭا ۚ فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا ۚ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ Turn your face toward the religion of truth. The nature of Allah upon which He has created all people. No change should there be in the creation of Allah. That is the straight religion, but most of the people do not know. فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا The nature of Allah is the same nature upon which He molded the nature of mankind.

God willing, we will explore the depth of this verse at another time. What I wish to draw out from it now is that Allah created human beings according to His own nature, and then gave them a religion that conforms to that nature. Whatever is natural, the human being accepts with ease and finds himself at home with it. Whatever is unnatural, he fears and flees from. This is illustrated by a beautiful example.

Movement is bound up with life; it is natural for the living to move. As long as you see a living person making some kind of movement, you remain at ease. Is this not so? If you see a loved one asleep, yet moving in some way, such as breathing, you remain content. But if you see that same loved one lying still, you grow afraid. You go and shake him to make certain he is still alive. Why is this? Because movement is natural to a living being, and when the living does not move, it frightens us. In the same way, if the dead were suddenly to move, that too would frighten us. Why? Because the dead are not meant to move; it is not natural for the dead to move.

So Islam is a religion of nature. Islam is in truth a very simple religion. People make it far more complicated than it is, yet in reality, in its essence, Islam is very simple, because it accords with the nature of human beings. And the Qur'an is the book that contains the description of all those natural laws. It is a book of guidance. You know how video games have walkthroughs; you can buy books that tell you how to get through each level of a game. The Qur'an is that book which helps you walk through the game of life. It is truly that simple. It truly is.

And we see examples of this all around us. Every company that makes a product always provides an instruction manual for it, does it not? You buy a radio, and it comes with an instruction manual; you buy a watch, and it comes with a user guide; you buy a laptop, a phone, a television, and they all come with a user guide, instructions on how to operate the device. There is no product in the world that comes without a set of instructions, is there? Well, this universe, and everything in it, is Allah's product; it is Allah's creation, and all of this too comes with a set of instructions, an instruction manual called the Qur'an.

Now, what is any instruction manual? It is nothing more than a set of dos and don'ts, is it not? Congratulations on the purchase of your brand-new iPhone. Begin using it by sliding the start button to the right. Select an application by clicking on it. Press the round button at the bottom of the phone to return to the main screen. Press these buttons on the side to increase or decrease the volume. Do not drop your phone from a height. Do not use it as a doorstop. Do not try to hammer a nail into the wall with it. If it gets dirty, do not wash it in the washing machine. If you accidentally do, do not dry it in the dryer. And if you do, and the dryer makes loud rattling noises, do not restart the cycle again. No, I never did any of that.

In the same way, the Qur'an is a set of do and do-not instructions for Allah's product, the human being. Do these things, so that you may gain the benefits that follow. Do not do these things, so that you may avoid the harms they cause.

as simple as that. Every company comes with a logo that identifies the maker of the product. You see a half-bitten apple, and you know the product was made by Apple. You see flying windows, and you know it was made by Microsoft. You see a strange-looking woman in a green circle, and you know it was made by Starbucks. Allah's brand, His logo, is His kalima, the shahada: la ilaha illa Allah. When you see a person reciting La ilaha illa Allah, you know his heart belongs to Allah. You know his heart is powered by Allah.

Every product also needs a demonstration. Companies spend millions of dollars building demonstration sites, videos, and conferences where someone shows how the product is used. Someone stands on a stage and walks you through its use in practice. He shows you, by example, how to perform each operation listed in the instruction manual. Yes?

Rasul Allah (SAS) is the living demonstration of the Qur'an. He is the embodiment of every do and do-not listed in the Qur'an. He demonstrated for us, in practice, what to do, how to do it, when to do it, and how much of it to do. He also demonstrated for us what not to do, how not to do it, and when not to do it. For every single instruction of the Qur'an, you can find its practical form in the seerah of Rasul Allah (SAS).

Every product also has a technical manual, and that is not for everyone. It is only for those who are technically advanced. It rises above the surface operations into the technical ones. How is this device structured? What is its schematic diagram? How does it function internally? How does a change in one part of the device produce a change in the other parts of the diagram? Why does this device work the way it does? How has it been designed on the inside? All the technical specifications.

Maulana Ali is the technical guide for Islam. All the branches of knowledge — taveel, mabda maad, haqaiq, daqaiq, haqaiq Aliyah, daqaiq ul daqaiq, ifadaats — all of these highly technical realms of knowledge emerge from him and from his progeny, the Imams of all times. They explain the why of things: why namaaz, why roza, what ruku is, what sujood is, what the mamsoolat are, how the universe actually functions, how physicality affects spirituality, and how spirituality has an impact on physicality. All these highly technical details, the inner workings of this universe, our existence, and our return — all of this lies in the technical uloom of Maulana Ali and the line of Imams in his progeny.

So you see, this idea of religion is not so far-fetched. It is quite straightforward. And the center of this circle is the Qur'an. God willing, we will look at everything only from the Qur'an, because if we want to know about Allah, who better to ask than Allah Himself? Through the miracles-of-the-Qur'an sessions, we are already convinced, God willing, that this message is in fact from Allah. Now let us actually begin to look at the message itself.

We should really examine our own lives and the lives of those around us. Why is it that the desires of our heart never end? Some people spend all their time on Facebook, WhatsApp, and all these social media sites, desperately trying to find a connection. Why does this heart constantly long for a connection? And no matter how hard we try,

why can we not find that eternal connection? Why do we always carry that feeling of emptiness in our hearts, no matter how hard we try to fill it? Some try to fill that emptiness with money, some with power, some try to drown it in alcohol, and some try to forget it with drugs. Yet the emptiness is always there.

If money is the key to all happiness, then why are so many wealthy people taking their own lives? It is understandable that the poor keep chasing after wealth, but why do we see the very rich chasing after money as well? The man is a millionaire, yet his heart still wants more. He wants to be a billionaire. Why is that? Even with all the comforts of this world, why is this heart never satisfied? Why is it always looking for more?

Consider the artists in the music industry. An artist begins by longing for his song to be heard. He gets his break, someone produces his album, everyone downloads it, it goes platinum, and overnight he becomes enormously popular, and enormously wealthy as a result. He wins a music award. Now, is that the end of his career? No. Now he must come up with the next great hit. But the next album he releases is not as entertaining, not as successful, does not sell as many copies, and does not reach the top of the charts. Now the artist begins to feel desperate. She begins to see her own decline. What does every artist want, even more than money? Fame. Appreciation, acknowledgment, recognition. They live off of it. But instead of that, now she is getting criticism: rotten tomatoes, one star, thumbs down. She begins to grow depressed. So she starts to think, what can I do to get back on top? I need to come up with a new song. Wait, I already tried that, and it did not work out too well. Perhaps if my new song were a little controversial, perhaps if it were a little more indecent, it might become more popular. Does that happen?

And then, when that does not work either, perhaps if I lower my standards of decency even further, perhaps that will get me there. And if that does not happen, perhaps I will simply shave my head, get drunk, get arrested, adopt a baby, adopt twelve babies. Perhaps if I cannot be mentioned at the award ceremony, I will be mentioned in the tabloid at the end of a grocery aisle. At least I will be mentioned somewhere. Does that happen? Certainly. They grow more and more desperate, willing to try anything. When nothing works, they turn to alcohol, then to drugs, and then one day they are found dead in the bathtub of their penthouse suite.

And, most importantly, what does this need for more indicate? It indicates that the heart is not getting what it truly needs.

Suppose you have some critical data on your phone that you need for work or school. You have no backup of it; the only original copy you have is on your phone. That data is so important that without it you cannot function at work or school. Now what happens when you lose your phone with that data on it? You will search for it, will you not? You will keep searching for it everywhere: in your house, in your office, in the places you visited. You will keep searching for it endlessly. Now, I can distract you for a while, take your mind off it for a moment, can I not?

I can distract you with Facebook, WhatsApp, time spent with friends, a PS4, an Xbox, and the rest. But the moment the distraction ends, what do you do? You begin searching for your phone again, do you not? Now there is only one way in which this need, this search, can come to an end. What is it? It is that you find your phone. Once you find it, will you go on searching for it? Of course not.

In the previous session we considered the words *al-Rahman* and *al-Rahim*. From Surah al-Rahman I showed you just one aspect of Allah's mercy. Today, God willing, we will consider the next verse, in which Allah says: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ.

The Meaning of *Malik* and *Malik*

The word مَالِك means OWNER, and it comes from three root letters: meem, laam, and kaaf. مِلْك means property, and so the one who owns property is the مَالِك. Now, there is another word in Arabic that shares these same root letters, which is مُلْك, meaning kingdom. And the one who rules over a kingdom is called مَلِك, a KING.

It is very interesting, when you read the Qur'an, that Allah speaks of both things. There is مِلْكِیَّۃ, and there is مُلْکِیَّۃ. مِلْكِیَّۃ means ownership, and مُلْکِیَّۃ means kingship, and Allah ascribes both of these things to himself. He is not only the OWNER; he is also the KING. And the KING is the one who judges. The KING is the one who decrees. The KING is the one who legislates. The KING is the ultimate authority in his kingdom. There is no one above the king with whom a plaintiff may plead his case. So Allah says:

وَٱلْأَرْضُ جَمِيعًۭا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَمَةِ . وَٱلسَّمَوَتُ مَطْوِيَّتٌۢ بِيَمِينِهِ

On the day of judgment, the entire earth and all of the heavens will be folded up in the hand of Allah. What does it mean for me to have something in my hand? It means that it is under my control; it is MY *milkiyah*. No one else can control this except me, because it is in MY hands. So Allah is saying that on THAT day, the earth and all seven heavens will be rolled up in his hand. This is *milkiyah*: complete ownership, complete control. And then he also says:

قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ مَلِكَ ٱلْمُلْكِ

Say: Allah is the king of all kingdoms. So in this verse he speaks of himself being the king. And then there is another verse in which he combines both together, his مُلْکِیَّۃ and his مِلْكِیَّۃ, and he says:

ٱلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لِّلَّهِ . يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ

On that day the مُلْك, the kingdom, will BELONG to Allah, which makes him OWNER. Yes? يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ: and he will judge and decree between them. And who judges? Who decrees? The King does! So both مُلْك and مِلْك will belong to Allah on that day of judgment.

You Cannot Tell the Owner What to Do

Now let us understand the implications of the word OWNER. When someone is *malik*, when someone OWNS property, he can do whatever he wants with that property. No one has the right to question that owner about his decisions regarding that property. Let us look at an example to understand this better.

Annu Khala and Ali Khaloo own a house in Joplin. That house, and everything WITHIN that house, is THEIR property, which means that they can make whatever decisions they want about that house. They can paint the walls whatever color they choose. They can decorate it any way they want. They can put things in whatever places they think work BEST for them. They can also discard and throw away whatever they want. Right?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
Now let us say that I visit them for a few days. They welcome me into their home, and in order to make sure that I am comfortable, they grant me certain privileges. Here is a room for you. You can unpack your things and put them in this closet that we have emptied out for you. Feel free to move about the house; use the refrigerator whenever you need anything. Feel free to use the television, or any other appliance. In other words, اس کو اپنا ہی گھر سمجھو, think of this as your own home. *Mi casa, su casa*, right?

So out of their love,

they share their property with me to make me comfortable in their home. In fact, they make me feel so comfortable that very soon I forget that I am only a guest in their house. I actually begin to behave as though I own the house. And so now I see my aunt making certain decisions, and I begin to question them. I begin to judge them by my own worldview and my own preferences. Aunt, why did you paint the walls this particular color? It makes no sense. It would be so much better if you painted them that color. Why are you decorating your room this way? Why not that way? Why are you throwing all of this out? It is perfectly good! Aunt, I do not think you are managing this house properly. I seriously question the decisions you are making. You are making all the wrong decisions!

Could I say that to her? Would that be acceptable? Absolutely not. Instead of being grateful to her for her hospitality, I am judging her decisions and criticizing them. And it is not even my property to judge or criticize. That is completely obnoxious, is it not? And what would her response be? What would your response be? If I did that to you, living in your house, enjoying the comforts that you provide for me, if I began to judge and question every decision you made, how would you respond?

It is one thing to question in order to understand. Aunt, please share with me your reasoning for why you made that decision. I want to understand. But to say, you do not know what you are doing, and to demand that you prove your rationality to me, that is completely unacceptable.

My aunt's response would be, who do you think you are? This is my house, and I will manage it as I see fit. You are only a temporary guest in my house. You do not know what happened before you came into my house. You have no clue about my short-term goals, my long-term goals. What do you know? You are going to leave in a few days anyway. I am the one managing this house. I am the one maintaining this house. I welcome you into my house. I let you use my things. And you have the audacity to question and judge my decisions? Get out!

Is she justified in being offended? Of course. Because she is the owner. Her house and everything in it is her property. She knows what she is doing, and I have absolutely no right to judge and question her decisions. First, because she is the owner, so she can do whatever she wants with her property, and nobody has the right to question that. And second, because I do not have access to the knowledge she has in making her decisions. Do you understand?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
And once the baby is ready, this first Rabb, the womb, hands it over to its mother, who becomes the next immediate Rabb of that baby, even before the father. It is the mother who becomes the next Rabb. Why? Because she feeds it. Now, for that newborn baby, who has ownership of it? The mother. Who has authority over it? The mother. Who is going to nurture it, help it grow and develop? The mother. Who is going to teach it things, set it to purpose in all the various stages of development? The mother. Who is going to shower gifts and blessings upon it? The mother. Who is going to maintain that baby's sustenance in all possible forms — physical, emotional, psychological — who is going to do that? The mother. So the mother becomes the next direct Rabb, right after the Rububiyyah of the womb, of the reham, is complete.

Father is Rabb too, but he exercises his Rububiyyah THROUGH the mother. Are you all still with me? I want you to keep these two Rabbs in mind. The first is the womb. The second is the mother of the womb. All right? And what did the people of Quraish reject and deny? The afterlife and the existence of God. And the Messenger of Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) says, الدنیا رحم الاخرۃ — this world is the WOMB of the afterlife.

Now let us examine the fetus in the womb. Was it the womb that was actually doing all the work, or was it the mother doing all the work? We know it was the mother. The mother was taking care of all the baby's needs. She was eating the right things. She was making sure she did not bump into anything so that her baby would not get hurt. She was getting all the ultrasounds done, taking the necessary injections and medicines, suffering for her baby. All of that. We know that it was the mother all along.

But for the fetus — does the fetus know that its mother is doing all the work? NO. If I asked the fetus, "Who do you think is doing all the work?" what would it reply? "The womb is." The fetus has absolutely no knowledge of the existence of her mother. What mother? Where is the mother? I do not see a mother. All I see is this womb. There is no mother. It is just a cause and an effect. And I say to this fetus, "LOOK! She is the one feeding you." "What are you talking about? It is the umbilical cord that is feeding me. It brings me this blood that carries nutrients. I get fed by it. THAT is what is causing my development. There is no mother! You are crazy to even suggest that."

I say, "No, no, no. Listen! There IS a mother. She is ALL around you. You are within the love, care, concern, and mercy of that mother. This womb would not exist if she did not exist. And this womb that you are in — it is temporary. This is NOT the world you were created for. Outside of this world there is an AMAZINGLY BEAUTIFUL world. It is SO HUGE. It is SO MAGNIFICENT that you simply cannot even imagine it right now within this womb. This womb is filth compared to THAT world. In that world your mother will take such AMAZING care of you, shower you with so much love."
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
And the fetus says, "What are you talking about? I am REALLY, REALLY happy here. Everything I need is being taken care of right here. Why do I need to have another world? I do not know why you keep talking to me about a mother and another world. There is no mother. There is no world outside of this womb. You are nuts! Show me! Show me this world right now! I want to see it. Prove to me that there is another world. Prove to me that there is actually a mother. UNTIL I see it, I am NOT going to believe you."

And I say, "But I cannot show it to you right now. But I promise, when you transition out of this world you will see both of them." "OH, so now I am supposed to trust YOU? I am supposed to trust YOUR intellect? What if you are wrong?"

I say, "Look! You have been given these eyes, but there is so little to see here. You have been given ears, but there is SO little to hear. You have been given taste buds, but there is so little to taste here. You have a nose with the ability to smell, but there is not a single fragrance here. You have arms and feet. You have all of these amazing gifts, but you cannot benefit from them within this womb. Think about it! These are of NO use to you inside this womb.

This means there must be another world beyond this one, a world where you will be able to use these gifts and benefit from them. Your only purpose in the womb, in this world, is to develop these organs and prepare them for the next world, where you will actually use them and benefit from them. And the fetus sighs and says, "I simply do not understand what you are talking about. This place is wonderful. I love it here. I am always going to live here. The idea of a mother and of another world is absurd. These things make no sense to me at all." And so this fetus lives on in its ignorance until the nine months are complete. And now what happens? The contractions begin, and the fetus starts to panic. What is going on here? What is happening? And with those contractions, that beautiful world of the fetus, the world it was living in so happily, begins to fall apart all around it. Is this not exactly the description of the Day of Judgment?

إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
When the earth is shaken with its earthquake,

وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا
And the earth discharges its burdens,

وَقَالَ ٱلْإِنسَنُ مَا لَهَا
And man says, "What is wrong with it?"

يَوْمَئِذٍۢ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا. بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا
On that Day it will report its news, because your Lord has commanded it.

يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَصْدُرُ ٱلنَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًۭا لِّيُرَوْا۟ أَعْمَلَهُمْ
That Day the people will come forth separated, to be shown the results of their deeds.

فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًۭا يَرَهُ
So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it,

وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍۢ شَرًّۭا يَرَهُ
And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
So the world of this fetus now comes to an end, and it is forced out of it. Does the fetus have any choice about whether it wishes to remain in the womb? Can it say, "No, I do not want to leave this place"? No. Whether it wishes to or not, once its time is up, it is pushed out into the next world. It dies in the womb to be born again into the world. This is precisely what the word inteqaal means. It comes from naqala, transference. It also means a copy or a replica, naqal. Why? Because the next world is going to be a copy; it is going to be a replica of the first. If you did good in that world, you will find good in this next world. If you did evil in that world, you will face evil in the next world.

So now this temporary world of the fetus is destroyed, and it comes into the huge world it was told about and promised while in the womb, the world, the afterlife, that it chose not to believe in. And then, as soon as it is out, to whom is that baby handed? To the mother, the very mother it said did not exist.

So the fetus goes through that same confusion of the seen and the unseen in the womb that we go through in this life. The fetus that accepted the rububiyyah of the mother through the womb comes out fully developed, and is now capable of enjoying all the benefits that this next world has to offer. And the fetus that rejected the rububiyyah of the womb comes out underdeveloped, incapable of benefiting from what this world has to offer. We are going through the exact same process in life. Why? Because الدنیا رحم الآخرۃ. Our Rabb tells us: look, follow the shareeah, keep yourself pure, perform your salaah, keep your fasts, pay your zakaat, perform your hajj. And we say: why? How is this going to help me? It is not going to help you here.

It's not meant for this world. It is going to help you in the next life. That is where you will benefit from these spiritual organs. All you are doing is developing them in the womb of this temporary world. Trust me, there is a HUGE spiritual world out there. There is a Jannah! It is INCREDIBLY BEAUTIFUL. There is ALLAH, who is INTENSELY merciful, who is CONSTANTLY merciful. Trust me! All of this is true.

الجنۃ حق والنار حق والموت حق والبعث حق والمیزان حق والصراط حق

Heaven is a reality. Hell is a reality. Death is a reality. Rising from the graves is a reality. The scales in which your actions will be weighed is a reality. The straight path is a reality.

وان الساعۃ آتیۃ لا ریب فیھا

And that appointed moment is coming. There is ABSOLUTELY no doubt about it. And our response to all of that is: what God? What afterlife?

That is the world in which JUSTICE will be EXACTED. Every incident. Every EVENT for you about which you and I have said: where is justice? On THAT day we will see justice. The innocent people who suffered momentarily in this world will be balanced out with immense, never-ending gifts and pleasures. And the one who CAUSED suffering for fleeting gains and pleasures will have his injustices balanced with grievous pain and everlasting torment.

إِذَا ٱلشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتوَإِذَا ٱلنُّجُومُ ٱنكَدَرَتْوَإِذَا ٱلْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْوَإِذَا ٱلْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْوَإِذَا ٱلْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ ‏‎وَإِذَا ٱلْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ ‏
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
All descriptions of the day of judgment, when this universe will be destroyed.

وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ

On that day when souls are paired together. When you finally meet those loved ones who left you behind in this world.

وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُۥدَةُ سُئِلَتْ. بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍۢ قُتِلَتْ

On that day when the little girl who was buried alive will be asked: for what sin was she killed? This is the day where Allah will EXACT justice. THIS is the day of justice. NOT this world that we are living in.

وَإِذَا ٱلصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ ‏

On this day when the books of deeds will be made public!

وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ

And on this day when the sky is stripped away.

وَإِذَا ٱلْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ ‏

And when Hellfire is set ablaze.

وَإِذَا ٱلْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ

And when Paradise is brought near,

عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌۭ مَّآ أَحْضَرَتْ

every soul will then know what it has brought with it. All good will be rewarded, and all bad will be punished.

It has been narrated by the prophet (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) that there will be a man on the day of judgment, and all this man ever did was lend money to other people. He was a money lender, and those people are usually black-hearted people. But when this man sent his servants out to collect the money that people owed, if the person was having a hard time returning the money, and if that is what the servant would come back and tell him, he would say: forget about it. So on the day of judgment this man comes before God, and he does not have any good deeds to his name except that he used to do this. And Allah (Subhanhu Wa Ta'ala) displays this man to everyone and says: Will I leave him to be more generous than me? He used to forgive people, and do you think now I am NOT going to forgive him?

So on this day EVERY single good deed will be balanced with reward. And ALL delusions of grandeur, whether it relates to wealth and power in this world, or in religion. There are people who are learned and ACT very pious.

but they are terrible in their dealings with people. And we say: that is not fair. How can he get away with that? He will get away with it in this world, but he will not in the next world. This person's illusion of piety will come to an end on that day.

On that day the *muflis* and the *ghanee*, the destitute and the affluent, will be set apart. The Messenger of Allah (salla Allahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) once asked his companions: من المفلس؟ Who is the *muflis*, the destitute one?

They said: المُفلِسُ مَن لا دِینارُ ولا دَرھَمُ عِندَنَا یا رسول اللہ The destitute is the one who has no dinar and no dirham among us.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
He said: No. The greatest destitute of my Umma on the Day of Judgment—أِنَّ المُفلِسَ مِن أُمَّتِی مَن یَأتِی یَومَ القِیَامَۃِ بِصلاۃٍ وَصِیَامٍ وَ زَکَاۃٍ—the greatest destitute of my Umma on the Day of Judgment will be the one who comes with all his prayers, and all his fasts, and all his zakat—ویأتی قد شتم ھذا وقذف ھذا وأکل مال ھذا و سفک دم ھذا وضرب ھذا—but in addition to all those deeds, he cheated this one, he slandered that one, he devoured the wealth of this one, he spilled the blood of this one, he struck this one. فَیُعطٰی ھٰذا مِن حَسَنَاتِہِ وَ ھٰذا مِن حَسَنَاتِہِ And so his good deeds will be taken from his account and placed in the account of this one, and this one, and this one. فَأِن فَنِیَت حَسَنَاتُہُ قبَلَ أَنْ یُقضٰی مَا عَلیہ And when his good deeds run out before justice has been fully served—أَخِذَ مِن خَطَایَاھُم فَطُرِحَت عَلَیہِ—the sins and faults of the remaining victims will be taken from their accounts and added to his account. ثُمَّ طُرِحَ فِی النَّار

Despite living an entire life full of worship—prayers, fasts, zakat—because of his injustices toward other people, this man will have to give up all his good deeds, and take on all the terrible sins of his victims, and then he will be thrown into the hellfire. This will be the greatest destitute of my Umma. نعوذ باللہِ من ذالک نعوذ باللہِ من ذالک نعوذ باللہِ من ذالک May Allah protect us all from being among these destitutes on the Day of Judgment.

Did Allah create me aimlessly? So that I may do what? Merely enjoy these things without purpose? Very well, let us assume it is all for my enjoyment and pleasure. Allah is Rehman; He is Raheem. He created this entire universe so that I might aimlessly enjoy my life and have fun. Then, simply at a practical level: if that is the case, why is there death? Why am I going to die eventually? If that is what He created me for—fun and games—then why must it come to an end? Why is this universe temporary? Why was it not built to last forever? کل من علیھا فان Everything within it is in a state of annihilation.

If this world is such a beautiful place, built for fun and games, why is there suffering? Why is there pain? Why does this world default to ugliness? Consider these beautiful gardens: they are not beautiful on their own. There is constant maintenance involved. What will happen if no one tends them? They will fall to ruin. That is the default nature of this world. Weeds grow all by themselves. Crops and plants that bear fruit need to be planted and grown with hard work. Ignorance is the default state of human beings; knowledge must be acquired. Our bodies become dirty, filthy, and foul-smelling all by default. It takes effort to clean them, to groom them, to maintain them. Why is that? The body grows hungry again and again all on its own, and I must keep feeding it constantly. Why is that? These are all signs. علامۃ.

operational knowledge, so that I may study its structure and arrive at the intent behind my creation. Why was I created? What is my purpose, and how do I put myself to that purpose?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
Yaum, of course, means day. But technically, yaum can mean any span of time. It could mean a second. It could mean a minute. It could mean a month. Most commonly, however, it refers to a day. And we know that the actual Day of Judgment will not be twenty-four hours long. Rather, that day will be of a length that corresponds to your faith and mine. If we are true to our faith, the yaum, the span set aside for that judgment, will be quick. If we have not been true to our faith, the span of our judgment will be long and painful. The level of our eman, the level of our faith, will dictate how long that day is going to be. The stronger our eman, the quicker that day will be; the weaker our eman—may Allah protect us from that—the longer and longer that Day of Judgment will become.

There is a hadees of Rasul Allah in which he says that the Day of Judgment, the span of judgment for a true believer, a true momin, will be like the time between the end of Asr and the beginning of Maghrib. It will be that short! The shortest interval between any two prayers is always that between the end of Asr and Maghrib. And for the one who has no eman, who has no faith, who took his responsibilities in this world lightly, who ignored the call to faith—for such a disbeliever, the Day of Judgment will be so long, so painful, so torturous, because of the shame and disgrace he will feel on that day on account of his actions, that the Quran tells us he will actually beg Allah AWJ to throw him into the fire, just so that he can escape the process of judgment. He will, in effect, say to Allah: let us get this over with, let us just move on to the next stage. He will himself pass judgment against himself on the Day of Judgment.

Now, the word deen. People think it means religion, and in certain contexts it does mean religion. But the word deen is a very comprehensive word. It could mean a "way of life," as in the ayah:

ان الدین عند اللہ الاسلام

the true religion, the deen in the eyes of Allah, is Islam—which is to say, a way of life. Another meaning of the word deen is retribution, the final judgment.

Now, what is the Day of Judgment? Allah Himself tells us:

وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ

What do you think Yaum al-Deen is?

يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌۭ لِّنَفْسٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا ۖ وَٱلْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لِّلَّهِ

On that day, no soul will be able to own—meaning, to benefit—another soul. Tamlik is from milkiyah, ownership. And the final command on that day will belong to Allah.

The story of a teacher, with the children taking advantage. "Hey! I think he sees you." "Yes, I know. But he won't do anything, because he is a nice guy." When you show only love and mercy, and love and mercy, and love and mercy, and love, then is it possible that we as human beings would take advantage of that?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
This is a rather silly example, but it may get the point across. Imagine there is a master and a slave, in the worldly sense. The master says: "Listen! You are my slave, but I do not want you to do all kinds of work. I have only a few requirements. All I want you to do is this—here is a fence. It is not even really a fence; it is just a line made with chalk on the ground. Do not go to the other side of it. Just stay on the inside. Do not step outside the line. Inside this line, do whatever you want."

Just do not step outside this line, this circle. That is all I am asking, and it is a fairly wide circle." The master says this to the slave and leaves him be.

So one day the slave is walking close to the line, and he trips and falls to the outside of it. The moment he lands on the other side, whom does he look at? He looks at the master. The master is sitting on his chair, watching him, but he says nothing. So the slave got up, dusted himself off, and jumped back inside the line. The next day, the slave was again walking close to the line, and this time he pretended to fall, and again he looked at the master. The master is still sitting in his chair, and he says nothing. The next day, he stopped pretending. He put one foot outside the line, then turned and looked at the master. Again the master says nothing, though he is looking straight at the slave. He says nothing. Before long, the slave is walking with one foot on the outside and one on the inside. Again the master says nothing. Now a few months go by, and he is spending most of his time on the outside, waving to the master. "How are you doing? I am having a wonderful time." And still the master says nothing.

Then one day the master calls him. "Come here." He comes over to the master with a foolish grin on his face. The master says, "Do you remember, when we first met, I told you not to cross that line?" He says, "Yes, yes, you told me. I remember." The master says, "Well, you began crossing that line. The first time, you made a mistake. The next time, you pretended to make a mistake. And after that, you have been crossing the line deliberately, again and again. And I have been keeping a record. I said nothing to you, but I have been counting exactly how many times you crossed the line. You have crossed it six thousand eight hundred and thirty-four times. And now I am going to punish you for every single time you disobeyed me. I have decided to whip you today for every single time you crossed the line. I will let go of the one you crossed by mistake, but for all the rest you will be punished today."

Do you know what that is? That is a master saying, "You took advantage of my mercy. You forgot that I have a right to judge you. You forgot that I have the power to punish you. I will show you mercy, so long as you do not try to take advantage of me, so long as you do not try to make a joke of my guidance."
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
But I am not really speaking about a master and a slave and a line drawn with chalk on the ground, am I? I am speaking about us and Allah.

So if you had only al-Rahman and al-Rahim, then people would take advantage. That is why, after telling us that He is al-Rahman al-Rahim, He puts us back in check: I am also Malik-e-Yaum ad-Deen. Do not forget that. I am the Master of the Day of Judgment.

Deen. Look at the thirtieth part, at Surah al-Ma'un and Surah al-Kafirun, for the word deen. Let us begin with the word deen. The word deen in Arabic means "precise dealing." They have a saying in Arabic:

کمَا تَدِینُ تُدَانُ

The way in which you deal with someone is the way they will deal with you. In other words, this is a verse about being dealt with according to justice. What we are learning through this verse is a very powerful philosophy of Islam. There are only two ways in which you will be dealt with on the Day of Judgment. Either you will receive Allah's love and mercy, or you will receive Allah's justice. Notice that Allah did not say you will receive mercy or you will receive punishment. Allah did not say you will receive either love, care, concern, and mercy, or anger.

That is not what he said. What he is saying is this: on the one hand you will receive love and care and mercy, and on the other you will receive justice. And we truly need to understand what that means.

The concept of justice appears in the short chapters of the final part of the Qur'an, in verses such as والشمس وضحاها. Consider مالک یوم الدین. This is an unjust world. On the Day of Judgment we will be questioned, we will be interrogated, and justice will be served.

Now, there are some people who do not believe in God, and the reason they do not believe is that they say there is injustice in this world. The injustice they see around them is what they offer as proof that God does not exist. There are two kinds of injustice: the injustice that happened to them, and the injustice that happened to others. Certain seemingly unjust events they experienced in their own lives, or unjust events they saw happening to someone else — on the news, an earthquake, a tsunami, disease, children dying, all the terrible things that occur in the world. So there are two kinds of injustice in this world. One is personal: something bad happened to them, and then they decided they no longer wanted to believe in Allah. The other is what they see outside themselves, and they say: if there were a God, and if He were so loving and caring, then how could He allow this to happen?

Now, the Qur'an's answer to that lies within مالک یوم الدین itself. How?

For there to be a God, He must be perfect. Is that not true? Anything less than perfect could not be a God, so everything about Him must be perfect. His love must be perfect. His mercy must be perfect. His knowledge must be perfect. His wisdom must be perfect. And above all, His justice too must be perfect. So the argument runs: if God were unjust, then He would no longer be God. You could not call Him God, because He would not be perfect, and to be perfect He must be perfectly fair. Is that not true?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
So the complaint being made against God is that if He exists, He is not fair, and therefore I cannot accept Him as God. Now this argument is in fact logical, but the Qur'an answers this logical complaint in the following way.

Allah, mighty and majestic, says that this world we live in was not actually designed to be perfectly just. Nothing in this life is truly perfectly fair. I keep returning to your parents. The truth is that whatever your parents have done for you, no matter what you do for them in return, you will still never be able to repay them. You will still fall short of what your mother did for you, or what your father did for you. It is not fair. It will never be fair. What they receive from you, set against what they gave to you, will never be fair.

Likewise, when you take a job — suppose you work in a grocery store, and you are paid thirty dollars an hour, and you work eight hours a day, and your boss gives you a set of instructions to complete all the work. Is it true that you are laboring every second of every minute of those eight hours, exactly as you are supposed to? Is that true? But is it also true that at the end of the day you are still paid thirty dollars an hour anyway? You are not rated by the second. Even though there may have been several minutes in that hour when you did no work at all and simply relaxed.

You stood around by the watercooler. You spent time with friends. You checked your Facebook status. Is that not true? In other words, even though you are being paid, the wage is not truly perfect. It is not perfect in the sense of exact. Do you understand? There is some element of unfairness in it. You still get away with something.

In the same way, suppose someone slaps you, and you say, "I want justice!" So what do you do? You slap them back. Except that you have been training with weights for a very long time, and the one who slapped you is two years old. Your slap could kill the child. But because you want justice, you slap the child anyway, and the child flies off and lands two feet away. Is that equal? Of course not. A little two-year-old child comes and pushes you, and you say, "I need justice!" Weeeeeee. You cannot have perfect justice in this world. You simply cannot.

In the same way, consider a court case. A person kills five people. He goes on a shooting spree and kills five people. Now, what is the worst the court can do? What is the maximum punishment the court can impose? Probably a death penalty. But how many times can he be killed? Only once. But that is not fair. He killed five times, and so justice dictates that he too should be killed five times. But how do you kill someone five times? Is that fair? No. In truth, that is not fair.

The Qur'an and Islam are actually stating very clearly that this world is not created for justice. This world is utterly unfair. On this we are in complete agreement with the atheist.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
Even in the life of the Prophet, two people came to him who had a disagreement between them, and they wanted the Prophet to resolve the difference. One of them spoke very well, and the other man was rather quiet; he was simply not a very talkative person. Now, the man who could speak very well made his case very well, because he could talk very well. He was like a used-car salesman. But the other man was shy and quiet, so he did not say much. Obviously, if he does not say much and does not make a good case, he might lose the case, right? But just because the first man can speak well, and the other man cannot speak well, does that necessarily mean that the man who can speak well is right, and the man who cannot speak well is wrong?

So the Prophet said to them, "Listen! I can only judge this disagreement based on what you are telling me. But Allah will give you the true justice." In other words, even when the Prophet judges a case, even when the most just human being who ever walked upon the face of this earth judges a case, even he recognizes that this world is not about perfect justice.

In fact, the Sharia law that people are so frightened of is not about delivering perfect justice; it is the best that human beings can do in this world. For instance, in the Sharia there is a law that if you kill someone, you can be killed for it. Now, is it possible that someone could come and be a false witness? Is it possible that this witness who lied could have a great deal of credibility in society, so that people listen to him, and he came and lied against you anyway? Is that possible? Certainly. And according to the Islamic judge, on the basis of that false witness, he will issue the death penalty, because he has a reliable witness, and I will have to die because of a false testimony. Now, would I die a fair death or an unfair death? I died an unfair death, even though I was judged according to the Islamic law. Is that not true? So that means that, just because there is a fair law,

does not mean that justice will always be served. Having fair laws is not the same thing as having justice, perfect justice. In this world we can only try; we cannot reach perfection. We can only do our best, and it is a powerful thing to understand this, because Allah is teaching us in the Qur'an that you and I must try without ceasing. That is all that is asked of us. We are not asked to be perfect. We are not asked to build a perfect society. We are human beings, and we are never going to be perfect.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
Now, if this line of questioning is unacceptable with an owner, it is certainly even more unacceptable with a king. It is completely unimaginable to stand before a king and tell him how to run his kingdom.

Allah is the owner, and He is the king. He is the owner and the king. He created this universe and everything within it, including us. This is His house. His property. We are all temporary guests living in His house. We have absolutely no partnership in His decisions. We have no partnership in His authority. ولم یکن لہ شریکٌ فی الملک. He has no partner in His rule over His kingdom. He is the sovereign king. And therefore we do not get to question Him about His decisions. We do not get to pass judgment on His decisions. He owes us no explanations. Whatever He has given us in the Qur'an,

in terms of explaining the reasons behind His decisions, they come from His mercy. They are part of the intellectual gifts He has bestowed upon us. He was not obligated to do that. Had He not done it, there is absolutely nothing we could do to change it, because we are His property, we are His subjects. And because of the privileges He has granted us, we forget our place before Him.

This is why the Qur'an says that on the Day of Judgment, when we are all standing before Him, He will announce in front of all of us: لِّمَنِ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْمَ. لِلَّهِ ٱلْوَٰحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ. To whom does kingship belong today? To whom does dominion belong today? To whom does ultimate power belong today? Allah will ask everyone this question on the Day of Judgment. Why? Because until that moment, you and I thought we were in control. We thought we were the kings of our own destiny. It is my life. I am the architect of my destiny. Allah has allowed every one of us the illusion of power and ownership. We think we own our bodies, our house, our cars, our jobs, and so we choose to do whatever we please with them. But on that Day of Judgment, Allah makes it clear to all His creation that He alone is the owner, His alone is the command, and His alone is the kingdom on that day.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
Now, having said that, Allah is still perfect, is He not? And if Allah is perfect, then He must be perfectly just. But we have already seen that this world is not perfectly just. This seems to present a problem. How can one who is perfectly just create a world that is not perfectly just? This is where the atheist runs into difficulty. The Qur'an's answer to that is that, in truth, you are looking at only one side of the equation. In algebra we learn how to balance an equation, do we not? When you do something to one side, you must do something else to the other side to balance it out. So the difficulty is this: someone who sees only this world has seen only one side of the equation, and there is a great deal of imbalance in it. All the crimes that a person committed in this world and got away with, or even if they paid for them, they paid only in part and did not pay for those crimes in full, and so escaped them, all these crimes will be paid for on the Day of Judgment. The purpose of the Day of Judgment is to take all the little injustices that a person committed in the world, and the great injustices that a person got away with, or all the good deeds that a person did and was never repaid for. It is not only about bad things but also about good things. Perhaps you did a great many good things but were never rewarded for them in this world. They went unnoticed. No one ever thanked you. You received no reward even when reward was due. That is not fair! All of this too will be balanced. When? On the Day of Judgment.

If you do not believe in the Day of Judgment, it becomes impossible for you to believe in a God. Let us work backward now. If you do not believe in the Day of Judgment, it becomes impossible for you to believe in a God. Why? Because if you do not believe in the Day of Judgment, then you are left with a world that is completely unjust; and if you are left with a world that is unjust, then you have a God who is unjust; and if God is unjust, then God is not perfect, and therefore there can be no God. Do you understand?

So now we are learning in the Fatiha that we will thank Allah for this world even though it is not perfect, and even though we ourselves are not perfect. There are still a great many wonderful things in this world. And as for the bad things that we cannot make any logical sense of, for example children who are terminally ill, or tsunamis that wipe out cities, all of that will be balanced on the Day of Judgment. Whatever suffering they endured in this world, they will be compensated for it in the next world. Nothing of this world will go unrewarded in the next. فمن یعمل مثقال ذرہ خیر یرہ There are some pleasures in this world that you enjoyed even though you should not have, and you will have to pay the price for them on the Day of Judgment. And there are some pains you suffered in this world while walking on the path of Allah, and Allah will repay you for your suffering on the Day of Judgment.

You know someone who is very, very sick.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
you know what the Prophet used to say to him? لا بأس طھور انشاء اللہ — he said: no problem. This is purifying you. What does that mean? What does it mean that it is purifying? This person who is sick, has he committed sins? Yes. And Allah is telling him that I am making you briefly sick right now, because on the Day of Judgment all of this sickness, every second of it, is actually taking sins off your record. It is simply cleaning you up. When you show up on the Day of Judgment you look better than anyone else. But you looked worse than everybody else in this world. You were always sick in the hospital bed in this world. Yet on the Day of Judgment you are standing there before everybody, looking better than everybody else. طھور — completely purified. No sins. SubhanAllah. That is the concept of the Day of Judgment.

Now these first four verses give a very comprehensive picture of what Allah wants from us, and of who Allah is. In order for us to expect this world to be fair, and to expect Allah to be fair, we must be fair to him. Is that not true? What Allah does for me is beyond comprehension, beyond measure. Which means, to be fair, how much gratitude and praise should I be offering to Allah? Am I able to do that? Will I ever be able to do that? Will I be able to do even a fraction of what I owe? No! Does Allah even ask me to balance the scales? Does he say that I have done so much for you, and now I need you to do just as much for me? No! Is he even in need of my praise and gratitude? No! We have a master who has absolutely no need for us. And we are slaves who have an absolute need for Allah. We need him for everything. He only gives. We only take. Even when we reach out to him with our praise and gratitude, it is only to take more, not to give anything back.

When you want to gain an audience before a king, you go in with precious jewels to attract his attention. When you walk into a chief executive's office, you dress up, you look sharp, in order to get a few minutes of his time. What is the quality of our prayers? Are they precious jewels? Or are they rocks and stones? They are nothing more than rocks and stones. And yet this master rewards us.

In order to have justice, there are two parts. The first part is fair people, and the second part is fair laws. If the rules are fair but the one implementing the rules is unfair, you cannot have justice. If the person is fair but the rules are not fair, justice cannot be served.

Now, is Allah a fair and just master? He is, which means his rules must also be just. So if justice is not being served, whose fault would that be? The Qur'an says that the priority is actually people being fair. That is the greater part of the problem. Most of the problem is that people are not fair. Once people become fair, it becomes easy for them to implement the laws that are fair, and it becomes easy for them to get rid of the laws that are not fair.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
The Day of Judgment is when your fairness and mine in this world will be evaluated. Out of concern for that evaluation, you had better become fair in this world.

Do a review at this point.

At this point Allah asks us whether we wish to have a relationship with him or not. Whether you accept it or not, he is still the master. So his being a master is not in question. The real question is whether you and I will accept being his slave. That is the real question, and that is completely up to us. We have to make that decision. If we do not reach that conclusion for ourselves, after studying these first four verses, then nothing can be done.

That is why we must come to terms with all of this, and say for ourselves: ایاک نعبد و ایاک نستعین
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
There are kings in this world who have delusions of grandeur. They believe they are the most powerful. But Allah clarifies it in the Qur'an. He says: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ. Allah alone is the true king. Every other king is a false king. Every other king is an illusion. Because there is no king who can rule by himself. Every king requires support. He needs military support, he needs advisors, he needs trustworthy cabinet members, he needs subservient people within his kingdom. Think about it. If everyone ran away from the kingdom, over whom would the king rule? The king is more in need of his followers, his military generals, and the people who stand behind him and put him up on the throne, than they are of him. So Allah says He is Malik al-Haq. He is the only true king. He is the owner of all kings. All these powerful kings are themselves part of His property. On the Day of Judgment, all illusions of ownership will be gone: وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَٰدَىٰ كَمَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ وَتَرَكْتُم مَّا خَوَّلْنَٰكُمْ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِكُمْ. You shall come to us individually, in seclusion, with absolutely nothing. All your mansions, your palaces, cars, and property, your wealth, your fame, will be left behind. All your illusion of ownership will be gone on that day, when you stand before the one true owner and the ultimate king.

And so He asks everyone: لِّمَنِ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْم؟ To whom does kingship belong on this day? And no one from the entire creation will have the courage to reply. The most powerful kings, the most powerful emperors who ruled continents, will be standing before Him with lowered gaze, and nobody will dare to speak before the king of kings. So then Allah, Azza wa Jal, will answer Himself: لِلَّهِ ٱلْوَٰحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ. Today the kingship, the kingdom, and ultimate power belong only to Allah, the One, the Qahhar, the Inconquerable. Today He is not al-Rahman. Today He is not al-Raheem. Today He is al-Qahhar. Just a couple of verses earlier, He called Himself Rabb: الحمد للہ رب العالمین. And the first meaning of Rabb was المالک, the owner. So how is it that today He does not say رب یوم الدین, Master of Yaum ad-Deen? No.

Because today He is not al-Sayyid, the Master; al-Murabbi, the Nurturer; al-Murshid, the Guide; al-Mun'im, the Bestower of gifts; al-Qayyim, the Sustainer. السَّیِّد المُرَبِّی المُرْشَدُ المُنعِمُ القَیِّمُ. Today He is ONLY al-Malik, the Owner. THAT time has passed. THAT time of Rububiyyah, of lordship, is over. That time of nurturing, of guiding, of bestowing gifts is over. Today is the day of EXAMINATION. Today is the day when the OWNER will question His property about what they have been doing with their gifts. And that is why today He is مالک یوم الدین, Master of Yaum ad-Deen, not رب یوم الدین, Lord of Yaum ad-Deen.

These are the various implications of the words Maalik and Malik.

Yaum

Next is the word Yaum, which is quite an interesting word in Arabic. Generally the word Yaum is translated as a day. But linguistically, Yaum does not actually mean twenty-four hours. It simply means a time interval. So a Yaum could be used for a moment; it could mean an hour; it could mean a day, a month, a year; and it could also mean several thousand years. It is simply a duration of time allocated for a specific purpose.

تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍۢ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍۢ
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day, the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He says that this Yaum will be fifty thousand years. In Surah Muzammil He says:

يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلْأَرْضُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًۭا مَّهِيلًا

That moment when the earth and the mountains will convulse, and the mountains will become like a heap of sand being poured down. Here it is used for a moment. So the word Yaum is used for various periods of time, including Time itself.

مالک یوم الدین

Owner, or King, of the Time, or the Period, of Deen.

Deen

Now the word Deen. The word Deen in the Arabic language comes from the root letters da, ya, na, دَیْن, which has several meanings. One of the meanings is a type of rain that falls again and again until it brings the dead earth back to life. Another meaning is to discipline something: من دان نفسہ, whoever disciplines his soul. It also means a way of life: لکم دینکم ولیدین, you have your way of life and we have ours.

But the root meaning of the word دَیْن is actually debt. It means a debt. And all the other meanings that I just mentioned, they all trace their meaning from this meaning of debt. So the rain keeps coming back to the earth to bring it back to life, because that is what it owes the earth. The rain is fulfilling its debt to the earth. We owe it to our souls to discipline them. The true way of life is to repay your debts. So all the various derivatives of this word are based on the meaning of دَیْن, debt.

And our religion is called دینُ الاسلام, the Deen of Islam. Literally this can be translated as the debt of submission. In other words, the idea is that we have been endowed with, or given, uncountable blessings by our Rabb, and so the debt that we owe is submission to the Creator. Allah says in the Quran:

أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ ٱللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ

Do they seek other than the Deen of Allah?

وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ طَوْعًۭا وَكَرْهًۭا

While all creatures in the heavens and the earth have bowed down to Him in submission, willingly or unwillingly. So what Allah is asking is: do they seek other than repaying this debt, when in reality everyone and everything in existence is paying its debt to its Creator? They are in a state of submission, willingly or unwillingly.

Now there are areas of submission that the human being recognizes.

One of them is the call of nature. There are certain things we simply have to do, that we cannot avoid. One of them is to eat. That is part of our nature. When we grow hungry, we must eat, or we die. We must drink water when we are thirsty; if we do not drink, we die. Once we have eaten or taken drink, we must relieve ourselves. We have no choice in this. We must sleep. When sleep comes upon us, we cannot fight it; in the end we must submit, or we fall into acute psychosis. So there is this idea of submission to nature itself.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
And then there is also submission to our own beings, to our physical bodies. We have limitations. We can eat only so much; we can drink only so much. We can do only so much physically before we are exhausted. Because of the structure of our bodies, our movements are limited. So there is a kind of submission of the self, given that we are temporal creatures bound by the physical aspects of our nature.

So in the Qur'an there is this idea, that everything is in a state of submission, including us, followed by a reminder that we will be returned. وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ, and to Him is their return. And if you look into creation, things are emerging, and then they are returning into nonexistence. Everything that has life comes into existence, and then returns back to nonexistence. The plants, the vegetables, the animal kingdom, and ultimately the mineral kingdom. All of this is going into nonexistence after it had come into existence. So everything that is in existence, except the human beings, is paying back its debt to its Creator, willingly or unwillingly, and it will return to its master. It is only human beings who are not actively paying back their debts of submission, their دین الاسلام. But they are also not being asked about their debts right now. So when will they be asked? Who will ask them? مالک یوم الدین, the owner and the king of the day when that debt of submission falls due. یوم الدین is the day when the debt of submission falls due. It is payback time. کیف ما تُدِینُ تُدان, how you transact with others is the way you will be transacted with. It is also called یوم الحساب, the day of accountability. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) says in a hadith, حاسِبُ قبل اَن تُحاسَبُ, take yourself to account before you are taken to account.

So there is a debt of submission that we owe Allah (glorified and exalted is He). But then there is also a debt that Allah (glorified and exalted is He) will owe us on that day. See, when the master issues a command to his slave, the fulfillment of that command is a debt that the slave owes his master. Now there are only two possibilities. He either obeys the command, or he disobeys it. In both cases, a return becomes due upon his master. If the slave obeyed his master and carried out the command properly, his master now owes him a reward. And if he disobeyed his master's command, the master now owes him punishment. That is یوم الدین, the day when debts fall due. Allah says in the Qur'an, مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا فَيُضَعِفَهُۥ لَهُۥٓ أَضْعَافًۭا كَثِيرَةًۭ, who will lend Allah a beautiful loan? Allah is asking us for a loan. Why? فَيُضَعِفَهُۥ لَهُۥٓ أَضْعَافًۭا كَثِيرَةًۭ, so that Allah multiplies it many, many times over, and returns it back to His slave?

In this verse Allah, Azza wa Jal, is asking His slaves: who among you will give Me a loan? Who will place Me in his debt, so that I may multiply its reward many, many times over and repay him? وَلَهُۥٓ أَجْرٌۭ كَرِيمٌۭ For his is the most noble of rewards. SubhanAllah. Even on the Day when He is Maalik, He is full of love, full of mercy.

This is an unjust world by design
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
Now, there are some people who do not believe in Allah, and the reason they do not believe is that they say there is injustice in this world. The injustice they see around them, they take as proof that God does not exist. And there are two kinds of injustice: the injustice done to them, and the injustice done to others — by people, or by natural disasters such as earthquakes, a tsunami, disease, children dying, and every terrible thing that happens in the world. So they see all of this and they say: if there is a God, and if He is so loving and caring, then how could He allow all of this to happen?

Yet if you have the courage to reflect honestly on this line of thinking, you will find it to be the most hypocritical thing of all — that we, of all creatures, should be the ones to speak about justice. For we are the most unjust, the most unfair of all when it comes to paying our own debt of submission to Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala. We are unjust people giving speeches on the importance of justice. We hold one set of standards by which we judge ourselves, and another, entirely different set by which we judge others. We tell our children not to lie, while we lie all the time. We silently judge everyone, all the time, while speaking about how wrong it is to judge others. We talk about world hunger and starving people, yet we waste food as though it were a joke — at parties, at weddings, in our own homes. When something bad happens to others, we tell them to be patient; yet we are the first to lose patience when something bad happens to us. When something goes wrong, we say: how could this happen to me? What did I ever do to deserve this? But when things work out, when something good happens to us, we never ask those same questions. How could this happen to me? What did I ever do to deserve this? We speak of how God is unjust and unfair to us. But what of our justice to Him? What of what we owe Him, in submission and obedience, for all the gifts He has blessed us with?

وکان الانسان کفورا No doubt, man is extremely ungrateful. وکان الانسان ظلوماً جَھُولا No doubt, man is extremely unjust and irrational.

So yes, the atheist is right: this world is an unjust place. But that is only because we are unjust people. And instead of taking responsibility for our own injustices, how easy it is to point fingers at others, is it not? Well then, why does Allah not do something about it? Because He wants to see what you are going to do about it. This life is an examination hall. We are all in a state of being tested. وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُم بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْخَوْفِ وَٱلْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْوَلِ وَٱلْأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَتِ And no doubt, surely We shall test you — with fear, with hunger, with loss of wealth, and life, and children.

and crops. وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّبِرِينَ And to those who are patient, give glad tidings. تَبَرَكَ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِ ٱلْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌ Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He has power over all things. ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلْمَوْتَ وَٱلْحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًۭا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْغَفُورُ He who created death and life to test you, and to see which of you is best in action — and He is the one most exalted in Might, and most Forgiving.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
This world is not made for justice. There is no such thing as perfect in this world. Nothing in this life is perfectly fair. I return again to your parents. The truth is that whatever your parents have done for you, no matter what you do for them in return, you will never be able to repay them. You will always fall short of what your mother did for you, or what your father did for you. It is not fair to them. It will never be fair. If you weigh what they receive from you against what they gave you, it will never be equal.

They labor to pay for your education, and justice would require that you spend every single moment of your time studying. But we all know that this will not happen. The institution they paid is supposed to teach you perfectly, every single thing on the curriculum, making certain that each and every student understands. That does not happen. Suppose I take a job in a grocery store and I am paid thirty dollars an hour, and I work eight hours a day. Do I work every second of every minute of those eight hours, exactly as I am supposed to? No. But is it true that I am still paid thirty dollars an hour at the end of the day? Yes. Justice would mean that I ought to have worked the whole day, but there were moments when I took my ease. I sat by the watercooler, I spent time with friends, I checked Facebook. In other words, even though I am paid the full amount, I did not work every minute of that hour to earn that money. There will always be some element of unfairness in whatever we do.

Consider what happened recently in Brussels and Lahore. One person blows himself up and kills hundreds. Did Allah do that? No. Some brainwashed, fanatical fool did that. And how many times did he die? Once. But how many did he kill? Hundreds. And not merely a hundred individuals — he destroyed a hundred families. Justice would mean that he ought to be killed a hundred times, multiplied by the number of every member of each family. Can that be done? No. It is not fair.

The Qur'an and Islam are in fact stating very clearly that this world was not created for justice. This world that we live in is absolutely unfair. So when the atheist says, "If there is a God, how can there be so much injustice in the world," we are in complete agreement with him on this point. Now let us reverse the argument. What should the world be like in order to prove the existence of a Creator? That there be justice? That no one in the world would sleep hungry? No disease, no pain and suffering. Everyone treated justly. Love and peace all over the world. No ugliness in the world, only beauty. People would love and help one another. The lion and the deer would drink peacefully together from the same river. Is that not the perfect world we all dream of?

Now I want all of you to think about this description of the perfect world that I have just given, the one that proves there is a loving God. What have I just described to you?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
I just described Jannah for you, did I not? Is that not EXACTLY what the description of Jannah is? This world is simply one side of the equation. You study how to balance an equation in algebra, do you not? When you do something to one side, you have to do something else to the OTHER side to balance it out. So the problem is that someone who is ONLY seeing this world is seeing JUST one side of the equation. And there are a number of imbalances on this side. If you do not believe in Judgment Day, then you are left with a world that is completely unfair. And if you are left with a world that is unfair, then you have a God who is unfair. And if God is unfair, God is not perfect, and therefore there cannot BE a God. Do you understand? NOT believing in a Judgment Day IS the underlying reason for disbelief in God.

This was the EXACT argument of the Quraish. They rejected the SAME two things. They rejected the notion of a Rabb, and they rejected the concept of an afterlife.

There was a man. I believe his name was Ibn Khalaf. He came to Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) with a decayed old bone in his hand. He showed the bone to the Prophet and then closed his fist, crushing the bone to a powder. He then opened his fist and blew on that dust, dispersing it into the air. And then he asked, "Ya Muhammad! Can your God bring this decayed bone back to life?" As soon as he said that, Jibraeel AS descended with the revelation.

أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلْإِنسَنُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

Does man not consider that We created him from a mere drop of sperm, and he dares try to become My adversary?

وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلًۭا وَنَسِىَ خَلْقَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ مَن يُحْىِ ٱلْعِظَمَ وَهِىَ رَمِيمٌۭ

And he presents for Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones after they have disintegrated?"

قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ

Tell him, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He has complete knowledge of all His creations."

ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلْأَخْضَرِ نَارًۭا فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنْهُ تُوقِدُونَ

The One who made fire for you out of green trees, from which you ignite.

أَوَلَيْسَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بِقَدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم

Did Allah not create the heavens and the earth? And the One who created that, is He not able to create the likes of them?

بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ ٱلْخَلَّقُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

Of course He is capable of doing that! For He is the ALL-Knowing Creator.

إِنَّمَآ أَمْرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيْـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ

When He intends for something to happen, He gives a command for it to "Be," and it becomes.

فَسُبْحَنَ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ

So exalted is He, in whose hand is the kingship of all things, and to Him you will be returned.

So Allah speaks about this transition that will take place from this world to the next. And if you notice, even the Fateha makes the transition from الرحمن الرحیم to مالک یوم الدین. There is a transition from RUBUBIYYAH, from the love, care, concern, and mercy of Allah in THIS world, to the one in which He is the owner and the king of the day when the debt of submission falls due.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
There is a transition from this world to the hereafter. And there is a very profound hadees of Rasul Allah (salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) in which he says: الدنیا رحم الآخرۃ — this world is the womb of the hereafter. We know that the very first stage of Rububiyyah is the womb itself. Allah made the womb of our mothers the first Rabb, and He made it the perfect symbol and the perfect sign of our existence in the world. Every one of us is here today because of our mother's womb.

Let us first understand the Rububiyyah of the womb. Rabb means six things. Do you remember? الرَبُّ ھُوَ المَالِکُ وَ السَّیِّد وَ المُرَبِّی وَ المُرْشَدُ وَ المُنعِمُ وَ القَیِّمُ. A Rabb is one who has absolute ownership and, at the same time, complete authority. He ensures growth, He nurtures, He protects, and then He also sets to purpose, showering numerous undeserved gifts and blessings along the way. And then He also sustains and maintains them for the whole extent of their duration.

The world is the womb of the hereafter.

Now let us look at the reham, the womb itself, and see whether these six meanings apply. First of all, does the reham, the womb, have ownership of the embryo? Absolutely. It has complete ownership of the embryo. Does it also have complete authority over it? Absolutely. The reham is in charge. Does the womb nurture the embryo, help it grow and develop, slowly and gradually, from one stage to the next, until the embryo becomes a fetus and so on? It does. So the womb is not only Maalik, it is not only Sayyed, it is also Murabbee, is it not? Does the womb bestow priceless gifts upon the fetus? Does it develop its eyes, its nose, its ears, its hands, its feet, the heart, the intellect, and all of its internal and external organs? Does the womb do that? Certainly. So it is also المُنعِمُ. Does it watch over and manage the entire process of the development of the embryo, from its inception to the time it is fully developed? It does. So it is also Qayyim.

Once the baby is fully developed, does the womb simply leave it in there, or does it now begin the process of contractions? What is the point of contractions? To push the baby out. Why? Because it has been fully developed, and now the baby needs to put to use what the womb has helped it develop. But wait — that is Murshad, the one who sets to purpose. So the womb, the reham, is the very first Rabb of the fetus, taking care of it, nurturing it, developing it, doing all these things for it, so that it can develop, so that it can progress, so that it can go from weakness to strength. So the womb, by all six definitions of the word Rabb, is the very first Rabb that we encounter.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment

body.text_en:
Some people misunderstood what I said in the previous session. In that session I quoted this hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): المسلم اخو المسلم لا یَظلَمُہُ و لا یَخذُلُہُ ولا یَحقِرُہُ — every Muslim is the brother of every other Muslim; do not treat him unjustly, do not abandon him, and do not belittle him. On the basis of this hadith I said that all Muslims are equal in the eyes of Allah. Some took this to mean that Sulemaniyat is the same as any other creed or belief, so that it makes no real difference whether a person is a Sulemani or not, since it all comes to the same thing. That is not at all what I meant.

So I want to state again, particularly for the children, that I firmly believe Sulemaniyat is the one true sect among all the sects of Islam.
