If I did not believe that, I would obviously not follow it. I am very proud to be a Sulemani, and all of us should be proud to be Sulemanis. As you study the higher levels of knowledge, you will discover that this is not something handed to us at random. Allah did not hold a raffle of the various sects and then assign different sects to different people by chance. We have rightfully earned our place as Sulemanis through hard work, struggle, and sacrifice. So I believe absolutely, without a speck of doubt, that Sulemaniyat is the best of all schools of thought. I believe in it spiritually, on the basis of faith, and also on the basis of intellectual evidence.

What I meant when I quoted the hadith المسلم اخو المسلم — that every Muslim is the brother of every other Muslim — is that all Muslims are equal in the brotherhood of Islam. The word اخو means brother. Every Muslim deals with another Muslim on two different levels: first as a human being, and then on the basis of his عقیدہ, the creed he follows. The distinctions that exist among the various schools of thought in Islam lie in their عقیدہ, in their creed, in their doctrines, in the various religious beliefs they hold. But there are no differences in Islam when it comes to the rights of one Muslim over another, as human beings, or as brothers. In that particular respect — as human beings — every Muslim is equal to every other Muslim in the eyes of Allah. They are not equal in their beliefs, but they are all equal as basic Muslims.

That is why the hadith uses the word اخو. For what is a brother? Brothers are peers within the hierarchy of a family. The parents stand at a higher level, and then all the brothers in the family stand at the same level. Now, parents may make a distinction in how they feel about an obedient son and a disobedient one, but they make no distinction between them when it comes to loving them and caring for them.
body.topic_title_en: A Misconception Concerning the Solomonic Arts

body.text_en:
Consider also Maulana Ali. When he appointed Malik Ashtar as the governor of Egypt, he wrote him a letter explaining how he must deal with those under his authority. In that letter he said: وَأَشْعِرْ قَلْبَكَ الرَّحْمَةَ لِلرَّعِيَّةِ، وَالْـمَحَبَّةَ لَهُمْ، وَاللُّطْفَ بِهِمْ — Fill your heart with mercy for your subjects, hold affection for them, and deal with them kindly. فَإِنَّهُمْ صِنْفَانِ — Because the people you deal with will be of two kinds. إِمَّا أَخٌ لَكَ فِي الدِّينِ، وَإمّا نَظِيرٌ لَكَ فِي الْخَلْقِ — They are either your brothers in religion, or they are like you in creation; they are human beings as you are.

So we learn this same lesson from the words of Maulana Ali (AS) as well. For this reason I am deeply grateful to Allah that He guided me to Sulemaniyat. And gratitude to Allah is expressed in three ways: first, in my dealings with Allah; second, in my dealings with my own soul; and third, in my dealings with Allah's creation.

In my dealings with Him, I should express my gratitude to Allah by holding complete faith in Him, in His messengers, in His message, which is to say the books, in His angels, and in the afterlife.

In dealing with my own soul, I should express my gratitude to Allah by following His commandments to the letter and by fulfilling the obligations of the ahad shareef that I took — not by force and not with resentment, but with complete and willing submission.

In dealing with others, I should express my gratitude to Allah by interacting with His creation — not only Muslims, but non-Muslims as well — with love, respect, kindness, restraint, and patience.

But above all, because I believe that Sulemaniyat is the true sect, I should be humble before Allah that He blessed me with such an honor and such a gift, and I should not become arrogant about it. That is what I wanted to highlight. Possessing the knowledge that we possess does not give us the right to disrespect other schools of thought, nor the right to insult them, or shun them, or call them kafir. That is not what it means to be a Sulemani. And if we do wish to show that we are better than they are, then we should show it by being more loving than they are, more tolerant than they are, more respectful than they are, and more humble than they are. That, to me, is what it means to be better than another Muslim.

This does not mean that we may not have disagreements. When I meet another Muslim brother from a different sect, I may have a conflict or a disagreement with him on the subject of aqeeda. We may both hold our differences. He may say what he believes to be right, and I may say what I believe to be right, and we may both present our evidence. We may even have a heated and passionate debate over our beliefs; that is acceptable. But we can carry on that argument while eating dinner at the same table, while sharing the same food, and while my children play with his children. These two things can coexist, and according to Islamic values they ought to coexist.
body.topic_title_en: A Misconception Concerning the Solomonic Arts

body.text_en:
Simply because I believe my aqeeda is correct, I am not thereby given the right to disrespect someone else's beliefs. It is acceptable for me to disagree with their beliefs, but it is not acceptable for me to disrespect their beliefs. These are two very different things. Because consider this: they too believe strongly that their belief is correct and that we are wrong.

I have made these terrible mistakes myself, and I think that is why I became so emotional in the previous session, because I have wounded people with such fanatical remarks without even realizing it. Only last week I learned that I had hurt someone with such a conversation many years ago, and this was someone I genuinely care about. But do you know what the saddest part was? It was that I do not even remember having that conversation or saying those things. That shows how often I must have been doing it, and how much heartache my words caused without my ever realizing it.

And that is why I raised this matter in the session for you children, in the hope that you will not make the same mistakes I made — because as you gain knowledge...

it becomes so very easy to fall into this trap of arrogance. It is as though I put on a very expensive Armani suit and step out into the street, and then everyone I see in simple clothes appears inferior to me. That is not right. We put on the elegant gown of sulemani concepts, and then we are unwilling even to listen to what someone else has to say, only because it does not match our concepts, or because that person does not look at things our way. In any case, that is all I was trying to say: to actually be a sulemani, because sulemaniyat is nothing but humility, and Islam is nothing but humility. This is what Hazrat Ibrahim also says constantly in his majaalis and asbaaq: be humble, acquire humility. Humility is our flag; humility is the flag of Islam. That is what is meant to identify us. We should be recognized as sulemanis because of our humility, not because of our arrogance. So I hope this explanation corrects that misunderstanding.

The second thing I wish to state once again is that in my sessions I am speaking only to young minds, who do not know much about the principles and concepts of Islam. I am not speaking to the learned people in the group, who have studied taveel, MM, and haqaiq. I am speaking to the youngsters in this group at a very basic level. So on occasion you will indeed hear me say things to them that may seem to conflict with Mabda Ma'ad or haqaiq. It is not because I wish to teach my children something wrong, but because they must first understand the general concepts before they can understand the details and the complexities behind those concepts. One cannot really teach calculus without first teaching algebra, and one cannot teach algebra without first teaching basic arithmetic. Is that not so?

So the learned people in this group really need to come down to this ground level with me when they listen to these sessions; otherwise I am afraid I shall keep offending you, because what I say may not match exactly what you have studied in the higher realms of knowledge. But that is how I plan these sessions. I actually plan not to share those concepts, because the children will eventually learn them when they study taveel or MM.
body.topic_title_en: A Misconception Concerning the Solomonic Arts

body.text_en:
It is like a young child asking me how a computer turns on. My answer will be that you simply press this switch at the back, and the computer will turn on. Now you could object that this is not true, that this is not how a computer turns on; it is the electric current that charges the motherboard, and that activates the BIOS, which causes the operating system to boot up. No. I am speaking to a child. All the child needs to know at this point is that this switch must be pressed for the computer to turn on. When the child later studies electronic computing, all these minute details will be learned. Is that agreeable?

So I hope you will all work with me and support me in this, because it is not easy for me either to come down to this basic level and speak about things. I always feel the temptation to share more, but I know that this will not benefit my children. So at times I really must restrain myself. I request the same patience from all of you. If you have questions or concerns,

we can always talk separately and discuss anything you like... Finally, I created this Sunday Sessions group on WhatsApp so that I could share images and quotes that relate to our sessions, our beliefs and the Qur'an... So if you have something that falls into those categories, then by all means post it... but I do not want this group to turn into a social thing... If you have prayers from the sahifas, translations... anything related to the Qur'an or quotes on Maulana Ali, then please post them to the group so that we may all learn from them... but anything else... I would humbly request that you refrain from posting, because that is not the intent of this group... Generally, in my opinion, if it says at the bottom, "please share this with as many people as you can," that is a fairly good indicator NOT to post it on this group... I hope nobody will take offense at this request... بارک اللہ لی ولکم
