This is a name that Allah himself uses for Surah al-Fatiha in the Qur'an. The word Masani comes from the word masna, and it means to follow up, to repeat. The Arabs would say masna masna for things that came one after another. Allah says in Surah al-Hijr:

وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَكَ سَبْعًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِى وَٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ

This is a very powerful verse, one that shows the elevated station of Surah al-Fatiha.

We have given you seven verses that are repeated over and over again... and along with them the magnificent Qur'an. Allah is saying: I have given you the seven verses of al-Fatiha, and along with these seven verses I have given you the rest of the magnificent Qur'an. This is a fascinating verse when you consider it. Allah could simply have said, وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَكَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ — I have given you the magnificent Qur'an — which would have included Surah al-Fatiha within it. But He did not say that. He set the seven verses apart from the rest of the Qur'an. He singled them out as a distinct entity, and He said, وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَكَ سَبْعًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِى وَٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ — I gave you the seven often-repeated verses and the Qur'an. In effect, He placed Surah al-Fatiha on one pan of the scale, and the remainder of the Qur'an on the other. This shows the power, the glory, and the elevated, unique station of Surah al-Fatiha. Allah showed us the importance of these seven verses. It is as though Allah is saying that these seven verses of Surah al-Fatiha are what you truly need to understand, what you truly need to internalize, what you truly need to act upon, because the rest of the Qur'an is simply a commentary and an explanation of these seven verses.

Now, why is Surah al-Fatiha called سبع المثانی, the often-repeated seven? There are many batini interpretations of this, but from the zahiri realm one interpretation is this: when you recite Surah al-Fatiha, it is only a matter of time before you must recite it again. You finish reciting it in the first rakaa, and you must recite it again in the next. One salah ends, and there is another salah right after it in which you must recite it again. So one interpretation of its being called سبع المثانی is that these verses are frequently repeated, one after another.

Nothing in the world is recited more than Surah al-Fatiha. At any given second, of any given year, millions of Muslims all across the world are praying salah, and in that salah we know they will be reciting Surah al-Fatiha. On average, a Muslim who barely prays — who barely prays, who prays only the fard and not even the sunnah and the nafl — if a Muslim prays just this bare minimum, on average he will recite al-Fatiha nineteen times a day, which comes to about seven thousand times a year. Even if we estimate that only fifty percent of the Muslim world prays only the bare minimum fard, going simply with that assumption, that would mean that on average this surah is being recited over twenty billion times a day. Twenty billion times in an average day. That works out to seven trillion times a year, and that is just fifty percent of the Muslims praying only the bare minimum fard in one year. Now imagine, since the beginning of time, since the Qur'an was revealed, in these past fourteen hundred years, just imagine how many times this great surah must have been recited. And how many more times it will be recited until the Day of Judgment. Allahu Akbar! Wallahi, there is nothing in the world — no document, no prayer, no supplication, no creed, no hymn, no song, no praise in any language of any religion in the world — that can come even close to a fraction of how many times this surah, this سبع المثانی,

This surah, this أُم القرآن, this أُم الکتاب, is recited. SubhanAllah.

If we can appreciate this magnificent quantity — how many times this surah is recited — then why should Allah not give it the honor it deserves by calling it سبع المثانی, the seven verses that are ALWAYS being recited? Why should Allah not elevate its status by giving it its own identity, separating it out from the rest of the Qur'an, and saying:

وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَكَ سَبْعًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْمَثَانِى وَ   ٱلْقُرْآنَ ٱلْعَظِيمَ

For indeed, no recitation performed on this entire globe comes even close to a fraction of the number of times this amazing surah is recited. And by the very definition of a miracle — something that incapacitates, that renders one incapable of a response — this alone is miracle enough, blessing enough, of Surah al-Fateha.

Surah al-Shifa

Another name for this surah is Surah al-Shifa, which means the Surah that Cures.

At the Battle of Siffin, a man came to Maulana Ali and showed him his broken wrist, and then said to him, "Ya Ali! My wrist is broken. I can no longer lift the sword." Maulana Ali took his hand in his own, laid a cloth over it, and recited something under his breath. When he had finished his recitation, he raised the wrist, and it was completely cured — there was not the slightest feeling of pain in it. The man was astonished. He asked Maulana Ali, "Ya Ali! What did you just recite?" He replied, "I recited Surah al-Fateha." The man was greatly surprised. In wonder he said, "You merely recited Surah al-Fateha, and that mended my wrist?" That is, in his heart he felt that a plain, ordinary surah like al-Fateha could not possibly mend his wrist. The moment he said those words, his wrist reverted to its broken state.

So this is a surah that cures — but only if I place my faith in it, only if I believe in its power and its magnificence. This surah has the power to cure ailments and diseases, both spiritual and physical. But it requires faith. It is like a person honoring an experienced physician, respecting him, acknowledging his knowledge and his skill before asking him for a cure. I cannot walk up to a specialist and say, "Hey! You are just an ordinary doctor. Where I come from, there is one of you sitting under every tree. Now cure me!" I cannot do that. It will not work. Naturally, he is going to prescribe tic-tacs to cure my kidney infection. If I am turning to a physician for help, I first need to have faith in him. I must trust his abilities, his knowledge, his skill — only then will he be able to help me.

Then there are other narrations in which those who perform spiritual healing (رقیا) make abundant use of Surah al-Fateha as well. Rasul Allah said:

فاتحة الكتاب علاجٌ لِكُلِّ السُّم

"The Opening of the Book is a cure for every poison." If the faith is strong, this surah can be the cure for every spiritual and physical poison that exists.

So one of the names of Surah al-Fateha is also Surah al-Shifa.

Surah al-Asaas

Then this surah is also called Surah al-Asaas, or Asaas al-Qur'an, which means the foundation, or the foundation of the Qur'an. In one of the narrations, Rasul Allah (SAS) said:

إنا لكل شيءٍ أساسٌ، وأساسُ القرآنُ سورۃ الفاتحة‏

There is no doubt that EVERYTHING in this world has a basis, a foundation. And the foundation of the Qur'an is Surah al-Fateha.

The word asaas, or foundation,

You know, we try to answer the question of Allah's existence through scientific analysis and all these different philosophies. But to me, personally, this book, the Qur'an, is enough proof for the existence of Allah. I truly do not need anything more than this book. The perfection and precision I see in this magnificent speech, the depth I find in the meanings of these words, to me, this is all the evidence I will ever need. It is simply not possible for any human being to produce such a perfect text. And that is the experience I want to share with all of you.

But even more than the style, what I really want to share is the actual message of this surah. For it is not only that the message of al-Fatiha is so beautiful; it is also the ultimate key to our salvation. So what I truly want us to do is enter the mindset of the ancient Arabs, so that we can truly appreciate this message as they appreciated it. I want us to hear what they heard. I want us to experience what they experienced. For this message completely transformed their lives.

And it has been transforming lives for the past fourteen hundred years. There is absolutely no reason why it cannot transform ours as well. People have devoted their entire lives to understanding this book.

And let me be clear: none of what I am about to share with you is my own work. I stand on the shoulders of many, many scholars, ulama, and duaat — my teachers, people who have given their lives to the comprehension of this book. All I have done is gather their work and put it in order. So everything you hear, I have taken from their labor. I take no credit whatsoever for this remarkable knowledge. All I did was study the research of these wonderful people and then make thorough notes on it — so that I might benefit from it, and so that, God willing, my children may one day benefit from it as well. But then, praise be to God, through the blessings of my elders, I was given this opportunity to share this knowledge with my family and with the children of the jamaat too. بأذن اللہ. So may God bless them and reward them abundantly for all their remarkable efforts, and grant us the strength to truly appreciate, absorb, and understand these remarkable ayats — these miraculous signs — and, above all, to turn them into action, so that we may better our life in this world and in the hereafter. God willing.

There are generally two ways to study the Qur'an. One is to study it surah by surah — we study all the ayats of one surah and then move on to the next. The other is to take a handful of topics and discuss them in detail, drawing on ayats from all across the Qur'an. God willing, I intend to do both. We are going to study Surah Fateha primarily, but we will also study some other surahs that fall within the context of, and are related to, Surah al-Fateha — because in the end, every single surah in the Qur'an is connected to al-Fateha. So while studying this surah, we will also discuss specific topics that fall within the realm of these ayats.

It means the lowest, load-bearing part of a building, or the underlying basis or principle of something. What, then, is the foundation upon which the very structure of our existence stands? Why is this surah called the foundation? It is called asaas because Surah al-Fateha discusses the three main phases of creation that form the foundation and basis of our existence.

The first is the beginning, مبدأ, which goes back to one of the names and attributes of Allah (swt), مُبدِع, the Originator, the Creator. Who created me? Where did I come from? I was not in this world before a certain date, so where was I before I was created in this world? And who created me? And why was I created? That is the first three ayats of Surah al-Fateha: بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم۔ الحمد للہ رب العالمین۔ الرحمن الرحیم. It is Allah who created me. بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم. It is Allah who brought me into this world, and creating me was an act of His mercy and His رحمۃ, because He is al-Rahman and He is al-Raheem. And why did He create me? So that I could fulfill the obligations and responsibilities of الحمد للہ رب العالمین, because Allah is worthy of my praise and my gratitude, for bringing me into this world, feeding me, clothing me, sustaining me, making this world beautiful and pleasurable for me, and giving me the senses and the capabilities to enjoy those pleasures.

The beauty of this world exists in exactly the same way for a blind man, but does he enjoy it the same way you and I do? The offerings of this world exist equally for a handicapped person, in exactly the same way as they do for you and me, but can he access them and enjoy them the same way you and I do? What if Allah had not given me the capabilities to enjoy this world? What if He took these capabilities away from me today? What would happen then? Where would I be then? For these things, and for so very many other things in this world, for the creation of this magnificent world, and for my existence within it, to enjoy its glory and its pleasures, and for the creation of those I love and care for, and for the creation of those who love and care for me, what must I do? الحمد للہ رب العالمین. I must praise Allah and be grateful to Allah. So the first foundation described in this surah is مبدأ, the beginning.

The second foundation this surah looks at is the end, the return, and the resurrection, معاد. Just as I did not exist in this world before a certain date, I know that I am not going to be in this world after a certain date. So where will I go? To whom will I return? And what is going to happen after that? Am I going to be held accountable? Will I be asked questions? Will I be judged? What happens if I pass that judgment? What happens if I fail the judgment? Who will be the judge? What will be his criteria for judgment? All of that is encapsulated in مالک یوم الدین.

Finally, this surah speaks of how we, as Allah's creation, must live our lives between these two stages of life and death. It is the state of being in His obedience and asking for His guidance in following the straight path, اھدنا الصراط المستقیم, the path of those upon whom He had mercy when they returned to Him, صراط الذین انعمت علیھم, and not the path of those who faced Allah's wrath, غیر المغضوب علیھم, not the path of those who strayed from the straight path, ولاالضالین. All of that is covered in Surah al-Fateha. So that is one of the many reasons.

why Surah al-Fateha is called Surah al-Asaas — because it speaks of the three primary stages of human existence: our birth, our return, and our life in between. That is why it is called Surah al-Asaas.

Placing Musa in a basket freed an entire enslaved nation.

So these are some of the names of Surah al-Fateha, and how the meanings of the names connect to their inner purpose. Now the real question is: what can I do with this information? Is this all simply great factual information, or is there any practical application to it? How does understanding the various names of Surah al-Fateha help me in my life? Well, let us think about it. Information creates concepts, concepts feed our beliefs, and beliefs then turn into our actions. So how do the names of Surah al-Fateha affect my concepts and my belief system?

I learned that the name Fateha means an opening, and it means victory. So now, when I am stuck in any situation of my life, when I am caught in a problem, when I cannot figure out a solution to a problem, or when the solution seems to be out of my hands, I know the recitation of this surah will provide me with that opening. It will provide me with that way out. When I am surrounded by problems and challenges with my family members, with my children, at work, in life, when I am not able to get through them, I know this surah can help me win over those challenges. It can create a path, an opening for me. It can give me a victory over my challenges.

I also learned that it is not just Fateha, but al-Fateha, and the al is the al of faith. A faith that transcends logic! A trust so deep that it defies all logical arguments.

Think about this. When Musa, peace be upon him, is born, Firaun has already passed a law that all newborn male infants should be killed. Babies are being killed left and right, and Allah decides to bring Musa, peace be upon him, into the world during that very time. He could have brought him into the world before the babies were killed, or after the madness was over, could he not? Would that not be logical? And He is علی کل شیء قدیر, so it is not as though He had any difficulty doing that, is it? So that is the first thing that defies logic.

Now, moving forward, we learn that Musa's mother turns to Allah for protection. And what does Allah do? Allah commands her to place Musa, peace be upon him, in a basket and cast him into the river. Excuse me? I am sorry, I do not think I heard you correctly. Did you say place my child in a basket and float him down the river? O Allah! You do know the idea is actually to save him, do you not?

Think about it! His mother wants to save Musa, peace be upon him, from death, and Allah is asking her to put him in a basket and float him down the river. Just imagine you are Musa's mother right now. Imagine you have been asked to place your child in a basket and cast him into the river. And all of this is God's great plan to do what? To save his life! You would be thinking, say what? Would you not? But what does history show us? We see later on that Musa's mother placing Musa in the river is what brings down the entire Pharaonic empire, does it not? That one act brings down not only Firaun's empire; it also frees an enslaved nation. Truly! Amazing lessons and messages in the Quran.

So too, if we truly study them with care. From the meaning of al-Fatiha, then, I learned that I must have faith. I can lay my anxieties, my worries, and my sorrows to rest, knowing that I have surrendered myself to the will of Allah. The solution is no longer in my hands; it is in my Master's hands. He will take care of me. He will place the right answer in my heart. If I have no option before me, He will suggest the right one by setting it in my heart. If I have many options, He will guide me and help me choose the best one possible, provided I turn to Him for guidance.

I also learned that the recitation of this surah is a reminder. It reminds me that I am not the one in control; Allah is the one in control. I can govern my actions. I can make the best effort of which I am capable. But the outcome of my action, its final result, lies in the hands of Allah. If Allah decides that success is the best outcome for me, then I will succeed. If Allah decides that failure is the best outcome for me, if He knows that this very failure will serve as a cause, as a catalyst that moves me in the direction He desires, then I will fail, and through that failure I will succeed at last. In either case, therefore, I must keep my faith in Him. It is a reminder of my constant submission to Him.

The brothers of Yusuf, peace be upon him, cast him into a well and left him there to die. A caravan drew him out and sold him as a slave in the marketplace. Yet he rose to the highest rank in the royal court. When we study this chain of cause and effect that unfolds in his life, we find that none of it would have come to pass had his brothers not pushed him into the well. So merely because matters do not look their best today means nothing at all. As long as there is breath, there is hope that the best is yet to come.

Then I learned that Surah al-Fatiha is the gist, the essence, and the mother of the Quran. It is ام الکتاب، أم القرآن. I now know that when I recite this surah, I am reciting the essence of the entire Quran through these seven verses. I already know how powerful the Quran is; and if that entire Quran has been distilled into these seven verses, then I now understand the power of the recitation of this surah. If I compare Surah al-Fatiha to the sun, then it is a sun that holds within itself the power and the glory of seven magnificent suns, in the form of these seven verses.

So now this idea connects with the earlier teachings: that once I truly grasp how powerful this surah is, why then should it be any wonder that it can open a path for me, that it can grant me victories over my challenges? For after all, I am not merely reciting a surah; I am reciting Surah al-Fatiha, which holds within it the power and the glory of the entire Quran. Why then should it be any wonder if it guides me, if it helps me, protects me, sustains me, elevates me, and cures me? Why should any of that surprise me? After all, this is al-Fatiha, the mother, the gist, and the essence of the entire Quran.

Then I learned that it is the most frequently recited seven verses in all the world. Even its name, al-Fatiha, has seven letters, which symbolizes this very fact. There is not a single moment in time when Surah al-Fatiha is not being recited somewhere in the world. This teaches me that this surah, and its lessons,

and their practical application must be a constant reminder in MY world, in MY life, in every single waking moment of my life. I should be aware of the teaching of this surah, and I should be putting it into practice in my life. May Allah grant me, and all of us, the strength to brighten our lives with the noor, the light, of this magnificent surah.

Then I learned that Surah al-Fatiha is a priceless treasure: فاتحۃُ الکتابِ مِن کُنُوزِ تحت العرش. It is a priceless treasure kept beneath the throne of our Master, which He holds close to Himself at all times, because He knows its worth. In olden days, when someone needed an audience with a king, they would bring beautiful jewels along with them to catch the king's eye. They would draw the king in with these precious jewels, and the king would be compelled to look at them and to listen to what they had to say. These seven verses of Surah al-Fatiha are those priceless jewels, which we carry with us to draw in Allah, our Master and our Lord, so that we may catch His attention. With the recitation of this surah we compel Him to look at us, to attend to us, and to fulfill our needs.

How sad it is that our Master, knowing and appreciating the worth of these priceless jewels, handed them to us, yet we, as servants, do not understand their worth. We see them as nothing more than stones. May Allah, through His knowledge, grant us the wisdom and the awareness of these glorious verses.

So another thing I learned is that when I approach my Master with this priceless treasure, He will not turn me away. He will fulfill my needs and bless me with what I ask for.

I also learned that this is a surah that cures both physical and spiritual ailments. It is Surah al-Shifa. If I have the faith it requires, I learned that this surah can work miracles in my physical and spiritual healing. If I am struggling with something, for example, if there is a bad habit that I am trying to quit, or a good habit that I am struggling to adopt and establish within myself, then I know that the recitation of this lofty surah can help me accomplish that goal. But I also learned that if I do not have the faith it requires in the power of this majestic surah, then even if someone like Maulana Ali were to recite it and attempt to heal me with it, it would have no effect on me. So faith in this surah is critical to its working.

I could go on and on about the practical, actionable tasks that I can draw from this surah, but I hope that what I have presented will be a good starting point. The more you reflect, the more you will be able to find ways to act upon this surah. And mind you, everything I have just shared has come ONLY from understanding the meaning of the various different NAMES of Surah al-Fatiha. We have not even begun to study the surah itself. Understanding the names of this surah alone is enough to transform our lives forever. Just imagine, after we study and learn the wealth of knowledge these names hold and their practical applications, what kind of potential there is for transformation in our lives! SubhanAllah!

InshaAllah we will begin studying the actual surah today. But just to bring this topic to a close, there are a few other names of Surah al-Fatiha that I will only touch upon briefly, in order to complete the topic. This surah is also called Surah al-Kanz, the Surah of Treasure, and we now know why.

Because it is the most valuable and priceless treasure that the king of the worlds keeps beneath His throne. It is also called Surah ash-Shukr, the Surah of Gratitude, a name drawn chiefly from the verse الحمد للہ رب العلمین. It is also called Surah al-Kafiyah, the Surah of Sufficiency, because in each and every situation of our lives we find this surah sufficient to solve all our problems and meet all our needs. In any moment of joy, this surah is sufficient to multiply our happiness. And in any moment of sadness or weakness, this surah is sufficient for me as a loving and caring friend. That is why this surah is called Surah al-Kafiyah, the surah that is sufficient. It is sufficient as a friend, as a protector, as a guide. It is sufficient for every aspect of our lives. It is also called Surah al-Wafiyah, the Surah of Fulfillment, because by fulfilling its obligations and applying its teachings in our daily life, we fulfill our covenant, the agreement, the promise, the عہد شریف we made with Allah, and in return Allah will fulfill His promise with us and grant us the ultimate success in the afterlife. Wafiya comes from wafa, which means faithfulness. If we are faithful to the teachings of our master through this surah, He will be faithful to us in keeping His promise. He says, وَمَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ. Who is more faithful than Allah in keeping a promise? And finally, it is also called Surah al-Waqiyah, the Surah of Protection, because it protects us from all the physical and spiritual harm of this world and the afterlife, as we will soon see, God willing. So these are the various names of Surah al-Fatiha.

We will study the topic of God and His messenger Muhammad Mustafa, peace be upon him, in particular. Then other topics that answer questions such as: What is the purpose of our creation? What are the things that you and I struggle with most as Muslims? What puts our faith, and ultimately our salvation, in danger? Those are primarily the topics I want to address. But above all, the topic of Salaah — of Namaaz — for that is the main component of Surah al-Fateha, as we will soon see, God willing. I want to discuss the what and the why of it.

But finally, before we begin, here is the most important thing I want to say. Look — studying the Qur'an is a wonderful thing. But all of this intellectual effort, and all of this remarkable content, means absolutely nothing if it does not bring about a change in our lives. There is informational knowledge, and then there is transformational knowledge. The purpose of our studying Surah al-Fateha is to acquire that transformational knowledge. Something in us needs to transform — even if only in the slightest. No one is perfect. None of us is perfect, and we never, ever will be. But you know what? God has not asked us for perfection. All He asks of us is a sincere effort. We need only take the first few steps, and then He Himself will carry us all the way to our destination. Perfection belongs to God alone.

So we do not need to feel that we must be perfect. We need only become better accountants. It is a matter of debit and credit, after all. And what a magnificent blessing it is: that on account of our beloved Prophet, peace be upon him, Allah said, "I will reward your umma tenfold for every good deed they perform, and for every sin they commit, I will record it only once. And know that good deeds consume evil deeds, as fire consumes dry wood." Glory be to God. Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate, did not say that His weighing of good and evil deeds would be done on an equal footing. It is to be on a ratio of ten to one. So we need only try, and make a sincere effort, and, God willing, we will succeed. How sorrowful and how wretched it would be if, in spite of this ratio of ten to one, we were still to end as losers in the life to come. May Allah protect us from such heedlessness.

And it is not easy. Sometimes we struggle with this most bitterly. I know that I do, and constantly, and that is why I keep confessing it to you. Simply because I possess all of this knowledge does not mean that my character and my conduct perfectly reflect it. They do not. I wish that they did, and I want them to, but they do not. So I will be the last person to tell you that you should or that you must do a certain thing. How could I? Indeed, to be wholly transparent with you, I have truly been struggling to continue these sessions. That is the very reason I cancelled the previous one. I actually went back to Javeed bhai and told him that I could not carry on these sessions on al-Fatiha, because I found such a disconnect between my actions and my knowledge, and I would feel like a hypocrite preaching to others. But then Javeed bhai, being the wise man that he is, said, "Look, Asif, you may cancel the sessions if you wish, and then neither you nor your group gains anything. Or you may make a decision that, from this point forward, you will make a sincere effort to bring your life into line with these teachings, and then you benefit, and your group benefits as well. Practice what you preach."

So I have decided that, God willing, I am going to make a very strong effort to transform my life according to these teachings. I know that I will struggle, and I know that I will fall, but I will keep rising again and I will keep moving forward, God willing, because I know that we truly must take these verses seriously. For once I have shared this knowledge with you, we are all held accountable. Listen to me very carefully. Once we have studied this Surah, these teachings will hang about our necks forever. About my neck most of all, for I am the one telling you all of this. Allah says, أَتَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ ؛ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ ٱلْكِتَبَ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ — You enjoin others to righteousness and forget to apply it to your own souls, even though you recite my verses to others? You fail to follow them yourselves? Do you not understand what you are doing?

So this is a truly frightening thing for me, because I know that everything I say will now hang over my neck and over yours. Allah is holding it over all of us. And if we turn back and ignore this, this word of Allah,

then listen to the punishment of those who ignored... listen to what Allah says about those who listen and then ignore....

وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ — Who is a greater wrongdoer

مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَتِ رَبِّهِ — than one who was reminded of the signs and miracles of his Master,

فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا — and then chose to ignore them; he did not care about them,

وَنَسِىَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ — and forgot all that he had done in the past. He did not care about any of his evil deeds. Even after hearing the ayats of Allah, even after hearing these very ayats, he went on sending his sins to Allah for processing, thinking: who cares!

إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً — We shall place a lock upon their hearts.

أَكِنَّةً — this actually means a place that cannot be reached... أَكِنَّةً is a truly hidden place, impossible to access. Allah says:

إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ — We shall set their hearts in a wholly inaccessible place, and they will never be able to understand these ayats of Allah. No matter how clearly and openly the ayats are recited to them, it will not reach their heart. "I simply cannot grasp these things. It makes no sense to me!"

وَفِىٓ آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًۭا — And in their ears I shall place a barrier.

وَقْر — this is in fact a very heavy load. When a person suffers from sinus pressure, the ears feel heavy and blocked; that is وَقْر. Allah says: I shall place a وَقْر, a spiritual block, upon their ears. And when the ears are badly congested, one can hear nothing at all. Allah says: I shall block their ears so that they cannot hear My guidance. Every time you hear it, it will be as though you never heard it; you will no longer be moved by it. No matter what good comes your way, it will bring about no transformation in your life.

And then He says:

وَإِن تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ فَلَن يَهْتَدُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًۭا — Allahu Akbar... This is the most frightening part of all.

وَإِن تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ — Even if you! O Messenger of Allah, even if YOU — أبلَغْ وَ أَقوَدْ دُعات العالَم — the most eloquent, the most powerful, the most extraordinary Dai the world has ever seen — even if you personally call them to guidance,

فَلَن يَهْتَدُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًۭا — they will never, ever turn to guidance again. O Messenger of Allah, you whose mighty speech shattered stones — even you will no longer be able to penetrate their hearts, all because they heard My ayats and chose to ignore them.

What am I compared to the Messenger of Allah? I am nothing. I am nothing. Our manaseeb are nothing, our elders are nothing, compared to the power of the تبلیغ of the Messenger of Allah (SAS). But when this dreadful crime is committed — the crime of hearing the ayats of Allah, understanding them, and then failing to act upon them — then even the Messenger of Allah (SAS) giving you and me guidance in person will make no difference to us. That is the punishment of one who continually ignores the ayats of Allah when he is reminded of them. This is a punishment that can befall me, and it can befall you, if we choose to ignore these ayats.

May Allah lengthen the lives of our duaat and manaseeb Kiraam, who are the source of this guidance for us; and may Allah protect us from being among those who do not take His ayats seriously — me most of all, for I am the one reminding you.

I'll translate this passage following the standard exactly.

I really have no excuse left after this... And I am so terrified to tread on this path... But because of the prayers of my elders and my loved ones, I am hopeful that Allah will help me walk on His straight path... Ameen Ya RabbulAlameen!

اعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم۔ بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم

Here is how I am going to do this: I am going to dive into a deep study of these verses of Surah AlFateha. I will be passing a lot of information your way, but I am going to try my best to keep things very simple for you. Still, I am aware that it might get a bit overwhelming for some of the younger children. If that happens, just try to understand the message and the purpose of the ayah, and forget about the linguistic analysis of the words. Those are only means to an end anyway. Our end goal is to understand the actual message of the ayaats.

This is a surah we all recite in our salaah all the time. The best way to remember what I am teaching you is to remind yourself of it during salaah. So once you understand the meaning of the ayah بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم, the next time you stand in salaah and recite this ayah, recite it with comprehension. Keep doing that until the next session, and then apply and practice what you learn in the next session during the week. That is how I am planning to do it, and I recommend the same to you. We learn something today, and over the next seven days we apply it and practice it in our lives. Then we learn something new next week, and then practice it for the next seven days, and so on.

A quick warning to parents: some of these sessions will be quite PG-13, which may not be appropriate for younger children. So parents, I will leave it up to you whether you want your children to be in these sessions or not. I will be talking about problems and challenges teenagers face in this day and age. You know what those things are. These are very difficult topics to talk about, but I think they are also really important to talk about. We cannot simply not talk about these things with our children and still expect them to do the right things. But at the same time, the way in which things are said does not have to be indecent or even uncomfortable. So InshaAllah I will try my best to talk about things in the best possible manner, using the style of the Quran itself. You know, the Quran talks about all these difficult topics, but it does so in such an elegant and decent manner. There is no reason why we cannot follow this sunna of the Quran and adopt the same method. I just wanted parents to be aware of that beforehand.

So let us begin.

Surah AlFateha is the most powerful, the most eloquent, and categorically the most recited surah in the entire Quran. As for the significance of this Surah, we know it is the most revered surah of the Quran. If we compare the Quran to a human body, Rasul Allah (SAS) called Surah Yaseen the heart of the Quran, قلب القرآن; he called Surah Ikhlaas the soul of the Quran, روح القرآن; and he called Surah AlFateha the soul of the soul of the Quran, روح الروح القرآن. As we know, the soul is the most essential component of our existence, the one that commands and controls and leads our body. If the soul departs from the body, the body would be reduced to nothing more than a rotting corpse. Similarly, if Surah Ikhlaas, which is the surah of tawheed,

It is the surah of the unification of Allah. If it were removed from the Quran, the Quran would be rendered worthless. And if Surah Fateha were removed, Surah Ikhlaas would become worthless, because the entire essence of the Quranic message is unification, the tawheed of Allah, which is Surah Ikhlaas, and the entire essence of the unification of Allah is the recognition of Allah, which comes through Surah Fateha. There is no loftier surah in the Quran than Surah Fateha. This is the reason it is the first and foremost, and the most obligatory surah when we pray. Without Surah Fateha there is no salaah.

The word salaah in Arabic comes from the word صِلی, or اتصال, which means connection. Connection with whom? Connection with Allah. This surah gives us human beings a way, a means by which we can recognize our master and connect with Him. It is the protocol ordained by Allah for His slaves when they approach Him. And, God willing, as we study this surah, the reasons behind this protocol will become clear.

Surah Fateha was not only one of the first Meccan surahs to be revealed, it was also the very first surah revealed in its entirety. Other surahs were not. For example, سورۃ العلق was the first surah to be revealed, but only its first few ayaats came down; the whole surah was not revealed at once. Likewise the early surahs Muzammil, Mudassir, and Noon were all revealed five or ten ayaats at a time, and the remaining ayaats were revealed later. Surah Fateha was the very first surah that came down in its entirety, and this shows its significance: before Allah revealed any complete surah, He sent down Surah Fateha whole, so that it could become the leader and king of all surahs.

Surah Fateha has many names. This surah is referred to by many names. But before we begin studying the various names of this surah and the reasons behind them, let us start with the meaning of the word "Surah" itself. Surah is very poorly translated into English as "Chapter." In the sessions on the miracles of the Quran, we studied why a surah cannot be called a chapter, because it does not match the definition of a chapter in any way, shape, or form.

The second question is: what is a surah? It is a collection of several ayaats. So who named this collection of ayaats a surah? These collections of ayaats were named by Allah AWJ Himself. He says in the Quran, وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍۢ مِّن مِّثْلِهِ — If you have any doubt about what We have revealed, then produce a surah similar to it. So Allah used the word surah in this ayah. In another place He says, وَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ أَنْ آمِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَجَهِدُوا۟ مَعَ رَسُولِهِ.

Linguistic meaning of Surah

So Allah Himself called these collections of ayaats a surah. Now, linguistically speaking, what is the meaning of the word surah? The word surah comes from the root word "soor," which means a fort, or the walls around a city. If you picture the old days, they did not have signs and landmarks at the borders to indicate that you were entering a new city. So what they would do is put up walls around a city so that they could control who entered and left. The Arabs called these outer walls around the city

صُور. So it is as if every surah has been fortified, every surah has been demarcated, like the boundaries of a city. With these defined boundaries, you know what is inside the surah, and you know what is outside the surah, just like the walls of a city let you know what lies inside the city and what lies outside it.

Now if we examine a city, inside each city there is always a great deal going on. There is commerce taking place, there are residential districts, there are military bases, all these different things happening within a single city. Yet even though they are all different things, they somehow all connect together to make up one city. In the same way, there is a great deal going on inside a surah. There are all these different and disparate passages within one surah, but they all somehow connect together to form one single context and one particular message. So even though the ayats within a surah may seem disconnected, they all come together, amazingly, in meaning, to deliver a single unified message.

Then we see that there is also a connection between separate, independent cities. When you leave one city, you automatically enter another; there is a common road or pathway that joins the last portion of one city to the beginning of the next. In the same way, there is cohesion between the last thing you read about in the previous surah and the first thing you read about in the next surah. So there is a link between the conclusion of one surah and the introduction of the next. The last thing said in Surah al-Kausar is connected to the first thing in Surah al-Kafiroon, and the last thing said in Surah al-Kafiroon is connected to the first thing in Surah al-Nasr, and so on. So although it may not seem apparent, these are not randomly arranged surahs. There is a very clear and precise flow and transition that takes place from one surah to the next. SubhanAllah!

Then the boundary walls of a city always follow an irregular circular pattern. In the same way, the end of a surah is connected to its beginning, and this is a very consistent feature of the Quran, which we saw in the symmetrical dimension of the Quran. Every surah, what it begins with is connected to what it ends with. There is a strong cohesion between the beginning of the surah (the مفاتیح الصور) and the end of the surah (the خواتیم الصور).

The Quran is partitioned into 114 distinct surahs, each surah having its own set of ayaats, meaning ayaats that are specific only to that particular surah, and it also has ayaats that are repeated across different surahs. This too is like visiting a different city: you see places, landmarks, and monuments that are specific to that city, but you also see places that remind you of places in your own city. So just as cities have their own unique places but also share certain commonalities with other cities, in the same way certain ayaats are unique within a surah, while certain ayaats are also repeated in various other surahs.

So even from a linguistic point of view, the word صورۃ, derived from the outer walls of a city, صُور, perfectly describes these collections of ayaats. We know that the word ayah means a miraculous sign. You put them both together, you put صورۃ and آیات together,

And we can now think of a surah as a boundary for a collection of miraculous signs. SubhanAllah!

Story of Adam — the Importance of Knowledge

As I explained last time, the first four verses of the Qur'an give us knowledge about Allah. The Qur'an addresses the اولو الباب, those who are people of sound essence. And sound essence is a combination of two things: a healthy heart and a healthy intellect. For the word عقل, in its linguistic sense, can mean both. It can mean the heart as well as the intellect. This عقل is a gift given to human beings so that they might recognize their Creator.

When Allah resolved to create Adam, upon him be peace, the angels raised an objection. They said:

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ. قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ

They said: You wish to create one who will spread corruption and shed blood? If you are creating man to glorify you and to offer you hamd, we are already doing that. You have no need of man for it, for we are here before you. We can see you, and we can hear you, and that is why we are able to offer you our hamd. You are creating Adam and the children of Adam for the earth. They will not be able to see you, and so they will not be able to recognize you; and because they do not recognize you, they will spread corruption in that earth.

And Allah answered:

قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

Allah said: I know what you do not know. I have knowledge of that which you have no knowledge of.

Then he taught Adam the names, the divine names:

وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا

He gave Adam the knowledge of all the names. And when he presented Adam, upon him be peace, before the angels, he asked them:

فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسْمَآءِ هَٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَدِقِينَ

He said: Inform me of these glorious names, if you are truthful in your claim — your claim to be the only ones able to offer me hamd and glorification.

قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

The angels said: You are exalted. We have no knowledge except that which you have given us. Without doubt, you are al-Aleem, the most knowing, and al-Hakeem, the most wise.

قَالَ يَٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ

He said: O Adam, inform them of all the names.

فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ

When Adam informed them of the names, Allah said: Did I not tell you that I possess the knowledge of everything, of what you reveal and what you conceal?

So we see that the word for knowledge, علم, is repeated again and again throughout these exchanges. And the message to the angels was this: Yes, I am creating Adam as my representative upon the earth, and he will not be able to see me with his eyes; but as Adam has just shown, I have given him the ability to learn, to know, and to acquire knowledge. And I have already taught him my names, my divine attributes, before sending him down to the earth. So even though he will not see me, he will see my attributes reflected in the universe I have created for him. He will see my signs, within himself and outside of himself, and they will remind him of me. And through those attributes, his heart will recognize me.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
And so these four verses give us the knowledge of Allah — بسم اللہ, with the name of Allah, with the name of the essence that is the sum of all its attributes.

The Allah who is الرحمن الرحیم, intensely merciful, constantly merciful. Then, الحمد للہ رب العالمین. What did that merciful Allah do? He created the ALAMEEN. He created everything that is known. And within that ALAMEEN, He reflected His divine attributes, so that we could recognize Him through those ASMAA. And then He took on its ownership, its rububiyyah. So this is what He did for the creation. And in return for His rububiyyah, the creation now owes Him a debt. A debt of submission, a debt of HAMD, of praise and gratitude. This is the message of الحمد للہ رب العالمین.

بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم was about WHO He is. الحمد للہ رب العالمین is about WHAT He did. Then الرحمن الرحیم gives us the knowledge of HOW He carries out His RUBUBIYYAH. The emotion behind His interaction with His creation, which is of intense love, care, concern, and mercy, and with CONSTANT love, care, concern, and mercy. And then finally مالک یوم الدین. The first three verses apply to ALL creation, including us, because He is the Rabb of everything that is known. He is Rehman and Raheem in His interactions with EVERYTHING in existence. But مالک یوم الدین is ONLY about human beings. Why? Because everything else is ALREADY paying its debt to its creator. It is ONLY human beings who have yet to pay their debt. This is why THIS is the central verse. It is right in the center. The first three verses are building up to this one. And the verses after this are in recognition of the fact that He is Malik Yaum AdDeen, which I will show you in a bit, InshaAllah. But this is the TRUE essence of the Fateha. That HE is our OWNER. He is the king, and we OWE Him a debt of submission. We owe Him دین الاسلام.

ان الدین عند اللہ الاسلام

No doubt, the true debt that creation owes Allah is their submission. And that day is coming when we WILL be taken to account for what we owe.

So the first four verses are essentially explaining Allah's relationship with His creation. They are constructing a mindset that everything that is CREATED is in a state of UBOODIYAH, and they have absolutely NO choice in the matter.

ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِىَ دُخَانٌۭ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًۭا قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ

He said to the heavens and the earth, come to me, willingly or unwillingly. Allah did not give them free will. But when it came to us,

وَقُلِ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ فَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن وَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ

Say to them, the truth of their Rabb has been revealed. Whoever wants can believe, and whoever wants can reject. So the entire ALAMEEN is demonstrating that Allah created them for submission, and they have no choice in the matter. This means YOU and I are created for submission, for UBOODIYAH, for slavery as well. The only difference is, they do not have a choice, but we do.

Why choose Allah as master?
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
And, by the way, if guidance were just information, how many times would we need that information? Only once. Once I have been given the information, I do not have to ask for it again. But how many times do we ask Allah for guidance? Over and over and over again, as a matter of course. It is like drinking water. You cannot say, "I drank water yesterday, so I do not need it again, I am fine." That does not work. If you want to survive, you have to drink again and again and again. Just as every few hours our bodies need water, every few hours our hearts need guidance. So we have to come back to Allah and say, اھدنا الصراط المستقیم. A few hours later our fuel runs low, and so we have to stand before him and ask for that guidance again. If guidance were only about information, it would not have been repeated in this way. Just as there is a constant thirst for water, there is a constant thirst for guidance, for renewal. Because those four enemies I spoke about are constantly weighing us down, and that is why we have to go before Allah again and again and ask him for that recharge.

TAKE A BREAK

SIRAAT

Now let us talk about Siraat. What is a siraat? A siraat is a path. But you know, in Arabic the word Siraat can only be used for a straight path. If a road is bumpy, or if it curves, or is wavy, it cannot be called a Siraat. By definition the word Siraat implies that the path has to be straight. A Suraat is in fact a perfectly straight sword. If the sword is curved, it is called Saif. So a Siraat is a perfectly straight path. That is the first meaning.

Siraat also means a wide path. It cannot be a narrow path. It is a wide path, so that many people can travel on it at the same time. So you do not have to push someone else aside to make room for yourself. You do not have to do that. You understand?

Now there are other words in Arabic that can be used for a path. There is Sabeel. There is Faj. There is Tareeq. The interesting thing about these words is that plurals are available for all of them. For Sabeel there is Subul, for Tareeq there is Taraiq, for Faj there is Fijaaj. But there is no plural for the word Siraat. It is a singular word. And this is why Siraat also means the only path that is available. So imagine there are two islands, and there is a bridge connecting the two. The water between these two islands is very turbulent, so you cannot take a boat to go from one to the other. The only way for you to go from one island to the other is the bridge, and there is no other path you can take except the bridge. So if there is no alternative route available, then that bridge,
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
that one singular path is called Siraat. So linguistically, Siraat has a few characteristics. It is a wide path. It is a straight path. And it is the only path possible. Do you know what that means for us? It means there can only be one true religion. And within that one true religion, there can only be one true sect. Is that not incredible? Simply by understanding the linguistics of the word, it answers all the questions we have. Because people ask this question all the time: Why must there be only one true religion? Why can every religion not be the true religion? Because the word Siraat has no plural. So it can only be singular. SubhanAllah!

Now every single human being believes that he or she is on the right path. Every single sect, including us, we all believe that we are following the correct sect. But according to the linguistic meaning of the word Siraat, only one religion, and only one sect within that religion, can be the right one. So now, why do we say that Sulemaniyat is the Siraat, the one true path?

Let us talk about that for a moment. In order to judge anything in the world, we need very specific criteria. How do we declare that the Himalayas are the tallest mountains in the world? We go by very specific criteria: height, air pressure, air temperature. We measure the Himalayas against these criteria, and then we compare our findings with all the other mountains, and based on the results, we conclude, with conviction, that the Himalayas are the tallest mountains in the world. We are not on the fence about that conclusion, are we? We are not of two minds about it. No. Because it is a definite conclusion. It is solid mathematical proof.

What did I just tell you about the criteria that Allah has set for us in the word Huda? Knowledge! To judge and measure the criteria of religion, the only tool, the measuring stick that has been provided to us by the Aleem, is Ilm. Knowledge. And because we possess knowledge of realities, of perspectives, that other sects cannot even imagine, concepts that perfectly align with the Qur'an, without a single contradiction, that is how we conclude, with absolute conviction, that we are on the Siraat.

You will find many Muslims who take an ayah and pass a fatwa on certain things based on that ayah. But then what they say contradicts other ayats in the Qur'an. And Allah says:

أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ ٱلْكِتَبِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍۢ

Do you believe in certain portions of the book and then deny or reject other portions? How does that make sense? Because Allah made consistency a very definitive argument for the Qur'an being the true word of Allah.

أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ؟ وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُوا۟ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلَفًۭا كَثِيرًۭا

Do you not reflect on the Qur'an? Had this been from anyone other than Allah, you would find tremendous amounts of contradiction within it. And the more you study the uloom of these other sects, the more contradiction you will find in their concepts. One scholar says one thing, the other scholar says the complete opposite thing.

Whereas the more you study our uloom — Taveel, MabdaMaad, Haqaiq, Daqaiq — extremely complex topics, but you will never find any contradiction between them. And that, to us, is proof that we are following the Siraat. And we have answers to every question that exists. And every answer is proven by the Qur'an. SubhanAllah!
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
Hazrat Zia Ali Sahab Muqaddas used to say: we have answers to questions that have not yet even been asked. AlHamdulillah, AlHamdulillah, AlHamdulillah. Truly, we cannot praise Allah enough, and we cannot thank Allah enough, for placing us upon the Siraat. Mustaqeem.

Now, mustaqeem. How is Mustaqeem usually translated? As the straight path. But consider this: the word Siraat already implies straightness. If it were not straight, it would not be a Siraat. So why would Allah repeat himself? He does not. Because Mustaqeem does not mean merely straight; it means straight upward. Mustaqeem comes from QAMA, or ISTIQAAMA, to stand up. Not to go forward, but to go up. It is from QIYAAM, which means to stand upright. We are asking Allah for guidance upon a path that heads in which direction? Straight up.

This means that the longer I travel this path, the further I move away from the duniya. Is that not true? And the higher I rise, the greater my rank becomes in the eyes of God, and the closer I draw to him. Is that not so? And as you climb higher, what happens? Your view improves; you begin to gain a better perspective on things. And because walking this path is a matter of acquiring knowledge, the more we learn, the more knowledge we gain, and the more aware we become of the realities of this world and of the afterlife.

But there is also a negative side to this. For the higher you climb, the greater the danger you face of falling. Is that not true? If you are only one foot above the ground and you fall, you will be fine. If you are twenty feet high and you fall, you will not be so fine. If you are a hundred feet high and you fall, انا للہ و انا الیہ راجعون. Right? In other words, the person who has been traveling upon this path for a long time, is he in less danger or in more danger? He is in more danger.

Sometimes people wonder about those who have reached such great heights in religion — and I am speaking of the sincere ones, not the false ones, for we have many of those as well. But one thing you will always notice is that the higher a person's rank, the more khushoo he has, the more fear he carries in his heart, the more he weeps upon the janemaaz during salaat. Why is that? He is such a good man; he never misses his prayers; he never misses a single fast; he has performed hundreds of Hajj. He is always reciting Qur'an. He never does the things that I do. Then why does he weep so much? I am the one who ought to be weeping all the time. Right? We say things about the Manaseeb: why does he not take affirmative action? Why is he so relaxed about everything? He sees everything, he has the power, so why does he not do something about it?

People do not realize that the higher you go, the more frightening it becomes. And these people do realize it, and so they take every single step with extreme caution, to make certain they do nothing that could cause harm in the long run. And in their salaat, when they are alone, they are forever weeping out of fear that they might do something that would make them fall. For is there any guarantee that you will not fall? No.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
So we say to Allah, اھدنا الصراط المستقیم. O Allah, guide us with true knowledge; guide us with the practical examples of your beloved and chosen people.

and as I set out on my own journey, as I begin to walk, be my companion at every single step upon this path that is straight, that is wide, and that is the only one — the path that rises upward. We begin our journey upon this dangerous path, and the higher we climb, the more beautiful and the clearer the view becomes; yet at the very same time it grows more difficult, and more terrifying. This is why we ask Allah for his constant help, his عون, his استعانۃ, so that we may reach the destination and not fall. That is اھدنا الصراط المستقیم.

And there is a linguistic point as well: the tone of this verse carries the cry of one in desperation. It is the tone of a person dying of thirst, begging for water. It is not a light and laughing "guide us on the straight path, or whatever — there is no rush." No. It is a desperate cry for help: O Allah, guide us upon this path, or we are doomed.

Then he says, صراط الذین انعمت علیھم. Why does he say siraat once more? He has only just used it in the previous verse. He should have said الذین انعمت علیھم, for to withhold a pronoun where a pronoun could be used is poor grammar. It destroys the eloquence, does it not? So to repeat the word siraat is a linguistic flaw — unless it is speaking of a different siraat. Do you understand this? This is very important to grasp. Grammatically, if both of these siraat referred to the same path, then the surah ought to have read اھدنا الصراط المستقیم الذین انعمت علیھم — "Guide me to the straight path, the one upon which you poured your blessing." Allah ought not to have repeated the word siraat. From the standpoint of eloquence, from the standpoint of balagha, the only reason it can be repeated is that this siraat is different from the one before.

And notice that this time he did not use the word mustaqeem. He did not say الصراط المستقیم الذین انعمت علیھم, which means that this is not a vertical path. So what path is it? This is the path of Islam. And the previous path was the path of Eman. This path lies upon the horizontal plane, just as Islam lies upon the horizontal plane. The previous path was the path of Eman, which by its very definition is always upon the vertical plane, because it concerns Allah, and the angels, and heaven, and revelation — all of which are above us — or it concerns the fire, which is below us. For that reason the word mustaqeem is used. SubhanAllah! Only look at the perfection of this speech. Allahu Akbar — I have goose bumps.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
Has anyone ever been to the Empire State Building? Or the Dubai towers? Or any high-rise building, for that matter? You know that there is an elevator that carries you up that tower. Its motion is vertical. But what must you do to reach that elevator? You must take the road that leads to the building, must you not? Only then can you board that vertical elevator. Islam is that siraat which brings us to the elevator, the siraat of Eman. Islam is easy, because it is upon the horizontal plane. Eman is difficult; it is dangerous, because it is upon the vertical plane. And this is why, when you remain strictly at the level of Islam — if the only knowledge you ever gain is knowledge of Islam — it becomes extremely confusing. This does not make sense; that does not make sense; why must I do this? And the answer given is almost always: because Allah said so. For that is the only answer available upon this horizontal plane. But when you begin to climb the steps of Eman, your perspective improves, and your view grows clear. Perspective upon what? As we rise above the duniya.

As we rise above this horizontal plane, our view improves upon what? Upon the duniya itself, upon the horizontal axis. In the same way, as we rise in the knowledge of Eman, our perspective upon Islam improves; through the knowledge of taveel, of mabda and maad, of the haqaiq, our clarity upon Islam and upon the shareeah improves.

The path of the one you had mercy upon. Then He says: صراط الذین انعمت علیھم. The path of those upon whom YOU bestowed Your favors. It is in the past tense. Why the past tense? Because all the role models exist upon the path. If you want some good career advice, from whom will you seek it? From your fellow students, or from those who have graduated? Obviously the graduates. You are not going to ask the friends who are studying alongside you in school for career advice. If you want to become a doctor, you will take advice from doctors who have graduated. What courses did you take? How did you get into that program? What are the things I need to focus on? So the Qur'an says: صراط الذین انعمت علیھم. The path of those upon whom YOU showered Your blessings. The path of the prophets, the path of the messengers, the martyrs, and the righteous people.

انعمت comes from the word نِعَم, which means something very smooth and soft. You know the Arabic word for cattle, for cows and sheep: they are called انعام, because they walk slowly, gently, and smoothly. So: Allah, walk me upon the path of those whom You carried through this trial of the world softly and smoothly. That is صراط الذین انعمت علیھم.

غیر المغضوب علیھم. Not upon the path of those who received GHADAB, who became the recipients of wrath. ولا الضالین. And not upon the path of those who are lost.

This is SO interesting. When the ayah spoke of blessings, نعمۃ, it read: upon whom YOU showered Your blessings. But when it came to GHADAB, the ayah reads المغضوب علیھم. Those who received the ghadab. It leaves out the subject. It simply says: THOSE who received anger. Not those who received YOUR anger. NO.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
When I say "He got beaten," the question is WHO did the beating? It could be one, it could be many, right? So what this is telling us is that those who receive the anger are not merely receiving Allah's anger. They are receiving the anger of the messengers, of the angels, of the other believers, of the heaven, of the earth. They are receiving the wrath and the anger from all directions. And so the ayah does not mention Allah when it speaks of GHADAB. It mentions Him specifically when it speaks of blessings. انعمت علیھم, the ones YOU showered blessings upon; but غیر المغضوب علیھم, not upon those who received anger. Because ANGER, GHADAB, was never the intention of Allah to begin with, for He is Rehman and Raheem. So whatever THEY did, they did to themselves. They earned it for themselves. But the ones who received blessings, Allah helped them all along, TOWARD the path, WITH the help of intermediaries, ALONG the way with His HUDA, with His knowledge.

So صراط الذین انعمت علیھم, in other words, means: upon the path of those to whom You granted KNOWLEDGE. The knowledge of realities, the knowledge of how to act upon them through role models like Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) and Maulana Ali, and then the divine companionship itself along the way. SubhanAllah!

By the way, who can speak with this level of perfection? The Qur'an is a spoken word, remember? Who can speak like this without ANY editorial process? AllahuAkbar! So صراط الذین انعمت علیھم.

The path of those to whom You gave knowledge, and who then acted upon that knowledge. غیر المغضوب علیھم. Not the path of those to whom You gave knowledge, but who still chose not to act upon it. ولاضالین. Nor the path of those who act, but who have no knowledge of what they are doing. Ad-dalleen means those who are lost, those who did not know any better.

Let us understand the difference between the maghdoob alayhim and the dalleen. I will give you an example. In my house I have Erum and Amir. Erum is nine years old and Amir is three, mashaAllah. They both love chocolate chip cookies. I buy a fresh box from the store, I show it to Erum, and I say, "Are these your favorite cookies? See how nice and fresh they look. Here, smell it. Does it smell good? Well, you cannot have them. I am going to place them here on the table, and then I am going to go downstairs to my basement for the Sunday sessions. When I come back up, we will all eat these together. Until then, do not touch these cookies, and also make sure that Amir does not eat them. All right? Do you understand? Good girl."

I go down to the basement, I finish my sessions, and when I come back upstairs, what do I find on the couch? Two little cookie monsters, both of them wolfing the cookies down. Now, with whom am I going to be truly angry, Erum or Amir? Erum, of course. Because I explicitly and clearly told her not to eat the cookies. Amir did not even know about it. So naturally I am going to be far angrier with Erum. You knew better. I told you plainly not to eat these cookies, and you disobeyed me anyway. You are grounded until you become a teenager. And while I am scolding her, Amir looks up at me innocently and goes on eating the cookies.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
So do you understand? This is the difference between the maghdoob alayhim and the dalleen. The maghdoob are those who were given the نعمۃ of knowledge, and who still disobeyed Allah and still did the wrong thing. But the dalleen are those who had no idea that they were doing wrong. This does not mean they are innocent. It does not mean they will not be called to account, because Allah gave us the intellect, which is the proof and the hujjah both for and against every single one of us, that we are to seek knowledge. These people ought to have striven to gain the knowledge of Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, that they needed, and to do the right thing. They ought to have made the effort to know better. So they are not off the hook in any sense. Yet they are still better than the maghdoob alayhim. Do you understand?

Some people, when they learn this, say, "You know what, I am not going to gain any knowledge at all. I am going to remain ignorant, because then at least I will not become one of the dalleen." Wait, wait, wait. That is not a good idea, my friend. Because Allah says, غیر المغضوب علیھم ولا الضالین. Not the path of those who earned anger, nor of those who remained lost. The dalleen will lose out too, and they will be punished for not trying to find the right path. Both are groups of losers. So it is truly not a wise idea to be from either group. The group we want to belong to is the انعمت علیھم group.

And this is the real message of the Fateha: the balance between knowledge and action. بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم. الحمد للہ رب العالمین. الرحمن الرحیم. مالک یوم الدین. These are all about the knowledge we need. Then, ایاک نعبد و ایاک نستعین. This is our recognition.

Our acceptance of this knowledge as the one true knowledge, and our commitment to Allah. Our sacred pledge. O Allah, we willingly give up our freedom to become your slaves. We will try our best to carry out your commands of worship and obedience, and we will need your help every step of the way. This is our commitment to Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala: that through the knowledge you have given us of the worlds, we have recognized that we are meant to become your slaves, and so we now give ourselves up, willingly, into your slavery.

And now: اھدنا الصراط المستقیم. Guide us to the one straight and wide path of knowledge that shoots up toward you. Guide us to the path of faith. Give us the ultimate gift of faith. صراط الذین انعمت علیھم — through the path of Islam, which is your true blessing. The path that is the perfect balance between knowledge and action. Through the examples of the role models among the people of the past whom you have favored, the ones who were wise, who had wisdom. Remember the definition of wisdom? To have correct knowledge and then act upon it. So make us among those who, when you provide them with knowledge, act upon it. غیر المغضوب علیھم — do not make us among those who gain knowledge but then do not act upon that knowledge, for those are the people who will receive wrath from all directions on the day of judgment because of their bad decisions. ولا الضالین — and do not make us among those who act without knowledge, because they are the ones who are lost.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
So the essence of Surah al-Fateha is three things. Gaining the knowledge of Allah. Striving to acquire the knowledge of his oneness. Making a commitment, a sacred pledge, which has to come first, before action. It is the intention of the action, which by definition precedes the action. And only after that come the instructions, the guidance. And then we ask Allah to make us among those who created a balance between their knowledge and action.

Maulana Ali says: اَلعِلمُ بِدُونِ العَمَل وَبَالٌ. وَالعَمَلُ بِدُونِ العِلمِ ضَلالٌ. Knowledge without action is a calamity upon the soul, and action without knowledge is ignorance; it is perversion. Success lies in the middle, in the balance of knowledge and action. And that is the true manifestation of servitude. A knowledgeable slave, who strives to understand the wisdom of his master's commands and then acts upon it — to demonstrate his praise for his master practically, physically, not through verbal claims or good intentions, but through action. He demonstrates that he indeed understands the value of his master's command.

If I am perplexed about something, and I ask you for advice, and then I actually take your advice and act upon it, does that not make you happy? Why? Because I respected your advice. I appreciated it. I saw you as someone worthy of taking advice from. If it works this way at our human level, it obviously works so much more at the divine level.

So this balance between knowledge and action is the essence of this surah. Even structurally it is perfectly balanced. The first half is Allah talking about himself to us, explaining to us who he is, what he has done, and how he did it. All of this is in the third person. The second half is us talking to Allah, based on what he explained to us in the first half. The first half ends with Allah being the king of the day when the debt of submission falls due. The second half is us asking Allah how we are to pay this debt of submission and its particulars.

إياك نعبد is the conclusion of everything we have learned and understood about Allah. Everything that comes before *iyyaka na'budu* is the reason we choose to become his servants. Everything that comes after *iyyaka nasta'in* is that in which we require his help. Al-hamdu lillah. The Arabs say: انا القدر الامورِ علی خواتیمھا — the worth of any undertaking is measured by how it ends.

Do not regard this as an ending. Let it be a new beginning for all of us. It is time for every one of us to commit ourselves to Allah and to set our priorities in order, and there is no better time to do so than these holy months. The aim has been to show the linguistic beauty of the Qur'an, and to show how beautiful this religion is. I have given it my best effort, yet I feel I have failed to show its true beauty, because there is so much more.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
Putting knowledge into practice. The parts of the body were created as a model of obedience: when the soul commands, the body obeys. So the point I am trying to make is that there is no such thing as servitude until you and I possess free will, and until the master gives us his instructions. Is that clear to everyone? Now, Allah has called himself Rabb, the master, which makes me the servant; therefore I understand that I do not have free will of my own, but I also need what? Instructions. In the Fatiha, is there any place where I recognized myself as a servant and then asked for instructions? Does that happen? What do we say in the Fatiha that asks for instructions? اھدنا الصراط المستقیم — guide us. Tell me what to do now. I have accepted you as my master, which means I have submitted myself as your servant; now tell me what to do. Guide me. Tell me which path I should walk upon. Guide me to the straight path. There is a logical connection between master and guidance, and that is why, all across the Qur'an — and it is so beautiful — in dozens of places Allah mentions Rabb and guidance. Rabb and guidance.

سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ

The first verse is Rabb, and then you find guidance, *hada*.

عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِ رَبِّى لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَذَا رَشَدًۭا
كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ
أُو۟لَٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ ۖ وَأُو۟لَٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدْ جَآءَكُم بُرْهَنٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ نُورًۭا مُّبِينًۭا

Rabb and guidance. Rabb and guidance. Rabb and guidance — because they are bound to each other.

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۗ هَذَا صِرَطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ

So Allah alone is our Rabb, and the only way he can grant us the benefits of his lordship, the benefits he wishes to give us, is this; that is why he singled out that attribute for himself and praised himself on account of it. الحمد للہ — all praise and gratitude belong to Allah. Why? رب العلمین — because he is the master of the worlds. And what is Rabb?

http://www.bayyinah.tv/posts/quran-for-young-adults-day-6
Part 1, beginning to 14:00

There is a psychological aspect of some of today's fictional entertainment that I want to point out. You know, today we have science-fiction films and books in which some alien force comes down from the heavens and tries to take over the planet or something of the sort — some outside force, some alien empire, that wants to seize the world. And if you look at it, in most cases these aliens want to bring some kind of order, some kind of discipline, to the human world. So they want to take over in order to control the chaos that is going on in the world.

Or else it is simply a matter of consuming resources. These, generally, are the themes that surround the idea of an alien invasion in movies and in books. Then there are movies like The Terminator, in which machines take over the world because human beings are too chaotic and not efficient enough. In all of these shows, in all of these movies, what must the human beings do? They must stand up against this alien power. They must fight against the tyranny of an outside force that is trying to control us and tell us what to do. They want to destroy this superpower that wishes to impose discipline upon them.
body.topic_title_en: You Alone We Worship, You Alone We Ask for Help

body.text_en:
So the common theme in all of these shows is that there is an outside force. It is very powerful, far more powerful than human beings, and it has far more resources than human beings do. It constantly wants to enslave humanity. It wants to force humanity into submission. And human beings — what is it that they constantly want? What must they fight for? Freedom! They would rather die than be enslaved or submit to a higher power, no matter how powerful that power may be.

Now, the reason I bring all of this up is that we are supposed to consider ourselves the slaves of a higher power. The slaves of whom? The slaves of Allah! And in all of these shows, it seems as though slavery is the most humiliating thing imaginable. In fact, in some movies you will see these higher powers, the leaders of these forces, calling themselves gods, or speaking as though they themselves are gods. And anyone who speaks of himself as a god in the movies you will find to be the ultimate villain of the story. So anything that sounds like a higher power, or resembles something from the sky, something that came down from above, something that means to impose its rules upon people, is evil. It only wants us to lose our freedom, to be unhappy, and to live under its control.

And do you know what that does to people who have been watching these kinds of things for a long time? Not consciously, but subconsciously, they simply become agitated by the very idea of a higher power. They think of themselves as someone who must fight for freedom against any higher power that would try to impose any sort of discipline upon them.

Now, what is revelation? Where does it come from? Does it not come down from the sky? Does it not impose a whole set of rules upon Muslims, rules that we are supposed to live by? Does it not come from a higher power, a higher source? Does it not sound similar?

Then there are certain other movies that were made in the late nineties: apocalyptic movies. What this means is that they show the earth about to be destroyed.
