Shukr, that is, gratitude, is for Allah: لَىِٕن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ ۖ وَلَىِٕن كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِى لَشَدِيدٌۭ

Shukr is offered ONLY in response to a favor done to you. Hamd, by contrast, is not in return for anything.

Now, what is the difference between Hamd and Madah? Madah in Arabic also means praise. But Madah may be a false praise, whereas Hamd is never a false praise. And Madah may be praise for something that lies beyond your control.

The AL signifies that every single type of Hamd belongs to Him. ALHAMDU, not Hamdan lillahi. Not: to Allah belongs praise. No! To Allah belongs ALL praise! Which means that every Hamd imaginable is for Allah. And the LAAM in Li-Allah means that all Hamd belongs ONLY to Allah and to no one else in the entire universe.

No one else in this world deserves Hamd unless Allah permits it for him. All Hamd belongs exclusively to Allah and to no one other than Allah. This is why Hamd is more specific than Shukr. It is more precise, more concise, and narrower than Shukr. Because Hamd can be done only by the tongue. You cannot show Hamd through your actions, but you can show Shukr. And Hamd is not done in exchange for a favor, while Shukr is always done in exchange for a favor. Even in Urdu we have the word Shukriya. But when do you hear Shukriya? Only when something has been done for you. You do not simply walk up to a person and, for no reason, say Shukriya to them. Because it is always in response to some good that was done for you, or in response to something that was given to you. Hamd, on the other hand, is not something you say because something was given to you, but out of recognition of the perfection of the being or the entity you are praising.

Rasul Allah SAS said, when something pleased him he would say: الحمد للہ الذی بِنعمتِہِ تَتِمُّ الصّٰلحات

Rasul Allah SAS said, when something pleased him he would say: الحمد للہ علی کل حال

All praise is due to Allah, no matter what the situation is.

What is the phrase common to both? AlHamdulillah. We do not praise Allah only when Allah shows us something good. No! Allah is worthy of Hamd regardless of the situations of our life. By Allah, if we did not exist, Allah would still be worthy of praise! Had He never created us, had He never created this magnificent universe, He would still be worthy of Hamd.

So no matter what situation we are in, no matter what conditions we are in, no matter what emotional states we are in, whether we are happy or sad or anxious or depressed, Allah is worthy of Hamd. That is what our Prophet SAS demonstrated. When something good happens: الحمد للہ الذی بِنعمتِہِ تَتِمُّ الصّٰلحات
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
When something bad happens: الحمد للہ علی کل حال

In every situation, in every circumstance, Allah is worthy of praise. There is never an occasion on which we do not praise Allah.

And how could it be otherwise, when Allah himself says that to him belongs Hamd from the very beginning to the very end, and that to him belongs Hamd in the heavens and the earth. The angels praise him as they circle around his throne. The people of Paradise close every single conversation of theirs with Hamd. Our father Adam began his existence with Hamd. And on the Day of Judgment the scales are filled with the Hamd of Allah SWT. How, then, could this magnificent book of Allah possibly begin with any word other than Hamd?

Why did Allah choose the word Alhamdulillah? Why did Allah begin in the third person? Suppose Allah had commanded us to praise him. A command is not as eloquent as a statement of fact. A command can be obeyed, but a command can also be disobeyed. A statement of fact, on the other hand, holds at all times. Whether you choose to obey or you choose to disobey, it does not change the fact that Allah is worthy of praise. A rule is a rule whether you follow it or not. And Allah AWJ states Alhamdulillah as a rule, without any exceptions.

Now suppose Allah had put this in the form of a verb: Nahmadullah, we are praising Allah. That too would not have been eloquent. Why? Because a verb always takes place at a particular time. When we say that we praise him right now, that means we were not praising him a second ago, and it means that we must necessarily be praising him after this moment. So using it as a verb, Nahmadullah, would have confined the praise of Allah within time. But the phrase Alhamdulillah means that whether you are praising him or not, Hamd belongs to Allah. So if Allah had used it as a verb, it would have been finite, it would have been temporary. Secondly, we would then be praising Allah according to the quality of our own praise, whereas Allah's praise is higher than our quality and our capacity.

So a verb would limit Allah's praise to a particular time: we are praising you now, meaning we were not praising you a second ago. And secondly, it would tie the praise to our own quality. And what will our quality always be? Inferior, limited, deficient.

So by saying Alhamdulillah we remove the limitations of time and of quality. Alhamd is a statement of fact.

The AL means استغراق الجنس. Every single kind of sincere praise belongs to Allah. There is no praise except that it belongs to Allah. Which means that nobody else is independently worthy of praise. Think about it. When somebody praises you, he praises you only for a blessing that Allah has given you. He says Mashallah, your face is so beautiful. Who gave you this face? Who gave you this beauty? Who gave you these features? It was Allah. Therefore, even though you are the one being praised for something, that praise in truth belongs to Allah, because he was the one who gave it to you in the first place.
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
If someone says you are so intelligent, who gave you that intelligence? Allah gave you that intelligence. Therefore that praise too belongs to Allah. For every single thing that you and I believe we are worthy of praise for, it is in fact Allah who gave us that quality, that feature, that capability, that capacity for which we are being praised. Therefore it is Allah who is in reality worthy of the praise that is being given to me. That is why, when somebody praises me, I must say Alhamdulillah. I must turn the praise toward its rightful owner: O Allah, all this praise belongs to you alone. And it is a reminder to the one who is praising me.

— that what you are praising is what Allah gave me. I cannot accept it. I am not truly worthy of it. The one worthy of this blessing that you see and acknowledge is my master. So when someone comes and praises you, or praises me, that person is in reality praising Allah indirectly, because it is Allah who gave you and me this blessing. Therefore, when I say Alhamdulillah, I am acknowledging that nobody, myself included, is worthy of praise except Allah. This is an unconditional statement of praise. Every other praise in this world is a conditional praise: Allah has given you something, and people praise you for it. This is what the two letters AL stand for.

وَإِن تَعُدُّوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَآ

If you tried to count the blessings of Allah, you would not be able to count them. Numbers would deceive you; they would abandon you. There is no number that could contain the blessings Allah has bestowed upon you. Imagine beginning the day as a rock, and then, as you say Alhamdulillah for each item, that item comes to life.

The Laam in Li-Allah indicates that this Hamd is reserved exclusively for Allah. No one other than Allah is worthy of praise. To Allah alone belongs every Hamd. Alhamdulillah: to Allah belongs every Hamd. And if we return to what we discussed about the meaning of the name Allah, He is the one who is worthy of worship. So we may translate Alhamdulillah as: every single ultimate praise belongs unconditionally to the one being, the only entity worthy of being worshiped. That is in fact the literal translation of the phrase Alhamdulillah. Every single, ultimate, and unconditional praise is exclusively owned by, and exclusively attributed to, the one entity worthy of being worshiped.

Alhamdulillah. Rabb Alalameen. 7:50

Why should all praise be due to Allah? Why is it that Allah alone should be praised? It is because he is the master of the worlds, because he is Rabb Alalameen. So out of all his 99 names, Allah chose the name Rabb, because Rabb — master — is the most significant relationship between us and our Creator.
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
What does Rabb mean? It means the ultimate owner. The maalik. The one who controls. This implies that he is the one who brought us into existence, because ultimate ownership always belongs to the creator. I repeat: the ultimate ownership always belongs to the creator. If you think about it, you do not own anything completely. Whatever you own today was handed to you, and it will be handed to someone else after you. You have to buy your car. You have to purchase your house. Even if you make something with your own hands, you first needed to purchase the raw materials to make it. You could not bring anything into existence by yourself. When we say Allah is the Rabb, and that there is no one competing with the Rabb, this means that Allah's ownership is unique and complete. He did not first have to obtain spare material in order to create anything. No ownership was transferred to him. Ownership always belongs to him, has always belonged to him, and will always belong to him. Which implies what? That he created from nothing. So when we use the word Rabb, we automatically imply that Allah is the creator who created from nothing, because ultimate ownership necessitates creation. Is that clear?

When we say Allah is the Rabb, when we say Allah is the ultimate owner, then this means that Allah AWJ created, because ultimate ownership cannot be transferred.

Our own ownership, by contrast, is always transferred. Whatever we come to own, ownership of it was first passed to us. Even when you discover something — a well, for example — you cannot say that you made that well. You can only find it, because you found it inside something that Allah had already created. He created the earth, and he made water run beneath it. All you did was dig a hole to draw that water out. You did not create the earth. You did not set the water running beneath it. Allah did all of it. So even when you discover a well, ultimate ownership still belongs to Allah. Even when you walk into a showroom and buy a car, that is nothing more than a transfer of title. Every ownership we hold is conditional. Allah's ownership alone is unconditional. And if Allah's ownership is unconditional, then this implies, indeed it necessitates, that Allah must have created from nothing, and therefore he is the Rabb.

The second meaning of Rabb is the one who is obeyed. Rabb means the one who is obeyed. In Surah Yusuf, when the prisoners are released, Yusuf says to the prisoners:

ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ

Mention me to the god whom you obey — that is, the king. He called the king Rabb here, because the meaning of the word Rabb is the one who is obeyed. So when we say that Allah is Rabb al-Alameen, it implies that Allah is obeyed. Everything in the universe, everything in the universe, everything in the multiverse, obeys Allah's command.

And the third meaning of the word Rabb is the one who takes care, the one who nourishes, the one who sustains. From this meaning of the word Rabb we get the word Tarbiyah. What does Tarbiyah mean? To take care of, to nourish.

So when we say that Allah is Rabb al-Alameen, we are implying three things:
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
1. Allah is the unconditional owner.
2. Allah is the one who is obeyed. Nothing happens in this world except by his command.
3. Allah is the one who takes care of all his creation. And from this we get the word Tarbiyah.

In other words, my existence cannot be sustained until my Rabb takes care of me. Without my Rabb, without my master, I cannot exist. My Rabb must give me tarbiyah. My physical, spiritual, and emotional Tarbiyah comes from my master.

Why is Allah worthy of praise? Because he is Rabb al-Alameen. He is the owner, the one who is obeyed, and the one who sustains and takes care.

Our problem today is not that we are an unappreciative or ungrateful people. The problem is that we are not acquiring this knowledge of the Qur'an. We are so busy acquiring the knowledge our academic or professional lives demand of us that we have thrown the knowledge of the Qur'an behind our backs. That is why we are unable to appreciate the blessings of Allah. Islam is a blessing. Emaan is a blessing. The Qur'an is a blessing. The Messenger of Allah and Maulana Ali are blessings. Taharat. Salaah. Zakaat. Saum. Hajj. All of these are blessings. But what is missing? Our knowledge. Our knowledge about these blessings is missing. And you must also understand that we will never, ever be able to acquire complete knowledge. We will never, ever be able to fully appreciate Allah's blessings and be grateful for them. We will never be able to do justice to Allah. It is simply not possible.

Rasul Allah (SAS) would wake in the middle of the night.

He would perform ablution, pray two units of prayer, and then fall down in prostration. In that prostration he would say: سبحنک اللہ — how exalted You are, O Allah — لا احصی ثَناءً علیک. أنتَ کما أثنَیتَ علی نَفسِک — I cannot do justice to Your praise. Now consider this for a moment. Who is saying it? The best of creation, among all creatures ever created. The most noble, the most pious, the most knowing of Allah's creation. And he says this in his mosque, which is the second holiest place on this earth. When? In the middle of the night, the best portion of the night for worship, when no one else is watching him. I want you truly to picture this. The one who worships Allah with a perfection no one else in the world can reach. The best of the best of creation. In the best posture of worship, prostration. In the best mosque. During the best hour of the night. And what does he say? لا احصی ثَناءً علیک! أنتَ کما أثنَیتَ علی نَفسِک — O Allah, I cannot praise You as You deserve to be praised. Even the Messenger of Allah (SAS) says: You are too great for me to praise. أنتَ کما أثنَیتَ علی نَفسِک — Only You can praise Yourself as You deserve to be praised.
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
So we praise Allah while recognizing that our praise falls short of what Allah deserves. We praise Allah while realizing that only Allah can praise Himself in a manner suited to Him, with the majesty that Allah deserves. The point, then, is that Allah is not asking us to appreciate Him and be grateful to Him at His level. He is asking us to appreciate Him and be grateful to Him at our own level. SubhanAllah, what a wonderful master. Take any other master in this world: is the work demanded set at the level of the master or at the level of the slave? At the level of the master. Slaves are whipped and tortured if they fail to meet the master's standards. But look at our Master. He demands nothing beyond what we are capable of. And He receives our feeble efforts with open arms.

Once Musa (AS) passed by a shepherd who was sitting under a tree with his sheep. The shepherd was combing the wool of his sheep and saying: O Allah, why do You not come to me as well? I would comb Your hair. I would pick the lice out of Your hair. I would feed You the finest grass in the land. I would give You the best milk to drink. When Musa (AS) heard this, he became furious. He went and stood before the shepherd and shouted at him: What nonsense and rubbish are you speaking about Allah? Do you think Allah is like your sheep? How dare you even think of Allah in such a way. The shepherd asked Musa: So Allah is not like my sheep? Musa (AS) grew angrier still: You compare Allah (Azza Wa Jal) to your sheep? If I ever hear you speak this way again, I will punish you severely. Hearing this, the shepherd began to weep.

That evening, when Musa (AS) climbed Mount Tur to meet Allah, Allah said to him: Musa, what have you done? You have turned My beloved away from Me. Whatever he was saying, in whatever manner he was remembering Me, at least he was remembering Me. At least he was appreciating Me. Why did you turn him away from Me, Musa? And then He commanded Musa to depart and not to return until that shepherd was content with Allah once again. SubhanAllah, what a wonderful master.

My point is this: we must strive to excel, and we must strive to gain more and more knowledge about our beautiful religion, and about this wonderful Master.

so that we may grow in our appreciation and gratitude toward Him. We must increase our prayer, our fasting, our worship. Yet do not underestimate the worth of whatever you are doing at this moment. Never think that it is not good enough. Even so, we must strive for more. Consider what people will do for worldly rewards. Think of that program, "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire," or any of those game shows in which money is at stake. People will go to every extreme in order to win. And in those game shows you may win or you may not; they are designed for you to lose. What, then, of a game that is designed for you to win, a game in which victory is certain?
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
This praise comes from the recognition of the perfection of the one being praised. The Messenger of Allah said: الحمد للہ تملأُ المیزان — saying "AlHamdulillah" fills the entire scale on the Day of Judgment. Simply saying "AlHamdulillah" fills the entire scale on the Day of Judgment. And our Master has used this word Hamd many times in the Qur'an. He used it when He spoke of bringing the creation into being: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ ٱلظُّلُمَتِ وَٱلنُّورَ — all Hamd belongs to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth. So Allah is praised at all times. وَهُوَ ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ لَهُ ٱلْحَمْدُ فِى ٱلْأُولَىٰ وَٱلْآخِرَةِ — to Allah belongs Hamd from the very beginning of time, and to Allah belongs Hamd until the very end of time. To Allah belongs praise wherever you are and whenever you are. وَلَهُ ٱلْحَمْدُ فِى ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّۭا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ — to Him belongs unceasing Hamd. Those in the heavens praise Him, and those on the earth praise Him. So wherever you are and whenever you are, Hamd always belongs to Allah alone.

How do you and I begin our day? How often do we truly praise Allah?

The Bedouin's greeting.

قال اميرالمؤمنين عليه السلام. إنّ‌قوماً عبدوا الله رغبةً فتلك عبادة التّجار . وإنّ قوماً عبدوا الله رهْبةً فتلك عبادة العبيد . وإنّ قوْماً عبدوا الله شُكراً فتلك عبادة الأحرار

Imam Ali — peace be upon him — has stated: [Among those who worship Allah] one group worships Allah in hope [of profit], and such is the worship of traders; another group worships Allah out of fear [of His wrath], and such is the worship of slaves; and yet another group worships Allah out of gratitude, and such is the worship of free, noble men. [Nahj al-Balaghah, short saying #237]

According to a hadith, Allah said that He was a hidden treasure and He wished to be known. For that reason, He created the universe. The last servant brought into being at the stage of the universe's creation was man. In truth, the creation of man was the very purpose for which the universe was created, since man was the only servant capable of being His khalifa. According to another hadith, this khalifa was created in His form, and so represented His authority over all things. There had been no creature before him capable of knowing, by itself, all the known Divine Names.

Allah wants us to draw nearer to Him and to know Him better. As long as we lack knowledge concerning the manifestation of His names, we will not achieve this and will remain animal-humans. This is why the Sufis add supererogatory prayers to the obligatory religious practices.

And most importantly, they aim to learn more and more of Him every day. The Sufis realized that we are not only created to serve Him; rather, all our actions serve Him of their own accord. That means we are servants not because Allah wanted us to be, but because we are servants in truth. What we call the universe is where His names manifest themselves, and all consciousness is attuned to Him. And so, as the hadith says: "He who knows himself, knows His Lord."
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
Now let us return to the example of the aunt's cooking. Suppose that, instead of appreciating her food, instead of showing gratitude, I take a bite from that leg of lamb and spit it out. I say: who cares if you cooked this leg of lamb for me? You did me no favor. You were going to cook dinner anyway. I did not ask you to do all this for me. Do not imagine that you are going to get any praise or gratitude out of me. How do I know you did this for me? What if you did it for someone else, and that man did not show up, and now you are simply trying to take the credit for it? Now, how do you think the aunt will feel? Does she have a right to be angry with me at this point? Does she have a right to take the food away from in front of me? Does she have a right to let me go hungry now? ABSOLUTELY. Why? Because I do not deserve it. You do not give gifts and blessings to people who do not deserve them, to people who are going to waste them. Is that not true?

What is praise, and when do we praise something? Let us take the example of cars. Who are cars designed for? Who benefits from cars? People. The consumers benefit from cars, do they not? Certainly the company makes money as well, so in the financial sense it benefits too. But then the company deserves that money for the efforts it has made, does it not? There is nothing wrong with a company receiving what it deserves. But from the standpoint of benefit, cars are designed to benefit people. The effort that is put into the design of a car, into its construction, is for people. Suppose I go to the head office of BMW and meet the designer of the latest BMW model, the one that is about to be released. He takes me on a tour and shows me this beautiful piece of machinery, and I say: WOW. THIS is absolutely awesome! What a look, what an amazing design. Such a beautiful interior. It looks so comfortable. This car is INCREDIBLY AWESOME!

Now the question is this: did the designer of the car NEED my praise? Had I said none of that, would it have put a dent in his day? Would he have gone home and wept on his wife's shoulder because I did not praise his car? NO! Of course not! He would not care. His design is AWESOME whether I appreciate it or not, is it not? But when I praised his work, do you think it made him happy? Do you think he valued my praise? He ABSOLUTELY did. Why is that? Let us think about why you and I feel happy when someone praises us.

And what have we just learned? When are we compelled to praise? When we gain knowledge about the one we are praising. In Paradise we will constantly gain knowledge about Allah's loftiness, about His mercy, about His grace, about His ninety-nine attributes. And with every bit and piece of knowledge we acquire, with every bit of awareness we gather, we will be compelled to praise Him. We will be driven by our immense gratitude for the gift of His awareness, so that we will have no choice but to praise Him, willingly.

Out of our love for Him. And out of our awe at His glory and loftiness.
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
The blessings of Allah are readily available. Yet when the time comes to respond with gratitude, we delay our salaah. A dog leaves a bone and answers its master's call.

Completed part 1

Language limits us

Child and breasts

Words and meanings

Circular relation of trust

Salaah is using the language described by Allah

Story of the cat presenting its owner a dead mouse

Heart: completely spiritual

Tongue: converting spirituality into language. Physical, yet not tangible

Body: completely physical

Salaah is combining all

A witness is required for a claim

44:00 paradoxes. Islam, emaan

The process of walking. Two steps, one after the other, creating movement. Repetition. Circular pattern

The format of prayer is motivated by Allah's commands in the Quran

Society is designed such that we want things instantly

Recap

Hadees: Praise You as You have praised Yourself

What is knowledge

Tie it with heart, tongue, and limbs

Salaah is knowledge in action

Now, because salaah is an instrument, it too has operational knowledge, structural knowledge, and essential knowledge. But where do we have to begin? We have to begin with operational knowledge. That is the first thing to learn. How does this THING work? What are the prerequisites? What are the dos and don'ts?

Which is not to say that you should not WANT to understand the structure and the intent. You ABSOLUTELY should want to. Because at the end of the day, salaah is just another instrument. And the BETTER you understand the internal structure and the INTENT in the design of that instrument, the BETTER you will be able to use it. So, to be VERY clear: I am NOT saying that you should not want to study its structure and understand its intent. In fact, you should absolutely WANT to. What I am saying, though, is that it is not a requirement for its operation. There is a difference, and I hope you understand that difference. This whole idea that I need to understand every single meaning behind every single action of salaah, and only then can I do it — that is ABSOLUTELY not true.

The only motivation you need for salaah is HAMD. That is it. That is the reason why Rasul Allah prayed. That is the reason why Maulana Ali prayed. That is the reason why an Imam prays, why a Dai prays, why a mansoob prays, why the most ordinary believer like myself prays. HAMD. We are all unified in that purpose. From the highest rank to the lowest rank, we are all unified in our HAMD. The Imam, with ALL of his TREMENDOUS knowledge, prays the same number of rakaats, the same Surah Fateha, the same tasbeeh in each action, the same tashahhud, as you and I do. We are all unified in action. We are all unif
body.topic_title_en: All Praise Belongs to God, Lord of the Worlds

body.text_en:
Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, opens the Fatiha by introducing Himself: بسم اللہ — with the NAME of Allah. In these words the attributes are set apart from the essence. Allah is the name of His essence, His very being, His ZAAT, while NAME stands for His infinite and beautiful attributes. Out of all those infinite attributes He then draws out the two that are dearest to Him: Al-Rahman and Al-Raheem. Both come from the word Rahama, which means love, care, genuine concern, and mercy. Rahma in turn comes from the root RAHAM, the womb of a mother. His love, His mercy, is like the love a mother has for the child within her womb.

When we begin an act with knowledge of the attributes of Allah, the result is BARAKAH. It creates abundance — an abundance many times greater than the original investment. And the more the blessing grows, the more stable it becomes, which meets the measure of AL-KAUSAR: uncountable, invaluable, and all of it good. So Allah's Rahma is what produces BARAKAH. We can witness this in practice in the womb, the RAHAM. A REHAM receives a drop of liquid, a sperm, that has no shape and no form; and with the name of Allah, with the manifestations of His beautiful attributes, it turns that drop of liquid into a fully developed, fully formed, beautiful child. That is BARAKAH. And the growth does not stop there. Once the child enters this world, it continues to grow in physical strength as well as in intellectual maturity. This is barakah. You and I today are that very same drop, that shapeless, meaningless drop, that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, turned into who we are today by His Rahma.

After that introduction Allah says: الحمد للہ رب العالمین. All praise and gratitude belong to Allah, who is the master, the Rabb of EVERYTHING that can be known, AL-ALAMEEN. And the transition is remarkable, considering that this immense universe also came into being from a singularity, a seed, that developed into this universe, this AALAM. It is the same image for the ALAM. It is astonishing how He created the ALAM on the same pattern by which He created us human beings — and this is to reflect and to manifest the barakah of His names and attributes. Now, when you create something, it becomes your responsibility to nurture it, to care for it, to make sure it is used for its intended purpose and properly maintained. So He made RUBUBIYYAH a critical component of ALL human activity, to reveal to us that this ALAM, THESE ALAMEEN, everything in existence that can be known, ALSO has a Rabb, and that Rabb is Allah. Therefore all praise and gratitude belong to Him ALONE.

Why? Because everything He created knows its purpose, which is praise, and is doing EXACTLY what He created it to do, which is gratitude. So everything Allah created in the ALAMEEN is PHYSICALLY proving, in ACTION — not with good intentions or lofty claims, but physically, through action — that HAMD belongs to Allah alone. And what I learn from this observation is that I ALSO must accept Him as MY RABB, and I too must PHYSICALLY express my hamd to Him through my worship.

Consider that one of the attributes of Allah He reflected in human beings is the ability to witness things, for He is the SHAHEED. And شھادۃ means to witness and to testify. Allah created this ALAM so that WE can witness HIS work.

and testify that there is no god but Allah — لا الہ الا اللہ. And the physical manifestation of that spoken testimony is ibaadah, worship. But then, through our worship, we are creating a world of our own — عالم العبادۃ — which Allah is witnessing, and to which He will testify on the Day of Judgment. SubhanAllah! We are witnessing His creation, and He is witnessing ours.

And the essence of this ayah, الحمد للہ رب العالمین, is this: Look! I am your Rabb. I am physically taking care of you. I did not stop at the level of good intentions, and I did not stop at the level of making claims. I love you. I said I love you in the Quran, and I am physically showing my love to you with every single breath you take. Now it is your turn. Do not merely love me in your heart. Do not merely talk about loving me. Show it to me, through your actions. And there is only one way you can show it to me. If you really mean what you say, if you truly believe in your heart that I am your Rabb, if your testimony of la ilaha illa Allah is true, then — فصل لربک وانحر — establish salaah for your master, and sacrifice, which, as I explained, includes all forms of worship and obedience. Physically show me that even within your own individual alam, within your own universe of existence, Allah is your Rabb. الحمد للہ رب العالمین. Reflect this ayah in your actions. That is the lesson we learn from this ayah.

Then he says, الرحمن الرحیم — the intensely merciful, the consistently merciful. He had already identified Himself with these attributes of love in بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم. He had already declared that Allah is Rehman and Raheem. But now that he has mentioned His rububiyyah and called Himself رب العالمین, he highlights the nature of His rububiyyah once again. And what is it? الرحمن الرحیم. I am an intensely merciful Rabb. I am a constantly merciful Rabb.

Now, if you look at all the ayats we have studied so far, there is a common thread running through the fabric of the Fateha, and that is rehma. اعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم — I seek protection from Allah from the cursed Shaytan. To whom do we turn for protection? To someone who loves us, or to someone who hates us or does not care about us? To whom does a child turn for protection when it is scared? To its parents, right? You can only seek the protection of the one whom you believe has rehma for you. Then, بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم — with the name of Allah, who is what? Rehman and Raheem. Rehma again. الحمد للہ رب العالمین — all praise and gratitude belongs only to Allah. Why? Because He is Rabb. And rububiyyah, we now know, is an act of pure love; it is an act of care, concern, and mercy. So we find rehma again! And then, finally, الرحمن الرحیم. Now Allah is saying: In case you still have not grasped it, let me highlight this for you. Let me spell it out for you. I will say this in an ayah all by itself. AR-REH-MAN AR-RAHEEEEEEM. Do you get it? I am intensely merciful with you. I am constantly merciful with you. Not merely a feeling in my heart. Not merely a verbal claim. But in action.

And then you come to me and say, Asif mamu, why does Allah have to say that? It is so mean. It is so bad. It makes me feel so strange to read all of that. Why can he not simply not speak of hell and fire, and all of this negative material? It disturbs my emotions. Is that not so?

Very well. Tell me something. First of all, is that all that Allah says in the Qur'an? And second, whenever He speaks of hell, does He begin with that? Never. You will not find a single instance in the entire Qur'an where Allah begins with the fire of hell. He always uses it as a last resort. That is the first point.

Now, why does He give such graphic descriptions of hellfire? Let me ask you something. Imagine that a dangerous tsunami, like Katrina, is heading straight toward your house. It is going to destroy your home, your entire family, your entire zip code. How would you like the newscaster to inform you of that danger? Kindly? Delicately? Oh, by the way, there is a tsunami heading your way, but it is all right, it is not so bad, it is only water and rain. Just put on your life jacket. If you know the breaststroke, that is good; otherwise the doggie paddle will work too. It will not be so bad. Do not feel afraid. I do not want you to feel sad and all strange inside. It is going to be all right. Just relax and watch a movie on Netflix or something to distract yourself.

Is that how you would want the newscaster to give you that news? It is only a category five hurricane, but nothing to worry about. Probably not a good day for a barbecue, but you can fly kites. Is that what you would want him to say? Or would you rather have him say: Listen! Wake up! A tsunami is coming your way. Get out of there. It is going to kill you. It is going to destroy you, and your whole neighborhood. Why are you still standing here staring at me? Get moving. Quickly. Is that not what you would want? Why? So that you can understand the level of the threat and take precautionary measures accordingly. Because you have time right now. Time to do something about it, before it is too late.

Is Allah boiling us in hot water, baking us, or frying us right now? No. He is saying: If you continue to reject my message, if you continue to mock my beloved messenger, if you continue throwing stones at him, calling him insane, calling him a poet, if you continue to ridicule him, if you keep rejecting my message, then you are heading down a very dangerous path. This is going to be a terrible price to pay. Listen to me. Wake up. Take me seriously. Stop what you are doing. Correct yourself. You still have time.

Do you know who does that? Someone who loves you does that. A ra'uf does that. When a mother tells her child, "Do not put your hand in the fire; it will burn you, it will scar you, your skin will peel off," is she being cruel to the child? Or is she protecting the child? The fact that Allah is warning us with such clear images of what lies ahead, if we do not correct ourselves, is part of his mercy. Allah telling us of all the pain and suffering, and describing to us, in the most vivid detail possible, the scenes of Jahannum, is part of his love and mercy for us. It is an immense favor to us.

How do we know that? Because right after that description he says:

فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ

How many favors of your Master will you deny? As a friend, as someone who loves you, someone who cares about you, who is concerned for you, I am telling you: this is the punishment in which your crimes will end. You are forgetting my kindness, my mercy, my leniency toward you have made you forget who I am. You are forgetting your place before me.

And if you honestly think about it, these punishments are absolutely just. Consider: you disobey your parents, you get grounded. You disobey the rules of your school, you get detention, or you are expelled from school. You disobey the rules of your job, you get fired. You disobey the rules of the state, you get arrested and sent to prison. You disobey a king, and your head is cut off. The punishment is always in relation to the position and the status of the one you are disobeying. Then what do you think should be a fitting punishment for disobedience of خالق السماوات و الارض؟ مالک الملک?

So Allah warns us. Why? Because he is ra'uf. He does not want us to get hurt. Pain and punishment is not what he desires for us. No one wants to tear up his own best work with his own hands. If you have worked on a project for hours and hours, you do not want to throw it into the fire. Allah made us with his own hands. وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَكُمْ. He created you and fashioned you. He gave you a beautiful form. He called us his best creation. لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَنَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍۢ.

He created human beings in the most beautiful way. Do you imagine that he wants to burn us in hell? Of course not. His punishments are always meant to render justice, and, God willing, we will speak of that as well. Even the fire of hell is in truth a part of his mercy.

So he uses fear and warning as a means to turn the hearts of the disbelievers toward himself. And if the fire does not move them either, he changes his method of teaching once more, and turns to enticement.

وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ جَنَّتَانِ ذَوَاتَآ أَفْنَانٍۢ فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ فِيهِمَا مِن كُلِّ فَكِهَةٍۢ زَوْجَانِ‏ مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ فُرُشٍۭ بَطَآئِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍۢ ۚ وَجَنَى ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍۢ فِيهِنَّ قَصِرَتُ ٱلطَّرْفِ لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إِنسٌۭ قَبْلَهُمْ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ كَأَنَّهُنَّ ٱلْيَاقُوتُ وَٱلْمَرْجَانُ هَلْ جَزَآءُ ٱلْإِحْسَنِ إِلَّا ٱلْإِحْسَنُ

I have prepared so many wondrous treasures, and they are for you alone. I wish to give you all of them: trees whose branches bend low under the weight of their fruit, beautiful flowing rivers, couches to recline upon whose linings are of silk brocade, and the fruit of two gardens hanging within reach. And why do I do all this for you? Because هَلْ جَزَآءُ ٱلْإِحْسَنِ إِلَّا ٱلْإِحْسَنُ — can the reward of something beautiful be anything other than something beautiful? Your worship and your obedience are an exceedingly beautiful act, and for that I will reward you with what is most beautiful. You give me your beautiful worship, offered according to your limited capacity; I will reward you with my beautiful blessings, according to my unlimited capacity. Glory be to God.

فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ — how many of the blessings of your Lord will you deny?

So in Surah Rahman, Allah turns toward the Quraish, and he turns toward us, and gives us a demonstration of his mercy. This is what true caring and true love are. Al-Rahman: the incredibly, unimaginably loving, caring, and protecting Allah. He, and no one else, is the one who taught the Qur'an. This single verse alone teaches us that when we recite the Qur'an, we are directly connected with Allah. Why? Because it is the Rahman who taught the Qur'an. There is no higher degree, no higher nobility, no higher station that can come from anything else in the world than the learning of the Qur'an and the following of its teachings. For it is the most noble, the most honored, the most elevated in station, who taught us the Qur'an. الرحمن علم القرآن.

We are forever running after honor and respect. We imagine that our money will purchase us respect. Some suppose respect will come from their car, their branded clothes, or their Rolex watches. People suppose respect will come from whom they are connected to: I know this governor; I dined with that actor. People suppose respect will come from whom they stood beside for a photograph. But when we understand the true meaning of this verse, الرحمن علم القرآن, we are no longer in need of honor from these outward sources. We no longer need constant validation from without, because the ultimate being has honored us. The ultimate being has given us respect, by accepting us as his students, by making us Muslim, by making us Sulemani. And why did he do this? He did it because he is Al-Rahman.

الرحمن علم القرآن.

Freedom from Slavery

Allah, by choosing us as his slaves, has dignified us. He has honored us. And when Allah honors, all of creation follows. I will say it again: when Allah honors, all of creation follows.

We do not have to go out and earn their respect; they will come and give it to us regardless. If we learn and follow the teachings of Al-Rahman, honor and respect will chase after us, because Allah has honored us. After that, we will never again be in need of anyone or anything. This is true freedom: freedom from all the slaveries and all the attachments of the world. Becoming a slave of Allah is what grants us that freedom.

يا ابن آدم. لاَ تَخَافَنَّ مِن ذِي سُلطَانْ

The Messenger of Allah (may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his progeny) tells us in a sacred tradition:

يا ابن آدم. لاَ تَخَافَنَّ مِن ذِي سُلطَانْ. ما دَامَ سُلطاَنِي بَاقِيَا. وَسُلطَانِي. لاَ يَنْفَدُ أَبَدَا

O son of Adam, do not fear the one who holds power over you, for his reign and his power will not last forever, and my power never comes to an end.

يا ابن آدم. لاَ تَخْشَ مِن ضِيقِ الرِّزْقِ. وَالخَزَائِنِي مَلْآنَة. وَخَزَائِنِي لاَ تَنفَدُ أَبَدَا

O son of Adam, do not let the constriction of provision frighten you, for all the treasures of the universe belong to me, and my treasures never run out.

یا ابن آدم. خَلَقتُكَ لِعَبادَتِي فَلا تَلعَب

O son of Adam, I created you for my worship. Do not waste your time in useless play.

وَقَسَمتُ لَكَ رِزْقُكَ. فَلا تَتعَب

I have already apportioned your provision for you, so do not tire yourself chasing after it. Do not let greed for provision distract you from doing what I created you to do.

فإذا أنتَ رَضِيتُ بِمَا قَسَمتُ لَك. أَرَحْتُ نَفسَك. وَقَلبَک. وَ بَدَنَک. وَكنُتَ عِندِي مَحمُوداً

If you choose to be content with what I have apportioned for you, I will grant peace and relief to your soul, to your heart, and to your body, and you will be among the best of creations before me.

وإِن انتَ لَم تَرضَ بِمَا قَسَمتُ لَك. فَوَعِزَّتِي وَجَلالِي. لأُسَلَّطَنَّ عَلَيكَ الدُّنيَا. وَ تَركُضُ فِيهَا كَمَا يَركُضُ الوُحُوشُ فِي البَرِّيَّة

And if you choose not to be content with what I have apportioned for you, then by my might and my majesty, I will set the greed and desire of this world in mastery over you, and I will abandon you in this world as I have left the beasts to roam the wilderness.

وَلا تَنَالُ مِنهَا إِلاَّ مَا قَسَمتُ لَك. وكُنتَ عِندِي مذموماً

And for all your efforts, you will still not obtain anything more than what I had apportioned for you, and you will be among the wretched in my presence.

The people we see in the world who chase after the pleasures of this world, as a dog chases after a bone, are a sign that Allah has abandoned them. Allahu Akbar. نعوذُ باللہ من ذالک.

یا ابن آدم خَلَقْتُ السمٰوات و الارضِ ولَم أَعْیٰ بِخَلقِهِنْ. أَيُعِينِي رَغِيفُ عَيشِ أَسُوقُهُ لَک؟

O son of Adam, I created the heavens and the earth, and I did not grow tired in creating them. Do you think that providing your provision to you would be a burden for me?

يا ابن آدم! إَنَّهُ لَم أَنْسَ مَنْ عَصَانِي. فَكَيفَ مَنْ أَطَاعَنِي؟

O son of Adam, I do not forget to care for those who disobey me; how then can you think that I would forget to care for the one who obeys me?

أَذکُرُکَ وَلا تَنسَانِی

I remember you, and you are the one who forgets me.

استرک فلا تغشانی

I keep covering your faults, and still you feel no shame before me.

خَیرَی اِلَیکَ نَازِل. و شَرُّکَ عَلَییَّ سَاعِد

Every day good descends upon you from me, and every day your evil deeds rise up to me in return.

أ تجعلُك النَّومِ وَكأَنَّكَ لَم یعصُونی

And despite the fact that you disobey me every day, I still let you sleep peacefully upon your bed each night.

يا ابن آدم ! لا تَسأَلُنِي رِزقَ غَد. كَمَا لَم أُطَالِبُكَ بِعَمَلِ غَد. يا ابن آدم ! Oh son of Adam, do not ask me today for tomorrow's provision, just as I do not ask you today for tomorrow's obedience. وأنا رب رحيم، وعلى كل شيء قدير؟ I am your loving and merciful master, and I possess might and power over all things. أنا لَكَ مُحِبُّ. فَبِحَقِّي عَلَيكَ . كُن لِي مُحِباً I love you, and I hold a right over you. Be among those who love me in return.

Now to the question that is, one hopes, on everyone's mind: what is the difference between al-Rahman and al-Rahim? We understand that both come from the same word, rahima. We understand that this is a mercy that will be shown to us, that will be demonstrated to us. But what is the actual difference between al-Rahman and al-Rahim?

By using these two names, al-Rahman and al-Rahim, and setting them together within a single verse, Allah is indicating how important rahma is to him. Indeed, Allah says this himself in the Qur'an: ورحمتی وسعت علی کل شئی — my mercy encompasses all things. And al-rahma is one of the

Should I take advantage of Allah's love?

If I have come this far in my understanding, then perhaps I should take the next step and try to understand something further: is this love and care simply something for me to take advantage of? Here again we return to the question of basic decency. If someone is doing kind things for you — if your parents are doing kind things for you, paying for your schooling, paying for your iPad, filling it with whatever applications you want — they are the ones being charged, not you. You do not pay a penny for it, nor for whatever else you desire. Even though they are obligated only to provide you with what you need, they give you what you need, and on top of that they give you what you want. They give and give and give. And the moment they stop giving, you decide to lose your composure: how could you do this to me, how could you do this to me, you do not love me anymore. Is that a sign of decency? Did you forget in those moments that they do not in truth owe you anything beyond the bare minimum? They truly owe you nothing; it is you who owe them. You do not deserve a bed at home; you could sleep just as well upon the carpet. That, too, is something they give you.

The idea here is this: when you are being given gifts constantly by Allah, and you have been taking advantage of them and failing to appreciate them — in fact, the more he gives, the more entitled to them you feel. You feel that you ought to receive still more, still better. Why does Allah not give me more? There are people who speak in this way. Why did Allah let me fail my test? I studied so hard, yet I still failed. Why did Allah fail me? Truly — why did Allah fail you?

When someone does so much for you, and you turn around and complain about them, that is an enormous sign of indecency. And do not imagine that, simply because Allah is so loving and caring, he will never, never, never grow displeased with you, or never question you about your obnoxious attitude toward his commands.

The human being — not even a believer, but simply as a basic human being — realizes, when he understands these matters, that there may come a time when he will have to answer for what he has been doing. Even though Allah has been loving and caring all this while, there must come some time when I, and every human being, will have to answer for what we have done.

and that takes us to the next verse of the Fateha: مالک یوم الدین

Now, what is the best way for us to obtain an increase in Allah's rehma? It is very simple. Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) said in a famous hadees Qudsi. He said: الرَّاحِمُونَ یَرحَمُہُم الرَّحمٰن. أِرحَمُ مَن فِی الارضِ. یَرحَمُکُم مَن فی السَّمَاءِ. Those who are merciful will be shown mercy by the One who is full of mercy. الرَّاحِمُونَ یَرحَمُہُم الرَّحمٰن — those who are merciful.

There will be shown mercy by the One who is AlRehman. أِرحَمُ مَن فِی الارضِ ؛ یَرحَمُکُم مَن فی السَّمَاءِ — Have mercy upon those who are on this earth, and the One who is in the heavens will have mercy upon you. And one of the greatest signs of rehma is patience.

Consider this: the Quran itself is a rehma from AlRehman. How do we know this? Because it is declared in the opening verses of Surah Rehman: الرحمن ۔۔۔ علم القرآن. What did AlRehman do? He taught the Quran. The Quran is a token of mercy. It is a token of love and care from Allah (Subhanhu Wa Ta'ala). He loves us intensely, without limit, and without ceasing, and so He gave us His message of rehma. And He delivered this message through the most merciful man who ever walked the earth, His beloved messenger Muhammad Mustafa (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam), the man who was mercy made flesh.

لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُم بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ — There has surely come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. It grieves him when you suffer. He is deeply concerned for you, and to the believers he is kind and merciful.

RAOOF versus RAHEEM. Raoof and Raheem are both attributes of Allah, and Allah (Subhanhu Wa Ta'ala) marks His messenger (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) with these very same attributes. Now, what is the difference between the two? Ar-Ra'uf is the One who has compassion, which is mercy in its intensified form. It therefore carries the same meaning as raheem, but heightened. The scholars have said that if a calamity strikes you, the Raheem shows you mercy after that calamity has passed. But the Ra'uf is one so merciful that His mercy reaches you before the calamity ever strikes. It shows itself in His caring for you and warning you, so that you do not fall victim to the calamity at all.

Let me give you an example. Picture a mother who is fiercely protective of her children. In the winter she dresses them in warm clothes. Why? So that they will not suffer from the cold. That is ra'fa. But suppose the child does not listen to its mother, takes off those warm clothes, plays out in the cold, and falls ill. Now the mother's heart aches, because her child has become sick, and she does everything in her power to ease the child's suffering. That is raheemiyyah. So ra'fa is the highest form of mercy, in which Allah protects His servants by warning them away from the deeds that would call down punishment.

And this is why the Quran is the most extreme form of mercy: because it is full of warnings, and it is full of love, care, concern, and mercy. This is why Allah called His beloved messenger Raoof. Because he came to us to warn us of the dangers of this world, so that we would not have to suffer. He was under no need to do this. He is already the beloved of Allah; Jannah was made for him. Yet he took it upon himself to accept this mission of guiding us, out of the ra'fa he carried in his heart for us. And because he is Raheem, he framed the shareeah for us as a medicine to heal our sick souls, so that they might be raised up and made worthy of the raheemiyyah of Allah in the world to come. That is why he is called رحمۃ للعالمین. Is this not remarkable? Allah is رب العالمین. Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) is Rehmatul-lil-Alameen. He is a rehma for the alameen — for everything that is known.

for which Allah is a Rabb. And raham takes an extraordinary measure of patience. Let me give you an example. Imagine that we are all seated together in a classroom, and not over Skype as we are now. At this very moment, some of you are having the finest sleep of your lives. Some of you are playing on your phones. Some of you are texting and updating your status on Facebook. Some of you are wondering, "Where am I?," and some of you are paying attention and taking notes. But I cannot see any of you, so you may do as you please. There is nothing I can do to stop you.

But imagine instead that we are all seated together in a classroom, face to face, and that I am teaching you this material on al-Fateha. I explain the whole of it to you, looking at you, reading your faces, checking that you understand. "Hey! What did I just say? Hey, you! Repeat what I just said. Hey! Let us have a quiz right now." This here is merely a lecture. Here you can get away with anything. But when you are in a classroom, the teacher makes certain that every student understands.

Yet there are always some students. Consider that I prepared for this session the whole of yesterday, wondering how I was going to teach this material. I say to myself that I am going to make this such a marvelous lesson that they will give me an Academy Award once I have finished teaching it. So I teach this lesson and I am so proud of myself. I truly feel that I have done it perfectly, that I have made the point land, that everyone in the class has understood, and that I am ready to give myself a pat on the back.

And then one of you raises his hand, after a full hour of teaching, and says, "Asif mamu!" I say, "Yes, X!" "Ahh, I do not understand!" "Oh, all right, no problem. What is it that you do not understand?" "Ahh, anything." All right, so you do not understand anything. No problem. Let me begin again. Let me give you the entire lesson once more, and this time I will make eye contact with you alone. Every two minutes I look at you and say, "Are you all right?" "Uh-huh, uh-huh." "Do you understand it?" "Uh-huh, uh-huh." One whole hour passes by, and I say, "Alhamdulillah." Everyone else is thinking, "Why are we listening to all of this again?" But then you raise your hand once more. "Asif mamu, I have a question." "Yes, yes, please." "I, I still do not understand it."

Now, if you have ever sat in a classroom, especially in Pakistan or India, and a student does this, after the whole lecture has been explained twice, and the student says, "I still do not understand anything," is the teacher pleased or angry? We cannot do such things here in America, but when we were in Pakistan, we would then receive a very special kind of lesson afterward.

So I say, "You know what, class is over, all the children are going home, why do you not come with me to my office. I will sit with you in the office. I will not take my lunch today. I will explain it to you all over again." If the first way did not work, and the second way did not work, I will try to explain it a third way. And so I explain it all over again. At the end of it, you say, "Asif mamu, I am not sure that teaching is the right profession for you, because I still, I, I just do not understand. I do not get it. Have you considered driving a taxi, or something else, because clearly teaching is not the right thing for you." So I say, "All right, all right. I am not giving up on you. Why do you not come over to my house for dinner. As we eat dinner, I will explain it to you again." The same thing after dinner. I say,

Why do you not simply move in with me? One can only laugh. Does any teacher ever do such a thing? Once a student says, "I do not understand." The first time, perhaps he is confused. The second time, perhaps he is a slow learner. The third time, he is certainly toying with you; he is merely playing games now.

Messengers as a Mercy

Now, if this is unacceptable behavior even at the level of ordinary teaching, then what of something as sacred and as exalted as the Qur'an? Yet if you study the history of revelation, to whom were the Qur'an and this Messenger sent? To the disbelievers of Quraysh — people such as Abu Lahab, Abu Jahal, and Abu Sufyan — fanatical disbelievers, haters of Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam). Should the Qur'an even be revealed to such people? Do they even deserve something as precious as the Qur'an? No. They do not deserve even a single verse of the Qur'an. They are not worthy of it. When al-Rahman gives them a surah, they reject it. He gives them another surah, and they cast it aside. He gives them another surah, and they mock it. Yet He keeps on giving them surahs — verses upon verses, surah upon surah. Why? Because of His intense mercy, because of His constant mercy. That is the mercy of Allah (Subhanhu Wa Ta'ala) in action.

And consider, too, that the Qur'an is in fact Allah speaking to us. The Qur'an is Allah holding a conversation with us. When you insult someone, when you reject someone, when you mock someone, the first thing they do is stop speaking to you. Is that not true? When you insult someone, the first thing they do is stop speaking to you. This is a normal human reaction. These people are not only insulting Allah; they are insulting His beloved Prophet, they are insulting His beloved, they are mocking His beloved Messenger (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam). And still Allah continues to speak to them. And He keeps telling His Messenger:

وَٱصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَٱهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًۭا جَمِيلًۭا

Be patient with them. I know that they say evil things about you; they are constantly wounding your heart.

وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ يَضِيقُ صَدْرُكَ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ

We know that your breast grows tight because of the terrible things these people say to you. Yet still you go and speak with them. This is what is called al-Rahman. No human being is capable of mercy such as this.

If any one of you were to insult me — if you were to call me insane, if you walked up to me and said, "Asif Mama, you are the devil! You are misguiding people. You are a disbeliever" — if even one of you said such terrible things about me, and then said evil things about my father, my mother, my family, my daughter — then at the very least, at the very least, what do you suppose I would do? Since I am afraid of going to prison, what is the very least I would do? I would throw you out of the session, or I would shut the sessions down. Now, did all of you insult me, or did one of you insult me? Only one of you insulted me. Yet I would be so discouraged that I would take the most extreme measure I could think of. In other words, one person is enough for me to say that I never wish to feel the pain of that insult again. Is that not so?

My beloved Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) is reciting the Qur'an to these people, and they are constantly saying terrible things to him and about him — about his parents, about his family members, about everyone connected with him. And is only one person saying this?

or is a whole group of people saying it? An entire group of them are saying it.

Consider this. I am nothing. If someone insults me, there is little I can say, because I am no one. If not through me, then Allah will provide someone else to teach you. After all, who am I? I am nothing. I am no one. But Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) — when someone insults him, he has every right to be angry. He has every right to take the severest measures. For he is not a nobody; he is a somebody. And he is a somebody to Allah, the most powerful of all creators. And to Him, His messenger is the most beloved of all His creation. Allah Himself says in the Qur'an:

وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ

Know that my messenger is among you. This is no small thing.

Now this same messenger of Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) is insulted by men such as Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, and Abu Lahab, and the next day he must return and speak with these very people again. And they turn to Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) and say: Oh, you did not have your fill yesterday? You have come back for more? Let me offer you some fresh insults today. And the man insults him even worse than before. Then the messenger returns, and Allah sends him back to recite yet more of the Qur'an to them, and permits them to mock the verses once again. And he does this every single day, for a decade or more. Is that easy? Reflect upon it, so that you may truly appreciate it.

You know the name Abu Jahl, which means the father of ignorance. That is what Abu Jahl means. This dreadful man — when the son of Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) died, this vile person, his own uncle, went out into the street beating a stick against a piece of metal, celebrating and shouting: بطر محمد، بطر محمد — Muhammad's lineage has ended, Muhammad's lineage has ended. These are the kind of people he was dealing with. These are the kind of people he was sent to help.

By the way, when someone insults us, why do we respond with the severest measures? Because we are all people of dignity, are we not? You go to school, and someone calls you by a foul name; you come home, and it shows upon your face. If someone asks what happened, you say you do not wish to speak of it. You are ready to abandon school altogether. Why do you have so extreme a reaction? Because you are a decent person.

You see, that is the difference between a decent person and someone base. People who use filthy language all the time have no respect for themselves or for others. So when others speak filth to them, they actually enjoy it. It makes no difference to them, for they have no self-respect. No dignity remains within them. So they take pleasure when others use foul language with them, and then they answer back with worse still. But people of dignity, people who respect themselves, cannot bear foul language when it is directed at them. It wounds them within. As the Arabs would say:

رُبَّ قَولٍ اَشَدُّ مِن ثَول

Harsh words wound more than a physical beating.

Rasul Allah is the most dignified person ever to walk upon the face of this earth. And he had to hear the most terrible things, over and over and over again. And we know that Allah loves His messenger (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) utterly, and yet Allah says to him: Go back to them. Only be patient, and keep delivering the message.

This is once again mercy that is completely illogical, mercy that is entirely beyond measure. And this astonishing love, this astonishing patience, is made real and practical in Surah Rehman through the repetition of a single verse: فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ. فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ. فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ. Then how many favors of Allah will you deny? Allah is constantly calling out to these disbelievers of Mecca, showing them His love, His care, His Rehmaniyah. And they, just as constantly, reject Him and His messenger (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam). He explains it one way, then another way, then a third way, then a fourth, and He goes on and on, explaining it in different ways, hoping that something will finally get through to them.

And the most beautiful thing about this surah is that it begins with the word ar-Rehman, and then every single thing Allah speaks of after that is bound up with His Rahmaniyyah, His intense love. ٱلرَّحْمَنُ. عَلَّمَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ. The Rehman taught you the Quran. ٱلرَّحْمَنُ. خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَنَ. The Rehman created human beings. ٱلرَّحْمَنُ. عَلَّمَهُ ٱلْبَيَانَ. The Rehman gave you the ability to articulate. ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍۢ وَٱلنَّجْمُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ. The sun and the moon move with precise calculation, and the stars and the trees are in sajda, in perfect obedience to their master. Who did that for you? The Rehman. وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ. He raised the heavens and established balance between all things. Who did that for you? The Rehman. Why did He do it? أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْمِيزَانِ. So that you would not transgress in matters of justice. وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلَا تُخْسِرُوا۟ ٱلْمِيزَانَ. So weigh your actions with justice, and do not try to skim off the top. Look! When it came to doing things for you, I was completely fair with you. I gave you everything you need, and more. I did not say, oh, that is good enough, that will do. So then why do you not respond in kind? Why are you not fair with me?

وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ فِيهَا فَكِهَةٌۭ وَٱلنَّخْلُ ذَاتُ ٱلْأَكْمَامِ وَٱلْحَبُّ ذُو ٱلْعَصْفِ وَٱلرَّيْحَانُ. And I laid out the earth for you. In it I created delicious fruits and palm trees loaded with dates. I created grain and husk and scented plants for you. Look at everything I have done for you! فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ. I have done so much for you. I have given you so much. How many more favors of your master will you deny?

And then He goes on to explain it in a different way. You see, a human being with a sound essence accepts Allah as Rabb and Rehman even before the revelation began. We spoke about that. But if someone is not of a sound intellect, then simply reflecting on these ayats I have just mentioned, in which Allah describes His favors upon them, that should be enough to make him a believer. But if even that is not enough, Allah explains it in yet another way. خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَنَ مِن صَلْصَلٍۢ كَٱلْفَخَّارِ وَخَلَقَ ٱلْجَآنَّ مِن مَّارِجٍۢ مِّن نَّارٍۢ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَيْنِ مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌۭ لَّا يَبْغِيَانِ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا ٱللُّؤْلُؤُ وَٱلْمَرْجَانُ وَلَهُ ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْمُنشَـَٔاتُ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ كَٱلْأَعْلَمِ. I am the one who created you from clay, and the jinn from smokeless fire. I created you using two completely different materials.

I submit myself as master of the easts and the west. Do you not see how I make two seas meet, بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌۭ لَّا يَبْغِيَانِ, from which you draw pearls and corals. I made it possible for enormous towering ships to sail upon the water. Only consider that. These vast, massive cargo ships, weighing thousands of tons, float upon something as fragile as water. It is by physics, yes. Allah created these laws of physics that make it possible. But the very idea of a colossal ship sailing upon something like water is astonishing. فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ. So then how many blessings of your master will you deny?

So you see, first he sets out his favors, then his magnificent powers. Look at what I can do. Do you now see that I am Rehman? No. Let me explain in another way. كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍۢ وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلَلِ وَٱلْإِكْرَامِ يَسْـَٔلُهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِى شَأْنٍۢ سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ ٱلثَّقَلَانِ. Everything in this universe that I have created, including you, is in a state of annihilation. Everything moves toward its end. The only thing that will not die is the powerful and noble essence of your master. Wajh is generally translated as face, but linguistically it means essence, because the essence of a human being is the five senses and the intellect, all of which reside in the head. سجد وجھی البالی الفانی لی وجھک الدائم الباقی. I submit my wajh, my essence, which is temporary and in a state of deterioration and annihilation, to your essence, which is eternal and everlasting.

يَسْـَٔلُهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِى شَأْنٍۢ. Everything in the heavens and the earth turns to me for its need, and every single day I am occupied in work for them. But do not think that my work has distracted me from you. سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ ٱلثَّقَلَانِ. Soon I will free myself to take account of your deeds, when you return to me. Do you think you will last in this world forever? Do you not see that everything in this duniya moves toward decay and ugliness? The most beautiful places turn into ruins. The most beautiful faces wrinkle. The most beautiful plants decay. Is it this duniya that you lust for and lose your mind over? Duniya comes from the word danaa, which means inferior. Akhira comes from the root word khair, which means superior. You would give up the khair I have for you over this dana? فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ. So then how many favors of your master will you deny?

You see, he spoke of these favors, then of his majesty, then of the temporal state of this world. Do you still not see that I am Rehman? Fine. Now a challenge. يَمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَن تَنفُذُوا۟ مِنْ أَقْطَارِ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنفُذُوا۟ ۚ لَا تَنفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَنٍۢ. All of you jinn and mankind together, you think you are so capable. Then try to pass out of the limits and boundaries of my heavens and earth. Try to escape the boundaries of my universe. Go ahead, try. فَٱنفُذُوا۟. You will never be able to. لَا تَنفُذُونَ إِلَّا بِسُلْطَنٍۢ. Except by the authority of the king. This is my kingdom, and you are my subjects. And you cannot leave my kingdom until I permit it through death. You are not as powerful as you think you are. فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ. How many favors of your master will you deny?

Now do you understand that I am Rahman? Now do you believe? No.

Another way I will explain it to you. He gives a warning of punishment. He brings forth His compassion. Consider this. If you intend to stand before me in this state of denial, having rejected my favors and refused my blessings, then that cause will have an effect. You can see it in the world I created: every cause has an effect. Do you know what effect you are bringing about through your disbelief?

يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُمَا شُوَاظٌۭ مِّن نَّارٍۢ وَنُحَاسٌۭ فَلَا تَنتَصِرَانِ

Flames of fire and smoke will be sent upon you, and you will not be able to defend yourselves.

If love does not work, if glory and majesty do not work, if lordship does not work, then perhaps fear will work upon you. Perhaps an awareness of the dangers that lie ahead will work for you. This is not how I wish you to believe. I want you to believe through my love, through my majesty, through my lordship. But if none of that works, and fear is the only thing to which you will respond, then let it be so. At the very least you will be saved from the fire of hell.

يُعْرَفُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَهُمْ فَيُؤْخَذُ بِٱلنَّوَصِى وَٱلْأَقْدَامِ

The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by their forelocks and their feet.

هَذِهِۦ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِى يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُون

This is the hell that you criminals have been denying.

يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍۢ

They will pass between it and scalding water whose heat is of the utmost degree.

You know, in the Qur'an, when Allah speaks of the fire of hell, He does not hold back. If you look at the imagery of hellfire in this surah, or in any other, it is horrible. Boiling water poured upon people. People burned alive. Yelling and screaming. It is extremely frightening. It is certainly not PG-13. It is fully rated "R." These verses contain descriptions and images of extreme torture and pain.

And this is what people quote to make their case against Islam. If your Allah is so loving, so merciful, how can He do that? How can a loving, caring god do that to his creation? Look, they say, it says so in the Qur'an, right here, in Surah Rahman. He will torture people. He will burn them. Does this sound to you like a loving god?

The Qur'an is filled with descriptions of the fire of hell and its torments, and these can be deeply disheartening. Even in the majalis and the asbaaq, these verses and examples are quoted constantly, which leaves me with the feeling that the aim is submission through fear. Is this the Islamic approach? The examples given to illustrate the ideal degree of certain qualities — worship, generosity, courage — seem impossible to follow in this day and age. So what good are these examples to us?

Allah asks His Messenger to say:

قُلْ يَعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

Why does Allah say "Qul" — you tell them? Is the Messenger not already telling them everything else? The words of the Qur'an, as we now know, are the words of Rasul Allah (SAS). So why is Rasul Allah himself saying QUL? Why does he not simply say the thing itself? Because in saying Qul, he is teaching us the way to speak to others about Islam. He is teaching us that when we speak to other Muslims, and even to non-Muslims, this is what our attitude should be. And what is that attitude?

It was critical for the people of that time to hear the message of hope from their Messenger (SAS), and to carry that sunnah forward to the generations after them. It is a command from Allah to His Messenger to deliver the message of hope to the people of that time. And when we read it, the grammar is structured in such a way that it becomes a command for us as well: that when we speak to other Muslims, and even to non-Muslims, our message should be one of delivering hope, so that we carry on the legacy of Rasul Allah in giving hope. You and I are meant to use Islam to give people hope. All of that is carried inside that QUL. zumar_hope: 10:00

Our deen begins with hope. It does not begin with warnings. The message we have mostly been exposed to since childhood is that Islam is full of threats, that our deen is full of threats: do this, and Allah will get you. From childhood, parents teach children this message. You are doing haraam! Allah is going to punish you for that — and then there is this kind of punishment and that kind of punishment in Jahannum. Where does this begin?

One of the things I come across from time to time is the awareness that on the one hand we are speaking about the Book of Allah and the time of the Sahaba and their immaculate character — we are speaking about that ideal era we learn about in our sacred texts — and on the other hand, in stark contrast to it, stands our own reality: the things we deal with day after day in our ordinary lives. Sometimes our realities are so far removed from some of the things we talk about, are they not? And we have to bring those two things together. Sometimes these two things — what we read about Islam and the Sahaba, and our day-to-day realities — are so far apart that at times it feels as though the Qur'an, the sunnah, the seerah of the Prophet, and the ashaab are speaking about an entirely different reality. It does not even seem to be speaking about my reality.
body.topic_title_en: How to Call People to Islam
body.topic_title_ur: How to call peple to Islam

body.text_en:
When many people hear the stories of the great companions, the Sahaba of Rasul Allah (PBUH), and of what they accomplished, it feels as though these were legendary superheroes who did astonishing things, so far removed from where I am, or from where anybody I know is.

I feel so far away from it that it seems as though none of this applies to me or to my times. What this does to people, psychologically, is that it reduces the counsel and the guidance of the Qur'an and the Sunnah to the very same level as the criticism voiced by the disbelievers. The disbelievers said: أساطیر الاولین. These are the stories and legends of ancient times, of the earliest nations. That is all this is, they said; these are merely stories.

And what we hear around us, even within our jamaat in various discourses, unfortunately sometimes creates this atmosphere, or a culture in which we speak about the past in a way that is completely disconnected from the realities of our own time. We make it feel as though we will never, ever come close to what has already happened in the past, and so we stop looking to that same text for counsel and guidance. We think this text is not for us; we think it is for people far better than ourselves, people who lived in those ideal times. This is genuinely harmful. It damages us psychologically.

To give an example: when we hear about charity and generosity, we hear the story of a companion who steps forward and donates half of all he owns to Islam. And then Maulana Ali steps forward and donates everything he owns in the name of Allah, keeping nothing but the clothes on his body. These are the heroes of Islam. Now, when any Muslim group, or even our own jamaat, asks for donations, these are the stories told to encourage people to give generously. There are some people in the gathering who become truly motivated: yes, I am going to give ten thousand dollars to Allah! But then there are people like me, sitting there and thinking, you know what, I am never going to give away everything I own. I am not even able to give half of what I own to Allah. Not even a tenth of what I own. The best I can manage is fifty dollars, and how can that possibly compare with those who gave half of their wealth, or all of it? Therefore I am scum. And that is not fair. That is simply not fair.

Because when we study the history of that period, we find that it was not made up only of these towering individuals. There were thousands upon thousands of companions who did not give half of what they owned, nor all of it. They gave less. Yet Allah spoke of all of them and said: رضی اللہ عنہ و رضو عنہ. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Allah.

In other words, what we do is take the highest examples in order to motivate people: the highest examples we can find of sacrifice, of generosity, of courage. But we do not realize that although some people may indeed be motivated by them, other people are in fact completely demoralized by them. They say: that is impossible! This must have been for that era; it no longer applies to me. So how do we reconcile these two things? How do we manage that?
body.topic_title_en: How to Call People to Islam
body.topic_title_ur: How to call peple to Islam

body.text_en:
Well, if you truly study the stories of the companions, you do not find only one kind of story. You find a great deal of variation. You find people of astonishing sacrifice, but you also find people who struggled with those very same qualities. They could not act at that extreme level, but operated at a far more modest one. And what we find is that Allah appreciated and loved every one of them.

Allah even spoke in the Qur'an about the degrees between them: لَا يَسْتَوِى مِنكُم مَّنْ أَنفَقَ مِن قَبْلِ ٱلْفَتْحِ وَقَتَلَ ۚ أُو۟لَٓئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنفَقُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدُ وَقَتَلُوا۟ ۚ وَكُلًّۭا وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ The people who sacrificed and spent before the victory came are not the same as the people who spent and sacrificed after victory came... but to everyone Allah promises the best! Is that not remarkable? Allah uses the word AlHusna, which is the superlative form in the Arabic language. The very best! He did not say that the very best belongs only to those who struggled in the hardest of times, and not so much to those who came later and had a far easier struggle. In His infinite mercy, Allah says that every one of them will have the very best. You simply do what you can. You do your best at your own level. In other words, there will always be people who are able to do a great deal more than you. But there will also be a great many people who are able to do a great deal less than you. And Allah has promised the best to all of them.
