The point I am trying to make is that the teachings of the Qur'an apply to all of us. But the way they apply to each of us individually may differ. They may apply to you at one degree and to me at another. Yet in the end it is all good, wonderful, acceptable, and appreciated by Allah.

So there is a common ground among all of us as Muslims. At the very baseline, at the foundation, we have our seven pillars: wilayah, taharah, salaah, zakaat, saum, hajj, and jehad. I do not need to give you a Sunday session about this; you all know what these mean. At the most basic level this applies to all of us as Muslims. We must fulfill these obligations: five prayers (at the very least the Farz), zakaat, thirty days of fasting, hajj once in a lifetime. We have to do what we have to do, and we have to stay away from what we have to stay away from. Right? That is the baseline for every single Muslim in the world.
body.topic_title_en: How to Call People to Islam
body.topic_title_ur: How to call peple to Islam

body.text_en:
There are various people in this session, with different circumstances and different challenges in life. Some are probably more knowledgeable than me. Some are certainly more pious than I will ever be in this lifetime. Some of you have been studying Islam for years. Some may be hearing what I am saying for the first time in their lives. And this is just within our small group. Widen the scope of this conversation, and we will find people who grew up in our jamaat and know nothing about Islam at all, because their parents wanted nothing to do with Islam. As a group we are diverse. Not everyone is on the same page. This is simply the reality, is it not? So it is irrational to think that the way the advice and counsel of the Qur'an affects you will be the same for everyone. It is illogical to believe that the way you live by its teachings will be the same. There are certain obligations expected of all of us, whatever our circumstances or situations. But then there are certain things that apply at a very personal level, and those will differ from one individual to another.

So let us talk about that baseline. I feel that my job in these sessions is to try to speak to the person here who is the least committed to Islam.

My job is to try to address the person who does not even want to be in these sessions. That is the person I am trying to reach. Why? Because I was once that person. Because I was once holding on to Islam by a thread — or perhaps not even by that much. I was convinced that I did not even want to be a Muslim, let alone a Sulemani. Now, if there is someone like that in this group, and I ask him or her to give up half of his belongings, he will say: "You know what? I was not even sure about giving a hundredth of my belongings, and you are asking for half, or for all of it. Forget it. I am out of here. This is far too much to ask!" The young man already walked in thinking that Islam asks too much of him, and I have just helped him along. I have just helped him along by handing him the highest possible standards — standards that not even the ordinary companions in the time of Rasul Allah could live by, standards that only the very, very, very topmost among them could live by. And I have just presented those demands to this young man as though this is what is expected of him. It is not fair. It is simply not fair. Yet this is what happens all the time around us. We need to start taking it easy. We need to start talking about the basics, and we need to give hope to the younger generations.
body.topic_title_en: How to Call People to Islam
body.topic_title_ur: How to call peple to Islam

body.text_en:
Here is something else I noticed in myself. When I became inclined toward religion, I began to learn more and more. And as my knowledge increased, my teacher expected more and more of me in terms of action and character, because he now held me to a higher standard, because he wanted me to rise to the occasion. But the mistake I made was this: as I began to learn more and more, and to take page after page of notes, and as I came to know far more than I had known years earlier — do you know what happened? As I learned more, I realized that more was expected of me; and as I realized that more was expected of me, I turned to everyone else and began to think that more was expected of them too. And that is not true. I have had the most radical, the most judgmental, the most unforgiving conversations with people, some of them in these very sessions. But later, when I found my path, I realized that I had been completely wrong. This was something that was simply expected of me, and yet I began to place that burden on the people around me. That is wrong. I cannot do that. But is this not what parents sometimes do with our children?

No one ever carried a heavier burden on his shoulders than Rasul Allah (SAS). No man in human history ever did, and no man in the human future ever will carry a burden greater than the one this man (SAS) had to carry for twenty-three years — which is no time at all in which to do what he did. And yet, when he is sending people out on a mission to spread the word of Islam, he tells his companions: یسیرا ولا عسیرا. Make things easy and not difficult. Make things easy. Go easy on people; do not be hard on them. SubhanAllah! He is instructing the sahaba in ease. He is not telling the sahaba to inform people that they had better submit to Islam and become the most ideal Muslims who ever walked the earth. No — just go easy on people, take it easy, have them do the best they can: یسیرو ولا تعسیرو. It is an extraordinary piece of advice.

And the optimism — we do not talk enough about the optimism of the messengers (AS).

You know that again and again in the Qur'an, Allah describes the messengers as the givers of good news and the givers of warning: مبشرین و منظرین, مبشر و نظیر. These words occur over and over in the Qur'an. They came to give good news, and they came to give warning. Now, those of you who stand in a teaching position, as a professor or a tutor — if you have a difficult crowd, is it easy to stay optimistic? Is it easy to keep smiling? It becomes impossible, does it not? If the children are not listening in a classroom, or if you are speaking and people are talking while you speak, or if you are delivering a lecture and people stand up and walk out — is that agitating or not? Is it disturbing? Is it frustrating?
body.topic_title_en: How to Call People to Islam
body.topic_title_ur: How to call peple to Islam

body.text_en:
This is exactly what the messengers faced constantly. Yet they are advised to hold to a positive attitude, even though holding to a positive attitude is very hard when the people you are speaking with are agitating to you. The Prophet (SAS) is told that he must keep a positive attitude even when people are not receptive. That is incredible. That is not easy. Giving good news to people is easy, but giving good news to people who are simply obnoxious, who do not want to hear a word you have to say, and still keeping your positive attitude, and still continuing to give good news — that is truly amazing.

And yes, نظیر as well, of course: to give warning. But the first thing mentioned every single time is good news. Always good news first, and only then warning. مبشرا first, and only then نظیرا. They were first givers of good news, spreaders of optimism; they were positive people. What that means for us is that our conversations about Islam have to be overwhelmingly positive. Our conversations about Islam have to be overwhelmingly positive — in light of the fact that the prophets are first بشیر and only then نظیر. They are first basheer, they are first givers of good news, they are first مبشر.

And by the way, by the way — SubhanAllah! There is only one place where Allah puts warning first and good news after. Allah, in His remarkable eloquence, does this even in the verb forms He chooses. I do not want to get technical with you, but it is a beautiful point. Allah speaks about the Qur'an itself in this beautiful Surah Al-Kahf:

قَيِّمًۭا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًۭا شَدِيدًۭا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّلِحَتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًۭا

He began there with warning — but He said ینذر. In Arabic the word أنذر means to warn, and نذر also means to warn; grammatically, however, انذر means to warn one time, while نذر means to warn over and over and over again. So Allah says ینذر, meaning to warn once. Yet in the same verse, when He speaks of giving good news, He says یبشر, which is the continual form. When He spoke of warning He used it in the single form, but when He spoke of good news He flooded it with continuity. SubhanAllah.

Even where it began with warning, the good news was multiplied immediately:

ُ وَيُبَشِّرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلصَّلِحَتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًۭا۔ مَّكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًۭا

They will live there forever. There is no مَّكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًۭا attached to the warning. That is mentioned only for the good news. SubhanAllah — over and over and over again.

So what does that mean for you and me? Think of the parents who tell their children, "You had better listen to me, otherwise Allah will put you in jahannam!"
body.topic_title_en: How to Call People to Islam
body.topic_title_ur: How to call peple to Islam

body.text_en:
The teacher who tells his students that if you do not do this, that, and the other, Allah will burn you in hell! What are we doing? We are undoing the legacy of delivering the message of Islam with love and with mercy. We want to plant the teachings of Islam within our children and within those we love, but the approach we take is not that of بشیر و نذیرا. The approach we take is نزیرا و نذیرا. We try to teach Islam to children in the most un-Islamic way possible. We do it by frightening them. We try to frighten them into submission. Now, I am not saying that this is never good. Sometimes a little warning is good. But what should there be in overwhelming measure? Overwhelmingly there should be love, good news, and encouragement.

Look, children can be annoying. I have two of them, so I know. They can truly get on your nerves. Sometimes they make Nazneen so angry that I go and hide in the basement. I do not know what else to do. But even in those situations we need to learn the manner in which the messengers carried out their message, because we are the messengers of Islam to our children and to the members of our family.

Many children grow up believing that everything in Islam is forbidden, or that they are going to be punished. Allah will be really angry at you! Allah will burn you in hell! I once heard a two-year-old say to her father in front of me, "Baba, I cannot eat ice cream, right? Because Allah is going to get really mad?" Ah, that is a tragedy. That is truly a tragedy. A two-year-old says that about Allah. That is very sad. They should know wonderful things about Allah, such as how much Allah loves them and cares for them, and how Allah made the ice cream sweet for them, not how Allah will punish them if they eat the ice cream. We impose our own anger and our own frustrations onto Allah. That is what we do, and it is not right. This happens in families, in communities, and in marriages. How is a parent comfortable talking about their children burning in hell? How is that even possible? How are you comfortable with that?

And then in the communal setting, every single khutba is about the Day of Judgment, and about how we will be punished for our sins, and about people being thrown face first into the fire, and about their good deeds being wiped away because they were munafiq. I am not saying that those warnings do not exist. I am certainly not saying that. But we receive so much doom and gloom, and we pass on so much doom and gloom to our children and to the people around us, that on a large scale the people around us simply lose hope. They begin to believe that they are headed for punishment anyway. And what happens when people lose hope and become convinced that they are doomed and are heading toward punishment? Then the doors to sin open wide. What is the point of any of this anyway? One might as well go out with a bang. People simply lose hope.

body.text_en:
Let me begin with the last part of the question: should the one who preaches always practice what he preaches? Yes, he should. No one, so to speak, stands above the law. This is especially true of a person who holds some position of authority and has been given permission to teach others; such a person must certainly lead by example. So let me take my own case, since I am in something of that position myself. Everything I share with you in these sessions is meant for all of us, myself included. The fact that I am the one speaking and you are the ones listening does not place me above you in any way. And Allah knows that I am the one most in need of these teachings. Before the eyes of Allah, then, we all stand in the same place.

Allah AWJ in fact speaks about those who speak about Islam: وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًۭا مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ? وَعَمِلَ صَلِحًۭا — who could be better in speech than someone who calls people to Allah and does good deeds himself? In other words, he is not above action himself; he cannot be all talk. He has to take action himself. وَقَالَ إِنَّنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ — and he openly declares that he is among the Muslims. This means two things: first, that he is proud to be a Muslim; second, that he does not consider himself above other Muslims.

So we are all in this together, friends. No one holds a higher position before Allah in this world. In the Akhirah He has ranks, but right now, as Muslims, we are all equals — because, as you know, we carry this chip on our shoulders called "Sulemani." We are staunch Sulemanis.

The Qur'an is full of descriptions of people who are punished. It is full of descriptions of hell. It is full of descriptions of people who are corrupt, whose good deeds are not accepted — do you see? — whose deeds are brought to nothing on the Day of Judgment. It describes people who stand on the Day of Judgment and are stunned. There are Muslims spoken of in Surat al-Hadid who are in shock, because they had been standing in the company of the believers, walking toward paradise, and all at once a wall is dropped in front of them. يُنَادُونَهُمْ أَلَمْ نَكُن مَّعَكُمْ — Were we not with you? We were supposed to be together. And they say: قَالُوا۟ بَلَىٰ وَلَكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنتُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ وَٱرْتَبْتُمْ وَغَرَّتْكُمُ ٱلْأَمَانِىُّ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ

This is an extraordinarily frightening verse. The people who are on the other side of the wall, walking toward paradise, say: yes, you used to be with us, but you involved yourselves in discord. You did not take religion seriously. You used to put things off. You used to procrastinate. You used to say, I WILL change. I will stop this forbidden thing I am doing. I will begin to pray regularly. But later. Let the summer break end, then I will get serious. After my children grow up, after they are married, then I will get out of the forbidden business. Then I will stop selling alcohol. Whatever it may be — you kept putting it off.

Those people say: yes, we prayed together, we used to live in the same neighborhood, we went to the same jamaat khana or mosque, we greeted one another with salaam — but you placed yourselves in discord. وَٱرْتَبْتُمْ — and you doubted my words. Pheww, that is never going to happen. No wall is going to be dropped in front of me. And if it is, I can climb walls. Do you see? That kind of attitude. Making jokes about religion. Not taking these warnings seriously.

وَغَرَّتْكُمُ ٱلْأَمَانِىُّ — And your false hopes deluded you. What does that mean? It means that after everything you were doing, you supposed you would simply weep a little on the prayer mat and offer a few supplications, and that would be enough, and you would walk straight into paradise. As Allah says: أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ — You assumed you would just walk into paradise! You were deluded by that thought, by that manner of thinking. حَتَّىٰ جَآءَ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ — until the decree of Allah finally came. وَغَرَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ — and the one who is truly skilled at deceiving deceived you thoroughly! He deceived you well. You were completely certain that paradise had been made for you. These verses too are in the Qur'an, and they are quite frightening.

Now, if you read only these kinds of verses and dwell on them, you will become altogether despondent. You will feel that nothing you do is good enough. I do not know whether I will be on the right side of the wall or the wrong side of the wall on the Day of Judgment. I do not know whether my repentance is genuine or artificial. So how am I supposed to know?

body.text_en:
We are going to spend this entire session together. In our previous session we began to speak about the meaning of the word intellect, العقل. I presented to you the hadith of Rasul Allah (SAS) concerning the intellect. Today I would like to examine those same ideas in greater detail. So what did we say the word Aql means? The first meaning of the word العقل, as I explained, is that of a container.

Now, when I explain the meaning of an Arabic word to you, you must always keep one thing in mind: I am not speaking about spoken Arabic. I am not speaking about Egyptian, Moroccan, Kuwaiti, or Saudi Arabic. The Arabic we hear all around us today is spoken Arabic. It is distorted, deformed, and unpleasant. You can listen to two Arabs speaking today, and it can actually offend the ear. Hammana Hammana Hammana — that is all one hears. And yet you also hear it said that Arabic is such a beautiful, such an eloquent language, is that not so? So you need to hold on to this distinction: when someone speaks of the beauty of Arabic, especially in connection with the Qur'an, he is not referring to spoken Arabic. He is not even referring to proper Arabic. He is referring to what? Ancient Arabic.

The Qur'an was not revealed for the Kuwaitis, the Saudis, or the Egyptians. It was revealed to the ancient Arabs. So, in order to understand the depth in the meanings of this book, we have to understand it through the mind of the ancient Arab, not the Arab of today. If you look up the word Aql in an Arabic-to-English dictionary today, you will find it translated simply as intellect, and nothing more, because that is all it means to the Arabs of today. But that is not what it meant to the Arabs in the time of Rasul Allah (SAS), and that is precisely what we are interested in learning: what did the word عقل mean to the ancient Arabs for whom the Qur'an was revealed? So you must always keep this distinction in mind, not only for what I say today, but also for all our future sessions.

We discussed, then, that العقل is a flexible container for علم, or knowledge, one that expands as knowledge increases. And as we learned from the hadith of Rasul Allah (SAS), it was the first thing that Allah created. It was the best and the loftiest thing that Allah created, and after its creation, Allah granted it complete freedom of choice.

اول ما خلق اللہُ العقل، فقال لہ اقبل فاقبل، و قال لہ ادبر فادبر

Let us examine this hadith a little further, from the standpoint of language. The first thing we notice is that the hadith states it was the very first thing that Allah created, اول ما خلق اللہُ العقل. Now, why is that significant? If you have many tasks to complete for school, what do you do? You set them in order of priority, do you not? What are the things you take into account when arranging your priorities? Urgency and importance may be among them; the length of the tasks in relation to the time available may be another. But the first thing you do is what? You draw up the list of tasks itself before you begin working on any of them. You have to write six different papers for your school. You have all the reference books stacked upon your table. You have a list of every link to the sites you are going to need. You have settled your order of priority as to which paper you will write first. You have your supply of cookies and your Cadbury eggs beside you.

you have chosen the playlist of the tunes you will play as you work on these papers. Wonderful. It is time to begin. It is time to write the first paper. What do you need? A pen. If you do not have a pen, does anything else matter, except the Cadbury eggs, of course? No. It is the very first thing you need in order to write your papers.

So Allah has created the heavens and the earths and everything that exists within them. He has created these mansions upon mansions in heaven, and He has created the hellfire. He has planned out His messengers: I will send Adam first, then Nooh, then Ibrahim, then Moosa, then Eisa (علیھم السلام). And then, finally, I will send My beloved prophet Muhammad (SAS) with this extremely elaborate, extremely eloquent, and symmetrically miraculous message for My creations, so that they may understand it, earn My reward, draw closer to Me, and to My love. But wait. What is the first thing they need in order to do that? The intellect. Without the intellect, nothing else will matter. Without the intellect, a person will not recognize My messenger, nor his message. He will not be able to see the miracles that I have placed for him within the message. And without the message, he will not be able to draw close to Me. He will not be able to enter this beautiful paradise that I have created for him.

Therefore, what was the first thing that Allah created? The intellect. SubhanAllah!

Now, if the intellect is the first thing Allah created, what is the first thing we should be using to understand His religion? The intellect. So tell me, how could I have agreed to responses such as, do not use your intellect, do not think too much about religion, it will drive you mad, and things of that kind? How could I have accepted that? Before any decision we make in our lives, how can we not present it before the intellect first? Will this benefit me in the long run, or will it harm me in the long run? Do I need this instant pleasure set right before me, or do I want the lasting, eternal pleasure that is to come?

فَٱسْتَبْشِرُوا۟ بِبَيْعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِى بَايَعْتُم بِهِ وَذَلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ

Congratulations, My believer! You have made a great sale. You are the one who will experience the ultimate, the greatest of all success.

The only one to congratulate you in these trying times will not be your friends. The only one to congratulate you will be Allah. Your congratulations will come from nowhere else; no one else will think you are making a wise decision. When you place your trust in Allah, let me tell you: sometimes the whole world will stand against you. And you will become so disheartened, so frustrated, that you will begin to lose hope. At such a time you must take hold of Allah's book and read it; and when you read it, you will hear Allah saying: Congratulations, My servant!

You've made an excellent trade. This is Me promising you your reward. May Allah grant me and you, and every one of us, the wisdom to take His promise seriously. Perhaps you have made a great many mistakes in the past. But today you can say: I want to make this sale now. What has happened has happened. I will not let my past determine my future. From this day onward, I am willing to choose this path. And if I fall short, if I make mistakes, that is all right; I will return to this bargain once more.

People will give up on you all the time. Your best friends will give up on you. Even your own parents may give up on you. Your spouse may give up on you. But Allah never gives up on you. Allah will never, ever give up on you. People will judge you and condemn you: You know what, you have broken your word too many times; that is it, the deal is off, end of story. But Allah will NEVER, NEVER close His doors on you. The only one who can close those doors is you! YOU can close these doors on yourself. Allah will never do it! SubhanAllah!

And this is what I want to show you children in these sessions: what Allah wants for us, how much He loves us, how much He cares for us, how He is the ONLY true friend you and I will ever have. But for that, we need to gain this knowledge from the Qur'an, so that the reward of the afterlife becomes visible to us, and we come to understand how the reward is so much greater than the fleeting, instant pleasures of this world. Because this world is dunya, which, as I told you, comes from the word "dana," meaning low — that is, easily accessible, instant — but inferior. Whereas akhirah comes from the word khair, which means superior. So Hayat al-Dunya means the inferior life, even though it is instant, whereas Hayat al-Akhirah means the superior life, even though it comes later. But everything worth anything always demands patience.

Yes, the rewards of this bargain come later. But if you honestly observe, the rewards of everything worth anything are always received later. Is school life inferior to professional life or not? Why? Because you are dependent. And why is professional life superior? Because you are independent! But to achieve this independent, superior life, where must you strive hard? Where must you sacrifice your pleasures? In your school life. Is it better to be an adult or a child? An adult! But you have to invest in those eighteen years of training to reap its rewards later. Is it better to have one mango, or to have a tree of mangoes? A tree, of course, loaded with mangoes! But do you get that the instant you plant the seed, or do you have to wait for it? You have to wait for it. But is the reward manifold greater than the instant gratification of one mango? Absolutely! Is it better to cut open the goose to get all the golden eggs today? Or to feed that goose and keep it alive, and delay that gratification by getting one golden egg every day? Is it better to enjoy all the money you have today, or is it wiser to invest it in stocks, or in long-term savings accounts, in order to collect double or triple the amount of the original investment? So the question before me and before you is this: Are these few temporary years of this dunya, of this inferior life, better? Or is the everlasting, superior life of the akhirah better? The akhirah!

But where must you strive in order to reap the rewards of that superior life? In this inferior life:

وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّن شَىْءٍۢ فَمَتَعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتُهَا ۚ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ

And whatever thing you have been given is only the enjoyment of this inferior life and its adornment. And what is with Allah is so much better and everlasting.

And then Allah asks us: أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ — so why do you not understand? What tool do you need in order to understand and to reason? The intellect! SubhanAllah!

بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا؟ وَٱلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰٓ

Do you really prefer the life of this inferior world, even though the afterlife is so much better and everlasting?

إِنَّ هَذَا لَفِى ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلْأُولَىٰ۔ صُحُفِ إِبْرَهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ

I have said these same things in the earlier books, in the books of Ibrahim and Moosa. This is nothing new that I am telling you. I have always told you this, from the beginning of time: that the afterlife is so much better than the life of this world. Why do you not understand? When will you understand?

The word أقبل comes from the root word قِبل, which means to face something or someone. From that same root word we get the word Qibla, as in, the Ka'aba is our qibla. Why? Because we turn our faces toward it in prayer. أقبل is an imperative verb. It is used when giving a command, a command to someone either to face them or to step forward toward them. So if I say, for example, أقبَلَ علیہ بالسَّیف, it means I am commanding someone: advance toward him with a sword!

ادبر, on the other hand, means to walk away from someone with one's back turned toward them. So if I tell you to step forward, you may move toward me while still facing me; and if I tell you to move back, you may also move back while still facing me. But that would not be ادبر. The word ادبر suggests that you actually turn around and walk away from me, showing me your back. So when Allah commanded the intellect to move toward Him by saying أقبل, it walked toward Him; and when He commanded it to move back by saying ادبر, it literally turned around and walked away from Allah, showing Allah its back. And what does it mean to turn your back? It means either to refuse something, to cease being involved in something, or to reject something.

What the hadith states, then, is that when Allah created this superior entity, which He named the intellect, He created it with the capacity to accept the truth and also to turn away from it. It had the ability to do both. It could walk toward Allah, and it could also turn its back on Allah and walk away from Him. Do you understand?

Other narrations extend this hadith further. They say that after commanding the intellect to move forward and to move back, Allah also said: ثم قال لہ اَقعُدْ فَقَعَدَ ثم قال لہ قُم فَقَامَ. After that, Allah ordered the intellect to sit down, and so it sat down; then Allah ordered it to rise, and so it stood up. What does this mean? It means to become passive, or to become active.

So this hadith suggests four possibilities within the intellect. The first is to move toward Allah. The second is to turn around and move away from Allah. The third is to sit down, which means to compromise for the sake of a greater good, as Imam Hassan (peace be upon him) did. He compromised with Mua'wiyah for the protection of Islam. The fourth is to stand its ground, no matter what, as Imam Hussain (peace be upon him) did at Karbala against Yazeed, also for the protection of Islam.

So after granting the intellect these four potentials, Allah informed the intellect of its importance, and of the role it would play in the lives of those who would receive this gift. Allah said: و عزتي و جلالي! ما خلقت خلقاً أعظمُ منک ولا اَطوعُ منک. By My honor and My superiority! I have not created anything more superior or more obedient than you.

The first thing to notice here is that Allah, out of His ninety-nine names, chose two particular names by which to swear: عزتي و جلالي, by My honor and My superiority. Now the question is, why did He choose these two names in particular? It is because this intellect that He created was a representative of these two names, honor and superiority.

First, a man is honored and dignified in this world and the hereafter by his intellect, and the Arabic word عزۃ represents honor and dignity. That is why He swore by عزتي.

Second, the intellect is also the most superior thing that Allah created, as He Himself declared: ما خلقت خلقاً اعظم منک, I have not created anything more superior than you. And this superiority comes from His جلالۃ. That is why He swore by His superiority, و جلالي.

Then He said: ولا اَطوعُ منک, I have not created anything more obedient than you. Now let us understand this word obedience, because it can carry a negative connotation. The word obedience, especially in the context of Islam, means willful compliance with an order, request, or law. It also means willing submission to an authority. This is truly important to understand, because obedience can also be achieved unwillingly. Obedience can be forced through fear; you can frighten someone into obedience. It can also be manufactured through the hope of a reward; for example, I can say that if you obey what I am asking you to do, then I will give you something in return as your reward.

God willing, we will cover the subject of obedience in detail later, when we speak about love. For now, I only want you to understand that the obedience Allah speaks of in this hadith is the obedience that stems from pure love. It is the willing submission of the soul to the command of Allah, purely out of deep-rooted love for Him, because of accepting Him as an الہ.

Not because of fear or hope.

So Allah informed the intellect that obedience, or submission, is part of your nature, because I have not created anything more obedient than you: ولا اَطوعُ منک. Only one question remains: to whom will you be obedient? To whom will you surrender yourself? Will you obey My message and My messenger? Or will you obey Iblees and his messengers? That I will leave up to you. But know that you will most certainly submit. You will either return to Me as My obedient followers, or you will return to Me as Shaitan's slaves. What you choose is up to you: بک أُعبَدُ و بک أُعصیٰ. You may choose to worship Me, or you may choose to disobey Me. Then He said: بک أُبدي و أُعيد، و لک الثواب و عليک العقاب. I am beginning My creation with you, making you their guide, granting you the capacity to accept truth or to reject it, to compromise with your desires or to stand firm upon your belief. And I am granting you complete freedom of choice. But know that, according to how you guide the souls, they will either receive My rewards or they will incur My wrath. In short, you will be responsible for their success, and you will be responsible for their destruction.

Does everyone understand everything so far?

Now a couple of questions arise at this point. I will state the questions first, and then let us discuss them one by one.

First, why did Allah give the intellect complete freedom? Is that not the root of all problems? We make bad choices because we can make bad choices. Allah could simply have restricted our intellects to do only good, could He not? He could have programmed it only to follow good and to turn away from evil. So why did He not? Would that not have been perfect for us?

A program is the definition of a machine. It would have created a slave mentality. Allah wants us to come to Him out of love, not by force. To distinguish the pious from the wretched. The example of the microwave.

Second, He says that all reward and punishment will depend on the choices that the intellect makes. What is this reward He is referring to? Paradise, yes? And what is the punishment He is speaking of? Hell. So why not simply create everyone in Paradise? After all, He did create Paradise for us human beings alone, did He not? So why did He not just do that? Why did He tie this reward and punishment to the intellect?

Justice to all creation. A reward is defined as something given in recognition of one's service, effort, or achievement. And if Paradise is a reward, then by the very definition of the word reward, it has to be earned. Paradise is a place of ranks, and ranks demand effort and achievements, and achievements depend on intellect.

In a school system, you have grades based on how students perform. But babies in a nursery have no ranks; they are all equal. A nursery teacher never says anything like, your baby just came first among all the babies, because first in what? Perhaps in soiling diapers? There is no intellect at that level, and therefore no effort, no achievements to be graded on. And justice dictates that reward has to be based on achievement.

Why not declare all the students in a class top of the year? Why not pay the doctors just as much as the clerks? In a company, why not have all the employees receive an equal salary?

So what have we discussed so far about the intellect?

First, it is a container for knowledge that expands as the knowledge increases.

Second,

The intellect was the first thing that Allah created. It was the loftiest, the most superior of Allah's creation, made for the purpose of obedience, willing submission to Allah. It was created with the potential to obey or to disobey in complete freedom of choice. And this is the stance that Islam takes in its message: the stance of choice.

وَقُلِ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ فَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن وَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيَكْفُر

My beloved messenger, reveal to them the truth about their Lord. Then whoever wishes may believe, and whoever wishes may disbelieve.

And why take this stance? Because Islam is a religion for the intellect, and the intellect has been given choice, and so the people of the intellect must also be given choice. SubhanAllah.

Then, in the previous session, we discussed that the intellect is also a scale. It can choose not only between good and evil, but also between two goods and two evils. Faced with a choice between two goods, it can choose the greater good, and given a choice between two evils, it can choose the lesser evil.

Now, in life, what dictates choice? Knowledge.

We did the exercise in which I compared the intellectual choices between a movie and namaaz as a choice between two goods. We discussed why choosing to watch a movie was the more intellectually convincing choice over namaaz. I chose watching a movie over namaaz for two reasons.

First, its reward, the pleasure that I will derive from the movie, is visible. I have complete knowledge of it through previous experiences. And second, the reward is instant. I can get it immediately.

In comparison, namaaz lost. Why? First, because its reward is invisible. I have no tangible experience of that reward. I have some superficial knowledge of it, but not a real experience of it, the way I do of watching movies, because I know exactly what the pleasure of enjoying a movie feels like, but I do not know what the reward of namaaz is going to feel like. Second, the reward is delayed. I have to wait however many years until I die and then receive that reward, and that is if such a reward even exists.

So, between these two, watching the movie obviously wins hands down.

Now, for namaaz to win over the movie, what are the things that need to change? What would have to change so that, given the choice between a movie and namaaz, I am willing to choose namaaz over the movie? What is it that will allow me to give up an instant gratification for a delayed one?

The pleasure of namaaz needs to be intellectually visible. It has to be greater than the pleasure of watching the movie. And the reward, if it is going to be distant, needs to be far, far greater than the reward I will gain from watching the movie. And both the pleasure and the reward have to last longer than the pleasure of the movie. Because the only time we are happy to delay our gratification is when the reward is far greater than the reward of instant gratification.

But for that, two things are involved. First, a clear knowledge of that reward, and second, the trust that the reward will be delivered to you. Knowledge and trust. And since trust comes with knowledge, knowledge then becomes the key component.

Let us say you have to miss school because of something really important, like a new Assassin's Creed came out, but you need the lecture notes for that day.

Now, can you think of a friend in your class whom you could trust to take down those notes for you, if he said he would? And can you think of a friend whom you could not trust to take down the notes even if he said he would? Why? What was it that allowed you to make that distinction? So it is knowledge about a person, his character, his previous dealings with you or with others: that is what creates trust, is it not? Knowledge about the person and his track record. The better the track record, and the more knowledge you have of that track record, the more you do what? You trust that person.

So now, if we are to trust Allah, what do you need? Knowledge about Allah, and knowledge about His track record. Because does Allah ask us to place our trust in Him? An immense amount of trust. He does so because He wants to make a completely opposite deal with us. When do we choose a thing? When the reward is visible and instant. But Allah says otherwise.

So let us study this verse piece by piece. There is no doubt about it: Allah has purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth in exchange for heaven. Whose souls has He purchased? Not everyone's, only the believers'. And who are the believers? What are the signs of a believer? Allah continues to explain. They fight in the cause of Allah. Does this mean jihad? So whom are these believers fighting? Their own souls. And in fighting them, what do they do? They kill and are killed. Kill whom? They kill their desires. They kill their greed, their impatience, their anger, their thirst for revenge, their craving for instant gratification. And what else do they do? They are killed. Meaning what? What happens when you are killed? You suffer, do you not? Is it a pleasure to give up your desires, or is it a pain? Is it painful to watch all your friends partying and having fun and enjoying themselves while you cannot, because Allah has forbidden it to you? Of course it is. Is it painful to hold back your anger even when you have the finest retort ready, the one that would make everyone gasp? Absolutely.

So what is Allah saying? He is saying: without doubt, Allah has purchased from the believers their souls and their wealth in exchange for heaven. And the believers I am speaking of are the ones who fight in the cause of Allah, and they kill or are killed. Meaning, in following the path of Islam and the teachings of their prophet, they fight their overwhelming desires and their craving for instant gratification, and in the process they willingly choose to suffer if they must.

وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّۭا فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَٱلْإِنجِيلِ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ۚ وَمَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ

This is a promise that Allah has made binding upon Himself. The promise of this reward of heaven is something that Allah has made binding upon Himself, and not only in the Qur'an, but in the books before it, the Torah and the Gospel.

وَمَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ

And who is more true to his promise than Allah? This verse is so beautiful. Notice that when Allah spoke of the promise, He spoke of Himself, not of the believers. That is, He did not use the word "promise" when He spoke of the believers; He used the word "purchase." But He used the word "promise" for Himself. Why? Because the believers can make mistakes. They can falter. But Allah does not make mistakes. He cannot make mistakes. The believers, however, can. So even if the believers make mistakes, even if they falter on their purchase,

Allah says that as long as they keep trying, my purchase, my deal, will remain valid. SubhanAllah. He imposed perfection upon Himself, not upon the believers.

So this is the first part of the verse. Now let us explore this part in a little more detail.

This verse begins with a transaction, a business deal, if you will. إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشْتَرَىٰ — in which Allah has purchased. From whom? مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ — from the believers. What did He purchase? أَنفُسَهُمْ — their souls, and وَأَمْوَٰلَهُم — their wealth. And in return, what is He giving us? What are we receiving for this transaction? بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةَ — we are receiving heaven. This is the exchange Allah speaks of in this verse.

Now, what is the verse teaching us? In order to understand this, let us simply speak about the idea of a sale for a moment, because He is, after all, speaking of a transaction, is He not? And a transaction is one in which you sell something and someone else purchases what you are selling. Allah says, I am purchasing your soul and your wealth — the two things most dear to every human being.

Now, first of all, can you purchase something from me if I am not willing to sell it to you? No. So the fact that Allah is purchasing means what? That I am willing to sell it. Do you understand? It is a mutual transaction in which both parties are in agreement. It is not a forced transaction.

Now, we have learned that we human beings, simply by nature, love immediate transactions — what the Qur'an calls تجارةً حاضرةً, correct? In other words, I pay for something now, and I receive it when? Right now. The only time we are willing to delay a transaction is when we say, I want the product now — I want the big-screen television now, but I will pay for it over a period of six months. That is the only time we are content to delay our payment. We like to pay over time but receive immediately. Otherwise, usually, when we pay now, we expect the product right away.

So human beings like to pay late but receive immediately. That is our nature. Do you agree?

In this verse, Allah says, you give Me your soul, and you give Me your wealth now, and in return I will give you heaven.

Now, do we like to receive immediately or later? We like to receive immediately. Is heaven coming immediately or later? It is coming later. But when do you have to make the payments to Allah? Now. And do you have to make this payment one time, or do you have to keep making it every day? Every day. We have to keep making those payments with our time, with our wealth, with our prayers, with our fasts, with the way we live, the way we dress, the way we speak, by giving up the things we want to do but cannot do because they are haraam, with the money we cannot earn because it is not the permissible way of earning it, the money we want to spend but not in the right way — and we are constantly holding ourselves back, because we are in a transaction with Allah.

And we have to constantly remind ourselves that we are doing this in exchange for what? Heaven. But human nature is such that if you are paying a price, if you are making a sacrifice to earn something, you want to see it right away. Even if you work forty hours at a job, at least two weeks later you see a paycheck — you are going to see something. But when Allah purchases our souls and our wealth from us in exchange for heaven, do we see heaven? No.

All we get is a spoken confirmation from Allah — I will give it to you; trust me — and that is all we get, nothing more. Allah says, very well, I will describe it to you in My book. It has trees, it has an abundance of fruit, it has rivers, you may marry, and so on. We are given a great deal of description of the Garden. But do we have a catalog? A brochure, a picture, perhaps a video? A short trailer — just give me a short trailer of the Garden. I do not want the whole film, only show me something like a thirty-second clip of it, so that I know what is coming. Nothing! All you are given is Allah's word.

Now let us stop here for a moment, step back, and consider what Allah is saying here. He is like a salesman who comes to us and says: Listen, I have this remarkable property, a prime piece of real estate, some fifty acres, a mansion! It is worth fifty million, but I am going to sell it to you for five thousand. All you have to do is pay me the five thousand now, and even that in small, tiny installments, and in about fifty or seventy years I will tell you where that property is. But this offer is open only right now. If you agree, the mansion is yours!

I will give it to you when? After fifty years — but you have to pay me right now! Now if any real estate dealer came to us with this offer, what would our reaction be? We would say, you sleazy scam artist, get out of here, do not waste my time. But this is Allah, our Creator, our Master, making this offer with us. Allah is saying, I will give you the Garden when you are being laid into the ground and dirt is being thrown upon your face — when you are in the ground, that is when I will give it to you. But when do you pay Him? Right now. And we go, ummmmm, and He says, "Trust Me." Just trust Me. Does this not take an incredible amount of trust? That is what we mean when we say "believing in the unseen."

ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ۔ وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ وَبِٱلْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ

That is what we mean when we say we believe and trust Allah. It is not an easy thing. It is a very easy thing to say — that I trust Allah — but it is a very difficult thing to do. And that is why Allah immediately reassures us:

وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّۭا فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَٱلْإِنجِيلِ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ۚ وَمَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ

Trust Me, My servant! Look at My track record from the previous books. I have a great track record, one hundred percent perfection. I have never failed on My promise — never have, never will. Trust Me!

And why do we need this assurance? Because when you walk this path, everyone around you will say you are a fool! You are missing out on life! You could have been doing so much more with your youth. You are wasting your life away with your Islamic values, and that scruffy beard you are trying to grow. You have to go to the masjid and pray and do this and that, when we could be having so much fun during that time. You only live once, you know. You are starting your college life. You will be living in the dorm, your parents will not even be around, you will be all by yourself. There is going to be so much partying, man!

Everyone is going to have the time of their lives. I think your lab partner likes you too! It is all good. Do not worry about it. You are a good-looking man; you are a beautiful woman; you can have anything and everything you have ever wanted. You have such a beautiful body — you need to show it! You have a six-pack, man; you need to be more like Salman Khan; take off your shirt for no reason at all. It is fine. It is not even Ramadan yet.

Shaitan, on the other hand, offers us the exact opposite bargain. He says: Listen, listen! I have some wonderful worldly things for you, some luxuries, some incredible pleasures. Yes, they are inferior, but you can have them right now. Just do this. Just drink this. Just smoke this. Just steal it. Just click on this link. It is right there — so easy! Yes, you might get into trouble later, but not right now; you are fine. For the next thirty or fifty years, at least, there will be no problems at all. And so he comes to us offering an immediately visible reward, with nothing to pay up front. Obviously this is far more tempting, far more powerful: to seize the reward that is here now and abandon what will only arrive so much later.

And because we are impulsive buyers — the moment a tempting product is placed in front of us, we simply have to put it in the cart, we cannot hold ourselves back — Shaitan makes us his sale, and most of us do what? We become customers. We become immediate customers. Allah, however, makes us a promise; and because we do not see the product, what do we say? "Ugh, maybe in Ramadan — that is, if the new X-Men movie does not come out. I know it is Ramadan, but I really want to go and watch the movie, and I cannot watch a movie without snacks. I am in such a religious dilemma; I do not know how to reconcile these two things."

And you say no. I have made a sale with Allah. I have made a transaction with Allah. And they will say: You are so foolish, man! What world are you living in? This is 2015, brother! Why can you not get smart? And you keep hearing this, seeing all of it around you, until eventually a point comes when you begin to feel: I cannot bear this pressure anymore. Everyone is telling me that I am being foolish and missing out on life. Am I really making a mistake? Am I really missing out on all the fun? Am I really a fool?

Then you open the Qur'an and read this verse, and Allah tells you:

We are seeking to understand the message of Allah from the Qur'an, and the tool with which Allah has blessed us, so that we may understand His message, is the intellect. So we have begun with the study of the intellect, or عقل. What, then, have we learned so far about عقل?

1. It is a container for knowledge, and it expands as the knowledge increases.
2. It was the first thing Allah created. This is the first sentence of the hadees I shared with you. This is the statement with which the hadees begins: اول ما خلق اللہُ العقل

Now why does that matter? Suppose you have a great many tasks to complete for school. What do you do? You set them in order of priority. And what do you take into account when setting your priorities? Urgency and importance could be one consideration. The length of each task measured against the time you have could be another. But the very first thing you do is what? You create the task list itself, before you begin working on the tasks at all.

Let us say you have to write six different papers for school. All the reference books are stacked up on your table. You have a list of every link to every site you are going to need. You have settled the order in which you will write the papers. You have your supply of cookies and your Cadbury eggs beside you. You have chosen the tunes you are going to play while you work on these papers. But the main instrument you need in order to begin writing is what? A pen! If you do not have a pen, does anything else matter — except the Cadbury eggs, of course? No! It is the very first thing you need if you wish to write your papers.

In the same way, Allah created the heavens and the earths and everything that exists within them. He created those mansions upon mansions in heaven for His creatures. He laid out the plan of His messengers: I shall send Adam first, then Nooh, then Ibrahim, then Moosa, then Eisa (علیھم السلام). And then at last I shall send My beloved prophet Muhammad (SAS) with this exceedingly elaborate, exceedingly eloquent, and symmetrically miraculous message for My creatures, so that they may understand it and earn My reward and draw nearer to Me and to My love. But wait — what is the first thing they need in order to do that? The intellect! Without the intellect, nothing else will matter. Without the intellect he will not recognize My messenger, nor his message. He will not be able to see the miracles I have placed in My Qur'an for him. And without the message he will not be able to draw close to Me. He will not be able to enter this beautiful paradise that I have created for him.

So what was the first thing Allah created? The intellect! SubhanAllah!

Now, if the intellect is the first thing Allah created, what is the first thing we ought to be using in order to understand His religion? The intellect! So tell me this: how can we be satisfied with answers such as, do not use your intellect, do not think too much about religion, it will drive you mad, and things of that sort? How could we accept such a way of thinking?

The reason Allah created the intellect first is so that, before any decision we make in our lives, we should first bring it before our intellect. Is this going to benefit me in the long run? Or is it going to harm me in the long run? Should I seize this instant pleasure set right before me?

Or should I choose the everlasting pleasure that is still to come? So the intellect is the first thing Allah created. We also learned that it is the loftiest thing Allah created for the purpose of obedience. It had the capacity to obey Allah and the capacity to disobey Him. It had the capacity to compromise and the capacity to hold its ground. And Allah gave it complete freedom of choice.

The intellect is a scale. It can choose not only between good and evil; it can also choose between two goods and between two evils. In the last session I spoke about this at length. The intellect works in this way: when it is faced with two good choices, it chooses the pleasure or the benefit that is visible and immediately within reach. The only time it chooses something that is not visible and that will only be available later is in two cases. First, when there is knowledge of the reward that is to come in the future, along with absolute trust in the one who has promised that reward. Second, when the benefit and the reward that are to come far exceed the benefit of the pleasure available at once.

And it is on the basis of such trust that we accepted the bargain Allah made with us.

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشْتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوَلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْجَنَّةَ

We sold our souls and our wealth to Allah, as believers, in exchange for His promise of paradise.

يُقَتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ

We agreed to the terms and conditions of being a believer as Allah laid them upon us. My believers are those who will sacrifice their worldly desires for Me, the desires that are visible and immediately gratifying, and they will be willing to suffer for it. It will not be easy for them. There will be times when killing their desires will mean literally cutting out their own heart. But they will do it, for Me.

وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّۭا فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَٱلْإِنجِيلِ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ۚ وَمَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ

And they can trust Me, because I have made this promise of reward binding upon Myself not only in the Qur'an but in all the earlier books, to all the earlier nations. I am not asking My believers to promise Me that they will never break this bargain. In fact, I am promising them that I will give them this reward no matter how many times they break this bargain with Me, so long as they sincerely and honestly keep trying, so long as they keep returning to this bargain with Me, so long as they do not take undue advantage of My love and My mercy. I am promising you: I will give you this reward.

We ought to examine our own lives, and the lives of those around us, in the light of this verse. We achieve so much in this world, yet why is it that the desires of the heart never come to an end? Some spend all their time on Facebook, WhatsApp, and all these social sites, desperately trying to find a connection, and still the heart longs for more. It searches constantly for more. However hard we try, why is it that we can never seem to find that perfect connection? We feel an emptiness that does not leave us, a void in our hearts that we cannot fill, no matter how hard we try. Some try to fill that emptiness with money, some with power, some try to drown it in alcohol, some try to forget it with drugs, and still the emptiness is there. If money is the key to all happiness, then why do so many rich people take their own lives? I can understand the poor man running after wealth, but why do we see the extremely rich running after money just as hard? The man is a millionaire, and still his heart wants more. He wants to be a billionaire. Why is that? What is he searching for? With all that money, with every comfort of this world, why is his heart never satisfied? Why is it always looking for more? Because they are wandering aimlessly in the valley of greed and deception.

فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ

There was once a sage who knew how to turn straw into gold. A man begged him to teach him that skill. The sage asked him, what will you do with all the gold you make? He said, I will become very rich. The sage asked, why do you want to be rich? He said, so that I may live a very comfortable and peaceful life. So the sage said, then it is not gold that you seek. What you really seek is comfort and peace for your heart. Would it not be better if I taught you how to find peace and comfort for your heart, instead of teaching you how to make gold?

Today we have people who think that gold is the key to peace and comfort. It is not. You may make as much gold as you wish, and your heart will never find comfort in it. Yes, you can distract it for a while with luxurious things, with jewelry, with branded cars, with great mansions, but this hunger, this thirst of the heart, will never go away, because the heart is not searching for gold. It is searching for something else.

Look at the artists in the music industry, how they wander and lose themselves in the valley of desire and fame. The artist begins with a desire to have her song heard. She gets her break, someone produces his album.

Everybody downloads it. It goes platinum. Overnight they become enormously popular and enormously wealthy. She wins a music award. Is that the end of his career? No. Now she has to produce the next great hit. But the next album she releases is not as entertaining, not as successful. The sales are fewer. It does not reach the top of the charts. Now she begins to feel desperate. She begins to watch her own decline. What does every artist want, even more than money? Fame. Appreciation, acknowledgment, recognition. They live on that. But instead of that, what she now receives is criticism: rotten tomatoes, one star, thumbs down. She begins to sink into depression. So she begins to think: what can I do to get back on top? I need to come up with a new song. Wait — I already tried that, and it did not work out well. Perhaps if my new song were a little controversial. Perhaps if it were a little more indecent, it might become more popular. Does that happen? Yes, it does. And then, when that does not work either: perhaps if I lower my standards of decency even further, perhaps that will get me there. And if that does not happen, perhaps I will simply shave my head, get drunk, get arrested, adopt a baby, adopt twelve babies. If I cannot be mentioned at the award ceremony, perhaps I will be mentioned in the tabloid at the end of a grocery aisle. At least I will be mentioned somewhere. Does that happen? Certainly. They grow more and more desperate, willing to try anything. And when nothing works, they turn to alcohol, then to drugs, and then one day they are found dead in the bathtub of their penthouse suite. أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ

And most importantly, what does this "need for more" indicate? It indicates that the heart is not getting what it truly needs.

Suppose you have some critical data on your phone that you need for school. You have no backup of it. The only original copy you have is on your phone. That data is so important that without it you cannot function at school. Now what happens when you lose the phone with all that data on it? What do you begin to do? You begin to search for it. Where do you look? Everywhere. In your house, in your friend's house, in the places you visited, in places where it makes absolutely no sense to search — but you search there anyway. You keep searching endlessly for it. Now I come to you and give you a brand-new model of your phone, a far more beautiful and far more powerful phone. Will that satisfy you? No. It does not have the content you need. Can I distract you for a while, take your mind off the search for a little time? Yes, I can. I can distract you with Facebook, WhatsApp, spending time with friends, a PS4, an Xbox, and so on. But the moment the distraction is over, what do you do? You begin searching for your phone again. There is only one way in which this need, this search, can come to an end. What is it? It is that you find your phone. Once you find it, will you search for it any longer? Of course not.

You see, the problem is that all these worldly luxuries can give comfort to our bodies, but not to our hearts. The heart was never meant for this world. And we constantly try to satisfy its needs with worldly possessions: money, fame, luxuries, and jewelry and glitter of every kind.

But its need is not physical in nature. The body's need is physical; the heart's need is spiritual. Until it finds the object of its search, the heart will always remain unsatisfied. And the heart is hungry because we have broken the rope of Allah — the عقال of Allah with which He used to bind us, to keep us close to Him. We broke that rope and moved away from Him. And now this heart longs for Allah. It is searching for Allah. It looks for Allah everywhere. It wanders through every valley trying to find Him. It thinks that it can replace the need for the love of Allah with gold and money, with fame and power and distractions. But nothing satisfies it. Why does it find no satisfaction? Because these material things do not bring peace to the heart. Then what does? Allah answers this question in such simple words in the Qur'an:

أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَىِٕنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ

Beware! Only by the remembrance of Allah does the heart find peace.

أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَىِٕنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ

Allah is the ultimate goal of our hearts. Until it finds Allah, the heart does not find peace. It cannot find peace. Like a fish out of water, it yearns to return to it; our hearts crave the love of Allah. Like a man thirsty for water, who is satisfied with nothing else, who is distracted by nothing except water — you may give him mountains of gold and silver, all the power and all the fame, and nothing can satisfy his thirst until he finds water.

أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَىِٕنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ

And when this world forces you to break this bargain with Me; when your friends force you to break this bargain with Me; when your family forces you to break this bargain with Me; when your own desires force you to break this bargain with Me; when everyone around you is calling you a loser, a fool, a fanatic, a coward, and you cannot take it anymore; when you cannot bear the pressure, when you cannot bear the pain of those insults, those criticisms and those sarcastic remarks any longer — in that moment of weakness, remember My words:

فَٱسْتَبْشِرُوا۟ بِبَيْعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِى بَايَعْتُم بِهِۦ وَذَلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ

In that moment, rejoice in the faith. Feel yourself congratulated by Me, your Master and your Lord, who loves you more than anyone in this world, who loves you more than your mother, your father, your family, your children, your spouse, and your friends — all of them COMBINED.

Feel yourself congratulated by Him for this astonishing bargain you have made, because you will be the one who succeeds. You will attain the great triumph: ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ.

Did we discuss these words, ٱلْفَوْزُ ٱلْعَظِيمُ, in the last session?

The word فوز in Arabic comes from the word فاز, which means success, or a gain, or some piece of good fortune. But in ancient or classical Arabic, the word فوز is used when you succeed, or are victorious, or gain something, only when two particular conditions are met. If either one of these conditions is not met, then it is not called فوز. The first condition is that whatever you have attained, you never afterward wish to part with it — ever, not even for a second. That is the first condition, but that is not all. What you have attained, as part of فوز, must also make you the object of others' longing. It must make you the object of others' envy. When others look at you, they should want desperately what you have. They should say to themselves: I would give absolutely anything, in a heartbeat, to obtain what this person has. That is when the word فوز is used.

So there are two shades to the word فوز. You must love it so much that you never wish to part with it, and others must crave what you have. Only when both of these conditions are met do you have فوز. And in this bargain, Allah has promised the believer فوز. He said: if you come through on this bargain with Me, I promise that what I will give you will not only make you so happy that you will never, ever wish to part from it; it will also be so magnificent that everyone around you today — your friends, your family, your loved ones, your enemies, every one of them — will wish that they had what you have been given.

Another beautiful derivation of the word فوز is فازَۃٌ, which to the Arabs meant an exceedingly comfortable tent in the middle of a scorching desert. Now imagine that you are an Arab wandering in the burning heat of the desert, very thirsty, hungry, and weary. And you come upon this cool and pleasant tent, holding within it every comfort you need: water, food, a comfortable bed, a big screen television. What would that tent, that comfort, mean to you at such a moment? Once you entered it, would it not also satisfy the two conditions of the word فوز just described? For it would be something you would never wish to part with. You would never wish to go back out into the scorching heat of the desert, and all the others still in that scorching heat would be craving what you had gained.

But then in this verse, Allah did not merely promise us فوز, did He? He promised فَوْزُ عَظِيمُ. Allah joined the word عظیم to it. If I begin to enter into the linguistic subtleties of this word, we will never see the end of this discussion on intellect. So I will tell you one small meaning quickly. The word عظیم comes from the word عَظُم, which is also the root of the word عظام, meaning "bone." Now, what are the qualities of a bone? It is solid, is it not? It is solid, it is stable, it is sturdy, it is reliable, and the whole human frame stands upon it. But then there is the word عظامۃ, as a verb, which literally means: when the bone grows strong — like the bones of a growing child. You know how a child's bones become stronger as he grows. So combine this with فوز, and the sense conveyed is a success whose pleasure keeps increasing.

and it grows stronger as time passes. Now, from the standpoint of grammar, the words فَوْزُ عَظِيمُ in this verse are used as a noun infinitive phrase. In grammar, an infinitive phrase is something that extends infinitely and indefinitely, something subject to no limitation. Take, for example, the phrase: 1. Everyone wants to enjoy life. That is a noun infinitive phrase. It is continuous and it is infinitive. The sentence implies that there will never come a time when everyone does not want to enjoy life. The same is true of the phrase: 2. She likes to be admired. The desire for admiration is an infinite thing, an indefinite thing.

So the grammatical use of فَوْزُ عَظِيمُ in this verse tells us that the reward you have attained is not only so amazing that you never want to be parted from it; it is not only something that makes others envy you; it is not only growing stronger as time passes; it is also growing without end. There will never come a time when this reward stops increasing. Never! So how much will the pleasure of this reward increase? It will keep growing, and growing, and growing! Infinitely! SubhanAllah. Now you tell me: is this فوز عظیم not a great reward?

We said that the only time we are willing to sacrifice instant gratification is when? When the reward we are going to receive later is far, far, far greater than the pleasure we are giving up right now, correct? Tell me honestly: no matter what we sacrifice in this lifetime, is this reward from Allah — this فوز عظیم that you love so much, that you cannot bear to part with, that makes you the envy of everyone around you because of how magnificent it is, that grows infinitely, beyond all measure, and whose pleasure never stops increasing — is this not a greater reward than any sacrifice we will ever make in this world? It certainly is.

But Allah did not merely say فوزٌ عظیم, did He? He said الفوز العظیم. He added the ال to both words, to فوز and to عظیم. AllahuAkbar. In Arabic the ال is called علامت المعرفۃ. When you want to make something specific — not just any book but a particular book, not just any car but a particular car — that is one reason you add the ال to a word in Arabic: to make it specific.

Allah says of this bargain you are making: I am not going to give you فوز, I will give you الفوز. That ever increasing reward I have just described will be specific to you. No one else in My entire creation will have the experience that YOU are going to have. Each one of you will have your own individual experience. And that experience is not merely going to be عظیم, it is going to be العظیم. It will not keep increasing infinitely in some generic way. It will increase in a way tailored specifically for you. It will increase infinitely in the particular way you want it to increase.

This is what I love about the Arabic language. Can you see the depth of this language in just two words!

Every one of us should memorize this verse with full understanding, because there are so many occasions when we need to remind ourselves of it.

What else does the word عقل mean?

It is a restraint! Another meaning of the word عقل in ancient Arabic is to tie or restrain a camel with a strong rope. And the rope used to tie the camel was called عقال.

Now let us explore the meaning of عقل as a restraint. A camel was to an Arab what a car is to a teenager. Your car, whatever it looks like, whatever its year, make, or model, is precious to you, is it not? That is why you polish it to a shine twice a day. Now, if you love your car so much, would you be concerned about its safety? Of course you would be. Why? Because it is YOUR car. It is your baby. You love it, and it is also your responsibility. Only you can take care of it in the best possible way. You make certain that it stays in good condition. You have the oil changed regularly. You attend to its service and maintenance needs. All of this grows out of your sense of ownership and also out of your attachment to it.

This is what a camel was to the Arab. It was not only his mount, and not only his source of livelihood; in most cases it was also his closest friend, for these were bedouins who crossed the deserts. They did not spend as much time with their wives and children as they did with their camels. Believe it or not, they actually composed long poems about their camels, about the camel's eyes and the way it moved. This should come as no surprise to you, for poetry was their art. Poetry was to them what conversation is to us.

Now imagine that you have traveled two thousand years back in time, and your parents have just bought you a camel of your own. This camel is now your new best friend. So you ride into town on your new camel to buy some groceries. When you reach the market, you park your camel outside and dismount. Now what must you do before you enter the market? No, you do not pull the hand brake. You have to tie the camel. Why? Why do you need to tie the camel? Why can you not simply leave it standing there? Because your camel does not know what is good for it and what is not. If you do not tie it, it may wander off. Someone else will find it, and a few hours later your best friend may end up on a huge platter, nicely cooked and tender. Possible? And it is not only that. You cannot take care of a camel in any way at all until you have tied it. You cannot feed it. You cannot bathe it and clean it. You cannot treat it when it is sick or injured. You cannot shelter it from the storm. You can do none of this until you have tied it up first. Why? Because first you HAVE to restrain it and bring it under your control, and only then can you do whatever you need to do to take care of it. Do you understand? The same holds true for your car.

Therefore I argue that restraint is necessary. It is required for safety and for the benefit of the one being restrained. Intellect is a restraint. Until you set a boundary, you cannot take hold of anything in life. That is why we have to-do lists. That is why we have particular subjects in school, taught within a fixed span of time. We restrain subjects within time frames. That is why we have the boundaries of a nine-to-five workday. That is why we build houses, within which we confine ourselves for our safety and our benefit. Everything we do in life, everything we are able to do in life, is possible only because of some form of restraint or boundary. Even the universe works on the principle of restraint. That is why we have seasons bound within particular durations of time.

That is also why we have a set duration for the day and a set duration for the night. Imagine if day and night came at random. Our entire life would be destroyed. We would not be able to make use of the day, nor would we be able to make use of the night. There is nothing in this world that can function without a restraint. In order to give benefit or to receive benefit, some sort of restraint is required. Anything that goes out of restraint goes out of control, and anything that goes out of control is a disaster. What happens when someone loses restraint or control over a car? Accidents. What happens when you lose control over your balance? You fall. What happens when the gas coming to your stove is not restrained or controlled? What happens when the flame of the fire is not restrained, not controlled, while you cook your food? And what happens when nature releases its restraint over its elements, such as wind and water? You get hurricanes and tsunamis. Therefore I argue that restraint is an essential component of physical human existence. Does everyone agree with me on this? Are there any questions about it?

So let us return to the camel. The reason you tie your camel is for its safety. You want to keep it controlled so that you can keep it safe, because you care about it, because it is your camel and it is your responsibility. So there are two reasons for tying your camel: love and justice. You keep it restrained because you love it and you want to take care of it, and you keep it restrained because you do not want the camel to hurt others. You do not let it damage other people's crops and property. This applies to everything in life: love for the self, justice for others. Do you agree?

However, by tying the camel, did you limit its freedom? Did you restrict its movement? You did. But was it absolutely necessary for you to do that? Yes, of course. Now, do you think the camel always likes that? As soon as you reach the market, does the camel jump up and down and say, "Hooray! Tie me up! Tie me up!"? Probably not. But you tie it up nevertheless, because you understand that the restraint is necessary for its safety and for the safety of others, whether the camel understands it or not, whether it appreciates it or not, whether it likes it or not. You are doing what you are doing in order to keep it and others safe.

But yes, tying the camel does limit the camel's freedom. The thing about safety is that it is directly proportional to the level of restraint, or, to put it another way, it is inversely proportional to freedom. That is to say, the higher the level of safety required, the stronger the restraint will be. To tie the camel you are not going to use a mere piece of string, are you? No. You will use a rope strong enough for the task. The restraint will be in proportion to the strength of the camel. And as the level of safety increases, the level of freedom will be limited. The more tightly you tie the camel, the more restricted and limited its movement will be.

You sit in your car. What is the first thing you do? You put your seat belt on. Now, as soon as you put it on, does it restrict your movement to a certain extent? Yes, it does. It does not disable you completely, but it does limit your movement. You can still move, only not as freely. But does that restraint save you in the event of an accident? It does, InshaAllah.

And what about when you sit on a roller coaster ride?

Does it restrict your movement completely? It does. Why? Because a far, far higher level of safety is required.

What about traffic lights? Do they limit freedom? Of course. You must wait until the light turns green. But are those lights essential to the safety of drivers? Yes.

What happens at airports? You must pass through all those security checks. Does that limit your freedom a great deal? Absolutely. Yet those controls and restrictions are required for your safety and mine, as well as for the safety of the other passengers. And the greater the level of safety required, the higher the level of what? Of restrictions.

So is Islam a restrictive religion? It certainly is. It is without question a restrictive religion. But why? Because of safety. Whose safety? Your safety and mine.
