Your safety as an individual and our safety as a group, collectively. We are Allah's creation. We are His camels. Rasul Allah is our shepherd, and Islam is the rope of Allah with which Rasul Allah (SAS) has tied us, so that he may keep us safe, individually as well as collectively.

Have you ever seen how a rope is made? It is made from two strings twined firmly together. Allah's rope is made of Islam and Iman twined together. And He says in the Quran: وَٱعْتَصِمُوا۟ بِحَبْلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًۭا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا۟ Hold fast to the rope of Allah and do not get divided. What is that rope of Allah? It is the rope of Islam and Iman.

Islam is a restrictive religion because it is a religion of safety. And there can be no safety unless there is restraint. The Arabic word Islam comes from the root word سلم, which carries many different meanings. InshaAllah, we shall explore all of them at a later time. One of those meanings is to surrender willingly and completely — willingly and completely.

إِذْ قَالَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥٓ أَسْلِمْ . قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَلَمِينَ

His master said to Ibrahim AS, surrender! He said, I completely and willingly surrender to the master of the worlds.

And the one who willingly and completely surrenders himself, his will, his desires, and his ego to Allah is called a Muslim.

أَلَّا تَعْلُوا۟ عَلَىَّ وَأْتُونِى مُسْلِمِينَ

Do not be arrogant before me. Come to me in submission as a Muslim.

Another meaning of the word سلام is safety.

قُلْنَا يَا نَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ

We ordered the fire to become cold and safe for Ibrahim.

So two meanings, out of many other meanings of the word سلام, are what? Submission and safety. And how do you become safe? By surrendering yourself completely to your master. Can you tie your camel if it keeps struggling? No. The camel needs to surrender to your rope, to your عقال, in order for you to keep it safe. We are Allah's camels, and Rasul Allah (SAS) is our shepherd. Islam is his rope, with which he ties us. We need to surrender to the rope he has given us. We need to accept him as our shepherd and surrender to the rope of Islam if we desire OUR safety and if we desire OUR success. Why? Because there can never be safety without restraint, and we need to surrender willingly and completely to that restraint if we want to be safe. Safety from what? From satanic temptations. Because what happens when a camel begins to wander? It will wander into every single valley that draws its attention. It will get lost.

It will be killed. The rope of Islam draws a secure boundary all around us for our safety, so that Allah, who is our master, may take care of us, and may give us the benefits, the rewards, and the success that He desires for us. If we do not surrender ourselves to this boundary of Islam, if we do not secure ourselves within this boundary of Islam, willingly and completely, we are going to lose our way to Allah. We will wander away from Him.

The reason we feel the restrictions of Islam so heavily upon us today is the times we live in. Look at the temptations that surround us, and at the outside pressures to which all of us are exposed. Beyond the restraint of Islam there are magazines, media, and people who tell you that you must dress a certain way, look a certain way, talk a certain way, and behave a certain way. If you do not, then you are not cool, you are old-fashioned, you are stupid. We keep feeling this pull constantly while we are tied to the rope of Islam. Of course it is difficult. But the question set before the intellect is this: what is the right choice? Instant gratification? Or الفوز العظیم? For satanic temptations surround us on every side. Everything that is cool today we find to be against the teachings of Islam, in every dimension of our lives. The only thing protecting us is the rope of Allah, the rope of Islam. The only way to save ourselves is to surrender willingly and completely to this عقال, this restraint of Allah, which is Islam.

If a hurricane is coming, what do you do? You surrender yourself to a house, a shelter, that you know has a solid foundation. You admit that you are not strong enough to face this storm alone, and that you need to take shelter in a structure stronger than yourself, so that it can keep you safe. You submit yourself and your freedom in exchange for the protection and safety of that shelter. Yes? What will happen if you try to stand and face the storm and say, "I can take it on! I am not scared of it!"? How long will you last? But once you are inside the shelter, are you restricted? Do you have to give up some of your freedom for your safety? Of course.

And what will happen if, once inside the shelter, you want to keep the doors and windows open? "Yes, I know there is a storm outside, but it is so suffocating in here. Let me just open the window. Let me just keep the door open for a nice breeze. It is fine; it is not as though I am standing outside in the open. I am only one step outside the door. I only have my neck outside the door. It is not the end of the world. Do not be so paranoid."

"I know Islam forbids it, but so what if I eat a little crab, a little lobster, some mushrooms? So what? So what if I smoke? At least it is not alcohol. What is the big deal? I know what Islam says about clothing, but so what if I dress provocatively? What is the big deal? It is 2015! What is the problem?"

Well, truly there is no problem for Islam. The shelter will still be standing after the storm has passed. The shelter is not the one that is going to be hurt. It is you who will be hurt, because you violated the rules of safety.

Islam is a religion of restraint, a restraint placed upon us by our master for the sake of our souls and our intellect. It is a restraint that Allah placed on us so that we remain connected to Him, because He loves us.

Because He cares about us. He does not want us to wander away from Him. He does not want us to leave Him. It is just as we tether a camel because we care about it and do not want it to wander off and be lost. Allah says:

أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ

Do you not see that they wander aimlessly in every valley?

In كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ, the word يَهِيمُونَ comes from ھاما. ھاما is used of a camel when it is lost in the desert searching for water. It goes into one valley, then another, then another, looking for water, wandering with no direction, until at last it dies of thirst. When the Arabs used the word ھاما, they meant that it is pointless to wait for the camel to come back, because it is never going to come back. This is how Allah describes those of us who wander about trying to find a connection somewhere other than with Him.

In the last few sessions we have been discussing the intellect. Today I want to discuss its counterpart, its partner in crime: the heart. The Arabic word for the heart is قلب. I want us first to understand the definition of the word قلب, and then we will look at its relationship with the intellect and at how the two are joined together, in the Quranic sense in particular. But before we discuss that, I want to set the stage. These next few sessions are going to become quite philosophical. So the young children in the group may need to ask their parents to explain things to them after the session, and the teenagers and older children may need to explain this material to their parents after the session.

Volunteer.

So imagine that you and X are in a tennis tournament together. The two of you are competing against each other in this tournament, along with many other players. You really want to win this game. You train day and night for it. You change your diet, you change your workouts, you put together a plan, and you carry it out with discipline, day in and day out. X, on the other hand, does nothing for the championship. Every time you see him, he is wolfing down burgers and washing them down with sodas. The only workout he is doing is with his jaws, when he is polishing off those packets of Snickers. Do you understand? Now the day of the tournament arrives, and guess what? For whatever unexplainable reasons, X wins the championship hands down. He ranks number one, and you get a lower ranking.

Now tell me: who won the championship? He did. But who trained really hard for the championship? You did. Who is in excellent physical condition, and who is in horrible physical condition? Yet despite that fact, who won? X did. Now, can you argue that he should not have won because you are in much better physical condition than he is? What if you go to the judges and tell them how you trained day and night, and how all X did was eat and sleep? Would that make a difference? No. Why not? You did train hard. You did work hard. He did not. So then why should you not be declared the winner? Because in the tournament, on the playing field, regardless of everything, he ranked first. Do you understand? So he gained precedence, even though you had excellence. Do you agree?

So the lesson we learn here is that in life, as valuable as excellence may be, as important as excellence may be, precedence trumps excellence.

I will give you another example. The new iPhone is going to be launched. They are giving one phone away for free at the mall. The first person to show up at the mall gets the phone. Again, you and X want that same phone. X is determined to get the phone, so he makes all the arrangements to get there before you. He buys a brand new alarm clock and brand new batteries, and he tests it out some fifty times to make sure it goes off at the precise millisecond. He sets the alarm to get up two hours before you do. He puts an alarm on his phone. He steals his father's phone and puts an alarm on that too, just in case. Then he puts one phone at each ear and runs a strip of duct tape around his face to make sure he does not miss it. Not only that: while you are sleeping, he sneaks into your room and turns your alarm off, and he lets the air out of the tires of your car. Basically, he does everything to win that phone.

Now that is a very good plan, is it not? So he wakes up, rushes to the mall, and what does he find? You are already there. Who gets the phone? You do. Was his plan not perfect? It was. He carried it out with precision. But did any of that matter once you arrived before him? No. He got the iPhone. So precedence trumps excellence. Precedence wins over excellence every single time. As the saying goes, you may win by an inch or you may win by a mile, it makes no difference. The one who wins, wins.

These are extreme examples I am giving you. In life what we normally see is that excellence SUPPORTS precedence, or that excellence RESULTS in the achieving of precedence. You study very hard, and you come out on top. You train very hard, and you win the tournament. That is what normally happens. But in the end it is precedence and not excellence that counts.

That is why I gave you these extreme examples: simply to make a point. No matter how well you plan, no matter how well you carry the plan out, in the end any sort of ranking rests on who reaches the top first, or on who makes the first move. Consider game shows: the one who hits the buzzer first is the one who gets to answer the question, whether or not he knows the answer. Precedence wins over excellence. Do you completely agree with that? Does anyone have any questions?

Now I want everyone to keep this at the back of the mind.

Let us quickly go over what we discussed concerning the intellect, or العقل. What does the word mean?

1. It means a limitless container for knowledge.

2. It was the first thing that Allah created, the most powerful and the most superior of the things that Allah created. He made it an instrument of obedience, so that only through the intellect would obedience be possible.

3. It means a scale. It allows us to choose between two goods and between two evils. We looked at the example of a choice between a movie and namaaz, and we saw why the movie won and why namaaz lost. We also discussed what would be required in order for namaaz to win over the movie. So the intellect is a scale, for choosing the better of two goods and the lesser of two evils.

4. Finally, we learned that the intellect is restraint. It is the rope used to tie the camel, for the camel's safety and comfort, but only if the camel surrenders to it willingly and wholeheartedly.

Now let us talk about the heart. The Arabic word for heart is قلب.

The word قلب literally means to turn something around onto its face, or to flip something over, like turning over a cloth: whatever side was on top, you flip it to the bottom. In Arabic that is called qalb.

For example, if a person is walking in one direction and then turns away from that direction and begins walking in the opposite direction, that is called قَلَبَ . The Arabs would say قَلَبَ کلاماً , meaning that he flipped the conversation. He was speaking about one thing, and then he switched and began speaking about something else. So قلب means to turn or to flip, in the literal or linguistic sense of the word.

There is another beautiful meaning of the word قلب, within this same sense of turning: to turn back to, to RE-TURN, to return to its original source. For the heart was designed by Allah to RE-TURN to Him. He was created in this world to face the duniya.

with the purpose of RE-TURNING back to Allah. فَانْقَلَبُوا بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ — So they returned to the blessings of Allah.

In the physical sense, our heart is called قلب because of its constant pumping. It is never in one state; it is constantly moving, constantly turning. It is constantly switching states, and that is why it is called قلب. But this is not only in the physical sense; it is also in the emotional sense. Even emotionally, the heart is always flipping. Emotions are never the same. We go through constant "changes of heart" when it comes to emotions, decisions, and opinions. They constantly flip and switch, and that is why the heart is called قلب, in the physical sense as well as the spiritual sense.

So that is qalb literally, linguistically, physically, and spiritually. Now, metaphorically, قلب was also used by the Arabs in the meaning of a vessel or a container. Where did we hear that word "container" before? Intellect! So it is not only the word عقل but also the word قلب that is used to represent a container. Maulana Ali once held the hand of Kumail Ibn Ziyad, took him to a cemetery, and said to him: يَا كُمَيْل بْن زِيَادٍ، إِنَّ هذهِ الْقُلُوبَ أَوْعِيَةٌ فَخَيْرُهَا أَوْعَاهَا — O Kumayl, these hearts are containers. And the best container is that which preserves its contents.

Finally, قلب is also used for the essence, or the innermost part, of something. In a hadees, Rasul Allah (SAS) said: every single thing has a heart, and the heart of the Quran is Surah Yaseen. This means that Surah Yaseen contains the essence of the entire Quran. Everything the Quran speaks about can be found in Surah Yaseen. So if I recite Surah Yaseen, it is as though I am reciting the essence, or the central idea, of the entire Quran, because Yaseen contains its essence. That is why, when someone passes away, we recite Quran for them; but when it is their barsee, their death anniversary, what do we recite? Surah Yaseen! We recite Surah Yaseen in his or her name, because it is like reciting the entire Quran for them, since it is the essence of the Quran.

And then Rasul Allah said: و قلبُ القلب ، الاخلاص — and the heart of the heart is Surah Ikhlaas. So Surah Yaseen is the essence of the entire Quran, and Surah Al-Ikhlaas is the essence of the essence of the Quran. The essence of Surah Yaseen is the tawheed of Allah. When we study Surah Yaseen, we find that everything stated in it points to the oneness, or Tawheed, of Allah, which is Surah Ikhlaas.

So when we cannot recite the entire Quran, we recite Surah Yaseen. When we cannot recite Surah Yaseen, we recite Surah Ikhlaas three times, which is equivalent to reciting the entire Quran. It is our common practice to recite Surah Ikhlaas three times before going to bed, because Rasul Allah (SAS) said that reciting Ikhlaas three times is equivalent to reciting the entire Quran. Now, there is a great deal of depth in these statements as to why reciting it three times is equivalent to reciting the Quran. My topic of conversation would change if I entered into that, so I am going to leave it for now. InshaAllah, if we get a chance, I will explain that concept at a later time.

And since we are on the topic: Surah Al-Fatiha is called Rooh Al-Quran, the soul of the Quran. The body cannot exist without the soul; therefore, if the Quran is a body,

then its spirit, its soul, is Surah Al-Fatiha. Surah Al-Fatiha is the most essential component of the Quran; without Surah Al-Fatiha the Quran would not exist. We actually saw this when we studied the miracles of the Quran, how Surah Al-Fatiha is the index of the entire Quran. The entire Quran is nothing more than a very detailed explanation of Surah Al-Fatiha.

So, coming back to the meaning of qalb: it means the essence, or the central and innermost part of something. Interestingly, قلب also refers to the pith of a date, because the seed contains the entire tree in a passive state. So qalb refers to the essence of something, without which that something cannot exist. In the same way, the entire machinery of the human body is working because of the heart. It is the essence. The heart stops, and then أنا للہ و انا الیہ راجعون. Right?

There are many, many other meanings of the word قلب, but these are the ones I need you to understand for our discussion today. InshaAllah, later I will explain more when we come across it in a different context. There are several other words used for heart, which have different meanings and nuances. There is فؤاد، صدر، لُب. All of them have different meanings.

Now let us discuss the relationship between the heart and the intellect. The intellect is a container and the heart is a container. Now, if they are both containers, the question is what do they contain? The intellect, we already know, is a container for what? Knowledge! The heart, on the other hand, is the container for spiritual components, such as faith, Tawheed, and so on. The heart is a container for abstract things, while the intellect is a container for concrete things. Do you understand? The heart can hold faith, trust, and emotions such as love, anger, bravery, fear, and the like. And the intellect holds concrete evidence supporting or opposing those abstractions.

When we were studying the miracles of the Quran, where was the Quran revealed? On the heart or on the intellect? On the heart!

وَإِنَّهُۥ لَتَنزِيلُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَلَمِينَ۔ نَزَلَ بِهِ ٱلرُّوحُ ٱلْأَمِينُ۔ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنذِرِينَ۔ بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّۢ مُّبِينٍۢ

This (Quran) has been revealed to you by the Lord of the universes. Revealed through the trustworthy spirit (Jibraeel). On your heart so that you can warn mankind in clear Arabic language.

What did we say contains the meanings, and what contains the language? The heart contains the meanings, and the intellect formulates the words, correct? Now, which is abstract and which is concrete? Meaning is abstract and words are concrete. That is why the Quran was revealed on the heart of Rasul Allah (SAS) and not on the intellect. He used the intellect to form the words of the Quran. So even there we see the heart first and the intellect second, right?

So my point is that the heart contains faith, and the intellect contains the knowledge or information that supports that faith. The more knowledge the intellect has to support the faith, the stronger the faith will be. The less knowledge the intellect has to support the faith, the weaker the faith will be. Do you understand?

I will give you an example. You meet someone at a bus station. You talk to him for ten minutes and you like that person. You do not really know the person, because you met him for the first time, but ten minutes later, when the two of you walk away from each other, you leave with a fondness for that person in your heart.

Do things like that happen in life? With friends, with people? Now you begin to meet him regularly at the bus station. What, then, could happen to that small fondness in your heart? It will either grow or it will shrink. Either you will come to like that person and he will become your friend, or you will come to dislike him and you will no longer wish to speak with him. The question is: what brings about that change? Knowledge about that person. The intellect. The more you come to know that person, the more knowledge you gain about him, the more you may like him — or you may dislike him, depending on the supporting or opposing evidence you gather. Is that not so? So what influenced your fondness? Knowledge about that person.

Now tell me: which came first with regard to that person, the fondness or the knowledge? The fondness. And is fondness related to the heart or to the intellect? To the heart. Would you have tried to learn more about the person, or wished to meet him again, if you had disliked him at the first meeting? No. So when did the intellect come into play? After the fondness had developed. Is it safe for me to say, then, that the fondness came before the knowledge about that person? So which is greater, precedence or excellence? Precedence. And which came first, the heart or the intellect? The heart.

So you see that the heart takes precedence over the intellect. That is why it is ranked higher than the intellect. The intellect gave it all the support, and yet the one that came first is what? The heart.

You teach a child to say "A," and the child says "A." Then you tell him, "After A comes B." Now if the child asks why, what do you say? You say, trust me. Have faith. When a child learns anything from its parents, is that learning based on faith or on intellect? On faith. The intellect enters the game much later. But as the child grows and gains knowledge, does his faith in the order of the alphabet increase or decrease? It increases. Could the child have learned the alphabet without faith? No. Because the heart comes first, and then comes the intellect.

In the tournament example I gave you, which came first, your desire to win the competition or your training? The desire came first. And where is desire generated, in the heart or in the intellect? In the heart. Where do the knowledge and the planning for the tournament exist? In the intellect. The heart comes first, and then comes the intellect.

It is the same with everything else in life. A film must capture your heart in the first ten minutes, must it not? Why? Because the desire to continue has to come first, and only then the intellect. Think about a new book you are reading. If you are intrigued, you will go on with it; if not, you will put it down after the first chapter.

Take losing weight. The heart wants that slice of cake, even though the intellect is supplying the information that you have already reached your quota of calories for the day. Now if the heart is strong in its desire to succeed and lose the weight, it will accept the recommendations of the intellect. If the heart's desire to lose weight is weak, then despite all the intellectual backing, despite all the knowledge about dieting, will I still eat the cake? You may be sure that I will.

So the heart first, the intellect later. And what comes first is ranked greater than what comes later. Precedence is greater than excellence.

That is why the heart is ranked higher than the intellect, by virtue of its precedence. The intellect is very powerful, and it has great influence over the decisions of the heart, yet it is the heart that is in control. The intellect may offer its recommendations. If the heart agrees, it will follow them; if it does not, it will reject them.

Think of the heart as the king and the intellect as the wazir. Or, in the terms more familiar to us today, think of the heart as the President and the intellect as the chief of staff. Who is elected first, the President or the chief of staff? The President. Once the President has been chosen, he appoints his chief of staff, correct? But who constantly gives advice and recommendations to the President on all matters? The chief of staff. And who is in control of carrying out those decisions? The President. Who completely manages, administers, and oversees the workings of the White House? Who decides who is permitted to meet the President and who is not? Who does virtually all the work? The chief of staff. All the work is done by the chief of staff, but who is recognized as the leader of the country? The President.

That is why we learn in the hadith that Allah created the intellect first. He called the intellect the most superior of creation because of its excellence:

اول ما خلق اللہُ العقل
و عزتي و جلالي ما خلقت خلقاً اعظم منک ولا اَطوعُ منک

And then He said to the intellect: because of you I will give reward, and because of you I will punish.

بک أُبدي و أُعيد، لک الثواب و عليک العقاب

Why? Because the intellect is the ultimate guide by Allah's design. Notice, too, that in Islam the faith is not imposed upon a human being until the intellect has developed. Two people are exempt from Islam: the child, until he reaches maturity, and the insane person, until he regains his sanity. What do the child and the insane person have in common? Neither has intellect. So the intellect is the key to entering religion.

Yet it is striking that the Qur'an states that when we return to Allah, Allah says that He will look at what is in the heart, not at what is in the intellect:

وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ

I will bring out what is in your heart. Why is that?

It is because of the final definition of قلب, which is the essence, or the innermost part, of a thing. In English we speak of the "heart" of the matter, or we say that the "heart" of the problem is such and such. What does that mean? It refers to the root cause of the problem, the place where the problem began, the seed of the problem. Fix that root cause, and the entire problem disappears. Is it not so?

That is why a person is identified by the traits of his heart. When it is said that so-and-so is a good person, a kind person, a generous person, a brave person, all these qualities are in fact qualities of the heart, because the heart is the true essence of a human being. The Messenger of Allah said:

Indeed, in the body there is a morsel of flesh, which, if it is sound, the entire body is sound, and if it is diseased, the entire body is diseased. Truly, it is the heart.

Why? Because it is the heart, and not the intellect, that is in control. If the heart is strong with love and kindness — and the only way it can be strong is if it is backed by strong intellectual evidence that to be loving and kind is the way to be — then the actions that flow out of that person will be loving.

If the heart is filled with hatred...

and it is backed by strong intellectual evidence that survival requires hatred, then the actions that flow out of that person will be hateful. Because the heart is in control. The heart is the essence. The heart is the controller. And it is in the heart that faith resides. It is in the heart that Allah resides. For it is in reality the heart that can "see" spiritual things, not the intellect. The intellect can make sense of things only by referring them to things in this physical world, but the heart can see beyond the physical world, even without intellectual backing.

Someone asked Maulana Ali, "Have you seen Allah?" He replied, "How can I worship Allah without seeing Him?" So the man asked, "Amir Almomineen! How can you see Allah?" He replied, "Eyes do not perceive Him, but hearts perceive Him."

And Allah says in the Quran:

فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى ٱلْأَبْصَرُ وَلَكِن تَعْمَى ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِى فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ

For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.

And history is filled with great achievements that were driven purely by faith. Look at Gandhi and the Indian freedom movement. Did it make intellectual sense to stand up against the British government, especially while they held power? No. But Gandhi had faith. He had determination. He had resolve. All of these are properties of the heart. Yet he used his intellect and his knowledge to carry his mission forward intelligently. He used his intellect to support his faith. But he began with faith, did he not? What about Martin Luther King? The same thing. So the heart is the main thing, because it is the true essence of a human being.

And this is what we find in the Quran in the request of Ibrahim AS:

وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَهِیمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ

And Ibrahim says, "O my Lord, show me how you bring the dead back to life." Allah says:

قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن؟

Why, Ibrahim? Do you not believe? Do you not have faith? Notice that Allah asked, "Do you not have faith?" He did not say, "Do you not have intellect?" Where does faith reside? In the heart. Now of course Ibrahim AS has faith. Who could have more faith than Ibrahim AS? But even Ibrahim AS asks for intellectual backing:

قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى

Of course I have faith. There is no doubt about it. But I ask you to show me so that it eases my heart. Notice that he did not say لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ عقلى, so that it eases my intellect. He said, لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى, so that it eases my heart. Through this incident Allah teaches us that even with faith, the heart can remain uneasy — until it receives knowledge about that faith. Only with intellectual evidence can faith become strong.

So then what does Allah do? He says:

قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ

Take four birds and sacrifice them.

ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍۢ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًۭا

Then go and place the dead body of each bird on a different mountain.

ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ

And then call them.

يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًۭا ۚ

They will fly back to you swiftly.

وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌۭ

And know that Allah is most powerful and most wise.

Allah gave Ibrahim AS the intellectual, physical evidence that he needed in order to strengthen his faith: that Allah can give life after death.

When we began studying the miracles of the Quran, did you not have faith that the Quran is the word of Allah? You did. But was it backed by intellectual evidence?

No! After we worked through the miracles in all their various dimensions, are you now completely convinced, on intellectual grounds, that the Quran is the word of Allah? Is your faith not far stronger now than it was before? So what made it stronger?

The intellect is the knowledge of how to drive a car; the heart is the actual driver of the car. The more the driver knows about driving, the better he will drive the car.

The intellect is the library; the heart is the librarian.

This is why there must be this connection, this balance, between the heart and the intellect, so that Islam and Iman may come alive within us. The heart is entirely a matter of Iman; the intellect is entirely a matter of Islam. We find the obligations of Islam hard to carry out because of the weakness of Iman, weakness in faith. And why is faith weak? Because it is not backed by enough intellectual evidence for that faith to grow strong.

Yet in some people we find a great deal of intellectual knowledge and no faith at all. It is all informative knowledge. That was exactly my own problem, as I told you earlier. I had studied so much and learned so much, but it all sat in my intellect. It was not supporting any faith in my heart. It served only to know more and to show off, and to win arguments and debates. That knowledge had nothing to do with increasing my faith in Allah or increasing Taqwa. As a result, I could speak to you about any aspect of religion, yet I was missing my prayers and doing all sorts of things.

It is only through the balance of the heart and the intellect, only through the balance of faith and the knowledge that supports that faith, that we can move toward Allah. Balance is the key. InshaAllah, I will show you that Islam is built upon balance. Balance is Allah's logo. The kalima of Tawheed, La Ilaha Illa Allah, is all about balance; even the letters of the kalima are balanced.

This brings us to our next topic of conversation, the debate of science versus religion. InshaAllah, we will look at this in the next session.

What I want you to take away from today's session is this:

Ramadan Mubarak. Happy Father's Day.

Allah created the intellect العقل as a vessel for knowledge, and by design He kept it without limit. The intellect عقل, as I came to learn, is an elastic vessel that expands to fit whatever is placed within it. We then learned from the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that Allah created العقل as His very first creation, before anything else. He gave it precedence over all other creation, so that we too would give it precedence and would use our intellects before we make any decision in life.

He granted our intellect complete freedom of choice, so that it might choose freely and willingly and move toward obedience to Allah. People confuse the freedom to choose with the consequences of their choices. It matters that we choose well, for every choice carries a consequence packaged together with it. When you pick up one end of the stick, you pick up the other automatically. Islam gives people the freedom to choose the path they wish to follow, and no one is compelled to follow any particular path. Yet each path has a destination, and each one ends in a different place.

لَا يَسْتَوِىٓ أَصْحَبُ ٱلنَّارِ وَأَصْحَبُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ۚ أَصْحَبُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ هُمُ ٱلْفَآئِزُونَ

The people of Paradise and the people of the Fire cannot be the same; it is the people of Paradise who have attained the great success.

We learned that العقل also means a scale — a scale not only for choosing between good and evil, but especially for choosing between two goods and between two evils, so that we take the greater of two goods and the lesser of two evils.

Finally, العقل is also meant as a restraint. He gave us the intellect so that we might use it as an instrument to restrain our desires and our passions, so that we might set a boundary of safety, so that we might protect ourselves and those around us, and so that we might live a controlled life of obedience rather than an uncontrolled life of disobedience.

I also proved to you, through the example of the camel and its rope, that happiness and comfort — not for human beings alone, but for all creation — can exist only within confines, within certain boundaries and limits. And when the desires and passions of the heart cross these boundaries and step beyond them, the soul is lost; and then, like a lost camel searching for water, it wanders aimlessly into every valley in search of the objects of its desire.

أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى كُلِّ وَادٍۢ يَهِيمُونَ

But the desires never end. Behind every desire stands another desire, and then another. Beyond every valley lies another valley. The soul keeps chasing them and in the end loses itself; it even loses the path of return to its master.

Intellect means restraint. Intellect means discipline. It means to train ourselves to follow and obey certain rules and a code of conduct. Islam is a religion of restrictions; Islam is a religion of disciplines. Why? Because it is a religion of safety, and a religion of comfort. And what did we study about the relationship between restraint and safety? The more safety is required, the greater the restraint must be. The greater the restraint, the less the freedom. Safety and comfort are directly proportional to restraint, and inversely proportional to freedom. Islam is a religion of safety; it is therefore a religion of restraints; it is therefore a religion of disciplines. It was designed by the Creator for His creation.

so that they might find peace and comfort by it. When we step within the walls, the very confines, of Islam, we find several restraints, several disciplines, set inside it. We find seven primary disciplines. There is wilayah, taharat, salaah, zakaat, saum, hajj, and jihad. These are the restraints, the disciplines, within Islam. So if you picture Islam as a house, then picture these disciplines as its pillars. The whole structure of Islam stands upon these pillars, upon these disciplines. Where there are no pillars, there can be no structure. Where the pillars are weak, the structure itself is weak. Is that not so?

So the structure of Islam rests upon seven substructures, seven disciplines. Taharat and salaah are the disciplines of a day, for at the very least they are performed five times a day. Zakaat and fasting are the disciplines of a year, for they are performed once a year. Hajj is a discipline performed once in a lifetime. Wilayah, which means love, and jihad, which means struggle, are the disciplines of every single moment; they are the disciplines of every single breath. For every moment of our life should be filled with the love of our master, and every moment of our life should be filled with our struggle, our striving, our effort to please Him. And it is only through these restraints, through these disciplines, that the soul and the heart can find peace, comfort, and safety.

So today I want to speak about the discipline of Ramadan. I had intended to speak of this at a later time, but since we are passing through this holy month, I judged that this would be the best time to speak briefly about it.

When we think of fasting, our first thought is of hunger and thirst. The things that come to mind when we speak of salaah, of namaaz, are wuzu and ghusl, qayam, ruku, and sujood. When we think of zakaat, what comes to mind is the loss of money. So there are certain actions, certain attributes, tied to each discipline. But here is a most interesting thing about Islam and all its disciplines: nothing is what it seems.

When Allah speaks of the Qur'an, He says:

إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌۭ وَقُرْآنٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

We recite to you the signs and the Wise Remembrance.

How would you feel if you gave me something to eat? You handed me a banana, and I took it from your hand and said, "Oh, thank you so much," and then tossed it into the trash can in front of you. How would that make you feel? Or suppose I wrapped it in a fine silk cloth and placed it on the top shelf of my cupboard. Would that not astonish you? You would say, "That is not why I gave you the banana. I gave it to you so that you could eat it." Is that not so? And what if I peeled it, threw the banana away, and began eating the peel? Would you not find that madness?

But that is exactly what we are doing with the Quran. The covering, the peel of the banana, is the words; the true meaning of the Quran is the actual fruit inside. We are so pleased and so content eating only the peel of the banana, completely disregarding the fruit itself. Is that why Allah gave us the Quran? He did not give us this precious gift, this constitution of our lives, merely to recite it like a parrot. He gave us this gift so that we would understand it, internalize it, and transform our lives with it. There is no greater gift for us than the Quran. And then He gave us this holy month of Ramadan especially to celebrate His gift. Now, if you and I spend the entire month without reciting a single verse of the Quran, without understanding a single verse of the Quran, without memorizing a single verse of the Quran, is that not similar to tossing this gift into the trash can?

And what is the message of taqwa that we discussed earlier? It is taqwa. Taqwa is the key to guidance. You cannot receive guidance and then establish taqwa; you must first possess taqwa, and then you receive guidance:

ذلک الکتاب لا ریب فیہ ھدی للمتقین.

This book is guidance for the pious... for the people of taqwa. So this Quran is a guidance for those who have taqwa. The Quran is guidance, and Ramadan comes each year to create taqwa within us. يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ Allah gave us the fast so that we might attain taqwa. Ramadan comes to create the connection between us and our Creator. It comes to create within us the state of submission, which is taqwa. Islam means submission. Ramadan comes to teach us submission: the submission of our will, our desires, our feelings, our emotions, our logic, and our intelligence to the will of Allah. Ramadan comes to teach us the most critical lesson, that Allah is to be obeyed, whether we find it easy or not, whether it is easy or difficult; we must obey Allah. Ramadan is a reminder that Allah has a right over us as Maalik, our Owner, as Khaliq, our Creator, as Haakim, our Ruler, and as Raaziq, our Sustainer, and that He is to be obeyed without question. In Ramadan, Allah makes forbidden during the day what is otherwise permitted, and we accept this without question and without hesitation. We accept it without irritation and without protest. We accept it joyfully, to please our Master and to receive His rewards. May Allah grant me and all of us the desire to read, to understand, and to internalize this precious gift.

And then He says: هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ Allah says that this Quran is a guidance for all mankind. This verse is not only for the Muslims. Allah did not say هُدًۭى للعالمین، ھدی للعرب، ھدی لی بنی اسرائیل، ھدی لی بنی اسماعیل. Allah did not even say ھدی للمؤمنین، ھدی للمسلمین، ھدی لی جماعت السلیمانیۃ. No, no, no, no, no. Allah said هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ, a guidance for all mankind. This is one of the most beautiful things about our religion, my friends; this is one of the most beautiful things about our religion. It does not matter whether you go to our jamaat khana or you go to a masjid in Australia, America, England, Pakistan, or India. If people of many nationalities are standing in one row, you do not make a distinction that the rich people should be in the first row, the middle class in the second row, and the janitors in the last row. No! Everybody stands in the same row. And it may be that the boss is standing next to the worker, and it may be that the worker is in the first row and the boss is in the last row; that too may happen. Allah made this guidance for all mankind. Do you know what that means? He made all human beings equal, simply through the institution of the Quran and the institution of Salaah. We cannot be racist, we cannot be racist, because we have namaaz. We cannot be supremacist, because we have salaah. Salaah is a symbol, a reminder for us that we cannot think that my nation is better than yours, my nationality is better than your nationality, my skin color is better than your skin color, my language is better than your language, my religion is better than your religion, my sect is better than your sect. We cannot do this. We cannot do this. And do you know when we are reminded of this? When we are standing together in salaah, when we are standing together in namaaz. When the black-skinned, flat-footed Hazrat Bilal is standing next to Ali ibn Abi Talib in prayer, that is when we are reminded of it.

We are all equal in the eyes of Allah. That is what هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ means.

Do you know why I am drawing attention to this? Because it has now become very common among us, among the Sulemanis, within our Sulemani Jamaat. We imagine that we are better than everyone else. We imagine that we are superior to everyone else. In Pakistan there is a term used for Sunni and Shia: کٹر سنی، کٹر شعیہ. Anyone from India or Pakistan has surely heard it. It means radical or fanatical Sunnis or Shias. Today we have become کٹر سلیمانی. We have become کٹر سلیمانی. We look upon the Sunnis as though they were beneath us. We look upon the Shias as though they were beneath us. We are the ones bound for Paradise, and everyone else is bound for the Fire. Who are we to decide such a thing? Who are we to decide such a thing?

Yes, we have our creed. We have our knowledge, and a doctrine on the strength of which we say that we are closer to the truth. Yes, indeed. But that ought not to make us arrogant; it ought to make us humble. If you and I were born Sulemanis, we should be grateful to Allah for it, not use it to look down upon other sects. Did Allah not create them with His hands, just as He created you and me? Does He not love them as He loves you and me? Does He not feed them as He feeds us? Do they not recite the same kalma, لا الہ الا اللہ, that we recite? What, then, gives us the right to claim superiority over them?

And, for that matter, being born a Sulemani means absolutely nothing. It guarantees absolutely nothing, unless we live by Sulemaniyat, unless we fulfill the obligations of the Ahad Shareef that we took. Simply being a Sulemani means absolutely nothing in the eyes of Allah. For our Prophet (SAS) said, خیرکم عند اللہ اتقاکم — the best among you in the eyes of Allah is the one who protects himself the most. Taqwa is the key to Allah's grace, not Sulemaniyat.

If our beloved Messenger (SAS) could turn to his own daughter, to Maulatina Fatimatuz Zehra — the queen and leader of all the mominaat, the mother of all the Imams, the Mishkaat al-Anwaar — and say, یا فاطمۃ بنتِ محمد اِتَّقِ اللہ۔ فأِنِّی لا أَملکُ لَکِ مِنَ اللہ شئیً — Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, you must have your own taqwa, you must be cautious and mindful of Allah, for I will hold no authority on your behalf, when I stand before Allah, without it — when the Messenger of Allah says this to one such as Maulatina Fatima (صلواۃ اللہ والسلامٌ علیھا), do you imagine that our merely being Sulemani, without taqwa, will help us in any way on the Day of Judgment?

If we truly believe that we are the right sect, then we should be grateful to Allah for creating us in Sulemani homes, for creating us as Sulemanis, and we should express that gratitude by fulfilling the obligations of our Ahad Shareef and by acquiring taqwa. And we should hold love and kindness for those who stand behind us, not look down upon them. To do so makes us less than Muslims. المسلم اخو المسلم, said the Messenger of Allah. He said that a Muslim is the brother of another Muslim. Whether Shia or Sunni, they recite the kalma, and so they are Muslims, and that makes us brothers. How can we mock them? How can we look down upon them? What is going on here? Do we not perform salaah? Do we not perform namaaz? For if we are not learning from our salaat, if we are not learning from this Quran, then I tell you: we are nothing but a shell.

We are just a shell with no egg inside — that is what our Islam becomes at times. We look like Muslims, we speak like Muslims, but there is no Islam within our hearts; there is no love for our faith. To look down upon another Muslim brother is not what Islam teaches us. If you are healthy and your brother is disabled, you do not look down upon him, you do not make fun of him. And if you do, will that make your parents happy, or will it anger them? We are just as much the creation of Allah as they are. This is not the way of Islam; this is not the way of Sulemaniyat.

Consider Syedna Hussain bin Ali AsSharfi, Qaddas Allah Ruhu, one of our great dais, when he came to India. And, by the way, who is more Sulemani — you and I, or a Dai? A Dai is far more Sulemani than we are, is he not? When he was in the jamaat khana and Sulemanis came to greet him and to do musafiha, he would sit and receive their musafiha. But when someone from outside — a Shia or a Sunni — came to greet him, he would stand and greet them, for he said that our brothers are to be honored.

On that same visit, there was a dinner held in his honor. When everyone had begun to eat, he saw the driver standing beside the entrance of the masjid, wearing the white uniform of a driver. He asked, who is that man, is he a Muslim? He did not ask, is he a Sulemani? Is he a momin? Does he believe in Maulana Ali? Does he believe in Syedna Suleman? None of that. He asked, is he a Muslim? They said, yes, he is a Sunni. So he asked, why is he not eating? He called the driver over with his hand, seated him next to himself in the thaal, and offered him food with his own hands. This is a true Sulemani. From where do we take a creed that calls a Sunni a kafir, a Shia a kafir? This is the humility of a true Sulemani. Humility should be our symbol, our insignia — not arrogance.

And who is greater than Rasul Allah (SAS), فدا امی و ابی? Has anyone more deserving of pride ever walked this earth? Has anyone of a more elevated station ever walked this earth? And Allah foretells him in the Taurah and the Zaboor with the sign of humility. He said, he is soon going to come, he is soon going to come: یُریدُ أَنَّ یَبعثُ أُمِیِّ مِنَ الأُمِّیِّن۔وأجعل السكينة لباسه ، والبر شعاره ، والتقوى ضميره ، والحكمة منطِقه ، والصدق والوفاء طبيعته ، والعفو والمعروف خُلقه ، والحق شريعته ، والعدل سيرته ، والهَدِىُ إمامه ، والإسلام ملته ، وأحمد اسمه ، أهدي به بعد الضلالة ، وأعلَمُ بِهِ مِنَ الجَهالة ، وأرفع به بعد الخمالة ، وأعرف به بعد النكرة ، وأكثر به بعد القلة ، وأغني به بعد العيلة ، وأجمع به بعد الفُرقة ، وأُؤلِفُ به بين أممٍ متفرقة ، وقلوبٍ مختلفة ، وأهواء متشَتَّتَة. How remarkable — I do not know from where I recalled this hadith after so long. This is a passage from one of the earlier books. Allah sets out all these beautiful, beautiful signs of Rasul Allah, foretelling him. It is a very long hadith; I have recited only a small portion of it. But after foretelling all these wondrous signs, He says: Indeed, I am sending this man; he will soon be among you. I will make him the king of all my creations. I will hand him the keys to my heaven. He will hold my flag on the Day of Judgment. I will give him the most praised of ranks, مقام المحمود. I will give him the highest rank in Jannah.

No man will be able to enter heaven without his intercession. No prophet will be able to enter heaven before him. I will open the doors of my seven heavens for him. I will grant him the honor of being in my presence and speaking with me face to face. I will unveil my presence to him. I will grant him the honor of قاب قوسین او ادنی. And this man, my beloved, who will hold so exalted a station — do you know how he will walk when he is among you? Do you know how he will walk among you? With all these traits, he will live among you in such a humble manner: لَو یَمشِی عَلی القَصَبِ الیَابِس۔۔۔ لَم یُسمَع مِن تَحتِ قَدَمَیہِ مِن سَکِینَتِہِ He will walk with such humility that, if he walked upon dry reeds, you would not hear them crack beneath his feet.

This was the way of our Prophet. When we call Sunnis and Shias unbelievers, when we look down upon them, whose example are we following? Which prophet's?

This Qur'an binds us together. هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ — and this was said to the Jews. Do you know why? Because the Jews believed they were special. They believed they were superior, that everyone else was second class, that they alone were first class. Everyone else is a gentile; we are the chosen nation — just as we say today that we are the chosen sect. Allah says that anyone can become a person of the Qur'an. هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ — an open invitation to all humanity, one that completely uproots racism, nationalism, tribalism, and egotism. It does away with these things. SubhanAllah, what an amazing religion! We have such an incredible religion!

This Qur'an is meant to unite us, not to divide us, because we are reminded of this unity when we stand in prayer. هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ — and there are many proofs, clear evidences of guidance, meaning the guidance itself holds miracles, so that if you study it you will be convinced this can only be the word of Allah. وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ — and it distinguishes between right and wrong.

In all of this, so far, Allah has said nothing about Ramadan. He opened this verse by speaking of Ramadan — شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ — but after that, what is the only thing he speaks of? The Qur'an. More than half this verse is about the Qur'an. Why is he doing this? Because he wants to make sure that no Muslim ever forgets that Ramadan is about the Qur'an. Ramadan is about the Qur'an — the outward Qur'an as well as the inner Qur'an.

May Allah grant us all — and me most of all — the wisdom to understand this beautiful, this miraculous message, and help us transform our lives in its light.

I have made these mistakes myself. I am ashamed to admit it. I have made these very mistakes of calling Sunnis and Shias unbelievers. I have had very judgmental, very fanatical, very unforgiving conversations with people — some of them on this group right now. But I was wrong. I was completely wrong. May Allah forgive me. Yet it was through this book that I found that light. This book can truly change our lives if we approach it with the sincerity it deserves. And may Allah protect our hearts, and by the blessing of this holy month help us fortify them against Shaitaan in the months to come.

may he help us understand the realities behind the symbols he created for us.... آمین یا رب العالمین۔    و آخر الدعوانا عن الحمد للہ رب العالمین۔۔۔۔

Allah says the Qur'an is a reminder. Everything about Islam and all its disciplines is in truth a reminder for something else. So fasting has, in fact, nothing to do directly with hunger and thirst; the hunger and thirst are a reminder for something else. The qayam, ruku, and sujood, though a part of namaaz, are in truth a reminder for something else. These are all symbols, and a symbol points to that which is symbolized. You see a half-bitten apple upon your phone, and it reminds you that the phone was made by the Apple Company. You see flying windows, and they remind you of Microsoft. For symbols are reminders of that which they symbolize.

So today I want to speak to you about what fasting is, and about what the hunger and thirst symbolize. Hunger and thirst are not the purpose of fasting. That would simply make no sense. Why would Allah keep us from eating and drinking? Why would He hold it against us that we eat and drink? Truly, He does not. But He created fasting for us, and He stopped us from eating and drinking during the day as a symbol, so that we would be reminded of something greater. And if our fast reminds us always of that to which it points, then we are truly fasting.

Otherwise, all we are doing is dieting. Do you understand? Are there any questions?

Today I want to speak with you about a few things concerning the discipline of fasting, especially in the context of restraint. A nation is known by its capital. When you have a nation, you must have a capital, particularly if you are a large nation. The capital becomes an integral part of your identity. If one city in a country falls to the enemy, or the enemy takes over one city, one village, or one town, it is no great matter. When do you know that the country is completely defeated? When the enemy takes over the capital. When the enemy takes the capital, the country is no more. The capital is regarded as the identity of the nation.

For the Muslims, the qibla is our identity. It is our capital. The Ka'aba is our Islamic capital. We all face in its direction. Before Islam, the qibla used to be Bait al-Maqdis for the Jews. When Allah changed that qibla, He changed our identity. He changed our identity. As soon as He changed our qibla, He said:

وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَٰكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا

That is how We made you a middle nation. He inaugurated us as a new nation by changing our capital, by giving us our own capital.

Now, an area near the outskirts of a country is never chosen to be the capital of that country. Why? Because, as I have just said, once the capital is conquered, the country is no more. So the capital is usually in the innermost city of a country. It is well protected on every side. The government operates from within the capital. The decision-making bodies operate from within the capital.

If we think of our body as a country, what is our capital? The heart. The heart is the capital of our body. It is located in the innermost part of our body, well guarded on every side. It governs all our decisions. It decides what we will do and what we will not do. Do you understand? I want you to keep this idea in mind for our conversation today.

So now let us begin to speak about fasting. This fasting is not something that was given specifically to the Muslims. The Qur'an says:

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

O believers! We have enjoined fasting upon you, made it obligatory upon you, just as We enjoined it upon those who came before you, so that you may become pious.

So Allah says that We made fasting obligatory upon those who came before you. Of whom is Allah speaking? The Jews. The people of Bani Israel, the Israelites. The shariah of Musa, peace be upon him. He says, We made fasting compulsory for you just as We made it compulsory for the people of Israel. And why did We give them fasting then, and why are We giving you fasting now?

لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

So that you people may become pious, so that you may have taqwa.

Now this is very interesting. If you read the first half of Surah al-Baqarah, you will find that Allah speaks about the Jews, and Allah complains about them the entire time: why do you not have taqwa? The whole time. The problem is that they have no taqwa. And now Allah says that you, the Muslims, are given the same exercise as they were, which is what? Fasting. And what is the point of all of it? So that you may have taqwa. In this ayah, Allah explains the purpose of fasting.

Why is it that we fast in the first place? لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ — to acquire taqwa. I want to speak to you about it from a practical standpoint, about what that means. One of the meanings of taqwa is to fear Allah, to be wary of Allah. Taqwa comes from the word وقایا, which actually means protection. Taqwa is similar to اتقا, to seek protection, to try to protect yourself. That is why, on the Day of Judgment, everyone will try to protect themselves; no one will care about anyone else; they will all try to protect only themselves. So Allah says: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِن كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًۭا يَجْعَلُ ٱلْوِلْدَنَ شِيبًا — how will you protect yourself on the Day of Judgment if you have disbelieved, a day whose terror will be so great that a baby's hair will turn gray? So He uses the word تتقون to describe protecting yourself, or entering Allah's protection. That is the real meaning of تقوی — protection, to protect yourself from Shaitaan. So Allah says: I gave you fasting so that you can protect yourself. What does that mean? Let us try to understand what that means.

As human beings, we all have to go through certain trainings in life. If you want to become good at something, you have to go through training, especially physical training. If someone wants to become a soldier, or a police officer, or a fireman, they have to go through specific types of training. And their body learns to adapt itself. At the beginning it is hard, and then it becomes easier and easier and easier for them, right? And when you are in training, things are easy. When you are in a training program, things are always easy for you. For example, when they train firemen, they set up a fire, but they control the fire. It is not like a real fire in the building, so it is easier. They make you jump down a building, but it is easier; it is not like the real thing. They go easy on you. And then, when you become good enough, they put you in a real-life situation. You understand that, right?

Now the same thing happens in fasting. During fasting, you are constantly feeling something, are you not? Especially if you are in the US and the UK, where the fasts are very, very long, you are constantly feeling thirst; you are constantly feeling hunger. There is not a minute that goes by that you are not feeling it. Your throat is fighting with you. It is yelling at you and saying: give me water, give me water, give me water. Whether you like it or not, your throat is begging you, and you tell your throat: be quiet, throat! It is not maghrib yet. Your stomach starts yelling at you; it starts talking to you, sometimes very loudly, especially when others are around: Come on! I am hungry. What is going on? Where is the supply? And you say: it is fajr! You are starting already! You literally have to have a conversation with yourself.

There is a constant war going on inside you when you are fasting. There is a physical war going on inside you when you are fasting. Your throat is against you; your stomach is against you; your body is against you; your headaches are against you; your coffee withdrawal is against you. Your body is getting weaker and weaker, and it is begging you: please disobey Allah, please disobey Allah. And you remain fasting the entire day.

fighting your body, you say: No. My heart is submitted to Allah, and so, even if my whole body wants something, I will not give it that until Allah permits me to. You train your heart to control your body. This is what you do when you fast; this is what I do when I fast. Why does it matter? Because when we fast, the body grows weaker but the heart grows stronger. The weaker the body grows, the stronger the heart grows, and our capital is fortified. We draw the power out of the body and give it to the heart. Why? Because for the country to survive, it is the capital that must be strong, not the cities and the villages.

When the fast is over, when these thirty days of training are over, it is time to face the real world. Now, when you step out into the world in the remaining months, your heart is ready to control your body. Your capital is completely fortified. All its defenses are strong. You are ready to face your greatest enemy. Who is your greatest enemy?

وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ خُطُوَتِ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

Do not follow the footsteps of Shaitaan; he is your open enemy.

إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَنَ لِلْإِنسَنِ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ

Indeed, without the least doubt, Shaitaan is man's greatest enemy.

So now your heart and body have gone through these thirty days of training. Once Ramadan is over, you are not going to eat whatever your body wants, you will not simply go wherever you want, you will not simply look at whatever you want, because all of those things are what the body wants. But who grew stronger through your fasts? Who grew weaker and who grew stronger through your fasts? The body grew weaker and the heart grew stronger. And where does taqwa rest?

فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى ٱلْقُلُوبِ

The heart is the place where taqwa lives. When you give your body its weakness, you give your heart the strength to gain control over the body. You train yourself to hold your body back from the forbidden things.

So I want to say to you young teenagers especially: do not take this month of fasting lightly. If you want to enjoy the safety and protection of Islam, do not take this discipline of fasting lightly. If you are fasting, and you spend the whole day at home just sleeping it off, or watching movies, or passing the day with PlayStation and Xbox, you are not really fasting. You are not really fasting if you are still watching things you should not be watching, if you are still listening to things you should not be listening to, if you are still cursing with your tongue and breaking hearts. You are not fasting, because your heart is still giving in to the wrong temptation. You are not completing the requirements of your training. The whole training of fasting is that you remember: just as I am fighting my throat, just as I am fighting my stomach, just as I am fighting my thirst, just as I am fighting my hunger, so too I have to fight my eyes, I have to fight my ears, I have to fight my tongue, I have to fight my desires, I have to fight my hormones. It is not only about eating and drinking. Those are only reminders; those are only symbols. And what is the purpose of a symbol? To remind you of the thing it symbolizes.

It is a symbol of far greater things. The physical restraint, the physical discipline, is a reminder of the spiritual discipline, the spiritual restraint. And if we do not remember this, then we become just like the Jews of the Children of Israel about whom Allah complained: they fasted, but they did not have taqwa. They did not have taqwa, even though they fasted. If you and I forget why we were given the fast, then we are doing exactly what the Children of Israel did.

Allah said to you and to me: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ. The word علیکم indicates مقدم; this is called maf'ool jar majroor muqaddam. Fasting has been made obligatory especially upon you. It is your turn now. I am giving you what I gave them. They did not benefit from fasting; they did not acquire taqwa. It is to be hoped that you will not make the same mistakes they made; it is to be hoped that you will gain taqwa. That is what Allah is saying. That is what Allah is saying when He gave us the fast.

What is the first thing we think of when we are fasting? We think of iftar. We think of iftar. Fasting is our training for real life, for the remaining eleven months. And, as I told you, when the training is underway, things are easier, are they not? A controlled fire, a controlled fall, a controlled situation. What does Allah do for us to make it easier? Does He not lock Shaytan up for us? Does He not put Shaytan away? He does. He goes easy on us, so that our heart can have a chance to train and grow stronger. But the moment Ramadan is over — Eid Mubarak — guess what? Shaytan is out, and the war begins. And now all of that training is going to prove useful. But if you did not train your heart properly, how will you stand against him?

For consider what happens when the enemy seizes the capital, our identity: the country is defeated. What happens when Shaytan seizes our hearts, our capital, our identity? We, as Muslims, as believers, are defeated. So we must take this Ramadan seriously, because you can complete all thirty fasts and accomplish nothing.

Let me give you an example, one for the young children. When a man goes through army training, they make him climb over a wall using a rope and come down the other side. Have you ever seen that? So two men join the military. One man climbs the wall; the other walks around it. Both of them reach the other side of the wall. They were supposed to do it thirty times. One climbed the wall ten times; the other walked around it ten times. Both of them reached the other side of the wall, correct? Now, when they are on the battlefield and they have to go over a real wall, who will succeed and who will fail? The one who climbed the wall will succeed, and the one who walked around it will fail. Do you understand? During training, both of them can say, "I did it. I reached the finish line. That is what you wanted, was it not? Well, I did it, Mom, Dad. You wanted me to fast for thirty days, right? Well, I did it."

You will fast and I will fast, but my fast will not be the same as yours if I did not take this training seriously. It will not be the same, because you truly applied yourself to this training and I did not. I merely went through the motions. We are not going to get the same results, because what you gained from your fasts was taqwa, and all I gained from my fasts was hunger and thirst. Do you understand?

In the remaining months of the year, your heart is ready to face the battle against shaitaan, and my heart is not ready at all. I will give in to my very first desire. I will give in to the first temptation shaitaan places before me. Do you understand? Now let us move on. Allah says in the next ayah: أَيَّامًۭا مَّعْدُودَتٍۢ — the counted days. This training is for a counted, a calculated number of days. The word used is مَّعْدُودَتٍۢ, which comes from the word عدد, meaning number, or to count. And مَّعْدُودَتٍۢ is the past tense, which means counted, calculated.

Now let me ask you something. You take thirty dollars out of your wallet. You count it. You make me count it, and you give it to me for safekeeping. You come back a year later and ask me for it. I say I do not remember how much you gave me. I think you gave me twenty-eight dollars, or I think you gave me twenty-nine dollars. What will you say? You will say, No, I gave you thirty dollars. I say, how do you know for sure? What will you say? Because we both counted it. You cannot change a number that has been counted or calculated in the past, correct? Once something is in the past, it is frozen in history. There can be no variations in it, correct?

So these fasts are counted and calculated days, أَيَّامًۭا مَّعْدُودَتٍۢ, and the tense used for the calculation is the past tense, مَّعْدُودَتٍۢ. So the number of fasts cannot keep changing once they have been counted in the past. They cannot be twenty-eight days one year, twenty-nine days another, and thirty days another. It is a fixed number of days. Do you understand?

Let us move on. In the next ayah Allah says: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْآنُ هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ. You know, when it comes to namaaz, there are many, many ayats in the Quran. When it comes to zakaat, there are many ayats in the Quran. On the subject of taqwa, there are many ayats in the Quran. But interestingly, when it comes to fasting and the month of Ramadan, this is the only ayah in the Quran. Allah says شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ, the month of Ramadan, ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْآنُ.

Now listen. What did I tell you? When people think of Ramadan, what comes to their mind? Iftaar, samosey, pakorey, fruit chat. You make sure you have enough ketchup in the house. You go out shopping extra for sodas and juices. Muslims usually do not lose weight in the month of Ramadan. We gain a few extra pounds in Ramadan. That is our practice. Even if you think beyond the iftaar, what you think of when you hear the month of Ramadan is fasting. If you do not think of the food, you at least think of fasting. We think, Oh man, Ramadan! This year it is coming in the summer. The fasts are going to be seventeen, eighteen hours long. It is going to be so hard. That is the thought that goes through our head.

Allah says in the Quran, the very first thing that you should think about when you hear the words شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ, the first thought that should go through our mind, is أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْآنُ — not کتب علیکم الصیام, but أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْآنُ, the month in which the Quran came down. Ramadan, the month in which the Quran was sent down. The thing that makes Ramadan special is not the fasting. The thing that makes Ramadan special is the Quran. That is what Allah is telling us. That is what Allah is telling us.

Now you must ask yourself: if you fast in Ramadan but recite none of the Quran, if you fast in Ramadan and have not committed even a small portion of the Quran to memory across all thirty days—not a single page, not half a page, not even two verses—if you have memorized nothing of the Quran, then how are you to understand what Allah is saying? You cannot. The entire purpose of Ramadan is to celebrate the Quran. The entire purpose of Ramadan is to celebrate the Quran.

Allah made us Muslims a nation: وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَسَطًۭا. I told you that the first thing a nation needs is a capital. What is our capital? The Ka'aba. The second thing a nation needs is a constitution. What is our constitution? The Quran. And when a constitution is written and passed, every nation celebrates it. Every nation that has a constitution has a constitution day—the day on which its constitution was put into force. Every nation has such a day.

Our constitution too was celebrated. It was revealed in the month of Ramadan. Allah did not give us only a single day to celebrate; He gave us thirty days. He gave us thirty days to celebrate the coming of the Quran. This month of Ramadan is a celebration of the fact that Allah made us an Ummah. Now we have our own capital, we have our own constitution, and we have our own days of fasting. No one before us had thirty days of fasting. They had a few days of fasting, fewer than ten. But no one had an entire month in which to celebrate their constitution. The Christians did not have شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ; the Jews did not have شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ; only we Muslims were given the gift of شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ.

Allah said: now, if you wish to be called یا ایھا الذین آمنو, O you who believe, you must change the direction in which you pray, and you must change the days on which you fast. You must change the direction in which your heart points, and you must discipline your body through your heart. The Quran is the message for our hearts; it is a reminder for our hearts. أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَىِٕنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ—only by the remembrance of Allah does the heart find peace. بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ is the key, and Allah called this Quran a remembrance: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَفِظُونَ.

This month of Ramadan is a gift to us from Allah. It is a gift of restraint for our hearts; it is a gift of discipline for our hearts; it is a gift of training for our hearts—so that we may train our hearts, so that we may fortify our capital against every attack of the enemy. Not only that, but Allah made the month of Ramadan a month in which sins are burned; they are quite literally incinerated. Ramadan comes from the word رَمَضَ, which means that which is intensely and fiercely heated by the sun. The word الرمضاء means the intense heat of the sun. The Arabs used to say رمضت الغنم when their sheep were scorched while grazing under the blazing heat of the sun, to the point that their livers were damaged. This month was so named because it burns away the sins of the believers. This month trains our heart, makes it strong, and weakens the desires of the body. A hadith of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, says:

Falsification Test

And although the Qur'an is not a book of science, it is very scientific in its approach when it speaks about things. In science there is a concept called the falsification test: if you propose a theory and it cannot be falsified, then your theory must be correct. So the idea is this: either prove me wrong or accept what I am saying. When Einstein came up with the theory of relativity, his peers said, "Now give us two theories that can disprove your theory; and if we cannot disprove it, then we will accept it." In the same way, the Qur'an, in numerous places, applies this very falsification test to validate its authenticity.

لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا

If this Qur'an were from anyone other than your Lord, you would find numerous contradictions in it.

قُلْ يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوٓا۟ إِن زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ لِلَّهِ مِن دُونِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا۟ ٱلْمَوْتَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَدِقِينَ

So, consequently, two movements sprouted. One of them was the Protestant Reformation movement. The church said that the average Christian had no business reading the Bible. The Protestant movement, then, is what a seventh- or eighth-grade summary of it would be. Therefore we must come to that which does make sense, and that is science, that is philosophy, that is logic.

So there is this revolt against the church from both directions: from the religious direction, the Protestants; and from the scientific, secular direction, this other revolution takes place. And together they finally remove and eliminate the authority of the church.

Now, once this revolution takes place in Europe—and there is no doubt that it is one of the bloodiest revolutions in world history—but once it is over, all of a sudden Europe is a free-thinking society. This was the time when a great many philosophies came out of Europe. And finally, once I had all this information, I tested the concepts I had learned against them to see whether they passed or not. But what I really appreciated about Noman's style was that he never forced anything on me. He provided me with all the tools; he helped me line up all my ducks in a row; but he never actually told me what to believe or not to believe. He left that decision entirely to me. He was so confident that I would make the right decision in light of the facts that it was not even a concern for him. And that is exactly what I want to do for you all in these sessions, because I have complete confidence in these beliefs. I am simply going to line everything up for you, and then it will be your decision whether you accept it or not. Allah gave us all the freedom of choice.

And who am I to take that choice away from you? I will not even ask you, at the end of these sessions, whether you now believe or not. That is entirely between you and Allah. All I can do is remain there for you when you have questions, which, InshaAllah, I pray I will be able to do. The only thing I ask of you is that you give me a fair chance. Take in all the information I give you, and do not reject it at once. Over the next few sessions, I will be assembling a jigsaw puzzle for you, piece by piece. Now, it is possible that, as the picture begins to form, you may jump ahead and guess at the final image, and then reject it on the basis of your own assumptions or preconceived notions. Do not do that. Let me set all the pieces in place until the final picture is clear. Then make your decision on the basis of all the evidence I have provided. So, with that background in mind, let us begin and define some terms. Let us start with science and religion. Wikipedia defines science as a systematic, methodical enterprise that builds and organizes knowledge in the form of testable explanations and predictions about the universe. In other words, science is a methodology for understanding a reality on the basis of a system of cause and effect. Everything in science is an observation grounded in cause and effect. There is an effect, and we try to understand the cause that produced it. Or we understand the cause, so that we can create the effect. Once we have knowledge of the cause, we can then control or manipulate the parameters of that cause in order to produce the effect, because we know how it works.

So, for example, when you build an airplane, there may be a thousand ways to put that plane together, but when it takes off you know almost for certain that it will reach its destination. Why? Because all the possibilities of risk have been tested, and it has been made certain that any potential danger is removed from the parameters of that flight, which then increases the safety of that aircraft, InshaAllah. That is all science is about. It is simply a methodology for producing an effect, that is all. It is not an ideology; it is a methodology, a systematic approach to understanding cause and effect.

Ideology is defined as a set of conscious and unconscious ideas that make up one's goals, expectations, and motivations. An ideology is a set of standards that are followed by people, government, and/or other groups, and that is considered the "norm."

Now, what is religion? Religion is an ideology that translates into a way of life. It is a way of life.

That is what is ideologically tracked. It is a way of life. And there again is that word, "ideology." What is ideology, once more?
