It allows new life to develop in its womb. It accepts and absorbs the water the farmer gives, and it uses that water to nurture the seeds into a fruit-bearing tree. Fire, on the other hand, rejects water entirely. Through fire there can be no growth, no development of life. That is the greatest and most important difference between clay and fire. It is the difference between humility and arrogance. The humility of clay, of soil, allows growth; it nurtures; it is a source of life. It yields; it submits. Fire, on the other hand, only consumes and destroys and kills. It burns and destroys anything and everything placed within it. Try sowing a seed within fire; you will not get very far with it. But sow those same seeds in soil, and it will give you back a tree laden with fruit.
body.topic_title_en: He created me from fire and him from clay
body.topic_title_ur: Allah created me from fire and him from clay

body.text_en:
The next matter I wish to discuss is the استعاذہ, which is what we commonly recite before we begin the recitation of the Qur'an itself: اعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم. This ayah is called the استعاذہ. It is not a part of Surah Al-Fateha itself, but it is certainly linked to the Fateha, and to every other surah of the Qur'an for that matter. The Fateha actually begins with the Basmallah, which is بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم. In the Arab world, this ayah بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم is referred to as the Basmallah, with a fatha or a zabar. But one thing to remember is that this Basmallah is an ACTUAL PART of Al-Fateha itself, while it is NOT a part of the remaining surahs. I will say that again. The Basmallah is an actual part of Surah Al-Fateha, but it is NOT a part of the remaining surahs. The Basmallah is recited before all the other surahs in order to honor those surahs, because it contains the primary name and attributes of Allah, and AlRehman and AlRaheem, and through it we begin the recitation of Allah's holy book. Yet it is not the first ayah of any of the other surahs. But when it comes to Surah AlFateha, it IS a part of the surah itself; it is the first ayah. It is the leader and the king of all the remaining ayats of Surah Al-Fateha. As we know, Surah AlFateha has 7 ayats, and the Basmallah is the highest ranking ayah among those 7 ayats. If you skip this ayah, you lose all the power and majesty of Surah AlFateha, and InshaAllah, when we study this ayah, you will understand why.

So what I want you to remember is that أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم is called the استعاذہ, and بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم is called the Basmallah! Now, before we begin the استعاذہ, let us get an idea of the topics we are going to cover over the next few sessions.

Since this استعاذہ is used to seek the refuge or protection of Allah from the cursed Shaytan, InshaAllah, as part of analyzing this ayah, we will try to gain an in depth understanding of who Shaytan is, what made him a Shaytan, and what the difference is between Shaytan and Iblees. Are they two separate entities? Or are they both the same? What is Shaytan's real agenda, and why is he so bent upon getting us into trouble? What is this fellow's problem? How does he attack? What are his whisperings? What is this thing called وسوسۃ? InshaAllah, we will cover all these topics over the next few sessions.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
As part of our analysis and study of the استعاذہ, we will also study two surahs: Surah AlFalaq and Surah AlNaas. The reason for that is that these 2 surahs are in reality the explanation of the details of the استعاذہ. We will look at the true meaning of the word protection, and why we need Allah's protection against Shaytan; why it is that we are not able to protect ourselves; why we need a higher power. We will also see why it is ONLY Allah, and no power other than Allah, that is capable of protecting us. We will see what the requirements of coming under Allah's protection are, and how we make ourselves worthy of His protection. These are some of the things we will InshaAllah cover in the study of this ayah, and trust me, once we are done with the study of this ayah, the استعاذہ will take on a whole new meaning for us. We will never again be able to say the استعاذہ in the casual, superficial way that we do today. Today, when we recite the استعاذہ against Shaytan.

He probably laughs at us, because he knows that our استعاذہ is an empty shell. It is a fake bullet, an empty cartridge, a blunt sword that does nothing against him except perhaps tickle him a little. But InshaAllah, once we are equipped with the knowledge of this ayah, our استعاذہ will become an extremely powerful strike against Shaytan, because it will be backed by an understanding not only of the ayah itself, but also of Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Naas, and because we will have met the requirements for gaining Allah's protection. أنشاء اللہ تعالی. So let us begin, بأذن اللہ.

Meaning of ISTIAAZA

What is the استعاذہ, and where did it come from? The استعاذہ comes from an ayah of the Quran itself. Allah commands us in Surah Al-Nahal:

فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

When you are about to recite the Quran, then seek refuge of Allah from Shaitaan AlRajeem. Also in Surah Aeraaf Allah says:

وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ نَزْغٌۭ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ

And before the shaitaan whispers his evil into you, seek refuge of Allah. إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ — because He is the all listener and the all knower.

Therefore, before we begin studying the actual ayaats of Surah Al-Fateha, I want us all to gain a really good understanding of this استعاذہ, and of how it is linked to Surah Al-Fateha and to the rest of the Quran.

Spiritual protection

So what does the word استعاذہ mean? The word استعاذہ comes from the word عاذ ، یعوذ، أعوذ, which means to turn to someone for protection, to turn to someone seeking their help, to tell somebody that you are in danger and cannot defend yourself on your own. It is an acknowledgment that I need the protection of another being, one more powerful than myself, to help me spiritually, not to help me physically. In Arabic you do not use the word عاذ or أعوذ for physical help. You use the word أعوذ ONLY when you require spiritual help.

When is it that we need physical help? When we are dealing with the seen. And when do we need spiritual help? When we are dealing with the unseen. Physical help is for things for which we need to dial 911, or call out to someone, saying, "Please help me, I am being attacked." In such situations in Arabic we would NOT say عاذ. We would use other words, such as نجد or نصر. You understand?
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
From this same root we get the word جُنون, meaning insanity or madness, and the person who exhibits this insanity is called مجنون, meaning insane. Why is that? Because a madman is someone whose intellect has been concealed, whose intellect has been veiled.

From the same word we also have جَنَّۃ, meaning heaven. Why? Because heaven is invisible. It is hidden. It is veiled and concealed from our eyes.

Also from the same root we have جَنِین, a fetus, because it is concealed and hidden in the womb of its mother.

So Jinn are called jinns because they are hidden from our eyes. They are invisible to us. They exist, but we cannot see them.

Jinns are not a different creation from human beings. They are not a separate creation. They are simply souls that are detached from their bodies.

When a human being who bears the attributes of a shaytaan, an evil man, dies and his soul detaches from his body, he is no longer called Insaan; he is now called a jinn. Insaan is the seen form. Jinn is the unseen form. Yet the two are one and the same entity. Consider a disbeliever, someone far removed from the path of Allah. During his life on this earth, while his soul is attached to his body, he is called Shaitaan AlIns, meaning the Shaytan in human form. But when this same disbeliever dies and his soul separates from his body, he is now called Shaitan AlJinn, the Shaytan in the unseen form. So the Jinn are not a separate creation of Allah. They are the same creation as we are, only disconnected from their bodies. Now, just as there are good human beings and evil ones, there are good jinns and there are evil jinns. Both types exist in spiritual form, just as both types exist in physical form.

So the Jinn and the Ins are not two separate creations. They are, in essence, one single creation. While they are joined to their bodies, in physical form, they are called Shayateen AlIns. When they die — and we know that it is the body that dies, while the soul lives on forever — when their souls become detached from their bodies, they are called Shayateen AlJinn, because they can no longer be seen. Do you understand?

Rajeem

So from what do we seek the refuge of Allah? From Shaitaan! From the Shaitaan that exists in physical form as a human being, and from the Shaitaan that exists in spiritual form as a jinn. We seek the protection of Allah from these evil entities, who are what? Rajeem! Just like the adjective Shaytan, Rajeem is also an adjective. Shaytan and Rajeem are both adjectives. So what is the difference? Shaytan is the primary adjective that describes the trait of an evil entity, and Rajeem is a secondary adjective that describes the evil trait itself. I will say that again. Shaytan is the primary adjective that describes the trait of an evil entity, and Rajeem is a secondary adjective that describes the evil trait itself.

The word rajeem comes from Rajama, and Rajam means to pelt with stones, to cast aside. So AlRajeem is the one who has been cast aside by Allah. Because of his actions he is pelted away by Allah. He is مطرود. He is rejected and denied the mercy of Allah. In fact, both words, Shaitaan and Rajeem, carry a similar meaning. Shaitaan: the one who is far removed. Rajeem: the one who has been cast away.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
So an evil entity, by its NATURE, is Shaytaan. It is far away from the truth. And the evil entity, by its ACTIONS, is rajeem. It has been cast away. I will say this again. Listen carefully. Shaitaan, by his NATURE, is far removed from the truth, and Shaitaan, by his ACTIONS, is rajeem: he has been cast away, he has been pelted away. Our thoughts, our concepts, and our beliefs translate into actions. When the thoughts are evil, the primary adjective Shaytan applies. When those evil thoughts turn into actions, the secondary adjective Rajeem applies, and Allah casts such beings away, or pelts them away from Himself, because of their evil actions.

Take an example. A disbeliever holds to the concept of multiple gods. That is a concept far removed from the truth. For what is the truth? The truth is لا الہ الا اللہ, there is no deity except Allah. So such a being is Shaytan. He is far removed from the truth of لا الہ الا اللہ because of his concept of polytheism. And because of his concepts, he commits the act of worshipping many idols. He prostrates to stones.

And because of this action, Allah rejects him. He pelts him away. He casts him away from Himself, and he becomes Rajeem.

So Shaytan by his nature is far removed from the truth, and Shaytan by his actions is rajeem, stoned away.

So with the استعاذہ we seek the refuge of Allah from Shaytan the Rajeem. We seek Allah's protection for the safety of our souls from those who are evil in their concepts and in their thinking, as well as from those who are evil in their actions. We also seek Allah's protection from becoming one of them ourselves. This is very, very important to understand. We too are human beings. We too have thoughts, beliefs, and concepts, and we too perform actions based on those concepts. The adjective shaytan applies to anyone in human form. We, being Sulemanis, are not exempted or excluded from this adjective of Shaytan. So with the استعاذہ we do not only seek Allah's refuge and His protection from other external evil entities; we also seek His protection for our own souls, and we also seek His refuge for our own lives. That is, O Allah, with this استعاذہ, by saying أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم, we turn to You for Your protection — not only from the external enemies, but also from ourselves turning into those very enemies whom You cast away. O Allah, protect our concepts, our beliefs, and our thinking from becoming evil. Protect our concepts from becoming far removed from the truth, because if that happens we too will become one of those whom You have called Shaytan. And we know that our thoughts will inevitably translate into actions, and when that happens we too will become one of the Rajeem, the ones whom You have cast away, and whom You have pelted and stoned away from Your company and Your mercy.

So this is the essence of the استعاذہ: that Allah protect us from the external evil entities who are shaytan because of their nature and rajeem because of their actions, and that He protect our nature from becoming a shaytan, and protect our actions from becoming rajeem. On the Day of Judgment, may we not be among those whom Allah has described:

هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ٱلْغَشِيَةِ. Have you heard the story of the Day of Judgment?
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
وُجُوهٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَشِعَةٌ. There will be faces that will be full of shame and abjection, faces that will be abased and degraded, faces of those far removed from the truth, faces of shayateen.

عَامِلَةٌۭ نَّاصِبَةٌۭ. With their actions of hard labor — actions done in the displeasure of Allah. Actions that are Rajeem, cast away.

تَصْلَىٰ نَارًا حَامِيَةًۭ. They will enter the burning fires of hell.

By the shafa'a, the intercession of Rasul Allah SAS, may Allah protect us all from being among such people on the Day of Judgment.

Iblees

Now that we have spoken a little about the adjective Shaytan, let us speak a little about their leader, Iblees. Most of you already know this story.

According to the Qur'an, the infamous career of Iblees begins with the creation of Adam AS. He was an angel of very high rank among the angels of jannah, and he enjoyed much respect, rank, and prestige. He held the title of معلم الملکوت, which means the teacher of the angels. Everything was going well in his life until one day, out of the blue, Allah says:

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ

Allah says to the angels: I have decided to create My representative on earth. What do you think?

And right at the outset,

the angels have a problem with that!

قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ

The angels respond: Seriously? You want to create someone who is going to create problems on this earth and spill blood? Why would You want to do that? Why do You need them? So that You may be glorified and praised? If that is all You want, we are enough for that! You do not need another creation to do it. This is the angels' reply to Allah SWT. So we learn that at the very mention of the creation of Adam, the angels begin to have a problem. Allah says:

قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

I have knowledge of things that you do not know. So Allah decides to go ahead with His plan and creates Adam.

فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى

After He created Adam, He blew His soul into him. Allah blew His soul into him. Then He granted him the knowledge of all the names.

وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسْمَآءِ هَٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَدِقِينَ

Then Allah asks the angels: now tell Me the names of these things. If you think you know everything, then tell Me the names of these things. They said:

قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

We have no knowledge except what You have given us. You are the All-Knowing and the All-Wise. So all the angels accept defeat, and they accept that Adam is superior to them in knowledge. Then Allah commands all the angels to do sajda to Adam.

وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟

And they all fell in sajda,

إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ

except for Iblees. He refused to do sajda.

أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَفِرِينَ

He became arrogant and proud and became one of the disbelievers.

So Allah asked Iblees: why do you refuse to obey My command?

قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ ۖ

What stopped you from doing sajda when I commanded you to do so?

قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ

He said: I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay. Fire is better than clay.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
So Iblees challenged Allah's command and His justice, and refused to do sajda. Now let us take a moment to analyze the argument Iblees presented. His argument was:

قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ

I am better than him. Why? Because You made me from fire and You made him from clay. Now let us analyze this argument for a moment. Iblees said he is better than Adam. Why? Because of the material out of which they were both made, the material of their bodies. He argued that fire is better than clay. Now is that true?

Let us see. Fire is bright, clay is dull, and bright is always better than dull. Fire illuminates; clay does not. That which illuminates is always better than that which does not. Fire is hot, clay is cold, and heat is better than cold. The flames of fire rise up toward the sky; the particles of clay always fall to the earth. The one that rises to the sky is always better than the one that falls to the earth. So what did Iblees do here? He used logic! He used deductive reasoning, which in Arabic is called Qiyaas. The word Qiyas literally means measurement. He measured the properties of fire.

against the properties of clay and arrived at his conclusion: أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ — I am better than him.

On the surface, the argument Iblees presented does appear to be entirely sound. But that raises a question. Why did Allah ask Iblees to prostrate to Adam in the first place? Why did He ask one of higher rank to prostrate before one of lower rank? That is an unjust command! The answer usually given is that Allah commanded Iblees, and he should have obeyed. Yes! But why did Allah issue an unjust command to begin with?

So is that what truly happened? Did Allah issue an unjust command? Absolutely not! (نعوذ باللہ من ذالک) Allah is above all injustice. He is indeed the Most Just! What, then, did Iblees miss here? If you think about it, fire and clay are both properties of the body, and both are physical, are they not? They are two different kinds of bodies, made of two different kinds of material, but they are both bodies and both physical. Now, at what moment did Allah ask the angels to prostrate to Adam? فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى — AFTER Allah blew His soul into Adam. ONLY after Allah blew His soul into Adam did He ask the angels to prostrate to him. And Allah's soul is greater than any body. The soul is spiritual; bodies are physical, and spirituality is ALWAYS greater than physicality, no matter what material the body is made from. So Allah was ABSOLUTELY just in commanding the angels to prostrate to Adam, because the command was not to prostrate to his body. The command was to prostrate to the soul that Allah blew into him, and to the soul that held the superior knowledge which Allah Himself taught Adam AS. SubhanAllah.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
This is the problem with Qiyaas; this is the problem with logical deduction. Iblees placed the content inside his own limited context, and then mixed his experiential biases into it. Because, as I said earlier, these angels all had their objections at the very mention of Adam's creation. قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ — Do you want to create someone who will cause corruption on earth and spill blood? We are enough for Your glorification; You do not need anyone else.

So at the very mention of Adam, the angels developed an experiential bias. Why does Allah need man? Are we not good enough for Him? What if He ends up loving him more than He loves us? What if he turns out to be more powerful than us? Will that take Allah's love away from me? Iblees had his own fears. What if he takes my title? I am معلم الملکوت — what if Allah gives him my title and he is ranked above me? What about my position? What about my power? My authority? So Iblees mixed his emotions and his experiential biases into his limited reasoning, and he strayed from the right path.

This is why we Sulemanis are not the people of Qiyaas. We are not people of measurement; we are people of obedience. We place our faith in the commands of our Imam, which were taken from the commands of Maulana Ali, which were taken from the commands of Rasul Allah (SAS), which were taken from Allah AWJ. These are commands delivered to us through the duaat and issued on the tongues of our manaseeb. And we accept their command, even when at times it seems unjust, because, as Allah said to the angels: قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ — I know what you do not know.

We submit to the idea that our elders know what we do not know. As children, we accept that our parents know what we do not know. If they ask us to stop doing something, or if they ask us to do something, then they must have a reason for it that we do not understand. They have lived longer, and they have seen more of the world. I have not experienced even a fraction of the life that they have experienced and lived through, and therefore they know better.

We submit to the idea that our teacher knows better. We are students. We have access only to what he is sharing with us at this moment, but my teacher speaks out of his vast knowledge. He sees things that I cannot see at this point. So even if he tells me something I cannot fully grasp right now, I must trust him. I must place my faith in him, and one day, as I move up through the levels of my education, InshaAllah I will understand.

And Shaytan, because he used Qiyaas, because he himself used deductive logical reasoning, blows and whispers and prods at us with that same logic. Why? Because he knows that what got him into trouble with Allah will get us into trouble with Allah as well.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
Why do you need to pray salaah? It is so foolish; it does not even make any sense. If it really is so important, why only five times a day? Why at these particular times? Why not whenever you wish? Why does Allah want you not to eat in Ramadan? If He is so loving, how is it that He deprives you of food? Why do you need to spend in Allah's way? Why can He not provide it Himself, if He is so powerful?

And so he instigates, he pokes, he prods. He creates frustration, he distorts the intellect, he binds us with the ropes of arrogance, desire, and temptation. We fall prey to his machinations and we give up Salaah, we give up fasting, we give up the various duties laid upon us through Dayam Al-Islam.

There is ONLY one reason to follow Dayam Al-Islam. Understand this! There is ONLY one good reason to follow the duties laid upon us, and that reason is the very same one that Allah laid upon the angels: OBEDIENCE! That is the ONLY reason good enough for a Muslim, for a Momin, to pray, to perform salaah, to fast, to give zakaat, to do everything Allah commanded — ONLY because Allah has commanded it, and because His beloved prophet Muhammad Mustafa (SAS) has shaped these rituals for us. For this concept of obedience, and this alone, is what separated the angels from Iblees. And what happens when we walk the same path that Iblees took?

قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّغِرِينَ

Descend from here. This janna is not a place for the arrogant and the proud. Get out of here; you are among the humiliated.

When we disobey Allah, we walk on the same path as Iblees. And if we think about it, knowing what we know about Allah's justice, we cannot imagine that Allah would reject Iblees for his disobedience and yet accept us for ours. That would be an injustice to Iblees. Allah is the most just. He will deal with us EXACTLY as He dealt with Iblees. He will say to us EXACTLY what He said to Iblees:

قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّغِرِينَ

Get out of my sight; you are arrogant. I told you to pray, and you disobeyed. I told you to fast, and you disobeyed. I told you to give zakaat, and you disobeyed. I told you to perform Hajj, and you disobeyed. Get out of my sight; you are arrogant, and my Jannah is not a place for the proud and the arrogant.

What will we do then? You and I can invent every excuse in the world. You and I can produce every justification, all the inductive and deductive reasoning there is. It will not be accepted, just as it was not accepted from Iblees. May Allah protect us all from being among the followers of Iblees.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
So now what do we do? We have done so much wrong. We have been so disobedient to Allah. So now what do we do? Are we doomed? Are we destined never to enter Jannah again? ABSOLUTELY NOT. ABSOLUTELY NOT. How do we know that for certain? By studying this very story of Adam AS. Further along we find that Adam too disobeys Allah. He eats from the forbidden tree, and because of Allah's immaculate justice, Adam and Hawwa receive the same treatment that Iblees received: they too are removed from Jannah. But there is a great difference. Let us take a moment to understand it.

Difference between the reaction of Iblees and the reaction of Adam

The word Iblees comes from the root word ابلس, which means to despair, to give up hope. When Iblees angered Allah, he brought Allah's wrath upon himself. He was pelted away by Allah and removed from Allah's mercy. But Iblees gave up hope in Allah. He gave up hope in Allah's mercy. He gave up hope in Allah's forgiveness, and he believed himself to be doomed forever. BECAUSE he gave up hope, BECAUSE of his ابلس, which means to give up hope, he did not return to Allah. That is why he is called Iblees.

Adam, on the other hand, did the very same thing. He disobeyed Allah, and he too brought Allah's wrath upon himself. He too was cast out of Jannah. Allah said to him as well:

وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ

Descend from here. You are now enemies of one another.

Do you remember what words Allah used for Iblees when He cast him out?

قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا

Descend from here.

The same word is used by Allah for both Adam and Iblees: اھبطو, descend, fall! So both received exactly the same punishment for their disobedience. But unlike Iblees, what did Adam AS say?

قَالاَ رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَآ أَنفُسَنَا وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَـسِرِينَ

O our Master, we have wronged ourselves. And if You do not forgive us, if You do not have mercy on us, we will surely become of the losers.

فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ

Adam received certain words from Allah through which he begged Allah's forgiveness. He repented. And as soon as he repented, Allah forgave Adam.

إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

Certainly, without doubt, Allah is the Most Forgiving.

SubhanAllah, what a beautiful Ayah. I want us to appreciate something here. The Ayah reads:

فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

This is one single Ayah. Allah does not even move on to the next Ayah to mention Adam's forgiveness. He could have stated Adam's repentance in one Ayah, and then in the next Ayah stated his forgiveness, and in the Ayah after that stated that He is All Forgiving. No! This Ayah is so beautiful that Allah's immense forgiveness is fused together with Adam's repentance. That is to say, the very instant Adam repented, Allah forgave him. The Quran did not even break to the next Ayah. SubhanAllah!

Do you know what that means? It means Allah is so eager for our repentance that as soon as the thought of repentance enters our hearts,

the rain of his mercy and his forgiveness begins. The moment we so much as think of repentance, Allah opens his arms to us. SubhanAllah.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
So if I realize today that I have disobeyed Allah, all I need to do is turn to him in repentance. Before my apology has even traveled from my heart to my tongue, Allah says: فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ — I forgive you, my slave. I am the most forgiving.

Iblees gave up hope. Iblees chose arrogance. Adam (AS) did not give up hope. He chose the path of repentance. We are the children of Adam (AS). We are not the children of Iblees. We are people of repentance. We are people of hope. We are not people of despair.

Seek Allah's forgiveness, and before your words are finished, see yourself forgiven. SubhanAllah! We may have been disobedient until today, but with the Istiaaza, by saying اعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم, we can seek Allah's forgiveness. We can seek Allah's refuge from walking the same path that Iblees walked.

And with our استعاذہ we can declare that from this day forward, Ya Allah, we fall into your obedience for the rest of our lives.

بارک لی ولکم فی القرآن کریم ! و آخر الدعوانا عن الحمد للہ رب العلمین

Revenge of Iblees

So this is how the career of Iblees begins. He is rejected. He is humiliated. And as his first order of business, he gets Adam and Hawwa (AS) thrown out of Jannah. But he does not stop there. To avenge his humiliation, he makes it his life's mission to ensure that none of their children ever make it back to Jannah. So he begins his recruitment and starts drafting Shayateen in. Again, who are the Shayateen? Shaytan is an adjective describing those who are far removed from the mercy of Allah. He creates an army of such beings and gets down to business. So this is Iblees and his army of Shayateen, for you and me. This is how the story of Iblees begins.

I only wanted to give you a basic idea of how it all started. We will study the mission statement of Iblees, his short-term goals and his long-term goals, in detail. In fact we will return to this entire story in far greater detail later on. But for now I simply wanted to introduce you to our good friend Iblees, and his buddies, the Shayateen — pun intended.

Shaytan has many evil tactics and machinations, and some of them are so cleverly crafted that we do not even realize they are coming from Shaytan. I will speak about some of the tactics of Shaytan so that you become aware of them.

Among the tactics of Shaytan is to make us forget and overlook. We forget the time of our prayers. We forget the time to give our zakaats. We forget to carry out a good intention we may have made. We forget anything good that we are supposed to do. That is one of the tactics of Shaytan. As the companion of Moosa (AS) says: وَمَآ أَنْسَىٰنِيهُ إِلَّا ٱلشَّيْطَنُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ — It was Shaytan that made me forget. So we seek the refuge of Allah, so that when Shaytan uses this tactic on us, Allah's protection comes to our aid and prevents us from forgetting, because it is Shaytan who causes forgetfulness.

Among the tactics of Shaytan is to make us feel sleepy, to make us feel lazy in the performance of good deeds. When it is time for salaah and you begin to feel sleepy, that is one of the machinations of Shaytan.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
Among the tactics of Shaytan is to make us frightened and terrified beyond what is natural. There is a natural fear: you see a snake or a scorpion, and that is natural fear. But then there is an abnormal fear, an obsessive fear.

part 17.You begin to think about the past or the future without stopping, until you sink into depression. That kind of frantic fear is a machination of Shaytan. So seeking Allah's refuge from Shaytan makes you optimistic and hopeful.

Among the tactics of Shaytan, believe it or not, is procrastination. The Prophet (SAS) said: التصویف من الشیطان — procrastination is from Shaytan. Putting off a good deed until later, or until tomorrow. Procrastination. Ah, not now. Perhaps tomorrow. Perhaps next week. That is from Shaytan, whether the matter belongs to this world or to the world to come. Shaytan does not want anything good to happen to us. He does not want us to worship. He wants us to waste all our good deeds. So when we seek refuge with Allah, we become more productive in our lives. SubhanAllah.

The chief thing from which we seek refuge is the whisperings, the وسواس, of Shaytan. Shaytan whispers. What is the whispering of Shaytan? That Shaytan whispers means that he puts thoughts into our minds that would otherwise never come there — thoughts that would otherwise never come. Shaytan does not have the power to force us to act. He does not put a gun to our heads and issue commands. He cannot do that. Rather, he entices us. He tempts us. For Allah says in the Qur'an that on the Day of Judgment, when the people he misled curse him and ask Allah to punish him and cast him into the Fire, Shaytan will answer them:

وَمَا كَانَ لِىَ عَلَيْكُم مِّن سُلْطَنٍ — I had no power over you.

إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَٱسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِى ۖ — I merely called you; you were the ones who answered my call.

فَلَا تَلُومُونِى وَلُومُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُم ۖ — Therefore do not curse me on this day; curse your own souls.

مَّآ أَنَا۠ بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُصْرِخِىَّ — I had no control over your actions; only you had control over your actions.

Sometimes we are sitting quietly, and out of nowhere a vulgar thought enters our minds. Out of nowhere at all. Suddenly there is a desire to do something that would be disobedience to Allah. This is the whisper of Shaytan.

Another such tactic concerns anger. Shaytan increases anger to the point where our veins are about to burst out. When you are very angry, when you are furious, that is from the tactics of Shaytan.

We also say the istiaaza when we enter the restroom. Why? Because the shayateen are filthy creatures, and they love to gather in places of filth. They love to be in places of najasah, and the restroom is a place of najasah. That is why, when we enter the restroom, we say:

اعوذ باللہ من الرجس نجس خبیث المخبث الشیطان الرجیم

So we seek Allah's refuge before we enter the restroom.

We seek refuge in Allah when we are frightened. Rasul Allah (SAS) taught his family that when they are frightened they should recite:

بسم اللہ اعوذ بکلمات اللہ التامۃ من غضبہ و عقابہ و شر عبادہ و من ھمزات الشیاطین و ان یحضرون

In other words, it is a longer form of the istiaaza, because being terrified is one of the tactics of Shaytan. Allah mentions in the Qur'an:

إِنَّمَا ذَلِكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَنُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَآءَهُۥ فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
Indeed, it is Shaytan who frightens the friends of Allah. Do not fear him, and fear Me, if you are a believer.

So when we say Aozubillah, it removes the unnatural fear within us and makes us brave.

We also seek refuge in Allah when we are distracted in the salaah. If we cannot concentrate, if we cannot focus, we say Aoozubillahi.

We seek refuge in Allah when we go to a new place.

from the evils that lurk there. We seek refuge as well whenever we feel drawn to act upon an evil thought or an evil desire, because the moment such a desire rises, Shaytaan arrives to pour fuel on the fire. For that reason we seek the refuge of Allah. And Allah states this plainly for us in the Qur'an: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ نَزْغٌۭ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ — If Shaytan urges you toward an evil, then seek refuge in Allah, because He is Samee, Aleem.

And finally, we seek the refuge of Allah under any and all circumstances, even for no reason at all. We may say Aozubillah this very moment, because we need no reason to utter this zikr. We may turn to Allah at any time for His protection and His refuge.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
So عاذ is used exclusively to ask for spiritual help and protection. Whose protection? The protection of a deity, a god, a divine power, a being that is all powerful.

So these are the two requirements of the word عاذ. It is used to seek spiritual protection, and ONLY from a deity. Only when these two requirements are fulfilled is the word عاذ used in Arabic. If I turn for spiritual guidance to a religious leader, or to a psychologist, or to a therapist, I CANNOT use the word عاذ, because it is not the same thing. I am not turning to them with the intention of seeking their protection. I am turning to them to gain knowledge, to seek guidance and help, not protection. And they are not a deity; therefore I cannot use the word عاذ for them, even though the guidance and help I need is spiritual in nature. You understand?

So who is that deity to whom we turn for spiritual help? أعوذ باللہ. That deity is Allah! Turning to a being in this manner is done EXCLUSIVELY for Allah (SWT). Now why is that important? It is important because this act of the استعاذہ

— this act of turning to Allah and seeking His spiritual protection — itself becomes an act of worship. Why is that? Because in doing it we are obeying a command of Allah. Allah commanded us:

وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ نَزْغٌۭ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ

Because we turn to Allah alone for our spiritual protection, in compliance with His command and in obedience to it, the act of استعاذہ itself becomes an act of worship. This is important to understand. For if I turn to some other being in this way, seeking spiritual protection from anyone other than Allah, then that act is itself the very definition of Shirk, which is to set up a partner alongside Allah. It means that I believe someone other than Allah has the power to protect me spiritually from the enemy I seek protection from. That would be the equivalent of prostrating or submitting before an idol. And this is exactly what people did before Islam.

In the age of ignorance before Islam (دور الجاھلیۃ), when a man traveled through the desert and made camp for the night, he was afraid of attacks by jinn and demons. He was afraid that they would fall upon him in the night. So he would climb up onto a high cliff and call out loudly:

أعوذ بِسَیِّدِ ھٰذا الوادی

I seek refuge and protection from the leader of the jinn of this valley in which I am spending the night.

And what did this accomplish? Did the jinn protect them? No! In Surah Jinn, Allah reports upon the tongue of the jinn that when those people did this, it only increased the jinn in their arrogance and in their efforts to lead humankind astray.

وَأَنَّهُۥ كَانَ رِجَالٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْإِنسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمْ رَهَقًۭا

And indeed, there were men among human beings who took shelter with the leader of the jinn, but they only increased them in sin and disbelief.

So we do not seek this kind of spiritual protection from any being other than Allah. The words اعوذ باللہ therefore mean that I turn for spiritual help and spiritual protection to a deity who is Allah, who is powerful, while acknowledging at the same time that I am not powerful.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
So when I say اعوذ باللہ, I am saying, I am accepting, that I have no power to protect myself. Therefore I turn to Allah, who is all powerful. I am incapable, therefore I turn to the One who is capable. I am weak, I am ضعیف, therefore I turn to the strong, the قوی, the عزیز. I am a slave who needs the protection of his master, therefore I turn to my master.

So my recitation of the استعاذہ contains, in and of itself, two acknowledgments: the acknowledgment of my weakness and of my inability to protect myself against the attacks of Shaytan, and the acknowledgment of the power of my protector, my deity, my Allah, who is strong, who is powerful, and who is capable of protecting me from my greatest enemy, Shaytan AlRjaeem, the cursed devil. And therefore my act of reciting the استعاذہ, my act of turning to Allah alone in search of His protection, becomes an act of worship. And every act of worship carries a reward. So the next time you recite the استعاذہ, think about this, and it will change the way you approach Allah's protection. And God willing, we will look at this further in much more detail.

3 versions of ISTIAAZA

But before we do that, let us speak a little about the semantics and the usage of the استعاذہ, and about why it is placed before the recitation of the Qur'an.

There are three common ways in which the استعاذہ is recited. The first is the short version of the istiaaza: أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم. This means: I seek Allah's protection from Shaytan AlRejeem, the cursed devil. That is the simple one.

The second is one which Rasul Allah sometimes used to say even during his salaah:

أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم مِن ھَمزِہِ وَ نَفْخِہِ وَ نَفْثِہِ

I seek refuge of Allah from Shaitaan AlRajeem, from his whispering, from his prodings and from his blowings. Let us examine these words.

The first word ھَمزِہِ comes from ھُمَزَہ, which means to prod and to poke. You know how sometimes people do that as well, with their words. They hurt people. They poke. They prod. They kick them when they are down. They verbally stick a knife in the heart and then twist it around a bit. And they do it under the disguise of being a well-wisher. So, for example, someone is already worried about his survival because he has lost his job, and the ھامز will say: Oh really? You lost your job? Oh, that is so bad, especially when the economy is so horrible right now. It is almost going to be impossible for you to find another. I know this family. The man lost his job. They eventually lost the house. His wife divorced him. His children left him. He ended up committing suicide. It is SO bad out there. But do not worry, you will be fine.

Have you ever met or interacted with such people? This is one meaning of Humaza. And Allah says:

وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍۢ لُّمَزَةٍ

There is destruction for those who prod and poke. Shaytan is constantly prodding and poking us, constantly urging us to do bad things. He is constantly pushing our buttons. He instigates us, makes us angry and mean, and forces us to overreact. All of that is ھَمزْ.

Nafakha means to blow, as Allah says in the Qur'an in the story of the creation of Adam AS:

فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
Once I completed the creation of Adam, I blew my soul into him. This is nafakha, to blow. Shaytan is constantly blowing his thoughts, his ideas, desires and temptations, fear and anger, jealousy and envy. He is constantly blowing these things into us, and all of that is نَفْخَ.

And then there is Nafasa (not with a س but a ث), which is also a type of blowing, but one in which a little bit of spit comes out, and this is worse than just blowing. This tactic is mentioned in the Qur'an in Surah AlFalaq:

من شر النفاثات فی العقد

InshaAllah we will look at this word in much more detail when we study the Surah. So Shaytan pokes us, prods us, blows on us, spits on us. He uses all these tactics and machinations to harm us. And that is why Rasul Allah SAS would seek Allah AWJ's protection from all these tactics of Shaytan by saying:

أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیمِ ۔ من ھَمزِہِ وَ نَفْخِہِ وَ نَفْثِہِ

This is another variation of this same أستعاذہ, which was used by Rasul Allah, in which he added السمیع العلیم to it:

أعوذ باللہ السمیع العلیم من الشیطان الرجیم ۔ من ھَمزِہِ وَ نَفْخِہِ وَ نَفْثِہِ

I seek refuge of Allah who hears all and who knows all, from Shaitaan AlRajeem, from his whispering, from his prodings and from his blowings. So this is the longest version of the أستعاذہ that our Prophet would sometimes use. Now, two attributes of Allah, السمیع العلیم, are used in this version, and we also use these two attributes in every Fard namaz when we recite Wajjahtu Wajhee before we begin AlFatiha.

What is the last sentence of that supplication? علی ملت ابرھیم و دین محمد و ولایت علی و أبرؤ الیہ من أعدائہ الظالمین۔ وَ أعوذ باللہ السمیع العلیم من الشیطان الَّعین الرجیم — and then we recite the Basmallah and Surah AlFateha.

Now the question is this: why these two names of Allah? Out of the ninety-nine names of Allah, why these two in particular? It is very interesting. What is the meaning of السمیع? It means the One who hears everything. And what is the meaning of العلیم? The One who knows everything. So السمیع العلیم is the One who hears everything and knows everything.

Can you and I hear the Shaytan when he whispers to us? When he pokes us, prods us, and tempts us, can we hear him speak? We cannot. But السمیع can hear. You and I cannot hear. Even though a Shaytan, a Jinn, is whispering to us, we cannot directly hear anything. The mental thought of that evil he is prodding us with comes into our minds. The evil thought he is blowing into us comes into our minds. But we do not actually hear him speaking. A السمیع, however, can hear him in the very act. So when we say:

أعوذ باللہ السمیع

we acknowledge that O Allah, I cannot hear Shaytan, but YOU CAN, because You are السمیع, and that is why YOU can protect me when Shaytan whispers to me.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
And then we say العلیم, because Allah knows everything. What does He know in this case? He knows the level of our sincerity, our اخلاص. He knows whether, when we recite the أستعاذہ, we are saying it with sincerity, or whether it is merely a parroted phrase that rolls off the tongue without any comprehension or any intention of actually seeking His protection. Allah العلیم knows whether we truly intend to turn toward Him for protection or not, because He knows what is in our heart. He knows whether we truly want to submit ourselves before His majesty, or whether we are just saying it for the sake of saying it. And only when the علیم finds us to be sincere does the سمیع protect us from the whispers of Shaytan.

Therefore, when we recite the أستعاذہ, we should make sure we say it sincerely, and with the intention of actually seeking Allah's protection. We should not make these merely parroted phrases that roll off our tongues without meaning. The need for His protection must come from the heart, with sincerity, because He is السمیع العلیم.

Now, why do we recite the أستعاذہ BEFORE we begin reciting the Quran, or even before reciting the Basmallah?

The reason is that any time we need to create something new, we must first take apart and clear away what is already there. If you need to put up a new building, you have to bring down the existing structure, clean out the rubble, remove the old foundation, and even level the land out. Only then can new construction begin. Similarly, before we recite the Quran, we cleanse our heart, we purify our intentions, and we humble ourselves before Allah — by accepting our weakness, by accepting our incapabilities, by admitting our need for His protection, and by accepting His ultimate power over us. We completely submit ourselves to Him. We admit to Allah that O Allah, I am weak, I am helpless, and I am turning to You for YOUR help and YOUR protection, because I lack the capability and the capacity to protect myself against the temptations and whispers of Shaytan.

Another reason is that we use the أستعاذہ to purify our tongues. We use it to purify our speech from the filth of anything and everything inappropriate that we might have said earlier. It is like performing wudu before the salaah.

in which we first empty the filth out of our bodies and cleanse ourselves before we stand before Allah in prayer. The أستعاذہ is the same. It is the wudu of our tongue. We wish to cleanse ourselves of the evil and the filth of Shaytan AlRajeem: his teachings, his whispers, his notions, his proddings. We want to cleanse our hearts of all of that, right before we mention the glorious name and attributes of Allah AWJ. We want to empty the cups of our hearts so that they may be filled again with what Allah is about to give us, especially during the salaah.

Now, why do we recite the أستعاذہ specifically before reciting the Quran? The answer is that Allah commanded us to do so.

فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

When you begin reciting the Quran, seek the refuge of Allah from Shaytan AlRajeem.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
So the first reason is obedience. But why did Allah give us such a command? Because Shaytan can corrupt and contaminate our understanding of the message of the Quran. And how does he do that? He does it by interpreting the wrong meanings of the ayats for us. Through Qiyaas. Through induction and deduction. We, especially as Sulemanis, do not use our own logic when interpreting the Quran. We follow the interpretations prescribed by Maulana Ali and the Aimma Tahireen from his progeny. Now, why is that? It seems counterintuitive. Why can I not use my own logic? Because when you and I use our logic, it will always rest upon the information we currently have access to, mixed in with our experiential biases. And then, as the information changes, our logical deduction will change to accommodate the new information.

Let me give you an example. You see the still image of a video in which a black man is pushing or shoving an old lady. From the still image you can tell that he is pushing the old lady quite hard, because she is almost flying through the air. Now mix that in with any negative experiential bias you may have about black people, and you reach a certain negative conclusion based on this information. Now, if you rewind the film, you see that a man is trying to haul a huge piano up to the window of his apartment on the fourth floor. The rope attached to the piano snaps. This black man sees the rope snapping. He rushes toward the old lady, who was standing under the piano, pushes her out of the way, and saves her life. Now, with access to this new set of data, our conclusion about the black man changes. So what changed? Our view of the big picture. When we saw only the still image of the man pushing the old lady, we reached one conclusion. When we zoomed out and gained access to the unseen, we reached a different conclusion.

So the only possibility, the only situation in which we can make a perfect logical deduction, is when we have access to ALL the information: what we can see and what we cannot see. And also when that information is not contaminated by our experiential biases. ONLY then are we able to make an accurate logical deduction. When we have all the content placed within the complete context, only then can we produce accurate logical deductions.

Now, if you study the Quran, you will find that it always delivers the content. But what does it NEVER provide? The context. The ayah states what Allah commands Rasul Allah (SWS) to say, but it does not describe the surrounding situations. It does not say

that Rasul Allah (SWS) was standing in the marketplace, that it was daytime, that the sun was shining bright, that a bedouin came to Rasul Allah (SWS) and asked this question, and that these were the conditions of that person when he asked it — and that now, on the basis of all this information, the following command is being issued, and that, if you notice, this command also applies in the following twenty scenarios. The Quran does not do that. The Quran simply issues the command.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
Content versus context. But what did we just say is the most important thing for content? Context. Content placed outside its context is disastrous. So where can we obtain that complete context in which the content is to be placed? The Imams are the only ones who can supply the complete context of the Quran — not only from what can be seen, but also from what cannot be seen; not only within the physical context, but within the spiritual context as well. Why? Because they have access to all the information, and their interpretations are not polluted by experiential biases. Therefore only they know the true interpretations of these ayats, interpretations that balance perfectly on both scales, the physical and the spiritual. And when this content is placed in its proper context, the essential goal and purpose of Islam is achieved, which is peace.

What Shaytan does is the opposite. He draws logical conclusions from incomplete context and mixes them with experiential biases, and the result is chaos and destruction. We see examples of this all around us. Many Muslims, misled by the whisperings of Shaytan and analyzing content out of context, take the very ayats that are meant to promote peace and tranquility and use them to promote violence and terror. And that is only one area. There are many, many other areas of the Quran in which Shaytan has been very successful in corrupting the thought process of mankind. And why does he do it? Why does he prod us, why does he whisper to us, so that we arrive at these inconclusive and inaccurate deductions? Because that is exactly what he did himself. InshaAllah we will speak about this when we speak about Iblees.

So now we know the purpose of the command that Allah issued in the Quran:

فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

Therefore, through our أستعاذہ we seek Allah's protection from the cursed Shaytan, so that he may not corrupt our understanding or contaminate our concepts of the message of the Quran. We say أعوذ باللہ to show Allah our sincerity: O Allah, we wish to seek guidance from Your message. O Allah, I want this book to help me on the straight path, on Sirat AlMustaqeem. I do not want to be deluded and deceived by Shaytan into straying from Your straight path. I do not want him to stand between me and Your guidance. Because only You can protect me from him, for You are السمیع العلیم. And once I have surrendered myself into Your protection, no harm can reach me from any Shaytan, however powerful he may be in his whispers, his proddings, and his machinations. Because now I have You to protect me from my greatest enemy, Shaytan AlRajeem.

And how do we know that he is our worst enemy? And why do we need Allah's protection? Because, in the words of the Quran, Iblees promised Allah that he would misguide each and every one of us. He said to Allah:

قَالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

I swear by Your might, O Allah, I will make it my work.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
I will make it my only purpose in life to misguide each and every one of Your creation. لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ He made this promise to Allah. Imagine that. Just imagine the hatred and the enmity in his words. O Allah, I promise You that I will misguide them. I will deceive them. But even Iblees had to add a clause. Even he had to add a disclaimer to his promise. He said: I will misguide each and every one of Your slaves, إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ except the slaves whom You have chosen. Except the slaves who turn to You sincerely, with Ikhlaas. Those I will not be able to misguide.

So through the أستعاذہ, by reciting أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم, we reach out to Allah, who is السمیع العلیم, and we beg Him to make us among His chosen ones. To make us among those whom He protects, and among those over whom Iblees has no control.

Linguistics of Shaytan

Now that we have spoken about seeking the protection of Allah, let us understand whom we are seeking protection from. We are seeking protection from the cursed Shaytan: أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم. So let us look at this word Shaytan. The very first thing to understand is that Shaytan is not the name of a person. There is no being named Shaytan. Shaytan is an adjective. It is a word that describes the traits of a being. It is not a proper noun. You cannot name a child Shaytan. First name Shaytan, last name Rajeem — you cannot do that. You may call a child a Shaytan when he sets fire to the living room of the host who invited you over for dinner, but you cannot name a child Shaytan.

Now, linguistically speaking, the word Shaytan has several meanings. The word Shaytan comes from the root word Shatana, which means "that which is far removed." A Shaytan is someone who is far removed from Allah's mercy, from Allah's rehma. He is far removed from righteousness. He is far removed from piety. He is far removed from the straight path. He is far removed from الصراط المستقیم. In Urdu we say دھتکارا ہوا. There is also another word in Arabic that carries the same meaning: لعنۃ, which means "removal from Allah's mercy." When we speak about Shaytan, and also about the tyrants of history who harmed the people of truth, we say لعنۃ اللہ علیھم, which means: may they be far removed from the mercy of Allah. This is the worst thing that could be said about anyone within the realm of Islam. This is the ultimate curse that we as Muslims can place upon someone, so we should be very careful when we use this word. It is a common practice, especially in our jamaat, to use this word لعنۃ very casually. We should be very careful, and we should truly understand what it means before we say it.

So anyone who displays these traits of being far removed from Allah's mercy is called a Shaytan.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
From the same root word you have شَطَنْ, which means rope. Why? Because Shaytan ties us and binds us with the ropes of desires and temptations. He binds us with the ropes and chains of desires, and emotionally and spiritually we feel trapped in those desires. He also traps us in hatred, in enmity, in contempt, in pride, and in jealousies, and we cannot escape from that place. We know that what we are doing is wrong — wrong spiritually, morally, and ethically — but it is almost as though our desires and temptations have bound us and we simply cannot help ourselves. That is شَطَنْ.

That is why he is called Shaytan. Therefore anyone who tempts us, who urges us toward evil, who binds us with the ropes of desires and temptations, of envy, of contempt, of jealousy — the adjective Shaytan applies to that person as well.

Shatan also means one who is consumed with rage. So the adjective Shaytan applies as well to a person who falls into a state of insane fury and loses all control of himself. Such a person too is a strong candidate for the title of Shaytan.

Another meaning is that of a coward. This is because Shaytan always works in the shadows. He never presents himself openly as an enemy. He attacks from behind, and when he does come from the front, he pretends to be a friend. He pretends that he cares, that he is appreciative, that he is loving, while all the while he harbors hatred and enmity in his heart against the very person he is dealing with. Therefore the adjective Shaytan applies to people with such qualities as well.

So the first thing to understand is that Shaytan is a very general term. It is an adjective, and it applies to any being, أنس or جن, man or spirit. Am I then saying that there are shayateen among human beings? I am saying exactly that. Those human beings who are far removed from the mercy and blessings of Allah, those who are far removed from the straight path, those who strive hard to pull others off the straight path as well, those who bind others with the ropes of desires and temptations, those who are consumed with rage, those who provoke others to the point of rage, those who are cowards and lack the courage to face someone with the truth but instead attack in the shadows or behind their backs — whether they are men or women, whatever their outward manners, whatever their outward display of piety, whatever their visible display of love and affection and sincerity, they are all called Shayateen. Anyone who prevents us from worshipping Allah, anyone who calls us to worship an entity other than Allah, through his various schemes, temptations, and desires — they are all among the شیاطین الانس والجن.

So Shaytan is not the name of an individual. That name is Iblees, who is the leader and king of all Shayateen. Iblees is a proper noun. Iblees is the name of an actual being; he is the leader. Shaytan is a general term that applies to all of his followers. Do you understand? Iblees is the master, the leader, and all his disciples and followers, whether they are from among human beings or Jinns, are called Shayateen.

Linguistics of Jinn

Now let us speak about the Jinn. What is a jinn? The word Jinn literally means that which is hidden, veiled, or concealed.
body.topic_title_ur: ISTIAAZA: I seek refuge from Shaytan

body.text_en:
قال الله تعالى ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل ، فإذا قال العبد الحمد لله رب العالمين ، قال الله تعالى حمدني عبدي ، وإذا قال الرحمن الرحيم ، قال الله تعالى أثنى علي عبدي ، وإذا قال مالك يوم الدين ، قال مجدني عبدي ، وقال مرة فوض إلي عبدي ، فإذا قال إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين ، قال هذا بيني وبين عبدي ولعبدي ما سأل ، فإذا قال اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ، صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ، غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين ، قال هذا لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل . وفي رواية ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ، فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي )

الشُّکرُ عِندَ الرَّخاَء؛ وَالصَّبرُ عِندَ البَلاء ؛ وَ رَّضَا بِمُرِّ القَضَاء ؛ وَ صِّدقُ فِی مَوَاتِنِ الِّقَاء؛ وَ تَرکُ الشَّمَاتَۃِ بِالمُصِیبَۃِ اِذا حَلَّتْ بِالأَعدَاء

Gratitude for blessings; patience for trials; to not show my back during a fight; to not be pleased at the suffering of an enemy

أنا اوصیک بخمس لِیُکَمِّلُ اللہ خصال الخیر کلہ۔ لا تَبنُ ما لا تَسکُنُون ؛ و لا تَجمعُ ما لا تأکلون ؛ وَاتَّقُو اللہَ اَلَّذِی الیہِ تُخشَرُون ؛ لا تَنَافَسُ فِی مَا غَدَاً عَنہُ تَزُولُون ؛ وَرْغَبُ فِی مَا غَدَاً اِلَیہِ تَسِیرُونَ وَ فِیہِ تَخْلُدُونْ

کُلُّ دار وَ اِن طاَلَت سَلامَتُھَا؛ يَوماً أَن يَكونُ هُناَكَ أي شيء وَلٰكِن بَيتُ العَنكَبُوت وَ البَردِ الرِّیَاح

Abandonment is the fate of every house... No matter how much you try to preserve a house... one day there will be nothing in it except spider webs... and the sounds of chilly winds....

Do not build huge houses where you will not live; do not gather what you will not consume; fear the lord before whom you will have to stand one day; do not have greed for the world that you will have to leave one day; and be eager to enter paradise where you will live for eternity,

کونوا فی الدّنیا أضیافا، و اتّخذوا المساجد بیوتا، عوّدوا قلوبکم الرّقّه و أکثروا التّفکر و البکاء و لا تختلفنّ بکم الأهواء تبنون ما لا تسکنون و تجمعون ما لا تأکلون و تأملون ما لا تدرکون.

اللهم أنت أحق من ذكر، وأحق من عبد، وأنصر من ابتغى، وأرأف من ملك، وأجود من سئل، وأوسع من أعطى، أنت الـملك لا شريك لك، والفرد لا ند لك، كل شيء هالك إلا وجهك، لن تطاع إلا بإذنك، ولن تعصى إلا بعلمك، تطاع فتشكر، وتُعصى فتغفر، أقرب شهيد، وأدنى حفيظ، حلت بين النفوس، وأخذت بالنواصي، وكتبت الآثار، ونسخت الآجال، القلوب لك مفضية، والسر عندك علانية، الحلال ما أحللت، والحرام ما حرمت، والدين ما شرعت، والأمر ما قضيت، الخلق خلقك، والعباد عبيدك، وأنت الله الرؤوف الرحيم، أغفر لعبدك ما علمت، ولا تهتك ما سترت، أرحمه بقدرتك عليه، وأرحمه في يوم العرض عليك، ذل مقامه بين يديك، اللهم إنك عفو كريم تحب العفو فأعفو عن عبدك

Everything I say has been validated by Javeed bhai. There are two allegations. The first is that I am teaching concepts that do not belong to our Sulemani sect, because the things I am sharing are not from our books. The second is that, in teaching these "non-Sulemani" concepts, I am quoting Islamic scholars and lectures from YouTube. Someone from this group heard a video online and told Javeed bhai that I am repeating what was said on that video, word for word. So, in essence, I am presenting something that is not mine, and perhaps even taking credit for the work of others.

Very well. Let us address these concerns. Let us begin with this: am I doing this? Absolutely! I absolutely am.

There is a concern that I feel we need to address. The first part of it is plagiarism, and the other is the authenticity of the material. The concern is this: is the material I am sharing authentic? Some of you feel that the material is not authentic because its source is not our dawat books. And the other matter appears to be my quoting these scholars word for word.

I believe I have been more than clear about all of this on several occasions. I have stated it openly in these sessions. I have also said it individually to those of you who have spoken to me. I said that none of this is of my own hard work. I am standing tall on the shoulders of many great Islamic scholars who have researched this amazing work. Have you not heard me say this before? Because I remember saying all of this very clearly.

But if it was not clear enough, I will say it again. Everything I have shared in these sessions comes from the studies and research that various Islamic scholars have done over the years. Everything I have taught you is available on the internet, on YouTube, and in books. It is all there. I took their work. I validated the content with my elders. I ran all of this through Javeed bhai, to make certain that these concepts align with our Sulemani beliefs. I took what was right and I discarded what was wrong. And then I organized all this beautiful material in a systematic order. I organized it under the umbrella of Surah AlFateha, because this surah has the most perfect progression in its ayats. And I did this so that it becomes easier for the children to absorb this information. I have spent a decade learning and filtering this beautiful material on the Quran, and I wanted to share it with my children so that they do not have to spend a decade doing the same hard work. I wanted to make it easy for all of you to appreciate the Quran.

Now, is any of this news to you? Are you hearing me say this for the first time today? Of course not. I have said it several times.

As for my quoting the material word for word, I most certainly do that. And what of it? If the way in which this material was originally presented, if that style is so beautiful, why would I want to change any of it? English is not my first language. If someone who is proficient in English states something beautifully and eloquently, why should I not use his words? The only time it would make sense for me to change those words is if I can present the matter in a better way. And when I feel that I can, I do use my own words; when I feel that I cannot, I use the original words. So? What is wrong with that?

Now, as for the authenticity of the material.

So the thought underneath it seems to be this: because this material does not come from our own books, it cannot be authentic. But how do you know that? Have you studied all of our books? How do you know that none of this is in them? Where do you suppose all these Islamic scholars obtained this information? Everything I have shared is present in the works of Imam Jafar as-Sadiq and Imam Baqir, and in the sayings of Maulana Ali in Nahj al-Balagha. Maulana Ali says: not a single word of truth has ever been spoken except that it has come from us. Suppose I entertain you by singing a song for you, a song made famous by a well-known singer. Will I not use the very same words? Will I not sing it in the very same tune? But what was my intention? To entertain you. Was it not? So what if I make use of the research of Islamic scholars? So what if I quote them word for word? The purpose is that all of us should draw nearer to Allah and to Islam. Is that not so? If I quote a beautiful saying or a proverb, will I not use the same beautiful words in which it was first spoken? Hazrat Sahab constantly uses the poetry of famous Muslims and non-Muslims in his majalis. Is he then guilty of plagiarism? And should I turn knowledge away merely because a non-Sulemani Islamic scholar carried out the research? Since when did we hold the exclusive rights to Islam? When did that happen? Since when did we become the exclusive owners of the Quran? I always understood that Islam belongs to all Muslims. Since when did we become the only Muslims? If I see the sun in the sky, does it now belong to me alone? The beauty of Islam and its teachings belong to me exactly as much as they belong to any other Muslim. They belong to me exactly as much as they belong to non-Muslims. This is the true beauty of Islam. This is the real beauty of the Quran. It invites with open arms.

Now, you young people must have heard your elders say to you again and again: Hazrat Sahab says that you should not study material belonging to non-Sulemani Muslims; you should study only our own material, from our own books. Have you heard that before? It is true. Hazrat Sahab did say it. But have you ever inquired into the context? In what context does Hazrat Sahab say it? Why does he forbid us to do this? Have you ever asked that question? It is a very important question, because content taken out of context is disastrous. We all know that. So what is the context in which the elders say this?

The difficulty with Islamic research and with Islamic scholars is that the good in it is mixed together with the bad. Some of their knowledge is factual, and some of it rests upon Qiyaas, that is, deduction, which may be right and may be wrong. Our duaat, on the other hand, speak through inspiration from the Imams, which is called Taedaat. Their words are therefore free of error, and they agree perfectly with the Quran and the Sunnah. When you accept the philosophies of Muslim scholars wholesale, you take in the good along with the bad, and you end in a state of conflict, because you cannot reconcile everything that is said. They do not possess the concepts of taveel, mabda, maad, haqaiq, and so on, and this sets up a roadblock in our spiritual progress. That is why our elders discourage us from studying outside uloom FIRST. That is the key word, and it is always the one that gets skipped over. They never said: do not study non-Sulemani scholars.

What our elders have always said is this: study our various branches of knowledge FIRST, and once you have gained a command of our correct principles, then go out and study whomever you wish. Islam, Christianity, Hinduism — study whatever you want, and you will be fine. Why? Because you will see that what they have is nothing in comparison to what we have. But no elder EVER said: never study anything outside our sect.

And in light of that, what did I do? I studied our concepts first and gained a sound understanding of them. Then I went out and researched these other Islamic scholars. I took what they had to say, validated it, authenticated it, and filtered it. And now, with the permission of the elders, I am sharing the knowledge of this beautiful Qur'an with you. Everything I share in the sessions I first confirm once more with Javeed bhai immediately before the session, simply to make certain that it meets with his approval.

Do you know what the difference is between a sect and a cult? A cult is a privileged group that follows its own philosophies and rejects everything outside those philosophies. That is a cult. A sect is a privileged group that follows its own philosophies but remains open to the truth from outside as well. A sect does not reject the truth, no matter where it comes from. That is the difference between a sect and a cult. Is Sulemaniyat a sect, or is Sulemaniyat a cult?

Do you even know why we are called Sulemanis? Because we are followers of Syedna Suleman. But what does the word Suleman mean? Do you know? Suleman comes from the root word salama, which means peace. And do you know what other word comes from the same root? Islam. Suleman means "Man of peace." Islam means peace. Therefore Suleman means Man of Islam. Syedna Suleman was a man who was a living embodiment of Islam. We are Sulemanis, which means that we too should be followers of Islam, followers of peace.

I openly challenge anyone in the group to step forward and tell me one thing I have shared that goes against our teachings. One single thing I have said. I openly challenge anyone in this group. Every truth I have shared with you aligns perfectly with our realities.

Tell me something. We have books written by the duaat on medicine — did you know that? There are a great many books on علم الابدان and on علم الحساب, and again, all of them come from the works of Imam Jafar AsSadiq and Maulana Baqar AS. So if you are such true Sulemanis, and hazrat sahab has forbidden outside knowledge, why do you go to medical school? Simply study the books of the duaat on medicine. Why study mathematics in school? It is because the truth is always the truth, no matter who states it.

And I personally do not belong to the Sulemani Cult. I belong to the Sulemani Sect, and therefore I am open to the truth, because I am a follower of Maulana Ali, the one who said: العم ضال المؤمن — knowledge is the lost she-camel of a believer. If an outsider brings me my lost camel, will I reject it because the man bringing it to me is an outsider? And the same Maulana Ali said:

ولا انظر من قال ۔۔۔ انظر ما قال

Do not look at who is saying it; look at what is being said.

Do not look at who is saying it; look at what he is saying.

ولا انظر من نجح ؛ انظر کیف نجح

Do not look at who succeeded; look at how he succeeded.

And who is saying this? The one whom Rasul Allah called باب العلم, the door to the city of knowledge.

he is saying this... انا مدینۃ العلم و علی بابھا — I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its door. What have I shared with you that seems wrong to you? I told you that the Quran is symmetrical. Do you not see that with your own eyes? You need a quotation from our books? How do you know that there is not one? There are numerous, numerous books on the miracles of the Quran. Just because you have not read them does not mean that they do not exist. I am sharing with you the linguistic analysis of these Quranic words, so that you may appreciate the beauty of the Quran. Why do you care who said it? What the source is? Is the fact that it is validated by my teacher not enough for you?

Oh, and it was also said: if I am quoting from these Islamic scholars, then why do we need him? We can do it ourselves. We do not need Asif for that. You know what — you are absolutely right! Please go ahead and research all of this for yourself. Everything I have shared with you is available on YouTube and on the internet. Knock yourself out. Go through all of it and sift the wrong from the right. I make no claims upon this knowledge. You do not need me to do this. MashaAllah — more power to you! May Allah be with you and guide you. I will send you the links.

Look, my friends: I am not doing this to be praised. I am not doing this for a salary. I am gaining nothing out of this. None of this is mine. All of this belongs to Allah, and to the uloom and the knowledge of the Ayma Tahireen. Islam is their property, not mine. I am nothing. I am nobody. Allah does not need me for this. Allah needs nobody for this. So I hold no delusions of grandeur about these sessions. I am only a humble slave of my elders. I found something beautiful that changed my life, and I had the desire to share it with those I love. That is all this is. And I am more than happy to stop right now.

So you decide what you want to do. If you do not feel comfortable with what I am doing, you do not have to be here. If you wish to be humble and to learn, then you are most welcome. But if you are in my sessions only to judge me and to accuse me of plagiarism — you know what, you are still welcome in these sessions. Perhaps in the midst of your judgments you may learn something that brings you closer to Allah, InshaAllah.

I have stated everything as clearly as I can. But this is it. I am not going to have this conversation again. If you feel that you do not wish to continue, no offense is taken. Wallahi, no offense is taken whatsoever. May Allah create for you sources far better than me. These sessions are not about me; they are about you!

Gift — Hadiya

Now let us speak about the word انعمت. The word *anamta* comes from the word نعمۃ, which means gift. Now, what are the two greatest gifts that Allah has given to every human being, in both a physical and a spiritual sense? They are the heart and the intellect. Allah gave these two gifts to all human beings.

Now, what was the purpose of these gifts? The purpose of these gifts was that human beings would use their intellect and their heart to arrive at the conclusion that there is indeed an Allah — glorious and magnificent, to whom gratitude and praise must be given, and who is intensely and exceedingly loving and caring — and that there must be a Day of Judgment, on which a balance will be struck between life on this earth and the life to come. These three realizations would lead human beings to the conclusion that they wish to give themselves up as servants to Allah. And once they do so, they stand in need of His guidance. These, then, are the conclusions that a person is meant to reach by using the two gifts that Allah gave him: the heart and the intellect. This is the conclusion that every human being is meant to reach entirely on his own, by means of the two original gifts that Allah gave him, for he is meant to reflect upon the creation of this universe by means of these two gifts, as Allah says:

إِنَّ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱخْتِلَفِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ لَآيَتٍۢ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَبِ

There can be no doubt about it: especially in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and especially in the striving between night and day — the conflict that takes place between night and day — there are signs for people of intellect. What are these conflicts of which Allah speaks? By day it is bright, and by night it is dark. As the day advances, the daylight begins to prevail over the darkness. And then, as the day draws to its close, the darkness begins to prevail over the light. The sun turns from bright yellow to orange, and the sky turns from bright blue to deep blue, until it becomes wholly black, and night at last wins out.

‏وَٱلَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ

I swear by the night and by all that it enfolds.

And then that full black night begins to lose its own battle with the day. And what happens? The sky grows brighter and brighter and brighter, until it is daylight once more and every trace of the night has been erased. And this battle continues, every single day. Allah says: especially in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and especially in the battle between the night and the day. In these two things there are many, many miraculous signs — for people who possess pure minds.

اولو الاباب — people of sound minds.
