body.text_en:
Let us begin by first understanding what these minds mean: what *uloo albaab* means. Who are these people of pure and sound minds? For if we are not people of pure and sound minds, then there are truly no miraculous signs for us in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and no miraculous sign for us in the conflict between night and day. For these things are observed by everyone in the world. But does everyone see the miraculous signs within them? No, they do not. And why is that? Because they do not meet the requirement of this verse — because they do not possess sound minds.

الُّب عَقلُ صَالحٌ ؛ خالصٌ من الشَّوائب

A clean mind is one that is not polluted by useless things; that is the definition of the word *Lubb*. A person whose thoughts are not polluted by useless things — a person who truly thinks about things that carry meaning.

This mind that Allah gave us is in truth a very powerful gift. Its capacity is extraordinary. You can commit whole books to memory. You can store staggering amounts of data. There are people who, when they set their minds to something, become extraordinarily knowledgeable in the very field on which they have concentrated. Tune in to ESPN, for example, and there are commentators who can recite sports statistics from fifty years ago, all of it off the top of their heads. They know the names of the athletes, how long each career lasted, which teams a man played for, which college he attended, the year he was drafted, who drafted him, how many championship rings he holds, when he was injured, when he was reinstated. My God, it is astonishing! These people set their minds to it, and they managed to store staggering amounts of data.

There are young children, twelve and thirteen years old, who take up a video game and can memorize every single complicated move it has. They begin playing a first-person shooter and can tell you every cheat code and every walk-through, reeling it all off from memory. There are people who become obsessed with television shows, people who become obsessed with fashion, some who become obsessed with the news, some with technology — which chip has just come out, which processor is being developed for the year 2080. Some become obsessed with cars. Are there not people exactly like this? This mind is an incredible thing. When you set your mind to something, you can truly do amazing things.

Now, this may be good material to know from a worldly point of view. On the strength of such information you can land a certain kind of job. But measured against our ultimate goal, is this useful knowledge? Is it something that will help us in the hereafter? It is not!

In this verse, then, Allah is telling us that there are people in this world who set their minds to all of this sort of thing. But then there are a very few who, rather than being distracted by one such pursuit — rather than taking this immensely powerful mind and spending all its muscle on something useless, like sports statistics or video-game data — instead turn their minds to matters you and I would not even consider. They stop and think about the skies, the earth, and how they were in fact created. And they begin to think about how there is a natural opposition between night and day.

body.text_en:
Consider an example. Your heart decides that you want to be a doctor. You want it. That is not rational; it is a desire. And because of the intensity of that desire, what do you then go on to study? Medicine. You will now exhaust your mind studying medicine, but the motivation behind it came from the heart. Your heart decided that you wanted to make your father proud. You wanted to help people. You wanted to make a difference in people's lives. You wanted to please Allah by serving His creation. Whatever that motivation was, it came from the heart. So what I am saying is that you will study hard because of what your heart desired. Your mind will exhaust itself on what you desire.

There are people, for example, who hate studying but love working out. They want to look a certain way. And in order to look a certain way, you have to learn something about nutrition. You have to learn something about exercise. You have to learn about good habits, and so on. So even those who hate studying, and biology and physiology in particular, will study some parts of physiology: the best time to eat what, how much protein and how much carbohydrate they need to consume, and at what time of day. Even they will learn all of that. Why? Because of their desire to look good, their desire to get lean, or whatever it may be. They will do it. In other words, your heart picks a direction, and then your mind focuses on it. That is why the heart comes first.

This is why remembrance comes first. Remembrance first, and then reflection upon the heavens and the earth.

I'll translate only the given part, following every rule.

So remember, I told you that people's minds are focused on the wrong sort of things. They are thinking about entertainment and video games and movies and things like that. But who is going to be thinking about the heavens and the earth? The one whose heart is focused on the remembrance of Allah.

Conclusion of the reflection. Now here is the epic part: رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَاطِلًۭا

So these people are thinking about the heavens and the earth, and after the reflection they reach a conclusion. And the conclusion is: Rabbana ma khalaqta haza batila. O Master, You did not create all of this without purpose. There is no way all of this is useless. There is no way all of this does not have meaning. When something has meaning, what is it called? When something has meaning and value and purpose, what is it called? It is called an ayah. So this person realizes that everything around him is a sign. It is an ayah. SubhanAllah.

This has to have some meaning. This has to have some purpose. All of this did not just come here for no reason. I am not here for no reason. I am far too intricate. I am far too involved. I have far too many gifts. I am far too advanced a creation to just exist without any purpose, out of an accident. There has to be something. There is no way that I can accept that I am here without a purpose. How can all of this around me have a purpose to serve me, yet I can exist without a purpose? That does not make sense to me. رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَاطِلًۭا. You did not create any of this without a purpose.

You know, there is this really interesting theory about games and sports. I am actually compelled by this theory. In any game there are certain rules. If you really understand those rules of the game and you abide by them, you will succeed. For example, basketball or cricket have fundamentals. If you get really good at the fundamentals, you will definitely succeed. And then you can add your own creativity above and beyond that. A video game has certain fundamentals. Once you learn the basic moves, you can advance and then learn the more complicated moves. And you can try more creative things and succeed. So if you simply follow the rules, you can get game points, trophies, one hundred percent synchronizations. So, you know, in video games there are these things that you can do, and if you do them properly you can actually synchronize your character up to one hundred percent. And now they can do everything that is possible at the maximum level. So they give you a sense of accomplishment. Why do you think people are obsessed with trophies? Are these trophies worth any money, especially within video games? Is one hundred percent synchronization going to make your couch more comfortable? Is anything valuable actually going to happen? No! Then why is it that we become so obsessed with these things when we are playing video games? It is very interesting psychology. And the psychology that is offered behind it is that in this life there are no set rules. In other words, somebody can work really hard in life and still not win. Does that happen? Absolutely. And somebody does not work hard at all and they win the lottery. That happens too. So it seems like this life is unfair. And even if you play by the rules, you will not necessarily get a trophy, and you will not necessarily get points. And it does not feel good to work hard and not get something in return. So we tend to turn toward a mechanism.

To a world in which there are six rules. And if you simply abide by those rules, you will surely earn points. You will surely win trophies. That will certainly happen, as long as you follow the rules. But does it work that way outside of the game? If you study very hard, if you go to school every single day, will you surely get a good job? Will you surely make it into the college you always wanted to attend? Will you surely earn the money you dreamed of earning? Is anything in life certain? No. Human beings love certainty. In our very conscience, we love having certainty. We love games. Because what do games give us? They give us certainty. If I do this, and this, and this, then I will surely win. I will surely be ranked higher. I will surely have more and more and more. We hate the notion that this life holds no certainties, no guarantees. And so we love to lose ourselves in a world that does give us some guarantee. Remarkable, is it not? And all of this is from the perspective of a disbeliever.

body.text_en:
Do you know what is even more remarkable? That from the perspective of a believer, there are guarantees in this world. Every single thing you do will be repaid. If you follow the rules that have been laid down, you will receive a trophy. You will receive points. You will receive a higher rank. Nothing you do in this world goes unpaid, unrewarded. There is most certainly a point system in place, and you are in this game of life. It is astonishing that the Qur'an says this life is nothing but a game.

وَمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا لَعِبٌۭ

Worldly life is nothing but a game. And in a game, what must you do? Follow the rules and try to win. Earn points. In a certain sense, that is exactly what we are trying to do. For a disbeliever, is there a point system? No. For us, is there a point system? Absolutely. And if we can truly grasp this — if we are truly devoted to this point system, this game that Allah has created for us — then we come to realize that we have no time for the other games. Because we are engaged in something with far higher stakes. Far higher points. SubhanAllah.

You did not create this without purpose. There is no way that You gave me this life and all my experiences, and yet none of them are worth anything. That they are worth no points. That I must go elsewhere and try to earn false points.

رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَطِلًۭا

Subhanak, You are far above that. Subhanak. You are too perfect for that — to create something without purpose.

That leads us to reflect: how could it be that I was created without a purpose? Only consider that. It is an astonishing realization. That everything in this universe, beneath the heavens and the earth — in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day — if all of this has as its ultimate purpose to serve me, then would I not have a purpose myself? Was I created merely to enjoy all of this, with no genuine ultimate goal? That makes no sense. Which means that I do indeed have a goal and a purpose. And that raises the next question: what is that goal? What is that purpose?

Now let us carry the analogy of that video game a little further. Suppose you are playing a game that has no end goal. Imagine it is a free, open world — a completely free, open world. Have you ever had this experience when you beat a video game, when you complete the final stage, and it simply lets you wander about? You have all your powers, because you have reached one hundred percent synchronization.

body.text_en:
But now that you have completed the game, you can simply roam around without any further purpose. You can do whatever you want. Is it as enjoyable as it was when you were actually playing the game, when you actually had an end goal in mind? No, it is not. You may have some fun for a little while, but do you know what you are going to do before long? Before long, what are you going to do? You are going to stop playing that game. You will lose interest. Why? There are no points anymore. There is no goal anymore. There are no trophies to win. There is no sense of accomplishment anymore. There is no sense of adventure anymore. All of it is gone. So eventually, what do you do? You quit.

There are people in this world who, when they begin to believe that there is no greater purpose to this life, that there are no more points, that life has no meaning — guess what comes next? They kill themselves. They get married. No, I am joking. And even if they do not give up on their lives, they live a very sad and miserable life of depression. It is a very sad way to live.

So the person arrives at the conclusion: you are far too exalted to create anything without a purpose. So now what? فقنا عذاب النار. Protect us from the fire of hell. In other words, do not let us lose in this game of life. We cannot afford to lose. So now you realize that this is about points, and this is about fulfilling a purpose. So if you do not fulfill that purpose, there is going to be a punishment.

What is that purpose of life? وما خلقت الجن و الانس الا لعبدونِ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ Master, whoever You enter into the fire has been humiliated. O Allah, whoever did not use Your gifts, who did not use his heart and his intellect to reflect on the universe and draw closer to You, who did not play this game of life, and who did not accomplish the purpose of this life, who did not win points and did not win trophies, and who became the loser in the afterlife, and entered Your hell — he is the one who has been truly humiliated.

This is the conclusion that all of us have to reach all by ourselves. Faith is not something that can be given to you by your parents. Faith is not something that can be given to you by your teachers. It has to come from your own heart and your own intellect. You have to believe for yourself.

body.text_en:
There is no taqleed in aqeedah. There is no imitation in creed. Rather, there is no blind imitation in creed. You cannot actually blindly follow anyone when it comes to being convinced. You will have to reach your own conviction, and that is of absolute importance. If the only reason you are a Muslim is because your parents are Muslims, and you have not reached this conclusion yourself, for yourself, then that faith is artificial. And that faith will not provide the right kind of results. I do not know if we can even call it faith. You have to come to this conclusion. The reason we are going through these verses together is because I want all of us to reach this conclusion again. And what is that conclusion? رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَطِلًۭا Master, You did not create all of this in vain. We all have to reach this conclusion for ourselves all over again. You have to think about the skies and the earth for yourself. You have to think about the conflict between the night and the day for yourself. Not because I am telling you. I do this exercise only for myself, but you have to do it for yourself. You have to sit and ponder. You have to sit and reflect.

For yourself. And you must reinforce for yourself what it is that you believe. This is what the call of the Qur'an is. It asks people to reflect. It asks people to think. What a powerful religion this is. This is not a religion that says: Just believe! And if you do not believe, you are going to hell. This is a religion that says: Think about the sky, think about the earth. Think about the night and the day. Come to the realization that there has to be a purpose. And then hear the call of someone calling that aligns with the belief system you have come to conclude. رَّبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًۭا يُنَادِى لِلْإِيمَٰنِ أَنْ آمِنُوا۟ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَـَٔامَنَّا ۚ رَبَّنَا فَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَكَفِّرْ عَنَّا سَيِّـَٔاتِنَا وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ ٱلْأَبْرَارِ BOOM! Now you have belief. That is what you call faith.

body.text_en:
We have grown accustomed to wearing out our minds on useless things. So let us speak of what happens when a person begins to think about the heavens and the earth, and to reflect upon the night and the day.

When you think about the heavens, what you notice is this vast expanse of the universe, and how everything within it is bound to everything else so intricately, so delicately. Just consider this. We have a solar system of tremendous power. We have these enormous, enormous planets. Yet how delicately they are joined to one another. At the slightest imbalance, the whole structure collapses. And consider how it bears upon us as human beings. If something were to happen to the solar systems, who is eliminated? There is no life form on any of these planets, so far as we know. But if anything happens to this intricate balance among them, the earth is destroyed, and all life on earth is destroyed. And so the mind begins to think.

There must be someone who created these enormous structures and yet balanced them so delicately. Even if he created science as a tool, what a magnificent creation that tool is, holding everything in its proper place. Then, when he turns his mind to the skies, he thinks of the winds. The winds are a means by which the clouds travel. They are also a means by which dust and pollen travel. And what do the clouds bring? Water. Pollen is what quickens the earth, and from it we get plants. These plants need water, and the water comes from the clouds, and the clouds are carried by the winds. So the breeze that we feel upon our faces is in truth a delivery system for this planet. One of the ways in which life on this planet is sustained comes directly through the winds. Without the breeze, we would not in fact be able to experience life at all, because the plants that must receive the pollen would not receive it, which means the plants would not come forth, which means the animals would have nothing to eat. And even were the earth quickened through pollen, the plant would still not be able to grow without water. Consider how we mow our lawns and water the grass in our backyards. Now look at Allah's backyard. Who is watering all these plants? It is the winds. It is not us. It is simply being delivered through this delivery system that Allah created. And then these trees: they inhale carbon dioxide and exhale oxygen, which you and I are breathing. And all of this is because of the wind. Is it not remarkable how everything works together with everything else?

When we reflect upon this, we see that the winds have a very special relationship with the clouds and the pollen. The sky that rains has a very cooperative relationship with the earth. They are working together, constantly, to make life on this earth possible. If you look around and truly observe, you see that all of creation is in fact working in cooperation with the rest. Everything depends upon something else for its own existence, and together they bring about a higher purpose.

body.text_en:
And then you begin to think about the night and the day. Does the night have a purpose? Does the day have a purpose? Do we actually need night and day? We absolutely do. Do we need sunlight? Yes, we do. But do we also need the absence of sunlight? We do. What would happen if there were only sunlight? The plants would not grow, and we would have no restful sleep. We would suffer all manner of physical, biological, and psychological troubles, and emotional troubles as well. There is research about places that do not receive a great deal of sunlight, and those places have the highest rates of suicide and depression. Sunlight has a bearing upon our emotional state. So when we truly begin to think about the heavens and the earth, and the day and the night, we realize that we have a very personal relationship with these things. We are not independent of them. We are wholly dependent upon them.

Now let us think about this a little further. Human beings are the dominant species on this planet. Is that not true? Every other species, and every other thing on this planet, is being used by human beings in one way or another. The resources of this planet are being used by us. We are constantly drilling for things, extracting things from the earth. And as for the other animals upon this earth, we are either milking them, or eating them, or using their hide to make clothing.

The plants of this earth we use to draw out all kinds of chemicals and nutrients. Even the bark of trees we use for our building. The stones of this earth are used for our construction. Even the silicon of this earth is used for our technologies. The metals of this earth are what provide us with electricity — copper and all the rest. Nearly everything that exists on this earth, we have found a way to put to use so that it serves us human beings. Yet the very fact that we have learned how to use these things to serve ourselves ought to make us wonder. Did I actually invent copper? I may have invented copper fiber, but did I actually invent copper? I may have made a table and a chair, but did I actually invent wood? Whatever things I needed in order to make the advancements that I as a human being must make — the raw materials for them were already here, were they not?

A child can take credit for building a marvelous thing out of Legos. But what can he not take credit for? The Lego pieces. The child was given certain pieces to work with. Who provided those pieces? And how is it that these pieces fit together so well? When you look at the Lego masterpiece, the final result of the making, it is not so much the genius of the child who put it together. It is really the genius of the designer who designed these pieces so that they work so well with one another, enabling the child to create this final masterpiece. Is it not so?

When you begin to think in this way, we start to develop a certain appreciation for our Maker. And this kind of thinking makes us realize that everything on this earth is valuable and has a purpose. And if everything has a purpose, then all of these inanimate things have a purpose to serve me. All of them were created for the purpose of serving me.

body.text_en:
Now let us see what the word ayah means. It means a great many things. It carries the meaning of something valuable. خرج القوم بآیاتھم. An ayah is something valuable. An ayah is something that has purpose and meaning. This is why the word اِی in Arabic literally means "meaning" — it comes from the same origin. The word أَی in Arabic, which comes from the same origin, means to separate one thing from another, or to distinguish one thing from another. And from this word comes ayah, which means that every ayah is distinct. Every ayah has meaning, and every ayah has value.

The word ayah also means a sign. A sign is something that points to something else. The wind is a sign that life is being delivered. Life being delivered is a sign that I am being taken care of. And that is the sign that I am in fact not my own caretaker — that someone is providing for me. One sign leads to another sign, which leads to another sign, which leads to another sign. Something is pointing to something, which is then pointing to something, which is then pointing to something else. That is part of the meaning of ayah, because one ayah leads to another ayah, which leads to another ayah.

So Allah is saying that in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the changing of night and day, there is something valuable. There is something meaningful. There is a lesson of some kind. There is a reminder of some kind. There is an indication of some kind. There is a clue of some kind. For what kind of people? For people of sound minds. For people of pure minds. But if people's minds are filled with sports statistics.

And with video games, and junk, and trivial, useless information. If their minds are filled with such things, they will not see it. They will not see the larger picture. They will not see the forest for the trees. They will remain lost in the small details. They will not truly appreciate what is really happening.

Consider a man who is obsessed with the glossy paper of a book, and with its beautiful leather cover, and with the print of its letters. If that is all he fixes upon, he will never actually think about reading the book. He will not concern himself with gaining the knowledge that comes from reading it. Why? Because he is focused on the wrong thing. He is preoccupied with the outward features of the book rather than with the purpose of the book itself. He attends only to the paper, the cover, and the print, but not to the content of the book at all.

That is the difference between people who can appreciate an ayah and those who cannot. Both are looking at the same thing, but they are focused on the wrong thing. They do not see what it is actually saying.

body.text_en:
Such people know a great deal about it. There is a man who knows so much about paper that he can feel the paper of the Qur'an and say, "This paper came from a particular kind of tree; it is of such a density; these are the sorts of factories that produce it, which exist only in these countries; I can tell that this is so many years old." They can tell us a great deal about the paper. All of this, by the way, is fine knowledge. But does that knowledge actually help him get anything out of this book? Does he actually receive any guidance from the book? No.

These are the people who do not have sound minds. They do not have pure minds. Their minds are contaminated with all of these other unnecessary facts. They do have remarkable minds; it took a great deal of learning, time, and effort to absorb all of that information. But they put it to the wrong use. They applied all of that muscle to the wrong thing.

People of pure minds, however, are not merely clever. They have learned to focus on the right things, on the useful things. That is the key to the whole discussion: to focus on the right thing.

You will meet many clever people in your life—college professors, professionals, people at the top of their game. The problem will not be that they are not clever. The problem will be that they are focused on the wrong things. And if you keep company with such people long enough, guess what happens to you? You become focused on the wrong things too. And you become so focused on the wrong thing that when you finally speak with someone who is focused on the right thing, it simply feels strange. It feels out of place. It is like the friend who is focused on Minecraft, who says, "Why are you thinking about the sky and the earth? You should be thinking about Minecraft, and food, and movies."

So a very good analogy is given about people of sound mind. It is that if you eat a great deal of junk food and then throw in an apple once in a while, it does not really make a difference. That would not be a healthy diet, and you are not going to see the positive effects of the fruit eaten once a year, simply because your digestion is overwhelmed with foods that are unhealthy. Do you understand? So what happens is that if you are constantly taking in useless information.

And then, once in a while, you sit in a session like this one, where you are, one hopes, learning something positive, something beneficial. Even so, you will not necessarily see positive results. It will feel as though the lesson went in one year and out the other. Why? Because your mind is still fixed on the wrong kind of information.

body.text_en:
Some of you children are so absorbed in your cell phones, so addicted to them, that you are texting even during the sessions. You cannot help yourselves. The phone controls you, which is truly a sad thing. Consider it: here are dignified human beings, each given this astonishing faculty called the intellect. It is an incredible gift, capable of amazing things. And when this incredible gift is used only to play Candy Crush, that is a tragedy of the human mind. What a waste of such a marvelous gift. So even if you cannot give up entertainment and video games and movies altogether, at least try to cut them down significantly, so that you can actually use your mind for what it was created for. For something higher! For something more! For something like the Qur'an.

One of the greatest dangers we face in today's world is that entertainment has become a god. Our entire lives revolve around it, whether that is movies, video games, or simply having a good time. Now, none of this is bad in itself. But this constant need to be entertained takes over our lives, and then it controls us. We are no longer in control of it. For if you think about it, there is really no end to it. Your life will end, but the number of movies will never end. Your life will end, but the video games will keep coming. You will never have played them all. You will never have had every pleasure that is out there to be had. So it becomes a kind of bottomless pit. We grow so addicted to doing these things that we can never find a break to do what we were actually created to do. So many people waste their whole lives chasing this never-ending high, and their lives never amount to anything in the true sense. This is why being among the uloo Albaab, the people of sound mind, is so important!

Now, thinking is an intellectual activity, is it not? But the people of sound mind are described as having two parts. This is the next lesson I want you to understand. The Qur'an is concerned with your mind, and the Qur'an is concerned with your heart. I will say it again. The Qur'an is concerned with your mind, and the Qur'an is concerned with your heart. What are some of the things the mind does? The mind thinks. It processes information. It reaches conclusions. It analyzes. It tells your body what to do. It stores, remembers, memorizes, recalls, and learns new things. So the mind does a great many things, does it not?

According to the Qur'an, what does the heart do? Not the physical heart; all that does is pump blood. I am speaking of the spiritual heart. According to the Qur'an, the spiritual heart does several things. According to the Qur'an, the heart actually remembers. For remember, one of the meanings of qalb is a vessel, and the task of a vessel is to store its contents. The heart also cares. It loves. It hates. It feels emotions. The heart grows excited. It becomes motivated. According to the Qur'an, the heart is the seat of all the emotions. Every emotion is associated with the heart, in a spiritual sense, not in a neurological one.

The Qur'an Appeals to Heart and Mind

The Qur'an's argument is that it wants to appeal to your mind.

body.text_en:
Now, how does one appeal to a person's mind? How does one impress the mind? Through logic. Through evidence. Through proof. One must tell a person something convincing. I could deliver a deeply emotional speech and yet be entirely wrong. I could be thoroughly impassioned and still say something foolish, because I do not know what I am talking about. And so there are situations in which people speak with great emotion. They appeal to the heart, but what they say makes no sense. There is no appeal to the mind at all. If you wish to impress the mind, you must be reasonable. You must provide sound evidence. You must be coherent.

And how does one appeal to the heart? Through emotion. Anger, love, tenderness. When your mother embraces you and says, "I love you so much. Please be kind to your father," she is not being rational. What is she being? She is being emotional. She is appealing to your sense of feeling. She is appealing to your heart. And it works. This means that human beings are not merely intellectual creatures. They are also emotional creatures. We are not moved and motivated by reason alone. We are also moved by emotion. We are spiritual, emotional beings, and yet we are also reasonable and intellectual. We are not purely one or the other. We are not. We are not robots.

The example I can offer to draw this distinction between the heart and the mind is that of a young man who likes to smoke. He is a young man who greatly enjoys smoking, but he is also exceedingly intelligent. He scores a hundred in biology. And if he scores a hundred in biology, you may be certain that he knows smoking is terribly harmful. In fact, he understands this better than most people, because he has seen photographs of ruined lungs. He knows exactly what smoking does to the body, how many minutes it strips from one's life, and everything else besides. And yet, after scoring a hundred on the very examination about the biology of the lungs, what does he do the moment he steps outside the classroom? He smokes.

You must ask this young man, "Why do you smoke?" And the most common answer you will receive is, "I do not know. It simply feels good." "But do you not know that it is so harmful?" "Yes, I do. But whatever." Is "whatever" an intellectual response? Is it a reasonable, scientific answer? It is not. What is it? It is emotional. It feels good. My friends do it. It makes me look impressive. I believe I appear especially attractive when I smoke, because when people walk past me and nearly retch at the revolting stench of cigarettes, I take that to be a mark of true manhood.

body.text_en:
Something is at work in this young man's mind. Even the Surgeon General's warning printed on the side of the cigarette packet, which states plainly that smoking this thing will give you cancer, is still clearly not enough to keep this young man from smoking. Now the same boy goes home. He climbs the stairs to his room, shuts the door, lights a cigarette, and begins to smoke. Then he sees his father pull into the driveway. What does he do? He puts it out. He flushes it down the toilet, reaches for the air freshener, pops a mint, and fans the air frantically. The Surgeon General said he would get cancer, and that was not enough. But the father pulled into the driveway, and that was enough. The father has not even said a word yet. He does not even know what his son was doing. Nothing at all. So what, then, drove the boy to change his behavior? Fear? Respect? May I say that he was moved not by reason but by emotion? Do you understand? Sometimes you can know that something is wrong.

From an intellectual standpoint, you know it is wrong, and yet you do it anyway, only because it feels good, because the emotion is too strong. The Qur'an recognizes that you cannot change your life through reason alone. Your heart must also be won over. There are two parts to you. You see this in the verse where Allah wants us to reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, and on the alternation of night and day. All of that is a work of the intellect. But the heart needs help as well; the heart, too, must be cleansed. So who are these people of sound mind, these people who say:

ٱلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَمًۭا وَقُعُودًۭا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَطِلًۭا سُبْحَنَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ

According to the Qur'an, remembrance of Allah is an act of the heart. So they remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on their sides; in other words, they do something that helps make their heart stronger. And they reflect deeply, and they reflect much, upon the creation of the heavens and the earth. Reflection is an act of the mind. So half of the verse is about the heart, and the other half is about the mind, and you must work on both.

Now this is where we need to look at the matter in its historical context. Before Islam there were two nations that were exceedingly clever: the Israelites and the Christians, the Jews and the Christians. The Jews were exceedingly clever. But Allah said that their hearts grew hard. They were extremely intelligent and very learned, yet their hearts grew hard, because their hearts were empty of the remembrance of Allah. On the other hand, there were people whose hearts were very soft. They would weep all the time. They were so emotional, so loving, so caring. But they closed the doors of their intellect. Allah says in this verse that the people of sound mind are in truth the people who remember Allah and who also reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth. Remembrance of Allah is, again, what? It is an act of the heart. And reflection on the creation of the heavens and the earth is what? It is an act of the intellect. These two things go hand in hand.

body.text_en:
So when someone comes and says, "Yes, I do reflect upon the heavens and the earth, but I feel no gratitude in my heart. I find no one worthy of praise for creating all of this. I do not feel that I owe anyone anything." Well, yes! Because you are using your mind, you are using your intellect, but you have not yet exercised anything in your heart. The Qur'an says you are made of both. You are not purely a rational creature, and you are not purely an emotional creature. You are a perfect combination of the two. And in fact, which of them is given priority in these verses? Which comes first? The heart! The remembrance of Allah is mentioned first.

And when we first began studying the Fatiha, with which word did we begin? Hamd, which means what? All praise and gratitude belong to Allah. Is that a matter of the mind or of the heart? It is an emotional thing! To feel appreciation toward someone, to thank someone. Allah says the heart comes first. And that is why Allah says in the Qur'an that successful people will come before Allah on the Day of Judgment not with a clean mind, but with a clean, sound heart. Because the heart comes first.

And this is truly important to understand, because we must set our priorities in what we love and what we hate. For that is what the heart is all about: what you love and what you hate.

What you fear and what you do not fear. This is the kind of connection we need to build with Allah. People who believe with the heart recognize His presence at all times. And once they recognize His presence, they no longer care about anyone else, or about any pressure from anyone else. If someone pushes them to do the wrong thing, it truly does not matter to them, because for them the heart comes first, and Allah now lives in that heart. They recognize His presence constantly. You always feel strengthened when you know that someone is there for you. You no longer feel weak. You no longer feel that you are all on your own.

This difference does not come when you believe in Allah only in your head. Even before you came to this gathering, you knew about Allah. You knew you were supposed to love Him. You knew you were supposed to be grateful to Him. You knew you were supposed to be thankful to Him. But none of that knowledge actually moves you to stand before Him in prayer. When the love of Allah enters your heart, however, and you truly feel His presence within it, nothing in the world can stop you from standing before Him in prayer. In the head, anyone can say that he believes in a God. But to be attached to Allah in the heart, to feel His support, His love, His protection, and His mercy always with you, is something entirely different. It is not something that can be explained in words. Words fall short.

So, according to this verse, the heart comes first. And when the heart comes first, you will naturally turn your intellect in the right direction. You will focus on the right things. If your heart has not yet been conquered, your mind will work in the wrong direction. That, as I understand it, is the whole Qur'anic theory: the heart gives direction to the intellect.
body.topic_title_en: There's no Urdu title to translate — the source field contains only the placeholder text "DRAFT", not an actual Urdu title. I can't render a dignified English title from a placeholder without inventing content, which would put a fabricated title into a printed edition.

body.text_en:
The Messenger of Allah (may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) was the finest teacher in the whole history of humanity, and not only in its history but in its future as well: there will never come a better teacher than the Messenger of Allah (may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family). In any kind of education, two things are needed — an excellent teacher and an excellent curriculum. There will never be a better curriculum than the Qur'an, and there will never be a better teacher than the Messenger of Allah (may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family). So here you have the best teacher and the best curriculum together. And the students were the Quraysh, the tribe most eloquent of all in understanding.

The lessons themselves were extremely easy. They were not calculus; they were not quantum physics. The lessons were simple. If I were speaking to seven-year-old children, and I were asked to summarize the Meccan Qur'an — and the Meccan Qur'an is two-thirds of the Qur'an — to summarize it for those seven-year-old children in five minutes, I would say that I do not need five minutes; I need only one. God is one. Do not be like the previous nations who did not believe in God. Believe in His messengers. Believe in the afterlife. Be an obedient servant to God. What else is there? That is all; it is complete. Everything is covered. That is the entire message of the Meccan Qur'an; that is the gist of it. The lesson is not difficult.

Yet for how many years was the Messenger of God (may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) told to teach the same people the same material, over and over again? Twelve years — more than a decade. He is teaching the same people again and again. They hear the finest lessons ever taught, and they hear them in their own language, and they say, "I do not understand it. Give me something else. I am not impressed; give me something else."

Does God have the right to be angry? Yes, He absolutely has the right to be angry. Any ordinary teacher would be greatly angered. But then those people go one step further. They do not merely say that they do not understand; they become stubborn. And once they become stubborn, they begin to mock the verses, and they begin to mock the teacher (may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family). Does that make God angry? Yes — it makes God very angry. And when God becomes angry, what does He have the power to do?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Glory be to God. Has He dealt in this way with the nations that came before? Yes, He has. They called their messenger a liar; they called him mad; they called him insane; they said he was possessed by a jinn. They said he was stealing from the Jews and the Christians. They invented every kind of accusation. But in the end, do you know what they said? They said: you keep speaking of the Day of Resurrection; you keep speaking of heaven and hell; you keep speaking of angels; you keep speaking of God; you keep speaking of all these things that we cannot see. Show us something. Bring the dead back to life. Move this mountain out of the way. Let us see the Day of Judgment. Let us see this punishment you keep speaking of. إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُۥ بَعِيدًۭا وَنَرَىٰهُ قَرِيبًۭا وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلْعَذَابِ They say: hurry, and bring the punishment. Let us have it. I have been hearing of it for ten years now, and I am weary of it. You said it was near; then let us have it, let us see it. Let us finally see some action. I will believe it when I see it. That is what they said. If you have nothing to show me, then do not waste my time. I do not wish to hear this talk of the Quran. I will believe it when I see it.

Our minds are like horses. A horse is a very capable creature. It can run very fast, and it can move in any direction. But until you guide the horse and tell it to turn in the right direction, it will not carry you to your destination. So every person may possess an equally capable horse; yet if he does not know how to ride it, it will not bring him to where he is going. For this reason, the mere knowledge of the Quran is not enough. It is also necessary to understand the thought of the Quran. How does the Quran want us to think? How does it want us to arrive at our conclusions?

This is an exceedingly powerful surah, because of the manner in which God delivers its message. And it ties perfectly to what we are now studying concerning Malik Yaum al-Din. The Messenger of God is preaching the message of Islam to them. He is explaining to them the love, the care, and the mercy of God. He is explaining to them how God is al-Rahman and al-Rahim. But the disbelievers reject it. They do not merely reject it; they actually make fun of it. They mock the Messenger of God. They call him insane, a poet, a magician. They call the Quran something that the Messenger of God has plagiarized from past religions. And so they mock both the message and the messenger of God, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family. The Messenger of God warns them of the horrors of the Day of Judgment, and they make light of it. Is God going to fashion dead bones anew? Where is this Day of Judgment with which you keep threatening us?

And so, in this surah, God expresses His astonishment. This surah is a response to the mockery of the disbelievers. In it, God addresses their mockery. عم یتسائلون؟ The verse begins with Amma. The Amma is in fact عن ما, which means "About what?" And it has been shortened.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
I was only sleeping. Yes! But apart from the fact that you were still breathing, how different were you from the dead? You were cut off from every pleasure of this world. You were cut off from your family and your friends. You were cut off from your plans for the day and from all your plans for the future. You were entirely helpless, at the mercy of whoever was still awake at that hour. They could set you on fire, and you could do nothing about it. They could sit right beside you and gossip about you, mock you, and accuse you of things you never did, and there was nothing you could do to defend yourself against it. How different was I from being dead? I was not. But then what happened the next morning? I woke again. Allah woke me again. Once more He gave me strength. Do you know what that means? Allah gave me another chance. Al-Rahman, al-Rahim, gave me another chance. Yesterday I did not believe in Allah; today I have the chance to believe. Yesterday I did not worship Allah; today I have the chance to worship Him. Yesterday I disobeyed Allah; today I have another chance to obey Him. This morning Allah gave me another chance to do what is right. I have hope!

Do you know how our past discourages our future? We have done certain wrong things in the past, and that drains the hope out of our future. I have committed so many sins in my life; I have no chance of redemption; I am doomed. But Allah says: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا — I have made your sleep a severing for you. I wake you revitalized and re-energized to begin a new day. If you repent, if you resolve to change your ways, Allah says you have hope today. Just as last night's sleep cut you off from yesterday, let it also sever you from your past guilt and shame. Begin a new life today. Make this day the first day of the rest of your life. If you do that, if you repent sincerely, I will cut off your past transgressions as I cut yesterday off from you.

How happy people are when they come out of a coma. "I have been given a second chance at life. I will live my life differently now." For a believer, waking in the morning is a reminder of a second chance. O Allah, I promise that I will strive to be good today. Forgive what I did in the past. I am going to begin a new life today. Thank You for giving me another chance.

This is why Subaat is so beautiful. He used the word that means "to sever," to cut off. You and I may have certain bad habits that have accumulated over time. Our true conviction in Allah will let us believe that every night Allah has cut us off from our past. So when we wake in the morning, we can wake entirely new, free from our former mistakes. After this, the only one who locks himself into his own pattern — who believes he cannot change what he has been doing in the past and is stuck in this habit forever — is you, not Allah. For Allah made your new day by severing you from the day before, as a sign and a reminder that you can start fresh again. The next time you wake, truly wake. Do not merely wake from sleep; wake from your ignorance, for that too is a sleep.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
So Allah, addressing the disbelievers,

They disbelieve in Allah and mock the Day of Judgment, so Allah reminds them of their weakness and helplessness through their daily sleep. You cannot even control your own body. You cannot even control the ordinary business of your day. By the end of the day you will have no choice but to sleep and be cut off from all your power, your wealth, your family, your children. Very well! Mock everything you please. But soon, what is going to happen to you? Sleep. Death. Soon you will stand before Me. Then We shall see who has the last laugh.

وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا

Then, continuing the subject of sleep, Allah speaks further, and let us look at the next few verses together, for they are bound to one another.

وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًۭا

We made the night a covering, a garment. So Allah says that He drapes us in the darkness of the night just as we drape our bodies by putting on clothes. We studied earlier that evils are associated with the night, that crimes are committed in the night. But set all of that aside for a moment. Do our capacities become limited in the night? They do. We cannot see clearly. Whatever we do, do we not need the support of light? Imagine there is a blackout during the night. No electricity. You do not even have a flashlight or candles in the house. Can you do anything now? No! You are wholly paralyzed. Now imagine the ancient Arabs of fourteen hundred years ago. Business, entertainment, everything came to a complete halt once the night arrived. So Allah says, once I make it dark, what can you do? How far do you suppose your torches and lamps can carry you? Once I wrap you in the garment of night, you do not have the power to take it off. You cannot rid yourself of it. There is nothing you can do about it. You can turn on the light in your room, but there is nothing you can do about the night itself.

And if you do not have the power to take off this garment that I have placed upon you, do you really imagine that you will be able to do anything about the Day of Judgment? See how I cover every single one of you, groups of you, your friends, your families, your associates, your allies. I cover all of you together with the night, and neither individually nor collectively can you do anything about it. My night has overpowered all of you, and there is nothing you can do about it. Does that not remind you? Does that not remind you that one day you, and group upon group of peoples, entire nations, will stand before Me, wholly helpless, accountable for their deeds?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Consider the extraordinary beauty that Allah has created in the nature all around us. A few months ago I was at a resort beside the ocean. I decided that I was going to watch the sun rise over the water. So I left my hotel room an hour before sunrise, went out, and sat on the shore. I could barely see anything around me or in the water. It was pitch dark. It was actually depressing, frightening in fact, to sit there alone in the darkness. But then the sun came out, brightening everything, and I saw this spectacular view of the ocean. Now, was all this beauty there even when I could not see it? Yes! But I could not see a thing until when? Until the sun came out. So Allah says,

وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلنَّهَارَ مَعَاشًۭا

and We made the day a time and a place to earn an honest living.

The word *Ma'aash* comes from the word عیش, which means not merely life but a good life. Even in Urdu you have the word *Ayesh*. So there are two implications in the word *Ma'aash*. The first is time and the second is place. Time in the sense that you can run your businesses during the daytime — most businesses run during the day. So one of the reasons we live a good life is because of the sun. Allah says: You think you are so great! Once I make it dark, what can you do? Can you make the sky bright again? Can you bring the sun out sooner than when I decide to bring it out? Is there anything you can do to remove this cover I have placed over the day?

And it is I who made the day a means for you to earn a good living and enjoy life. The only reason you are able to enjoy a good life is that I bring out the day for you. I place the cover of night upon you, and the next day I remove that cover. And because I remove this cover, you are actually able to have a good life. And you want to make a joke of my religion?

And are you not also able to sleep peacefully at night because I made the night dark? Those of us who have had a rough night and must go to work the next morning — what kind of day do we have? Allah says: I put everything in place for you so that you can have a restful night, and so that you wake up refreshed in the morning to earn a good living the next day. And you are going to disbelieve in me? You are going to disobey me?

Then He says: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًۭا شِدَادًۭا — And We constructed above them seven mighty ones, seven immense powers, referring to the seven skies.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Note that in the previous verse Allah speaks of *Ma'aash*, a good living, and in this next verse He speaks of construction. And interestingly, you can tell how well the economy of a country is doing by the amount of construction going on there. That is a mark of a nation with great *Ma'aash*: you will see an abundance of buildings and skyscrapers. And this is not only in modern times. Even in ancient times, cities that flourished economically always had the greatest amount of construction going on. Construction is in fact a sign that a city is booming. And when you see abandoned buildings and orphaned construction projects — the cranes gone but the pits still there — what does that mean? It means construction has stopped, which is directly related to the fact that *Ma'aash* is no longer good in that city.

So Allah mentions *Ma'aash*, and then immediately mentions construction: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلنَّهَارَ مَعَاشًۭا... وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًۭا شِدَادًۭا. You build — and look at what Allah builds. What kind of construction could you ever do that could compare to the construction Allah has made? And again: سَبْعًۭا شِدَادًۭا — not سبع سموات. He did not say I constructed seven skies. He said I created above you seven mighty ones! And He does not explain what those seven mighty ones are. Why not mention it? Because at this point in the surah there is an expectation: people are pretending, asking these foolish questions and making fun of the Day of Judgment — when the fact of the matter is that they already know.

They have heard of the seven skies often enough. They need not be told again. This is Allah calling them out: you are asking one another, but you are only playing; you are not serious. I know that you know.

But He also uses the word Shidaad so carefully in this context, because after all, what is the tone of this surah? It is a threat, is it not? Shidaad comes from the word شِدۃ, or shadeed, meaning intense, like intense pain. In Urdu we say شدید تکلیف, intense pain. So Allah is saying: do you not see these skies, magnificent though they are, and merciful too, because they provide you with rain, the water that is the source of your life on this planet? But when I will it, they can be intensely harmful as well. Do you not remember the floods I sent through the rains upon the disbelievers in the time of Nuh, peace be upon him? Fire falling from the sky? Do you not see the magnificence, the intense power, of these seven skies? Do they not remind you of My power? You wish to disbelieve in Me? You wish to make fun of My Day of Judgment?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
And then He says: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًۭا وَهَّاجًۭا. And I hung in those skies this blazing lamp. Siraaj means anything that is lit from within. So a modern light bulb can be called a Siraaj, because it lights from within. But when you add Wahhaaj, it means blazing, fiery, intensely burning. And wahhaaj is referred to as صیغۃ المبالغۃ, meaning something that is blazing, something brilliant, something that keeps burning over and over again. It means it keeps rekindling its flame; it is self-sustained. Which lamp is Allah speaking of? He is speaking of the sun. Which lamp can you and I produce? What lighting can mankind collectively produce, what light source, what power source can we produce that will compare with Allah's Sirajan Wahhaaja? Who do you think you are comparing yourself to? Who do you think you are showing your attitude to? So Allah illustrates His creative power, and at the same time brings out the powerlessness of human beings.

وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَتِ مَآءًۭ ثَجَّاجًۭا. And we sent down from the Mo'siraat abundant water. This is again the style of the surah. It does not directly say winds; it says Mo'siraat. أَعصَرَ, or اِعصَار, in classical Arabic literally means to take a wet cloth and wring it out, so that all the water is drained from it. That is اعصار. It also means clouds that are so full of water that they can hold no more and end up dripping. So these are the two implications of the word معصرات. Mo'siraat is those that squeeze. What is that? What is Allah speaking of? It is a reference to winds that squeeze the clouds, as you take a wet cloth and squeeze it by wringing it. In Urdu we say نچوڑنا, and all the water comes out. The winds squeeze the clouds and the water comes out. ثَجَّاجًۭا. Sajj literally means something that overflows, or heavy, profuse rain, or flooding. So we send down this intense supply of water, which again human beings cannot compare to, because we know that water is yet another thing by which human beings are overpowered: either by its excess, causing floods, or by its shortage, causing droughts. When Allah does not send it—

I'll translate only the given part, following every rule.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
it can create death and famine, and when he sends too much, it can also create death and destruction. SubhanAllah! So you see, pouring rains come out from these few clouds that squeeze, and you think nothing of them, and yet the entire life of this earth is sustained through them. لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِۦ حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا ..... وَجَنَّتٍ أَلْفَافًا So that we may take out from the earth—Habb, meaning grain, and then Nabaat, meaning all kinds of vegetation. In these two things we have sustenance for ourselves and our animals, the animals upon which we depend. You know, we think we are so modern, that we do not need animals anymore. We have grocery stores and boxed food items. Where do you think our food comes from? Where is the milk coming from? Where is the bread, the cheese, coming from? It was not manufactured in a factory in a plastic bag. It came from a farm. It came from the same animals that people depended on thousands of years ago, and they literally herded them. The only difference is that somebody is herding them for us now. Someone is taking that produce to factories and packaging it. But at the end of the day, we are just as dependent on these animals as the people of fourteen hundred years ago were, and these animals are just as dependent on Habb and Nabaat as the animals back then were dependent on them. So nothing has really changed. We have not grown out of these needs.

وَجَنَّتٍ أَلْفَافًا This is the beauty of the Qur'an. Allah, in numerous, numerous places, did not just highlight the things we need, but he always highlighted the things that we enjoy. He could have stopped at حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا. He provided us with what we needed simply to survive, but then he says وَجَنَّتٍ أَلْفَافًا. Jannah means lush green gardens, gardens that are surrounded by flowers and trees and fragrance. And then, not just that, he says وَجَنَّتٍ أَلْفَافًا. Lafeef in Arabic means gardens that are so lush that the branches actually fold into one another. They mesh together. You cannot tell where one tree ends and another begins. That is Lafeef. And Alfaaf is the plural of Lafeef. They are meshed together, endless, endless greenery.

So Allah does not just speak about the bare necessities. He mentions his Rehma, his love, his care, his mercy. He always mentions how he goes far above and beyond the basic needs to make things easy for us. You know, that is how parents operate. You, as children, have bare necessities. You need food to survive. They are obligated to give you just the bare minimum. I have two children. From an obligation standpoint, as religion dictates, I am supposed to provide them with basic necessities. I can take them both to the backyard on the green grass and say, "Lunch time! Enjoy!" I can buy them clothes from the homeless shelter that can protect them from heat and cold. That is my basic obligation. I can have them sleep in the garage on a mat on the floor. I can have them use the cover of my car as a quilt. It will serve the purpose. Hahaha. Bare minimum, right? But do parents do that? No! They give you the best food they can afford. They buy you the best clothes they can afford. You have your own rooms, with your comfortable beds, your toys, your gadgets.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Your Playstation games, your entertainment, your pocket money — all of these things that you take for granted. All of this that they give you, what is it? It is their love. It is their care. It is their mercy toward you. They want to provide for you far above and beyond your basic necessities. That is all love. We, as human beings, do not make that distinction, do we? We simply take all of it for granted. But the truth is that, according to religion, and even according to the law, they are only required to provide you with your basic requirements. Yet we, as children, mistake all of that love for a sense of entitlement. We begin to think we are entitled to all of it, because we have never known anything different. Do you understand?

We eat the best food our parents can provide, and we say that it is not good enough. It does not taste good. I do not like it. We wear the best clothes they can afford to buy for us, and we say that it is not the right brand, that another brand is better. Yes, you bought me a computer, the iPad, an iPhone, but it is not the latest version. You do not do enough for me. You do not love me. What have you ever done for me? Whatever you are doing, it is your duty to do it. Do children behave that way or not? Hopefully you do not, but does it happen in the world or not? It does. Are such children ungrateful or not? They absolutely are.

This is the very same thing we do with Allah. He gave us everything we need, and then He provided us with a great deal more that was not necessary for us to live a good life. Yet we take all of it for granted, just like the ungrateful child, and then we complain about that child ourselves.

So this is what Allah says to those disbelievers who enjoy all of Allah's love, all of Allah's care, all of Allah's mercy. They enjoy all of His Rehmaniyat and all of His Raheemiyat, and then they say: What Allah? What Judgment Day? All of this is nonsense. There is no such thing.

With those people, Allah is now angry. And now He speaks to them in a very different tone. Who do you think you are? Look at what you do, and look at what I do. This is Takbeer. Allah is glorifying Himself. You think you can take My religion lightly? You think you can take My beloved Prophet lightly? You think you can make fun of him? Just because I am AlRehman AlRaheem, you are going to take My mercy lightly? Well, I am not only that. I am also Malik Yaum AlDeen. Do not forget that. The parent who loves you, the mother who stayed up all night at your side, weeping and praying for you while you slept peacefully — that same mother has the power to withdraw her love and her mercy from you. She has the power to turn you out of the house, to disown you, if you do not correct your ways.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
An interesting point to note in these ayaats, in which Allah speaks about His creation, is that they come back to us human beings. I made the earth comfortable for whom? For man. I made the mountains for whom? For mankind. I made sleep for whom? And so on. So, indirectly, all of these ayaats point to human beings. All of this always comes back to us — to our helplessness, even before the creations of Allah.

In the creation of the heavens, there is absolute conviction for the believer. And how dependent we are upon the other things that Allah has created for us. So with all of these arguments, human beings are being put in their place. You do not deserve to speak in this way about the hereafter. You need to know your role. You need to know how utterly powerless and weak you truly are.

So after this warning, Allah now comes to the point. What have we seen so far? People are asking about the Day of Judgment casually, making fun of it, not taking it seriously. And then Allah speaks about His magnificent creation. So the Surah moves forward: You speak about the afterlife as though it were a joke. How is it that you do not think about My creation? How is it that you do not ask questions about these creations all around you? Why do you not ask one another where the earth came from? Why is it so comfortable for you? Why is life so perfectly designed for your existence — and not merely for your existence, but for your luxury? Why do you not ask one another that? Where did all of this come from?

This is the Qur'an's fundamental argument. The Qur'an gives us roads to conviction. How are you absolutely certain that this is the truth, that this is revelation, and that there is in fact a God, that there is in fact an Ilah? How do you know that this is not a theory, that it is not a theology, but that it is a matter of fact? How do you know that for certain? The Qur'an's argument is that if people genuinely reflect upon creation, there is no way they will arrive at any other conclusion. That is the Qur'an's argument.

ان فی خلق السماوات آیات لی المومنین

In the creation of the heavens, there is absolute conviction for the believer.

Allah did not even mention revelation as a means to arrive at conviction. You do not need the Qur'an to prove to you that God exists. The proof of the existence of God is not in the Qur'an. Interestingly enough, Allah never speaks about proof of His existence in the Qur'an. It is not even a subject of the Qur'an. Which doubt does the Qur'an address? Is this revelation or not?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
ذالک الکتاب لا ریب فیہ — not ذالک الہ لا ریب فیہ. That is not a discussion in the Qur'an. Because Allah's declaration in the Qur'an is that I have already given you another set of signs that will bring you to that conclusion. You do not need these signs of the Qur'an to arrive at that conclusion. What are the signs — the signs that will bring you to that conclusion? The skies, the heavens, the mountains, the winds, the sun, the habb, the nabaat, the mo'siraaat, the perfection of your own body. All of this will bring you to that conclusion, if you seriously reflect. If you give it truly absolute thought, then it is very hard for you to say that all of this is the product of an accident. No one in their right mind will say that this is the product of an accident. And we have spoken about many of those things in earlier sessions. Beauty, taste, beautiful symmetry — why would these need to exist as the result of an accident? Everything should be chaos. It should be mangled and twisted. Why is it so beautiful? This reflection, this serious pondering and thinking about these things, will bring you to that conclusion, that there is an Allah.

When people have a crisis of faith, they think that some super mysterious

extremely abstract answer will bring them back to faith. It will not. It is the same answer it has always been: reflection upon creation. That is the only requirement. It is not a new answer. The verses of the Qur'an compel us to look at the verses of the world, and the verses of the world compel us to look back at the verses of the Qur'an. We keep moving between one set of verses and the other, so that in the end no one can say, "I received no reminder." On the Day of Judgment, Allah is able to say: What? Did you not feel the wind? Did you not feel the breeze upon your face? You and I imagine that the sermon, the gathering, is a reminder; Allah says that the wind is a reminder. The wind is enough to strike them across the face and wake them. Yet after everything Allah created for us as His signs, He then sent a book and a messenger to spell it out for us, to show us His love, His care, His mercy through these reminders, and still we keep taking it for granted. We truly have no excuse before Allah on the Day of Judgment when He asks us: Did you not look at the sky? The sun? The mountains? Your own body?

Now Allah changes the manner of His speech. First He speaks of the denial of the disbelievers. Then He confronts them with His magnificent creations, to put human beings in their place. And now He speaks of the very thing they were mocking and being sarcastic about: the Day of Judgment itself.

إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَتًۭا
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Indeed, the Day of al-Fasl. Al-Fasl in Arabic means to take two things that are together and to separate them so completely that they stand clearly apart from one another. The Day of Judgment is called the Day of Fasl, the Day of Separation, or the Day of Clear Distinction, because on that day truth will be separated from falsehood. In this world, truth and falsehood are all mixed together. Realities are embellished; they are distorted. Beliefs are contaminated. It is not that people do not believe in Allah; people believe in Allah and in other things as deities as well. People do not simply do good; they do good and evil alike. Everything is blended into everything else. The Day of Judgment is the Day of Fasl, where a disbeliever will be separated from his disbelief. He will no longer deny the existence of Allah, because he will stand in the presence of Allah. He will no longer deny the Fire, because he will see it with his own eyes. He will not disbelieve in the resurrection, because he himself has just been awakened from his sleep. He will be separated from all his false hopes, his false gods, his false beliefs. The arrogant will be separated from their arrogance; the proud will be separated from the object of their pride. So kings will be separated from their kingdoms. Aristocrats will be separated from their wealth. Warriors will be separated from their strength. So everything a disbeliever possessed, on the basis of which he disbelieved in Allah, on the basis of which he disobeyed Allah, will now be clearly separated from that object itself. Followers will be separated from their leaders.

إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوا۟

When those who were followed will disown those who followed them. Children follow the trends of their popular friends at school.

They follow the trends of celebrities. They dress like them, they walk like them, they talk like them. On the Day of Judgment, these children will want to be disassociated from them, to disown them. Why? Because they can see where these people are heading, and they do not want to follow them there. But the justice of Allah will prevail. Allah says that it is only fair you follow today those whom you followed while you were living in the world. You had a choice to follow Rasul Allah, peace be upon him. You had a choice to follow Maulana Ali, and Maulatena Fatema. You had that choice. But you chose to follow these other social idols. Then follow them today.

وَرَأَوُا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ ٱلْأَسْبَابُ

And they see the torment, and then all their relations are cut off from them. On that day they will want nothing to do with them. The very people whom you desperately want to impress today, for whose sake you change your life until you become, quite literally, a slave to their pleasure and displeasure — on that day they will want nothing to do with you.

Allah says:

إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ

There is no doubt that on that day there will be a clear distinction drawn between everything that is false and everything that is good. And the most graphic description of this separation is when a mother is separated from her child. That is perhaps the most vivid picture of al-Fasl on that day.

Allah says:

إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَٰتًۭا
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
They have been fused together to express shock. The word تسائلون suggests a light form of questioning. You know how an interviewer sometimes puts hard questions to a guest, pressing him with pointed, offensive questions and putting him on the spot? In Arabic that is مُسائلۃ. It is not تسائل. The word تسائل suggests that they are speaking casually among themselves about these matters, not taking them seriously. And so God says, عم یتسائلون؟ About what are they asking? About what do they imagine they are asking? About what are they raising questions so casually?

Then God adds, عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ. About the great news. Naba is different from Khabar. Khabar means any piece of news at all. For example, I had a boiled egg for breakfast: that is khabar. Naba is major news, ground-breaking news. An earthquake is naba. A tsunami is naba. The outbreak of war is naba. I found my car keys is khabar; it is not naba. Naba must be a great matter, and not only to you, but to everyone. Naba is something that concerns everyone, and it demands some sort of action. So an earthquake is a naba, meaning you had better take precautionary measures. A khabar may not be so. Do you understand?

So naba by itself is already a great matter. But then God adds AlAzeem: the great and mighty news. He raises it to the highest degree. Yet He does not say what that great news is. Now this suggests that the disbelievers already know what God is speaking about. If I ask you, "Have you heard what happened? Was that not astonishing?" then I am quite certain that you have already heard of it. If not, I would spell it out for you. Have you heard about the championship? Have you heard about the promotion? Have you heard about the accident? Have you heard about the election result? Do you understand? The verse refuses to spell it out. It simply says عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ.

So God is saying, About what are they asking? About the great news? The suggestion here is that this great news is no mystery to anyone. The ones hearing these verses know exactly what God is speaking about. It is no mystery to any of them; they know what the great news is. The idea behind this is: you people know what you are laughing about; you people already know. God says that they ask one another so casually, so jokingly, about something that should be their most serious concern. For this is not merely naba; this is naba AlAzeem. Azeem comes from azam, which means a very strong bone. This is great news, magnificent news, powerful news, solid news, like a strong bone. News that is serious business. Meaning: you have heard about earthquakes, but not one like this. You have heard about floods, but not one like this. You have heard about earthquakes, but not one like this.

Then He says, ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ. The one about which they are in disagreement. These are two separate verses, but grammatically the two are a single sentence. So, in terms of language, this is عَم يَتَسَآءَلُونَ, About what are they asking? عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ, About the great news that they are constantly disagreeing about. And Mukhtalifoon has been used as a noun rather than a verb; it is not یختلفون.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
There is no doubt that this day of clear separation had already been appointed. Meeqat means a time that is fixed; it is an appointed time. It had to happen. Like death, it is an appointed time. Like taxes, it is a meeqat. It will come whether you like it or not. The hour will, without doubt, strike.

What is truly worth noting is that everything Allah spoke of in the preceding verses — the pairs, the mountains, the skies, sleep, rain, growth — all of it happens within a fixed span of time. There is a period allocated to each of them. Even scientifically we know that this world will eventually come to an end. Even physically, this world is not permanent, just as our life on this planet is not permanent. We have an appointed time of death, at which point our life will come to an end.

And just as Allah said that He created everything in pairs — وَخَلَقْنَٰكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًۭا, We created you in pairs — that too is a reference to the fact that, just as this world exists, it also has a pair. Your life in this world is paired with the hereafter. Just as you have a life in this world, this worldly life also has its pair, which is the afterlife. Just as you see that the seasons have a fixed, appointed time, a meeqat, after which a new season begins whether you like it or not; just as this day of yours has a fixed number of hours, after which another day begins, whether you like it or not; just as the sun has a fixed span of time, after which it sets, whether you agree with it or not — in the same way you too have a fixed span of time, after which you will have to leave. You too have an appointed time, a meeqat, after which you will have to die, whether you like it or not, whether you agree with it or not.

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًۭا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ

O man!

There is no doubt about you. You had best realize it: you are marching forward toward your Lord with your deeds and your actions, and you are surely going to meet Him.

Then He says: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًۭا — the Day on which the horn will be blown, and you will come before Me obediently, in armies.

So the imagery here is of a horn, or a trumpet, being blown. In olden days, that is how severe warnings were transmitted. Someone standing on the top of a mountain would see a huge army advancing, and he would blow this horn to alert everyone in the village and warn them that a danger was coming.
