And if you have watched those films, what do we see? As soon as that horn is blown, what happens right after it? All chaos breaks loose. It is chaos everywhere. People start running about. There is screaming. Things fall as people rush. No one cares about anyone else; everyone cares only for himself. That is the imagery in this verse. On that Day, that appointed Day referred to in the previous verse, when the horn is blown, you will begin to see chaos, which is described in the verses that follow. But what will be the end result? Once the chaos is over and the dust settles, what will the final outcome be? فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًۭا — you will all come before Me obediently, in large groups.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Now, فَتَأْتُونَ is used in the second person. Allah is now speaking to the disbelievers; He is no longer speaking about them. The chapter began with عم یتسائلون, not تتسائلون. It began in the third person, but now the tone has shifted, and Allah is speaking in the second person. He is speaking to them. In the beginning, Allah was expressing His disgust with them by not even addressing them directly. He was speaking about them. This is called تبعید in Arabic — to distance oneself from the one with whom one is displeased. This was the style of the ancient Arabs. So fourteen hundred years ago, if you were truly angry and disgusted with your friend, you would not begin by speaking to him. You would speak about him in the third person, even while he or she was standing right in front of you, along with your other friends. You would first express your disgust in the third person, saying something like, "Who needs enemies with such horrible friends? What kind of horrible friend does this?" And then you would actually turn to him in anger and address him directly: "I cannot believe you did this horrible thing." Do you understand? Teachers do this in class. They walk in and say, "Some of you did really badly on your exam." Now some of the students are nervous, but they are not certain whether it is truly them. The teacher then turns to Abdullah and says, "You, by the way." Now Abdullah is caught off guard all of a sudden. This is a very consistent style of the Qur'an in the way Allah carries out a threat: He switches from the third person to the second person.

Now, the word ta'toona. The word أتا، یئتی does not merely mean to come. Unlike جاء، یجیئُ, which means to come, ata means to come in submission. فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ ٱئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًۭا قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ — We commanded the heavens and the earth to come willingly or unwillingly, and they said, أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ.

We come in submission—that is, we surrender ourselves completely. So فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًۭا: you will not merely come in multitudes; on that day you will come in submission, in multitudes. You will give yourselves up in multitudes. Why is this important to know? Because right now you are in rebellion. Right now you are arrogant. Right now you are unsubmissive. But on that day you will come to us in complete submission.

Now he describes what will happen between the moment the trumpet is blown and the moment everyone is presented before him in submission. وَفُتِحَتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَٰبًۭا—the skies will be opened and become like doors. Earlier in this same Surah, Allah had mentioned وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًۭا شِدَادًۭا—I constructed above you seven magnificent things, which are the skies. He pointed to his power and to their weakness by pointing out this magnificent construction: I created the skies; what construction do you have that can compete with mine? So he overpowered the disbelievers with his creation, and now he begins to speak of the changes that will take place in his own constructions and creations. وَفُتِحَتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَٰبًۭا—these skies that I had constructed will be opened and become like doors.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Now, what is a door? A door indicates a transition in state. You are outside the house; once through the door, you are now inside the house. Things are different when you are outside—the scenery, the weather, the temperature are different outside; once you enter through the door, everything is different on the inside. It is a transition of state. Do you understand? So now Allah says, I will make the skies doors. It is a metaphor to indicate that it is time to come through. It is time for you to be presented before me, and there is nothing you can do about it. You will have to pass through this door. What are you going to do now?

He said about the skies: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ طِبَاقًۭا ۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتٍۢ ۖ فَٱرْجِعِ ٱلْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٍۢ—See as far as your eyes can see: do you see a crack in my construction? ثُمَّ ٱرْجِعِ ٱلْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْبَصَرُ خَاسِئًۭا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌۭ—Send your vision as far as you can; push it to its limits, and do it over and over again. Your vision will return to you unsuccessful, but you will not find a flaw in my perfection.

And now, on the day of judgment, he says the exact opposite. He says the entire sky will become a door. A door serves as the greatest gap in a wall; it is what we pass through. So something that Allah created that was perfect—he will not open it up and make a door; he will crack it open. وَسُيِّرَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًۭا—and the mountains will walk casually and will look like a mirage.

Suyyirat comes from the word taseer, which means something that moves easily, moves casually. If you take a ball and slowly roll it on the ground, and it slowly rolls, that is taseer. It is moving easily; there is no force necessary; it sails by itself. All right?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
So when you walk about casually, you are performing taseer. Allah says that you will see the mountains moving with ease. And what did He say about the mountains a little while ago? وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًۭا—And I made the mountains as pegs, remember? He compared the pegs of a disbeliever's tents to His own pegs, the mountains. And what is the work of pegs? To hold the tent in its place. The whole purpose of pegs is to keep the tents firmly grounded. The mountains keep the earth firmly grounded. Now, when its day of judgment arrives, what does He say? وَسُيِّرَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ—these firm mountains will look as though they are drifting about casually. They will simply be rolling along, floating along, with careless ease. The last thing you would associate with movement—let alone casual movement—is the mountains. And then He adds فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًا, and this carries several effects at once. The word saraab means mirage. You know how a mirage seems to float in the air? So it will be as though these mountains are floating in the air. And also, because a mirage has no reality—when you go up to a mirage you find nothing there. So Allah is saying that these enormous mountains will be turned to nothing. For what are the disbelievers firm in? Their disbelief, their arrogance, which are firm like what? Like mountains. Allah says that these enormous mountains I have created will be reduced to nothing on the day of judgment. What do you think will happen to your mountains of disbelief and arrogance? On that day, not only will My mountains turn to nothing; you will see your firm mountains of disbelief and arrogance and pride reduced to nothing. SubhanAllah!

Now, everything up to this point was the first kalla saya'lamoon, the 'ayn al-yaqin. You were given knowledge about the day of judgment, but you disbelieved. Now, when you see this destruction happening all around you, you will believe; you will receive visual confirmation of what you had been given knowledge of. So these were the preceding ayats. Now He begins to speak of the final stage of certainty, when they will be standing before Allah and will see the hellfire they are about to be cast into. So first the Resurrection, and then al-Naar, the hellfire. إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًۭا—No doubt the hellfire has always been lying in ambush. Mirsaad. There is another word related to it, marsad, which comes from rasada in Arabic. This refers to the one who is trying to ambush. A marsad is a place you hide in so that you can attack someone. That is marsad. Mirsaad is a different word. It is a place that is ideal for an ambush—meaning it is designed for the sole purpose of hiding and attacking the enemy when they are unaware. Allah describes the hellfire as a place that has been hiding and waiting to strike. That is how it is described in this Surah: kaanat mirsaada.

Then, who is it lying in ambush for? لِّلطَّغِينَ مَـَٔابًۭا—It is in ambush for al-Tagheen. Allah did not say it is in ambush for the disbelievers, al-Kafireen, al-Mushrikeen. So many other words could have been used here—al-Zalimeen, al-Fasiqeen. The word used specifically here is al-Tagheen, because this is not speaking about kufr, or disbelief.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
That is on the outside. What is on the inside? Tughyaan—rebellion. I want to do what I want to do, and no one else is going to tell me what to do. Consider people who do not believe in God, even the atheist: their disbelief in God is not born of some profound intellectual evidence that they hold. At the heart of the matter, they want to live the life they want to live. They do not want to accept a higher authority over them. In other words, they want to rebel against any higher authority. That is the root of this whole problem.

It is out of this that they are so curious about Naba al-Azeem, the great news. The Surah opened with Amma Yatasaaloon, An Naba il Azeem—they are asking one another about the great news. Why are they asking? Because of their Tughyaan, because of their rebellion.

So Allah says this ambush, this hellfire that lies waiting in ambush—for whom is it? It is for the rebellious. And then He says Ma'aab, a place to which they must keep returning. The idea is that they want to escape it, but it keeps drawing them back in. Ma'aab is a place you come back to for rest. They may get away from it, yet Ma'aab is a place to stay, and it is a resting place itself.

Now let us speak of this hellfire and this ambush. People complain: if there is a loving God, how can He allow the fire to lie in ambush? He is Almighty, He is all-powerful; He ought to protect us from this enemy that lies in wait. To answer that, let me ask you a question. You have a friend whom you truly care about. You discover that someone is in fact planning to hurt her as she walks home from school—that someone means to hide and ambush her and attack her. So, in order to protect her, in order to warn her, you tell her about this plan. You say, "Look, today, as you are walking home, so-and-so is planning to attack you. They are going to hide beneath this particular tree, and what they intend to do is that, the moment you pass by it, they will jump out and attack you. I just want you to know ahead of time so that you can protect yourself. Take a different route if you must, or whatever precautionary measures you need to put in place, I want you to take them, so that you can remain safe."

Now, were you being a good friend, or were you being a terrible friend? Are you warning her because you love her, or are you warning her because you hate her? Clearly you love her. You are being a very good friend, because you want to protect your friend, and so you are warning her about this threat.

Now, is that not what Allah is doing for us right now? Is the Qur'an read and recited while you are alive, or after you are dead? We are reciting it while we are alive, and Allah is warning us about a threat, which is the hellfire. He is telling us that the hellfire is there to ambush us. He does not want us to be hurt; He wants to protect us, and so He is asking us to change our path. Is that a sign of love, or is it a sign of hatred?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
What if He had never mentioned these verses in the Qur'an? What if these were dangers that He had left for us to discover only after we died? Would that have been better, or worse? It would obviously have been far worse.

Because we would have been caught completely off guard. But Allah did not do that, did He? He warned us beforehand. He told us about these dangers at a time when we still have the power to change our path. We can change what we are. We can change our system of belief. We can do whatever it takes to guard ourselves against this enemy that is coming. Is that a sign of love? Is that a sign of mercy? Or is it a sign of evil and hatred?

So Allah's warning us in the Qur'an about these terrible punishments is not because He does not love us, and not because He hates us. It is because He cares for us. He loves us, and He does not want us to be hurt.

Then Allah says:

لَّبِثِينَ فِيهَآ أَحْقَابًۭا

They will remain in it for a very long time. Labitha, with the letter tha and not with the letter seen, means to remain somewhere for a very long time. So these rebellious people are going to stay there for a very, very long time. And that very long time is then given a measure, and that measure is a haqab. Ahqab is the plural of the word haqab. Maulana Ali was asked about this verse and the length of a haqab, and he replied that a haqab is eighty years, each day of which is a thousand years. A haqab is eighty years, each day of which is a thousand years.

Now this is a very long time, and it is usually translated as "forever." But if you think about it, even if a haqab is eighty years, and every day of those eighty years is a thousand years, that is still a finite span of time, is it not? It is still not an infinite duration. This shows us that even the time spent in the Fire is not permanent. It will eventually come to an end. It is a very long span, no doubt, but it is not forever.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
But He did not say haqab. He said ahqab, which is the plural form. Haqab would have been one set of eighty years in which every day is a thousand years. But Allah did not use the word haqab. He used the plural form, ahqab, which means there are multiple sets of haqab. And here is another interesting thing to note: even though He used the plural form, He did not state exactly how many. This means that it is different for different people. The punishment will fit the crime. If Allah had given a number—if, for example, He had said a thousand ahqab—that would have made it a thousand ahqab for everyone. But Allah did not do that. He simply used the plural form, ahqab. So a set of two haqab is ahqab, and a set of a thousand haqab is also ahqab. This means that every criminal will be judged according to his crime. It is not one level of punishment for every crime; but the least of it is at least that much. So for these criminals, once they finish one haqab, the next one begins. When that one is finished, the next begins. When the third is finished, another begins. And this goes on until their sentence is complete and their punishment is served.

Now here is another question: why this long duration? After all, even for a disbeliever this punishment seems very harsh, does it not? I understand that he is denying Allah, but eighty years, every day of which is a thousand years, in the Fire? That seems like a great deal, does it not? So how do we reconcile this? You know, we see this even in this life.

That the punishment for the same crime is actually in proportion to the authority against which the crime is committed. So, for example, if you say something back to your friend — let us say you curse at them — they will probably be angry for a few minutes, and then they will laugh it off and everything will be fine. Now let us say you use the same curse word at your schoolteacher. That is not simply going to be laughed off. You will be taken to the principal. You will be reprimanded for what you did. You might even be expelled; it all depends. Now let us say you use the same curse word at your parents — the exact same curse word. This time it is not that you will only be yelled at or reprimanded. You will first, most likely, receive a hard, ringing slap across your face. So for the same crime, the punishment changed because of the authority against which the crime was committed.

You use the same curse word against someone in authority, such as the president of the company, and you will be fired; and if he has some power, he will ruin your reputation to the point where no other company will ever hire you again. You use that curse word against the president of a country, and most likely your house will blow up because you left the gas open. Do you know what I mean? You stand before the king of a country, in his palace, and you use the same curse word, and he will behead you. Again, the same curse word that, when you used it against your friend, was laughed off, but when you used it against a king, it cost you your head.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Now what about Allah? What about the majesty and glory of Allah? Can you compare it to the president of a company? Can you compare it to the president of a country? Can you compare it to a king? You cannot compare it to anyone. So now, a crime committed against Allah — what level of punishment do you think that would bring? And especially after all the warnings. After the enemy has been clearly identified for us. After we have been told the exact places where the enemy is hiding in order to ambush us. After all his love and mercy have been shown to us. After verse upon verse upon verse has been sent so that we might be able to accept the truth. If, after all of this, we still do not accept him as our master; if, after all of this, we still commit the crimes that he has forbidden; after he has explained to us his power, his glory, his magnificence; if we still continue to treat him as though he were nothing; if we still disrespected him, constantly disobeyed him — you tell me, what kind of punishment would we deserve for our crimes? I would say that Haqab, or even Ahqaab, seems like a very lenient punishment to me. So these criminals will remain in this for a very long time.

And then he says: لَّا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًۭا وَلَا شَرَابًا — they will not taste in it any coolness, nor any drink. Now let us understand this verse. You know, Allah speaks in the Qur'an about the very least, the least of the least, of the punishment in the Fire, when he says: وَلَىِٕن مَّسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌۭ مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَوَيْلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَلِمِينَ — even if a little whiff of the punishment of your Lord touches them, they will cry out, "Woe unto us, we were surely among the unjust." The word used in this verse is Nafha.

with an *h*. In Arabic, this is the word Nafha, spelled with a *nun*, alongside the word Lafha, spelled with a *lam*. Lafha is a warm breeze, and Nafha, with a *nun*, is a cool breeze. So Allah says that even if the coolest breeze of the fire of hell were to touch them, even that is so hot. They will cry out again and again, "Ruin has come upon us. We were the wrongdoers. We were the wrongdoers without ceasing."

And so, in this same passage, Allah says they will taste no such thing as coolness — وَلَا شَرَابًا — nor any drink. Once again, keep in mind the desert life of the ancient Arabs. In the heat of that desert life, what are the two things a person longs for? A cool breeze and a drink. Allah says: I gave you all of that in the world, so that you might appreciate it, so that you might come to know my love and mercy toward you. And after providing for you, I called you toward me — for your own benefit, not for mine. And still you disobeyed me. Now I will show you what it is to be in the heat of hellfire and to have nothing cool to drink. For in Arab culture, coolness was a great pleasure.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Consider this: if you have a sibling or a friend to whom you are constantly showing kindness, and they do not value you, they take you for granted. Not only that, they do not even treat you as an ordinary friend. They do not so much as acknowledge that you exist. What do you do? You withdraw your love from them. When a child does not value the gift its parents gave, what do the parents do? They take the gift away.

So Allah says: I will take those gifts away, and replace them with what? إِلَّا حَمِيمًا وَغَسَّاقًا. These two things are the answer to Bard and Sharab. Instead of Bard, they will have boiling water to drink. Instead of becoming cool, they will now be scorched. And then, instead of a drink, instead of Sharab, He says: I will give you Ghassaq. Ghassaq is pus, or infected blood. Instead of cool water, they will be given infected pus to drink. Now they will appreciate what they had and what they took for granted.

This imagery is so terrifying. These do not sound like the words of al-Rahman and al-Rahim. Do you know whose words they sound like? Malik Yawm al-Din. And why did it come to this? Because His mercy and His compassion were not enough to convince you. Now you will be convinced. This did not have to happen. They could have answered the call of al-Rahman and al-Rahim. They chose to ignore it. They mocked it. Now the situation is very different.

Think about how you would teach a lesson to someone upon whom you pour out your love, and who in return mocks you and makes fun of you. Now you and I might think that this is a rather severe torment. This is very intense. Is it not going a little too far? Do these people truly deserve this? But then look at what He says in the next verse: جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا. Jaza means recompense. The word Jaza in itself carries the meaning that you receive exactly what you worked for. By the very meaning of the word Jaza, the recompense is complete. But then He adds the word Wifaq, and this word means that there could be no more fitting, no more perfect, no more just a recompense than the one being delivered. That is to say, the very thing these people did

For the crimes that these people committed. This is the perfect punishment that could be given to them. Down to the last ounce. This is exactly what they deserve. Not a bit less, not a bit more. جَزَآءًۭ وِفَاقًا And now the disbeliever is thinking, what have I done to deserve this kind of punishment? What did I do that was so bad that the payback for it is so painful? And Allah answers that question in the next verse. إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًۭا Now this verse is opening up the subject. There is no doubt that these were the people who had absolutely no hope that there is one day going to be a reckoning. They thought there was never going to be a day of accountability. They had no hope of accountability.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Now the wording here is very precise. It is not that they did not expect it. Allah did not say tawaqqa'un. He said yarjun. They did not hope it would happen. What is the difference between expectation and hope? When you do not expect something, that means you did not know about it. But when you hope for something not to happen, that means you have knowledge of the potential for something bad that could happen, and then you hope that it may not happen to you. That is the difference between expectation and hope. Allah did not say expectation. He used the word hope. إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًۭا There is no doubt that these people did not have the hope of accountability. They understood that everything being said is true, but then they hoped that they would not be held accountable for it. And therefore they chose to remain in their false hopes.

Do you understand? They wanted to remain deluded. They thought that if they closed their eyes, if they just ignored it, if they just did not think about it, if they just did not talk about it, these impending dangers of the afterlife would simply disappear. Is that not what we do so much of the time in life? Oh, do not talk about the exams. It is fine, we will deal with it when the time comes. How will you deal with it? You are not at all prepared for it. Oh, do not talk about that. You are depressing me. This is not the right time for me to study. I want something different for my life at this point in time. I cannot be bothered about exams right now. How do we know there is an exam? Maybe there will not be an exam. Why do we even need to have an exam? Why can it not simply be enough for us to study? Why is the school system so rigid? Why can it not be more merciful? You know, we have so much to deal with in life. Then, on top of that, we have to take exams. That is just not fair. The school system is horrible. I hate school. Why do my parents force me to go to school? I hate my parents.

So do you see how these conversations escalate? And all of it started with what? How did this whole conversation begin? It began with hoping that there would not be an exam. For the student who knows and hopes that there will be an exam, his life is completely different during the school days. He is not wasting time. He has his priorities straight. He is still having a good time. He is enjoying life. Playing video games. Having a good time with friends. But what is his priority always? His school. Because he has not lost the hope of what?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
And that, linguistically, suggests that they are in constant disagreement about it. About what? About the great news, indicated here by فِیہ. Are they asking one another mocking questions about that? Is this their attitude? These verses open in a tone of anger — the tone one takes when people treat a most serious matter without any seriousness at all.

Consider an example. Suppose I spend an hour teaching you children the story of Surah Yusuf. I tell you how Zulaykha tore his shirt from behind as he ran toward the door. I try to explain the fine points of the language, the strength of will and resolve of Yusuf, peace be upon him, against Zulaykha, the anguish of mind he passed through, and how he called upon Allah for help in those trying moments. I show you how many beautiful things there are to learn from these verses. And then one of you asks: What color was his shirt? Was it cotton? Was it one hundred percent? Was it a branded shirt? What sort of tear was it? Did the collar get torn as well, or was it in the middle? What kind of rip was it? Was he able to mend the shirt afterward? Did they even have tailors back then who repaired shirts? Then another asks: Did he have shoes on? How did he run so fast? Were they running shoes? And did the woman have long nails, since she must have had claws to tear a shirt from behind like that? Are long nails permitted for women? Is the Qur'an suggesting that women may have long nails? May they put nail polish on those nails? Is nail polish forbidden? Once you begin asking that kind of foolish question, what am I going to do at some point? I am going to lose my composure. Here is the serious matter I am trying to teach you, and here are the idiotic questions you are asking me. Would I be justified in growing angry at such questions? Certainly. What are you asking me? What is the matter with you? Do you even understand what I am speaking about? We are speaking of a prophet here. We are speaking of fleeing from temptation, and you are asking me about the brand of his shirt? What is the matter with you?

عَم يَتَسَآءَلُونَ

About what are they asking?

عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ

You know what? Joke about it all you wish. Soon you will know. Wait until the day of the examination arrives. Then you will understand whether this was a serious matter or something to be joked about.

كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ

They will very soon find out. They will soon come to know. And then He says it again:

ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
The day of the exam. Does the student who wastes his time and does not study for his exam not know that he is going to fail it? He knows. Does he not know that if he fails this exam he will not get into a good college? He knows. And when he does not get into a good college, does he not know that he will not be able to find a good job? He knows. And if he does not find a good job, does he not know that he will not be able to enjoy a good life? He knows. Yet knowing all of this, what did he hope? How does he speak to himself? This is not going to happen to me.

Now consider the same thing among Muslims. A Muslim who does not lose hope of the Day of Judgment lives very differently from the one who has lost that hope completely. The one who has lost hope will take his life in an entirely different direction, and where does it end? In hellfire, where he will have to live for a very long time, enjoying what? Heat and infected blood. Why? Because he did not take the time of comfort seriously. He could have worked hard in that short span of time and enjoyed the cool breeze and the cool drinks, but he chose not to. So now he must face the consequences of what he did.

Their false hopes led them to make wrong decisions in life. But that is not the worst thing. Do you know what the worst thing they did is? It is in the next verse. وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَتِنَا كِذَّابًۭا

So there is the inside of the disbeliever, which is false hopes, and then there is the outside of the disbeliever, which is what those false hopes manifest as. They lie against Our verses. They lie against Our miraculous revelation. I told you earlier that the signs are of two kinds. There are the Ayaat Kawniyah and there are the Ayaat Quraniyah, the creational signs and the Qur'anic signs. The Ayaat Kawniyah, the signs of creation and existence, are the mountains, the oceans, the earth, and our own bodies. The fact that we are created in pairs, the night that covers us, and the sleep we cannot avoid. These are the signs we find in our own existence. And then there are the verses, the signs of the Qur'an. This person refuses to believe. He refuses to reflect on either of them. So what do they do? وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَتِنَا كِذَّابًۭا
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Kizzab is an intensive form of Kizb. There is takzeeb, which is to lie, and there is the far worse form of it, Kizzab. This is a liar who continues to lie in the face of all possible evidence. Suppose someone tells me that they are going to hurt another person, and then, right in front of my eyes, they actually hurt that person. Now I not only had knowledge of that person's bad intentions, I also saw him commit the crime with my own eyes. Yet when I am asked about it, I lie. I say I did not see anything happen. That is Kizzab. That is defiant lying against something that was clear evidence for me. It is not as though I could have justified it with some excuse. You know how we sometimes delude ourselves in life. We make up excuses for ourselves, and we justify our lies on the basis of them. That is takzeeb. But Kizzab suggests that these people had so much evidence before them that there was no way in which they could deny the truth.

They chose to lie about it instead. That is the word Kizzab. What happens in this world when there is no sense of accountability, even to the laws of a country? There would be complete anarchy. It would simply be a natural consequence. The powerful would triumph over the poor. The big fish would swallow the small fish. It would be the law of the jungle.

So these people saw Allah's ayats, His miraculous signs. They saw that what these signs point to is the truth, that it is reality. Their hearts accepted it as reality. Yet they chose to lie about it. So this passage is explaining the reasons at length. Why are these people facing such terrible punishments and the fire of Hell? And how are these punishments in fact perfectly balanced against their crimes? Because these were the people who hoped that there would be no day of accountability. And even though the miraculous signs were made plain to them, both within the Qur'an and outside it, they still lied profusely and continuously against Our signs, against Our messengers, against Our revelation. To lie against someone, or to belie someone who is speaking the truth. So these people are not worthy of any leniency now. They are not worthy of any mercy. And they thought that all their deeds, all their sins, were going unnoticed. But guess what?

وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ كِتَٰبًۭا

Their every last thing. Not only their deeds, but even their intentions, their thoughts, their judgments, their arrogance, their pride, their hypocrisy, their contempt, their actions, their cruelty. Each and every last thing. We have completely encompassed. أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ. Ahsaa, in modern Arabic, means to count, like Adad. But there is a difference between Ihsaa and Adad. The difference is that Ihsaa is to count something and also to protect it.

وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ كِتَٰبًۭا
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
To archive it and to save it. And to have complete protection over it, so that no one else and nothing else can modify it. It means that you are not going to lose your data. You know that accountants can do their accounting in the books, and the books can be destroyed. They could be burned in a fire. Or the hard drive could crash, or something of the sort. But Ihsaa is not merely that you counted it, but also that it is protected and preserved. Allah says that We have not only counted it but We have also protected it. In Kitaaba, in a record, in a written document. Allah has placed two angels upon our shoulders, who write down everything we do. The angel on the right hand writes down all the good that we do, and the angel on the left hand writes down all the bad that we do. These are the records.

فَذُوقُوا۟ فَلَن نَّزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذَابًا

Now go ahead and taste this punishment. If you look at the ayats that came before, Wa Kazzabo, they lied against it, that is third person. There is more distance in that ayah. But now in this verse, Allah says Fazooqoo, all of you taste. It has simply changed from third person to second person. It is not they taste. It is now you all taste. This transition from third person to second person illustrates the intensity of Allah's anger. And it is also an indication that something you feel today to be far away.

This is soon going to be close. The third person refers to something far away, and the second person to something close. Even in the workings of language, this is so. So today you lie against my miraculous signs; today you mock the day of judgment, because that day is far from you. But soon it will be upon your heads. When you see the fire of hell with your own eyes, when you sense and feel its heat upon yourselves, when you taste the pain and the torments of those punishments — now Allah says: now taste this punishment. It comes even closer. From "they" to "you," and now "taste." The one who tastes is the one who truly experiences. It has shifted to the self. SubhanAllah. What you think is so far away will soon be near — so near that you will actually taste it. All of that carried by a single grammatical turn in the sentence. SubhanAllah.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
So Allah says: now go ahead and taste. We will not increase you in anything except further punishment. Allahu akbar. Because when I kept increasing my mercy upon you, when I kept increasing my love and care and mercy upon you, you rejected it. You lied against it. You lied against ME, the Lord of the Worlds. Now taste the punishment I warned you of, but which you mocked and derided. Now I will increase my punishment upon you. You will beg for what you rejected in this world. You will beg for coolness and for drink — the comforts I showered upon you throughout your life, which you kept denying. I kept increasing them, and you rejected. I increased them still more, and you still rejected. Today you will have none of that. The only thing that will increase for you is pain and torment. You will beg me for a little coolness, a little drink, a little comfort. And you will get nothing in return. The only thing you will get is more pain and punishment — so that now you can know what rejection feels like. When I was showering you with comforts, instead of coming toward me, you rejected me and turned away from me. Now I will reject you and turn away from you, so that you can understand how my beloved messenger felt. You can feel his pain now.

Now the pages have been turned. And now Allah changes the tone and speaks to the believers, who are being tortured and afflicted by the cruelties of these people who do not believe in the day of judgment. They mock the prophet; they mock the believers; they constantly hurt them, in body as well as in heart. So after warning the disbelievers, Allah now turns to the believers — who do believe in Allah, who do believe in a day of judgment, who do believe in accountability, who do appreciate the miraculous signs of existence and of the Qur'an. Now Allah turns to them and says: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا. No doubt, there is great success for the people of taqwa. Not even "believers" here. He does not say "believers." He does not say ان للذین آمنو. He says إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ. The people of taqwa — why? Taqwa is generally understood as fear, meaning the fear of Allah. That is not truly its meaning. That is خوف اللہ, the fear of Allah. For example, we see in the Qur'an: انی اخاف اللہ رب العالمین.

Taqwa in fact means the precautions you take out of fear — the things you do because you are afraid. So when you lock the doors of your house at night, you are exercising taqwa. When you travel somewhere and you make certain that your passport is with you, that you have the money for the journey, that your luggage is packed — because you want to be sure you will not run into trouble at the airport or when you reach your destination — all of that is taqwa. When you do not want to fail your examination and you study hard on that account, that is taqwa. So any precaution taken as the result of a fear is taqwa. فَتَزَوَّدُو فَأِنَّ الَخیرَ الزَّاد التَّقوی
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Taqwa, then, is literally to take precaution. Allah also says in the Qur'an: فتقو النار — take precaution against the hellfire. Do certain things, refrain from certain things, act in a way that will ensure you do not enter the hellfire. This is precaution. So make sure that you protect yourself, because if you do not protect yourself, if you do not take the necessary precautions, you will end up in the hellfire. These are the people of taqwa, the people of piety. Taqwa is more than a feeling. Taqwa is a feeling that issues in some kind of action: you do something to protect yourself. This is taqwa.

So now Allah says: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا — those who took the necessary precaution, who, when they heard these signs, these verses, took certain actions to make sure they would not end up where they were being warned about. What does Allah have for them? Mafaza. Mafaza comes from fawz, on which, if you remember, we did a whole session on this one word. Mafaza means three things. It means success. It means a place of success, that is, Jannah. And it means the time of success, the experience of success within Jannah. It means all three things at once. So Allah is telling the believers: be patient. All of that is coming. Just as these disbelievers are not seeing their punishment right now, you are not seeing your reward right now. But just as their punishment is soon coming to them, your reward is soon coming to you as well. It is not right there with you at this moment, but it is guaranteed for you; that time of success is guaranteed for you. And what is that success? حَدَآئِقَ وَأَعْنَبًۭا
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
And they will most certainly come to know. Now, why did Allah repeat it a second time? You know that there are various stages of knowledge. You can know a thing by reading about it. So I know that accidents are dangerous because I read about it in a storybook. That is one level of knowledge. It is called عِلْمُ الْيَقِین, certainty based on knowledge. I can make light of it; I can crack jokes about it. But when I witness a car accident with my own eyes, I truly know that car accidents are dangerous. Now that is a different kind of knowledge, a stronger form of it. It is called عَیْنُ الْیَقِین, certainty based on witnessing a thing. Now I will not joke about it, because now I know how gravely dangerous car accidents can be. And then, if I actually get into a car accident myself,

then I truly, truly, truly know that car accidents are dangerous. That is the greatest form of knowledge; that is the strongest form of knowledge, حق الیقین, the certainty of direct experience, because now I have actually lived through it. And now, will I ever joke about it? No.

So on what basis are these disbelievers mocking the Day of Judgment? On the basis of علم الیقین. They are merely listening to the Messenger of Allah, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, speak about the Day of Judgment. To them it is theoretical, and that is why they make fun of it. But when they die and stand before Allah, will they then witness the fire of hell? Will they see it with their own eyes? That is the first warning:

كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ

They will come to know about that great and momentous news. They will know it truly, when they are raised from the ground and made to stand directly before the fire of hell, and they cry out, realizing that all of this is real. The Qur'an tells us so:

قَالُوا۟ يَوَيْلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَاۜ ۗ

What is happening here? Who has woken us from our sleep? What is going on?

هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمَنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

This is what the Most Merciful promised you while you were in the world. This verse, I must say, astonishes me: هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمَنُ, this is what the Most Merciful promised. They are undergoing the torments of hell, and Allah says that this is what was promised by ٱلرَّحْمَن, the Intensely Merciful. At first glance this does not seem to make sense. How can Allah be called the Most Merciful in such a situation? Why not:

هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ ذو انتقام، الجبار، القوی، القھار، ، العزیز

Yet ٱلرَّحْمَن? Why? Because He was offering you such kind and gentle warnings. With love, He kept asking you to set yourself right. You simply did not care. Now, when it is too late, you care. Now you realize how gentle He was being before, how harsh He could have been, and how He chose not to be. Only then do you realize what the Most Merciful truly means. One of the things we will realize on the Day of Judgment is how loving, soft, kind, gentle, merciful, and forgiving Allah has been all along. You and I may not realize this today, but on the Day of Judgment we will realize it, when we see what power He holds and what He is capable of doing.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Consider, for example, a parent who spoils a child, who only gives and gives, until the child grows used to it. Then that parent is gone, and the child is sent to a foster home where the warden treats him without care. That is when he realizes how good he had it all along. All the love his parents showered upon him is now gone, and he realizes what he has lost, and the mistakes he made. Now he appreciates their kindness.

So they used to joke about the Day of Judgment and make fun of it. But now, standing before it, they will truly know that this was no laughing matter. Then they will know that this was a serious affair. Why? Because now they possess عین الیقین; they are witnessing the Day of Judgment with their own eyes. It is no longer theoretical. And then Allah repeats it:

ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ

After that, they will again come to know. What is this now? It is the stage of حق الیقین, where they will actually experience the fire of hell. That is why the word ثم is used, which means "after that." First they will witness it with their eyes, عین الیقین, and after that they will enter it and truly experience it.

That is حق الیقین. But then the subject switches.

أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ ..... وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًۭا ..... وَخَلَقْنَكُمْ أَزْوَجًۭا ..... وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا ..... وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًۭا ..... وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلنَّهَارَ مَعَاشًۭا ..... وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًۭا شِدَادًۭا ..... وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًۭا وَهَّاجًۭا

He had been speaking about the disbelievers, and about how they mock the day of judgment, and how they will soon find out that none of this is a joking matter when they see the fire of hell. And now the topic of the conversation changes. And you can see that the rhyme scheme changes too. We studied this when we looked at the miracles of the Qur'an, remember? When the topic of a surah goes off on a new course, the rhyme scheme changes with it.

So do you know what Allah does in the verses that follow? He begins to compare his own creations with the creations of human beings. You think you are so remarkable. You think you are powerful. Let us make a comparison. And now Allah begins to set his own power and his own magnificence before their faces. And, by the way, this whole imagery is drawn from the life of the desert.

Allah says:

أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ مِهَدًۭا

Did we not make the earth into a mihaad? مھاد comes from the word مھد, which means a cradle. When a mother holds her baby in her arms, that is called a مھد — comforting it, protecting it, the neck supported, the back not bent over. She cradles the child perfectly, for the child's comfort. Allah says: I made the entire world a mihaad for you. The most beautiful image of sleep is the image of a child, is it not? Allah says: I made the entire world as comfortable for you as a mother's cradle. What bedding will you set against it?

وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًۭا
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
And I made the mountains as pegs. So the mother cradles the baby, and then she walks into her tent. What holds the tent together? The pegs — the اوتاد! Allah says: look at your pegs and compare them to my tents. And, by the way, what shape does a tent have? A mountain! Allah says: look at your tents, and look at my tents. This is what you made, and this is what I made. Just to look at my mountains should fill you with awe, because this is what you construct, and this is what I construct. Our abilities and our capabilities — or rather our inabilities and our incapabilities — are what this verse is comparing. Who do you think you are? What makes you think you can joke about these things? Oh, you think you will see Allah's powers only then? What about now? What about right here?

وَخَلَقْنَكُمْ أَزْوَجًۭا

And we created you in pairs. This is not only male and female. It is about compatibility. The word zawj means compatible. He made the one physically stronger and made the other physically weaker. He made the one rugged, and made the other soft and delicate and beautiful, so that there could be attraction between the two. Allah says: I created you, physically, as the compatible half of another half. We did not design ourselves. That was set in place for us. And, by the way, azwaj also means social groups. We created you into social groups. We created you into different kinds of nations, different kinds of classes within nations, different kinds of cliques, different kinds of friends. Even within a group of friends, there are some you always spend time with more than others, because of the mental compatibility. That is a zawj.

When you have a friend who completes you, and whom you complete, that is a zawj. One of you is quick to anger, the other has a calming effect; the two balance each other. One rushes to get things done, the other thinks them through; the two balance each other. They complete one another. This, too, is zawj.

But do you know what Allah is truly speaking of here? He is speaking of the perfect companions He has created within us. A zawj is like the two halves of a whole. One is incomplete without the other. However perfect a thing may be in its existence, its shape, or its form, it means nothing without its partner. Take the eyes. He gave us eyes, and He gave us sight, the ability to see, as their zawj. Sight is the perfect companion of the eye. You may have the most beautiful eyes in the world, eyes that poets would praise in verse, but if those eyes cannot see, do they mean anything to you? No. That is the perfection of zawj. He joined the eye with sight, the ears with the sense of hearing, the nose with the sense of smell, the tongue with the sense of taste.

And zawj also means the one that balances the other perfectly. So He made the left eye and balanced it with the right eye. He made the left nostril and balanced it with the right nostril; the left ear and the right ear; the left hand and the right hand. Perfect balance, perfect zawj. Perfect balance. SubhanAllah!
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
And do you know what is symbolized by a balance or a scale? Justice. He created all of us, and every part of our bodies, with perfect justice, with perfect balance. Picture a scale. There is one upright post in the center, and then a tray on each side. Now, for this scale to be accurate, the tray on each side must be exactly the same, must it not? They must be made from the very same material, have the very same shape and size, and weigh exactly the same. Is that not so? If it is not so, you will never have balance. You will never have justice. Do you agree?

Allah says: I created you with perfect balance. Only look at yourselves. Every part of the body that lies at the center is single, and every part that lies to the side comes as a pair. Two eyes, two ears, two cheeks, all to the sides. One nose, at the center. Two nostrils, because they are to the side. One mouth, at the center. Two hands, two feet, one heart, one navel, two kidneys to the side, two lungs. SubhanAllah!

Allah says: this is the perfection of My creation. Look at what you make, and look at what I make. Today we see so much architecture built with perfect symmetry and balance. Where do you suppose all of that is drawn from?

So Allah says: وَخَلَقْنَكُمْ أَزْوَجًۭا. I created you as these perfect pairs within your very body. Your body itself. And then as man and woman. How can you say there is no god? Can you not see the perfection of this pairing? Pairs upon pairs upon pairs. I gave you eyes, I gave you sight; I created beauty so that you might see it and cherish it. I created the sun that brightens the world around you so that you might appreciate that beauty. I could have given you eyes, given you sight,

created magnificent beauty, and yet not created the light of the sun. Would any of it be of use? Only reflect on the pairing I have arranged. And still you mock me? Still you deny that I exist? I gave you lungs, and I also gave you oxygen. I set in motion this natural, cyclical process in which plants convert carbon dioxide into oxygen, so that your supply of it never fails. Consider this pairing as well. SubhanAllah!

وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا

And We made your sleep a severing for you. SubhanAllah! This is one of my favorite verses. Subaat means, quite literally, a cutting, a severing; سَبَتَ الشَّعَر is said of one who takes hold of a lock of hair and cuts it off. And Naum is deep sleep.

ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌۭ وَلَا نَوْمٌۭ

Sina is light sleep, the moment when you are about to drift off; that is sina. Nawm is deep sleep. Raqad is long sleep. When you fall asleep and wake a week later, that is raqad; when you sleep for a very long time in a very comfortable bed, that is raqad. And it is used figuratively as well, to describe someone who is utterly gone.

وَتَحْسَبُهُمْ أَيْقَاظًۭا وَهُمْ رُقُودٌۭ

You suppose them awake, but they are in the deepest of sleep; they are long gone. That is, they are so sunk in their ignorance that they can never be roused from it.
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
Allah says: I made your sleep a severing for you. What a beautiful experience this is. People question the day of judgment; they question the existence of Allah; they question the signs of Allah. And Allah says: you do not even have control over your own body. I cut you off from all the things you wish to do. Your body fails you, and your eyes close. You long to finish that program, and you fall asleep in the middle of the episode. You have a great examination before you, and you truly wish to study; you drink cup of coffee after cup of coffee, and still you doze off. You want to keep playing, you want to keep playing, but your eyes give out and you pass into sleep. You cannot even remain awake. Your sleep cuts you off from the work you were doing, the film you were watching, the entertainment you were enjoying, the conversation you were holding. Allah says: will you not reflect upon your sleep, upon how it overturns all your plans? You can get no work done while you sleep. You cannot hold a conversation while you sleep. You cannot finish your assignments while you sleep. You cannot advance your business while you sleep. All of it is gone. You are dead to the world, and the world is dead to you. You are finished!

وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا

It is as though Allah were saying: every single night I give you the experience of being cut off from this world. Sleep is one of the most powerful spiritual reminders of the day of judgment.

You are a great and mighty figure in life. "I am the president of my company. I am the leader of my group. I am the owner of the firm. I am so powerful." But what are you when you are fast asleep? What are you when you are in deep sleep? You are as weak as a newborn kitten. You are as helpless as a lifeless corpse. Allah says: when your sleep cuts you off from this world,

do you not see what you are reduced to? If you are fast asleep, and someone wishes to harm you — to cut off your head, or merely to amuse himself at your expense, to paint your face and turn you into a clown — do you not see how helpless you are in that state? Why do you not reflect upon it? Do you know why it is worth reflecting upon? Because a time is coming when you and I will be cut off from this world, severed from it, and never rejoined to it again. That is death.

And then we will stand before Allah, as weak and as helpless as we are during our sleep. Allahu Akbar. This is how weak you are, in this very life. Do you not see how your own sleep serves as a daily reminder of how weak you are? And you intend to stand against me? To mock My Day of Judgment?
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
There is another beauty in this reminder of sleep. You know how our today depends upon our yesterdays. The life we are going to live today is built upon the actions of the days before it. Is that not true? I was kind and loving to my parents yesterday, and so today I enjoy their smile and their love. I studied for my examination yesterday, and so today I succeed in it. I left the half-eaten pizza on the floor of my room today, and so I must wake to its stench the next day. Our days today rest upon how we lived our lives in the days that came before. Is that not so? The one who did not study and prepare for his examination has no right to complain when he fails it. Correct? He must simply grit his teeth and face the consequence of his own actions.

So our today rests upon our yesterday. And what draws that distinction? What is the separator? Sleep. One day we will all enter an eternal sleep, and that is death. And we will wake into another day, called what? The Day of Judgment. Now imagine that day is today. Imagine we are no longer in the Sunday Sessions, but that we are all now in the afterlife — in the Judgment Day sessions. And what brought us here? Our eternal sleep, our death. And now an eternal life lies ahead of us. Upon what will this eternal life be based? It will be based upon our yesterdays, which are what? Our life in this present world.

A time is coming when our future days in the afterlife will depend upon our present days today. If we desire a good life in those days, when must we live a good life? In these days, today. And our definition of a good life must match whose criteria? Allah's criteria. After all, our future lies in His kingdom, does it not? To enter Cambridge or Harvard, you must meet their requirements, you must meet their selection criteria, must you not?

وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا

We have made sleep a severing for you. This is a very powerful reminder for us. SubhanAllah.

Now another beautiful reminder — one that has helped me tremendously and continues to help me every single day. Those of you who recite the morning supplication, the one the Messenger of Allah used to recite every morning upon waking:

الحمد للہ الذی أحیانا بعد ما أماتنا

Praise and gratitude to Allah, who gave us life again after we were dead. Wow! Wait a moment. What is that? I was not dead!
body.topic_title_en: The Master of the Day of Judgment: Surah al-Naba

body.text_en:
We're studying the Isti'aza. اعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم

We studied the words *A'udhu*, *Shaytan*, and *Rajim*. We saw the difference between the words *Shaytan* and *Iblis*. *Shaytan* comes from the adjective *shatana*, which means the one that is far removed, and so this adjective, this label, applies to anyone, whether human or jinn. Anyone who is far removed from the mercy of Allah is called *Shaytan*. We studied that *Rajim* means someone who is cast away, stoned away, pelted away, is called *Rajim*. So *Shaytan* by his NATURE is far removed from Allah's mercy, and he is *Rajim*. He is pelted away, cast away because of his actions. In contrast to that, *Iblis* is actually an entity. He was the angel who refused the command of Allah. He refused to prostrate to Adam, upon him be peace, because of his pride and arrogance, and his underlying jealousy against Adam, upon him be peace. And that is what earned him the name *Iblis*. *Iblis* comes from the word *ablasa*, which means "despair." He completely gave up hope in the mercy of Allah, and that is what made him *Iblis*. *Iblis* gave up hope in the mercy of Allah. And because of that, what does he want? He wants to have everyone far removed from the same mercy of Allah that he gave up hope in. So the goal of *Iblis* is to create an army of *shayatin*, an army of people who will be far removed from Allah's mercy (*Shaytan*) and pelted away because of their despicable actions (*Rajim*).

So the Isti'aza is our seeking Allah's protection from all *shayatin*. And from that we came to the two words مستعاذ بہ and مستعاذ منہ. *Musta'adh Bihi*: seeking protection OF, meaning Allah. *Musta'adh Minhu*: seeking protection FROM, meaning *Shaytan al-Rajim*. So we are running FROM the *Shaytan*, and we are running TO the protection of Allah.

And then we have two surahs, Surah al-Falaq and Surah al-Nas, that are the surahs explaining the استعاذہ. These two surahs explain what exactly we are seeking protection from, and what it means to actually seek the protection of Allah. Surah al-Nas is primarily *Musta'adh Bihi*, because Allah is mentioned three times and protection from evil is mentioned once. Whereas we saw Surah al-Falaq is primarily *Musta'adh Minhu*, because Allah is mentioned once and protection from evil is mentioned three times. So there is this beautiful symmetry and perfection that we see between the two surahs.

Then we looked at the historical background of why these surahs were revealed. They were revealed together, first Surah al-Falaq and then Surah al-Nas. And it was revealed as an antidote for the magic that was performed on the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by Lubaid ibn Asim and his daughters. These surahs are basically Allah stepping forward to protect His beloved messenger, Muhammad Mustafa, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, against the evil of the *kuffar* and *mushrikin*.

Now let us start linguistically analyzing Surah al-Falaq. Allah says: قل أعوذ برب الفلق

We have already looked at the word أعوذ, but let us just go over it again, and then look at the word *falaq*, and then come back to *Qul*. So the word أعوذ has several forms in morphology, as we saw previously: أعاذ، یعیذُ. You can say یعوِّذ، تعویذ، أستعیذ, so several forms are used, even in the Qur'an. For example:

فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

Similarly, Hazrat Maryam, peace of Allah be upon her, says:

وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

So there are many variations of this word.

But the root word عاذ means to seek the spiritual protection of a deity. It also means to cling to someone for protection, to hold on to someone and not let go, out of fear of something dangerous that is unseen. It is like a child who wakes from a nightmare and clings to its mother. So it means to cling to someone out of fear of the unseen. The key word here is unseen. It is dangers that cannot be seen.

If you want protection from an enemy who is attacking you, the word is أجارۃ. أجارۃ means to give someone protection against a physical enemy, an enemy who can be seen. But for unseen things — jealousy, sorcery, satanic whispers, and the like — the word is استعاذ. Hence أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم. We seek Allah's protection. أعوذ باللہ is protection against an enemy who cannot be seen. And it is also used in the sense of clinging to someone and not letting go.

We also have the word معاذ. معاذ is a place where you can find refuge. You may have heard معاذ اللہ. It means a place, a very secure place that has Allah's protection from the unseen. This word was used by Yusuf, peace be upon him. وَرَوَدَتْهُ ٱلَّتِى هُوَ فِى بَيْتِهَا عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ وَغَلَّقَتِ ٱلْأَبْوَبَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ ۚ قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِ. When Zulekha closed the doors on him and trapped him, he said معاذ اللہ. He sought Allah's refuge, a place that could protect him from the evil intentions of this woman, and so he said معاذ اللہ.

Now, why do linguists take issue with the translation "I seek refuge" for أعوذ باللہ? They disagree with that rendering, because if you say أعوذ باللہ means "I seek refuge," then how do you translate أَستَعِیذُ? In Arabic أستعاذا means to seek. Therefore أَستَعِیذُ means "I seek refuge." So then what does أعوذ mean? Linguists say that عاذ actually means "I am entering into the refuge." I am giving myself into the refuge of Allah. I am not merely seeking it. It is not that I only want it. I am actually giving myself. I am surrendering myself to it. From a linguistic point of view, it is an act of complete submission when you say اعوذ. You are saying, "I have no power to protect myself. I am therefore giving myself up to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for protection." It is one thing to say that I want to do that, that it would be a good idea to do it. But it is an entirely different thing to declare openly that I am in fact doing it: I am giving myself up to Allah for protection, because I cannot do it myself. Do you understand?

أَستَعِیذُ باللہ means "I am seeking Allah's protection." I want Allah's protection. But أعوذ means that I do not only want it, I am not only seeking it. I am actually giving myself up. I am surrendering myself to Allah's protection. So Allah says in the Qur'an: فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ. Seek protection from Shaytan. And in response, we do not say, "All right, I am seeking protection." We say أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم. We say, "I willingly and completely give myself up. I surrender. I submit myself into the protection of Allah from Shaytan."

Falaq

He became arrogant, thinking: خلقتنی من نار و خلقتہ من تین. I am created from fire. Adam is created from clay. Therefore انا خیر منہ. I am better than him. It was the choice of that angel that turned him into Iblees. Allah never created Iblees. And that is the evil we seek Allah's protection from: protection from the evil of His creation. Because the harm and the evil are caused by the creation. That is why we turn toward the protection of the Rabb of creation, the Rabb of Al-Falaq and the Rabb of An-Naas. The one who created the creation is more powerful than the creation, and therefore He can protect us from it. He can save us from its harm. Because in the end, Allah alone is the master of the creation, the creation that tries to cause harm by doing evil. Allah has power over all creation; therefore He also has power over the harm that His creation is capable of producing.

So the شر in these verses is not attributed to Allah. It is attributed to His creation. The bottom line in Islamic studies, when it comes to the concept of شر, is that evil is not actually an entity in and of itself. It is considered only the absence of good. It is just like darkness, the imagery of tawheed and shirk, of darkness and light. Darkness does not actually exist. There is no physics or chemistry of darkness. What actually exists is light. When you do not have light, what do you have? You have darkness. So darkness in and of itself is not an actual entity. It is goodness that is the entity, and a lack of goodness is what evil is. Therefore evil, in the end, is nothing but a lack of good. Do you understand?

But this verse holds profound lessons within it, because Allah left the language open and universal. When He said مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ, He did not reduce it to shayaateen, to devils. The evil in the next surah, من شر الوسواس الخناس, speaks of a very specific creation. But when He said مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ, He said: whatever was created. From the harm of whatever was created. Do you know what we learn from this? We learn that there is no creation on the face of this earth that comes without a flaw. The only one free of all flaw is Allah AWJ Himself. SubhanAllah! Every creation besides Allah has some inherent flaw in it. Something will be missing in it. Some element of شر is possible from everything.

Think of the most amazing creations of Allah, like the sun. So very many benefits come from the sun. But are there harms as well? Yes, there are. Do people die because of sunstroke? Do plants get destroyed because of excessive heat? Its benefits are beyond measure, but it can cause harm as well.

There are so many benefits from water. But can water cause harm and damage as well? Floods? Tsunamis?

There are so many benefits in the earth. But are there harms in the earth too?

So many benefits from the sky. Are there harms that come down from the sky also?

So everything that Allah has created has an element of harm, of شر, in it. So we ask Allah AWJ to protect us from the potential harmful elements of everything, things that are above and beyond our perceptions. Think of a car: very beneficial for human beings. But can it be harmful? Can you die in a car accident? Can you get injured? All of that is possible. So every element, every creation, has that element of harm in it. So we ask Allah for His protection from all possible harm, from all of His creation.

مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ.

Ghasaq. Then Allah says: وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ. In Arabic literature, غَسَق is regarded as اول الیل, the first part of the night. In other words, when the blue of the sky is gone and everything has turned black — that is غَسَق. Allah says: أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِدُلُوكِ ٱلشَّمْسِ إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ ٱلَّيْلِ. Allah says: establish prayer from the setting of the sun until the night grows deep. That is غَسَقِ ٱلَّيْلِ.

Now the word غَاسِقٍ is also used in the literature for that which sinks, or that which disappears. In that sense we find the word غَسَق used even for the sun and the moon. For example, غسق القمر, when there is a lunar eclipse, is called ghasaq al-qamar. غَسَقَتْ عَیْنُہُ means the eyes grew dark with tears — when a person weeps too much and bags form around the eyes, it is called غسق العیُون. غسقت السمآء is said when the sky becomes truly dark with clouds, when it is daytime yet it feels like night, and there is very heavy rain; that is called غسقت السمآء.

So what are these expressions telling us? Allah is referring to a time in the night when it is completely and absolutely dark. But He does not stop there. He goes a step further and says: إِذَا وَقَبَ. He begins the verse by saying مِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ, from the evil and harm of the dark night itself, meaning that Allah is saying there is potential harm inherently present in the darkness itself.

The Messenger of Allah would advise his companions not to go out at night. He would say: if you knew what I know, you would not step out at night. The devils hold their gatherings and their meetings in the night. And even in our society today, when is it that people act like the devil? On Friday and Saturday nights. Watch the documentaries made about the emergency rooms in America. Do you know when the emergency rooms are full? On Friday and Saturday nights. They are full: car accidents, people killing one another after a few beers, drugs, alcohol, assaults. When does all that evil take place? At night. Subhan Allah. The potential for evil is far greater in the darkness of the night, and of course that is why travel at night is dangerous. You will most likely not go out late at night. You would certainly not let your children go out or stay out in the middle of the night. It is in human nature. So we ask Allah to protect us from those dark evils of the night, the evil of غسق.

There is something interesting I want to share with you about غسق, especially غسق القمر, when it is used for a lunar eclipse. Some very interesting studies have been done recently about the moon. This used to be considered folklore, but now there are actual studies about it: that when there is a full moon, it has an effect on the tides of the ocean. The tides of the ocean change. It becomes high tide, and the waters gain a tendency to become violent. Now, the human body also has fluids inside it. So do you think the magnetic pull of the full moon has any effect on a human being? There are in fact studies being done on this. There are people who tend to become more violent when there is a full moon. You know that whole genre of mythical literature, about werewolves and things of that kind — it is a fantasized version of these facts. They are an exaggeration of an actual scientific phenomenon, in which people experience psychological changes and agitation during certain cycles of the moon.

This is actually documented physiological behavior. Glory be to God! People begin to act insanely. And that is in fact where the English word "lunatic" comes from — you know, like "crazy," "lunatic." It comes from "lunar." Even in older tradition this was understood. Glory be to God!

So God says مِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ. But then He adds on, إِذَا وَقَبَ. Now what does وَقَبَ mean? In the literature, وَقَبَ is also a reference to darkness. So it is like saying, from the evil of the dark night when it grows dark. But it is already dark! So what is this growing dark all over again, and why a different word for it? Because وقب الظلام means that the night grows so dark that things begin to become invisible. وَقَبَ is used when things grow so dark that they disappear from sight. You know, it is like a ditch inside a mountain at night, and something goes down into that ditch in the middle of a dark night. Now you cannot see it anymore. That is in fact called وَقَبَ. So there are things hiding in the dark that we cannot see. This includes the shayateen. I told you that عاذ، استعاذ، أعوذ in Arabic is used for seeking protection from things that are unseen, invisible, that you cannot see. So the verse is using apt and perfect language when it says we are seeking refuge from the evils of the dark night, especially when it hides things inside itself, when there are things lurking in the dark that we cannot see. So we are asking protection from these kinds of things that we do not have the ability to perceive for ourselves, and God teaches us about them.

وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ

This is precisely the context I mentioned to you at the beginning. God called out نفاثات, which is in fact a feminine plural. In modern Arabic this would mean the women who blow on knots, and scholars say this is attributed to the daughters of Labid ibn Asim, who blew spells on the knots. That is what it is referring to. But نفاثات could be an adjective of نُفُوس or أنفس, meaning people! The word نفس in Arabic is considered feminine, and its adjectives are considered feminine too. Now the word نفاثات could also refer to groups, because many times this sort of sorcery and dark magic, things like that, are done in groups. The word نَفَثَ actually means to blow with a little bit of spit coming out. It is a soft, wet blow. If you blow really hard out of your mouth, the word is نفخ, like:

وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَجَمَعْنَٰهُمْ جَمْعًۭا

That is نفخ. When the root words are close in Arabic, the meanings are close in Arabic too. نَفَثَ — this is with a tha, with three dots. But if you say نَفَسَ with a سin, that actually means breath. تَنَفَّسَ means to draw breath. حیاتُکَ أَنفَاس, the poet says: your life is nothing more than a set of breaths. You are going to draw these breaths in and out, and eventually it will all be done. So نَفَثَ, نفخ with a tha with three dots, and نَفَسَ with a seen, they all have shared meanings.

And by the way, نفاثات is the one who blows over and over and over again, engaging in the acts of trying to produce this magic فی العقد, into knots. So we surrender to God for protection from those who perform magic. Now there are some very interesting interpretations for the various words used in this verse. So ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ, the ones who blow on knots. So the knots exist first, and then they blow on them.

And I have just told you that نفاثات is an act of blowing over and over and over again. It is not a one-time thing. If you merely go "Phoo," that is not nafatha. Nafatha implies constant, repeated blowing. Do you follow? And blowing upon what? Upon knots, عُقَد. This is interpreted as those people who harbor the intention of creating constraints for someone. That is what knots are, is it not? Evil people who intend to trap others in a situation, in an emotion, in a difficult position. All of this is drawn from عُقَد. And how do they accomplish it? By blowing upon them constantly. That is to say, they are perpetually gossiping, spreading rumors, poisoning the minds of others against a certain individual, in order to constrain, in order to restrict.

One person does not like another; one person becomes jealous of another. They wish to stop the other from whatever he is doing. So what do they do? They try to create roadblocks. They try to halt him. And how do they do it? By quietly gossiping, by planting doubts in the minds of others, by attacking his character, his knowledge, his credibility, in very, very subtle ways, and over and over and over again, a little at a time on every occasion. "I mean well! I am doing this for you. I do not want you to be hurt by this person. I am looking out for you." So all such gossip and rumor is presented for your benefit. But what is the aim? To turn you against the other person. And what happens is that now you believe that it is you who dislikes that person. You feel this sense of negativity welling up from within yourself. But it had nothing to do with you. It was blown into you over and over and over again, until now you believe that you are the source of that hatred. And then it is you who ends up creating the roadblock. It is you who ends up creating the obstacle.

I truly want you to pause for a moment and reflect upon this. It was the other person who wished to create the roadblock. It was the other person who wished to stop this someone. But with his naffathat fil uqad, what does he do? He uses you to carry it out on his behalf. You end up being the one who actually creates the obstacles for this person. Is that not exactly what magic is? Does the one suffering from magic know that he is a victim of magic? No, he does not! He simply begins to feel sick. He begins to feel ill, stressed, depressed. But all this while, it was the doing of someone else! Can you grasp how sinister and horrible this evil is? نعوذ باللہ من ذالک. May Allah protect us all from this.

This is why, when you hear someone gossiping, you should put an end to it right there and then. And be alert to when this verbal magic is being worked upon you. Because the one who is inciting you against someone or something, against an elder, against religion, against the duaat, that is exactly what he is doing. He is casting a spell upon you. In order to do what? To create problems and constraints and restrictions against the one he wishes to harm. He will incite, but you will become his hands! He will use you as his tools to actually perform the evil deed. He will use you to carry out the actual evil. You will be the one to disobey the elder, to insult him, to be rude to him. You will be the one actually mocking Islam. You will be the one actually denying the existence of Allah. May Allah protect us all, first of all from committing this horrible, evil act.

and then from the effects of those who act in such ways against us. The final part of it is this: وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ.

Here you must appreciate something. There is always the problem, and then there is the root of the problem. The first part of the surah dealt with the problems. But this last verse takes you to the root of the problem. Why would someone perform magic against another person? Why would someone cast a spell on another? Why would someone want to spread rumors and poison others against a person? Why would someone want to harm another? It is jealousy. It is always jealousy. They do not want the other to have what they have. They do not want the other to succeed. They want the other to fail. So the root of the problem is mentioned at the end: وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ.

Observe anyone who engages in the act of jealousy. Observe it when it shows itself in you. It will always come from your own inability to bear someone receiving something better than you. Even at the lowest levels. One man works as a janitor. Another man also works as a janitor, but he is given the metal broom and you are given the plastic one, and now you want this man fired. It can truly be something as pathetic as that. Or it can be about land, money, wealth, or a woman. It can be based on anything. Matters of inheritance. Matters of importance. It can be anything.
