It is all around us. Friends becoming jealous of friends. A daughter-in-law becoming jealous of her in-laws. Mothers-in-law becoming jealous of their daughters-in-law. This is a real evil. I mean jealousy, not mothers-in-law.

Now, it is one thing to feel jealousy inside, and it is another to act it out, to do something about it. Someone can feel jealous but then choose not to do anything about it. I feel it, but I am not going to act on it. Do we say that? Have you heard others say that? Allah says that if you actually have حسد within you, it is inevitable that you will end up doing something evil. He did not say وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِن حَسَدَ — from the evil of the jealous person if he acts on his jealousy. No. He said إِذَا حَسَدَ — when he acts out his jealousy. What is the difference between if and when? If may or may not happen. What does when mean? It is definitely going to happen. If there is a person who has حسد, it will definitely show itself in one way or another, whether it be the evil eye, or manipulations, or schemes, or even in a conversation with someone else. It will surely appear. And that is why we have to seek refuge from it.

Now, if you notice, إِذَا حَسَدَ is redundant. Allah has already said وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ — from the evil of the jealous person. Why does He have to say from the evil of the jealous person when he is acting out his jealousy? Because حسد is a dormant quality. حاسد, on the other hand, is an active quality. So this protection of Allah is not for the mere feeling of حسد. It is not for that dormant feeling of jealousy that a person carries within. But it is for the active quality of حاسد, when he is actually acting out that jealousy. It is for when that dormant trait is now showing itself. That is when we seek Allah's refuge.

Now, placing this hasad within the generalized context of darkness with which the surah began.

We learn something very interesting here—something we touched on in the previous verse. Those who are jealous of you will never harm you to your face. They will always hide in the shadows and strike from there. They will go behind your back. They will do it in ways that leave you unable even to tell who is behind it. Unseen, once again! SubhanAllah! You will never see it coming. The very person sitting beside you may be jealous of you. He intends you harm, and you imagine he or she is your closest friend. This too becomes a harm that is unseen to you. That is why اعوذ is so perfect in this context, because it is protection from a harm that is unseen.

Now, when Allah has already gathered every evil under مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ, why did He need to go into the specifics? When He said مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ, it already included all of these things. So what is the point of naming each of them? This is Allah alerting us that these particular categories of evil are the greatest ones. So you say to Allah, exalted is He, that you want protection from every kind of harm, and especially from these three great ones. The three big ones: the potential harm of the night, the potential harm of those who work sorcery against you, and the potential harm of the jealous one when he acts out his jealousy against you. These three are the great ones. So we ask Allah for protection from all evils, and specifically from these three great ones.

Now, finally, from a grammatical standpoint: how is it that Allah placed the definite article, the ال, only on النفاثات and on none of the others?

وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ
وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

He did not place it on غاسق—مِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ—there is no AL-GHASIQ. Likewise مِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ, no AL-HAASID. Only when He mentioned sorcery did He use the word AL: شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ. When do you use a definite article? When you want to make something specific. Not just any book, but THE book. Why did I tell you these two surahs were revealed? They were revealed to solve which specific problem? The problem of the sorcery that was worked on the Messenger of Allah by Lubaid ibn Asim. This surah was not revealed to address the problem of the night specifically. It was not revealed to address the problem of the jealous one, when he acts out his jealousy, specifically. This surah was revealed to address the problem of sorcery specifically, and so when He said وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ, Allah used the word AL. SubhanAllah! Can you appreciate the perfection of this text? SubhanAllah! It gives me goosebumps every single time! And all of this is spoken text. It is not written or edited literature. How does one arrive at such precision and perfection in speech? AllahuAkbar!

Switch back to 10 a.m.

So the first ayah says: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ. Say: I am surrendering myself for protection to the Master of Al-Falaq. Now let us look at this beautiful word Falaq. Linguists say that Falaq is in fact a cause of the word "Khalaq," which means creation. They both come from the same phonetic pattern, Falaq and Khalaq.

And so Falaq results in, or causes, Khalaq. And what is the next ayah we find in the Surah? مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ. SubhanAllah. Let me explain how the two are related.

The word Falaqa in Arabic literally means to rip something open. To tear something open so that something else comes out from inside. So if I tear open a pillow and the fluff comes out? That is falaqa. Falaq is used for the morning or daybreak because the rays of the sun literally tear through the darkness of the night, and morning comes out. That is why it is called falaq. Do you understand? It cracks and rips through the darkness, and that is why it is called daybreak. So falaq means to rip through, and then what comes out is creation. Khalaq. SubhanAllah. So Khalaq proceeds from Falaq.

So Falaq is, for example, when a seed slowly rips open and a plant comes out. Allah says فالق الحب, from the same root. He says فالق الحب و النوا. The One who tears open the seed. و النوا, which means the pit of a date, which is called نوا, and when that tears open, the tree begins to come out of it. Allah says فالق الحب و النوا.

Similarly, the One who brings the morning out. فالق الاصباح is used in the Qur'an as well. The night literally rips open and the day comes out. We use this word in our tasbeeh after Istamsaktu of the sunnat of Fajr: سبحان رب الصباح و فالق الاصباح. Perfect is the Master of the morning and the One who rips open the night and brings out the morning.

So do you see how beautiful this relationship is between Falaq and Khalaq? Between ripping open and creation? Because everything that is created is a result of something that tears open. SubhanAllah! Something that tears open. ما یخرج من اصلٍ کل عیون من الجبال. What comes out from something else, for example the springs that come out of a mountain. That is falaq also. The springs tear out of the mountain, and water comes out. والامطار من السحاب, and rain, ripping out of the clouds. It tears through the clouds and comes down. That too is part of falaq. والنبات من الارض, and plants ripping out of the ground, tearing the ground open and coming out. والاولاد من الارحام, and children who come out of the womb of their mother.

All acts of creation are a kind of tearing or ripping apart, through which the creation comes into existence. Like the big bang that exploded. It tore open. The singularity ripped open, and this universe came into existence. That too is falaq. SubhanAllah.

So Falaq refers to everything that has been created that tears open. Even, for example, if you study microscopic creatures that rip, that tear apart, like the amoeba, and they split. This kind of tearing open happens in plants, in animals, in microscopic organisms, in the sky. Even in human beings, both in the physical and the spiritual sense. Physically, Allah tears us out of the wombs of our mothers. But Allah's guidance also rips open the veils of disbelief and arrogance, and reveals the truth to the one who wishes to believe. He tears down the walls of problems and restraints, and takes the believer out of them into comfort and ease, from confusions and indecisions into clarity, just as the dark night tears open and the day comes out. All of that is also implied in the word Falaq.

So now, if you look at it from a literary standpoint, Allah is saying that He is the Master of birth. He owns it. He is the Master of all kinds of birth and creation. Because falaq is speaking about birth.

It is speaking of creation: the birth of the morning, the birth of a child, the birth of a plant, the birth of an animal, the birth of rain from the cloud. Now I want to show you how these two surahs are connected with the preceding one, Surah al-Ikhlaas. As I said earlier, there is a connection among all of these surahs, each one flowing into the next.

So in Surah al-Ikhlaas, what did Allah (may He be exalted) declare? لم یلد ولم یولد — He did not give birth, and no one gave birth to Him. Rather, He owns the creation of birth; He is not bound by it, because He is the Master of creation itself. He created the very process of creation, which in my way of putting it is science. Creation has nothing to do with His own existence. He is above it and beyond it. So رب الفلق is the continuation of that same theme.

Then there is the word الصمد. الصمد is the one whom everyone else needs and who needs no one. Everyone needs الصمد, and الصمد needs no one. That is الصمد. In Arabic, صمد الیہ is used when you turn to someone in complete desperation. It is a situation in which you need them, but they do not need you. Now, in these two surahs, are we desperately turning to Allah for protection? Yes, we are. Does Allah need our protection, or anyone else's? No, He does not. What does that make Him, then? الصمد. We have a need that we cannot fulfill ourselves, and so we ask for Allah's protection. Subhan Allah!

So these two surahs are also, in many ways, a practical manifestation of what it means to say اللہ الصمد. In Surah al-Ikhlaas, اللہ الصمد is a theoretical notion describing who Allah is. But within Surah al-Naas and Surah al-Falaq there is a practical manifestation of our declaration of our need for His protection and of our desperation. When Allah says that He is الصمد, in theory that means we are in need of Him and He is not in need of us. But when we say اعوذ برب الفلق, I am giving myself up, I am surrendering myself to the Master of Falaq. Then I am practically acknowledging my need for Him — my need for Him and His sufficiency without me, His صمدیت. That seed, that lesson taught in Surah al-Ikhlaas, is now bearing its practical fruit in Surah al-Falaq and Surah al-Naas.

Then there are several other implications of the word Falaq. وَسعۃ بعد الضیق. If you look at the entire theme of this surah, it is bound up with darkness. It speaks of the night and of the things that happen in the night. Night is considered a time of fear; darkness is associated with evil. Black magic is something dark, which implies that someone wishes to harm you. Jealousy is a dangerous emotion that can cause a great deal of harm. So all these darknesses and evils mentioned in the surahs create a sense of ضیق; you feel constricted. And by Allah saying قل أعوذ برب الفلق, He is saying: when you feel this way, when your heart feels constricted because of whatever difficult situation you are in, come under My protection. Surrender yourself to Me. I will take care of you, because I am رب الفلق. I am the Master of Falaq. I will rip and tear through whatever problems you are facing. It is as though Allah is saying: I will grant you openness and ease when you feel constricted and tight. So it is as if we were imprisoned, constrained by our problems, our confusions, our indecisions, and our procrastinations, and we call upon Allah, the Master of Falaq.

The one who tears things open. He will tear open our constriction and bring us out of it, granting us ease and creating expansion for us. SubhanAllah!

There is also الظلمات الی النور. This Surah speaks of Sharr, of evil, from beginning to end. In nearly every literature in the world, evil is associated with darkness. If someone is said to have evil intentions, many literatures will call them dark intentions. They say he has a dark mind, a dark personality. Darkness is tied to evil in virtually any literature in the world, and this holds true in Arabic as well. So merely by using the word Sharr, the Surah attaches yet another dark tinge to it. It is already speaking of the night and of darkness, and then, on top of that, of the evils that lie within the dark nights.

So Allah says, من شر غاسق اذا وقب. Here is the literal mention of night and darkness, and then another kind of darkness: و من شر النفاثت فی العقد, black magic. And then the darkness of the envious one when he acts out his envy. How is envy associated with darkness? Because the one who is envious will always work behind your back. They always operate in the shadows, never openly. You are left in the dark. So Allah mentions three kinds of darkness in this Surah.

Do you know what other word is associated with darkness? Shirk! Associating partners with Allah. In the words of Hazrat Luqmaan: يَبُنَىَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشِّرْكَ لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌۭ. Oh my son, do not associate partners with Allah. Shirk, associating partners with Allah, is the greatest darkness of all. But look at the word he used: ظلم عظیم. The word used is Zulm, injustice, which shares the same root as ظلمات, darkness.

So the Surah speaks of darkness, and shirk is the greatest darkness of all. Now what is shirk? Is it not the absence of tawheed, just as darkness is the absence of light? Just as the word used for shirk is Zulm, injustice or darkness, one of the words used for tawheed in the Quran is noor. The word NOOR is used for the tawheed of Allah.

So shirk is a darkness, and it is the greatest injustice toward Allah. And Allah says, ٱللَّهُ وَلِىُّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ يُخْرِجُهُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ. Allah is the friend of the believers; He guides them from darkness to light, from shirk to tawheed. وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَوْلِيَآؤُهُمُ ٱلطَّغُوتُ يُخْرِجُونَهُم مِّنَ ٱلنُّورِ إِلَى ٱلظُّلُمَتِ. And the rebellious shaytaan is the friend of the disbelievers; he misleads them from light to darkness, from tawheed to shirk.

Then again, من شر حاسد اذا حسد. Envy, once more a dark emotion. It is a Zulma, a darkness.

So this entire Surah carries this imagery of darkness, and Allah begins the Surah by ripping and tearing through the darkness and bringing light, and He does all of this with one word: AlFalaq! So we call upon the Lord who creates the brightness of the day by ripping through all these elements of darkness that afflict us. What a beautiful contrast is presented in this Surah with just one word, AlFalaq.

So you see how this Surah begins with surrendering ourselves willingly to the protection of Rabb AlFalaq. It starts with قل أعوذ برب الفلق. Say, I am surrendering myself to the master of Falaq! And then Falq, which means ripping and tearing through the darkness and bringing light, is then connected with all the remaining ayats: من شر ما خلق. From the evil of all that was created.

the master of Falaq will rip those evils apart and bring you out from among them.

و من شر غاسق اذا وقب

From the evil of the dark night. The master of Falaq will rip all those evils apart and bring you out from among them.

من شر النفثات فی العقد

From the evil of those who blow upon knots — from the evil of black magic. The master of Falaq will rip through that magic and take you out of it.

و من شر حاسد اذا حسد

From the evil of the envier when he acts upon his envy. The master of Falaq will rip through the harm of that envy and bring you out of it.

Consider, then, the relation of Rabb AlFalaq to all these different kinds of evil. Allah says that when they surround you, if you come into My protection, if you surrender yourself into My protection, I will tear these evils open and take you out of them. SubhanAllah.

Now a final hadees about the word Falaq. This is a hadees in which a companion recited Surah AlFalaq to Rasul Allah (SAS). After he finished the recitation, Rasul Allah asked him:

ھل تدری ما الفلق؟

Do you know what AlFalaq means? And then Rasul Allah himself answered:

بابٌ فی النَّار، اِذاَ فُتِحَت سُیِّرَت جھنَّم

It is a door in the Fire. When it is opened, the whole of Hell is set ablaze; the flames leap up. It is one of the doors within Hell. Once again there is the imagery of the door that tears open, and then, quite literally, all of Hell breaks loose. Another hadees says:

ھُوَ سِجنٌ فی جھنم، یُحبَثُ فیہِ الجبَّارُون و المتکبرون ۔۔ و اِنَّ جھنَّمَ تَتَعَوَّذُ بِی اللہ مِنہُ

AllahuAkbar! This Falaq, over which Allah takes mastery and lordship, the Messenger says is a prison within Jahannam — a prison within Hell. In it are all the tyrants and the arrogant. And it is so terrible that Hell itself seeks the refuge of Allah from this Falaq! That is how horrible that place is.

Now the question is why this word Falaq is used. It carries all those literary meanings that we spoke about, and how it brings relief; but now it also appears that the word Falaq delivers punishment. The question is: punishment for whom? This surah is a surah that is not dedicated only to the seeking of refuge; it is also a surah dedicated to describing certain kinds of criminals — certain kinds of criminals who engage in acts of sharr, who commit various acts of evil. There are many kinds of evil, but which ashraar in particular are mentioned? The ones mentioned specifically are sorcery (النفاثات فی العقد) and envy (حاسد اذا حسد). غاسق اذا وقب is only a general statement; the dark night may or may not be evil, for we know that there are auspicious nights as well — Lailatul Qadr, Lailatul Mubaraka. So a night can be good as well as bad. But sorcery and envy are always, always categorically evil.

So what we are learning is this: on the one hand, Falaq is a release, a breakthrough, a relief, a comfort for those who become the victims of evil. But on the other hand, for those people who engage in these acts of black magic and envy, or who act upon them, AlFalaq is a severe punishment for them — because Allah is the master of AlFalaq. So not only is the crime mentioned, but the punishment worthy of that crime is also mentioned, at the very beginning of this surah.

So it is glad tidings for the victims of evil. If someone is performing black magic upon us, or acting out their envy against us, then this surah brings glad tidings, happy news for us: do not worry. Surrender yourself to Me, to Rabb AlFalaq, your master of Falaq.

and I will take care of you. But if we are among those who engage in these crimes of evil, then this same surah is a severe warning for them. It is a threat from Allah, because AlFalaq is also the door to the blazing fire of hell. اللھم لا تجعلنا من الظالمین

Qul

Now let us speak of the word Qul. It is found throughout the Qur'an. What is so remarkable about it? It carries a different literary context in every ayah in which it is used. There are qualities that are common to the word Qul wherever it appears, and there are qualities particular to the context in which it stands. So let us look at what the word Qul accomplishes in the معوذتین.

Notice that both of these surahs open with the word Qul, which, from a linguistic standpoint, is a command. It is called حرف الامر. It carries an invisible exclamation mark before it: Say! This is a direct command to Rasul Allah, and by extension it is a command to all of us. It is a remedy for him, and through him it becomes a remedy for all of us.

Now, why did Allah wish to give this command? He did so because He wants human beings to announce and to admit their weakness with their tongues. It is one thing to realize that I am weak; it is another to admit it and to announce it. Now, when you announce your weakness, is it an act of arrogance or of humility? It is an act of humility. It is an act of declaring: I have no power. I am powerless. I need your protection. Now, is it not possible that someone needs protection, yet their ego stands in the way, and so they do not ask? They truly want and need the protection, but they do not ask because their ego stands in the way. Or, even when they ask, they do not say it aloud; they hint at it softly, under their breath. Why? Because they are too embarrassed to say it aloud, for when they say it aloud, it exposes how weak they are. So Allah says: I want you to expose how weak you are to yourselves. I want you to be rid of every ounce of arrogance that may exist within you. The word Qul removes arrogance from us. It removes from us what is called استغنا.

So let us look at the benefits of this word Qul, for making this announcement of our need before Allah, aloud, is important for several reasons.

In that declaration, the first thing is the killing of our being impressed with ourselves. It kills our ego when we admit before Allah: I am submitting to YOUR protection. It kills our ego, and that false sense that, you know, I do not need any protection, I can handle everything without Allah. It removes the false pretenses of our own capability and strength. It gets it out of your system, because holding that false sense of protection is a kind of shirk and arrogance. For Allah says: كَلَّآ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَنَ لَيَطْغَىٰٓ۔ أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰٓ — The human being truly rebels because he thinks he has no needs. So Allah says: QUL, declare openly that you have a need. This ensures your sincerity.

Command

The second thing is that Qul is a command. So when we say Qul, when we actually accept and declare our weakness and incapability, we have now actively obeyed a command of Allah. For the word "Rabb" necessitates the existence of an authority. You obey Him because He is your Rabb, because He is your master. Now, why is that important?

And this is truly important to understand. It is important, because how can it be that we are asking for Allah's help while disobeying Him? If I am constantly disobeying Allah, how can I ask Allah for His help? We would never ask for anyone's help while disobeying them and disregarding them at the same time. What we are learning here in the word Qul is that if we truly want Allah to protect us, what must we be doing first? We must be obeying Him. So the discussion begins with the command of Allah, and with our complying with that command; and what this does is that it makes it necessary for us to be in obedience to Allah, so that the protection can actually come to us. We are entering not only into the protection of Allah, but also into the obedience of Allah.

And that is why Moosa (AS), through these words, explains this concept: the concept of one who kills his ego by seeking Allah's protection. Is that not what we are trying to do? We are trying to connect two things. Surrendering ourselves to Allah's refuge means killing our ego. What does Moosa (AS) say?

وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنِّى عُذْتُ بِرَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم مِّن كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍۢ لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ ‏

There is no doubt about it: I surrender myself for protection to my master, and I seek refuge with my master and yours from every single one who is possessed with arrogance. This ayah connects two things together: seeking refuge and what? Arrogance. And then he says, لَّا يُؤْمِنُ بِيَوْمِ ٱلْحِسَابِ, the one who does not believe in the day of judgment, the day of audit, the day of standing before Allah and presenting his case. This also tells us that not accepting our weakness, and not surrendering ourselves to the protection of Allah, has directly to do with a lack of Emaan, a lack of faith. Because remember, what did Rasul Allah say about Falaq in the context of punishment?

ھُوَ سِجنٌ فی جھنم، یُحبَثُ فیہِ الجبَّارُون و المتکبرون

It is a prison in jahannam, it is a prison in the hellfire. In it are all the tyrants and the arrogant people. So if we do not accept our weakness, and if we do not realize a sincere need for Allah's protection—I do not need anyone to protect me! My money can protect me. My power can protect me. My family can protect me. This mountain can protect me. My knowledge can protect me. My government can protect me. If we have this egocentric mentality, then that makes us among the arrogant and it makes us among the tyrants, because that is the very thought process of a tyrant, of a Jabbar, and it is the very thought process of an arrogant mind, Al-Mutakabbir.

اللھم لا تجعلنا من الجبارون و المتکبرون

So this surah, Surah Al-Falaq, is a source of protection for the one who squashes his ego and openly declares his need for the protection of Allah, all covered by the word Qul; and who then understands that he is a helpless victim of various dark evils over which he has no control. He realizes that he is weak, that he is helpless, and so he willingly surrenders himself to the protection of Rabb Al-Falaq, who tears open, who rips open the darkness and brings forth the day; who rips and tears through the veils and prisons of depression, confusion, stress, hopelessness, and constriction, and then brings out clarity, happiness, relief, and expansion for us. And at the same time, this very same surah is a warning of a horrible and painful punishment in the next life.

against those who commit the evils of sorcery and jealousy — once again through the use of that same word, AlFalaq. May Allah make us among those who genuinely surrender themselves to the refuge of Allah and seek it sincerely.

Sharr

Consider now the word Sharr. There are three words in the Qur'an used for what is "bad." There is the word شر, there is the verbal form بِأسَ, and there is the word ساءَ, and each of these has various derived forms. Any one of them could have been used here. Why, then, Sharr specifically?

What is the difference between them? To begin with, from the standpoint of vocabulary, each has a different antonym, a different opposite. شر is the opposite of خیر, and I will define that in detail at the end. First let us speak of بِأسَ. بِأسَ is the word you use when you find something detestable, despicable, and terrible. For example, you drink something and you recoil in revulsion and declare it a dreadful drink; you say بأس الشراب. That would be بأس الشراب. But if you drink something delicious and wonderful, you say نعم الشراب. So the opposite of بِأسَ is نعم, and the pair is used to express one of two states: being extremely impressed by something, نعم, or being extremely disgusted by something, بِأسَ.

Then there is the word ساءَ. It refers to something that is not merely extremely evil but also ugly, and its opposite is حَسُنَ.

وَسَآءَتْ مَصِيرًا

وَحَسُنَ أُو۟لَٓئِكَ رَفِيقًۭا

ساءَ in fact means deformed, disfigured, hideous. So actions that are ugly and hideous in and of themselves are called سیئات; the actions themselves are ugly. A سَیِّئَا could be, for example, gossiping, committing gheeba. It is an ugly act, ugly through and through, a horrible and terrible thing to do; and so it is called a سَیِّئَا.

Let us turn now to the word شر. شر is that which is universally and unanimously understood to be harmful or evil. More precisely, شر refers to that which will cause someone harm. شر is that which will cause someone harm. شَرَارَا in Arabic is the spark of a flame that can burn you. You know how, when a great fire is burning, sparks and flames sometimes leap out, and they may land on your skin and burn you. That is called شَرَارَا. So شر is literally that — that which causes someone harm. Now, the verses in these surahs are profound, and utterly explicit in their declaration:

مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ

وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ

وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّثَتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ

وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ

Surrendering to the protection of the Master of AlFalaq and AnNaas. From what? From the evil. From the harm. From the شر of that which was created.

مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ

This verse has been translated in the worst of all ways. It is rendered as "from the evil of that which He created." This is the most terrible translation, and the most unjust translation ever made — evil that He, meaning Allah, created. Allah did not create evil. He did not create شر. He is the source of nothing but خیر. He is the source of all the good that exists.

It was human freedom of choice, the deviation of human emotions away from good, that created evil. Allah granted freedom of choice to His creation, and by the use of that freedom of choice, it is His creation that created evil. For what is evil? It is the absence of good. Allah did not create Iblees. He had created an angel. But then that angel grew jealous of Adam AS.

I received some very good and honest feedback from the children in the session, and the feeling was unanimous: that I am going too fast, and that too many details are being delivered in the session, which the children are finding hard to keep up with. So my apologies for that. I am definitely going to slow down. My challenge is that I now have children, teenagers, and adults in this session, and I feel that if I try to focus on one group, I lose the other. But since these sessions were begun for the children in any case, I am going to focus on the children alone from here on. InshaAllah, I pray and hope that the adults will still continue to find something new to learn.

I am going to return to making these sessions interactive, InshaAllah! I feel that there are two main categories in the study of AlFateha. There are the concepts. There are the linguistic miracles of Quran. And then there is plain information — three things, rather. I will continue to deliver all three, because I truly want you children to be able to appreciate all of it. But if you find it hard to keep up, then what I would like you children to walk away with is at least the concepts, which are the message and the teachings of these ayats, and the miracles of Quran. If you do not understand the pieces of information, that is all right. That is simply interesting information about things, which the adults will probably appreciate more. I will try to push that to the end, so that if the children wish to leave at that point, they will at least walk away with what I want them to know. So InshaAllah, let us try this, and I will keep in touch with you to make sure you understand this material.

Now that we are making this interactive, my partners in crime, get ready to be called upon. And all children are welcome to take part. I only want to keep it voluntary; I do not want to force anyone. So if you would like to participate — and I truly hope that you will — then simply send me a WhatsApp message, and InshaAllah I will call on you during the session. Participation only means that I will try to explain the material to you. I will tell you a bit of it, ask you whether you understand, you will say, "Aha, aha," and then I will move on. So it is more rhetorical than anything else. But it not only makes sure that you receive the material, it also helps control the pace of the sessions. Volunteer.

We started with the Istiaaza: اعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم. We looked into the meaning of each of these words individually, and then moved on to the two surahs, Surah AlFalaq and Surah AlNaas. And why did we do that? Because, as we learned earlier, Surah AlFateha is the mother of Quran, Umm AlQuran, meaning that it is the essence or the gist of the entire Quran. Surah AlFateha is like the summary, or the index, of the Quran, and the remainder of the Quran is a running commentary on the surah. You know how books have indexes that simply outline the chapters and topics. They give you the summary of what is in the book. But when you need to understand the details, you have to turn to the chapter itself. It is the same thing here.
body.topic_title_en: Seeking Refuge: A Summary of Surah Al-Falaq

body.text_en:
These 7 ayats of AlFateha are the index, and their explanations exist in the rest of the Quran. So in order to understand what these ayats mean, we will need to study these other surahs that provide us with an explanation of these ayats.

Now, AlFateha begins with the Basmallah: بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم. But before we come to that, we have begun studying the Istiaaza.

This is because Allah has commanded us: فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ — Before you begin reciting the Quran, seek the refuge of Allah from the accursed Shaytan. So we began with the Istiaaza, which is: أعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم

Now let us go quickly over the terms, to be sure that you understand them. First of all, the difference between Shaytan and Iblees, because both words are used in the Quran.

We said that Shaytan is a general label. It is an adjective that may be applied to anyone who fits the description. There is no person named "Shaytan," just as there is no person named "Arrogant." Anyone who behaves in an arrogant manner is called what? Arrogant. It is an adjective. In the same way, no one is named "Shaytan." Shaytan means the one who is far removed from the mercy of Allah. So anyone who behaves in a manner that carries him far away from Allah is called what? Shaytan. Anyone at all may be labeled Shaytan if he acts in that particular manner. The word may be applied to human beings as well as to jinns. Is that clear?

Iblees, however, is the name of a particular being. He is the angel who disobeyed the command of Allah and refused to prostrate before Adam. He is one specific being, called Iblees. That is the primary difference between the two.

Then, in order to understand the details of the Istiaaza, we began studying Surah AlFalaq. Let us review it quickly, just to be sure that you have grasped its substance.

The surah begins with قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ — Say! I surrender myself for protection to the master of Al-Falaq.

Falaqa means that something rips open and something else comes out of it. If you have a bag of potato chips, or a bag of candy, and you press at the bottom, the top of the bag rips open and the candy comes out. That is Falaqa.

You see how I carry out this linguistic analysis of words. I hope you can understand why it matters so much, because it truly helps us grasp the message and meaning of the ayats. Otherwise, how is this ayah usually translated? Say, I seek refuge from the master of daybreak. That is how it is rendered. But what does that mean? That translation actually means nothing to me. So He is the master of daybreak. What am I to appreciate in that? That He brings the day? Well, He brings the night as well. He brings the four seasons, one after another, as well. So what is special about it? My appreciation of this ayah would be no different had He said قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلشجر, or قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الفاحۃ — I seek refuge of the master of the apple.

But once we understand what the word Falaq implies — that this is how Allah creates, by ripping through things to bring forth new things — now I can truly appreciate the remaining ayats in the Quran, because I can connect them with the meaning of the word Falaq.
body.topic_title_en: Seeking Refuge: A Summary of Surah Al-Falaq

body.text_en:
So this surah speaks of evils, and evils are like darkness. Allah is the master of Falaq, which means that He rips through the darkness and brings forth the day. In the same way, if I surrender myself to His protection, He will rip and tear through the darkness of these evils and bring me ease and comfort. And notice how, when something rips through, it happens at once. It does not take much time. It implies something hard and fast. When you press that bag of chips hard, the bag rips open and those chips come flying out. Just like that, Allah.

who is Rabb al-Falaq, can take me out of the darkness of these evils — right away. Simply by understanding the meaning of the word Falaq, I can now truly appreciate this surah. Do you understand?

Aoozu means that I willingly surrender, that I willingly and desperately cling. To whom do I surrender? To whom do I cling? To the Master of Falaq. Now, when is it that we desperately seek protection? When we are being what? Attacked! But this is not merely surrender; it is desperate surrender. And desperation comes from two things: (1) when you understand the power of your enemy, and (2) when you understand your own helplessness against that enemy. That is what produces desperation.

Then we said that, linguistically, the word Ao'zu suggests seeking spiritual help from a deity. It is not physical help, and it is not sought from human beings. All of that is captured by the word Ao'zu.

Then there is Qul. It carries two things: a call for submission, and a call for obedience. By declaring, we crush our ego; we openly accept and admit our weakness and our need for Allah's protection. So humility comes first. And then, in this declaration, there is also the call for obedience to Allah's command. If a person is disobedient to Allah, he has no right to ask for Allah's protection. Even before he seeks His protection, he must come into His obedience.

مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ

From all the evil of what was created.

The word Sharr means something that is harmful, something that will always cause harm. Everything that is created has the potential for harm within it. A knife is a fine tool. It can be used to cut fruits and vegetables. But it can also be used to stab someone, to cut someone's throat. So even though the knife is a fine tool, it has the potential to cause harm. I cannot say that the one who invented the knife is evil.

The same applies to all of Allah's creation. Allah did not create evil. Freedom of choice in human beings is what created evil. So we surrender ourselves to Allah's protection FROM the potential and active evil of all creation.

وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ

From the evil of the dark night when things become invisible.
body.topic_title_en: Seeking Refuge: A Summary of Surah Al-Falaq

body.text_en:
So we surrender ourselves to the protection of Rabb al-Falaq from the evil of times when things become confusing, when situations and circumstances begin to cloud our judgment, when we can no longer tell who our friends are and who our enemies are. Protection from the evil of enemies who hide in dark shadows. This can mean the evil spirits we will speak about in the next surah, but also the dark emotions of the people we come into contact with: greed, arrogance, pride, pettiness. All these emotions can be very harmful, and they are completely invisible to us. For we do not know what negative emotion the person standing before us with a broad smile on his face may be holding against us. So in this ayah we seek protection from all that is invisible.

وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّثَتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ

From the evil of the women who blow on knots.

This is a specific reference to the daughters of Labed Ibn Asim, who assisted him in casting spells on Rasul Allah (SAS). But there are other spells that work as magic, which we spoke about last time: gossip, backbiting, things that can poison our minds against someone. And we remain completely unaware of the psychological changes taking place within us — changes that come not from anything we ourselves experienced.

It is because of something a gossiper said to us. That is exactly the behavior pattern of the one who has fallen victim to black magic. Someone else casts the spell, yet they behave as though the trouble were their own. They begin to have psychological and physiological reactions. And then, once we become victims of this evil, we end up becoming the hands of the gossiper. He becomes our silent master, and we become his minion. We do his dirty work for him, and we are the ones who end up punished — not the one who actually cast the spell. So this is indeed a great evil. And this is why Islam closed the door on gossip and backbiting.

وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍۢ مَّهِينٍ. هَمَّازٍۢ مَّشَّآءٍۭ بِنَمِيمٍۢ

And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer. And scorner, who goes about spreading malicious gossip.

May Allah protect us from this evil. And not only protect us from this evil, but also keep us from committing this evil against others.

وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

Finally, from the evil of the jealous one when he is acting out his jealousy. So Allah reduces the root of all evil to Hasad, jealousy. But what is interesting to note here is that the protection we seek is not from the jealousy itself. Rather, it is from the one who is acting out on his jealousy. Because we as human beings will feel jealous. It is a negative emotion, but as humans we cannot claim that we will never feel jealous. So feeling jealous is one thing, and how we navigate that jealousy is an entirely different thing. So the evil we seek protection from is in fact the jealous one when he is acting out his jealousy. Because that is when he will actually cause the harm.
body.topic_title_en: Seeking Refuge: A Summary of Surah Al-Falaq

body.text_en:
So in this Surah Allah highlights jealousy as the root of all these evils — the one who is acting out his jealousy. وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ. Because what will he do? He will cast spells, whether that be black magic, or spreading rumors and gossip and poisoning our minds against others. Therefore, مِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّثَتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ. And he will carry out that hidden emotion in a way that cannot be seen. He will attack us while keeping us in darkness. Therefore, وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ. And since we cannot keep track of everyone, and of every single instance in which we are being attacked by evil, therefore, مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ.

And who is the one who can protect us from all these evils? Who can rip and tear through all these evils and save us? Rabb AlFalaq. Therefore, قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ.

So this is why this Surah is named Falaq: because it ties in with every single ayah. And it ties in not only as Allah's protection for us as the victims of these evils, but also as a threat and a warning to us if we choose to commit these evils ourselves. Because, as Rasul Allah (SAS) stated, Falaq is also the name of one of the doors of hell.

بابٌ فی النَّار، اِذاَ فُتِحَت سُیِّرَت جھنَّم

It is a door in hell. When it tears open, the fire within is stirred up and rips and rushes out through it. He also said that it is a prison in hell for tyrants and arrogant people.

ھُوَ سِجنٌ فی جھنم، یُحبَثُ فیہِ الجبَّارُون و المتکبرون ۔۔

And it is so incredibly terrible that even the fire of hell itself seeks Allah's protection from it.

و اِنَّ جھنَّمَ تَتَعَوَّذُ بِی اللہ مِنہُ
body.topic_title_en: Seeking Refuge: A Summary of Surah Al-Falaq

body.text_en:
25:54 (The beautiful names of Allah) Hamza Yusuf

One of the characteristics of Rasul Allah (SAS) was forbearance. He never allowed trials and tribulations to disquiet him. In other words, no difficulty or hardship that he faced ever shook him, and we know that no man on earth faced as many difficulties as our beloved Prophet (SAS). Yet he never allowed them to perturb him, or agitate him, or put him into a state of turbulence. The word in Arabic for someone who has forbearance is Haleem, and this word has been used of Rasul Allah (SAS) in the superlative form: کان أحلم الناس — he was the most forbearing of all mankind.

So the word used for forbearance is Hilm. The word for intellect, in the metaphorical sense, is also Hilm. One of the things they accused the Prophet (SAS) of was: یُسَفِّہُ أحلامَنَا — he causes us to lose our intellect, or he causes us to look like fools. This is because Safeeh is the opposite of Haleem. The man of intellect is somebody who has Hilm, and the one who does not have intellect is the one who has Safaha. And Safaha, they say, is خِفَّتُ العَقِل. Safaha is when you have no stability, because what intellect should do is stabilize you: in your manners, in your school life, in your professional life, and in your religion. And because the Haleem is someone who is stabilized, he does not become disquieted. He is not perturbed in life.

Now, what is interesting about the word "disquietude" is that the word for "dreamer" is Haalam. The word for a person who is dreaming is Haalam. Why do you think the word for somebody who is not perturbed is Haleem, and the one who is dreaming is called Haalam? What is the commonality between the two? What do you think is the connection between a dream and intellect? Dreams need a state of quietude. You cannot dream if you are agitated.

Now, the word for nipple is Halama. You have seen pacifiers that are given to babies. A pacifier is called مصاصۃ, but the nipple on the pacifier is called Halama. Why is that? When a child is crying, when it is perturbed, what does the mother do? She gives the child the breast. And what does that do to the state of the child? The child goes into a state of complete quietude and relaxation.

Now, is it not interesting that milk and knowledge come from the same source? The source of milk is the nipple, and the source of knowledge is intellect. Both are identified by the same word, Hilm. And what is more interesting is that غَوَایَۃ, which means to go astray, has a root, Ghawa, which means the inability to digest milk. What leads a person astray? The inability to digest knowledge. They are spiritually not strong enough to digest that knowledge, and so they become sick, and they go astray. That is غوی.

This is because our first stage is to get through the two years. When a baby is born, the mother breastfeeds the child — in Islam, for two years. In Western developmental psychology they call it the "first crisis": Trust versus Mistrust. That is the first thing the child needs to realize, that they are in a safe environment. And if they are not given milk, if they are neglected by their mother, if they are mistreated,

they do not pass through that first stage of development, and every stage that follows is a disaster. This is a theory in developmental psychology. The whole trust of the infant depends upon whether the mother removes the child's disquietude or not, because that is the essential thing the mother has to do: to recognize the cry of the child, to know how much to feed, and how to regulate the timing of feeding. If you under-gratify the child, or if you over-gratify the child, either one leads to problems later in life.

So a ḥalīm is a person who, in the face of tribulation — whether the trauma is caused by another person, or whether it is a condition or a circumstance — does not lose composure and does not become perturbed. This was the hallmark of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his conduct both with people and with circumstances. For instance, whenever people spoke ill to him: ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ — the Qur'an says, repay an evil deed with the best that you have.

There is a famous story of a Jew who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and deliberately tried to upset him in order to draw out a response. He insulted the Messenger of God to such a degree that one of the Companions grew furious and drew his sword to kill the man. But the Messenger of God remained entirely calm and silent, even though he had been insulted to his face by this man. Afterward the man said that he had seen in the Messenger of God every characteristic of prophecy except one — ḥilm — and that he needed to test it. So he deliberately tried to provoke a negative response, and he could not obtain one from the Messenger of God.

One of the marks of people who are disconnected from God is that they are perturbed. They become completely disquieted and agitated whenever matters grow difficult. It is a sign of weak faith. It is a sign of disconnection from God. The infant cries when it is separated from the nipple; in the same way, when we lose the slightest thing, we are perturbed and we fall into trauma.

One of the things we are becoming ever less capable of is listening to one another — simply talking as human beings, without becoming disquieted. People today cannot hold a civil argument. We cannot have discussions, because as soon as we begin to speak I grow heated, you draw a response out of me, and matters pass beyond control. This is because of the absence of ḥilm, the absence of forbearance. Ḥilm is the ability not to let your buttons be pushed. It is truly one of the gifts of Islam, if we take it seriously. It is something all of us ought to work upon, and it is not easy. Some become better at it than others, but it demands a great deal of effort. Its growth does not come to a stop; it keeps becoming finer and finer. Yet to remove resentment from the heart is a genuinely difficult thing — ḥasad, kibr, ḥirṣ, envy, greed, pride, arrogance, contempt: all these diseases of the heart.

So these calamities make the slave realize and admit that he is under the dominion of Allah. Ultimately he must return to His judgment and His decree. It is to realize that it is not the slave's planning but Allah's planning that takes effect. It is Allah's decree, His will, and His command that is finally carried out. It is Allah who has the final say in all matters. They have no place of refuge from Him, and no way out of the trial in which they have been placed, except that Allah chooses to take them out of it.

The third benefit of calamities is أَلاخلاصُ لِلہ تَعالیٰ ؛ لا مَرجَع فِی دَفعِ الشَّدائِد اِلَّا اِلَیہ — sincerity to Allah, because one has no place of return in warding off calamities except to Him. So it makes you sincere, because the sincere one is he who calls upon God without any partner. If you realize that you have no other place to go — they realized that they had no refuge from Him except with Him — that state is a great gift from Allah, because it places you in a state of sincerity. One of the scholars said that a single moment of sincerity in this world is enough to save a person: simply to stand before Allah in a state of sincerity. So that is a great gift which calamity brings. Allah says: وَإِن يَمْسَسْكَ ٱللَّهُ بِضُرٍّۢ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُۥٓ إِلَّا هُوَ — if Allah afflicts you with some harm, there is no remover of that harm except Allah, except Him. When people board a boat and the sea grows rough with turbulence and waves, all at once they are calling upon Allah sincerely. These are people in a poor state, yet Allah says that in that state they are sincere, because the calamities have come. So that is a benefit of calamities.

The fourth benefit is أَلانٰبَۃُ الی اللہ تعالی و الاِقبَالُ عَلَیہْ ؛ وَ اِذا مَسَّ الاِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَا رَبُّھُم مُنِیبٌ اِلَیہ — he returns to Allah and becomes suddenly fervent in his longing for his Lord. So that is a benefit. Allah says that when harm afflicts a human being, he calls upon his Lord, turning back to Him, to his Lord.

The fifth is اَتَضَرَّعُ وَ الدُّعَاء — that it leads to a humbled state before God and to prayer, so that you are calling upon Allah. When harm afflicts a person, he calls upon Us.

There is a hadith that Allah afflicts the people He loves simply so that He may hear them call upon Him. SubhanAllah. It is only a short while, if you keep it in perspective. It is just like the dentist: it is going to hurt for only a second, but he is doing it for your benefit, and that is why you let him do it. Is that true or not true? When somebody is pulling out a splinter, you know that this is going to hurt for only a second, and you say, go ahead. It is over. That is what you say when you do something to a child, when you take a splinter out. It is only for a second, and the child cries and cries. It is over, it is over — then you hug the child and everything is all right. That is the thing about this world. It is just . . . we are getting the tooth pulled out. Seventy or eighty years at most, but if you set it beside infinity, beside infinity, it cancels out, so stop complaining. Truly, sit back and relax.

You know what it is like. I have seen this with my own child, and you can do it — but do not do it! Take the child . . . I do not want to be responsible; this is America, and people sue you for things like this. If you take a child and throw the child up into the air, there is a point where you see this: the child goes into a state of complete panic, and then, when the child comes back into your arms, the child is laughing. That is this world. I guarantee you, that moment is your life. You came from God and you are going back to God, and there is only a moment in which you are in a state of complete panic. But relax; you are in good hands. Simply relax.

The Moroccans say: relax the mind and learn to swim. Seriously, relax the mind. Do you remember when you first learned to swim? I remember; I shall never forget it. I was placed on my back, and the person told me to relax completely. I was frightened to death. Relax completely? What are you talking about? I am going to drown. No, you are going to float. Relax. It was frightening at the beginning, but once you learn to relax, suddenly you are floating and everything is fine. That is this world. You simply have to relax. We are in the ocean of this world, and we need to float, to keep afloat, and not to drown. Everyone out there is drowning, because the person who drowns comes up and is in a state of . . . if such a person would only relax, he would not drown. It is the panic that causes him to drown, and that is what is happening with all these people out there. It is the panic. إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَنَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا "Human beings are created in a state of anxiety, إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعًۭا when any harm afflicts them they panic, وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا and when good comes to them they withhold it, they do not want to share it with anybody, إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ except the people of prayer."

They are in a different state, and those are the people we want to be among, the people who are exempted from that other state, because that trust in Allah is what saves you. Allah says بَلْ إِيَّاهُ تَدْعُونَ فَيَكْشِفُ مَا تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ إِن شَآءَ وَتَنسَوْنَ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ — they call to Him; rather, to Him may your call be, and فَيَكْشِفُ مَا تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ إِن شَآءَ He will remove what you are calling Him for, He will remove the calamity if He desires. So that is one of the benefits. قُلْ مَن يُنَجِّيكُم مِّن ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ تَدْعُونَهُۥ تَضَرُّعًۭا وَخُفْيَةًۭ "Say, who will save you from the darknesses of the land and the sea when you call Him, abased and humbled, in fear and in concealment."

The sixth benefit is الحِلمُ عَن مَّن صَدَرَت عَنہُ المُصِیبَۃ, that you are forbearing toward the One who has afflicted you. Allah says in the Qur'an إِنَّ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ لَأَوَّٰهٌ حَلِيمٌۭ "Ibrahim was someone who had compassion for other people, he felt compassion." Halim is gentleness. فَبَشَّرْنَٰهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ حَلِيمٍۢ "We gave them good tidings of Ismail." A young boy, a forbearing boy. The Prophet (sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam) said أَنَّ فِیکَ خَصلَتَینِ یُحِبُّھُمُ اللہُ؛ الحلم و الاَنا "You have two qualities that Allah loves: forbearance and deliberation." There is a difference in the ranks of forbearance according to the differences among calamities in their enormity and their severity, whether they are great or small. Forbearance shown when the calamity is great is far greater than any other kind of forbearance. So one of the great blessings is the ability to show forbearance, because it is a gift from Allah.

The seventh one, العَافُ عَن دَانِیھَا, is that you can forgive them. So it is not merely having forbearance; you actually forgive them, and one of the greatest rewards comes from forgiving people who have wronged you. Allah says ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِى ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلْكَٰظِمِينَ ٱلْغَيْظَ وَٱلْعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ "Those who forgive people — Allah loves those people." فَمَنْ عَفَا وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَجْرُهُۥ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ "The one who pardons and who sets things right, his reward is with Allah." When you forgive people for great calamities, it is better than any other forgiveness. If you have family members who cause you problems, you have to forgive them for the sake of Allah. Do not do it for them; do it for Allah. Consider one of the things people do: if you get angry and leave, if you run out of the room and then do not speak to that person, the longer you delay, the deeper it festers. It is like a boil. If you go at once — truly, I once became upset with somebody, I took a shower and then simply went and asked for their forgiveness, and I was not the wrongdoer — the thing can be healed. If you do not do that, it becomes more and more difficult as time goes on; it festers. Then pride enters. Shaytan says it is not your fault, you did not do it. He should be the one asking your forgiveness. Who does he think he is? Do not worry about who he thinks he is; worry about who you think you are. That is the problem.

The problem with the world is who we think we are, and so asking forgiveness of people is a great blessing from Allah.

The eighth one is to be patient during the tribulation. إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّبِرِينَ — "Allah is with the patient ones." So when you show patience, it is a great blessing. انتظارُ الفَرَج — to wait for an opening from Allah is one of the greatest acts of ibadah. There are Muslims you see, and if you tell them to be patient, they say, how long do we have to be patient? There is this kind of thing, we have been patient — that is not patience. You cannot call a donkey patient in Arabic. You cannot say something like الحمار الصابر ..... It does not work, because patience is based on understanding. You can bear things; they simply bear it. Patience is different. Patience has ihtisab, which is where you actually reckon with your Lord a reward, where you believe that a reward is coming from being patient. This brings on the muhabbah of Allah, the love of Allah, and also the abundant reward. Allah loves the patient ones, so by being patient you are incurring the love of Allah, engendering the love of Allah. إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ — the sabiroon are given their rewards without any reckoning. Some rewards you receive are already reckoned, whereas patience is without reckoning. وما أُعطِیَا أَحدٌ عطاءً خَیراً وَ أَوسَعُ مِنَ الصَّبَر — no one was given a blessing better or greater than patience.

The ninth one, الفَرَحُ بِھَا الاَجرِ فَوَائِدِھَا, is to actually be happy, to be glad about what is happening because of these benefits. The Prophet (sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: وَلَّذِی نَفسِ بِیَدِہِ کاَنُ لَیَفرَحُونَ بِالبَلآءِ کَمَا تَفرَوحُونَ بِالرَّخَاءِ — that is in a hadith that Imam Ahmad relates about the people who went before, who used to be as happy during times of calamities and tribulations as you are during times of abundance. حَبَّ ذُی المَکرُوھَان ..... الموتُ و الفقر — how wondrous those two distasteful things are: death and poverty ..... because in the akhirah, poverty in this world is a blessing, since your hisab is much less if you are poor. That is what Imam Ali said about wealth: حلالُہُ حِساَبُ وَ حَرَامُہُ عِقَاب — "what is halal from it is a reckoning and what is prohibited from it is a punishment." And that is why the zuhad are called أَعقَلُ النَّاس ..... the most intelligent people are the zuhad, because they give things up ..... because they do not want the problems that go along with these things. They were happy with it, not because these things happened, but rather because of the rewards and the fruits that came from those tribulations.

So it is just as with someone who is happy though he has grave diseases, when he drinks that bitter cure that will remove the disease. He drinks it and he is happy about it, because he is thinking not about the bitterness and the difficulty of the remedy, but about the benefits that will come from taking the bitter remedy. This is the way the people of Allah are with tribulations.

The tenth, الشُّکرُ عَلَیھَا, is to be grateful for it ..... because of the benefits contained within it, as a sick person would be grateful to the doctor who is severing one of his limbs or preventing him from his desires, because he believes that this is a cure for him. You go to the surgeon, and the surgeon cuts your hand off because there is gangrene. What do people say to the surgeon afterwards? Thank you so much, doctor.

He has just cut off your hand. Why are you thanking him? Because you understand that he was doing you a benefit, even though outwardly he harmed you. In the same way, those people who receive tribulation from Allah know that Allah does such things only to benefit them and to make them grow, and so they truly say alhamdulillah. The eleventh, طُھُورِھَا بِالذُّنُوبِ وَ الخَطاَیَا, is the purification that these calamities work upon their wrongs and their sins. وَمَآ أَصَبَكُم مِّن مُّصِيبَةٍۢ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُوا۟ عَن كَثِيرٍۢ‏ Allah said that whatever afflicts you comes from what your own hands have earned, and that He pardons much of what you have done. In other words, what afflicts you is in fact far less than what you deserve. On this, Imam Nasafi says something in his commentary — and his commentary is a beautiful one — he says that if you reflect on the meaning of this verse you will show gratitude for your calamities, because you will realize that it is a blessing that they are far less than they might have been. That is the secret of this verse. وَيَعْفُوا۟ عَن كَثِيرٍۢ That is why Allah followed the first part with this. You are afflicted because of your wrong actions, and you may feel badly about that; but when you realize how much He has pardoned, it makes you grateful that Allah has overlooked so many of your shortcomings.

The believer is not afflicted with any hardship, exhaustion, fatigue, or anxiety that troubles him, not even a thorn that pricks him, without Allah removing his wrong actions by means of it. He steps on a thorn, and by that Allah removes his wrong actions. So all of these are blessings. No illness, no exhaustion, no fatigue, nothing of that sort comes except as a removal of wrong actions, subhanAllah.

رحمَتُ اَھلَ البَلآءِ و َالمُسَاعَدْتُھُم عَلی البَلوٰھُم The twelfth blessing is the compassion that Allah enables you to show to people who are in tribulation, and the help you give them. "Whoever relieves a quorba, one of the calamities of this world, for a believer, Allah will relieve a calamity for him on the yaum ul qiyammah." So people in tribulation become an opportunity. Imam Muhammad al Hasan says something in his commentary on the Mudhara: he says that people are in one of two conditions:

Either you have عافیۃ , wellbeing in yourself and in your family, but you meet the problems of other people;

Or you have these problems yourself.

If you do not help people who have problems, then Allah will give you those problems. That is the nature of this world: it is there to test you. So you are tested either in yourself or through others, and you must respond in the right way. Avoiding such things is a danger, and that is why the tribulations of others are in fact a blessing. If they come to you for help or the like, it is an opportunity to earn some closeness to Allah.

In the Muwatta of Imam Malik, Isa (sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam) was reported to have said, "People are of two types, people of wellbeing and people of tribulation, so have compassion for the people of tribulation and show gratitude for wellbeing." That is why, if you are in good shape, you should not complain. Tell somebody to punch you if you complain, because if you complain when you have nothing to complain about, Allah will give you things to complain about, and then you will think back on how good things were.

Remember how we used to complain about that? What were we thinking? There are people who say that when real calamities strike them, they think, "What was I complaining about before?" The truth is, stop complaining now, because it could get worse. That is the whole point. It could get worse. And one of the poets said:

و أِنَّ مَن یَّرحَمُ العُشَّاقَ مَن عَاشِقَۃ

"The only people who really feel sorry for people in passionate love are the people who have been in passionate love."

So when you see people in tribulation, you should remember: I have been there, I should remember what that was like and show compassion to them.

The thirteenth one:

مَعرِفَتُ قَدرِ نِعمَتِ العَافِیَۃ و الشُّکرُ عَلیھَا

Tribulations give you the blessing of true knowledge of how great the blessing of wellbeing is. So when tribulations come, you really appreciate what wellbeing is. It is better to appreciate it while you still have it. The nature of blessings is that nobody realizes their extent until they have lost them. That is a human being.

إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَنَ لَظَلُومٌۭ كَفَّارٌۭ

He is simply oppressive toward himself and constantly denying the blessings of Allah.

مَا أَعَدَّ اللہِ تَعَالیٰ عَلی ھٰذِہِ الفَوَائِدِ مِن ثَواَبَ الآخِرَۃِ عَلی اِختِلافِ المَراتِبِھَا

The fourteenth. What Allah has prepared, from the blessings of the reward of the akhirah, according to these varying ranks. So this too is a blessing: that Allah has prepared rewards for the calamities you bear with patience or with contentment, according to different ranks. There are people who are content who will have a higher station in paradise than people who were merely patient, and patience is the lowest maqam among the maqamat of the tawbahs — in fact the first one.

مَا فِی طَیِّھَا مِنَ الفَوَائِدَ الخَفِیَّۃ

The fifteenth: what is hidden inside the folds of these calamities are blessings. That is another benefit.

فَإِن كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُوا۟ شَيْـًۭٔا وَيَجْعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًۭا كَثِيرًۭا

Perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah will place in it much good. You do not know; there are things hidden in blessings. Let me give you an example.

I lost my job in order to find a better job. I lost friends in order to find better friends.

I once missed a flight, and alhamdulillah I have never been upset about missing a flight — I guarantee you that — because I always think that if the plane goes down, I am going to feel like such a fool for having run to catch it, or something like that. So I just relax. You never want to be on a plane that you ran to catch and then it goes down. What was I running for? So if you miss it, you miss it. But I missed a plane, and they ended up giving me $500 back, because they had to re-route the ticket and so on, and the difference in time and other things came to nothing. There are always benefits hidden inside what you think is a trouble. The thing about the world is this: if you enter into a state, in your experience of the world, in which you simply accept these things whenever they happen, you will always find the benefit. You will always see them. Allah will show them to you. You will know there is a benefit. In every delay there is God's choice, and that is part of what the mumin does: he submits to it.

The sixteenth one is that tribulations prevent you from arrogance and from evil, pride, and tyranny, from doing all these things, like Nimrud.

Had Nimrud been a poor, sickly person, deaf and dumb, he would never have done all those horrible things that he did. It is the same with the tyrants of the world. Had they been born impoverished, and so on, they would not have acted so; it is those very things that make them arrogant. The seventeenth is contentment, اَلرِّضَا المُوجِبُ لِرِضوَانِ اللہِ تَعَالیٰ ؛ فأِنَّ المَصَائِبَ تنزیلُ بِالبِرِّ وَ الفَاجَرْ — ridha — because tribulations afflict the good and the evil alike. Whoever does not like it, then it is simply upon him, and he has lost the dunya and the akhirah. Whoever is pleased with it is pleased because he knows that paradise is better than anything in this world, and if these are the tribulations it takes to bring him into paradise, then he is content with them.

So these are some of the blessings. There are many blessings, but these are the ones that Sultan al-Ulema Abdul Aziz Salaam enumerated, and they are good to remember in these times.

But I will end by saying: read history. These are not bad times. Muslims should not be so negative. There have been much worse times. There are aspects of this time that are bad, and certainly one of the greatest calamities of the age is that we no longer have many people of knowledge, and we do not have the levels of deen and things like this. But simply in terms of outward, worldly calamities, this period is nothing, if you read history. This period is nothing.

The real calamities of this age are spiritual calamities; they are not worldly calamities. So if we are going to weep over the calamities of this age, we should be weeping over the lack of religion, over the lack of spirituality. We should not be weeping about all this that we see out there, because it is simply not that bad. I am sorry, and if you think it is, you have not read history. Things have been much worse. Read about the earlier wars and how many people died, and about the plagues that afflicted people. A third of Europe was wiped out by the black plague.

There are too many blessings; the blessings we have are overwhelming. That is why, inshaAllah, we will ask Allah to put us in a state of gratitude with Allah and to make us among the shaakireen — truly to make us among the shaakireen — and simply not to complain. The thing about complainers is that even complainers do not really like complainers. They want to complain, but they do not want to listen to anybody who complains. So insha'Allah we will stop whining. It is the maqam of the tifl to whine. It is what I always tell my boys: nobody likes a whiner, not even a whiner — and they laugh, because they know it is true. So whining is a maqam; it is the maqam of the tifl. That is what a whiner is. The rijaal, in haqiqah, does not mean male. The rujul is male and female; it is the one who has reached the maqam of the adult, the mature one. That is what it means: the mature one. Rujula is maturity.

So insha'Allah, may Allah make us all mature. — See more at: http://shaykhhamza.com/transcript/17-Benefits-of-Tribulation#sthash.C5FSYcng.dpuf

Summary of the 17 Benefits of Tribulation

1. You realize the power of Lordship over you

2. You realize your abject servanthood and your complete state of resignation and brokenness before the will and power of Allah

3. Sincerity to Allah

4. You return to Allah and are suddenly fervent in your desire for your Lord

5. It leads to a humbled state before God

6.

You are forbearing toward the one who has afflicted you. 7. You are able to forgive that person. 8. To be patient during the tribulation. 9. To be genuinely happy and glad about what is happening, because of these benefits. 10. To be grateful for it, because of the benefits contained within it. 11. The purification these calamities work upon your wrongs and your sins. 12. Allah enables you to show compassion to people who are in tribulation and to help them. 13. Tribulations give you the blessing of true knowledge of the extent of blessing. 14. What Allah has prepared, in the way of the blessings of the reward of the akhirah, according to these varying ranks. 15. What lies hidden within the folds of these calamities, which are blessings. 16. Tribulations guard you against arrogance, against evil, pride, and tyranny. 17. Contentment. — See more at: http://shaykhhamza.com/transcript/17-Benefits-of-Tribulation#sthash.C5FSYcng.dpuf

How is it possible for tribulation to hold benefits? Is it not all pain, suffering, and sadness? Knowledge for the seeker! Knowledge is wealth, and the study of knowledge is an increase of that wealth. The wealth of a scholar is the knowledge from which others may benefit. God the Most High is all-hearing, all-knowing, all-seeing, and all-wise. He is the knower of the seen and the unseen, and He knows what is beneficial for us — for those who take time apart in solitude to contemplate and reflect. We ask of Him what we want, but He gives us what we actually need. Sometimes matters do not turn out as planned, or as fully as we wanted and desired them to be; yet with insight you will see that what happened was in fact better for you in some shape or form. Sometimes you will see God's wisdom and intelligence in His planning, and sometimes you cannot understand it at all, because our own thinking and wisdom are limited. We have to accept and acknowledge our limitations as human beings.

Passing through hard and difficult times is part of the journey of life in this temporal world, and it is not easy; it is truly hard, and it can break the heart. Spiritual and personal development, training, growth, and the experience of learning how to place total and complete trust in God (Tawakul), so that, Inshallah, you will come through it. How to deal with the matters and situations we face day by day in this chaotic and busy world, with daily du'as and supplications from the Prophetic tradition. I hope you all benefit from this enlightening lecture by Hamza Yusuf.

The Noble Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was someone who passed through unparalleled hardships, and yet he never allowed any difficulty to disturb him. He always remained a vibrant personality, positive and hopeful. In one very powerful and concentrated session, Hamza Yusuf explains why. Commenting on the treatise of the seventh-century scholar 'Izz ibn Abdul-Salam, he sets out seventeen benefits of tribulations for those who would see them. This lecture will not only transform your outlook on calamities entirely; it will also leave you in complete awe of God's magnanimity and infinite mercy.

Being patient is the most difficult medicine to take, and it does not taste good either — it tastes horrible — but it is a highly beneficial medicine for your spiritual immune system. Patience is extremely difficult, yet the reward, the enlightenment, and the wisdom behind patience are very great. It is a great station to stand upon!

Seek help in patience and prayer, for supplication to God is a powerful tool.

Hamza Yusuf was born in the United States, in Washington state, to a Catholic father and a Greek Orthodox mother. He was raised with eclectic ideas about God and religion, and was baptized into the Orthodox Church of the Greek Diocese in the States. Hamza began to study religious traditions at a young age, out of curiosity, and this eventually led him to discover Islam, the way of life he embraced at the age of seventeen. Thereafter he studied and traveled extensively in the Muslim world for ten years, to places such as the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and North and West Africa, traveling in search of true knowledge of Islam and its branches of the sciences. His thirst for "golden knowledge" and "treasures for the seeker" led him to the uncorrupted desert bedouin scholars in Africa, who taught him true, authentic spiritual Islamic knowledge and enlightenment: the message of Islam, "Peace with himself, with his Creator, the environment, other living beings and creatures," based on the works of the great Islamic scholars of the past. He also became fluent in the Arabic language, and then began his studies of the traditional Islamic sciences under the tutelage of some of the greatest Muslim scholars of our age. He received teaching licenses in various Islamic subjects from several well-known scholars in various countries. After ten years of study and learning he returned to the United States and completed his Western education, obtaining a degree in Religious Studies at San Jose State University in California and a degree in Health Care.
