It is not, do not fall into shamelessness. It means, do not even go near shamelessness.

And if you do, what happens? فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّلِمِينَ. You will become one of the wrongdoers.

Consider: we cannot wrong Allah. We cannot harm Allah. There is nothing we can do to injure Him. But we can transgress against a right, against a right that belongs to Allah; we can transgress against what is due to Him. And what is due is that Allah be obeyed when He commands us to do something. That is His right over us as our Creator, and that is His right over us as our Master and Benefactor.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
How did Iblees humiliate Adam? فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَنُ.

Now this is the verse I truly wish to share with you. If we understand this, then we understand the true intentions of Iblees. So far we have established that he is our worst enemy. Iblees, or Shaytan, hates us, and he is bent on revenge. Now, what was the worst thing that befell him? He was cast out. Yes. But being cast out of Paradise was only the half of it. The real matter is this: when that happened, how do you think he felt within himself? He felt humiliated. And humiliation is one of the greatest pains a creature can suffer. Any creature with dignity can feel humiliation. Animals feel no humiliation, because they have no dignity. Evidently, Iblees too had dignity. He had a sense of respect for himself. And when he was thrown out of Paradise, he felt humiliated. And for that humiliation he wishes to take revenge against humanity.

Now, what would be the ultimate revenge against humanity? For if he could somehow bring human beings to be humiliated, if he could somehow accomplish that, then he could feel that he had achieved something. So how does he do it?

Through waswasa. فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَنُ — So shaytan whispers to both of them. Now, what Allah could have said here is فَوَسْوَسَ اِلَیْہِمْ, meaning shaytan whispered to them. But instead He said فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا, and the use of lahuma points to a very specific intent. In other words, shaytan had a very specific goal here. فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا — he whispered to them for a particular reason. I told you earlier that he whispers in so many ways, in uncountable ways: anger, jealousy, greed, pride, contempt, so many different ways. But in the end he has only one single goal. What is that? Allah tells us as the verse continues: لِـ... لِيُبْدِیَ لَھُمَا. Notice this laam before يُبْدِیَ, this laam with a kasra. This word لِـ has a mountain within it. It tells us everything. It tells us the ultimate goal of shaytan.

Allah says فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَنُ — shaytan whispered to both of them — lee, for the reason. Why do you think shaytan whispered to them? What do you think was his ultimate agenda? Now, I would guess it was because he wanted them to disobey Allah, or because he wanted to get them both thrown out of janna, or because he wanted them to disbelieve, or because he wanted them to go to the hellfire, or because, because, because. Is that not so? But Allah says: let Me tell you what his ultimate agenda was.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَتِهِمَا — So that he could expose to them that which was covered of their ugliness. Shaytan's ultimate agenda was to get the clothing removed from Adam and Hawwa, peace be upon them. That is what he wanted. We really have to stop and think here. I was thinking that Allah would say shaytan wanted them to eat from the tree, is that not so? Because Allah had said, do not go near this tree. And so I thought shaytan would want them to eat from the tree. But Allah says: no, that was not shaytan's real agenda. His real agenda was humiliation. And he knew, through his own personal experience, that disobeying Allah would end in humiliation. And what would be the ultimate form of humiliation? The ultimate humiliation would be that the greatest gift of janna, the libaas, the clothing of janna, be removed from them. Because if you are disqualified from janna, what are you no longer qualified for? The clothing of janna.

The clothing that Adam and Hawwa were wearing was the clothing of janna. Clothing was a gift from Allah. It was the first gift given to Adam, peace be upon him, to honor him, because before him no one had ever worn clothes. Allah did not create us with clothes. When we come into the world, we do not have clothes on. Animals are born with their clothing; animals are born with their fur or their hide or whatever it may be. We are not. Clothing is the first gift our parents give us, by covering us and our private parts. Because when Allah created human beings, do you know what He said to the angels? وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى خَلِقٌۢ بَشَرًۭا — And when their Master said to the angels, I am creating a bashar. Do you know what the word bashar comes from? It comes from bishar, meaning skin. Allah created a creature that was just skin. But then Allah clothed that creature. He gave him a gift of His own, one that human beings were not originally created with.

So clothing itself is a divine gift, and Satan wants those clothes removed. Now let us look at the verse, word by word: لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا. لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا — so that he could expose to both of them; مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا — what had been covered up, wrapped up, and kept a secret; مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا. This word simply astonishes me. Allah could have used so many different words: مِن جِسْمَيْهِمَا، مِن أَعْضَائِهِمَا، مِن بَدَنَيْهِمَا — from their bodies, from their limbs. But He said مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا.

In Arabic, sawa is used for something that is ugly, something that is disgusting, something that is evil. A human being exposed without clothes, in public, is something evil, something ugly, something disgusting. It is something indecent in itself. And sawa is also used in the Qur'an for a decaying corpse. Allah says: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًۭا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيُرِيَهُۥ كَيْفَ يُوَٰرِى سَوْءَةَ أَخِيهِ. When Qabeel killed Habeel, peace be upon him, Allah sent a crow to show Qabeel how to hide the sawa, the decaying corpse of Habeel, peace be upon him. A corpse is not something you want to look at. It is something inherently ugly.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
In the nature, in the fitra of human beings, it is not tempting to look at nakedness. But when our nature becomes corrupt — Allah created us with a beautiful nature, but when that nature becomes corrupt, when it becomes distorted — the desire to look at nakedness arises. And if that temptation is overwhelming us, then it means that something in our nature is corrupted, that something has been removed. Because in itself, nakedness is called ugliness in the Qur'an. Nakedness itself is called ugliness — sawatihima. That is what it is called. This is truly something to think about.

And what better revenge than to humiliate human beings by getting them to disobey Allah? Because what happens when we disobey Allah? What does it result in? It results in our clothes — the very thing that honors us above the beasts, the very thing that makes us look beautiful. These clothes are stripped off of us. The story of Adam, peace be upon him, teaches us that Satan's ultimate agenda is to humiliate us by having humanity remove its clothes. When dresses grow shorter and shorter, when clothes grow tighter and tighter, when images grow filthier and filthier, when advertisements begin to promote the idea that there is no harm in showing a little skin, when the pornography industry becomes worth trillions of dollars — then Satan sits back and says: I am accomplishing my goal. I am getting my job done. This is what I always wanted to do — for the children of Adam to remove their clothes and to delight in exposing their bodies. Wow! I am now finally getting my revenge for my humiliation, because now I have taken their dignity away.

Because what is the sign of dignity? Shame! Shame is the sign of dignity. And Satan says: I have taken their shame away. Look at what is happening in the world of design today. Look at what is happening in the world of entertainment today. How are we justifying ourselves for watching shows that say the following has explicit content? We say, oh, it said some sexual content — it had the word "some" in it, I can forward past that part — after we have watched it. Or, I will just watch the beginning of it, and then say, ohhh.

Astaghfirullah — that was disgusting. But you see, this is exactly what Shaytan wants. He knew that human beings would lose their dignity if they lost their clothing. Today we live in times where the loss of clothing is celebrated. It is literally celebrated. Why do most young people work out today? To show off their six-pack abs. And you cannot show your abs with your clothes on, can you? Girls dress in provocative ways so that they will get the attention of boys. Really? Do we truly need to take off our clothes to get attention? Is our self-esteem really that low? You know, women of a certain profession used to dress that way not too long ago, and that was their only purpose: to get attention.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
Look, my friends, I am only speaking to you the way your mamu or khaloo would, or the way an older brother would. I am not telling you what to do. I am only pointing things out, as the Qur'an is stating them to us. I am not enjoying speaking about this any more than you are enjoying listening to it. This is not easy to talk about. But if I do not say this, if I am afraid to point it out, then what am I doing here? What are we doing here if we are not willing to have these difficult conversations? My own daughter will have to hear this from me as well. I am only telling you how it is, the way the Qur'an says it. And the point of telling you all this is not so that I call you out. The point is that you call yourself out. You have to make that choice — that you will not let Shaytan trick you into believing that this is the way you will look beautiful. Because it is not. It really is not. Exposing yourself for the attention and the dirty looks of other men — that is sad. It is pathetic that we feel the need to expose our bodies in public just to look beautiful. This is for people who have nothing higher to aim for. This is for people who cannot find any other meaning in life. This is for them. This is not for us as Muslims. This is not for us momins. We have a purpose. We have a higher goal. We have a direction.

And I am not saying that you should not dress nicely. Girls have a natural tendency to dress nicely — by all means. Look, we men have no problem dressing like homeless people; we are fine with that. Girls want to look beautiful — that is wonderful. Look beautiful, but look beautiful by means of your clothing, not by removing it. You do not have to look beautiful by being provocative, and you are smart enough to know the difference.

Because we are playing right into the hands of Shaytan. We are doing exactly what he wants us to do when we lose our clothing. Imagine if your clothes accidentally fell off in front of your parents — imagine how embarrassed you would feel. And he wants us to lose our clothing before Allah. He is dishonoring us before Allah, and we are constantly making his work easy. This is truly something to think about.

We looked at the difference between fire and clay, remember? Nudity is the very nature of fire — hence the term "a naked flame." Soil, or clay, has as its very nature to veil and to cover up. We momins, we Sulemanis, we are not people of fire; we are people of clay. We are not children of Iblees. We are children of Adam. The world is playing with fire.

The world plays with fire because it has chosen to follow the one who was made from fire, the one who will himself end in the fire and carry all who follow him into it along with him. May Allah guide them as well. But we are not people of fire. We are people of clay. The one whom we follow was not made from fire; he was made from clay.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en: Those who blindly follow their own desires have at least an excuse. They have at least some reason for going astray. They know no better. They have no access to the wisdom of the Qur'an. But you and I do. And so our lives, and the very way we think, must be different.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
Adam was created as viceregent

You see, Adam AS, and even we, as the children of Adam, Banee Adam, are Allah's very special creation. That is why He called us His khaleefa. That is why He said to the angels, أنی جاعل فی الارض خلیفۃ. I am going to create My representative on earth. Khalifa comes from the word Khalaf.

or *Yakhlufhu*, meaning to succeed someone, or to take one's place. A person who takes the position or the place of another is called a khaleefa, or a caliph, or a deputy. Another meaning of khaleefa is one who has been fully taught, or fully trained. This is because only the one who has been taught can now take the place of the teacher. I am a software developer. If I train and teach someone everything I know about software development, that person can then take my place. He can step into my role. He can be my khaleefa. Do you understand?

Now, did Allah teach Adam AS something? He did. وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا. Allah taught Adam AS all the names. Kullaha, meaning everything, is very important here. It is possible to teach someone some things, is it not? I can teach someone a few things about software development, but then that person cannot be my khaleefa. He cannot be my representative. For someone to be a true representative, he must be taught everything. Do you understand? If Allah had taught Adam AS only a few things, he could not have been a khaleefa. The fact that He taught him everything, وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا, and Allah taught Adam all the names, is what made him a khaleefa.

And this is the reason we claim that Maulana Ali was the true khaleefa of Rasul Allah SAS, because of this one fact: that it was only Maulana Ali whom Rasul Allah taught everything. Did he teach things to Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, and Hazrat Usman as well? Of course. But did he teach them everything? No. That is why we believe that they could not be the true khaleefa, the true successors of Rasul Allah. It was only Maulana Ali whom Rasul Allah taught everything. And then he himself testified to it: انا مدینۃ العلم و علی بابھا، فمن اراد المدینۃ فلِیَاتَ الباب.

And an exemplary proof of that is that these three caliphs, Hazrat Abu Bakr, Umar, and Usman, each turned to Maulana Ali for guidance throughout their lives. Hazrat Umar said at least seventy times, from that which has been recorded in the Sunni books; it has been recorded at least seventy times: لولا علی ھلک عمر. If it were not for Ali, Umar would have been destroyed. All the caliphs turned to Ali for guidance. And nowhere in the seera of Maulana Ali, throughout history, whether in the history books of the Shias or the Sunnis, do we find any place where Maulana Ali turned to anyone for guidance except Allah. Just as we never find one event in which Rasul Allah turned to any human being for guidance except Allah. This was because he was taught everything by Rasul Allah, which made him the true representative, the true replacement of Rasul Allah after him.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
In any case, let us return to our topic. We were talking about why Allah gave Iblees time until the Day of Judgment. Allah created Adam as His khaleefa by teaching him all the names. And then He honored him above the angels by teaching him everything, علم آدم اسمآء کلھا. And then He honored him again by asking the angels to prostrate to him. Now, you do not give that kind of honor to just anyone. You do not give that honor to someone you hold to a low standard. So if He made the angels bow down to him, and, by his association, to us, and not merely bow down but prostrate, Allah made the angels prostrate before us. That means Allah must have had some seriously high expectations of us. And so, when Iblees asked for time, time to do what?

To misguide us, to mislead us, He granted him that time. Why? Because Allah knew that He created us human beings out of His love. He blessed us with innumerable gifts, intellect being the greatest gift of all. He surrounded us with His immense mercy. He then also sent us His message, this Qur'an, His messengers, His true Khulafa, His representatives, to explain the Qur'an to us, to teach us everything we need. And through their holy lives, He set living examples of these messages for us. In addition to all of this, He gave us the gift of free will, the capability and the strength to stand against Shaytan if we chose to do so. And then His protection on top of that: the Istiaaza, to call upon Allah when things get difficult.

Think about it. He gave us capability through the intellect, freedom of choice, the guidance of the Qur'an to distinguish between right and wrong, His messengers to explain the Qur'an to us and set practical working examples for us. And then, on top of that, the Istiaaza, to call upon Allah for His protection. Have you ever seen a more partial examiner than Allah? He is like a principal who sends teachers to teach his students everything, and then puts them in the examination room to take the exam, and then stands in the room as the invigilator. He makes it an open-book exam. Refer to the Qur'an all you want. And then, on top of that, He says: if you have problems in your exams, let me know, I will help you, I will give you the answers. Oh, and by the way, when I grade your papers, I will be extremely lenient with you. For every correct answer, I will give you ten points, and for every wrong answer, I will deduct only one point.

Where will we find such a merciful, such a kind, such a helpful, such a lenient invigilator? Have you ever heard of an examiner like this? SubhanAllah. He literally gave us everything. He covered all grounds for us. There is nothing left. And now, after all this, if I still choose to fail His exam, then I do not deserve His rewards anyway, on the simple principle of justice.

Some have this Christian mentality where we think, oh, He is Allah, He should be all-merciful, He should just give us heaven regardless. Why do we need to prove anything? How can that make sense? Where is the justice in that?

أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّلِحَتِ كَٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ

Should I make the one who believes and does good deeds equal to the one who creates mischief on this earth?

أَمْ نَجْعَلُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ كَٱلْفُجَّارِ
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
Should I make the pious equal to the wretched? Do you want me to make an alcoholic, lying, cheating adulterer equal to an honest, pious, God-loving, God-fearing momin? Should I give them both the same reward? Even our own sense of social justice would not accept that. Then how can we attribute this trait to the one who is the most just of all? It just does not make sense.

So what we fail to understand is that when Allah gave Iblees time, in whom was Allah putting His trust? Whom was Allah honoring once again? He was honoring us. He was honoring us human beings once again. He honored us by putting His trust in us, just as He had honored Adam, peace be upon him, before us. More than the ability of Iblees to misguide us, He trusted us more, to not be misguided by him. Why? Because He gave us everything we need.

It doesn't make any sense why we would choose Iblees over Allah. It makes no sense to Allah. That is why He said to Iblees: Fine! Do whatever you want. You will not be able to misguide My servants. What a disappointment we turned out to be!

So that was the second part. Now for the first part of this question. Why is Iblees asking for time? Allah actually explains that in the next verse.

قَالَ فَبِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِى لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ

This is so interesting. Iblees says: because YOU misguided me. Because YOU led me astray. Whom is he talking to? He is talking to Allah. And look what he is saying. Because YOU led me astray. فَبِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِى. He is blaming Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for his own disobedience. Iblees is blaming Allah for his misguidance. Can you see the psychological state of this creature? A complete lack of responsibility. It is not MY fault. It is YOUR fault. YOU did this to me. You gave me a command that I was not able to obey. It is all YOUR fault. I am in this position today because of what YOU did to me.

Crazy, is it not?

Attack from all directions

Is it? Is it really crazy? Because we do it all the time, do we not? We shift the blame all the time. Instead of taking responsibility for our lack of faith. Instead of taking responsibility for our lack of willpower. We blame everything else, and everyone else around us. It is my parents' fault. It is my teacher's fault. It is this school system that is so terrible. It is Islam that is so difficult. It is so inconvenient. Why do I have to pray five times a day? Why do I have to fast? Why do I have to pay Zakat? It is MY hard-earned money. Why do I have to give it to someone else? If Allah is so powerful, why can He not give it to them Himself?

See. Always very logical justifications. If Allah is so powerful, why does He not feed the poor? They are, after all, His creation. Why do I have to spend MY money? Your money? Who gave you YOUR money? Your job? Why did you get that job? Because of your education? Who gave you that education? Your parents? Who gave you those parents? And their jobs and their sustenance, which enabled them to secure your education, which led to you getting your job, which led to you making the money you make?
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
So Iblees says: قَالَ فَبِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِى. Because You led me astray. Because of what YOU did to me. لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ. I will now make sure I get them into trouble with You. I will mislead THEM from Your straight path. I will sit on Your straight path. قعد means to sit. But قعد with a laam, لَأَقْعُدَ, means to sit somewhere in order to ambush somebody. You know, like someone waiting behind the bushes with a baseball bat for his enemy to come out. That is لَأَقْعُدَنَّ. So he said: I will sit on Your straight path, waiting for them, to ambush them. Now, someone who is waiting that way, does he expose himself? No, he does not. And does he attack all the time, or at the right moment? He waits for the right moment, and then he attacks. So all of that is captured inside لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ. I will lurk on Your straight path. Which straight path? The straight path that they constantly seek guidance for. اھدنا الصراط المستقیم. Oh Allah, guide me to the straight path. This is what we constantly ask Allah for in Surah Fateha. Iblees says:

I will misguide them from that same straight path they are asking to be guided along. But I will not come out all the time. I will find that right moment, and then I will slip something in and slip out from there before they can realize what has happened. ثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَنِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ ۖ وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَٰكِرِينَ

I will then come at them from right in front of them. What is right in front of us? It is the straight path that leads to paradise. I will come to them and say, do not go this way. You do not have to wait so long for paradise. That is too far. It is too much of a walk. Why tire yourself? You want pleasures, do you not? I will give them to you right here. Why do you have to wait that long? I will give you all of it right now. And remember what we spoke about earlier: cash against credit. Are we people of credit, or are we people of cash? Iblees says, I will give you the benefits right here, in cash, at once. Paradise is credit. Why wait? Who knows whether you will even receive the rewards or not. I am guaranteeing you all the pleasures right here, right now. You would be a fool to leave this visible cash for that invisible credit. Do you see? Logic again.

وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ

And I will come from behind them, pulling them back. They will make progress, and I will pull them back. Even if a million things are going well for them, the moment one thing goes wrong, I will be there. How could Allah do this to you? Look, you have been so good. You have been so obedient. Praying five times a day, fasting, giving charity. He took your loved one away? He took your job away? You studied so hard, and He made you injured and sick. He made you fail your exam. How could He do this to you? Is this the Allah who claims to love you so much? Again, logic.

وَعَنْ أَيْمَنِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
I will come to them from the right, and I will come to them from the left. That is, if they are in good company, doing good things, I will attack them. If they are in bad company, doing bad things, I will still attack them. The right hand is associated with good deeds; the left hand is associated with bad deeds. He said, even when they are doing good things, I will slip myself in. Even when they are reading the Qur'an, I will slip myself in. That is why Allah says فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ. When you are reading the Qur'an, first seek the refuge of Allah from Shaytan. Why? I am doing a good deed. Why do I need protection? What has Shaytan got to do with a good deed? No, I will come at them even then. I will attack them when they are doing good deeds, and I will attack them when they are doing bad deeds. I will not stop. I will find the opportunity.

وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَٰكِرِينَ

And then you will see. You will see that most of them will be ungrateful to you. You are not going to find most of them on your side at all. In other words, I will get them to obey me, and when they obey me, they will disobey you, and that means they are not grateful to you.

Now notice something here. Iblees says: ثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَنِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ. I will come upon them from in front of them, and from behind them.

and from their right, and from their left. What is striking is that Iblees named four directions: north, south, east, and west. He named four directions. But there are six directions. There is also above and below. Yet Iblees did not mention those. He did not say: وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ. I will come upon them from above them and from below them. Why is that?

The reason for this is deeply interesting. What comes from above is revelation. And as long as you and I keep a connection with Allah through this revelation, he will have no access to us. He cannot cut us off from Allah, unless we ourselves choose to cut ourselves off from Allah. And he will not come from beneath us, because that is a place of humility. It is a place of prostration. And Iblees is arrogant. He will never lower himself beneath us. So as long as we remain humble, in the state of prostration, connected to Allah through his revelation, Iblees can gain no access to us.

And when, according to the hadith, does Satan flee? When you are in prostration, because he cannot bear it. It reminds him of his own disobedience. Our prostration is the proof of his failure, because it is the very thing he wants to keep us from doing. That is his ultimate aim: to keep us from being humble, to keep us from surrendering our will for the sake of Allah's will. So when we prostrate, he knows that he is defeated.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
The horizontal and the vertical directions, then, are deeply interesting. What this story teaches us is that if we place Allah in his rightful position, and place ourselves in our rightful position — which is to see Allah above us and to see ourselves beneath Allah, in prostration, in this state of submission — then Satan has no access to us. But as long as we wander about on this horizontal plane, which is this world, Iblees has complete access to us. This world is the horizontal plane. As long as we wander upon this horizontal plane, Iblees has full access to us. But the moment we connect with the vertical plane, Satan loses all access to us. This is why Allah created human beings upright. He created human beings vertical, upon a horizontal plane. Allah created us vertical, upon a horizontal plane.

If you go horizontal, you are lying down on the job. Then Satan gets in. And that is why sleep is a very easy time for him to attack. That is why we perform ablution and recite all these supplications at the time of sleep. So the key is to operate always upon this vertical plane. To keep our actions always aligned with the vertical plane. As soon as our actions fall into the horizontal plane, for the sake of this world — even if it is the ritual prayer, or fasting — as soon as it becomes horizontal, done to impress people, Iblees gets in. And this is what happens when you decide to make a change in your life. As soon as you try to become vertical, he tries to pull you back to the horizontal plane. What about your friends? What will they say? What about your job? What about money? What about your house? What about the children's tuition? All of them concerns of the horizontal plane.

So this is what Iblees says to Allah. Now, I always imagine: if I had been in the place of Adam, peace be upon him, what would my reaction have been? My reaction would be something like, "What on earth? What did I do?" It was Allah who taught me everything. It was his decision to make me his vicegerent. He taught me everything. He asked the angels to prostrate to me.

You disobeyed Him. He is casting you out. But what did I do? What did I do in any of this? Why are you angry with me? The angels, and Adam — brothers, all of them. Truly, what did poor Adam, peace be upon him, do in any of this? Why is Iblees so furious with him?

Let me give you an example, so that you may understand. Suppose that you and your sister, or your brother, are playing a video game. It is your turn to play, but your sister will not hand you the controller. You grow upset, and the two of you begin to quarrel over it. Your parents come into the room. They learn what has happened, and they scold your sister. "You must learn to share. None of this is his fault. You are supposed to be kind to your sister. Shame on you." The entire reproach falls upon her. Then they take the controller from her, place it in your hands, and walk out of the room.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
Now, even though it was your sister who was scolded by your parents, at whom does she look with eyes that now blaze? She blames you. "It is all your fault. I hate you so much. Because of you, I got into trouble. Everything was fine before you came into my life. Everything was wonderful before you were even born. My life was good. You ruined my life. There is nothing wrong with me. I do not have a temper. It is you who made me look bad." Do you understand?

Iblees asks Allah for time. Why? Because he got into trouble with Allah on account of Adam, peace be upon him, on account of this human species. He believes that, had Adam never been created, he would forever have kept his exalted station. It does not make sense, does it? But that is precisely the point. Iblees is deranged. He is in a state of constant, never-ending rage. And when a person is angry, what happens? He cannot think clearly. So now he holds a bitter grudge against the human race. In his mind, he lays the blame upon us. Iblees had been exceedingly close to Allah, and now he has been humiliated because of the presence of whom? Of human beings. And so he develops a severe hatred for human beings.

Now he says, "O Allah, let me prove to you that you made the wrong choice. Let me prove to you that you should not have honored them. You should have honored me. I will prove to you that you made a mistake. I should not have been the one in trouble; they should be the one in trouble. Only give me time, until the Day of Judgment, and I will prove it to you. You will see that most of them will not be grateful to you."

وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَكِرِينَ

And that is why he asks Allah for time.

قَالَ أَنظِرْنِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ

"Give me time until the Day of Judgment, and I will prove it to you, that they are not worthy of this honor you have bestowed upon them." Allah says:

قَالَ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَ

"Very well. I grant you time until that Day."

So Iblees challenges Allah, and He accepts his every challenge. And why would He not? It is not as though Allah is afraid of Iblees. But when Iblees challenges Adam and his children, Allah agrees to put them to the test. For, as I have said, He gave them everything they will ever need to meet this challenge. Why would they not choose Allah over Iblees?

And in the Hadith, this dialogue between Iblees and Allah is explained much further. Syedna Ghulam Hussain Sahab, may Allah sanctify his soul, writes in his book Qatrunnida that Iblees did not, in fact, merely ask for time; he asked Allah for strength and power as well.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
Iblees said, "Allow me the power to dominate these human beings through their desires." Allah said, "I will allow that for you." Iblees said, "For every son that Adam has, allow me two sons, so that I may be double their strength." Allah said, "I will allow that." Iblees said, "Allow me to make a home in the breast of the children of Adam, and allow my influence to flow through their lives just as their blood flows through their veins." Allah said, "I will allow that." Iblees said, "Allow me to attack them with my ground forces as well as my air forces" — meaning, to use both human beings and jinn against them — "so that we may mix and mingle into their wealth, and confuse them with false hopes and vain promises." Allah said, "I will allow that too."

When Adam, upon him be peace, heard all of this, he became alarmed. "O Allah, what are You doing? You have allowed Iblees and his army to become so powerful. My children and I will be crushed under his attack. How are we to defend ourselves against him?"

Allah said, "Do not worry, Adam. With every child of yours I will assign a protector, whose only task will be to guard him against the attack of Shaytan, should he choose to listen to him." That is our conscience.

Adam said, "O Allah, give us more." Allah said, "Listen. For every good deed they do, I will record it as ten good deeds; and every sin they commit, I will record only once; and if they repent of it, I will erase it completely."

Adam said, "O Allah, give us more." Allah said, "Listen. Go and tell your children never to despair of the mercy of their Master. My mercy will always accompany them, no matter how disobedient they are."

Adam said, "O Allah, give us more." Allah said, "Listen. Go and tell them that I will never close the door of repentance upon them. Until their very last breath they will have the opportunity to repent and seek My forgiveness, and when they do, I will forgive them."

Adam said, "O Allah, give us more." Allah said, "Listen. Go and tell your children that no matter how many times they repent and seek My forgiveness, I will keep on forgiving them again and again, and I will not even keep an account of how many times I have forgiven them for that very same sin."

It was then that Adam, upon him be peace, said, "That is enough, my Master. What You have given us is now more than enough for us to stand our ground against Iblees and his army."

After accepting Iblees's challenge, Allah says:

قَالَ ٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُومًۭا مَّدْحُورًۭا

Allah says: Get out of My paradise, in disgrace and as one who has been expelled. Leave like one who has been humiliated, and do whatever you wish to do to misguide the children of Adam.

لَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ

Whoever follows you among them.... Now consider. Allah did not say "whoever disbelieves in Me"; that is not the condition He placed. The only condition He set here is whoever listens to you — whoever pays attention to you and follows you from among them.

لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

I will fill hellfire with all of you together.
body.topic_title_en: The Devil's Plan to Lead Astray

body.text_en:
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّجِدِينَقَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ ۖ قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢقَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّغِرِينَقَالَ أَنظِرْنِىٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَقَالَ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُنظَرِينَقَالَ فَبِمَآ أَغْوَيْتَنِى لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَثُمَّ لَآتِيَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ وَعَنْ أَيْمَنِهِمْ وَعَن شَمَآئِلِهِمْ ۖ وَلَا تَجِدُ أَكْثَرَهُمْ شَكِرِينَقَالَ ٱخْرُجْ مِنْهَا مَذْءُومًۭا مَّدْحُورًۭا ۖ لَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَوَيَٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَكُلَا مِنْ حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّلِمِينَفَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَتِهِمَا

Deception of IBLEES — through Logic

وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنْ هَذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ

Iblees said to them: the only reason Allah prevented you from approaching this tree is that, if you did so, two things could happen.

إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ

Either you would turn into angels,

أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَلِدِينَ

or you would become people who live in Jannah forever. And Allah, obviously, does not want that for you.

Does this logic sound familiar? The only reason my parents are stopping me from doing this is because, and so on. Obviously they do not understand. Obviously they do not love me. Right?

Now let us try to understand what tempted the two of them. We already learned in Surah Baqarah. Allah said:

وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ

And Allah said to the angels: I am going to create a representative who is going to live on earth. Live where? On earth. That was Allah's declaration right from the start: that I am creating a representative, a caliph, for the earth. Not for the heavens. Not for Jannah. But where was Adam living at the time? In Jannah. And in Jannah, you would think that they would live forever. But Allah said:

وَقُلْنَا يَٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ

And Allah said to Adam: Settle! Settle here! ٱسْكُنْ. Allah did not say اُخلُد فیھا. Those of you who read the Qur'an know how, when Allah describes Jannah, He does not say فیھا ساکنین; instead, what does He say? فیھا خالدین. Khalid means to live forever.

So when Allah described the creation of Adam to the angels, He said: I am creating him for the earth. And also, when He spoke to Adam and Hawwa about their stay in heaven, He said: Settle here! ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ. And the word sakana actually comes from sukoon. Not the Urdu sukoon — as in "they are sitting in great comfort" — not that sukoon. When you learn to read the Qur'an, there is fatha, kasra, damma, shadda, and sukoon. What is sukoon? When you stop moving temporarily. You stop temporarily on the letter that has a sukoon on it. So sukoon means to stop temporarily. So there was motion before, as you were reading, and then you stop. That does not necessarily indicate that the stop is permanent. If the stop were permanent, then the word used would have been خُلد. You understand?

Instead of saying.

ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ. Allah would have said أُخلُد أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ. So when Allah made His announcement to Adam, upon him be peace, and his wife Hawwa, He told them to settle here. He told them to stop here, but He did not tell them to stop here forever. And He had already announced to the angels earlier that He was creating Adam for the earth: إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ. So the angels actually knew that Adam, upon him be peace, was created not for the Garden but for the earth. They knew that he would play out that role until he finally made his way back to the Garden. All of this was part of Allah's original plan.

Now, even though the angels knew, did Adam, upon him be peace, know it? No. Because all of this dialogue between Allah and the angels took place before Adam was created. So the angels knew the specific details about their eventual dwelling place, and Iblees knew them, but Adam and Hawwa did not. When Allah made this announcement to the angels, the two of them had not yet been created. But when Allah spoke to them both and told them to settle in the Garden temporarily, they understood that their stay in the Garden was temporary and not permanent. You understand? They knew their stay was temporary, but they had no idea that they had never been created for the Garden in the first place. And that is what Iblees took advantage of.

So Iblees came to Adam and said, listen. The two conditions for the people who get to live in the Garden forever are these: إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيْنِ — either you are angels — أَوْ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْخَلِدِينَ — or you must have permanent residence. You need a green card in order to live here. Now, you are clearly not angels. Therefore, the only way you can live here is to get a green card. And the way to get that green card, the way to obtain that permanent residence, is to eat from this tree, because the permanent residents are called Khalideen. So if you are not an angel — and I am fairly sure you are not going to become an angel anytime soon — then the only other option you have, the only move you have, is to apply for a green card. And how do you do that? Eat from the tree. That is, if you like the Garden. That is all I am saying. I am sure you have enjoyed yourselves here a little, have you not? Look, I mean well. I am your friend, and I really like the two of you. I want you to stay in the Garden. But unfortunately, the only two options you have are either to be angels, which is obviously not going to happen, or to eat from the tree. So the way I see it, you really do not have a choice.

This is how Iblees approached them, with the logic of survival. You see, this is the greatest challenge of all. Iblees comes with perfect logic that is grounded in the seen, and he sets it in conflict with faith, which rests in the unseen. He makes us choose between cash and credit, making cash the only smart choice. That is a truly astonishing challenge, a truly demanding test that we as human beings are placed into.

This is the difference between Adam and Iblees. They both made mistakes. Adam faltered. We are Bani Adam. We are the children of Adam. You and I make mistakes. We will continue to make mistakes. Look: making a mistake, committing a sin, is no great thing before Allah's mercy. Being arrogant and persisting in it—that is what is destructive. Coming up with justifications to continue a life in sin—that is what is disastrous. It is not possible for us human beings not to sin. It is part of our nature; it is part of our very fabric. The only person who does not sin is a corpse, a dead person. Other than that, we all sin. The question is: when we realize our mistake, how do we respond? That is what it all comes down to. Do we choose to persist in that act or not? That is the measuring stick.

If we choose to persist, if we choose to justify, if we choose to rationalize, if we choose not to take responsibility and to blame others, then that is arrogance. That is the path of Iblees. So what if I smoke? Everybody smokes. So what if I drink? Everybody drinks. That is what is truly dangerous; that is the path of Shaytan. And if we follow the path of Shaytan, then we will necessarily end up at the same final destination that he ended up in, which is the fire of hell. On the other hand, if we accept our fault and we change our path,

stop doing what we are not supposed to do, or start doing what we are supposed to do, then we are walking the path of Adam and Hawwa, peace be upon them, and in the end we arrive at their destination, which is once again Paradise. But that can only happen if we believe in two things: the immense forgiveness of Allah and the immense mercy of Allah. Those who choose to continue a life of sin are the ones who reject and deny the forgiveness and mercy of Allah.

قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ

Fall down from here. Descend from this place. From this day on you are enemies to one another — meaning Shaytan and Adam. But then Allah says:

وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّۭ وَمَتَعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ

I have appointed a fixed time for you all, and I have given you the means to enjoy life. متاع means the material things a person can enjoy. Then He said:

قَالَ فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ — in this world you will live; وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ — and in it you will die; وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ — and from it you will be brought out again.

Children of Adam.

يَبَنِىٓ آدَمَ

O children of Adam! Whom is He speaking to now?

يَبَنِىٓ آدَمَ

O children of Adam. He has just told us the story of our parents, and now Allah says: Were you listening? Were you listening? That was your parents I have just described. I have just told you the story of your parents. Now you listen.

يَبَنِىٓ آدَمَ قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًۭا يُوَرِى سَوْءَتِكُمْ وَرِيشًۭا

SubhanAllah! What does the Most Merciful, the Most Loving, do once again? What is the first thing He does for us once again, after sending us into this world?

قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًۭا يُوَرِى سَوْءَتِكُمْ وَرِيشًۭا

We have sent down clothing upon you, so that you may cover your nakedness. Some of the most beautiful words of the Qur'an: قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًۭا — We have sent down, انزلنا, clothing upon you. The Qur'an is revelation from the sky, sent down upon us. Rain is a gift from Allah, sent down upon us. Angels descend from the sky, protect us, and pray for us; they are gifts from Allah. All of these are gifts from Allah that He sends down upon us. And Allah sent down clothing upon us. Allah says: you did not make clothing! I sent clothing down for you! I sent down for you all the material that you can use to make clothing. Clothing — the very idea of covering up — is in truth a part of revelation.

Look at the words قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا. Where have we heard the word أَنزَلْنَا before? انا انزلناہ فی لیلۃ القدر. We revealed the Qur'an. We sent down the Qur'an on Laylatul Qadr. And here He says قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًۭا. SubhanAllah! Allah gave clothing the same status that He gave His revelation. Clothing is a revealed gift! To disregard clothing is to disregard a piece of revelation. The Qur'an was sent down; clothing was sent down. If we truly try to understand, if we truly fathom what Allah is saying here, we will have a completely different appreciation whenever we dress from now on.

What was the first thing given to Adam and Hawwa in Paradise? Clothes. What was taken away from them as a result of their disobedience? Clothes! What is the first thing given to us once again, when we are sent into this world? Clothes! Allah honored us once again — with clothes.

قَدْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمْ لِبَاسًۭا يُوَرِى سَوْءَتِكُمْ. Here, once more, is My gift to you. Once more I will cover your shame; once more I will cover your ugliness. يُوَرِى سَوْءَتِكُمْ — just as I did for your parents.

Now consider this: clothing could have been hideous, could it not? If the sole purpose of clothing were to cover the private parts, it did not need to be beautiful. It could have been plain; it could have been ugly. Yet Allah says: I am not giving you clothes merely to cover your ugliness. I am also giving you clothes so that you may look beautiful. يُوَرِى سَوْءَتِكُمْ وَرِيشًۭا.

Reesh is the Arabic word for beautiful feathers — the feathers of a peacock. When it spreads its feathers, that display is called Reesh. And when archers fix a feather to their arrows — قَبلَ الرَّمِی یُرَاش السَّھَمُ — before shooting the arrow, one feathers it, because it then flies with better guidance. So reeshan carries the sense of adornment. Allah says: We sent down clothes for you to cover your ugliness, and also for beauty — to dress well, to look lovely, to adorn yourselves. All of that is reeshan. You do not need to remove your clothes to look beautiful; you can look beautiful by means of your clothes.

Another lesson we draw from this verse is this: dress well. Dress well, especially the boys and the men. Allah did not give us clothes merely to cover the body. If we appear disheveled, we are not honoring Allah's gift. It need not be costly; simply iron the shirt from time to time, and do not go about looking unkempt. Dress well. And see — here is another waswasa of Shaytan: the whisper that Islam wants us to look ugly. Shaytan says: the more clothing you remove, the tighter the clothing you wear, the more skin you show, the more beautiful you will appear. Wear the tighter shirt. It is fine — reveal some skin, you look attractive, expose yourself, you look beautiful.

But the real question is: beautiful to whom? Beautiful to Shaytan! Beautiful to the followers of Shaytan — not to Allah, certainly not to Allah. For in this verse Allah says that you do not need to expose your body to display your beauty. I have given you clothes for that. So clothes are not a means of making us look ugly; clothes are a means of making us look beautiful. وَرِيشًۭا.

And then He adds: وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌۭ. And the clothing of taqwa — being mindful of Allah at all times — that is the best clothing for your soul. He honored us with clothing for the body; He honored us with clothing for the soul. SubhanAllah! Taqwa is the ultimate garment in which you can dress your soul. Every single day Shaytan is stripping us of both these garments, and we do not even realize what we are doing.

So Allah says that the idea of clothing is not merely physical; it is also spiritual. Physical clothing will protect your bodies, and spiritual clothing — taqwa, piety — will protect your soul. وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌۭ. ذَلِكَ مِنْ آيَتِ ٱللَّهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ. That is among the great signs of Allah, so that they may strive to remember Allah — to remember Allah every single time we put on our clothes. Everything I have shared with you about the Istiaaza — every part of it — is meant to flash through our minds. لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ. So that you may remember Allah through your clothing. When I put on my clothes, I am to remember that this is an honor for me from Allah, even as I cover up my shame.

I cover my ugliness with clothes. I need to cover my soul in piety. I have to protect myself from Shaytan, who will try to strip away my clothes — not by taking them off me directly, but by setting me on a path that will end with my clothes being stripped from me before Allah. SubhanAllah. Then He says: يَبَنِىٓ آدَمَ لَا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَنُ كَمَآ أَخْرَجَ أَبَوَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ. O children of Adam, do not let Shaytan do to you what he did to your parents. In other words, learn the lesson from the story of your parents that happened before you. The Arabs say: السَّعِیدُ مِنَ الطَّعَتْ بِغَیرِہِ. True happiness belongs to the one who learns his lessons from other people; he does not have to prove those lessons for himself. This is the idea that those who do not know their history are condemned to repeat it over and over again.

This is why we are being told this story: because here on this earth, there is a struggle going on. And there are two components to this struggle. The first is your own desire, because if you did not desire the thing in the first place, then no one could persuade you even to try it. So you and I have this thing called هوی — caprice, or desire. And then there is an unseen element at work in the world, which suggests to us that we explore that desire, that we test it, that we try it. That is ذوق, or ذاق — the wish to check it out, to see what it is like. That is what got our parents expelled from Jannah.

You see, they had within them the desire to live in Jannah forever. Had they not had that desire, they would never have listened to Iblees — even when he swore before them, they would not have listened, if they had had no desire. But they did have that desire, and Shaytan made them explore it. Yet it was only the taste, the Zawq, that constituted their disobedience.

And then Allah says: يَنزِعُ عَنْهُمَا لِبَاسَهُمَا لِيُرِيَهُمَا سَوْءَتِهِمَآ. He pulled off their clothes, so that he could expose their ugliness. Look at these words: يَنزِعُ — he pulled off their clothes. The word نزع means to pull out. You know how, when someone is about to die, in their final moments, they say he is in the state of نزع. It means his soul is being pulled out of his body. This ayat says that Shaytan pulled their clothes off them. Now that would indicate that Shaytan had more power over them! Yes or no? To suggest taking off clothes is one thing; to pull off clothes is another. So how is it that Allah says Shaytan pulled off their clothes?

This ayah is teaching us — and please listen to this very carefully — this ayah is teaching us that disobeying Allah grants authority to Shaytan. Disobeying Allah grants power to Shaytan over us. Every time you and I dress inappropriately, in both the physical and the spiritual sense, we give more and more power to Shaytan. Shaytan gains more power over you and me every single time we disobey Allah. The more we disobey Allah, the more power Shaytan gains over us, until we reach the point where he can simply tell us what to do, and we comply like his slave. He will merely command, and we will obey.

The only power Allah had given Shaytan originally was to do waswasa, to whisper. But we give him the real power of command — by accepting his whisper, by listening to it, and by complying with it. And the more we do this, the more power he gains over us.

He keeps growing stronger and stronger and stronger, until he gains complete authority over us. Now he can simply command us to do a thing. For Allah says: ٱلشَّيْطَنُ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱلْفَقْرَ وَيَأْمُرُكُم بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ — Shaytan promises you bankruptcy. Bankruptcy where? Before Allah. He promises that by the time you stand before Allah — I promise you — you will not have a single good deed to your name. يَعِدُكُمُ ٱلْفَقْرَ. And how does he do it? وَيَأْمُرُكُم بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ ۖ — he commands you to lewdness, to shamelessness. Allah did not say یُوَسوِسُ لکم الفحشاء, یَنسِحُو لکم ان تفشحو — that he suggested lewdness to you, that he whispered it to you. No, no, no, no. Allah says that he commands you to shamelessness.

How does he command you? People have come to me and said, "I cannot stop watching pornography. I cannot stop smoking." I know you cannot, because Shaytan is commanding you, because you keep disobeying Allah. You have to cut it off. That is the only way for Shaytan to let go of you: you have to stop. You and I have to take back that control, by giving that control to Allah, where it belongs. For Allah said to Shaytan: ‏إِنَّ عِبَادِى لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَنٌ — you will have no authority over My slaves. What does that mean? It means that if they are not truly My slaves, you will have complete authority over them. ‏إِنَّ عِبَادِى لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَنٌ. This is our legacy in this world.

Then Allah says: إِنَّهُۥ يَرَىٰكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُۥ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا تَرَوْنَهُمْ — he is constantly watching you, he and his tribe of followers. Did he not say to Allah that he would sit upon the straight path, waiting to ambush us? And when someone is waiting to ambush you, can you see him or not? Allah says, "I made that a part of your test. He is watching you, he and his entire tribe." مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا تَرَوْنَهُمْ — from a place where you cannot even see them. إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّيَطِينَ أَوْلِيَآءَ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ — all the devils, and legions of them, have made friends with people who do not believe. People who do not believe will accept that whisper, and they will enjoy that whisper. The fellow will say, "My parents are not home right now. I can watch whatever I want. I can do whatever I want. Nobody will ever know. I can smoke. I can take a Tic Tac afterward. Nobody will know." Allah will know.

So after narrating the entire story of Adam and Iblees, Allah speaks to us, the children of Adam, and warns us: Do not repeat the same mistake your parents made. Do not listen to Shaytan. He got your parents thrown out of Jannah, and he will do the same to you, so be careful; do not repeat the same mistake. I warned them too, and they did not listen. I am warning you now. Be careful. Do not disobey Me. And if you do end up disobeying Me, then follow the pattern of your parents, by admitting your fault, by accepting accountability for your actions, and then, after taking complete responsibility for what you have done, repenting before Allah. Do not follow the pattern of Iblees and invent logical reasonings to justify your disobedience. For he will entice you. He will attack you. And once you give him power through your constant disobedience to Me and your constant obedience to him, he will then make you his slave. He will command you to sin, and you will comply.

Because he wants to dishonor you before Allah. He wants to strip you of your clothing—clothing that I have equated with revelation, clothing for your body as well as for your soul. I have made physical clothing not merely a covering for your ugliness but also a means of adornment for you, so that you may look beautiful. And I have made piety, taqwa, a clothing for your soul, so that it not only covers up your sins but also adorns your character and makes you respectable before Allah and His creation. And of the two, this spiritual clothing of taqwa is the better. وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌۭ. Why? Because in order to be pious, you will need to dress appropriately. You will need to dress modestly. You cannot dress in a lewd manner and be pious. That is why it is the better of the two. It is also better because it adorns your soul, which is going to return to Me. Your body is going to decay in the dirt, so what is more important is the clothing of the soul. But you cannot have one without the other. And how do you fashion this spiritual clothing? What is the raw material from which you fashion this spiritual clothing, this taqwa? It is this revelation. That is why I sent down revelation, and I sent down clothing. The first step is to be mindful. Nothing has to happen overnight. The farmer and the seed. You fall; you dust yourself off and begin again. The toddler versus the child who stands. I always saw Amir fall—this boy is never going to walk. We are toddlers in the eyes of Allah. Al-wida. The next session is November 22nd. All excuses will fail on the Day of Judgment. Now look at this. Allah continues. Now, these are comments on the mushrikoon of Mecca; this is in fact a commentary on all of society. وَإِذَا فَعَلُوا۟ فَحِشَةًۭ—when they did something shameless—قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَآ آبَآءَنَا—they said, our parents did this. What are you talking about? This is completely normal. There is nothing wrong with this. Our parents used to dress like this; why can we not dress like this? What is the big deal? My parents watched Indian movies; we watch American movies, so what is the big deal? I have been raised watching a man go after a woman and a woman go after a man; so what if I did it in college? This ayah is not speaking only about the Quraish; it is not speaking only about the disbelievers of Mecca. It is speaking about you and me, because these are the words your children and mine will say when they grow up, if we do not change ourselves today. This is what we will have to hear our children say one day. What will you do then? What will I do then? What is happening at weddings today—the dresses, the functions? And what do we say? It is all good, it is all normal. But normal for whom—Allah or shaytaan? This then develops further into: so what if I have a girlfriend? So what if I have a boyfriend? So what if I watch this filth on the internet? Anybody and everybody does it; it is not such a big deal. Now let me tell you something.

On the Day of Judgment, this social circle you are using as an excuse, those friends you are using as an excuse, even your parents whom you are using as an excuse—on the Day of Judgment you will not be able to stand before Allah and say: I did it because they did it; they are the reason I turned out this way. It will not work. يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ ٱلْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ—on that day each person will run away from his brother.

He abandons his own brother—وَأُمِّهِۦ وَأَبِيهِ  and his mother and his father—وَصَحِبَتِهِۦ وَبَنِيهِ  and his wife and his children. These are terrifying, forceful words. They are not words for you and me to take lightly, because the people of Quraish tried exactly that. They said: our ancestors did it, so what does it matter if we do it too? وَٱللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا—God has commanded us to do this. They went even a step further and said it is Allah's own will that we behave this way. If He did not want us to dress like this, to do all of these things, why would He allow all of it to happen? God wants us to be happy! There is nothing wrong with wanting to be happy, with wanting to look attractive. God wants us to be happy! That is why I love her; that is why I love him! Those people went as far as to say وَٱللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا—Allah wants us to do all of this! Allah wants us to be this way.

ۗ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ ۖ—Tell them: Allah does not command you to shamelessness. He does not want you to be lewd or indecent. There is another lesson here. When people deviate from Allah's path, they grow so arrogant that they begin to speak on Allah's behalf. Allah does not want us to be so harsh; Allah does not want us to be so conservative; do not be so hard on yourself; Allah forgives. Where does Allah say in the Qur'an that you must do this or that or the other? Have you ever heard that one before? I will show you where Allah says all of that! You want to know where Allah says it in the Qur'an? I will show you! Because when someone speaks that way, do you know what the truth is? They have already made up their minds to disobey Allah. So as we grow in arrogance, we begin to speak on Allah's behalf, and we begin to say there is nothing wrong with that, that it is perfectly fine.

Allah says: أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ—Are you saying things about Allah that you have no knowledge of? Tell them: قُلْ أَمَرَ رَبِّى بِٱلْقِسْطِ—Tell them: my Master commands fairness, commands justice. وَأَقِيمُوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍۢ. Now look: Allah had been speaking about lewdness and indecency, and now the subject changes to justice and prayer. He says: قُلْ أَمَرَ رَبِّى بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَأَقِيمُوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍۢ—Tell them: my Master commands justice and to turn your faces toward the masjid, meaning: establish prayer, establish salaah. What this teaches us is that shamelessness will lead us to injustice, and shamelessness will lead us to abandoning our prayers.

Now you tell me: is the filth industry an injustice and a manipulation of women? Is this industry built upon the violation of women's dignity? Yes or no? And by the way, the old form of it was prostitution. Was that not a form of injustice to women? Was that not an oppression of women? That was a subject the Qur'an actually attacked; it spoke of prostitution and of how it must come to an end. Because shamelessness became an industry and a vehicle through which injustice is spread, and Allah says that He does not command injustice. And that is only at the level of society.

But at the personal level, how will you keep yourself away from shamelessness? You will remain upright before Allah and do justice with yourself and with Allah, through the means of salaah. Now, what does salaah have to do with staying away from shamelessness? Everything! Everything. Salaah has everything to do with shamelessness.

Allah says so explicitly in the Qur'an: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ Keep reciting the book that was revealed to you, and establish prayer. Indeed, without any doubt, prayer prevents you from every form of shamelessness and other evils.

People say, "I pray five times a day, yet I still cannot keep away from filth." My answer to them is this: you are not really praying. You are not really connecting with Allah. You are only going through the motions. For according to this verse, Allah says إِنَّ — without any doubt, absolutely, one hundred percent: if you are praying, if you truly are connecting with me, it will protect you from shamelessness. So if you pray and still struggle with shamelessness, you need to examine and evaluate your prayers in earnest.

The final topic: يَبَنِىٓ آدَمَ خُذُوا۟ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍۢ وَكُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ وَلَا تُسْرِفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ Children of Adam, take your beauty seriously, take your clothing seriously, and beautify yourself. Dress up. Come decked out. At every time of prayer, and in every place of prayer, beautify yourself when you speak to me. Dress nicely when you pray. Do not wake up and pray fajr in your pajamas. Dress nicely before Allah.

If you have a meeting with the CEO of a company, you dress up. If you have a meeting with the dean of academics, you dress up. If you have an interview at immigration, you dress up. The prayer is a meeting with Allah, and you do not dress up! Dress nicely. Allah says, beautify yourself. Do you know why this is important? Because when you engage in the act of ironing your clothes because you are about to make salaah, when you engage in the act of picking the right color and dressing nicely, when you engage in the act of applying itr to please the angels who are about to visit you, and ladies, when you engage in the act of wearing beautiful gold jewelry to stand before Allah and beautify yourself for Allah, your prayer will change of its own accord. Your khushu, your reverence, will change of its own accord.

When do people dress up? When they are going to a party, is that not so? So that they can be in the picture! If nobody is going to look at you, why would you dress nicely? Other people are going to look at you, so you dress nicely. When you dress up, it means you are conscious of the one who is looking at you. The greatest party you will ever attend happens five times a day, where you are the guest of honor, surrounded by angels on every side, holding a conversation with none other than your Master. That is the prayer! Dress nicely.

Allah created us in comfort. Allah says in the Qur'an to human beings: وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَيِشَ. قَلِيلًۭا مَّا تَشْكُرُونَ We settled you down on the earth, and we gave you good housing. Makanna means good housing. And especially for you, وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ, especially for you, we placed every means on this earth so that you could live well. معایش comes from معیشۃ, which means a life that is well lived. In Urdu we use this word, عیش. بڑے عیش سے رہ رہے ہیں. That is an Arabic word. It means to live very well. العیش is a good life. Allah says, we placed the means of a good life for you on this earth. So that is the first misconception addressed. People think Islam has so many rules; it does not want us to live a good life. Allah does not want us to enjoy ourselves. Allah is telling us.

that he created us on this earth so that we might have a good life. You know, this same word عیش is used to describe paradise. فھو فی عیشۃ راضیۃ. They will live a wonderful life in jannah. And there is a glimpse of that even in this world. There are glimpses of معائش — means of living really, really well on this earth, of enjoying ourselves.

And by the way, where does enjoyment come from? Enjoyment happens when you get what you desire. Enjoyment happens when you get what you desire. It is very simple. You have a craving, and you fulfill that craving, and that is what enjoyment is. I am really craving to play some tennis. I get to play. I enjoyed myself. I am craving to play a video game. I get to play. I enjoyed myself, right? I am craving some chocolate ice cream. I was able to have it. I enjoyed myself. Cravings! When cravings are fulfilled, that is when enjoyment happens. You have an itch, you scratch it, that is enjoyment. Enjoyment does not happen outside of that.

And so our temptations are also cravings. The attraction a man has toward a woman is also a craving. And Allah says, in this world I gave you the means by which you can enjoy yourselves. You can fulfill all your cravings in a legitimate way. I have given you provisions for all of that. All of that is covered. وَجَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَعَيِشَ

This is how Iblees tries to confuse them. But the two of them do not believe him. So what does Iblees do? He swears to them both: وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّصِحِينَ. He swore to them both that he was one of their well-wishers. Iblees swore to them by Allah: اُقسِم باللہ. Now you see.

This is Iblees. He will go to any lengths to do what he needs to do. So he lies to both of them. And you must understand something here. Adam and Hawwa had no concept of a lie. All they had ever known was the truth, because they had never heard anyone lie before.

Also in this verse Iblees says: إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّصِحِينَ. Now in balagha, in Arabic rhetoric, when you say انی — انی یقول ھذا — that is called mutaraddid. It means you are speaking to someone who is doubting you. He is not sure; maybe he believes you, maybe he does not. So when you use انی, it is like saying: I know you doubt me, but I assure you that I am telling you the truth. But when you use a laam a second time along with inni — إِنِّى لَكُمَا لَمِنَ ٱلنَّصِحِينَ — he did not say مِنَ ٱلنَّصِحِينَ, he said لَمِنَ ٱلنَّصِحِينَ. That is for someone who does not believe you at all. So Iblees used that to say: I know you do not believe me at all, but I am swearing to the utmost that I am telling you the truth. That is the language he is using. In other words: believe me, I swear I am sincere with you.

Now here are two people who do not even know what a lie is, because they are in that pure state, and then they see this creation of Allah swearing by his Creator: وَقَاسَمَهُمَآ. It was simply unthinkable to them that somebody could swear by Allah and lie. That was something completely unthinkable to them, and that is what they fell for. Iblees tempted them for the longest time, as we will learn in the next verse. They did not immediately fall into temptation. But when Iblees swore by Allah, they believed him. That is how he got to them. The point is that Iblees will go to any extremes.

We think: how could he deceive me? How could she want to hurt me? She is my best friend. He is my best friend. No. You cannot put anything past Shaytan, or someone who is under the control of Shaytan. He will go to the most extreme ends to do what he needs to do.

فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍۢ. Dalla in Arabic is a verb. Tadliyah, the infinitive verb, is actually used when you have a bucket, and you have a rope attached to that bucket, and then you pull the bucket slowly, little by little by little. If you pull it immediately, if you pull it hard and fast, it is adla. If you pull it slowly, then it is dalla. In the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him, when his brothers left him in a well, a caravan passed by and lowered a bucket into the well for water, and when they pulled it out, a boy came out sitting in the bucket. In that verse, what does Allah say? وَجَآءَتْ سَيَّارَةٌۭ فَأَرْسَلُوا۟ وَارِدَهُمْ فَأَدْلَىٰ دَلْوَهُ. Here the word adla is used, implying that they pulled the rope hard and fast, and the bucket, with the boy in it, came up rather quickly. Now you and I know that a boy is not that light, so it must still have taken some time to pull it up, right? But that is still adla. Yet when Iblees is described figuratively, when he took Adam and Hawwa, peace be upon them, and he yanked them out of Jannah, like a bucket pulled out of a well, Allah uses the word dalla, meaning he took his sweet time.

You are like modern-age children. I do not know if you ever watched old-school cartoons like Tom and Jerry. Tom is a cat. Jerry is a mouse.

Tom has a piece of cheese in a bucket, and there is a rope tied to the bucket. Jerry smells the cheese, and as he draws near the bucket, Tom slowly pulls it toward himself. Then a little more, and a little more, and a little more. And what does Jerry do? He keeps walking toward Tom, until at last Tom catches him. So Tom is using the bucket to lure Jerry in, very, very slowly, so gradually that it is never noticed. That, in Arabic, is called دلا.

In other words, Iblees did not simply walk up to them and say, "Hey! That fruit on that tree — ah, ha ha ha, so delicious! Eat it! Do it! Do it!" It did not happen that way. Nor is it as though he walked up to them and said, "Hey, you! Eat from that tree," and the two of them said, "Ah, all right." No, no, no, no. He whispered his waswasa to them again and again and again. He came in the morning. He came in the evening. He came at night. "Hey, are you hungry? Are the two of you hungry? I know of this one tree." Now, Jannah has countless trees, does it not? Jannah is far larger than the earth. So how difficult would it have been to find this one forbidden tree? Think about that. Of all the trees in the entire universe of Jannah, there is one that is forbidden. And Shaytan first had to guide them, step by step, back to that one forbidden tree, little by little. "Hey, why not take this turn? Why not come over here? Look at those strawberries — they look rather delicious, do they not? Drink from this river; it is so sweet."

So دلا suggests that he did not call them to the forbidden thing at once. He brought them to it very slowly, in a calculated manner. "Hey, look at this waterfall. Go to that mountain. Taste this mango. Then go over here. And then over here." And they are listening to him, and they are thinking this has nothing to do with any larger plan. They do not see that this is part of a larger plan. And Allah is teaching us that this is exactly what Shaytan does. This is what he did to them, and this is what he does to us. He tempts you into doing something. And when you first do it, you say, "It is not forbidden. I mean, it is not as though it is totally forbidden. It is not as though it is absolutely, totally, completely forbidden. At least I am not doing such and such" — and that is where you fill in your own creativity. "So what if I have a girlfriend? So what if I have a boyfriend? We are only friends. We are simply enjoying a good time together. I enjoy talking to her. I enjoy talking to him. At least we are not doing such and such." "It is only a cigarette. It is not even lit. I simply like holding it. It is not as though I am doing such and such." "I am in love with her. I am in love with him. What sort of a religion comes between two lovers?" All of it is very compelling logic.

But the truth is that Shaytan will not bring you to the destination immediately. He wants only to bring you to the first milestone, because from there he will work on you for a month or two to bring you to the next milestone. And then to the third, and then to the fourth. Eventually you will end up doing that very thing that you spoke of in the beginning, when you said, "At least I am not doing such and such." You will now be doing exactly that. And guess what: when you do it, you will still have wonderful logical justifications for it. But he will not bring you to that point immediately. He will work on you slowly, very slowly.

That is فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍۢ. He lures very slowly, by deception. He will work on a young man and a young woman to draw them into a forbidden relationship, and he will do it very slowly. He begins the affair in the most innocent manner. Oh, she is only my study partner. She is only helping me with my biology assignments. It is all harmless. We will meet in this house. We will study right in front of you. We will keep the door open. We are only two friends studying. It is not as though we are — dot, dot, dot. Right?

And then, slowly, after a few weeks: So what films do you like? Who is your favorite actor? Oh, really? Mine too. His film is showing tonight — would you like to see it? Now the parents ask, why are you going to the cinema with him? Why is it forbidden? Is watching a film forbidden? Am I not even permitted to watch a film? Does Islam say it is forbidden to watch a film with another person? Now the parents cannot tell you that it is forbidden. But it is not the film that worries them, is it? They know what Satan is doing — just a little, just a tiny turn here and there.

So, are you on Facebook? Of course I am. In fact, I have already looked you up. Little by little. And then the late-night texting begins. Oh, we are only texting. Is texting forbidden? Am I not even permitted to text someone now? Is WhatsApp forbidden? It was only a picture we shared. It was not even a video. One justification, then another justification. It is only a dinner. It is with the whole school group. It is about learning biology. Mm-hmm. Yes. I know. I know exactly what biology you are learning. One thing leads to another, then to another, then to another. And then the elders receive the telephone call. Oh, I truly need to marry her, as soon as possible. Why, what has happened? Oh, you know — that Satan. فَدَلَّىٰهُمَا بِغُرُورٍۢ. He got to us. Now I truly need to marry her. But I am only thirteen years old.

He will get to you, no matter how long it takes. In the end he will get to you. And you will end up doing the very thing you spoke of at the beginning. Remember? I am only studying biology. It is not as though we are — dot, dot, dot. Well — dot, dot, dot. That is Satan for you.

Tasting the tree. Then Allah says, فَلَمَّا ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ. So they eventually — and note this — اذا means when they did it, حین means when they did it, but فلما means eventually, when they did it. So again, this did not happen at once. ذَاقَا ٱلشَّجَرَةَ — the two of them tasted the tree. Now much has been said about not going near the tree. Do not go near the tree. And now Allah says that they both eventually tasted the tree.

Has any one of you ever tasted a tree? Has any one of you ever been tempted to taste a tree? What is there on a tree by which you would be tempted? It is the fruit — the fruit of the tree, not the tree itself. And is the fruit usually within easy reach? No, it is not. The fruit ordinarily hangs upon a branch. The tree itself may be within reach.
