There is a subconscious association with punishment when the word "mercy" is used, and then with the idea of escaping that punishment. In mercy, the default position is punishment.

Now, if we constantly use that word "mercy" for Allah, and repeat it for Him over and over again, then it brings up the idea that Allah wanted to do something bad to us and then decided not to, and so He spared us and showed us mercy. In other words, when Allah is being merciful, what He is actually doing is sparing me from punishment. But that is not the true intent of the word Rehmah. Rehma has nothing to do with punishment; it contains no concept of punishment at all.

In classical Arabic, Rehma has four meanings: first, unconditional love; second, care; third, genuine concern; and fourth, mercy. Mercy is the last piece of it, not the first. Love comes first, then care, then concern, and then mercy. This is Rehma. When we call Allah Rehman and Raheem, we acknowledge four things: that Allah has intense love for us, that He cares for us, that He is genuinely concerned about us, and that He shows us mercy. That is the implicit acknowledgment in any word derived from the word رحمۃ.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
Now, what is it about the mother's womb that is important for us to understand? There are a few things. First of all, when the child is inside its mother's womb, is it being punished? Is there any association with the idea of punishment for the baby while it is inside its mother's womb? No! What is the mother's relationship with the baby? It is pure love, is it not? So this is the very first relationship of Allah with His creation: it is founded on pure love, and it has nothing to do with punishment. The moment a woman learns that she is pregnant, she falls in love with the baby. She has not even seen the baby yet. She has not even met it, and yet she falls completely and unconditionally in love with her baby.

Now, did the womb exist even before the mother conceived? Or does the body simply create the womb when she becomes pregnant and then discard it afterward? It exists within the mother. Baby or no baby, the womb is always there. In the same way, Allah's رحمۃ is always there. His رحمۃ does not exist because of us. His رحمۃ is always there.

Now, when the child is inside its mother's womb, does the child even know that it is being cared for? Does it even know that the mother exists? It does not. It is being cared for in ways it cannot even comprehend. Allah is caring for us in ways we cannot possibly comprehend. He is caring for us in a manner so subtle that, forget His رحمۃ, even His presence is not visible to us. He is caring for us in a manner so subtle. That is why one of His names is Lateef. Lateef means something extremely subtle. It is there, and it is working for you, but you do not even feel its presence. That is Lateef. But what is amazing is that in the Quran, every time the attribute Lateef is mentioned, which other attribute do you hear alongside it? Khabeer, the All-Knowing. لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ Your eyes cannot see Him, but He is aware of what your eyes are seeing. He is extremely subtle, yet All-Knowing at the same time. SubhanAllah! So the child does not even know that the mother is caring for it.

The next thing that comes to mind when you think of the womb is protection. The mother is constantly protecting the baby. She watches the corners of the table when she walks; she tries to stay safe; she sleeps on her side; she watches what she eats; she is constantly caressing the baby. She loves the baby. She cares for the baby. And she is extremely protective of it. That is what Allah is doing for us, constantly. You do not simply make it to school on your own. Can you even imagine how many things could go wrong in just the time between leaving the house and entering your school? Millions of things could go wrong, but Allah is protecting you, keeping you safe. Every morning I have to walk twenty minutes to my bus stop, and back home again every evening. I have to cross a highway, and streets, and parking lots. I could be hit by a car at any moment. It takes only one second. And on top of that, I have my headphones on. I am not even being especially careful. Yet I make it to work every day, and make it back home every day, without incident.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
SubhanAllah! That is Allah constantly protecting me. Then consider how much a mother endures for the sake of her child. She contends with unrelenting morning sickness. Some must submit to dreadfully painful examinations. For the health and growth of the baby they must take medicines that leave them intensely nauseated, and they must give blood again and again — one painful ordeal following another. A mother passes through so much suffering for the sake of her child, and the child, once more, is wholly unaware of it. The child takes the mother entirely for granted.

And this child, strictly speaking, does nothing for the mother, while the mother does everything for the child. The baby consumes her food, does it not? The poor woman eats, and the child takes it all for itself, until she can only wonder whether it will ever be satisfied and let her be. She has just finished an enormous meal, and minutes later she is hungry again. And then the poor husband must hurry to the store in the middle of the night for ice cream. So the baby takes everything from her and gives nothing back to its mother in return. Indeed, when the baby does thank her, how does it offer its thanks? By kicking her from within. It stretches whenever it pleases, performs its own strenuous exercises whenever the impulse takes it, and presses against her ribs as though lifting weights. The mother is kept in a constant state of discomfort because of this baby. Is this not so?

We do nothing for Allah, yet Allah still does everything for us. We do nothing for Allah! We could do nothing for Allah even if we wished to. We cannot add to His kingdom. We cannot take anything away from His kingdom. Our good deeds add nothing to His kingdom. Our sins take nothing from His kingdom. We cannot make Him any wealthier than He is. We cannot make Him any poorer than He is. We cannot praise Him any more than He is already praised. We can add nothing to Him. We can do nothing whatever for Him. There is absolutely nothing that we are able to offer Allah. And yet He is constantly doing things for us, without our even being aware of His presence, and in many cases without our even acknowledging His presence.

كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِى شَأْنٍۢ

Every moment He is engaged in some work, to keep this universe, and everything within this universe, in working order. SubhanAllah.

Then we see that all of the child's needs are met by its mother. The child is completely surrounded. It is completely enveloped by the care of its mother. Its food, its drink, and even the removal of its waste — all of this is provided for by the body of the mother. Everything the child needs is fully supplied. The rent is paid. Housing and lodging are free. It has no utilities to pay for. Every meal is included. In other words, the baby is completely wrapped up in the love and care of its mother.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
In the same way, we are completely wrapped up in the unconditional love of Allah. He provides us with our sustenance. He grants us the comforts of a good life. He is keeping the world outside of us in working order, and He is keeping the world inside of us in working order. My heart is beating, my organs are functioning, my breath is passing in and out. I can walk. I can speak. He is making all of this happen for me. He gave me parents. He gave me teachers. He gave me knowledge. He gave me a family of my own. He surrounded me with all the comforts of my life.

Consider how we complain about paying the bills — the mortgage, the utilities. Yet stop and think for a moment: how much do we pay for our sight?

How much do we pay Allah for our ability to hear, for our ability to speak, for our ability to breathe? Forget everything else — how much are we paying for each breath? How much would you pay for a single breath? If you could not breathe, and Allah asked you to pay for your next breath, what amount would you be willing to give Him for it? How much would you pay for your hands? What would they be worth to you? We pass through life immensely blessed with His bounties, immensely blessed with the riches He created us with, and all of it we take completely for granted. Allahu Akbar.

Now let us speak about the motivation of this mother. The baby is not paying the mother. The baby is not giving anything back to her. So what, then, is the motivation that keeps this mother going, despite all the discomfort this child puts her through? What is it that keeps her going? The only motivation the mother has for the baby is an extreme form of unconditional love. Consider this: as the child grows within its mother's womb, it becomes more and more of a burden to her from a physical standpoint. Yet the more of a burden it becomes, the more deeply she falls in love with her baby. Her love is constantly increasing. This is incredible. And then, when the baby finally comes, it almost kills her. As though nine months of hardship were not enough, this baby brings on the intense pain of childbirth.

I have been in the delivery room twice, and I feel I have been traumatized for life. Nazneen was in labor for eight hours when Erum was born. I have never seen anyone endure so much pain. And yet, when Erum was finally out, covered in all that fluid, they tried to hand her to me, and I thought, ewww. But then they brought Erum to Nazneen, and she so lovingly touched her cheeks and said, "Hi, baby," and then she passed out. That was such an astonishing moment in my life. I still do not understand it. I probably never will. I would have thought she would hate this baby who had caused her so much pain, that she would yell at her, scream at her, curse her — "You almost killed me! I hate you!" But no, that is not what happened. The first time they brought Erum to her, she gave her a big hug. She kissed her. She began to cry because she was so happy to see her. And then she began to feed her. Subhan Allah.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
Anyone else who caused you so much pain, who made you bleed in this way, you would not embrace. We make our mothers bleed, almost to death, and the moment we come out, she has more love for us than she ever had before — and this is right after we have tried to kill her. This is a completely illogical relationship. This is not a relationship you can make any sense of. It is beyond all logic. It does not happen in any other relationship. There is no other relationship that works this way, where you never give — you never, ever give, you only take — and still all she does is keep giving you her love. You keep taking more, and she keeps giving more.

And consider this: your mother bled so much to give you life. She has just been through childbirth, or surgery, and what happens right after you are born? She now has to feed you. And I have heard that, for many women, feeding too can be extremely painful. Anyone else in this world who goes through surgery, or such intense pain, says, "I need six weeks off."

I need 2 months off. I need a break. I need a vacation. Does a mother receive a two-month vacation after she gives birth? No! You break a leg, and you get six months off. She has just given birth, and now she is on the clock, working full time, the very second the baby is born. And what does the baby give her back in return? She gives it milk. She gives it love. She gives it care. She gives it protection. She bathes it, oils it, changes its diapers, all through countless sleepless nights, month after month, year after year. And what does the baby do in return? Does it say thank you? Does it show gratitude? Does it praise the mother? No! But does the mother still keep loving and caring for the baby, over and over and over again? She does! She receives nothing from the baby. The most the baby does is reward her by urinating on her, defecating on her, throwing up on her. And even when the baby does that, she says, "Aww, so cute," and then she cleans it up. "Oh, it is all right, my little baby." Is this not incredibly beautiful? But is this not, at the same time, an utterly senseless relationship?
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
Yet this is what Allah is doing for us. This is what Allah is doing for us, on a much greater scale. And does that not also fail to make sense? Allah's love for us simply does not make sense. It is beyond all logical reasoning. We cannot confine Allah's love to common sense, because we do not deserve this kind of love from Allah. That is what common sense dictates. If we compare our actions, if we look at our ingratitude toward Allah — we do not even remember him five times a day. Two hours. That is all it takes. We cannot even manage that much, just to say thank you, after everything he does for us. We constantly disobey him. We do everything he tells us not to do. Some do not even acknowledge his existence. Who knows whether there is an Allah or not, and who cares if there is. After everything he does for us, we do not even have the decency to say thank you, simply by praying to him five times. Even just the obligatory prayers. Thirty minutes a day, if you do only the obligatory prayers. We do not even give him that much. And yet he keeps giving to us, keeps giving to us. Despite my constant ingratitude, my constant disloyalty, my constant defiance of his every command, I am still waking up. I am still breathing. I am still going about my day, eating, drinking, enjoying, celebrating. And he does not take that away from me. This does not make sense. It simply does not make sense.

Just look at what we do with food. How much food do we waste? His greatest blessings for mankind, the means of sustenance — look how we disrespect food. Look at the etiquette of eating. The Prophet (salawaat) said: sit before your food as a slave sits before his master. Cover your head before you eat, to show it respect. Do not place it on the floor; raise the table off the ground to honor it. When you are finished, gather and eat the crumbs that are left behind. That is how much esteem food should hold in our lives. Do we ever think of the amount of effort it took, behind the scenes, to get that food onto our plate? Do we think about the time, the effort, the protection, the management, the design that went into taking that seed and growing it into a plant; into taking that animal, raising it until it reached the proper age, feeding it all that time, and getting it into the hands of the one who performs zabeeha, who makes it halal for us.

then to bring it to the supermarket and the butcher's shop, so that you might buy it, and to give you the means to cook it, until at last it arrives on your plate. Years upon years of Allah's labor sit before us on that plate. Do we care? No. We take a few bites and throw it away, only because it is not warm enough, not fresh enough, or has too little salt. Imagine that you labor over a school project for months and months, only for it to be thrown out at the end. Tell me how that would feel to you. Tell me what your answer would be the next time you were asked to build a project.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
We disrespect and disregard Allah's efforts without ceasing, and yet He keeps giving us food, each dish finer than the last. It is just as a mother keeps feeding her baby no matter what it does. Does the baby care about the months of intense effort that went into growing it from a drop into a child, and then from a child into an adult? No. But does the mother stop loving the child? No. This is a mad, boundless love. There is absolutely no reason for Allah to love us in this way, but He does. He does. Why? Because He has Rehma for us. Because His relationship with us, as His creation, is a relationship of Rehma.

اِنِّی سَمَّیتُکَ بِاسْمی

O Womb, I have named you from among My names. I have named you Reham, because I am al-Rehman and al-Raheem. I have made you a symbol of My love, so that every human being might recognize My unconditional love for them through you and because of you. This is why Allah is al-Rehman and al-Raheem. SubhanAllah. We can never truly understand the love and care of Allah, but so that we might grasp something of this relationship, He gave us the mother. If you wish to taste a single drop of that endless ocean of love, of whom do you think? Your mother.

Rehma is His universal attribute. His Rehma is greater than His wrath; over His ghadab He has Rehma.

إن الله لما قضى الخلق كتب فوق عرشه …. رحمتي سبقت غضبي

The Rehma of Allah is over His anger. And the anger of God is a matter of justice, which we will consider when we study Malik Yaum al-Deen.

The essence of human Rehma is from the womb. Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, spoke to the womb — and this is the archetypal womb from which all the wombs of women come. Allah spoke to this Reham.

إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَهُ قُرْءَنًا عَرَبِيًّۭا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

Arabic has a unique capacity to ignite the intellect by its very nature, because of certain elements of the Arabic language that are not found, in particular, in the European languages such as English. The Qur'an demands that you think; it does not let you off easily. The Qur'an, by its nature in Arabic, makes you think. You cannot understand it without due contemplation.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en: So Allah has made the womb a source of mercy. Allah says, وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِى تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِۦ وَٱلْأَرْحَامَ ۚ "And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs." This is one of the few times that God pairs the command to be conscious of Him with something else. He mentions this only twice in the Book, as far as I know. We must have a conscious awareness of God, and a conscious awareness of the wombs. If a person's humanity is not nurtured within the house, among our own relatives, then there is no way it will come to exist outside it. If we do not treat our own blood properly, we will never be able to treat anyone else properly. To sever ties with relatives is among the worst things in Islam. Why? Because if you cannot learn to live with these people, to whom you are bound by blood, how can you live with the rest of the people, who share no such bond with you? If we are not made humane within the house, how is society to function? Where will mercy come from, if not from our own flesh and blood? How can I then extend it out to the rest of society? کان بالمومنین رحیما — He is Raheem with the believers, not with the disbelievers. So Rehman is for everyone; Raheem is for the believers alone. Rehman is for this world; Raheem is for the life to come.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
Another thing to understand about the word Rehma is that it means to show love and care in order to bring benefit to someone. رِقَّۃٌ تَقتَدِ الأحسانُ أِلی المَرحوم. It is a love or tenderness that is intended to benefit the beloved. So رحمۃ is not merely love and care; it is a kind of love and care that is intended to benefit, and that actually ends up benefiting the beloved. So if you have true رحمۃ, it will translate into action, and not remain merely in theory.

And by deriving these two words, AlRehman and AlRaheem, from the same root, Allah is emphasizing His loving nature. He is emphasizing that He has رحمۃ, that He is characterized by رحمۃ. This is a trait, a characteristic, that is extremely important to Allah.

There are many verses in the Qur'an in which Allah mentions His رحمۃ. He says:

وَمِن رَّحْمَتِهِۦ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ

Out of His love, He created the night and the day.

مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِۦ وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُم مِّنْ أَمْرِكُم مِّرْفَقًۭا

Out of His love, He will make your tasks easy for you.

وَمِنْ آيَتِهِۦٓ أَن يُرْسِلَ ٱلرِّيَاحَ مُبَشِّرَتٍۢ وَلِيُذِيقَكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِ

Out of His love, He sends the winds that carry good tidings.

مَّا يَفْتَحِ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍۢ فَلَا مُمْسِكَ لَهَاۖ

When Allah opens the doors of His love, no one can close them.

The purpose of all of this is to explain one thing to us. We have spoken about Allah being our master. And when you think of the word master, you think of the word authority; and when you think of authority, the last thing you think of is unconditional love. Yet Allah tells us at once, right after mentioning His name Allah, that He is a different kind of master. You will never find a master in this world who is as powerful as He is and yet has the kind of رحمۃ that He has.

Choose any other master in this world; he will not give you unconditional love the way Allah will love you. Such masters tell you what to do. They force you to fulfill their needs and desires. They judge you by their own standards, not by your capabilities. They put you through painful punishments when you do not obey. They may even care for you once in a while, but they will never love you. Is this not the case? Is this not true of every master who owns a slave? Masters will always give their love only to their own, but they will never love their slave.

But this master, our master, Allah, says that the very first feeling He has toward you is unconditional love. Any other master will not care about you, but Allah will always care about you. No other master will be genuinely concerned about you; He will always be concerned for you. No other master will show you mercy when you disobey him or do not complete a task to his standards; He will always have mercy on you. His judgment will not be by His standards, but by your capabilities.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
In a hadith, Rasul Allah (SAWAS) said that when Allah created the creation, He wrote a rule book for Himself. He made something compulsory upon Himself. Think about this for a moment. Allah is our master, and in our dealings with Him, He has made certain things compulsory on us. He made salaah, hajj, zakaat, and saum compulsory on us. All of these are forms of our interaction with Him. But when it came to His interaction with us, He too made something compulsory upon Himself. Rasul Allah (SAWAS) said that Allah wrote a rule book for Himself, which He keeps above His throne.

إن الله لَمَّا قضى الخلق كتب فوق عرشه

And in that rule book He wrote:

اِنَّ رَحمَتِی تَغلِبُ غَضَبِی

My love and care for My creation will always extinguish My wrath. My رحمۃ will always extinguish My anger. My رحمۃ will always overcome My wrath. Allah has made it compulsory, He has made it mandatory upon Himself, that whenever He deals with His creation, His dealings will always be moved by love and care, and His love will always overpower His anger. He has imposed this rule of love and care upon Himself for our sake. SubhanAllah.

And there is another hadith, in which Rasul Allah said:

that Allah has seventy times more love and care for His servants than a mother has for her child. In this world we live in, the finest exhibition of rahma, the finest display of mercy, the finest showing of love and care, is what a mother has for her child. This is the highest example our imagination can reach. And what did Rasul Allah say? He said: Indeed, I swear, Allah's love for His servants is seventy times greater than a mother's love for her child. This is why, in their supplications, some people would quote this hadith and say: O Allah, Your Prophet has told us that Your love and mercy for me are greater than the mercy of my own mother, and I know that my mother would never want to see me in pain and in suffering; so, O Allah, by Your mercy, remove my pain and my suffering. O Allah, no mother wants to see her child burn in the Fire. O Allah, by Your mercy, forgive my sins and draw me closer to Yourself.

So both words, AlRehman and AlRaheem, come from this word رحمۃ. Now let us look at these two words, AlRehman and AlRaheem. Let us first understand Rehman.

Al-Rehman

This particular attribute of AlRehman has certain characteristics that no other attribute has. These are interesting to note, because they highlight the importance of this attribute. The most prominent characteristic is that this is a name that applies only to Allah; it is not used for anyone other than Allah. You can call a human being Raheem: if a person is very loving and caring and shows mercy, you can call him Raheem. But you can never use the word Rehman for another human being. That belongs to Allah alone. In fact, this attribute is so important to Allah that He equates it with His اسم الجلالۃ, the name of His essence, Allah. He says:

قُلِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ أَوِ ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلرَّحْمَنَ ۖ أَيًّۭا مَّا تَدْعُوا۟ فَلَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
Allah says: Call upon Allah or call upon AlRehman; whichever name you choose, know that to Him belong all the beautiful names. So Allah quite literally said to call upon Allah or to call upon AlRehman; it does not matter, they are both the same. It is almost as though He highlighted the name AlRehman and made it complementary to the name Allah.

Another distinction that this name AlRehman has is that it is the only name of Allah for which Allah revealed an entire Surah to explain it. That is Surah AlRehman. Allah did not reveal a surah named AlMalik, AlQuddus, AlSalaam, AlAziz, or AlJabbar. No. But AlRehman is the only name of Allah that exists in the form of a surah. And every single ayah of Surah AlRehman is an explanation of the word Rehman.

He is ٱلرَّحْمَنُ. Why? عَلَّمَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ. Because He taught him the Quran.
He is ٱلرَّحْمَنُ. Why? خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَنَ. Because He created man.
He is ٱلرَّحْمَنُ. Why? عَلَّمَهُ ٱلْبَيَانَ. Because He taught him how to articulate.

And on and on and on. Every single ayah of Surah AlRehman is an explanation of why AlRehman is AlRehman. There is no other name that Allah chose to reveal an entire surah upon.

Another interesting fact is that the name Allah typically occurs all by itself in the Quran, because we know that all the other attributes of Allah are mentioned in pairs in the Quran. When you read the Quran, the attributes typically occur together in pairs: السمیع العلیم؛ الغفور الرحیم؛ العزیز الحیم. The names of Allah typically occur in pairs in the Quran.

but the name Allah itself rarely occurs with any other name. And so it is with the attribute al-Rahman: it never occurs with any other attribute, except al-Raheem. رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلرَّحْمَنِ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ وَٱلْمَلَٓئِكَةُ صَفًّۭا ۖ لَّا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَنُ قُلْ هُوَ ٱلرَّحْمَنُ آمَنَّا بِهِ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلرَّحْمَنِ مِن تَفَوُتٍۢ So al-Rahman always comes on its own, and when it is paired, it is paired always and only with al-Raheem, as in بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ عَلِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَدَةِ ۖ هُوَ ٱلرَّحْمَنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌۭ وَحِدٌۭ ۖ لَّآ إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلرَّحْمَنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ There are very profound reasons for this, but they lie beyond the scope of our sessions. God willing, when you study the inner truths you will understand why. These, however, are some of the most prominent traits of the word al-Rahman, and above all that it is used for Allah alone.

Al-Raheem is likewise one of the attributes most beloved to Allah, glory and majesty be His, and He has therefore given it only to those He loves. To no one did He give it more than He gave it to our beloved prophet Muhammad Mustafa, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Because Allah is al-Rahman, He has sent النبی الرحمۃ. وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةًۭ لِّلْعَلَمِينَ Because Allah is al-Rahman, He has chosen for us the best of human beings and sent to us the best of messages, and our prophet, blessings upon him, said انا نبی الرحمۃ, I am the prophet of رحمۃ.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
So you can see that Allah described Himself, identified Himself, with رحمۃ. He gave us a book that He called کتاب الرحمۃ. In that book, He imposed رحمۃ upon His own soul: كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ, I have written, I have imposed, I have made رحمۃ compulsory upon Myself. And then this loving and caring and merciful Master, this Rabb al-Alameen, gave us a prophet who is Rahmatul lil Alameen.

Linguistic meaning of al-Rahman

Now let us understand the meanings of these words linguistically. We will begin with al-Rahman. You now understand that both words mean love and care. But al-Rahman has three characteristics. I want you to remember three things about the word al-Rahman.

The first is that the love, care, concern, and mercy of Allah are extreme; they are beyond expectation. That is the first thing. What this means is that Allah is loving, but not merely loving. He is extremely loving, and His love is beyond all expectation. He is not merely caring. He is extremely caring. So whatever you expect from Allah in the way of love, care, concern, and mercy, know that it is beyond your expectation. That is the first meaning.

The second meaning of al-Rahman is that it is something that is happening immediately. You do not have to wait for it; it is happening right now. Let us think about this for a moment. In English, what is the difference between someone who is patient and someone who is being patient? Which one is showing patience right now? The one who is being patient. For example, if I say of my wife that she is a patient woman, I do not know whether she is going crazy with the children right now or not. Perhaps she is yelling at them; perhaps she is throwing them against the wall. I do not know that. She is generally a patient person, but I do not know whether she is patient at this very second. But when I say she is being patient, whom am I talking about, and when? Right now!

Do you see the difference? The love and care of al-Rehman is not something that unfolds in a general way. It is happening right now. In naming al-Rehman, we acknowledge that we do not have to wait for Allah to show us love. We do not have to wait for Him to care for us. We do not have to wait for Him to be concerned for us in the middle of a hardship. He is doing all of this right now. He loves every one of us right now. He cares for every one of us right now. He is genuinely concerned for every one of us right now, and He is being merciful to us right now. All of it is happening, in its most extreme form, right now. Do you understand?

So the first characteristic is that it is extreme. The second is that it is immediate. Now here is the third part of the meaning. This third part is a little hard to receive when you hear it for the first time; it feels wrong. The third characteristic of the word al-Rehman is that it is temporary. It is not permanent. I will explain why it is temporary. For now, understand that these are the three characteristics of the love and care of Allah in al-Rehman. It is intense. It is immediate. And it is temporary.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
These are, in fact, the characteristics of every other word that follows this phonetic pattern. Take any other word that rhymes with al-Rehman in Arabic — words such as عطشان، جوعان، غضبان — and they all share these same traits. Take غضبان, for example. It means extremely angry, and extremely angry right now, but that anger is temporary. A person who is extremely angry is not going to remain angry forever. He cannot; his head would burst and he would die. Even the Hulk calms down eventually. Likewise جوعان: extremely hungry, and hungry right now, like you wild teenagers, but temporary. You eat something and the hunger goes away. عتشان: extremely thirsty, thirsty right now, but the moment you have a drink you are no longer thirsty. So it is temporary.

So when we say al-Rehman, what are we saying? We are saying that Allah's love is extreme; it is beyond all expectation. It is coming right now. But it is not permanent. It can go away. Yet it does not simply go away on its own. That is what this pattern suggests. These states do not change by themselves. Thirst does not vanish on its own; you have to drink something. Hunger does not disappear by itself; you have to eat something. In the same way, Allah's care and love is present, and it is extreme. But if we do something gravely wrong, something truly terrible, if we make a ruinous mess of things, that state of رحمۃ can change. It can go away. Do you understand?

Linguistic meaning of Al-Raheem

Then there is the word al-Raheem. His love and care are manifested also through Raheem. There are two characteristics of Raheem that we need to know; it has two qualities. The first is that it is permanent. The second is that it is not necessarily happening right now. It is long-term. For example, if I say that my khala is loving toward me, that is a long-term quality, is it not? But does that mean she is being loving toward me right now? Not necessarily. I know she will always love me, but she may not be showing that love to me at this moment; and yet her love for me is always there.

There are other attributes of Allah that follow the same pattern as al-Raheem: Hakeem, Kareem, Jameel, Aleem.

And these too share the same two characteristics. Hakeem means wise, which means that He is always wise. Aleem means all-knowing, which means that He is always all-knowing. Jameel means beautiful, which means that He is permanently beautiful. So al-Raheem is a state that is not intense, but it is permanent.

al-Rehman before al-Raheem

Now the next question is this: why is al-Rehman first, and why is al-Raheem second? Please listen to this very carefully.

If Allah had said only al-Rehman, then His love, care, concern, and mercy would have been extreme. It would have been immediate, but it would not have been permanent. If Allah had said only al-Raheem, the love and mercy of Allah would have been permanent, but it would not have been extreme. So how do I speak about the love, care, concern, and mercy of Allah in such a way that it is extreme, and it is beyond expectations, and it is right now, and it is permanent, and it is long-term, all at the same time? The only way to do that is al-Rehman al-Raheem. SubhanAllah! You cannot speak about the qualities of the love and care of Allah in better terms than al-Rehman and al-Raheem.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
I will give you an example to understand this better. You are at work. Today is payday. Your boss is not at the office, and you have a flight booked to Timbuktu for seven o'clock in the evening, so you need to leave the office at exactly five o'clock, or you will not reach the airport. It is already 4:45, and you still have not received your paycheck. And you desperately need your paycheck, because you need the money for your trip. You were counting on this paycheck for the expenses of your trip. You are growing desperate. It is 4:50 now, and your boss is still not there. And your coworker says, "Do not worry. Our boss is reliable. He will be here. Relax."

Now it is 4:55, and you are utterly panicked. And your coworker is still telling you, "Do not worry. He is reliable. He will be here." Now what will you say to him at that point? No, do not say that; that is very rude. You will say, "Listen. I know he is reliable, but I need him to be reliable right now. Right this very minute. I need his quality of reliability right now!" Is that not the case?

When I am in trouble, when do I need Allah's help? Right now! So I need the name of Allah that gives me the help I need right now. That is al-Rehman. And then I want the other name, al-Raheem, which takes care of my future. Because when Allah says al-Raheem, it is permanent, is it not? Which is a guarantee for the future. But when Allah says al-Rehman, it is a guarantee for the present. So short-term love and care, and long-term love and care, are both covered by al-Rehman al-Raheem.

Another example. You teenagers will be able to relate to this. I come home, and I am really, really hungry. I did not have breakfast; there was too much work at the office; I did not get a chance to have lunch. So I come home, and I am starving. So I sit at the dining table, and Nazneen comes and asks me, "So, what do you want me to cook for next week?" I will say, "Woman! Who cares about next week? Give me something to eat right now!" When you are extremely hungry, the only thing you can think about is what? Right now. And when my right now is taken care of, once I have finished eating my dinner tonight, and I let out a burp — aah, AlHamdulillah! — then I will say, "So what are we eating next week?" When you pay this month's bill.

you begin to worry about next month's bills. When you have paid this semester's fee, you begin to worry about next semester's fees. Do you understand? So we think only about the future, once our immediate concerns are taken care of. So Allah says: I am al-Rahman. I am taking care of your immediate needs right now. But when my immediate concern is taken care of, where does my mind go? Into the future. So He says: I am al-Raheem too. Do not worry. I will take care of you in the future as well.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
Someone asked Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him — one of the great companions of the Prophet — about the difference between al-Rahman and al-Raheem. He said: Allah is Rahman in this life, and He is Raheem in the afterlife. This is because the love and care of Allah will be withdrawn from the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. Until that day, He is al-Rahman to both, the believers and the disbelievers — to all of us, to every human being. So He does not love and care only for you, and He does not love and care only for me. He loves and cares for every single being He has ever created: plants, animals, human beings. No matter what religion, color, or race they belong to. Muslim or non-Muslim. He even loves and cares for those who hate Him, who deny His existence. His doors of Rahmaniyat stand always open to everyone, in the hope that they will choose to turn back to Him. His invitation never expires, because Rahman is a universal quality. رحمتی وسعت علی کل شیء. My mercy extends to all. The rain comes down from the sky, and all human beings drink from it; they all draw their sustenance from it. The good person drinks. The wretched person drinks. The sinner drinks. The pious person drinks. The friend of Allah drinks. The enemy of Allah drinks. The scholar drinks. The ignorant person drinks. Everyone drinks. This is the universal mercy of this world.

But once the Day of Judgment comes, He is no longer Rahman to the disbelievers. On that day He is Qahhar. لِّمَنِ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْمَۖ لِلَّهِ ٱلْوَحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ Who does dominion belong to on this day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer. On the Day of Judgment there is no rahma for the disbelievers. There is only ghadab. There is only wrath. And that wrath is to exact justice. Allah's ghadab, His wrath, is not the same emotion that we feel. You see, our ghadab is directed toward hurting. When we fly into a rage, all we want is to hurt the other person, to offset some of the pain they have caused us. In fact, we want to hurt them even more if we can. But Allah's ghadab is not born of a desire to hurt the disbelievers or to cause them pain. It is not personal. It is to exact justice. And we will speak of this when we come to Malik Yaum al-Deen. But the point is this: on that day, His Rahmaniyat will be replaced with ghadab to establish justice against the disbelievers. Yet until the Day of Judgment He is Rahman, to the believers as well as the disbelievers. And then, for the believers, on the Day of Judgment He is Raheem. This is because this word carries the trait of permanence, and the akhira is a place of permanence.

So Rahman is general love, and al-Raheem is very specific love, because He decrees it specifically for those who have piety. This is the love, the care, and the mercy of the afterlife, which He has decreed for the believers alone. The mercy of eternal peace.

This is why you find in the Qur'an, in Surah Ya-Sin, سَلَٰمٌۭ قَوْلًۭا مِّن رَّبٍّۢ رَّحِيمٍۢ. You do not find سلام قولا من رب الرحمن. Allah says that in paradise Allah will turn to the believers and declare eternal peace for them—salam. This salam will come from a Lord who is Raheem: وَكَانَ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَحِيمًۭا, He is Raheem with the believers, not with the disbelievers.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
So Ibn Abbas said that Allah is al-Rahman in this world and He is al-Raheem in the next world, because this world is temporary and the next world is permanent. And I can truly appreciate the genius of this man, because he saw something. He saw that this world is temporary, and which mercy is temporary? Al-Rahman. And he saw that the next life is permanent, and which mercy is permanent? Al-Raheem. Subhan Allah! The companions saw it at once. We need hours to work these things out; it has to be explained to us. But they saw it the moment they heard it. Subhan Allah!

In any case, that is one interpretation of these two words. Another interpretation is that al-Rahman indicates that Allah is loving and caring by nature, and al-Raheem indicates that Allah is loving and caring in His actions. Rahman means that by His nature Allah is loving and caring. And Raheem means that in His actions Allah is loving and caring.

Al-Rahman is the one who gives when you ask Him, and al-Raheem is the one who is displeased when you do not ask Him. I will say it again. Al-Rahman is the one who gives when you ask. Muslim, disbeliever, believer, unbeliever—it does not matter. Al-Rahman will always give. But al-Raheem is the one who, if you do not ask, becomes displeased: Why did you not ask Me? This is that special kind of closeness that Allah has for the believers. It is like us with our closest friends. Your best friend needs something and turns to someone else. You are hurt. Why did you not ask me? I wanted to be there for you. This is a very intimate love that Allah, mighty and majestic, has for His believers. Subhan Allah!

The womb of a mother

So we have looked at how al-Rahman and al-Raheem both come from rahma, which means intense love, care, genuine concern, and mercy. Now let us look at where the word rahma comes from. Once you understand this, you will appreciate Allah as never before, God willing.

The word rahma comes from the word raham. The word raham in Arabic means the womb of a mother when she is carrying a child. The place where the baby lives inside the mother is called raham in Arabic.

A mother's womb is what describes the relationship between Allah and His creation. This is what makes it so beautiful. Both parents love their child, but in the Qur'an, when Allah compares His love for His creation, He never uses the example of a father; He always uses the example of a mother. So to truly understand the meaning of the word rahma, to understand the kind of relationship Allah has with us, we first have to understand the relationship of a mother with her child when she is carrying it in her womb.

There is a famous hadith in which Allah is speaking directly to the womb—and here the womb means the archetypal womb, because the womb of the mother is how humanity was spread. All of us came into being as a result of the wombs of our mothers. And Allah spoke to this creation, the womb, and He said: اِنِّی سَمَّیتُکَ بِاسْمیْ. I named you from My names. I am al-Rahman and al-Raheem, and I am naming you raham.

I am making you a symbol of My mercy, My unconditional love, because every human being will come through you, and you will remind them of My love for them. This is what Allah says to the womb.
body.topic_title_en: The Meanings of ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim

body.text_en:
The Prophet was with Ali, and he said to him: ستكون فتن كقطع الليل المظلم — there will be tribulations like portions of a dark night. Then he said: تُرَطِّقُ بعضُہُ بَعضَا — one tribulation will make the next look easy by comparison. And so Ali said: وما الخلاصُ یوم اذن یا رسول اللہ و ما مَخرجُ یوم اذن یا رسول اللہ — what is the deliverance on that day, and what is the way out on that day? The Prophet answered: the Book of God. فیہ نبأُ ما قبلکم و خبر ما بعدکم و الحکم ما بینکم. He said that the Book of God was the way out, and he said that in it is the news of those who went before you, and also the news of those who will come after you.

The sense in which it is news of the people who are to come after us is this: the customs, the sunan of God, do not change. Every story mentioned in the Qur'an is not there for historical purposes alone, but so that we may draw a lesson from it. It is there for عبرۃ. The Qur'an is not a history book. It contains history, yet its function is not to teach us history; its function is to teach us the customs of God, so that we can apply those customs to any situation in which we may find ourselves. Situations change only in their names, their places, and their people. In terms of conditions or circumstances — ahwaal — the states never change. They are always the same. Zulm is zulm in whatever language and in whatever country; oppression is oppression. Pharaoh is a historical figure, but he is also the archetypal embodiment of a pattern of behavior that is oppressive by its very nature. This is what the Qur'an is laying out.

So God gives us this book, and then He gives us a book within this book in the form of Surah al-Fatiha: سبع المثانی. Surah al-Fatiha is a summation of the entire Qur'an in seven verses, and it is one of the characteristics — the mojizaat — the disempowering element of the Qur'an, because the Qur'an is a book that has completely disempowered creation from producing anything like it. The majority of the people of eloquence, of balaagha, hold that the incapacitating nature of the Qur'an lies in this: that it is not within human capacity to produce the like of it, whether in its language or in its meanings, either one alone, and certainly not the two together.

I'll translate only the Urdu source given, following every rule.

--- ENGLISH RENDERING ---

We are studying the Basmallah. We have looked at the word Allah and His attributes in considerable depth. We have spoken of the heart as the center of all consciousness, which Allah gave us so that we might witness His attributes within His creation. And in the last session we spoke of Rehman and Raheem. We saw how the word comes from Rehma, which in turn comes from Reham, the womb of a mother. Now, assuming you were all awake during those sessions, today I want to speak about Akhlaaq, or character. But Akhlaaq is such a vast subject that it would take a great many sessions to cover all of its aspects. So what I thought is this: today I will simply try to explain what Akhlaaq means, and the science behind Akhlaaq, and then we can cover the rest in later sessions as matters arise, InshaAllah.

Seen versus Unseen — body versus soul

Today, when we look at any functioning thing, we find that it has two parts. There is the seen, which is the body or the exterior, and then there is the unseen, which is the energy that moves or animates that body. And this principle holds true for everything that "works," from a battery-operated toy car to massive construction machines, such as tractors and cranes. This is something we have come to recognize almost instinctively in this day and age. There is the object, and then there is the energy or force controlling the object. When your phone does not turn on, the first thing you check is whether it is charged, is it not? If the battery of your phone goes dead, no matter how expensive it may be, it becomes completely useless.

Your phone might have some truly excellent hardware. Let us say it has a twenty-megapixel camera, a microphone, a million-pixel resolution, a great deal of memory, and a great deal of storage space. So the phone's hardware is excellent, and that is all wonderful. But without the software, without the apps that control the hardware, that actually put the hardware of your phone to its proper use, your phone would be useless to you. You would not be able to draw any benefit from it, would you? And how would you know whether my phone has an app installed on it? By the functions of the hardware. Things are happening on the screen, the camera is working, the microphone is capturing and transmitting my voice, is it not? So the functions of the hardware prove the existence of the app that is controlling it.

And between the hardware and the software, between the object and the energy that uses and animates that object, between the seen and the unseen, it is always the unseen that holds real value. Both are important. Both the hardware and the software are important, but between the two, it is the software, and not the hardware, that takes the prize. Because the software is the master and the hardware is its slave. Its existence is simply to serve at the commands of the apps that use it.

Now, Allah too created us human beings with a hardware and a software. We have a body, which is the hardware, and we have a soul controlling the body, which is the software. And following the same logic as the phone, how do I know I have a soul? By the movement of my body. As the Arabs would say, حرکۃ الجسم دلیلُ المُحَرِّک. The movement of the body proves the existence of the one who moves it. So Allah created us with these two completely distinct, completely different entities.

Just as the hardware and the software are two completely different entities, the way in which the body develops is completely different from the way in which the soul develops. The two even come from different places. The body is created from the earth. وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًۭا — He raised you up from this earth like a plant. For, just as a plant grows over a period of time and through stages, so too the body grows from a child, to a toddler, to a teenager, to a mature adult. But the soul does not come from the earth. It is a subtle essence created by the command of Allah. وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِ ۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى — They ask you about the soul; tell them it is from the command of their Lord.

So the source of the body is the earth, and the source of the soul is the heavens. Then, in the fourth month of pregnancy, Allah joins the two together, and human life begins. As the child grows and matures, he begins working toward certain goals. He becomes a doctor, or an engineer, or a scientist, or a chief executive, or even the president of a country. These are all accomplishments and achievements of the soul while it is joined to the body.

But then a day comes when Allah separates the two. And as soon as that happens, all worldly titles, all accomplishments, all achievements, all relationships—everything comes to an end. The only title that remains is that of a "mayyat," a dead body, a corpse. When I die, and it is time for you to carry me to my grave, you will not say, "Let us take Asif Mamu to his grave." Even my own children will not say, "Let us pick up Babu." Do you know what you and everyone else will say? "Let us take the body." I have attended so many funerals in Karachi, and I never once heard anyone say چلو بابا کو اٹھاؤ. I have always heard them say چلو میت اٹھاؤ—let us take the body.

When King Faisal of Saudi Arabia died—I do not know whether you know this—in Saudi Arabia, after every Zuhr and Asr prayer, they hold the prayer for the deceased. It is called صلواۃ المیت. When Shah Faisal was alive and would go to visit a place, it would take fifteen minutes to announce his arrival. They would go on and on with his titles: Pride of Arabia, Glory of the Desert, the Wise, the Generous, and on and on—like Apollo Creed in Rocky 4. If you have not seen Rocky 4, then please pray two rak'ats of repentance after this session.

Never be that person. Do not cut off the bonds of blood. And you must do it for the sake of Allah, not for the sake of the person you are dealing with. A man once came to the Messenger of Allah and said: یا رسول اللہ. اَصِلُ اَخِیہِ. وَ یَقطَعُنِی. وَ اُعطِیہِ وَ یَمنَعُنِی. O Messenger of Allah, I give to him and he withholds from me. I come to him and he cuts me off. What should I do? The Prophet replied: that is Silatur Reham. What you are doing is the right thing. Continue doing it, even though he is cutting you off. That is Islam. This is Islam. And it is hard. Do not think this is an easy religion. But we want to be people who strive. We want to be people who honor ourselves, because Allah has honored us when He said: وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِىٓ آدَمَ وَحَمَلْنَهُمْ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ. We have ennobled the children of Adam. We have made you leaders over the land and the oceans. We gave you a heart. We gave you an intellect. We nourished them with our revelation. We give you the ability to overcome the worst aspect of yourself. And even if from time to time you capitulate, we have given you the means to renew and to restore the self, through tawba, through repentance. What a gift from Allah. So this is what we have to do, and we have to do it with Ikhlaas, with sincerity, only for the sake of Allah. But it is not easy. It is very hard to give up your akhlaaq in a moment of anger.

And this is truly a great litmus test for us: how we react to anger, how we react to desires and passions, how we react when things do not go our way. That is a true indication of where we stand on the scale of character. And our reaction will show us how much we actually do believe in the Quran. The next time someone mistreats you, speaks to you disrespectfully, observe how you handle that situation. That will tell you how well nourished your soul is. Truly.

Once Rasul Allah saw a man speaking to Maulana Ali in a very disrespectful manner. But in return, Maulana Ali responded with kindness. And despite this kindness, the man continued to act in a disrespectful, wretched manner with him. Yet Maulana Ali kept responding with kindness, over and over again. When the man left, Rasul Allah asked him: Ya Ali, I saw this man speak to you in such a disrespectful manner, treat you in a horrible way, over and over again. But you kept showing him kindness and respect. Why is that? And Maulana Ali replied: Ya Rasul Allah, if this man is not willing to give up his wretched and evil nature for me, why should I give up my good nature for him? SubhanAllah! What a beautiful statement. If this man is not going to give up his wretched manners, then why should I give up my good manners? Meaning, if he is going to continue to hold on to something ugly, why should I let go of something beautiful that I possess? That is the beauty of Akhlaaq.

That is the beauty of Islam. Rasul Allah was sent with the beauty of this light, the light of divine attributes. And with this light he purified the most barbaric group that ever existed. Read the history of Islam. Understand the mentality of the people he was sent to reform. They were worse than animals. There was not one virtue that existed in them. They were literally barbarians. They would eat the flesh of elephants and crocodiles.

When they ate a goat or a sheep, they would even boil the hide and eat it. They burned their enemies alive. They tore off their skin and wore it like a scarf. They cracked open the skull and drank wine from it. Their women dyed their clothes in the blood of their enemies. They did not merely kill the enemy; they tied that man's camel to his grave until it starved to death. Sons married their mothers. Daughters were buried alive. They used the children of their enemies for target practice. Even their prayers—even their prayers were barbaric.

یا ربِّ فَلا  تَجعَل حَیَاتی مَذِلَّۃُ ولا مَوتَتِی بَینَ النِّسآءِ نوائِحِ ولاکن قَتیلاً  تَمزَقُ الطَّیرِ حَولَہُ . و تَشرُبُ غِربانُ الدَّم من جوارح

O Lord, do not disgrace me in my life by letting me die in a bed among grieving women. Grant me instead a death in which birds tear at my flesh and crows drink the fresh blood gushing from my limbs.

This was the state of the Arabs when Rasul Allah came among them, and he transformed this nation—into people of whom, when we mention their names, we say Rehmatullah Alayhe, may the mercy of Allah be upon them. He transformed them into the Companions whom we hold up today as examples of generosity, kindness, and love. How did he do this? Through his akhlaaq, through his character. And this is why, on the day of Ghadeer, when Rasul Allah asked, الست اولاکم من انفسکم—Am I not more beloved to you than your own souls?—what did they reply? بلا یا رسول اللہ—Indeed you are, O Messenger of Allah. كنا الحيوانات. كنت جعلنا البشر—We were animals; you made us human beings. Do not underestimate the power of akhlaaq. This is what Rasul Allah was sent for. He himself said, انما بعثتُ لأُتمِّ مکارم الاخلاق—I was sent to perfect noble character. And innama, in classical Arabic, is taken to mean: the sole reason I was sent is to perfect noble character.

Two types of death

Because this is what we will take back with us. As Rasul Allah said in a hadith, at the moment of our death, angels descend. اخرِج اَنفُسِکُم الیوم—O soul, come out of this body now. And in the case of those who have not worked on the development of their souls, they say, رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِی. لَعَلِّی عَمَلاً صَالِحا—O Allah, let me remain a little while longer, so that I may do some good deeds. I promise that I will now live like a true believer. And then: اَیَّتُھَا النَّفسَ الخَبِیثَۃ کاَنَت فِی الَجسَدِ الخَبِیث—O you wretched soul, dwelling within a wretched body, اُخرُجِی—come out. And that soul feels the greatest fear it has ever known, because it can now see the ugly face of its own deeds. The angel of death says, اَبشرِیِ بِحَمِیمٍ وَ غَسَّاق. و آخِرَ مِن شَکلِہِ اَزوَاج—prepare yourself for painful torments, for boiling water and thorny bushes, and for many punishments of this kind. And then that soul is taken to the hellfire.

On the other hand, when a believer dies, as Allah says in the Qur'an, إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَقَمُوا۟ تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلَٓئِكَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُوا۟ وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا۟ وَأَبْشِرُوا۟ بِٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ—Indeed, those who have said, "Our master is Allah," and then remained on the right course—the angels descend upon them, saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."

نَحْنُ أَوْلِيَآؤُكُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِى ٱلْآخِرَةِ ۖ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِىٓ أَنفُسُكُمْ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ.

نُزُلًۭا مِّنْ غَفُورٍۢ رَّحِيمٍۢ

We were your friends in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and in Paradise you will have whatever your souls desire, and you will have whatever you ask for, as a gift from your master, who is most Forgiving and most Merciful.

These are the angels who descend from the heavens and say to this believer:

اَیَّتُھَا النَّفسَ الحَمِیدَۃ کاَنَت فِی الَجسَدِ الحَمِید. اُخرُجِی

O righteous soul, dwelling in a righteous body, come forth.

و اَبشِرِی بِرَوحٍ و رَیحَان. وَ رَبِّ رَاضِی عَنکِ غَیرَ غَضبَان

Receive this good news: Paradise is prepared for you, your master is pleased with you, and you will not face his anger.

The soul is then carried to the gates of Paradise, where the angels greet it and say:

مَرحَباً بہ

We all welcome you into Paradise. And then he enters Paradise.

But anyway, they would go on and on with his titles for ten minutes. Yet when he died and his body was brought into the mosque for prayer, everyone in the mosque was thinking that perhaps today, too, they would announce him by all his titles. But everyone was left in a state of complete shock when the imam said, ھذا صلواۃ المیت. That was it. The Pride of Arabia, the Glory of the Desert, and God knows what else—all of it reduced to a single word: mayyat.

For the wise, this is the true nature of this world. Why are you calling him that? What has changed about him? Only yesterday you were calling this man by a thousand titles. What has happened today? What has changed? He still has the same body, the same face, the same eyes, the same organs. He is still the same person he was yesterday. How has he suddenly lost all his value? He has lost all his value because something valuable, something essential,

no longer exists within this body: the soul. All the titles, all the ranks, the accomplishments — these are what the soul earns, not the body. The body was merely a facilitator, an obedient servant working on behalf of the soul. And as we know, once a master disowns his slave, that slave holds absolutely no value in the market. No one will buy him again, because his own master has cast him off. In the same way, once the soul departs from the body, the body is reduced to nothing more than an empty, useless vessel. Even if it remains in excellent condition — beautiful eyes, fine features, sound and healthy organs — all of that becomes wholly worthless without the soul.

So this is the true nature of our existence. These two companions come together, one from the earth and the other from the heavens. They labor together to accomplish a certain purpose for as long as they remain joined, and whether they succeed or not, at the appointed time they both depart, and each returns to its origin. کل شئی یرجع الی اصلہ. Everything returns to its origin. The body goes back into the earth from which it came, and the soul returns to the heavens from which it came. This is the process.

The Soul Has Needs Like the Body

But what I wish to speak with you about today is that brief span of time when these two companions are together. The first point is that both of them have needs, and both draw those needs from their original source. This body is created from the earth, and so all its needs come from the earth as well. Its needs are food, air, clothing, and shelter, and precious metals such as gold and silver — that is, money — all of which are produce of this earth. When the needs of the body are not met, it grows sick and weak. But when all its needs are properly satisfied, in a balanced measure, the body grows strong, healthy, vibrant, and beautiful.

Just as the body has its needs, the soul too has needs, and those needs come from its own original source, which is the heavens, the spiritual world. And that source is revelation.

So the body and the soul are two separate beings with entirely separate needs, and neither can be nourished by what sustains the other. These earthly things cannot satisfy the needs of the soul, because the soul was not created from the earth. It can be distracted for a while by these pleasures — certainly, and this happens all the time — but such pleasures cannot hold its interest permanently. In the end the soul loses interest; it grows bored; it grows weary of whatever thing or relationship it had attached itself to. We see this constantly. When a new game is released, we are entirely absorbed in it. Once we have played it for a while, we need the next one. When your phone first appeared, it was the most incredible thing imaginable. You spent half the day polishing it to perfection. Someone asks, "Do you like your phone?" and you answer, "I love it — it is absolutely wonderful." Six months later, when the next version comes out, someone asks again, "Do you like your phone?" and you answer with a shrug, "It is all right. It is not the newest model, not the latest edition, but it is fine." What happened? Only six months ago it was the most incredible thing. What has changed today? This is simply the nature of this world, and of everything that comes from it. Interest rises, reaches its peak,

and then its decline begins. Now you need the next new thing. Look at anything in your life; this holds true for everything of this world. It is temporary. It is a phase. It passes. And this is because these pleasures have to do with the body, which is also temporary, which comes from this earth, which is also temporary. And so any and every attachment the soul forms, with anything or anyone in the worldly sense, will always be temporary.

But the soul is different. It is eternal. And that is why it needs an attachment that is eternal. That attachment is Allah, because Allah is eternal. And just as the body needs nourishment to grow and develop, so too does the soul, and that nourishment is revelation. Revelation is the nourishment of the soul, just as food is the nourishment of the body. The body grows in strength with physical nourishment; the soul grows in character with spiritual nourishment. It grows in what is called Akhlaaq. The perfection of the body is measured by its strength, and the perfection of the soul is measured by its Akhlaaq, its character.

Now, what is Akhlaaq? The word Akhlaaq comes from the word Khulq. And this is truly interesting, because we are called Khalq. Khalq means creation, which is related to the body, and Khulq means character, which is related to the soul. They are both made up of the same letters, in the same sequence. And I have shown you how there is this science in Arabic: when two words share the same letters in the same sequence, they are identical in meaning; and when they share the same letters in a different sequence, they are connected in meaning. For example, we looked at the words Ilm and Amal, knowledge and action. They both have the same letters, but in a different sequence, and that is why they are connected in meaning, because knowledge produces action, or action is based on knowledge. And then we saw Qalb and Qabl, heart and precedence, and qibla, direction, and they are all connected in meaning because they share the same letters in a different sequence.

But when the letters and the sequence are the same, they both represent identical things. For example, there is Ilm, which means knowledge, and then there is عَلَم, which means flag. And what a flag does is identify and honor a country, and what knowledge does is identify and honor a scholar. So they are both identical in meaning, because they both share the same letters in the same sequence. This is why Arabic is so beautiful: because it is extremely precise, and it is perfect in its form and construction. SubhanAllah!

And so now we have Khalq, and we have Khulq, because Khalq is the body, nourished by this physical world, and Khulq is character, which is a nourishment from the spiritual world. Khalq represents the existence of the body, and Khulq represents the existence of the soul. And they both begin with Kha, which, as I explained to you, is a sound of friction. It is a sound of effort, because the body takes effort to develop, and so does character. Character takes a great deal of effort to develop. So if Khalq is the essence of the body, then Khulq

or character is the essence of the soul. When we die, the fully developed body, or as much of it as has developed, returns back into the earth, and the soul, with its fully developed character, or however much of it has developed, returns back to its master. What the soul returns with is what it has acquired and developed in terms of its nature. That is the true earning, the real acquisition of the soul. A soul that returns to its master without a developed Khulq is an impoverished soul. When the body is weak, it cannot benefit from the offerings of this world. This world has a great deal to offer in the way of temporal pleasures, but if you are so weak that you cannot even get up off the bed, you will not be able to enjoy those pleasures. In the same way, a soul that is devoid of, that is bankrupt of Akhlaaq, will not be able to benefit from the pleasures of the afterlife. That is why it is extremely important that we develop our character, or we will find ourselves in the midst of all these heavenly pleasures and be unable to draw any benefit from them. So now, what is character, and how do we develop it?

Character is developed with revelation. Consider revelation. The Qur'an, in a sense, is nothing more than the explanation of the divine attributes of Allah. If I may oversimplify, that is all the Qur'an is doing: it is stating the attributes of Allah and explaining why He has those attributes. He is Azeem, because He created this vast universe. He is Qawee, All-Powerful, because not only did He create this universe, He created it with a single command: KUN, Be, and FAYAKOON, and it was. So in essence the Qur'an is simply the description of Allah's attributes, explaining why He is THE ILAH, why He is Allah. And then, as Allah, as our master, what are His rights over us? The favors He has done for us, the favors He has given us right now, the favors He has in store for us later. What will happen if we obey Him, what will happen if we disobey Him. All of that relates back to His divine attributes, does it not? So that is all revelation is.

So here is the sequence of events. Allah created this universe and placed His divine attributes within all of His creation. He created us with a body and a soul, and He gave us a heart. For it is the heart that can witness these divine attributes of Allah through His revelation. It is the heart that sees the UNSEEN working behind the SEEN, and reaches the conclusion that I must have a master, and testifies لا الہ الا اللہ, there is no god except Allah. It is the heart that does all this. So the universe reflects the attributes of Allah outside of us, and a heart inside of us can witness the divine attributes in the light of revelation, which then creates BELIEF. The more the heart understands the revelation, the stronger the belief becomes, and the stronger the belief becomes, the more the soul grows in character. And so character is nothing more than absorbing these divine attributes into the heart through revelation, and then reflecting those same divine attributes into the rest of Allah's creation. That is all character is. It is internalizing, developing, and training the heart in the light of these divine attributes, and then reflecting them in our interactions with Allah's creation. That is Akhlaaq. And that is Islam. That is what Islam is. In its simplest form, Islam is all about interactions. It is معاملات.

There are three kinds of interaction in Islam: interaction with Allah, interaction with the self, and interaction with the creation of Allah. This is because Allah, as our master, holds certain rights; our soul holds certain rights; and the people around us hold certain rights. Huqooq Allah. Huqooq al-Nafs. And Huqooq al-Ibaad. Those are the three rights: one toward Allah, which is Huqooq Allah, and two toward his creation, Huqooq al-Nafs and Huqooq al-Ibaad. And even though these last two are placed in separate categories, they are all in truth a part of the rights of Allah. Because the self and others are all the creation of Allah, fulfilling the rights of the self and fulfilling the rights of others is in fact part of fulfilling the rights of Allah. Now let us look at each of these on its own.

Huqooq Allah

The first is Huqooq Allah, the right of Allah. How do we arrive at it? By observing the divine attributes of Allah, Subhanhu wa Ta'ala, in his creation all around us. For everything he created is a symbol of his love, and the purpose of a symbol is to point to that which it symbolizes. He made the relationship of our body and soul the perfect example of this, because the seen points to the unseen. The movement of my body points to the existence of an energy that moves it. And the master-and-slave relationship that exists between the soul and the body symbolizes the kind of relationship I am meant to have with my master. I should be in obedience to my master, just as my body is in obedience to my soul. All of this is the recognition of the unseen by means of the seen, and then gratitude for both. For if I cannot be grateful for the seen, how am I ever to be grateful for the unseen? I must therefore recognize the force working behind the blessings in my life through the symbols created for me in the seen world. Do you understand? And only when I do this, only when I recognize the divine attributes of Allah made manifest in all of his creation, within myself and within those around me, can I then recognize and accept Allah as my master.

For example, I see the sun and the moon, two magnificent creations of Allah, governing the day and the night for my benefit. If there were no day, I would not be able to survive. If there were no night, I would not be able to survive. And so both of these are a blessing for me. And who is giving me these blessings? In the seen sense, it is the sun and the moon. But these two heavenly bodies are not autonomous; they are not self-governing. The sun does not simply come out when it pleases. The moon is not full whenever it feels like it.

لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنۢبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ وَلَا ٱلَّيْلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِ ۚ وَكُلٌّۭ فِى فَلَكٍۢ يَسْبَحُونَ

It is not permissible for the sun to reach the moon, and the night cannot overtake the day. They are both floating in their own orbits. These are both gigantic bodies. The earth is nothing compared to them. And yet I see that they have been made subservient. For all their mass and immensity, these planets are not doing whatever they wish. I see that they have been bound by the forces of gravity. They have been assigned certain responsibilities, and they are fulfilling them without question, without argument, without resistance.

Who bound them?

لَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيْلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِى ٱلَّيْلِ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ

كُلٌّۭ يَجْرِىٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running its course for a specified term? فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ وَجَعَلَ ٱلَّيْلَ سَكَنًۭا. وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ حُسْبَانًۭا He is the cleaver of daybreak, and He has made the night for rest, and He created the sun and the moon for the reckoning of time.

So when I witness these gigantic, these extremely powerful heavenly bodies in complete submission and servitude to the forces with which Allah has bound them, it makes me think: how powerful Allah must be. How Jaleel. How Azeem. How Qawee Allah must be. And then I see that these powerful, gigantic planets are constantly engaged in Allah's worship and obedience, and that makes me think: what am I, in strength and might, compared to them? They are Allah's creation, and I am Allah's creation. And if they are in a state of submission to their powerful master, despite their majesty and glory and enormity, then should I not be in a state of worship and obedience to that same powerful master? This realization forces me to submit to Allah in worship and obedience. And that is where the rights of Allah come into play. Huqooq Allah. That is where all forms of worship come in: wilayah, taharah, salaah, zakaat, saum, hajj, and Jehad. These are all Huqooq Allah, the right of my powerful, yet extremely Rehman, Raheem, Kareem master over me.

Huqooq an-Nafs

Then the next thing is Huqooq an-Nafs. I mean, this is something even the non-believers have come to see, with all these talks about human rights. But this is what the Quran teaches us: that my soul has a right, my body has a right, that they be properly nourished. The nourishment of the body is food, which comes from the harvest of this earth. And the nourishment of the soul is Akhlaaq, which comes from the harvest of the divine attributes. So the next thing is that I recognize and understand the divine attributes of Allah, and train my heart in the light of these attributes to develop my character. He is Kareem. He is generous. So I need to be generous with my self. And the greatest generosity that I can show my self is to protect it from sins, and to put it to work in good deeds. I make it do what it was created to do, and that is to work for the pleasure of my master.

Allah is AlHaqq. He is the truthful. So I must now train my self in becoming truthful. Truthful with whom? Truthful with myself. I need to stop deluding myself with the attractions of this temporal world. I need to wake up to the reality that I am only here for a short period of time. Everything that I am working for in the worldly sense will be left behind. I will be left with nothing other than the title of a Mayyat in this world when I die. My loved ones, the people that I am slaving for day and night, they will be the first to put me in a grave and throw dirt in my face. That means being ready to be unplugged from the matrix. (Again, if you have not seen The Matrix, you know what to do after the session.) But this is not easy. Waking up from deep sleep is never easy. What I tell you in these sessions, if it is difficult for us to hear.

makes us uncomfortable, then it is actually working. Because we do not like it when someone tries to wake us from a deep sleep. ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ أَفْوَهِهِمْ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَتَشْهَدُ أَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ

On that Day, We will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they have earned.

We truly need to wake up to the harsh reality of Huqooq AlNafs, the rights of our soul. Because our souls are dead. Our hearts are dead.

يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا۟ ٱسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ

وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ وَأَنَّهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ

When will we answer his call? When will we respond to the call of Allah and His Messenger, something that will bring us back to life?
