So you ask, "How can this be? If he is such an amazing teacher, how is it that so many students fail every year?" Right?

Well, the question is this: is the failure because of the teacher, or is it because of the students? It could not be the teacher, because there are many, many students each year who do graduate the class, and they are full of praise for what a wonderful teacher he is. So the problem may not be the teacher; it must be the students. And any teacher among us can appreciate this.

The fourth meaning of the word Rabb is Murshad — the one who sets a thing in the right direction, who places it on the right path, who puts it to proper use. That is Murshad. Murshad comes from the word رُشد, which in classical Arabic means to ripen, which is the final stage for a fruit. That is why rushd also means rationality, or reason, or maturity, because those are the final stages of the intellect.

So a Murshad is someone who takes something raw and works upon it until it ripens, until it matures, and then puts it to its proper use. He sets it in the right direction. Suppose you have a teacher who trains you in computer science and then also finds you a job, so that you can now apply what you have learned. That would be a Murshad. A Murshad is not someone who merely trains you to maturity and then leaves you to rot. He actually places you on the path; he guides you forward from your point of maturity, so that you and others may benefit from what you have acquired.

So Allah, as Rabb, is not only the one who owns us, who holds complete authority over us, who nurtures us with love and care. He also creates opportunities for us, so that we can put our training to good use. He will train you by placing people in your path who will help you develop. He will find the perfect friend for you, one who will help you grow, until you mature.

and then he will also put that training to use for you. Even parents and teachers cannot always do that. They complete the upbringing of their children, but they cannot always set them to a proper use afterward. The children have to find their own way. But Allah as Rabb goes further, and sets us on the right path after our training is complete. Subhan Allah.

Now, the next meaning of the word Rabb is Munim. The Munim is the one who gives gifts, who bestows blessings. The word مُنعِم comes from نِعَم, or نعمۃ, which means gifts, or blessings. We do not have slavery today, but imagine for a moment that we own a slave. In fact, just think of your boss, because he owns a slave. So it is one thing to own a slave, to take care of it, to put it to proper use — but now, on top of all of that, to also give it gifts. And the word نعمۃ suggests gifts and benefits that come on top of what one deserves. Gifts are not deserved things. Gifts, by definition, are always beyond what is deserved.

Imagine that you own — I do not know — a goat. You own a goat, and so you take care of it. But you do not buy it gifts. You do not buy it jewelry, right? I hope you do not buy it jewelry. You do not need to. It is a goat! It is part of the property. So in the old days, slaves were no different from a goat or an animal. They were barely taken care of, let alone given gifts.

Interestingly, the Arabic word نَعَم, which means yes, also comes from the same root word as blessing. Why? Because what is the natural human response to the question, "Would you like a gift? Would you like a blessing?" It is نَعَم. Yes! This is what I love about this language.

But Allah as Rabb is an owner who not only takes good care of his property, who has complete authority over it, who ensures its growth to maturity, who looks after it, protects it, sustains it, and sets it on the right path. On top of all of that, He also gives it numerous gifts. Think about that for a moment. He owes us nothing. Therefore, anything and everything He gives us has to be a gift. It is not something He is obligated to give us at all. I did nothing to deserve my eyes. I did not pay for my hand. How much would you charge if I asked you to sell both your eyes to me? Forget both eyes — how much would you sell me one eye for? How much would you sell both your hands for? How much is your ability to walk worth to you? How much would you charge for your heart? We cannot, because these are priceless gifts. And He will question us on the Day of Judgment about these gifts.

ثُمَّ لَتُسْـَٔلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ

On that day you will be asked about the greatest of all gifts, which is Eman. Naeem means the greatest gift of all. What is that gift? It is the gift for which all these other gifts have been given to us, and that is Eman. That is the ultimate gift. Eman. On the Day of Judgment He will ask about this Naeem, the greatest blessing of all. Otherwise, what was the purpose of giving us these gifts? So that we could see the creations, reflect upon them, and draw closer to Him.

That is why the Rabb is منعم. He gives نعمۃ, so that we can say نَعَم to the نعیم. We can affirm the ultimate blessing of faith. Oh, there is a nice tongue twister there.

So now we understand that Allah as Rabb is someone who not only owns us, who has authority over us,

not only does He nurture us, with love and kindness, and patience. Not only does He bring us to maturity and set us on His chosen path. He also showers us with tons and tons of undeserved gifts.

The final meaning is that of al-Qayyim. The Rabb is also Qayyim. The Qayyim is the one who makes sure that things hold together, that they do not fall apart. Because when you do not take care of things, what happens to them? They fall apart. In gardening, sometimes you have very, very delicate plants; if you fail to care for them even for a single day, they die. Some people keep fish as pets; do not feed the fish for one day, and you have Nemo kebab for dinner. That is horrible.

So Qayyim, the sustainer, the maintainer, is also embedded in the word Rabb. That is why the Qur'an says, اللہ لا الہ ھو الحی القیوم. Qayyum is the constant sustainer, the constant maintainer. I am not alive because I take care of myself, from one breath to the next. It is not because I eat well, exercise, and follow a good diet. It is not because I live in a healthy environment. That is not why I am alive. I am alive because He allows me to be alive. It is not because of my efforts. There are countless ways I could cease to exist in a second: simply crossing the road, one small earthquake, one snowstorm. A man in my office lost his wife while she was picking up their children from school; a clot in the brain, and that was it. A perfectly healthy woman, a fitness trainer by profession, with no history of anything. She picked up her children, reached the car, and was reaching out for the door, and she dropped dead. She probably had many plans for that evening, just as I do. I am sure she had many short-term goals and long-term goals. All gone, in a second. We exist because the Qayyim is letting us exist. We are completely and constantly dependent on Allah.

There is another thing in this verse. We see two attributes mentioned: al-Hayy and al-Qayyum, the Ever-Living and the constant maintainer. Now, why are these two attributes placed together? They are together because the One who gives life knows how to sustain it, how long to sustain it, what stages and steps to carry it through, how to end it, when to end it, and what happens after it ends. The entire plan of action for each individual creation, not just human beings but all creation, is already and completely laid out.

That is part of the meaning of Qayyim: to have a plan. You cannot begin something or maintain something without a plan, can you? When you decide to start a business, you do not choose which business to pursue by rock, paper, scissors. You must have an entire business plan, do you not? What your initial investment will be, how you will grow the business, cost and expense analysis, budget allocations; you plan the whole nine yards. And all of this comes before you have even begun the business. Do you think Allah simply created us without a plan? That is not possible, is it?

So now let us look at the complete definition of the word Rabb. الرب ھو المالک والسَّیِّد و المُرَبِّی والمُرشِد وَالمُنعِم والقَیِّم. Rabb is someone who is Maalik, who has absolute ownership. At the same time He is Sayyed, who has complete and unconditional authority. At the same time He is Murabbee, who ensures growth, who takes care, who nurtures and protects, with love, care, concern, and mercy. At the same time He is Murshad, who brings us to physical and spiritual maturity and then sets us on His straight path, who puts us to proper use. At the same time He is Munim.

who showers us with undeserved and countless gifts and blessings. And at the same time He is Qayyim, who sustains us for the whole span of our existence. Allah, as our Rabb, is ALL of these things. ALL at the same time. This is something you must ALWAYS understand. Rabb is not ONE of these things at different points in your life. He is ALL of these things. ALL at the same time. His ownership contains His authority, which contains His nurture, which contains His guidance, which contains His blessings, which contains His sustenance. ALL at the same time. SubhanAllah.

This is why that person of sound essence, the one from among the UlilAlbaab, called his Creator Rabb. Because when he reflected on the creation of the heavens and the earth, this is what he saw. He saw an absolute owner, who also holds complete authority, who nurtures and develops His creation with love and care and mercy, who sets everything to its purpose, who bestows upon every creature its gifts and blessings, and who sustains them through time, without pause. This is why he said, رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَطِلًۭا. OUR RABB. You did not create all of this without a purpose. And this is an EXTREMELY beautiful conclusion, because Allah matched that conclusion in His revelation.

What is the VERY first ayah that was revealed to Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam)? ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ‎. Read with the name of your RABB who created you. Not ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ اللہِ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ‎. Now here is God introducing Himself to His Messenger for the very first time, is it not? And when you introduce yourself, how do you do it? With your name or with an attribute? If I met you for the very first time and I said, AsSalaamAlaykum, I'm the Sunday session teacher, you would be like, WalaykumAsSalaam. You're also a weirdo, right? Because that is not normal. When you introduce yourself, you use your name.

So I would imagine Allah should have said, ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ اللہِ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ‎. Read with the name of ALLAH who created you, is it not? Huh! Instead He says, Read in the name of your RABB who created you. Allah chose to introduce Himself as RABB. What does this tell you?

Plan of Shaytan

We began with the استعاذہ, which is seeking Allah's protection from the accursed Shaytan. What we learned in our study of the Istiaza, and of Surah AlFalaq and Surah AlNaas, is that Allah is identifying for us, or rather pointing out to us, our worst enemy: Iblees, and all of his followers, who are the Shayateen. What Allah does is disclose for us ALL of Shaytan's plans. He tells us about his short term goals, his long term goals, how he sets his traps for us, and how he, very patiently, places us on the path of destruction. For he has one single goal. All his whisperings have one single agenda: to get human beings to take off their clothes.

فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَنُ لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَتِهِمَا

Shaytan whispered to them, to expose what was covered of their ugliness, their private parts. Allah honored and dignified Adam AS and his children with clothing. Why? To raise them ABOVE the animals, because animals have no care for clothing. There is no reason to honor and dignify animals, because they are base creatures. But Allah gave Adam AS and his children the intellect, made them His representative on earth, and therefore honored them with clothing. And Shaytan wants to bring humanity to remove their clothing. He wants them to strip off that honor and degrade and humiliate themselves down to that base level of the animals. And what is the ULTIMATE humiliation?

رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُۥ

Oh master! No doubt, the one you entered into the hell fire has been truly humiliated.

So this is what he wants. But he does it in such a subtle way. He does not simply tell us to do the wrong thing. He makes the wrong thing beautiful to us, and then we do it ourselves. And we see the evidence of that all around us today. People are so happy to take off their clothes, to show some skin, as they say.

لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَتِهِمَا

to expose to them what was covered of their ugliness. The human being, the intellectual being, Khaleefatul Allah, Allah's representative on this earth, the one He created to manifest His divine attributes on this earth, reduced to the level of an animal. This is what Shaytan is doing. This is what he has already done. Look at us today. Not only do we do this today, we are damn proud of it too. We talk about it. We announce it. We post it on facebook. We make fun of those who do NOT do it, and call them backward, and cavemen, and what not.

It is really amazing if you think about it. How Shaytan has changed our idea of what is beautiful. One step at a time, without our even realizing it. Making it seem entirely logical. Oh, I have freedom. Freedom to express my sexuality. Why did Allah make me beautiful if He did not want me to show it off? Some of the reasons I hear simply amaze me. SubhanAllah! You do not even use your phones without a cover. Because they will get scratched. Because they will become ugly. It is so beautiful, I need to protect its beauty. But when it comes to your own beauty, the beauty that is a manifestation of the divine essence, AlJameel.

The Most Beautiful. He gave you something from His own divine names, and you are throwing that name about in front of the whole world. You value your phone more than you value a divine name of Allah. Astaghfirullah! What amazing logic! But this is what Shaytan does, because he is a trickster. He will produce the most perfect logic. He will convince you, and prove to you, that fire is better than clay. Logic is his craft.

Shaytan is a liar

Junaid Baghdadi relates that he once had a dream in which he met Iblees, and in that dream he held a conversation with him. He asked Iblees, "Why would you not prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him? Why would you disobey Allah? How could you be so foolish as to refuse and stand against Allah when He gave you a command? What is wrong with you?" And Iblees replied, "O Junaid, how could I prostrate to anyone other than Allah?" Junaid was completely thrown off. He was astonished. That answer struck him as profound. He fell into a state of utter confusion, because what Iblees had just said to him now made perfect sense. But you see, this is what Iblees does. He is a trickster. He presents perfect logic.

So Junaid went to the Imam, peace be upon him, and told him about his dream. The Imam, peace be upon him, said, الابلیس ھو الکذاب — Iblees is a liar. That could not have been his reason for refusing the command of Allah. For what he says, that he could not bow down to anyone other than Allah, belongs to adab. It belongs to the etiquettes. But الامر فوق الادب — the command of Allah is greater than all etiquettes. If you are the president of your school, or a teacher of your class, and the school principal tells you to do something, such as reprimand a student for something he has done, that may not be the finest etiquette. It may not be a pleasant thing to do. But you have to do it, because the command came from someone who is superior in rank. So even though I would not prostrate to anyone other than Allah, if it is Allah Himself commanding me to prostrate, I have to do it. I will not prostrate if you tell me to do so. But if Allah Himself issues a direct command, I have to obey, because الامر فوق الادب — command trumps etiquettes. This is what Iblees does. He tricks and confuses through logic.

Speech of Shaytan

And so, through these Quranic stories, Allah informs us how Shaytan completely destroyed the people before us, how he deceived them, and how he humiliated them into the hellfire by pretending to be their best friend. Yes? So by telling us about our past, Allah warns us about our present in order to protect our future. Look! He did this to the people before you, and this is where they ended up. And now he is doing exactly the same thing to you. Be careful. Do not take him for your friend.

But Allah does not stop there. He goes further still and tells us what is going to happen in the future, on the Day of Judgment. He says that Iblees will stand before his followers on the Day of Judgment and deliver a speech.

وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيْطَنُ لَمَّا قُضِىَ ٱلْأَمْرُ — when the affair is over.

فَرِيقٌۭ فِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيقٌۭ فِى ٱلسَّعِيرِ — a group has been sent to hell.

and a group has been sent to paradise. That is when Iblees says: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمْ وَعْدَ ٱلْحَقِّ وَوَعَدتُّكُمْ فَأَخْلَفْتُكُمْ — Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you a false promise. This is what he says in hell. He delivers a sermon; he gives a khutba in hell. All the members of hell are present there to listen to this sermon, and this is what he says to them: Allah promised you the truth. Everything that was in the Quran was the truth. Everything that was in the Torah was true. Everything that was in the Gospel was true. All those prophets spoke the truth. He gathers all of them — that harvest of humanity, the whole lot that disobeyed Allah. He gathers all of them, and this is what he says: Allah promised you and I promised you. You believed me and you did not believe Allah. I betrayed you.

Then he says: وَمَا كَانَ لِىَ عَلَيْكُم مِّن سُلْطَنٍ — I had no authority over you. إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَٱسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِى — the only thing I could do was invite you to sin, and you responded. I invited you to be miserly. I frightened you. I said: what is going to happen to your children if you do not collect all this money? What is going to happen to your children if you do not build these big houses for them? I frightened you with poverty. Put aside, put aside. قِرش أَبیَد بِیَومَ الاسْوَد, as the Arabs say — a white penny for a black day. Put aside, put aside. That is Shaytan. I brought forth temptations and desires for you. فَلَا تَلُومُونِى وَلُومُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُم — so do not blame me, blame yourselves. مَّآ أَنَا۠ بِمُصْرِخِكُمْ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُصْرِخِىَّ — I cannot save you now, and you cannot save me. That is what Shaytan says to everybody.

And on that day Allah says to this group, this harvest of the fire of hell, Allah says: أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ يَبَنِىٓ آدَمَ أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوا۟ ٱلشَّيْطَنَ ۖ — Did I not make you promise, O children of Adam, that you would not become slaves of Shaytan? إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّۭ مُّبِينٌۭ — I told you: without a doubt, he is your worst enemy. وَأَنِ ٱعْبُدُونِى ۚ هَذَا صِرَطٌۭ مُّسْتَقِيمٌۭ — Be my slave instead; worship me instead of him. This is the straight path.

Allah identified our enemy for us. So Allah revealed to us everything we need to know about Shaytan: the past, the present, and the future. Now, when I read about this, it makes me think. Who does that? Who would point out for me who my enemy is, where he is hiding, how he plans to attack me, and why I should not listen to him, and then collect and present all the evidence against him, and show me how he has already hurt so many others who believed him? Who would do that for me? That sounds like a friend to me. A friend who loves me, who cares about me, someone who is genuinely concerned for my well-being. But then, do you know what is more amazing? He did not simply point out all of this and then leave me by myself, did he?

Think about your best friend in school. Let us say he finds out that someone is going to hurt you; let us say that person is planning to ambush you after class. So your friend tells you.

"Listen — this fellow is going to come to you after class. He will speak sweetly and talk you into walking with him down one particular path. But I overheard him talking with his friends. Two of them will be hiding behind the fourth tree on the left side of that path, and the moment you walk past that tree they will jump on you, beat you badly, and steal your things. So no matter what he says to you, do not listen to him."

In short, your friend tells you everything about the person who is planning to hurt you. Now, doing even that much for you is enough to mark him as a true friend, is it not? That alone would convince you that he truly loves you and cares about you. But then he adds, "Do you know what? I know you cannot resist ice cream. The moment he tells you there is an ice cream truck down that path, and that they have chocolate, I know that as soon as you hear it you will forget everything I have just said, and you will say, 'Ahh, lead the way!' So here is what I will do. If you wish, I will walk with you. I will stop you from taking that path at the very moment he tempts you. And if you still choose to walk down it, I will try to protect you when those two try to jump on you. I will not let them hurt you. But you must keep choosing, at every moment, to stay behind me. I promise I will not let them harm you in any way."

If your friend does all of that, what sort of friend is he then?

Allah did not merely inform us of Satan's schemes and then leave us to deal with them on our own. He knew that we are facing an enemy we cannot see, and that we stand at a clear disadvantage against him. So what did He do? He offered us His own protection. He said: Do not be anxious. I will protect you. If you choose to submit to My protection, I will protect you from Satan.

So now, if I have even half a mind, after knowing all of this, after realizing that I will not be able to fight Satan by myself — because he is an extremely powerful and ruthless enemy, and on top of that I cannot even see him or hear him when he is whispering to me — then I need the protection of the One who can see him and who can hear him, the One who is strong enough to stop him at the very moment he attacks me. If I possess at least that much sense, I willingly submit myself to Allah and I say: اعوذ باللہ من الشیطان الرجیم. O Allah, I seek Your refuge against the accursed Satan, because You alone can protect me from him.

So even before we begin our spiritual journey, if we wish to have any chance at all of actually completing it, we must first accept and submit ourselves to Allah's protection. It is like this: before you begin any serious training program, professional trainers tell you that you should first see a physician. Why? Because if you have some physical condition you are unaware of, something you cannot see, you want it attended to before you begin your exercise. Otherwise you will not be able to gain any benefit from the exercise itself. Is that not so?

That is precisely what we are doing with the Isti'adha. We are entering into Allah's protection.

We do this so that Shaytan does not interfere with our spiritual journey, the journey that begins with the first ayah of Surah al-Fatiha. Tie the camel first in order to protect it. This is truly important to understand. We will gain nothing from the Fatiha if we do not meet the requirements of the Isti'adha.

A man came to the mosque for prayer, and he had his camel with him. He met the Messenger of Allah outside the mosque and asked him: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ, أَعْقِلُهَا وَأَتَوَكَّلُ, أَوْ أُطْلِقُهَا وَأَتَوَكَّلُ — "O Messenger of Allah, should I tie my camel first and then trust in Allah, or should I leave it untied and then trust in Allah?" The Messenger replied: اعْقِلْهَا وَتَوَكَّلْ — "Tie the camel, and then trust Allah to protect it."

So we must tie the camel first. We cannot simply leave the camel untied and then expect Allah to protect it. We have to do our own part first. The camel is a symbol of our desires, because our desires are enormous; they are a powerful beast, just like the camel. The camel is no ordinary animal. It is a very large, very strong animal, exactly like our desires and our temptations. So we must tie and bind this camel of our desires — which, if you recall, is literally what the word 'aql means.

We have to empty the cup before we can fill it again. The Isti'adha is the turning over of the cup, the pouring out of it, completely. That is literally what the heart is: it is a container, and every container has its limits. If the heart has reached its limits with what is forbidden, it will have no room left for what is lawful to enter. And that would be a disaster.

This is why the Companions (رضی اللہ عنھم) said that the Prophet literally emptied them out. He emptied out their hearts of the darkness of ignorance and filled them with light. So an emptying has to take place before the filling. It is just as you must breathe out before you can breathe in. It is just as the heart must contract before it can expand. This is the nature of creation, is it not? The diastole and the systole — this is the very nature of human beings. The pupil expands in order to take in light, and then it contracts to keep light out. These are all signs. These are all ayaat. This is the very nature upon which Allah has created us, because He is al-Qabid and al-Basit; He is the One who expands and the One who contracts.

So the more we expand for Shaytan, the more we contract for al-Rahman. And the more we expand for al-Rahman, the more we contract for Shaytan. That is La ilaha illa Allah. "La ilaha" — there is no god. That is contraction. That is tying our camel at the doorstep of Allah. And then comes "Bismillah," which is entering the mosque of Allah.

That is the whole concept of the Isti'adha. We are emptying out our hearts. We are emptying them of the whispers of Shaytan, of every desire for the forbidden, of every forbidden temptation. Why? So that we may now fill them with the Fatiha. We are closing the doors on the cursed Shaytan so that we may walk through the doors of Allah's mercy.

And this is how we come to  بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم. Now we begin our spiritual journey, which is the verb missing from the Basmallah. What is it that the Basmallah teaches us? It gives us an introduction, or rather, I should say, a reminder of who Allah (Azza Wa Jal) is. And how are we reminded of who Allah (Azza Wa Jal) is? By observing the divine attributes of Allah (Subhanhu Wa Ta'ala) WITHIN his creation. Not everyone will do this. It is a very particular group of people who are actually able to witness the attributes of Allah through his creation. And this is where the Quran and Allah's messenger come into play. The Quran is the map. I need the direction, and I need someone to explain the direction to me. I disobey my purpose if I do not fulfill the purpose of my existence, and if I let my free will go, that too must have a consequence. So my creator must want me to submit my will to him. He must want me to choose something.

When I realize this, the next thing I am learning from the Fateha is that this incredibly powerful, completely self-sufficient Allah is characterizing himself with Rehma. He is EXTREMELY loving, extremely caring, extremely merciful. And I have to think: does Allah actually need to be merciful? Does he really need to be merciful? What if he were not? What would you and I do if he were not merciful? Suppose this ayah had read, instead of BARR, what if it read بسم اللہ العزیز العادل — with the name of Allah, the most powerful and the most just. Instead of intense and constant mercy, what if he had characterized himself with power and justice? Because that would mean that the second I do something wrong, the all powerful decrees his justice against me. He punishes me right away. I miss a prayer, and he sends angels down upon me to beat me to a pulp. Because prayer is Allah's right over me. And he has the right to demand that right from me, and to punish me if I do not fulfill that right. Because he could certainly force me to fulfill that right whether I want to or not.

We all pay taxes every year, so we know what that feels like. We cannot escape a government, which is a body of created beings; there is no way at all that we could escape Allah. What if Allah, being my creator, imposed a property tax on me? I mean, he would be entirely justified. He would not be wrong to do it. After all, he is my creator, and that makes me his property. So he can do with me whatever he chooses. What if my sustenance and my daily ration of food, water, sleep, even oxygen — what if all of this were given to me according to my level of obedience to him? Does he have the power to do that? He certainly does. مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ — There is not a moving creature that Allah does not hold by its forelock.

So the question becomes: if, instead of AlRehman and AlRaheem, Allah had chosen to characterize his relationship with his creation as that of AlAzeez AlAadil, what would you and I have done? What COULD you and I do? What could you and I and all the rest of creation combined do to stop him? Is there anything we could have done? No. Absolutely not.

A very powerful king does not have to be kind, and history shows us that such kings usually are not. They have no fear of accountability. Is Allah accountable to anyone? No, he is not. Everything and everyone is accountable to him.

يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ

O people, you are all in complete need of Allah, and Allah is entirely self-sufficient without you.

إِن يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَأْتِ بِخَلْقٍۢ جَدِيدٍۢ

If he so desires, he can remove all of you and put a new creation in your place.

But from Barr I learn that he is not only powerful. He is also extremely loving, extremely caring, extremely concerned for me, extremely merciful, even though he has absolutely no reason to be that way. The relationship that he himself has chosen to have with me is not merely one of love and mercy, but one of intense love and mercy, and of constant love and mercy. It is the relationship that a mother has with her child while it is in her womb. SubhanAllah!

And how do I experience this? That is to say, how do I know that Allah loves me, and cares for me, and is concerned about me? How do I know that this is his relationship with me? I know it because when I look at his creation around me, I see that all of it is in a state of complete submission to Allah. All of it is following Islam. That is what Islam means: submission.

So then what is my purpose?

وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ

And we did not create Jinn and Man except for Ibadah. And Ibadah, as I mentioned earlier, is two things. It is worship, and it is obedience. The time when we are in salaah is worship, because worship is bound to particular times. And in the rest of the time, from the moment I wake to the moment I sleep, what do I have to do? Obedience. I have to remain in obedience to Allah, just like the rest of Allah's creation. That is exactly what the rest of creation is doing. It is doing what it was created to do, and that is obedience; and it is doing it at the time it is supposed to do it, and that is worship.

And how do I know what kind of obedience he expects of me? Did he give me an example of it, something I could understand and relate to? The body and the soul.

So this is where the Istiaaza and the first ayah of the Fateha bring me. After placing myself under Allah's protection with the Istiaaza, I now understand who my Allah is, through his divine attributes manifesting in his creation. I understand the kind of relationship he has with me. I understand now how much he loves me, how much he cares for me, and how he is intensely and constantly merciful toward me, even though he has absolutely no need to be so. Recognizing all of this, I also understand now what my purpose is: that I need to be in a state of constant worship and obedience to him. I begin my journey toward him. That is Bismillah AlRehman AlRaheem. I begin my journey toward him.

Because it is the verb, the action, that is going to prove his love for you. The one who truly begins with Barr will think about the blessings of food, of taste, of smell. He will become obsessed with Allah.

constantly reminded of Allah's mercy through Barr. That is why Barr is said before you begin something, because the act will show you his mercy if you choose to find it. And as soon as I begin my journey, what is my natural response to Allah? Seeing all his love for me, what is my natural response? AlHamdulillahi Rab Alalameen.

In the previous session we looked at the linguistic meaning of the word *Rabb*. We learned that a Rabb is المالک والسَّیِّد والمُرَبِّی والمُرشَد والمُنعِم والقَیِّم. A Rabb is one who is *Maalik*, who has absolute ownership, and who at the same time holds complete authority. Within that space of complete ownership and unrestricted authority, he ensures growth. He cares for his creation, he nurtures them, he protects them. And he does not only nurture them to maturity; he also sets them upon his straight path. He puts each creation to its proper use, showering them along the way with numerous, undeserved gifts and blessings. And then he sustains them and maintains them for the whole span of their duration, the span he has planned for us upon this earth. And the most important ingredient in this recipe is that all six of these meanings are grounded in that one fundamental emotion of *rehma*, of intense and constant love and care. الرحمن علم القرآن. The Loving, the Merciful, taught the Qur'an. Not الجبار علم القرآن. So *rehma* is the most important element of his *Rububiyyah*.

And so, when this person of sound essence reflected upon the creations of the heavens and the earth, he used the word *Rabb* to call upon his creator. رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَطِلًۭا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُۥ رَّبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًۭا يُنَادِى لِلْإِيمَنِ أَنْ آمِنُوا۟ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَـَٔامَنَّا. So he used *Rabb*. And he used that word because he saw the creations reflecting the *Rububiyyah* of their creator. The existence of the Rabb, and his *Rububiyyah*, is made evident by the *murabbee*. In other words, the *murabbee*, the one being nurtured, becomes a sign that points back to his Rabb. He becomes an *Ayah* for his Rabb.

And this applies even to us. For example, our parents take the role of a Rabb, of a creator, for our nurturing and training. And we, as *murabbee*, as children, play the role of their creation, and the same principle applies. We, as the creations of our parents, then reflect the attributes and the training of our creator. So you can see that this is a universal principle. It is not falsifiable.

I will give you an example. Let us say you meet a person, and you see that he is a very skilled electrician. From a rational standpoint, simply by observing his knowledge and skill, you would have to conclude, logically, that he went to a good electrical engineering school, or that he had a very skilled teacher who taught him this electrical work. Now, you have not actually seen the teacher, nor do you know the name of his school, yet you are still able to reach that conclusion. Why? Because this electrician is his teacher's creation. And through his skill and knowledge, he is manifesting the attributes and the training of his teacher. Because that is what every creation does: it manifests the *Rububiyyah* of its creator. And if this is true at a microcosmic level, it certainly holds true at the macrocosmic level. This universe too, being a creation, is manifesting the attributes of its creator. This sign, this *Ayah*, has been placed in the design, in the DNA of creation, so that it cannot help but reflect the attributes and the *Rububiyyah* of its Rabb. And the more you think about this, the more you will be able to appreciate the reality of this design. You will always be able to identify the creator through the creation.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
No matter where you look in the world. Now, although *Rabb* is commonly translated into English as LORD, linguists agree that a more suitable one-word replacement for the word *Rabb* is Master. For master represents not only ownership, authority, and control; it also represents the perfection of knowledge and skill required to nurture, guide, and maintain. So MASTER is far closer in meaning to the word *Rabb* than lord, or than any other English word available to us in the language.

Once we understand the word *Rabb*, the next thing to understand is that the word *Rabb* implies a relationship. There are certain words that automatically imply a relationship. They require a counterpart. For example, when I say teacher, whom does a teacher have a relationship with? With students. It automatically implies that relationship. I cannot be a teacher if I do not have any students, correct? When I say parent, whom do they have a relationship with? Children. When I say boss or employer, it implies a relationship with employees. There are certain titles that necessarily carry a relationship. But when I say "intelligent," it does not necessarily carry a relationship with anyone, correct? When I say "tall," that does not imply a relationship with anyone.

In the same way, Allah has certain names that do not imply a relationship. For example, Allah is lofty. He is الأعلی. It is a powerful attribute, but it does not imply a relationship. It is simply a fact. It is a description of one of His attributes, which is independent of anything else. But then He also has certain names that DO establish a relationship. For example, خالق, the creator. If He is a creator, there must be مخلوق; there must be creation. In the same way, if Allah is غفور, He is forgiving, there must be someone TO forgive. Yes? So some attributes of Allah are relational in nature, and others are not.

But when Allah begins His revelation with the word *Rabb* — اقرأ بسم ربک الذی خلق — when He introduces Himself as *Rabb*, as master, to Rasul Allah (*Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam*), and then, by extension, to us, what He is essentially doing is setting all of those other relational attributes aside and saying to us: When you think of Me, the first and foremost relationship you need to think of, the ONE relationship you should never let go of, EVEN if you forget all the other relations I have with you, the one you should ALWAYS be mindful of, every single waking moment of your life, is that "I" am your *Rabb*. I am your master. You understand? He is saying: Above and beyond everything else, I want you to know that I am your *Rabb*.

Now, if Allah is *Rabb*, if He is master, then what does that make me? And what does it make you? It makes ALL of us His slaves, and the Arabic word for slave is عبد. So when we accept Allah as our *Rabb*, simply by doing that we automatically accept the fact that we are His slaves.

عبد

So today I would like us to understand a little about this word عبد, because understanding our place in this hierarchy, in this relationship, and accepting it, will complete our relationship with Him. And it is truly important to do that. For a teacher cannot benefit a student until the student acknowledges and accepts that person as his teacher. A student can ONLY benefit from the teacher.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
When a slave is wronged by someone, who is ultimately insulted? The master. In the old days, wars would begin because a member of one tribe unjustly harmed or killed the slave of another tribe. That slave's master took it as a personal insult. Why? Because the offender had disrespected his property. A slave is his master's responsibility. Even if the slave was in the wrong and deserved to be reprimanded, to whom should the complaint be brought? To his master.

So Allah says: I am Rabb al-Alameen. Be careful how you deal with my creation.

No matter what group, what religion, what caste, what belief system, what country they belong to. No matter what your relationship with them is on this earth. It does not matter. Before he is your son, he is MY slave. Before she is your daughter, she is my slave. Before he is your father, before she is your mother, they are MY slaves. Before she is your daughter-in-law, she is my slave. Before he is your son-in-law, he is my slave. No matter what the relationship. Do not forget: I am here! And I am watching. If you treat them unjustly, if you hurt them, if you torture them mentally, insult them, degrade them, if you misuse your authority over them, you will have to answer to ME!!! Because I am Rabb al-Alameen. SubhanAllah!

Now here is what is, in my opinion, the most beautiful meaning of all. And this again connects back with the idea of our accepting and submitting to him as his slaves. The scholars say that what this title رب العلمین does is bring us all down to the same level in the eyes of Allah. ALL of us are slaves. No nation, no single group, is better than another. And if it is better, it is better only by whose standards? In the eyes of whom? In the eyes of the master.

The Humility of Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam). This is something I really want you to take away from today's session. If you forget everything else, I want you to remember just this. Because in today's world we are afflicted with this disease of superiority, with this feeling of a chip on our shoulders, whether we admit to it or not.

Superiority in rank can exist only through the eyes of the master, on the basis of a slave's service. NOT through the eyes of the slave. إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ. The most honorable in the eyes of Allah is the one who is the most pious. That is all. By nothing else. Because even the HIGHEST-ranking person is Allah's slave, and even the LOWEST-ranking person is Allah's slave. اشھد ان محمد عبدہ و رسولہ. I testify that Muhammad (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) is his SLAVE and his messenger. AllahuAkbar. The highest-ranking person who has EVER walked this earth — WE testify, in every salaah, that he is the SLAVE of Allah. Then what right do WE have to claim superiority OVER one another, or over people of other sects and religions? If we believe that we hold any superiority on the basis of our creed, THAT superiority has to be by the standards of Allah, NOT ours!! We cannot make that judgment for other slaves. Allah is the master of a Sulemani just as much as he is the master of a Sunni, of a Shia, of a Hindu, of a Christian, of a Jew, even an atheist. Allah is the ultimate master.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
And if Allah is the master, and we are ALL his slaves, who is the ONLY one who can judge a slave's rank? ONLY the master! Right? Can one slave stand before his master and say to another slave: You are a disgusting person. You are horrible. You are beneath me. I am better than you because you drink and I do not, or because I pray five times a day and you do not. Allah loves me more than you? NO. That is not up to the slave!!! But can a slave help another slave? If one slave has received guidance, and he understands it, and he has been blessed by his master, can he help another slave? Can he try to guide the other slave? And if not, can he at least pray for the other slave? Of course he can.

But to behave as though one were high and mighty. And has such a thing ever happened before? Does the Qur'an tell us of any such incident, when one slave set himself up to judge another slave? أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ. I am better than him. I am created from fire; he is created from clay. Do you remember who said that? Iblees! Iblees was an angel, from the عالَم of the angels. Adam was a human being, from the عالَم of Insaan. They were both slaves of Allah. And Iblees stood before Allah. He stood before the Rabb Alameen, and said: أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ. I am better than him.

And what do we learn from that story? What did his master do? Did his arrogance bring him nearer to Allah, or did it have him removed from His divine presence? Do you truly think that an act for which Iblees was punished, Allah would let pass for you and me? Would that befit His justice — that He punishes Iblees for his arrogance and removes him from His divine presence, and then draws us nearer to Himself?

Because you have to understand: when you and I judge one another, when you and I, as slaves, judge other slaves in terms of who is superior, what position do we set ourselves in? We set ourselves in the position of our Rabb. Now, does the Qur'an also tell us of someone who did that? Did someone not say, انا ربکم الاعلی — I am your greatest Rabb. Who said that? Firon said that. And how did he end up?

And the reality is that Firon knew he was human. He knew he was not a Rabb, for he was aware of his own weakness, and in spite of that he laid claim to a station he did not deserve. You know, he did not like the fact that he had to go to the toilet, because that was not befitting a Rabb. So he gathered all of his physicians together and asked them how he might be rid of this problem. And so they told him to eat bananas. So he ate bananas for forty days. And then he had a far greater problem.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
And so we truly must be constantly aware of this. Because this, today, is not merely a Fironic problem. This has become a global problem. Everyone wants to become Ilah. Everyone wants to become Mabood. There are people who want to be worshiped. And these are the people whom Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, addresses when He says: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَنَ مِن سُلَلَةٍۢ مِّن طِينٍۢ — you are from some chain of dirt, of mud and water mixed together. ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسْلَهُۥ مِن سُلَلَةٍۢ مِّن مَّآءٍۢ مَّهِينٍۢ — We created your progeny from a vile fluid. Who do you think you are?

Allah tells these people: get down off your high horse! Be a rajul. A rajul is the one who has ِرَجَلَ. ِرَجَلَ عن فَرِسِہ. A rajul is the one who comes down off of his high horse, and reaches the earth, and sets his feet upon the ground. He does not see himself raised up above the earth. He comes down to the level from which he came — from dust. That is الرجل. And all of these other people are merely playing games, trying to be Ilah. And Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, says no! Be a rajul. Be banee adam. Be Adamee. That is what it truly means to accept the station of Rabbul Alameen. Humility, not arrogance.

But it is the nature of the human being that as soon as he receives a blessing, he becomes arrogant. We immediately climb up onto our high horses. Oh, you know — I run the Sunday Sessions. Who are you to tell me anything?

Who are you to give me advice? How dare you? This is pure arrogance. The very fact that Allah honored me — a slave — by placing me in this position, where I am now able to benefit others, this honor itself ought to ground me in humility, not arrogance. Because I am a slave. This Rububiyyah is an honor granted to me by my master, by my Rabb. It is a burden. And the proof that I truly regard this responsibility as a burden is that you will see it bend my back. When you carry a burden upon your back, do you bend forward, or do you walk upright? The burden makes you bend. It makes you humble. This is why humility is the essence of spiritual progress.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
Hazrat Ibraheem sahab's words are ringing in my ears at this very moment. The one who is the most humble will rise the highest. If you wish to climb a mountain, how will you climb it? By bending forward in humility, or by walking upright? This is why the highest ranking person in this world, my beloved Rasul Allah (salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) — of all the prophecies that foretold his coming, the greatest mark of his prophethood was his humility. یُریدُ أَنَّ یَبعَثُ أُمِیِّ مِنَ الأُمِّیِّن۔ وأجعل السكينةَ لباسُهُ ، والبِرَّ شَعارُهُ ، والتقوى ضَميرَهُ ، والحِكمَةَ مَنطِقَهُ ، والصِّدقَ والوفاءَ طَبِيعَتُهُ ، والعَفوَ وَالمَعرُوفَ خُلقُهُ ، والَحقَّ شَريعَتَهُ ، والعَدلَ سيرَتَهُ ، والهَدِىُ إمامُهُ ، والإسلامَ مِلَّتُهُ ، وأحمد أِسمُهُ . أَهدِي بِهِ بَعدَ الضَّلالَة ، وأعلَمُ بِهِ مِنَ الجَهالة ، وأَرفَعُ به بعد الخَمالَة ، وأعرِفُ به بعد النَّكِرَة ، وأكثَرُ بِهِ بعدَ القِلَّة ، وأغنِي به بعد العَيلَة ، وأَجمِعُ به بعد الفُرقَة . وأُؤَلِّفُ به بين أممٍ مُتَفَرِّقَة وَقُلُوبٍ مُختَلِفَة ، وأَهواءٌ متشَتَّتَة Allah revealed all of these remarkable signs that would help nations identify him. But the greatest of them all: لَو یَمشِی عَلی القَصَبِ الیَابِس۔۔۔ لَم یُسمَع مِن تَحتِ قَدَمَیہِ مِن سَکِینَتِہِ You will see him walk with such humility that if he walked upon dry leaves, you would not hear the sound of them cracking beneath his feet.

If you wish to know why this slave, Rasul Allah (salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam), attained the honor he received from his master, it was through one thing: humility. And that is what distinguishes a true believer from a hypocrite — humility. This is why atheism is such a blatant form of arrogance. For the atheist rejects something that is the most obvious and the most fundamental aspect of his own existence: that he was created. Even he cannot claim that he was not created. Now, if I say that my father created me, and his father before him created him — that is what they call Dawr, that is tasalsul; it simply keeps going back and back. And then, where do you stop? If it stops at Adam, then who created him? Because that is where the buck stops. وکُلُّکُم مِن آدَم. وَ آدَم مِن تُرَاب All of you are from Adam, and Adam is from dust. And arrogance does not befit the dirt, because it is trampled upon at every moment.

Maulana Ali saw a man behaving arrogantly, and he said to him: Who do you think you are? Your beginning is a vile, filthy fluid. Your end is a disgusting, decaying, foul-smelling corpse. And between these two stages, you walk through life carrying two loathsome things within your body: your urine and your feces. And your very creation is the result of the union of two unseemly parts of the body.

What right do you have to behave arrogantly before Allah and before his creation? And so this is the first thing: to know our station in this world, to know who we are. We are the ones who are ruled over. We are created. We will die. We will be raised again. This understanding — that we are the ones who are ruled over — this is the station of the slave: the knowing that I am not the Lord who rules, that I am not the creator.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
By Allah, I give you sincere counsel. I counsel you, and I counsel my own soul, because this is something we do all the time. I made this mistake so many times in my earlier life, when I did not understand these realities. May Allah forgive me for those wrongs. I try constantly to keep myself in check on this matter, even though I still do slip. But I do try to keep returning to this station of humility. And I give you children the very same counsel. For arrogance is the call to prayer, the summons of our age today. Arrogance is what we are constantly being called to in every walk of life: in school, in college, at work, in families. It is all about — life has become all about — I am better than you. And that does not befit an obedient slave.

If we would only grasp this one thing, if we truly understood the real meaning of the Lord of the Worlds, this world would become such a beautiful place. If we all understood that it is Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, who guides everyone — he is the king, he is the owner, he is the one who cares, he is the one who guides, he is the one who gives gifts — then everything about my life is between me and him. He will take care of me. I have no need to worry about anything. I have no need to judge another slave. I have no need to hurt another slave. I have no need to display my authority or my power over another slave. Even if I am hurt, even if I am wronged, especially if I have been wronged — because my master will take care of me. My master will come to my rescue. He will come to my defense on the Day of Judgment. And he will make that wrong right. He will stand behind me and support me. I have no need to worry about anything. For whether we believe it or not, whether we wish it or not, that day is coming, when the Lord will gather everyone and carry out justice.

رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ ٱلنَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍۢ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ ۚ

Our master, indeed you will gather all of us on a day about which there is absolutely no doubt, because you have promised us that.

إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ ٱلْمِيعَادَ

There is no doubt: Allah never breaks his promise.

Remind yourself of this every time you recite the Fatiha. There is a reason we pray fifty-one units of prayer in a single day, and all fifty-one times we recite the Fatiha — so that every time we say the Lord of the Worlds, we remind ourselves of this order of things: who he is and who we are in this relationship.

وآخر الدعوانا عن الحمد للہ رب العالمین
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
There was a man who traveled a long distance to meet the Messenger of Allah, and when he met him, he gave the Messenger a bottle of wine as a gift. He said, "O Messenger of Allah, I obtained this special wine as a gift for you." What would we do if someone did that? If someone very secular showed up at your doorstep with a bottle of wine as a house-warming gift, how would we react? "There is no power and no strength save in Allah. How dare you. Do you not know that I am a Muslim? Do you not know that this is forbidden? Get out of my house, and never show me your face again." Is that not so? And to whom did this man bring the bottle of wine? To the Messenger of Allah!

The most pious man we can imagine. And do you know how he responded? He smiled. He smiled and said, "Brother, did you not hear Allah's command that alcohol has been prohibited?" The man said, "No, Messenger of Allah. I never heard that!" He at once handed the bottle to his slave and said something in his ear. The Messenger of Allah asked, "What did you just say to him?" The man said, "I told him to sell the bottle in the market." The Messenger of Allah smiled again and said, "The One who has prohibited the drinking of intoxicants has also forbidden their trade." So the man told the slave to pour it out. This is the character of the Messenger of Allah. This is his humility. This is the nurturing, his rububiyyah. Glory be to Allah! He did not say, "Do you not know who I am? How dare you bring this filth into my presence." He never did that. For hearts can never be conquered with harshness. Hearts have always been conquered only with love and kindness. We should truly study and learn what kind of a Rabb, what kind of a parent, what kind of a teacher our Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, was. Glory be to Allah.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
when he ACCEPTS that relationship, and submits to it. Is that not so? A doctor cannot help a patient until what? Until the patient accepts and submits to the doctor's cure. Suppose the patient has diabetes and the doctor is telling him to stop eating candy. But every time he sees candy, he thinks: Oh, I know the doctor told me NOT to eat it, but what does he know anyway? It is only a little bit. It is not as though I am eating the whole bag, or anything like that. It makes no sense to me why I cannot eat candy. After all, what has candy got to do with diabetes? Now, if the patient behaves that way, he is not accepting the doctor as his doctor, and he is not submitting to him as his patient. So will the doctor be able to benefit the patient? No. The patient must first accept that relationship and complete the process, and ONLY then will he be able to gain benefit. Do you understand? It is a two-way street. The doctor HAS the knowledge to benefit the patient. The doctor WANTS to benefit the patient, because he cares about the patient and is genuinely concerned about him. But he can do nothing to help the patient. Why? Because the patient has not yet completed the relationship.

This means that even though Allah is my Rabb, even though He is المالک، و المربی، و المرشد، و المنعم، و القیم، و السید, and even though ALL of these are TRULY beneficial attributes, still, for me to gain the benefits from my Rabb, what must I do? I have to complete the relationship. How do I complete the relationship? By submitting myself to Him as His عبد, as His slave. Do you understand?

Now listen to this very carefully. The greatest CHALLENGE, the greatest DIFFICULTY, the greatest HARDSHIP that you and I will CONSTANTLY face, EVERY single waking moment of our lives, is to accept Allah as Rabb. I will say it again. The greatest and constant challenge that you and I and everyone else in this world face is NOT in accepting our Creator as Allah. Everyone is fine with that part. Even the jahili Arabs accepted Him as Allah. The REAL problem is in accepting Him as Rabb, as master. Do you know why? Because if we accept Him as Rabb, that means we have to become what? We have to become slaves. We have to become عبد. And do you know what a slave is? A slave is someone who no longer has a choice. He no longer has free will. He now has to obey the will of his master. He is nothing more than an extension of his master's desires.

And we live in the age of choices. We live in the age of free will. We live in the age where I am in charge, I am in control, I am the master of my own destiny. I am powerful. I am wealthy. I do not have to listen to you. You are not the boss of me. I can do whatever I want, whenever I want. I am the king of my domain. This is MY life. If I want to do it, I will do it. If I do not want to do it, I will not! In other words, I AM MY OWN RABB!! I AM MY OWN RABB. I am my own god. I am my own master.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
And Allah is saying: No! I am your master. I gave you this life. I gave you this authority. I gave you these gifts of parents. I gave you these gifts of children. I honored you with position and power. I gave you health and strength. So do not abuse them, because I can just as easily take them away from you. Do not forget.

I am your Rabb! ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ. This is the greatest challenge you and I will ever face in our lives. It is the greatest challenge we will face constantly: to accept that Allah is my Rabb, and I am his slave. My master's will is my command. That is the signature act of a true abd. My master, I am not going to make my own decisions. You will make my decisions for me. If you tell me to do something, I will do it, even if I do not feel like doing it. If you tell me not to do something, I will not do it, even if I am dying to do it. Willingly and happily, I give up my freedom to become your slave, because you are my Rabb. And no one can be a better Rabb than you.

Now here is the next question. Am I a slave only if I accept Allah as my master? In other words, suppose I do not accept him as Rabb. Does that then mean I am no longer his slave? Well, let us return to the definition of Rabb. He is Maalik. He is the owner. Set aside all the other definitions and hold to this one alone. By the simple fact that he is Maalik, he is the owner of every single creation. That fact alone makes every single creation his property, his slave. Does it not?

This means that being his property, or his slave, has nothing to do with whether one is a Muslim. For that word now applies to every single creation. The sun is his slave, the moon is his slave, the galaxies, the whole universe and everything within it is his slave. Everything is his property. So this means that when believers choose to submit to him, they are his slaves, and when disbelievers choose to disbelieve in him and to reject his ownership, guess what? They are still his slaves. They are still his property. Do you understand? The question, then, is not who is a slave and who is not, because in the final analysis everyone and everything is his slave. The only difference now is who is an obedient slave and who is a disobedient slave. That is the only real question.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
So now, who will truly benefit from the Rabb? In a sense, both will, because this Rabb is AlRehman and AlRaheem. The Rehman will benefit every creation, obedient or disobedient. In that respect he is neutral. Just as a mother feeds all her children equally, the obedient and the disobedient, but when it comes to rewards, whom will she naturally reward? The obedient child or the disobedient child? A good mother, though she loves all her children equally, will not reward a child for bad behavior. A teacher teaches all of his students equally, but the obedient and hardworking student will attract the teacher's favors and blessings more than the slackers, will he not? He will go above and beyond the call of duty in teaching the students who truly want to learn, who have truly submitted to that relationship. In the same way, the Rehman will be a Rabb to both, the disobedient and the obedient slave. But the obedient slave will receive special rewards, permanent rewards, from the Raheem.

And now, if we return to the verses about this person of sound essence, we learn that when he uses the word Rabb for his creator, he did not only accept his creator as his Rabb; he also submitted himself as his obedient slave. For a little later, when he hears Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) calling out to this revelation.

we see that he accepts at once. رَّبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًۭا يُنَادِى لِلْإِيمَنِ أَنْ آمِنُوا۟ بِرَبِّكُمْ. Now, the verse says that we HEARD a caller calling — in the past tense — yet the address is directed to the Rabb in the present tense (Rabbana). By that logic he ought to have said Fanu'minoon. "Our master, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, saying, 'Believe in your master.'" فَـَٔامَنَّا. "We have believED." The point I want you to grasp is WHEN the acceptance actually took place. This is exactly why a knowledge of Arabic grammar is so important for understanding the Qur'an. The word فَـَٔامَنَّا is in the past tense. It does not say فنؤمنون, "we now believe." No. فَـَٔامَنَّا. We have already believED. Why does he speak in the past tense? Because the believing happened in the past — when he was reflecting upon the creation of the heavens and the earth. That is when belief in his Rabb took place. At this point there is only affirmation.

Another lesson we draw from these verses is that sincere reflection makes the acceptance of revelation EASY. The one who finds the teachings of the Qur'an difficult is the one who has NOT YET taken the time to reflect upon it honestly and sincerely. For revelation — this Qur'an — simply CONFIRMS what REFLECTION concludes. This person's reflections force him to CONCLUDE that his creator is Rabb. And then, through revelation, Allah merely confirms his conclusions when He says: الحمد للہ رب العلمین. Praise and gratitude belong to Allah, who is what? Rabb al-Alameen. Allah confirmed that indeed, I am your Rabb. All that revelation did at this point was give his Rabb a name: Allah.

The relationship between the words Allah and Rabb. And, astonishingly, the meanings of the word Allah and the meanings of the word Rabb are PERFECTLY correlated. Do you still remember the various meanings of the word Allah, or AL-ILAH?
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
Allah is the one I worship. The one to whom I surrender my will. And what is the Arabic for worship? عبادۃ. And who performs عبادۃ? The A'bd — the slave. By accepting Allah as our Rabb, did we not thereby submit to being His slaves? So Allah is Rabb. The two are bound to each other.

Allah is the one to whom I turn for protection. And is protection not one of the very things that ownership, authority, and nurture provide? When a child is frightened, to whom does it turn? To its parents. To its Rabb. So Allah is Rabb.

Allah is the one to whom I am completely loyal and devoted. Does a student not become completely loyal and devoted to his teacher — his Rabb — in order to gain his knowledge? He must. Allah is Rabb.

Allah is the one who is so LOFTY, so far beyond my capacity to comprehend and understand, that I would be dumbfounded every time I tried to approach Him. Is that not so? Now, if you consider Allah as Rabb — is Allah only your Rabb? Is He only my Rabb? Or is He the Rabb of EVERY SINGLE CREATION — not only of this world, but of solar systems within galaxies, and galaxies within the universe? Parents have a couple of children, and their needs drive them to distraction. How many is Allah caring for? ALL AT THE SAME TIME? If you reflect on JUST this ONE thing — this ONE single aspect of His Rububiyyah — and there are millions of other things to reflect upon, but even if you consider only this ONE thing — where does it leave you? Dumbfounded. Gobsmacked, as you English people say. Is that not so? Once again, Allah is Rabb.

Allah is the one upon whom I can lean, upon whom I can rest my whole weight.

the one I can trust. Do we trust a Rabb? Does a student trust his teacher? Does a child trust its parents? Is it wholly dependent upon them? Absolutely. Allah is Rabb.

Allah is the one with whom I am passionately in love. He is the one over whom I am consumed. Do children love their parents absolutely, and their mothers above all? My son Amir is three and a half years old. He cannot bear to be apart from his mother for a single minute. She leaves him with me for five minutes, and he cries, "Mama, mama, mama. I want Mama." That is his love for her rububiyyah. He cannot bear to be away from her. Allah is Rabb.

You know this idea of the love of Allah in Islam. It is truly a remarkable thing. Some of the poets — and this is my own view — there is truly no poetry like Arabic poetry, purely because of this language, and because of the way certain people have given voice to their love for Allah. It is simply this:

فَلَيـتَكَ تَحلُو وَالحَيـاةُ مَـرِيرَةٌ . وَلَيـتَكَ تَرضـى وَالأنـامُ غِضَـابُ
وَلَيـتَ الَّذِي بَيـنِي وَ بَينَـكَ عَامِرٌ . وَبَـينِي وَبَيـنَ العــالَمِينَ خَـرَابُ
فَيالَيـتَ شُـربِي مِن وِدَادِكَ صَافِياً . وَشُـربِي مِن مَـاء الفُراتِ سَـرَابُ
إذا نِلتُ مِنكَ الوُدَّ فَالكُلُّ هَيِّـنٌ . وَكُـلَّ الَّذي فَوقَ الـتُّرابِ تُـرابُ
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
If only I may taste the sweetness of your joy, I do not care though life should turn bitter for me. If only you are pleased with me, I do not care for the anger of all the rest of the world. If only what is between me and you remains beautiful, I do not care though the whole world should become a ruin to me. If I drink from the wine of your pure love, it turns even the water of the Euphrates into a mirage. If I attain only your love, I attain everything; and if I do not attain your love, then everything upon this earth is, to me, dust.

In any case, you can see how beautifully these two words are bound together — Rabb, Alameen.

The next thing we find worthy of notice, in this conclusion drawn by a man of sound intellect, is that he says:

رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَطِلًۭا
رَّبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًۭا يُنَادِى لِلْإِيمَنِ

Our Master. He does not say ربی ما خلقت ھذا باطلا — my Master, you did not create all of this in vain. No, he says ربنا — our Master. He speaks in the plural. Why? Because he also understands that he is not alone. He has been created to exist among other creations, and Allah is not his Rabb alone; He is also the Rabb of every other creation. And this conclusion is once again confirmed by Allah, Azza wa Jal, when He calls Himself رب العالمین — the Master of the Alameen.

Now let us look at the meaning of this word, العالمین. Its singular form is عالَم, which is an ism maf'ul bihi — an object for the subject, which is عالِم. But set the grammar aside. I want you only to look at these two words: Aalam and Aalim. You can see that they both have exactly the same spelling. The only difference between Aal-a-m and Aal-i-m is the fatha and the kasra. Apart from that, they both share the same spelling. And we have seen this principle in Arabic a few times before: that when two words share a common spelling, they have a deep connection in their meaning. This is because they both also share the same root word, which is Ilm — knowledge.

عالِم is the one who knows. And عالَم is that which he comes to know. عالِم, the one who knows, is the cause; and عالَم, this world, is that which is known — it is the effect.

See, human beings can know a great many things. But even with all the knowledge we have gained, we still cannot know everything.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
We are knowledgeable about certain things, and at the same time we are ignorant of others. Allah, by contrast, is علیم — the one who possesses absolute knowledge of everything. But there is no way for human beings to know Allah directly. We can no more know what God is than we can know what God is not. The reason is that we are speaking of Allah, the infinite Creator of the heavens and the earth. The very fact that we understand Allah to be infinite tells us something, for infinite means without limit. Imam Jafar as-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: اللہ اکبر من ان یحد و یحسر. Allah is great in the sense that He has no boundary and cannot be confined within comprehension. In other words, Allah cannot be defined. Yet the only way human beings are able to understand anything is through definition, because a definition is what defines — what gives finiteness to a concept. It limits the concept, it sets it within a perspective. That is what intellect, or aql, means: to set a boundary, to confine. And so we face a problem. How are we, as human beings, as creatures of finiteness and definition, to understand a Creator who is infinite and cannot be defined?

The only way this is possible is through an intermediary, like an interpreter. If all you speak is French, and all I speak is English, then for me to understand what you are saying I need someone in between who understands both languages, someone who can take your message in French and render it for me in English. In the same way, we human beings needed a third entity that could act as that interpreter between Allah and us — something itself defined, something confined in its existence so that we could understand it, yet reflecting the infiniteness of its Creator. And that is the عالَم. That is this world.

The universe manifests the existence of Allah.

So Allah created this عالَم, this universe, so that the عالِم might come to know the علیم. Do you understand? The one who knows, the عالِم, comes to know Allah, who is علیم, through this universe, the عالَم. In other words, this universe is the medium through which we Muslims have always understood Allah. We believe in Allah, glorified and exalted is He, because of the overwhelming proofs that this universe displays. And that is why, for us, the ultimate proof that Allah exists is that this universe exists — together with the simple fact that every created thing requires a creator. A poet says: وُجُودُہُ لَہُ دَلِیلُ قَاطِع، حَاجَتُ کُلِّ مُحدَثٍ لِصَانِع. The most convincing proof that He exists is that every sculpture requires a sculptor. کُل عالَم لِی حَاجَّتاً الی العَالِم — every world requires the existence of a knower. Nothing can exist in a passive state. And therefore the proof by which we know that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, exists, is through the آثار, through the effects of creation.

Someone once asked a Bedouin: بِمَ عَرَفتَ رَبُّك؟ — How did you come to know your Lord? He said: إن البِعرَةُ تَدُلُّ علی البَعِیر، والرَّوثَةُ تَدُلُّ علی الحمیر، و آثارُ القدم تَدُلُّ علی المَسِیر. The camel dung shows me that a camel was there. The donkey dung tells me that a donkey was there. Footprints in the sand tell me that people passed by. فسمآءُ ذاتُ اَبرَاج، والارض ذاتَ الفِجاج.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
واَبحَرُ ذَاتَ الامواج So when I look at the sky, with its perfect constellations, and at the earth with its perfect valleys and passes, and at these oceans with all of their waves — الا تدل علی لطیف الخبیر؟ Does not all of this point to the presence of the *lateef* and the *khabeer*? SubhanAllah! To him it was so simple. Consider how we make things far more complicated than they are. The truth is that the existence of Allah is the clearest and most manifest truth there is. The atheist says, "I wish there were a proof of the existence of Allah," and the believer answers, "I see nothing but the proofs of His existence."

So, speaking linguistically, this is the meaning of the word عالَم: that which is known by the عالِم, so that through it he may come to recognize the علیم. This is why "world" is not the best translation for Alameen. It narrows the scope of the meaning. If it meant "world," then it would mean nothing other than the world, and the plural form of that would have been العوالم, not العالمین. The word العالمین takes in a far broader spectrum than the physical world alone. Rabb AlAlameen means that Allah is not only the master of worlds; He is also the master of every species and of every distinct group of creation. Every group and category we can conceive of is an عالَم, because this, again, is how we as human beings operate: we take a set of known things and gather them together, and we classify them. So العالمین means all the categories, classifications, and groups that exist.

It can be عالم الروحانی، عالم الجِرمانی، عالم الجسمانی — the spiritual world, the galaxies and solar systems, and this physical world. Then, if we focus only on this physical world, it includes the various sub-domains and kingdoms: for instance, عالم المعدنیات, the mineral kingdom; عالم النبتات, the plant kingdom; عالم الحیوان, all animal life, including human beings; عالم الانسان. And if you look still more closely within the human category, it means all the different races and different nations. All of these are called عالمین.

For instance, Allah says in the Quran: يَبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّى فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَلَمِينَ. I gave you preference over every other nation — and the word used for nations here is Alameen. It can also mean different generations across time: قُلْ آمَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَهِيمَ وَإِسْمَعِيلَ وَإِسْحَقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَٱلْأَسْبَاطِ. Say, "We have believed in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to Abraham and Ismaeel and Ishaq and Yaqoob and his Descendants." Now these are all separate and distinct generations, father after son, yet together they all represent عالمین. So it also carries the meaning of different periods of time. And so when Allah calls Himself Rabb Alalameen, what He is saying is that no matter what category, what group, or what sub-group you come to know of, you will see My Rububiyyah at work in all of them.

This is a concept we also find in the English language. So the translation "world" is not entirely wrong, if you take it in the broader sense. For example, if you speak with an elderly gentleman who is eighty years old and ask him to tell you what life was like when he was young, he will begin by saying, "Oh, it was a different world." Have you ever heard that? You visit a different country.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
People who have lived their whole lives in the United States say the same thing when they visit a third-world country for the first time: this is a different world; they had no idea people could live like this. Someone will tell you, "I work in New York, so I am used to a certain kind of culture. A few years ago I visited Texas, and even St. Louis, and the people there are actually nice — they are truly nice. It is a different world. They say the strangest things, like 'Good morning!' and 'How are you doing today?' It is very strange. In New York, if somebody walks up to you and says, 'Hey, good morning, how are you doing?' — you run. You run like the wind, or you pull out your pepper spray and let it hiss, or whatever you have."

In other words, it does not matter which civilization you belong to. It does not matter which culture you belong to. I am the master of them all. I am Rabb al-Alameen. I do not merely hold ownership and authority over you. I do not merely nurture you, care for you, and protect you with love and kindness. I do not merely shower blessings and gifts upon you. I do not merely sustain your existence and put you to proper use. I do all of this for the whole of my creation, for every created thing.

Interpretations of Rabb al-Alameen

The scholars have offered many beautiful interpretations of this word, Alameen, and of why Allah called himself Rabb al-Alameen. I will share only a couple with you; otherwise we would be speaking about this for months.

The first is that by saying Rabb al-Alameen, Allah points out that because it is He who created the different cultures, the different creations, the different civilizations, and the peoples of different languages — because He alone is the master of them all — you do not have to be like anyone else. You can simply be who you are. You do not have to look a certain way, dress a certain way, walk a certain way, or talk a certain way. You can simply be yourself, and that is fine. I love you just as you are, because you are my slave every bit as much as the next creation. I will give you guidance, and as long as you accept yourself as my slave and follow my guidance, you can live happily within whatever culture, civilization, society, or country you find yourself in. For all cultures, all civilizations, and all nations are honored by Allah.

The second implication here, and the more important one, is this: when you deal with people in this life, whatever their race or religion, do not forget that Allah is Rabb al-Alameen. Do you know why that matters? Because if you hurt them, if you break their hearts with your words, if you torment them with the authority I have temporarily granted you over them, you had better not forget that I am Rabb al-Alameen. And not only human beings — the animals too, the plants too, this earth too. Before you are cruel to them, you had better remember that I am their Rabb as well.
body.topic_title_en: The Bond Between Lord and Servant

body.text_en:
The womb is the first rabb of a child. It converts sperm into a child. Then the parents become rabb, and they nurture the child until the process of development is complete and he reaches maturity.
