So in a sense, Allah put him through all of his training so that he could train me. Now, if I want to be TRULY grateful to him, I must also be grateful to his teachers, and their teachers, and their teachers, and so on. And if I go all the way back, where will I eventually reach?

I am grateful to my teacher, Javeed bhai, who learned from and is grateful to the manaseeb, who learned from and are grateful to the Duaat, who learned from and are grateful to the Aimma, who learned from and are grateful to Maulana Ali, peace be upon him, the source of all true knowledge. And when I get there, whom do I find Maulana Ali grateful to? انا عبدٌ من عبید محمد. He is grateful to Rasul Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his progeny, who is grateful to Jibraeel, peace be upon him, who is then grateful to Allah, Azza wa Jal. Once again, even at the spiritual level, the buck stops with Allah. You understand?

This is why Allah says in the Quran: أُو۟لَٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ — Those whom they call upon, they too seek MEANS, intermediaries, to access their Rabb. أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ — Each one of them closer to their master. Closer in what? وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُۥ وَيَخَافُونَ عَذَابَهُ — In their hope for His mercy, and their fear of His punishment.

This is why, in every dua that we recite, we mention the names of Rasul Allah, Maulana Ali, and the Aimma Tahireen BEFORE we begin our conversation with Allah. Why is that? Why can we not just pray directly to Allah? Why do we have to place these individuals between us and Allah? We have to do that because Allah HIMSELF placed these intermediaries in between. We came to know of Allah THROUGH their rububiyyah. And so now justice dictates that we have to be grateful to them first, we have to honor them first, we have to do what they ask us to do FIRST. And then we have to use them as waseela, as means, to approach Allah.

أنا مولى من ضرب بسیفین ..... و طعن برمحین ..... وصلى القبلتین ..... وبایع البیعتین ..... وهاجر الهجرتین ..... ولم یکفر بالله طرفة عین..... أنا مولى صالح المؤمنین ..... ووارث النبیین ..... وخیر الوصیین ..... وأکبر المسلمین ..... ویعسوب المؤمنین ..... ونور المجاهدین ..... ورئیس البکائین ..... وزین العابدین.....  وسراج الماضین ..... وضوء القائمین ..... وأفضل القانتین ..... ولسان رسول رب العالمین ..... وأول الوصیین من آل یس ..... والمؤید بجبرئیل الامین ..... و المنصور بمیکائیل المتین ..... المحمود عند أهل السماء أجمعین ..... والمحامی عن حرم المسلمین ..... والمجاهد أعداءه الناصبین ..... ومطفئ نیران الموقدین ..... وأفخر من مشى من قریش أجمعین ..... وأول من حارب واستجلب.....  أمیر المؤمنین ..... ووصی نبیه فی العالمین ..... وأمینه على المخلوقین ..... وخلیفة من بعث إلیها أجمعین ..... سید المسلمین والسابقین ..... وقاتل الناکثین والقاسطین ..... ومبید المشرکین وسهم من مرام الله على المنافقین

سئل قنبر مولى من أنت؟ فقال: أنا مولى من ضرب بسیفین و طعن برمحین وصلى القبلتین وبایع البیعتین وهاجر الهجرتین ولم یکفر بالله طرفة عین، أنا مولى صالح المؤمنین ووارث النبیین وخیر الوصیین وأکبر المسلمین ویعسوب المؤمنین ونور المجاهدین ورئیس البکائین وزین العابدین وسراج الماضین وضوء القائمین وأفضل القانتین ولسان رسول رب العالمین وأول الوصیین من آل یس والمؤید بجبرئیل الامین و المنصور بمیکائیل المتین المحمود عند أهل السماء أجمعین والمحامی عن حرم المسلمین والمجاهد أعداءه الناصبین ومطفئ نیران الموقدین وأفخر من مشى من قریش أجمعین وأول من حارب واستجلب، أمیر المؤمنین ووصی نبیه فی العالمین وأمینه على المخلوقین وخلیفة من بعث إلیها أجمعین سید المسلمین والسابقین وقاتل الناکثین والقاسطین ومبید المشرکین وسهم من مرام الله على المنافقین [ ولسان کلمة العابدین، ناصر دین الله وولی الله ] ولسان کلمة الله وناصره فی أرضه وعیبة علمه وکهف دینه إمام الابرار مرضی عند العلی الجبار، سمح، سخی، حیی، بهلول، سنحنحی، زکی، مطهر، أبطحی، بازل جری (2) همام، صابر، صوام، مهدی، مقدام، قاطع الاصلاب مفرق الاحزاب عالی الرقاب، أربطهم عنانا وأثبتهم جنانا وأشدهم شکیمة، باسل، صندید، هزبر، ضرغام، حازم، عزام، حصیف، خطیب، محجاج، کریم الاصل، شریف الفصل (3) فاضل القبیلة، نقی العترة، زکی الرکانة، مؤدی الامانة من بنی هاشم وابن عم النبی، الامام المهدی الرشاد، مجانب الفساد، الاشعث الحاتم، البطل الجماجم (4)...
body.topic_title_en: He Who Struck With Two Swords

body.text_en:
In the last few sessions we considered praise and gratitude toward Allah, and praise and gratitude toward the intermediaries of Allah, and how the two are connected. Today I want to try to explain a topic that often causes confusion: why does Allah need our praise and gratitude?

In the previous session, someone asked a question. It seems that Allah does not need us at all, and that He created us solely for worship. So if He has no need of us, and we had no need to exist, and we never asked to exist, then why create human beings in the first place? It seems that Allah could have spared Himself and everyone a great deal of trouble.

It is a fair question, because we do meet such apparent contradictions in the Qur'an. On one hand, the Qur'an tells us that Allah is lofty. He is majestic beyond measure. His is the ultimate power. He is able to do anything and everything. He is absolute and complete in Himself.

قل ھو اللہ احد. اللہ الصمد

He is unique and absolute. He needs no one and nothing.

الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ

Everything in the heavens and the earth sings His praise and is grateful to Him — and not only today.

وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ

Even in the future, in the life to come, all praise and gratitude will belong to Him.

يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ

O people, you are the ones who stand in need of Allah, and Allah has no need of you.

وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ

Allah is praised in and of Himself. He does not need your praise, nor does He need your gratitude. All of these verses point to the same truth: that He is a Master utterly beyond His creation, because He is too great. And that is fine. Fair enough. I can understand it. After all, I do not expect the president of the United States to take an interest in what I am having for dinner. So I understand it.

But then there are also verses in the Qur'an in which He plainly asks us to praise Him and to be grateful to Him.

وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَم يَكُن لَّهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ

And say: "All praise and gratitude belong to Allah, who has taken no son, and who has no partner in His dominion."

وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا

And say: "All praise and gratitude belong to Allah. He will soon show you His signs, and you will recognize that He is your Master."

Wait. I thought You said You did not need us — that You are too majestic, too lofty, to need us. We are the ones who need You. But now You are saying that You do want me to be grateful? You do want me to praise You? Why? You do not need it. Besides, everything else in the heavens and the earth is already praising You and is already grateful to You. So why do You need my praise and gratitude? It does not seem that You are short of it. What difference does it make to You whether I praise You or not?

And then, on top of all this, He says:

وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ

I did not create jinn and man except to worship Me. So which is it? Do You love me, or do You not love me? If You love me, how is it that You do not need me? And if You do not need me, then how can You love me? And not merely love me, but love me the way a mother loves the child in her womb. It does not add up, does it?

Understanding how Allah does not need us

Now, why are these questions so important to us? They are important because to love, and to be loved, is a very, very important thing for us as human beings — right from the moment of our birth.

Consider it. Why are we drawn to Allah more by love than by punishment? The Qur'an speaks of both, and both methods do work. Yet we naturally wish to move toward Allah through the feeling of love and not through fear. Is that not so? It is because love is a truly important thing to us. So when we hear something like "Allah does not need us, since everything else is already praising him," what happens is that we hear that message with our human ears, and we then confuse it with our own experiences of rejection, and we end up responding in the same way. It is as though someone were to say, "I have SO many friends. I have so many people who love me. I really do not care whether you are my friend or not. I really do not care whether you love me or not." And when we hear this, we are naturally hurt, and we say, "FINE! WHATEVER. Go and get your praise and gratitude from THEM." نعوذ باللہ. Yes, it is an egotistic response, but then we are egocentric creatures.

Why did it make her happy? This is the part I want you to understand. It made her happy not because I said those words, but because I appreciated why she had done all of this for me. Why did she do all of it? To show me that she loves me, that she cares for me, that she values me in her life, that I am someone special to her. And she showed it by laboring over a dish that I wanted, to make me happy, to benefit me. When I praised her, I did not see only the food; I saw her love behind it. I recognized and appreciated the purpose of her hard work. Do you understand?

And because I appreciated it, because I recognized its value, what did I do? I dropped whatever I was doing, and I rushed to receive the benefit, to enjoy it. My appreciation of her cooking moved me to benefit from it. And after I ate her cooking, after I enjoyed the fruit of her labor, I felt gratitude toward her. I felt love for her. My heart drew closer to her. And so what was the next thing I said? "Thank you, Khala. Thank you so much for loving me, for caring about me, for doing this for me. Even though you did not have to, even though you had no need to do this, you did it for me, and I love you for that." That is what made her happy — not merely my words of praise, not my eating her food, but my recognizing and appreciating her love. And once I had done that, my natural response to her love was to love her back.

This is why Allah asks us in the Qur'an, هَلْ جَزَآءُ ٱلْإِحْسَٰنِ إِلَّا ٱلْإِحْسَٰنُ Is the reward of good anything but good? Allah asks us in Surah al-Rahman: Where is my appreciation? Again, not because He needs my appreciation — I hope you understand that by now. Not because He needs us to reciprocate, but because He wants us to reciprocate. I did so much for you because I love you; will you not love me back? Will you not give me even that much? Is the reward of something good not to reciprocate in kind? هَلْ جَزَآءُ ٱلْإِحْسَٰنِ إِلَّا ٱلْإِحْسَٰنُ

Hamd must be both — praise and gratitude

Now let us understand why hamd is a combination of appreciation and gratitude. Why can it not be one or the other? Let us look at some scenarios. And I am speaking here about the rule, not the exceptions. We will talk about the exceptions another time. Let us first simply understand the rule, all right?

Khala cooks this delicious leg of lamb and calls me for dinner. I come to the table and I say, "Oh, Khala, this is so amazing. This looks so tasty. Oh my, you did all of this for me? You really love me so much. You are wonderful. I love you." But I do not really feel like eating. It is great that you did all this for me, and it does look really good.

But I will not enjoy it. Do you think that would make her happy? No. Why not? I did appreciate her effort and her love, did I not? I did praise her. So what is the problem? The problem is that I received no benefit from it. I did not eat it. And that was the real reason she did all the work, was it not? She did not prepare something I love merely so that I could praise it and then not eat it. That means I do not truly appreciate what she did for me. My refusal to take the benefit is proof that I do not genuinely value it, because appreciation should lead a person to desire the benefit and to take it.

Now let us look at the other side of the coin. My aunt calls me to dinner, and I eat the whole thing. I do in fact receive the benefit, but then I do not say a single word. I finish the meal. I let out a loud burp. And then I stand up and walk away. How do you think my aunt feels now? Would she feel hurt? Would she feel disappointed? Why? It cannot be because I did not eat it, because I did. I devoured the whole thing. So I took the benefit. I proved that I appreciate it. Now what is the problem? The problem is that I felt no gratitude for what she did for me. She did all of this for one single reason, to show me how much she loves me. And I ate her food. I enjoyed all her hard work. I benefited from it, yet I failed to feel, or to acknowledge, any gratitude toward her. I took her completely for granted. So yes, she would be justified in feeling disappointed.

So you see, it is not one or the other. It is both. Hamd is when I appreciate something, benefit from it, and let that benefit move me to gratitude. Miss any part of this, and it is no longer hamd. It is incomplete. It is ناقص. It is imperfect and defective.

Now what if I kept doing this to her again and again? Every time I visit her, she prepares raan for me. And either I do not eat it, or I devour it all and never speak a word of thanks. What will eventually happen? She will beat me to death with that very raan, will she not? Of course not. But she will certainly stop making raan for me. Why? For two reasons: justice and tribulation.

Justice, because I have proven to her that I am not worthy of that blessing. Her hard work is being wasted on me. Why? Because I am either failing to appreciate it or failing to be grateful for it, and so I do not deserve it. And when you give a blessing to someone who does not deserve it, you are denying that blessing to the one who does deserve it. Someone else could be enjoying and appreciating my aunt's hard work instead of me. She could be showing her love to another person, who would then return that same love to her. That is one reason blessings are withheld.

The second reason is to bring about tribulation. I am accustomed to my aunt making raan for me every time I come to Karachi. The first time she refuses to make it, I say, "Aunt, when are you making raan?" She says, "I am not making it for you anymore. You do not deserve it." How am I going to feel? I will feel pain. I will feel upset. It will cause some tribulation, will it not?

Trials and tribulations are wake-up calls. They shake us. How could you, Aunt? What did I do wrong? You have always done this for me; why not now? It will force me to think. I have been ungrateful. She has been doing this for me all this time, and I have been taking her love for granted.

If I am a person of sound heart and sound intellect, this is precisely what tribulation is meant to produce in me: repentance. But if I am self-absorbed, conceited, and ungrateful, my response will be altogether different. I will say, "Fine! Whatever! I always knew you never loved me to begin with. You are no longer my aunt!" Do you understand?

When I constantly and continuously deny and reject Allah's blessings, when one blessing follows another and I neither appreciate them nor draw any benefit from them, and when I do benefit I am never grateful, when I keep taking His blessings for granted, He withholds them from me. Why? The first reason is justice, for someone else could be benefiting from these blessings that are being wasted on me. The second reason is that, perhaps, just perhaps, the absence of the blessing now might make me realize the errors of my ways. And once I do, I will, one hopes, repent and make the effort to return to Him.

Now, when do you want someone to return to you: when you love them, or when you hate them? When you love them. Why? Because you wish to restore the lost blessing to them. I must show you that I have realized what I did wrong, apologize, and mend my ways, and then you will give me back the blessing you took away. Is that not so?

This is only one of many reasons. There are many reasons for trials and tribulations, which, God willing, we will cover in a future session. But one reason is that when a person is ungrateful and unappreciative of Allah's blessings, He puts him through trials and tribulations so that he may realize what he is doing wrong, correct it, and return to Him.

And do you know the word for returning back in classical Arabic? Tawba. Tawba means to return, or to retreat. When we move toward what is forbidden, we move away from Allah. When we realize our sin and abandon that forbidden thing, we return to Him; we retreat. That is the meaning of tawba. That is what a retreat is. When armies retreat, where do they go? They return to their homes, back to the source.

This is the philosophy, the design, behind praise and gratitude. Allah does not need me, but He does love me. And He has manifested His love physically, through the عالم. Remember what I told you in the session on Alameen: عالَم is what is known; عالِم is the one who knows; علیم is the absolute knower, which is Allah, azza wa jal. So Allah created the عالَم so that the عالِم could recognize the علیم. Recognize what? His love for His creation. To show that even though you contribute nothing whatsoever to His existence or His attributes, He still loves you, He cares for you, He is concerned for you, and He has mercy for you. He has Rehma. The physical world manifests the love of the Rehman. The spiritual world manifests the love of the Raheem. Because He is the Rabb of both, that is why: الحمد للہ رب العالمین.

The Rehman created external blessings. The Raheem creates the ability to experience and enjoy those blessings. All that is asked of us is to recognize it and appreciate it, for appreciation is praise. And praise will create the desire to benefit from the blessing we appreciated. Think about it. Suppose you see a new phone that your friend has just bought. What is the first thing you do? You say, "Oh, this is wonderful! I have to have one of these." Why do you want it? Because you appreciated something about it, and now you want to benefit from it. Is that not so?

Would you buy a phone you did not like? Would you buy a car, or a house, or anything at all that you did not care for, that you did not appreciate? Of course you would not. And when you do buy something, what is the purpose? To benefit from it. So all benefit begins with appreciation.

In the same way, when we benefit from the blessings of Allah, it leads us to gratitude toward Allah. And what happens when we are grateful to Allah? He increases His blessings upon us. Why? Because we have proven to Him that we are worthy of His blessings. We are ready for the next level. This, once more, is part of the Rububiyyat we spoke of earlier.

When a child finishes his fourth-grade studies and passes the examination, what does passing the examination mean? It means he appreciated the knowledge he was taught, and that is why he worked hard to acquire it. His hard work is his expression of gratitude for that knowledge. And so what happens next? He is promoted to the next grade, and the cycle of appreciation begins again at a higher level. And if he does not appreciate it, what happens? He fails his examination and must repeat the same class, or in the end is expelled from the school.

So when an abd proves to his master that he has appreciated his master's blessings and is grateful for them, his master rewards him with a greater blessing. But a greater blessing plainly calls for a greater appreciation: more praise, more gratitude. So we press ourselves further, and as we press ourselves further, he keeps increasing his blessings further, and the cycle goes on and on and on. And the abd keeps advancing toward the love of his master.

And what is the greatest of all blessings? Faith! Emaan. That is the greatest blessing of all. Emaan comes from the word أمن, which means security. It also means peace and tranquility. For the closer we draw to Allah, the closer an abd draws to his master, the more secure, the more peaceful, and the more tranquil he becomes. And the means, the intermediary, for attaining that closeness is Ibaadah, worship. All forms of worship, and salaah above all, these are the means of attaining that nearness to Allah.

Now, for what did Allah say He created us? وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ And I did not create jinn and human beings except for Ibaadah. That is: I did not create jinn and human beings except to witness My love and to draw closer to Me. SubhanAllah! This is the true meaning of لِيَعْبُدُونِ. Appreciate My gifts, benefit from them, be grateful for them, express your gratitude through Ibaadah, and draw closer to Me. And the closer you draw to Me, the more I will increase My blessings upon you, and you will grow continually in Emaan. You will become more secure, you will become more peaceful, you will find more tranquility. And the cycle will go on and on, until the day you come and meet Me.

The Hamd of Allah unlocks His blessings

And this is why Allah loves our hamd, our praise and gratitude. Not for Himself, but for us. To unlock His blessings, while preserving justice. Consider this: I am praising my khala in today's session, recognizing, acknowledging, and appreciating her love for me. I am openly declaring that my khala loves me. And because I do see her love, I am grateful to her for everything she has done for me. How do you think she is feeling right now? Is she happy or sad? I would wager that she is happy. Why? Because I saw what she had wanted to show me all this time.

I will get a bigger, better leg of lamb next time. But think about it. If my khala is made happy by my appreciation of her work, do you think Allah will not be happy when His servant calls out to Him with praise and gratitude? And the way to express that praise and gratitude is the prayer. What are we constantly repeating in the prayer, in every single unit of it? سبحان ربی العظیم و بحمدہ, ربنا لک الحمد, سبحان ربی الاعلی و تعالی. Constant praise and gratitude. And then Surah al-Fatiha in every unit: الحمد للہ رب العالمین, three times.

You know, Shaytan comes to us and says, what is the point of your prayer? You do not even understand what you are saying. Look, you cannot even keep your focus on the prayer. Do you think Allah is going to accept such prayers? You are wasting your time. He does not need you anyway. What are you praying for? You do not know Arabic. You do not even understand why you are praying. What is the point of this kind of useless prayer? Right? Does that happen or not? It happens to all of us. It happens to the best of us. But Allah has not asked for a perfect prayer. He has only asked us to do the best we can. All He has asked of us is to show up. Just show up, with praise and gratitude in the heart. That is all.

Look, this is something you children need to understand. These physical forms of worship — prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, the alms — these are all the mechanics of worship. They are all reactions and responses to hamd. The real thing is recognizing Allah's blessings, and appreciating Allah's blessings, and feeling gratitude after benefiting from them. Once you do that, worship and obedience are simply natural responses. The problem is that we make the prayer the primary thing. No. Praise and gratitude — hamd — is what is truly essential. Worship will naturally follow.

In fact, I challenge all of you. Just once, truly, truly appreciate Allah's love in your heart. Just once, truly feel gratitude in your heart for Allah's blessings. And then I challenge you not to pray when the time for the prayer comes. It will become impossible for you not to pray. اِذا ھَلَّۃِ الحمدُ قَلباً . نَشِطَت فِی العِبَادَۃِ الاَعَضاءُ. When hamd penetrates the heart, the limbs naturally respond in the worship of Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He. Now you cannot wait to stand before Him, to express that appreciation and gratitude to Allah. This was the way of the forebears, of the companions. It was not that they were born extremely pious. They simply, truly and completely, witnessed the love of Allah in their hearts. That is why, for them, not to pray was simply unthinkable. How do I not pray? I need to praise and thank my master.

I will tell you another thing about the prayer. You know, my khala is listening in on these sessions. But when I am praising her, expressing her gratitude to her, she is not the only one listening. Her husband, Dillu chacha, is listening. Her sister, Annu khala, is listening. Her two daughters, Naveen and Nabila, are listening. Her grandchildren, her nephews and nieces, are listening. Tell me. When I am praising my khala, did it not make all of you happy to hear her praised? Did you not feel proud to be related to her? I am sure you did. Why is that? I am not praising you. I am not talking about you. What are you happy about? You are happy because I am praising the one you love. Right?

When you and I stand for the prayer, and we call out, حی علی الصلوۃ . حی علی الفلاح, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, says in a hadith.

We get surrounded by angels. We get surrounded by angels who listen to every word of praise that comes out of our mouths during the prayer. You may not understand Arabic. But guess what? They do. And they love it. The Messenger of Allah said that when a believer stands in prayer, all the angels who are listening to the praise of their beloved master fall into a state of ecstasy, وجد. And they begin to pray for the one who is praying, saying, "O Lord, we testify, we bear witness that this servant praised you. We bear witness that he expressed his gratitude to you." And then one angel comes, and places his mouth upon the mouth of the one praying, and he takes in every single word, every single letter, every single syllable of every single word, until the moment the worshiper gives his salaam. And then he rushes back into the presence of Allah, glorified and exalted is he, and repeats the entire praise before him, testifying that this person praised you, that he repented of his sins, that he sought your forgiveness. "O Allah, I plead with you on his behalf to forgive him."

So do not you dare think that your prayers go unappreciated. Even if you do not understand a word you are saying, it is appreciated. Your effort. The simple fact that you are showing up. The fact that you are setting aside whatever you were doing and presenting yourself before Allah. The fact that you are making the praise and gratitude of Allah a priority. Believe me. Wallahi. I swear to you, it counts. It counts far more than you can imagine.

The only time a human being gets to act like an angel is during the prayer. Allah says in the Qur'an that if we look upon the throne of the Most Merciful, this is what we will see: وَتَرَى ٱلْمَلَٓئِكَةَ حَآفِّينَ مِنْ حَوْلِ ٱلْعَرْشِ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ ۖ وَقُضِىَ بَيْنَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ. You will see the angels circling the throne of Allah, glorified and exalted is he, and you will see them praising Allah. And how will they be praising Allah? What will they be saying? وَقِيلَ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَلَمِينَ. They will be saying الحمد للہ رب العلمین. As they walk around the throne of Allah, as they express their servitude to Allah, there will be a single sound humming around the throne, and it is this: الحمد للہ رب العلمین. All praise and gratitude belong to Allah, the master of all the worlds.

And this is also what the people of Paradise are constantly doing. This was Vaqar's question many sessions ago. He asked, "What will we be doing in Paradise?" And I waited for this day to answer his question, so that everyone could fully appreciate it. Allah tells us about it in the Qur'an: دَعْوَىٰهُمْ فِيهَا سُبْحَنَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلَمٌۭ وَآخِرُ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَلَمِينَ. Glory be to Allah, what a beautiful verse! There will be only one statement declared in the heavens. There is only one acknowledgment that will resonate and echo throughout the heavens. سُبْحَنَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ. My master is perfect. وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلَمٌۭ ۚ. And the people will greet one another with messages of peace. But the final statement, after every single conversation, after every single interaction, their final statement will always be the same. وَآخِرُ دَعْوَىٰهُمْ أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَلَمِينَ. Praise and gratitude belong to Allah, the master of the worlds. The people of Paradise will be people of hamd. They will be people of praise.

and they will be people of gratitude. اللھم جعلنا من الحامدین. May Allah make us among these people.

This is the status we are elevated to during Salaah. We turn into angels, and we turn into people of Paradise, for that span of time, doing what they are doing.

What was that narration about the Bedouin praising Allah? The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and Hazrat Bilal walk into the Prophet's Mosque. A Bedouin was busy in prayer. So the Messenger of Allah and Bilal went and sat behind him. The Bedouin has no idea that the Messenger of Allah is sitting behind him. He finishes his prayer, gives the salaam, raises both hands, and begins to praise Allah.

یا مَن لا تَراہُ العُیون. ولا تُخالِطُہُ الظُّنون. ولا یَصِفَہُ الواصِفون. ولا تُغَیِّرُہُ الحَوادِث. ولا یَغشِی الدَّوائِر. یَعلَمُ عَدَدَ قَطرِ الأمطار. وعَدَدَ وَرَقِ الأشجار. وعَدَدَ ما أَظلَمَ علیہِ اللَّیل. وأشرَقَ علیہِ النَّھار. یَعلَمُ مَکائِیلَ البِحار. ومَثاکِیلَ الجبال. لا تُوارِی مِنہُ سَماءٌ سَماءً. ولا أرضٌ أرضًا. ولا بَحرٌ ما فی قَعرِہِ. ولا جَبَلٌ ما فی وَعرِہِ. اِجعَل خَیرَ عُمری آخِرَہ. وخَیرَ عَمَلی خَواتِیمَہ. وخَیرَ أیّامی یومَ ألقاکَ فیہِ.

What was he saying? O the One whom eyes cannot see. O the One whom the flights of imagination cannot reach. The One who is above and beyond the praise of all those who praise him. There is no one who can do you justice in praise and gratitude. Time cannot influence you. Space cannot confine you. You know the count of every drop of rain that falls upon the earth. You know the count of every leaf that grows on the trees. You know the count of everything that the night conceals. You know the count of everything that the day reveals. O the One who knows how much salt there is in the oceans, and who knows the weight of all the mountains. The ceiling of the sky cannot hide anything from you. The floor of this earth cannot hide anything from you. You see what the ocean hides in its depths. You see what the cave hides in its belly.

اِجعَل خَیرَ عُمری آخِرَہ. Make the rest of my days the best days of my life.

وخَیرَ عَمَلی خَواتِیمَہ. Make my last action in this world the one that is the best in your eyes.

وخَیرَ أیّامی یومَ ألقاکَ فیہِ. And make the day I finally meet you the best day of my life.

He is saying all of this, and the Messenger of Allah is sitting behind him, listening to his praise, and he becomes so moved that he asks Bilal, "Do you have something I can give as a gift to this man?" Imagine how happy the Messenger of Allah is, listening to the praise of his master. He does not have anything to give, so he asks Hazrat Bilal whether he has something. Hazrat Bilal says, "I have this small piece of gold." The Messenger of Allah takes it as a loan from Bilal and gives it to the Bedouin. The Bedouin is greatly surprised. He asks, "O Messenger of Allah, why are you giving me this?" He says, بحسن ثنائک علی اللہ. "For this beautiful praise you have just recited for Allah."

Now imagine this. This is the Messenger of Allah, entering a state of joy at hearing the praise of his master, and unable to keep himself from rewarding the man, even if he must take a loan to do so. When he dies and stands before his master, what reward do you think his master will give him?

What do we say in that supplication, Mutee al-Suwalat, when we open our fasts? یا مُعطِیَ السُّؤالات. یا وَلِیَّ الرَّغبات. یا مُنَفِّسَ الکُربات. یا کافِیَ الھَمِّ والغَمِّ. O the One who answers needs. O the One who is the custodian of all my desires. O the One who removes suffering from me.

O the One who cares for me in my anxieties and my sorrows. یا حنان یا منان یا ذاالجلال والاکرام O the kind, the beneficent, O the mighty, the generous. یا من اعطیٰ خیر ما فی خزائنہ الایمان بہ قبل السؤال O the One who gave us the best of what is in his treasures, which is iman, which is faith, before we ever asked. لا تمنعنا اقل ما فی خزائنک العفو مع السؤال Do not withhold from me the least of what is in your treasures, which is forgiveness, now that I am asking you for it.

SubhanAllah! What a beautiful supplication. O Allah, you gave me the best of what is in your treasures, which is faith, without my having asked you for it. Why, then, would you withhold the lowest and the cheapest thing in your treasures, which is forgiveness, when I am the one asking you for it? It makes no sense.

So I will try to explain this idea to you with an example. But first I want to say something again about examples and analogies when it comes to Allah. This is one of those subjects that makes me REALLY nervous, because I am speaking about MY master, and I know that I have neither the capacity nor the capability to speak of him. But then, to understand things, all we have is examples. All we have is شئی — things. And if you look at the word شئی, it is the masdar, the verbal noun of شَاءَ ، یَشَاءُ،شَئیً. In other words, it is Allah's مَشیئا, his will, that brought forth the اشیاء into existence. Every THING, every CREATION, is a manifestation of his divine will. That is why it is called شئی — because it represents Allah's مشیئا, his will. This is what the Arabs called analogies: تقریبٌ الافھام, a means of nearness or closeness in understanding. This is why ضرب اللہ مثل — even Allah strikes examples for us in the Qur'an. You see, a مثال, an example, is an analogical symbol for something we know, which can help us understand something we do not know. If you already understand something, then, using that example, a person can explain to you something you do not know. And you say, "Ahhh, I have it! It is LIKE this," is that not so? But when it comes to Allah, لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِۦ شَىْءٌۭ — there is no شئی, there is NO THING, LIKE him. Not in essence, not in attributes. So it is always a challenge to explain a divine relationship through creation. Therefore we have to keep in mind that even though we use human emotions and experiences to understand a relationship with Allah, we cannot reduce Allah down to the level of our human emotions and experiences. He is too exalted for that. All right? These examples and analogies are only a tool to help us form an idea. They are nowhere close to the real relationship or experience with Allah. When it comes to Allah, things become amplified and intensified beyond our imaginations. We always have to keep that in mind.

Understanding "Need"

So now, what does Allah mean when he says that he does not need us? The word NEED, in the context of these ayaats, has to do with existence, and it has to do with survival. So when Allah says that he does not NEED us, what he is saying is that his existence, his essence and his attributes — his Zaat and his Sifaat — are not dependent on us. His omnipotence, his being ever living, his being glorious, kind, and forgiving, his being an Ilah.

The people are not dependent on our existence. But that does not mean he does not care about us, or that he does not love us. There is a big difference here.

Let me give you an example. Alhamdulillah, I have two children, and I love my children — most of the time. I love them. I care about them. I am always concerned about them. I am always merciful in the way I deal with them. But I do not need them for my own survival and my own physical existence, even in the biological sense. Consider the need to have children, to leave a legacy, to have love — these are all benefits of having children and a family. But they are not a necessity. Not having children is not a threat to my own existence or survival. If I do not have a child, I am not going to die. It may be a threat to my future — my name, my legacy will not continue. But it is not a direct threat to my own existence or survival. In other words, in order to exist, I do not need my children at all, in both the physical and the spiritual sense. Do you understand?

I need oxygen to survive. I need food to survive. I need water to survive. I need a beating heart and a working brain to survive. But children — as wonderful as it is to have them, alhamdulillah — I do not, technically, need them for my existence. There are people who never have children, as a deliberate choice, and they live a good, happy life. There are people who want children but cannot have them; they too live and survive. There are people who have children and then, God forbid, lose them, and even though they miss them every moment, they still survive. They still live out their whole lives. Do you understand my point?

So when Allah says, يَٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ — People, you are the ones who need me; I do not need you — what Allah means is that his existence, his essence, and his attributes are not dependent on your existence. You are dependent on him for your existence and survival, both physically and spiritually. He does not need you to survive; you need him to survive. Just as I do not need my children in order to exist and survive, my children need me in order to exist and survive.

But not needing is not the same as not caring. It is not the same as not loving. I do not need my children, but I do love my children, intensely. I do care about them, a great deal. Do you understand? When Allah says that he does not need my praise and my gratitude, what it means is that his being someone worthy of hamd is not dependent on my act of hamd. He is praised, and will continue to be praised, regardless. But that in no way means that he does not love my praise, or that my gratitude does not make him happy. It does not mean that all my efforts go to waste, or unappreciated. Absolutely not. He loves my praise. He loves my gratitude. In fact, he appreciates it like no one else can appreciate it. But he does not need it. I hope you understand the context now.

And the reason he emphasizes this in the Qur'an is that only the one who does not need love can truly love. I will say it again: only the one who does not need love can truly love.

Consider this: there are three levels of love. There is the love in which I need to be loved — I need someone else to love me. Then there is my need to love someone else. As human beings, we do not only need to be loved; we also need to love. But notice the word "need" in both sentences: I need to be loved, I need to love someone. And both of these needs are selfish in nature.

It's not that these needs are bad. They are simply part of our genetic makeup. But the difficulty with love that is driven by need is this: as long as the need exists, the love exists. Once my need to be loved is satisfied, or I find someone else who can love me, the person I was attached to before will no longer hold any value for me. In the same way, once my need to love someone or something is satisfied, the one I loved will no longer hold value. This is why marriages fall apart. This is why lovers separate and friends turn against each other. This is why we grow tired of the very toy we once loved. The need within the self is gone. Do you understand?

But then there is a third level of love, which is love itself. Here there is no need for love. It is simply pure love, free of every need. Allah has no need to be loved. Allah has no need to love. Allah is love itself. He is Samad, absolute in each and every one of His attributes. And only the one who is love, who is free of the need to love, will love continuously, constantly, and unconditionally. Do you understand? Because Allah is free of all need to love us, and free of all our need to love Him in return, Allah loves no matter what.

Sometimes we feel—rather, Shaytan whispers to us—how can Allah keep forgiving you for the same act again and again? You repent, then you break your repentance. You repent again, and you break it again. How many times do you think He will keep forgiving you? Or you have done something so terrible, you have wasted your entire life, and now it is too late. You are finished. You are doomed. When we think in this way, look at what we are doing. We are reducing the forgiveness of Allah down to the level of human forgiveness, because we would not keep forgiving again and again, and we would not forgive a great transgression. But because Allah is free of all need in His forgiveness, because He is absolute in it, He forgives in an instant. No matter what you did, no matter how many times you did it, no matter how great the sin, if you sincerely repent, He will forgive. It is no trouble to Him. The only condition is sincerity of heart, true repentance. And part of true repentance is not committing the offense again, walking away from it. If we keep committing the same sin again and again, then we are not sincere in our repentance. But to forgive is no trouble for Him at all.

So the idea of true love in Islam is a love that is free of all need. In fact, this is also the definition of true worship: the kind that is free of every need and attachment. It rests purely on love, and that love arises from the purity of hamd, a deep sense of appreciation and gratitude for His blessings. This is why Maulana Ali would say in his prayers:

یا الہی. ما عَبَدتُک بِشَوق جَنَّتِک. ولا مِن خَوف نَّارِکَ. بَل وَجَدتُّ مُستَحِقًّا لِعِبَادَۃ فَعَبَدتُکَ

O Allah, I do not worship You because I desire Your heavens, nor do I worship You because I fear the hellfire. I have found You truly worthy of my worship, and for that reason alone I worship You. This is true worship, free of the need for paradise, free of the need for protection from the fire—a deep sense of appreciation and gratitude.

And Allah has given a fraction of this selfless love, as a symbol, to mothers. Even the worst child in the world—his mother can never stop loving him. She may be deeply unhappy with him, she may be disgusted by his actions, she may never want to see his face again.

But she can never stop loving him. She can never stop praying for him. Now if a mother cannot stop loving the child she alone brought into the world, do you think Allah can stop loving you and me, whom he created with his own hands? Yes, Allah becomes angry. Allah becomes intensely angry, and he punishes with severe punishments—but that is to establish justice, which we will discuss later. It is never out of hatred, never out of vengeance. That belongs to a different context altogether.

The Messenger of Allah (salla Allahu alayhi wa aalihi wa sallam) was once traveling somewhere with a group of his companions. Along the way, he saw a woman sitting in the shade of a tree, gently feeding her infant. He turned to the companions and asked, "Do you think this mother would want, or would be willing, to throw her baby into the fire?" They all answered, "No, Messenger of Allah. It is unthinkable that she would ever want such a thing." So the Messenger said, "Then how can Allah want that? How can the one who holds seventy times more love for his creation than this mother holds for her child—how can he wish to cast his creation into hellfire?"

So that is the first thing. In our minds, we have to separate the word NEED from the words LOVE and CARE. These are two entirely different things. Allah does not need me, yet he still loves me and cares about me. He does not NEED my praise and my gratitude, but he LOVES to hear me praise him, and he loves to see my gratitude. All right?

Why Allah cares about praise and gratitude

Now the next question is WHY he cares about praise and gratitude. All right, fine. I can understand that he does not need me, yet he still loves me and cares about me, because I am his creation. And there is not a single creator who does not love what he has created. So I understand that. But why does he care about my praise and my gratitude? If he loves me unconditionally, why do I need to praise him and be grateful to him? He should love me anyway. Right?

Now let us talk about that. I will give you an example to show you how "I" understand this, but I hope you will connect it to your own experiences, God willing. For we now understand that everything in life is an ayah—everything: every experience, every interaction, every emotion. They are all ayaats. They are all meaningful, they are all valuable, they are all signs that point to something else. They are all in the SEEN realm, there to teach us something about the UNSEEN realm. Right?

So I was thinking about my interactions and my experiences with Affifa khala when I visit Pakistan. And you can think about your own mothers for this example. Most of you probably know that my Afifa khala and Dilawar chacha are on these sessions. I have noticed that whenever they learn I am planning a trip to Karachi, even before my plane lands, they begin doing these things for me. They make sure the fridge is stocked with ALL the things I like to eat. Khala knows I love these kachoris and cutlets and certain kinds of sweets, so she has them prepared in advance and then freezes them for me. She thinks about the kinds of foods I like to eat, the restaurants I always want to go to. She knows the things I will want to buy while I am there, and so she plans all of THAT out. But she does not stop there. She even plans for the little, little things no one else would ever think of. For instance, if I sleep over at her place, she knows that because of jetlag I will be up in the night—so what if he wakes up and he is hungry.

So she leaves snacks in the refrigerator for me, in case I grow hungry during the night. And not only that; she even stocks ANTOX and antibiotics for me, in case my stomach is upset or some other trouble arises. She will plan that far ahead on my behalf, and I have not even landed in Karachi yet. Yes, I do have a wonderful khala and chacha. AlHamdulillah.

Now the question is this: did she need to do any of that? If she had not done it, would it make any difference in her life? It would certainly make a difference in mine, for I would not enjoy all these fruits of her labor. But she gains nothing by it. So why does she do it? I am not paying her. I did not even ask her to do it for me. And there is no promise of return or reward in it either. There is no agreement that if she does this for me, I will do that for her. She has nothing to gain by doing all of this for me. Quite the opposite: chacha must drive in the heat, through terrible traffic; they go from shop to shop and wear themselves out in the doing of it. It is not easy. They truly put themselves through a great deal of effort and discomfort to do these things for me. And there is no need for it, yet they do it anyway. Why? There can be only one explanation. Because they love me. They do all of this for me because they love me, because they wish to benefit me, because they want my trip to be pleasant, because they want me to be happy. Your mother, too, does things for you, little things she has no need to do, yet she does them anyway, because she loves you.

In the same way, we have spoken of how Allah did things for us. Things we did not ask for. Things we did not work for. Things we did not pay Him for. Yet He did them anyway. He prepared this world, and all of its pleasures and comforts, for us, even before we were born, even before we set foot on the earth. Why? Because He loves us. That is the only possible explanation. Because He loves us, and He loves us intensely.

Consider that, linguistically, the word نعمۃ means something smooth and soft, something that glides along without friction, something pleasing, something enjoyable, something that gives comfort. These are all the images of نعمۃ. Who created نعمۃ? Allah did. Then He created me with the senses needed to enjoy those blessings. Would the blessings of the physical world mean anything at all if Allah had not given me these five senses? No. So think about this. Allah created the blessings for me, and He gave me the senses to enjoy those blessings. He did both things for me. What did I do? What did you do? Nothing. Nothing at all.

Now let us take the example of a single blessing. One single نعمۃ. For those of you who do not know, khala makes an extraordinary raan. She makes a roasted leg of lamb that is beyond words. It is remarkable. I have never gone to Karachi without her making raan for me. But it takes a great deal of effort to cook. Chacha always goes and buys the meat fresh. Then khala must marinate it with all these spices. She tastes the spices to make certain that the combination is just right, that it is not too spicy, nor too salty. Then she must cook it at the right temperature. There is a great deal involved in the process. There is a whole process of rububiyyah that has to take place here. And then she cuts a great many things to garnish it. It is a great deal of work. I have watched her do it. But do you know what? She does it with a smile. She does it gladly. She does not mutter, "Ullo ka pattha. Kya museebat hai."

"When he comes, it turns into a nuisance." She does not say that. Because she loves me. And so she does not mind doing all of that work for me. And, I should add, I do absolutely nothing. Who is it who will finally enjoy the leg of lamb? Who is it who will benefit from it? I am. But who does all the hard work of preparing it? She does. Can one buy ready-made food in Karachi? Can one buy cooked leg of lamb in Karachi from a restaurant? Certainly. So my aunt could simply have it ordered or delivered for me, could she not? She could make her own life easy. But no. She cooks it for me with her own hands. Why? Because she loves me.

Allah is constantly working for us. These causes and effects of nature — someone is controlling them. Nature is not an intelligent being. However much capacity and potential it may have to make things happen in the world, it has no intelligence of its own. Just as the soil, the water, the sunlight, and the fertilizer may all have the full potential to grow a plant, it is the farmer who manages these things so that the plant may grow. So although he does not interact with the plant directly, he controls the various intermediaries on the plant's behalf. And the farmer is constantly at work. He is constantly concerned for his crops. So is Allah. يَسْـَٔلُهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَوَتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ Everything in the heavens and the earth turns to Him for its needs. كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِى شَأْنٍۢ Every moment He is occupied at work for them. Why? Because He loves His creation.

Very well. So my aunt has prepared this meal, this blessing, this نعمۃ for me. Now dinnertime arrives. When the food is all ready, she does not simply lift the cooking pot off the stove, set it down before me, and say, "Here, eat this. Drop dead. The starving one has arrived from America." No. She makes a whole great affair of presentation, which I never understand. She will set it upon a beautiful tray. She will arrange all the garnishes upon it. She will then make all this additional effort to present it in the most beautiful manner. Why? It already looks amazing. It already smells amazing. I would happily eat it straight from the pot. Why does she need to decorate it on top of that? To make it look beautiful, to make it pleasing. For whom? For me.

In the last session I pointed out that Allah gave us sight, but He also gave us the ability to see color. Black and white would have worked perfectly well, but He went above and beyond and gave us color. He could have given us the ability to see only the seven primary colors. That in itself would have been wonderful. But no. He gave us the ability to see and enjoy every shade of color in between. SubhanAllah! He went far above and beyond what was merely necessary. He gave us the ability to hear, and He created the amazing sounds of nature: the sound of the winds, the chirping of birds, the waves of the ocean, the sound of a waterfall, rivers flowing, rain falling. AllahuAkbar.

He did not give us the ability to feel until He had first created the warmth of the sun, the coolness of the breeze, the sensation of water, the sensation of sand upon the beach. He did not give us taste until He had made delicious foods for us to enjoy. Just look at fruit. Look at the variety of tastes that exist within fruit. All the way from sweet to sour, and everything in between. The skin of the fruit has its own taste and texture; the flesh of the fruit has its own taste and texture; the juice of the fruit has its own taste and texture. To eat one fruit by itself is one taste; to mix it with other fruits and make a fruit salad is another taste.

To have one juice by itself is one taste; to mix a combination of juices is another taste altogether. Allahu akbar. Do we ever take the time to reflect on these things? فَبِأَىِّ آلَآءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you deny? Subhan Allah. Allah did not merely give us things; He made them, for our sake, wonderful beyond all necessity.

Now, imagine I eat this leg of lamb and I say, "Subhan Allah, Khala. This tastes amazing. It is so good. I love it. You are the best." Did Khala need that praise? Is that why she went through all of that hard work — so that she could hear me say "You are the best"? No. And yet, after I enjoyed that dinner, when I told her, "This food tastes amazing, you are the best, Khala, I love you," did that make her happy? Yes, it did.

This is a continuation of the previous session. I divided the concept of hamd, as it relates to us, into two parts. We covered the first part last time, in which I explained what hamd means and the kinds of hamd. There is hamd for Allah, and there is hamd for the sake of Allah, which is the hamd offered to his intermediaries. We spoke about the fact that although Allah does not NEED us, he still DOES love us. He does not NEED our praise and gratitude, but he DOES love and appreciate it. We also spoke about how hamd is a mechanism, designed by the Rabb for the progression of his abd. It facilitates his physical and spiritual growth and brings him closer to his Rabb. And this ability to appreciate and to be grateful has been placed within the core essence, the lubb, of every human being. Every child is created with this capacity for hamd.

In fact, it is narrated in a hadees of Rasul Allah (Salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) in which he tells us that when Allah fashioned his first creation, Adam AS, and blew his rooh into him — ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِ — this rooh was blown into Adam from the head down. And the hadees says that when the rooh reached his nose, it tickled him. And when something tickles your nose, what happens? You sneeze! So Adam AS sneezed. And appreciating the fact that he had been given the blessing of life, that he was now alive, he instinctively cherished the gift of life and became grateful for it. And so his immediate response to that sneeze, WITHOUT anyone teaching him anything — the first words that came out of the mouth of the first human being — were AlHamdulillah! Allah did not teach him that.

And this is very interesting, because when it came to proving himself before the angels — وَعَلَّمَ آدَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا — Allah TAUGHT Adam all the divine names. When Adam and Hawwa made the mistake of reaching for the forbidden tree, they were punished. But they wanted to seek forgiveness — فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ — their master taught them certain words through which they presented their repentance. So at every stage we find that Adam needed training. But not when he sneezed. Not when he recognized, appreciated, and was grateful for the blessing of life. He instinctively said AlHamdulillah. Because hamd is something that Allah had ingrained within him, within his inner nature, within his lubb.

When Allah heard these words, he was so pleased that his slave had appreciated his blessing and expressed his gratitude to him, that he responded, saying, Yarhamakul Allah Ya Adam — your Allah will ALWAYS have mercy on you, O Adam. Think about this for a moment. This is the very first conversation taking place between the very first abd and his Rabb. And what is this conversation? An exchange of hamd and rehma. This is the first rule being set between the Rabb and the abd. You come to me with hamd; I will respond to you with love, care, concern, and mercy. Rehma!

This is why today, when we sneeze, we say AlHamdulillah, and the one who hears us sneeze says یَرحَمَکُ اللہ — may Allah have mercy on you. It is a reminder of this relationship that we, as abd, have with our Rabb. And this is why, even in Surah AlFateha, immediately after الحمد للہ رب العلمین, what comes next? الرحمن الرحیم. And notice that there is no other word attached to it. It is now part of a sentence. It stands entirely on its own. Just pure rehma. The more hamd the abd does, the more mercy.

the more love. The more blessings the Rabb responds with. SubhanAllah! What a beautiful relationship this is!

Then I explained why hamd has to be both elements. It has to be praise and gratitude. We talked about why it cannot be one or the other. And then finally we talked about the relationship between hamd and salaah, which is a physical manifestation of hamd. We find in Surah AlKausar that Allah says to his beloved messenger (salallahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam):

إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ

No doubt about it, we have granted you Kausar. Most translations will explain Kausar as abundant. No doubt we have given you abundantly. But that word does not even come close to capturing the meaning of Kausar. The word Kausar belongs to an Arabic pattern, فَوعَل, and this is one of the patterns of hyperbole in Arabic. It is called صیغۃ المبالغۃ. AlKausar comes from kasra, or kaseer, which actually means to have in abundance, to have plenty, to have lots. But AlKausar is then a hyperbole of Kaseer. It means incredible amounts of something. When you have lots and lots and lots and lots, then you do not call it kaseer, you call it کَوثَر. Allah says I have given you lots and lots and lots and lots, and I can keep repeating the lots as much as I want, because it is کَوثَر.

Then کَوثَر is not just about huge quantities. It also implies something extremely valuable. For example, if someone owns a huge quantity of hay, or tons and tons of grass or straw, they would not use the word کَوثَر. They would still have to use the word kaseer. For کَوثَر, it not only has to be huge in quantity, it also has to be enormous in its value. That is another implication in the word Kausar. No doubt we gave you huge quantities of blessings, and each and every blessing that we gave you is extremely valuable.

Now when you say a lot of something and a lot in value, it is possible that it could be all good, or it could be all bad, or it is a mix of both. For example, having a lot of drugs, a lot of ammunition, centuries-old wine cellars. These can be in huge quantities, and they can be very expensive, but they are not good. So it is possible to have huge quantities of expensive stuff that is bad. Or some is good and some is bad. In all those cases, you would still have to use the word kaseer, because the word kaseer can be used for both good and bad things. But the word کَوثَر can only be used for good things. It is مُتخَصَّص. It can only be used in the context of that which is good.

Let us say your parents buy you a phone, which you do not pay for. They pay for it. But they buy it for you, so that they can always make sure you are safe, so that they can reach you when they need to, so that you can contact them in case you are running late, or in case of an emergency. That is why parents buy their children a phone. Now, it is fine if you use that phone to talk to your friends, play games, text them, chat with them, use it as an alarm. All of that is fine. But if you do all those other things, and yet you never call your parents when you are supposed to, to let them know you are safe; if you do not answer their call when they are trying to reach you; if you do not call them when you have an emergency; then you are not being grateful for that phone. You may be feeling gratitude in your heart, you may be saying thank you. But physically, practically, you are not showing gratitude for that phone. Do you understand? Why? Because true gratitude manifests in action, when you fulfill the purpose of that blessing. And this is why: الشُّکرُ نِعمتُ العَین، خِفضُ البَصَر. The eye is a blessing. The ability to see is itself a blessing, and the gratitude for the eye, the way we thank Allah (Subhanahu wa Ta'ala) for the blessing of the eye, is to lower it from the forbidden. We do not look at the things that Allah has prohibited us from seeing. The gratitude for the blessing of hearing is to not listen to the forbidden: the gheebah, the nameemah, the bohtaan, all these types of things.

The gratitude of the tongue is to speak the truth, and not to engage it in lies, in gossip, in backbiting. For every single part of the body is a blessing that has a specific purpose. To understand that purpose and to fulfill it is the true Hamd for that blessing. This is what Allah means when He says:

تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَوَتُ ٱلسَّبْعُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّ. وَإِن مِّن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ.

The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a single thing that does not exalt His Hamd.

وَلَكِن لَّا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ. إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًۭا

But you do not understand their ways of exaltation. No doubt He is Forbearing and Forgiving.

What does it mean that everything in the world is doing His Hamd? Have you seen the sun saying, Thank you, Allah? Have you seen the moon, the stars, the sky, the earth, praising Allah? How are these things showing their gratitude to Him? They are praising Him, and they are showing gratitude to Him, by fulfilling their purpose. That is what Shukur means: to fulfill one's purpose. And we find the evidence of this in every single creation in this universe, in nature. Every organ, every cell within our body knows what it is supposed to do, which is praise, and then it is doing exactly what it is supposed to do, which is gratitude.

وَإِن مِّن شَىْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ

There is not a single thing that is not doing His Hamd. If there is a creation that is in fact not doing Hamd, it is us human beings. The only creation for which this entire universe was created in the first place.

False Praise

A praise that begins in the heart and ends on the tongue, and does not translate into the act of benefiting from the blessing, is false praise. It is hypocrisy. Because you are saying one thing, but then you are doing something contrary to what you are saying. You believe that Allah is your Rabb. You admit that Allah is your Rabb. But then you do not want to do what He asks you to do. That is false praise. In the same way, a gratitude that begins in the heart and ends on the tongue is a false gratitude. It is a delusion of gratitude. It is gratitude that has no physical, no tangible evidence. Not for you, not for anyone else. You are only fooling yourself that you are grateful.

Consider this. I can believe that I love Allah. I can claim that I love Allah. But if I am not obeying Allah, then I am deluded about my love for Allah. Because true love is doing what the beloved asks. Even in the worldly sense.

َزعَمتُ حُبُّ الاِلٰھِی وَ تُعصِیہُ

You claim that you love Allah and then you disobey Him.

ان کان حُبُّکَ صَادِق. لَطاَعَتُہُ

If your love were real, you would obey Him.

لأِنَّ المُحِبَّ لمِنَ یُحِبُّ. مُطِیعُ

Because the one who loves someone is always obedient to them. Otherwise it is only lip service, which means nothing. And this is why in Surah Yaseen Allah says:

ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰٓ أَفْوَهِهِمْ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَتَشْهَدُ أَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ

On the Day of Judgment, We will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they have earned. Why? Is the tongue not the organ of speech? Why is Allah sealing my mouth and making my limbs speak? Because on that day, action is all that is going to matter. Actions will literally speak louder than words on that day.

And look at this verse. The word used is کسب, earned. Why earned? What is an earning? It is something you receive in return for labor or service. An earning is not something you are given for good intentions. An earning is not something you are given for verbal claims. An earning is based on action alone. Blessings are always earned through the action of hamd. This is the most natural phenomenon in the world. Consider it from birth. When a child is born into this world, its mother's milk is the first blessing it tastes. It is not even milk. What the baby receives is colostrum, which is not even sweet. But even to get that, does the baby simply receive it, or does it have to work for it? The baby has to suck it out. And that is how it grows. The muscles are engaged; they grow stronger. And when the baby shows gratitude for it, which is to demonstrate that it can digest it — because that is gratitude, to demonstrate that it is able to use the benefit for its intended purpose — what happens next? Allah gives it the blessing of milk, which is better and sweeter than colostrum. When it can digest that, that is, show gratitude for it, the child begins to eat semi-solid foods, then solids, and then a world of different tastes opens up. So the benefits keep increasing as the child demonstrates that it is grateful for the previous blessing, and earns the next one. In other words, it is the hamd of the child that advances it through the various levels of its feeding.

Salaah is hamd in action.

Let us recap. What have we discussed so far? Hamd is a response to a blessing. That response has been divided among three components: the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. The action of the limbs is the proof of the claim made by the tongue about the intention of the heart. Which means the proof of sincere praise is that it is generated in the heart, articulated by the tongue, and acted upon by the limbs in receiving the benefit. And the proof of sincere gratitude is that it is generated in the heart, articulated by the tongue, and then the limbs begin to use that gift for the purpose for which it was given.

انا اعطیناک الکوثر — We gave you al-Kausar. So now what do you do? Appreciate all those blessings and be grateful for them. And how do you express that hamd physically?

فصل لربک والنحر — The first step is: pray to your Master. Now, if you look at salaah in this context of hamd, it is a perfect manifestation of hamd through the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. When the abd hears the azaan, having already recognized the glory and the blessings of his Rabb in his life, he drops whatever he is doing to answer the call of his Rabb. The hamd is already in his heart, which physically brings him onto the musalla, the janemaaz, in order to receive the rewards of salaah. That was praise, was it not — the desire to receive the benefit? And then, once he begins his salaah, it is all an expression of his gratitude. And so salaah demonstrates this perfect harmony among action, speech, and belief. The body is doing what the tongue is articulating, and the tongue is saying what the heart believes. There is absolutely no contention, no contradiction among any of them.

Another thing that I find incredibly beautiful about salaah is that it is composed of two states: rest and motion. All the duas that are recited in the state of rest are either praise of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, or a listening to revelation.

Notice our state when we are reciting the Fateha or a surah. Physically, we are to be completely at rest. There should be no movement in the body. Why? Because our master, our Rabb, is speaking to us through the Qur'an. So we stand there, attentively listening to his speech. And then, as soon as the revelation ends, we move into motion, in obedience to what the Rabb commanded us to do. And in every movement after that, we do not recite the Qur'an; we recite a tasbeeh. And what is a tasbeeh? It is the affirmation of the Rububiyyah of Allah, Azza wa Jal. And what you believe in your heart and affirm with your speech, you must back up with action. So we bow down before him in rukoo, with the affirmation of سبحان ربی العظیم و بحمدہ. We say, my Rabb is great and is truly deserving of my Hamd, and then, in order to prove that belief and that claim, we bow down before him in rukoo, physically expressing our humility, our servitude, while at the same time expressing our belief: سبحان ربی العظیم و بحمدہ.

Then, سمع اللہ لمن حمدہ. Allah listens to the Hamd of those who praise him and show their gratitude to him. And as we say that, we lift our hands to our ears, because we too have the ability to listen. And we have heard his message; that is how we know that he listens to our Hamd. Once again you can see this perfect harmony between the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. And now that we believe and affirm that Allah does listen to our Hamd, what comes next? ربنا لک الحمد. Our Rabb, we praise you, and we are grateful to you. And with that affirmation, we fall into sajda, which is a greater form of humility. It is complete physical submission. And then, in that state of submission, we express why we are submitting: سبحان ربی الاعلی و تعالی, because my Rabb is lofty and almighty.

And what do you do before someone whom you believe is lofty and almighty? You submit your essence, your intellect, to them, which is the act of placing your forehead on the ground, because the head contains the essence of all five senses. If you recall the word sajda, it means the moment when a camel lowers itself before its master, submitting and relinquishing control of its movements to its master. And then, if you notice, sajda is the most vulnerable state from a physical standpoint. Because our head is on the ground, we can no longer see who is around us, who is behind us. If somebody attacks us, we have no way of knowing. If someone is speaking to us, or about us, we cannot know, because our face is on the ground with both hands at our sides. Why is that? Because سبحان ربی الاعلی و تعالی. My Rabb is lofty and almighty. He is lofty, so I do not care about anyone speaking to me or about me. I am no longer going to be distracted by the enticements of this world. He is almighty, so he will protect me from my enemies, my troubles, my sorrows, my anxieties. I do not have to worry about it. My Rabb will take care of me. It is complete physical submission. So salaah is the perfect expression of Hamd, unifying the belief of the heart, the speech of the tongue, and the actions of the limbs. It is incredible.

Now, if you take this same analogy and apply it to life, take it to the next level: the entire salaah is a state of rest, and the time between the two prayers is the time of motion. Salaah is like a charger for the soul. When you charge your phones, ideally you are not using them while they are charging, right? But why are you charging it? So that you can use it when it is off the cradle.

Is this not true? So the prayer charges the soul. It reminds our soul of our Hamd at all three levels: at the level of belief, at the level of speech, and at the level of action. But when the prayer is over, it is now time to put all of that energy to use in our daily activities.

During the prayer I say: سبحان ربی العظیم و بحمدہ. سبحان ربی الاعلی وتعالی. اللہ اکر. ربنا لک الحمد These are all claims, are they not? I am making all of these claims as I stand before Allah in the prayer. But where am I going to prove that I truly believe what I claim to believe? In the world, in school, in my house, at my job, in my dealings with people, with my parents, with my teachers, and in my dealings with my own self. That is where I am going to prove it.

But then, when I am out in the world proving my beliefs, I am gaining still MORE blessings from Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala. And not only that, because this world is an extremely challenging place for a believer to ACT out our beliefs, on account of all these distractions around us. So, despite our best efforts, we make mistakes, and our soul grows weak under the constant challenges. Our battery is drained. And so what did Allah give us after a few hours? Another prayer. Time to recharge once more. Time to be grateful once more. Time to remind ourselves of our purpose once more. Time to revitalize our beliefs, and to make those same claims once more. And then, when that prayer is over, we return to the world and begin proving those claims true once more. And so it goes on and on. It is truly amazing.

And this is why a true momin is ALWAYS in the state of prayer. When he is not before Allah, affirming his beliefs and making his claims, he is out in the world proving those claims to be true. And when he is not in ACTION, he is reminding himself of HAMD through the prayer. This prayer is an amazing gift to us. This is why Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, says: إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَنَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا There is no doubt about it: the human being has been created in a state of anxiety. He is always anxious. His heart is never at rest. He is easily disturbed. إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعًۭا The moment a hardship touches him, he screams. وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا And when something good comes to him, he becomes miserly. إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ Except those who pray. ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ دَآئِمُونَ Except those who are CONSTANTLY in the state of prayer. They are in the state of prayer during the prayer, and they are in the state of prayer when they are out in the world.

Then there are several other meanings which I will skip. For our discussion today, in this ayah Allah is saying to his messenger, انا اعطیناک الکوثر. We have given you enormous amounts of invaluable blessings, and each and every one of them are incredibly good. Now let us quickly look at some of these incredible gifts that Allah (subhanhu wa ta'ala) is referring to.

Allah says to his messenger in the Quran:

مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ

We did not leave you, nor are we displeased with you. تَودِع in Arabic is when you say goodbye. That is where you get the word الوداع. And you say الوداع when you are leaving someone. So Allah is saying to his messenger, your Rabb is not saying goodbye to you, nor is he displeased. There is a special gift in this verse, because the expected sentence should have been

ما وَدَّعَکَ رَبُّکَ وَ ما قَلاک. There should have been a "ka" at the end of qalaa as well. The English translation of that would have been: your master did not say goodbye to you, and he is not displeased with you. But with the goodbye — with وَدَّعَکَ — the messenger is mentioned. Yet with the displeasure, the messenger is not mentioned. And that is a gift of Allah to his beloved messenger (salla Allahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam), because it shows Allah's extreme love for his messenger. The word goodbye does not carry any negative connotation. But the word displeasure clearly does. And so Allah does not place his beloved messenger beside that negative word. This is how careful Allah is when he addresses his messenger. And of course the lesson of the verse is that Allah is never going to be the one to abandon his beloved messenger, not ever.

Then he says to his messenger: وَ لَلْآخِرَۃُ خَیْرٌ لَکَ مِنَ الْأُولیٰ. There is no doubt about it — what is coming at the end is better for you than what is at the beginning. What an amazing gift to the messenger (salla Allahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam). Allah is saying to him: you are being honored right now, and only a few people are becoming Muslims at this moment. But in the times to come, Islam will spread like wildfire, and your name will be honored more and more as time passes. So what is coming later, in terms of your honor, is far greater than what you are seeing right now.

Then, on top of that: وَ لَسَوْفَ یُعْطِیْکَ رَبُّکَ فَتَرْضیٰ. I will give you so much that you will be pleased. You know, when you tell someone you are going to give them a gift, the response to that, spoken or unspoken, is always: what are you going to give me? How much? What is it going to be worth? How valuable will it be for me? I bet it is the new iPad Pro, because he knows I want that. And then, when you unwrap it, it is a nail cutter. What a laugh. (A true story.) But the real question is: how would you place a value on a gift? Look at the value that Allah placed on his gifts for his messenger. He says: فَتَرْضیٰ. The quantity, the value, and the goodness of the gift have been described in such a way that Allah says: I will give you so much, and I will keep giving you so much, and I will not stop until you yourself say it is enough — until you say, "O Allah, I am pleased; you can stop now."

And look at the love of this amazing messenger for us (salla Allahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam). فِداً اُمّی وَ اَبی. He said: I will not be pleased until every single person from my Ummah is saved from the hellfire. This is the value that he (salla Allahu alayhi wa aalihee wa sallam) placed on our freedom, on our salvation. This is the kind of love he had for us.

And even when it comes to the rewards that Allah is going to give to his messenger: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍۢ. My beloved messenger, you have a reward that cannot even be quantified. It cannot have any brakes on it; it cannot have any limits on it. Think about it. When it came to giving the messenger blessings in this world, where was the limit set? Until the messenger himself says enough. And when it came to giving his beloved messenger the rewards for his work in the afterlife, Allah says: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍۢ. There is no doubt about it — I will give you so much reward that there is no number that can possibly define it, and my reward will never end; it will only keep increasing for all eternity.

Allahu Akbar. Then another gift from al-Kausar is that Allah raised his messenger beyond the seventh heaven and spoke to him directly on the night of the Meraaj. This was a gift granted to no prophet and no messenger before him or after him. Then, in the course of that conversation, Allah bestowed upon his messenger another gift: ان لا ذُکرتُ الاَّ ذُکرتَ معی. Allah said, "My name shall not be called upon without your name being mentioned along with it." We say, اشھد ان لا الہ الا اللہ, and immediately what follows? اشھد ان محمد رسول اللہ. This is a gift of immense value, given by Allah to his beloved messenger. Name one other human being on the face of the earth who is mentioned in this way, without ceasing, without ceasing. And instead of the mention fading over time, what happens? It rises over time. It keeps increasing. Subhan Allah!

And then, following the very same pattern, the messenger of Allah said the same thing for Maulana Ali: that I will not accept my name being called upon until your name is mentioned along with it. That is why, immediately after the mention of the Prophet, we have اشھد ان مولانا علی ولی اللہ.
